It applies to occupiers of cotton ginning, pressing, and seed oil factories, as well as cotton dealers and company managers in specific districts of West Pakistan. metadata.summary: This Act abolishes the bonded labour system within the whole of Punjab to prevent economic and physical exploitation. It declares all agreements, customs, or contracts related to bonded labour void and extinguishes liability to repay bonded debts. The legislation empowers District Magistrates and other officers to implement provisions, establishes Vigilance Committees, and prescribes punishments for enforcing bonded labour or failing to restore property rights.

It establishes pounds under the control of District Magistrates and appoints pound-keepers to manage impounded animals. The legislation outlines procedures for seizing damaging cattle, levying fines, feeding impounded livestock, and providing compensation for illegal seizures or damage caused.

The Act prescribes punishments for contracting, solemnising, or promoting such marriages, including imprisonment and fines. It also grants courts the power to issue injunctions to prevent child marriages and specifies jurisdictional limits for trials.

metadata.short_title: The Commercial Documents Evidence Act, 1939
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Law of Evidence with respect to certain commercial documents.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Law of Evidence regarding presumptions and relevance of specific commercial documents.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Law of Evidence to treat statements of relevant facts in scheduled commercial documents as themselves relevant facts. It establishes legal presumptions regarding the genuineness of documents issued by recognized authorities, such as Chambers of Commerce, shipping registries, and port authorities. The Act applies to the whole of Pakistan and lists specific categories of documents for which courts shall or may presume accuracy and authenticity.

metadata.short_title: The Companies Profits (Workers Participation) Act, 1968
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for participation of workers in the profits of companies and for matters ancillary thereto
establishes: Punjab Companies Profits Workers Participation Committee
metadata.administering_body: Punjab Companies Profits Workers Participation Committee
metadata.one_line: Provides for worker participation in company profits via a dedicated fund managed by a Board of Trustees.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a mechanism for workers to participate in the profits of companies operating in Punjab. It mandates the creation of a Workers Participation Fund managed by a Board of Trustees, which distributes benefits to eligible employees based on net asset values and specific schemes. The legislation defines eligibility criteria, including provisions for seasonal industries, and outlines tax treatments for both the fund and worker income.

metadata.short_title: The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish an order wherein the State shall exercise its powers and authority through the chosen representatives of the people, observe principles of democracy, freedom, equality, tolerance and social justice as enunciated by Islam, enable Muslims to order their lives in accordance with the teachings of Islam, make adequate provision for minorities, safeguard fundamental rights, secure independence of judiciary, and safeguard integrity of territories.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Federal Islamic Republic of Pakistan with fundamental rights and democratic principles.
metadata.summary: This document establishes the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, defining it as a federal republic based on Islamic principles. It outlines the structure of government including Parliament, Provincial Assemblies, and an independent judiciary. The Constitution guarantees fundamental rights to citizens, safeguards minority interests, and ensures social justice while maintaining the sovereignty of Almighty Allah.

metadata.short_title: The Contract Act, 1872
metadata.long_title: An Act to define and amend certain parts of the law relating to contracts
repeals: The enactments mentioned in the schedule hereto
metadata.one_line: Defines and amends the law relating to contracts, agreements, sale of goods, agency, and partnership.
metadata.summary: This Act defines and amends the law relating to contracts in Pakistan. It covers the communication and acceptance of proposals, voidable contracts, contingent contracts, performance of contracts, and consequences of breach. The Act also addresses certain relations resembling contracts, such as necessaries supplied to incapable persons and liability for goods found. Specific chapters on sale of goods, indemnity, guarantee, agency, and partnership are included, with some sections repealed by later legislation.

metadata.short_title: The Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the laws relating to narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances
repeals: Control of Narcotic Substances Ordinance, 1996
establishes: National Fund for Control of Drug Abuse
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regarding narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances, trafficking, and addict rehabilitation.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends existing laws concerning the production, processing, and trafficking of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances. It establishes prohibitions on cultivation, possession, import/export, and financing of drug offenses, while providing for punishment and asset forfeiture mechanisms. The legislation also creates a National Fund for control of drug abuse, sets up Special Courts for trying related offenses, and outlines procedures for international co-operation and mutual legal assistance.

metadata.short_title: The Cooperative Societies (Repayment of Loans) Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the repayment of certain unsecured loans or loans insufficiently secured.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: Provides for the repayment and securing of unsecured loans taken from cooperative banks and societies.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance mandates the repayment of specific unsecured or insufficiently secured loans taken from Cooperative Banks and other Cooperative Societies. It requires borrowers to repay at least twenty percent within six months and secure the balance with adequate property within two years, subject to Registrar approval. The Ordinance empowers the Registrar to conduct inquiries with civil court-like powers to determine liability and issue notices for repayment.

metadata.short_title: COTHM Global Institute, Lahore Act 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the reconstitution of the COTHM Global Institute, Lahore.
metadata.one_line: An Act to reconstitute the COTHM Global Institute, Lahore as a private sector body corporate in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the reconstitution of the COTHM Global Institute, Lahore as a private sector institute located in Lahore. It establishes the Institute as a body corporate with perpetual succession and defines its structure, including the Patron, Board of Governors, Academic Council, and various faculties. The Act outlines the functions, powers, and governance mechanisms for the Institute, covering administration, instruction, examinations, and financial management.

name: COTTON GINNING AND PRESSING FACTORIES ACT, 1925

metadata.short_title: The Cotton Ginning and Pressing Factories Act, 1925
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the better regulation of cotton ginning and cotton pressing factories.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Provincial Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint
metadata.one_line: Regulates cotton ginning and pressing factories in Punjab regarding registers, marking, and returns.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the better regulation of cotton ginning and cotton pressing factories within the Province of the Punjab. It mandates the maintenance of specific registers for ginning and pressing activities, requires the marking of bales, and establishes rules for returns and structural requirements. The Provincial Government is empowered to make rules under this Act, and it defines key terms such as 'bale', 'cotton', and 'Occupier' to ensure compliance.

metadata.short_title: The Cotton Industry (Statistics) Act, 1926
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the regular submission of returns of quantities of cotton goods manufactured and cotton yarn spun in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.max_penalty: five hundred rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act mandates monthly submission of cotton production statistics by mill owners in Punjab and grants inspection powers.
metadata.summary: The Cotton Industry (Statistics) Act, 1926 requires mill owners in the Province of the Punjab to submit monthly returns on cotton goods manufactured and yarn spun. It empowers officers authorized by the Provincial Government to inspect mills and verify the accuracy of these returns. The Provincial Government is responsible for compiling and publishing the aggregated statistics while prescribing penalties for false declarations or refusal to comply.

metadata.short_title: The Court Fees' Act, 1870
metadata.long_title: An Act to define the fees payable in respect of documents presented to Courts and public offices.
metadata.one_line: This Act defines fees payable for documents filed in courts and public offices across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Court Fees' Act, 1870 establishes the framework for levying fees on documents presented to High Courts, other courts, and public offices. It details specific fee structures for various types of suits, appeals, and probate proceedings, including provisions for exemptions and refunds. The Act also outlines procedures for valuing property in deceased estates and managing stamp duties.

metadata.short_title: The Criminal Law (Special Provisions) Ordinance, 1968
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make special provision for trial of certain offences in certain areas of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: The Divisions of Quetta and Kalat except the Tribal Areas; The District of Lasbela; The Added Areas of Hazara District specified in the First Schedule to the North-West Frontier Province (Enlargement of the Area and Alteration of Boundary) Order, 1952; The Added Areas of Mardan District specified in Schedule A to the North-West Frontier Province (Increase of Area and Alteration of Boundary) Order, 1953; The Added Areas of Hazara District specified in the First Schedule to the North-West Frontier Province (Enlargement of the Area and Alteration of Boundary) Order, 1955; The former excluded Areas of Upper Tanawal and the Baluch Area of Dera Ghazi Khan specified in the Schedule to the Excluded Areas (Cesser of Exclusion) (West Pakistan) Order, 1961.
repeals: The Quetta and Kalat (Civil and Criminal Law) Ordinance, 1965
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance establishes special procedures and Tribunals for trying scheduled offences in specific areas of West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance makes special provisions for the trial of certain offences in designated areas of West Pakistan where the Provincial Assembly was not in session. It empowers Deputy Commissioners to take cognizance of scheduled offences and constitutes Tribunals to try these cases, often bypassing standard court procedures. The law also addresses issues such as bail, security for keeping the peace, collective fines, and compensation, while repealing earlier ordinances related to trial procedures in Quetta and Kalat.

metadata.short_title: The Defamation Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make provisions in respect of defamation and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance defines defamation, establishes actionable wrongs for libel and slander, and sets procedural rules for trials in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Defamation Ordinance, 2002 provides legal provisions regarding defamation, distinguishing between slander (oral) and libel (written/visual). It declares the publication of defamatory matter an actionable wrong without requiring proof of special damage. The law defines key terms such as 'editor', 'publisher', and 'broadcasting', and establishes specific time limits for filing actions and appeals.

metadata.short_title: Defence Housing Authority Lahore, Ordinance, 1999
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish the Defence Housing Authority Lahore
metadata.territorial_extent: the area notified by the Government
repeals: XXXI of 1999
metadata.status_evidence: It shall come into force at once and shall be deemed to have taken effect on the day the Defence Housing Authority Lahore, Ordinance, 1999 (XXXI of 1999) stands repealed under Article 128(2) of the Constitution.
metadata.repealed_by: XXXI of 1999
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to two thousand rupees per day or imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with both
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Defence Housing Authority Lahore in Punjab to regulate housing facilities and manage authority funds.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Defence Housing Authority Lahore as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It vests general direction in a Governing Body comprising military and government officials, while an Executive Board exercises delegated powers. The Authority is empowered to plan housing development, acquire land for public purposes, maintain a fund, and enforce compliance through penalties for unauthorized construction or use of property.

metadata.short_title: The Defence Housing Authority Rawalpindi Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Defence Housing Authority Rawalpindi.
metadata.territorial_extent: the Specified Area in Rawalpindi Division
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from 15 August 2010
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Defence Housing Authority Rawalpindi for land development and welfare of defence forces families.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Defence Housing Authority Rawalpindi as a body corporate to carry out schemes and projects for land development. Its primary purpose is to provide housing and financial security for bereaved families of martyrs, war-injured, disabled, and other personnel of the defence forces. The Authority has powers to acquire land, frame regulations, cancel allotments, and manage property within the Specified Area in Rawalpindi Division.

name: DERA GHAZI KHAN DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (REPEAL) ACT 2017

metadata.short_title: The Dera Ghazi Khan Development Authority (Repeal) Act 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the Dera Ghazi Khan Development Authority Act, 1991
repeals: The Dera Ghazi Khan Development Authority Act, 1991 (VI of 1991)
The Dera Ghazi Khan Development Authority (Repeal) Ordinance 2017 (X of 2017)
metadata.one_line: Repeals the Dera Ghazi Khan Development Authority Act, 1991 and the corresponding 2017 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act repeals the Dera Ghazi Khan Development Authority Act, 1991 to allow the authority to be constituted under the Development of Cities Act 1976. It also repeals the Dera Ghazi Khan Development Authority (Repeal) Ordinance 2017 which had previously been in force. The savings clause ensures that rules, appointments, contracts, and rights acquired under the repealed Act continue to have effect unless specifically cancelled.

name: DERA GHAZI KHAN EXCLUDED AREA ELECTORAL LAWS REGULATION, 1950

metadata.short_title: the Dera Ghazi Khan Excluded Area Electoral Laws Regulation, 1950
metadata.territorial_extent: the Excluded Area in the Punjab province situated to the west of the Dera Ghazi Khan district
metadata.parent_law: Government of India Act, 1935
metadata.one_line: Regulation applying Punjab Legislative Assembly electoral rules to the Excluded Area west of Dera Ghazi Khan.
metadata.summary: This Regulation applies certain Rules framed under the Government of India Act, 1935 regarding elections to the Punjab Legislative Assembly to a specific excluded area. The regulation extends specifically to the Excluded Area in the Punjab province situated to the west of the Dera Ghazi Khan district. It was promulgated by the Governor-General with immediate effect on September 9, 1950.

name: DERA GHAZI KHAN EXCLUDED AREA LAWS REGULATION, 1950

metadata.short_title: The Dera Ghazi Khan Excluded Area Laws Regulation, 1950
metadata.long_title: Regulation for the peace and good Government of the Dera Ghazi Khan Excluded Area, under section 92 of the Government of India Act, 1935.
metadata.territorial_extent: the Dera Ghazi Khan Excluded Area
metadata.commencement: on the date when the Baluch Area was declared an Excluded Area
metadata.one_line: Regulates peace and government in the Dera Ghazi Khan Excluded Area by enforcing specific laws.
metadata.summary: This Regulation applies to the Dera Ghazi Khan Excluded Area to ensure peace and good government. It ceases the enforcement of certain laws that were active before the area was declared excluded while enforcing laws from August 14, 1947. The text also provides savings for legal proceedings initiated under previous laws.

metadata.short_title: The Disabled Persons (Employment and Rehabilitation) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the employment, rehabilitation and welfare of disabled persons.
metadata.commencement: on such day as the Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to one thousand rupees and, in the case of non-payment of fine, with an additional fine which may extend to ten rupees for every day
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance provides for the employment, rehabilitation, and welfare of disabled persons in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the President to ensure the employment, rehabilitation, and welfare of disabled persons. It establishes National and Provincial Councils to execute policies and undertake welfare projects. The law mandates establishments to employ a certain percentage of disabled persons and contributes to a Rehabilitation Fund, while also defining key terms like 'disabled person' and 'establishment'.

metadata.short_title: The Dramatic Performances Act, 1876
metadata.long_title: An Act for the better control of public dramatic performances.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: Empowers the Provincial Government and Magistrates to prohibit scandalous, defamatory, seditious, or obscene dramatic performances.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Provincial Government and Magistrates to prohibit public dramatic performances that are scandalous, defamatory, seditious, or likely to corrupt persons. It grants powers to serve prohibition orders, notify them publicly, and arrest individuals or seize articles used in prohibited performances. The Act also allows for licensing requirements in specific local areas and excludes religious festival performances from its scope.

metadata.short_title: The Drugs Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the import, export, manufacture, storage, distribution and sale of drugs
repeals: The Drugs Act, 1940 (XXIII of 1940)
the Drugs (Generic Names) Act, 1972 (XXIV of 1972)
the Drugs Ordinance, 1976 (IV of 1976)
metadata.one_line: Regulates the import, export, manufacture, storage, distribution and sale of drugs in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the import, export, manufacture, storage, distribution, and sale of drugs throughout Pakistan. It establishes various boards and laboratories for quality control and licensing while defining terms such as 'adulterated drug' and 'counterfeit drug'. The Act also outlines penalties for offences related to drug regulation and provides powers to the Federal and Provincial Governments to make rules.

metadata.short_title: The Ehtram-e-Ramazan Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for measures observe the sanctity of the month of Ramazan
metadata.max_penalty: six months imprisonment or fine up to fifty thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: Prohibits eating and serving food in public places during Ramazan fasting hours in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides measures to observe the sanctity of the month of Ramazan. It prohibits persons obligated to fast from eating, drinking, or smoking in public places and forbids proprietors from serving eatables to such persons during fasting hours. The law also mandates the closure of cinema houses and theatres from sunset until three hours thereafter. Offences are punishable by imprisonment up to six months or fines up to fifty thousand rupees.

metadata.short_title: Emerson University, Multan Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of Emerson University, Multan.
repeals: Emerson University, Multan Ordinance, 2021
metadata.administering_body: Higher Education Department of the Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Establishes Emerson University, Multan as a body corporate with defined officers and authorities.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes Emerson University, Multan as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It defines the university's structure, including its Chancellor, Vice Chancellor, Syndicate, and Academic Council, and outlines their respective powers and duties. The legislation also provides for the transfer of assets from Government Emerson College to the new university and sets out mechanisms for appeals, staff mobility, and the repeal of the preceding Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Employment (Record of Services) Act, 1951
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provision for the compulsory maintenance of the record of service of persons in certain classes of employment in certain areas.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.max_penalty: a fine which may extend to five hundred rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act mandates the compulsory maintenance of service records for specific classes of employment in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Employment (Record of Services) Act, 1951 provides for the compulsory maintenance of service records for persons in certain classes of employment within the Punjab. It defines key terms such as 'employee', 'employer', and 'Government' (meaning Government of the Punjab), and outlines the requirements for producing and maintaining service books. The Act empowers the Government to make rules regarding the form and content of these books, while also establishing penalties for non-compliance and procedures for prosecution.

metadata.short_title: Essential Personnel (Registration) Ordinance, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the compulsory registration of essential personnel at Employment Exchanges.
metadata.max_penalty: fine not exceeding five hundred rupees
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance mandates the compulsory registration of essential personnel and their employers at designated Employment Exchanges.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the compulsory registration of essential personnel at Employment Exchanges established by the Government. It defines 'essential personnel' based on professions listed in Schedules I through VI and outlines the liability of individuals over 18 and under 60 to register, as well as the obligations of employers. The document details the procedure for registration, including personal visits or postal applications, the issuance of certificates within ten days, and penalties for non-compliance.

name: EVACUEE PROPERTY AND DISPLACED PERSONS LAWS (REPEAL) ACT, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Evacuee Property and Displaced Persons Laws (Repeal) Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal certain laws relating to evacuee property and the rehabilitation of the displaced persons
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan (adapted for Punjab)
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on the first day of July, 1974
repeals: Registration of Claims (Displaced Persons) Act, 1956
Pakistan Rehabilitation Act, 1956
Pakistan (Administration of Evacuee Property) Act, 1957
Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1958
Displaced Persons (Land Settlement) Act, 1958
Scrutiny of Claims (Evacuee Property) Regulation, 1961
Price of Evacuee Property and Public Dues (Recovery) Regulation, 1971
metadata.one_line: This Act repeals specific laws regarding evacuee property and displaced persons rehabilitation in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Evacuee Property and Displaced Persons Laws (Repeal) Act, 1975 was enacted to repeal several older Acts and Regulations concerning evacuee property and the rehabilitation of displaced persons. It establishes the Full Board and other officers with powers similar to a civil court to handle inquiries and hearings related to these matters. The Act also provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the law and bars civil courts from interfering with decisions made by the appointed officers.

name: EX-EMPLOYEES OF THE FORMER GOVERNMENT OF EAST PAKISTAN (APPOINTMENT TO PROVINCIAL POSTS) ACT 1986

metadata.short_title: The Ex-Employees of the former Government of East Pakistan (Appointment to Provincial Posts) Act, 1986
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the appointment and conditions of service of former employees of the Government of East Pakistan to posts under the Government of the Punjab.
metadata.commencement: at once and shall be deemed to have taken effect on the sixteenth day of December, 1971
metadata.one_line: Provides for appointment and service conditions for former East Pakistan government employees in Punjab posts.
metadata.summary: This Act facilitates the appointment of former employees of the Government of East Pakistan to existing or supernumerary posts within the Government of the Punjab. It ensures that their prior service counts towards seniority and pension eligibility under the Punjab Province. The legislation applies to individuals who repatriated or migrated from East Pakistan between December 16, 1971, and December 31, 1974.

name: EXCISE DUTY ON MINERALS (LABOUR WELFARE) ACT, 1967

metadata.short_title: The Excise Duty on Minerals (Labour Welfare) Act, 1967
metadata.long_title: An Act to impose a duty of excise on certain minerals for financing measures for promoting the welfare of labour employed in the mining industry and to provide for the administration and utilization of the proceeds of such duty and for matters ancillary thereto.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: Act XXXII of 1947
establishes: Mines Labour Housing and General Welfare Fund
metadata.one_line: Imposes an excise duty on minerals to fund labour welfare and housing measures for the mining industry.
metadata.summary: This Act imposes a duty of excise on specified minerals to finance welfare measures for labour in the mining industry. The proceeds are collected by designated agencies and credited to the Mines Labour Housing and General Welfare Fund, which is apportioned between housing and general welfare accounts. The Act establishes two boards, the Mines Labour Housing Board and the Miners Welfare Board, to administer these funds and provisions. It also repeals the Coal Mines Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1947, transferring its assets and liabilities to the new framework.

metadata.short_title: The Exit from Pakistan (Control) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the control of exit of certain persons from Pakistan.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance empowers the Federal Government to prohibit persons from exiting Pakistan and prescribes penalties for contravention.
metadata.summary: The Exit from Pakistan (Control) Ordinance, 1981 provides the Federal Government with the power to prohibit any person or class of persons from leaving Pakistan, even if they possess valid travel documents. The Federal Government is not required to specify grounds for such orders or provide an opportunity to show cause before making them. Any person aggrieved by such an order may seek a review within fifteen days, but the order remains final and cannot be questioned in any court.

metadata.short_title: The Explosive Substances Act, 1908
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the law relating to explosive substances.
metadata.max_penalty: death or imprisonment for life
metadata.one_line: Amends the law relating to explosive substances, defining them and prescribing punishments for causing explosions or possessing them.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the legal framework regarding explosive substances. It defines what constitutes an explosive substance and includes materials used to make them. The legislation prescribes severe punishments for causing explosions likely to endanger life or property, attempting such acts, or making/keeping explosives with malicious intent. It also covers possession under suspicious circumstances and establishes forfeiture of property upon conviction. Finally, it restricts the trial of offences against this Act unless consent is obtained from the Provincial Government.

metadata.short_title: The Explosives Act, 1884
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the manufacture, possession, use, sale, transport and importation of explosives.
metadata.commencement: on such day as the Government, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoints
repeals: Act XII of 1875 (portions)
metadata.one_line: Regulates the manufacture, possession, use, sale, transport and importation of explosives in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the manufacture, possession, use, sale, transport, and importation of various explosive substances. It grants powers to the Government to make rules regarding licensing and prohibits specific dangerous activities by certain persons. The Act also provides for inquiries into accidents, forfeiture of explosives, and defines key terms such as 'explosives' and 'manufacturer'. Portions of an earlier Act were repealed upon its enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Extradition Act, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to the extradition of fugitive offenders
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: The Extradition Act, 1903 (XV of 1903)
subjects: offences at sea or in air
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates and amends the law regarding the extradition of fugitive offenders to and from treaty and non-treaty states.
metadata.summary: The Extradition Act, 1972 consolidates and amends laws concerning the extradition of fugitive offenders. It applies to the whole of Pakistan and covers both treaty and non-treaty foreign states. The Act outlines procedures for requisitions, magisterial enquiries, surrender liabilities, and specific offences subject to extradition.

metadata.short_title: The Eye Surgery (Restriction) Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to prevent surgery on the eye by persons other than registered medical practitioners.
metadata.max_penalty: seven years imprisonment and fine up to one thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Prevents non-registered persons from performing eye surgery and prescribes punishments for such acts.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance prohibits any person who is not a registered medical practitioner from performing surgery on the eye. It defines terms such as complete blindness, partial blindness, and eye surgery to clarify the scope of the restriction. The law prescribes imprisonment and fines for unauthorized performance of eye surgery or unlawful practice, with heavier penalties if the act results in blindness. Offences under this Ordinance are cognizable and must be tried by a Magistrate of the first class or higher.

metadata.short_title: The Factories Act, 1934
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law regulating labour in factories.
repeals: The Schedule
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regulating labour conditions, safety, and welfare in factories.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law regulating labour in factories. It defines key terms such as child, adolescent, and adult, and establishes standards for health, safety, and working hours. The Act empowers inspectors to enforce regulations regarding cleanliness, machinery safety, and restrictions on the employment of young persons.

metadata.short_title: The Faisalabad Medical University Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Faisalabad Medical University
repeals: The Faisalabad Medical University Ordinance, 2017 (VI of 2017)
metadata.one_line: Establishes Faisalabad Medical University by upgrading Punjab Medical College Faisalabad.
metadata.summary: This Act reconstitutes and upgrades Punjab Medical College Faisalabad into Faisalabad Medical University to improve medical education and research. It establishes the university as a body corporate with perpetual succession, defining its functions, structure, and governing bodies like the Syndicate and Academic Council. The legislation also sets up the University Fund, outlines financial provisions, and repeals the previous 2017 Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Family Courts Act, 1964
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provision for the establishment of Family Courts.
metadata.commencement: on such date or dates as Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify
metadata.one_line: Establishes Family Courts in Punjab to expeditiously settle disputes relating to marriage and family affairs.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the establishment of Family Courts within each district or other necessary places in Punjab. It outlines the qualifications for judges, including a requirement for at least one woman judge per district, and defines the jurisdiction over matters such as dissolution of marriage, dower, maintenance, and custody. The Act also specifies that certain provisions of the Evidence Act and Code of Civil Procedure do not apply to these courts.

name: FATIMA JINNAH MEDICAL UNIVERSITY LAHORE ACT 2015

metadata.short_title: The Fatima Jinnah Medical University Lahore Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Fatima Jinnah Medical University Lahore.
metadata.one_line: Establishes Fatima Jinnah Medical University Lahore to upgrade medical education and research in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act reconstitutes Fatima Jinnah Medical College Lahore as Fatima Jinnah Medical University Lahore. It establishes the university as a body corporate with perpetual succession, defining its functions in medicine, surgery, and research. The Act outlines the structure of authorities including the Syndicate, Academic Council, and various boards, while also providing for financial provisions, staff appointments, and mechanisms for appeals.

name: FATIMA JINNAH WOMEN UNIVERSITY RAWALPINDI ORDINANCE, 1999

metadata.short_title: The Fatima Jinnah Women University, Rawalpindi Ordinance, 1999
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the Fatima Jinnah Women University Rawalpindi.
repeals: The Fatima Jinnah Women University, Rawalpindi Ordinance, 1999 (XX of 1999)
metadata.status_evidence: It shall come into force at once and shall be deemed to have taken effect on the day the Fatima Jinnah Women University, Rawalpindi Ordinance 1999 (XX of 1999) stands repealed under Article 128(2) of the Constitution.
metadata.repealed_by: Public Sector Universities (Amendment) Act 2012
metadata.one_line: Establishes Fatima Jinnah Women University, Rawalpindi and defines its powers, officers, and functions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Fatima Jinnah Women University, Rawalpindi as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It outlines the university's powers to provide instruction, conduct research, and manage property. The document defines various authorities including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Syndicate, and Academic Council, detailing their respective functions and duties.

name: FOODSTUFFS AND FERTILIZERS (CANCELLATION OF AUTHORIZATIONS AND DEALERSHIPS) ORDINANCE, 1978

metadata.short_title: The Foodstuffs and Fertilizers (Cancellation of Authorizations and Dealerships) Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the cancellation of authorizations and dealerships issued for distribution of foodstuffs and fertilizers.
subjects: protection to persons acting in good faith
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance empowers the Punjab Government to cancel foodstuff and fertilizer authorizations/dealerships without notice or compensation.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the cancellation of authorizations under the West Pakistan Foodstuffs Distribution Order, 1967, and dealerships under the Punjab Fertilizers (Control) Order, 1973. It grants the Government of the Punjab the power to terminate these authorizations or dealerships without notice and without paying any compensation. The Ordinance also bars courts from granting injunctions against actions taken in good faith under it and protects persons acting in good faith from legal proceedings.

metadata.short_title: the Foreign Private Investment (Promotion and Protection) Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the promotion and protection of foreign private investment in Pakistan.

metadata.summary: The Foreign Private Investment (Promotion and Protection) Act, 1976 provides for the promotion and protection of foreign private investment in Pakistan. metadata.long_title: An Act to remove certain existing disabilities in respect of the power of disposition of property by Hindus for the benefit of persons not in existence at the date of such disposition.
metadata.one_line: Removes disabilities regarding Hindu property disposition for beneficiaries not yet in existence.
metadata.summary: This Act removes existing legal disabilities preventing Hindus from disposing of property for the benefit of persons not yet born at the time of the disposition. It applies to both transfers inter vivos and wills, subject to specific limitations found in the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, and the Succession Act, 1925. The legislation also provides a mechanism to extend its provisions to the Khoja community if desired by that community.

metadata.short_title: The Hindu Inheritance (Removal of Disabilities) Act, 1928
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Hindu Law relating to exclusion from inheritance of certain classes of heirs, and to remove certain doubts.
metadata.one_line: Amends Hindu law to prevent exclusion from inheritance based on disease or defect for persons governed by it in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Hindu Law to ensure that no person governed by it is excluded from inheritance or joint-family property rights solely due to disease, deformity, or physical or mental defects. It explicitly excludes persons governed by the Dayabhaga School of Hindu Law from its application and clarifies that accrued rights or liabilities prior to the Act's commencement remain unaffected. Additionally, the Act does not confer new rights regarding religious offices or charitable trusts.

It defines a 'Muslim shrine' as a shrine of a recognised Muslim saint including its attached premises. The Act prescribes punishments for women or girls who sing or dance with musical instruments in such shrines, as well as for abetment of such offences. Offences under this Act are cognizable, bailable, non-compoundable, and triable by a magistrate of the first class.

metadata.short_title: The Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to give effect to certain recommendations of the Commission on Marriage and Family Laws.
metadata.max_penalty: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months and fine of one hundred thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates Muslim marriages, polygamy, talaq, and maintenance in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 was promulgated to implement recommendations from the Commission on Marriage and Family Laws. It establishes an Arbitration Council to oversee matters like polygamy and divorce, while mandating the registration of all Muslim marriages by Nikah Registrars at Union Councils. The law defines specific procedures for talaq and dissolution of marriage, presumes dower is payable on demand if not specified, and sets penalties for non-compliance with registration requirements.

metadata.short_title: Muttehida Ulema Board Punjab Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provisions for reconstitution of the Muttehida Ulema Board Punjab.
metadata.one_line: Reconstitutes the Muttehida Ulema Board Punjab to address sectarian issues and promote religious harmony.
metadata.summary: This Act reconstitutes the Muttehida Ulema Board Punjab to provide recommendations on objectionable literature, curriculum changes, and interfaith harmony. The Board consists of a Chairman nominated by the Chief Minister and twenty-four Ulema representing various sects, along with ex-officio members from government departments. It is empowered to administer its fund, approve accounts, and offer opinions on matters related to religious topics and cyber crimes involving hate material.

metadata.short_title: The Namal University, Mianwali Act 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Namal University, Mianwali.
repeals: The Namal Institute Mianwali Act 2019 (III of 2019)
metadata.one_line: Establishes Namal University, Mianwali as a private sector body corporate in Punjab and repeals the 2019 Institute Act.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes Namal University, Mianwali as a private sector institution located in Mianwali, Punjab. It defines the university's structure, including the Patron, Board of Governors, Rector, and Academic Council, and outlines its functions such as providing instruction, conducting research, and awarding degrees. The Act also sets up committees for finance, planning, and faculty selection, while repealing the previous Namal Institute Mianwali Act 2019.

name: NAWAZ SHARIF INSTITUTE OF CANCER TREATMENT AND RESEARCH ACT 2025

metadata.short_title: Nawaz Sharif Institute of Cancer Treatment and Research Act 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Nawaz Sharif Institute of Cancer Treatment and Research, Lahore.
establishes: Nawaz Sharif Institute of Cancer Treatment and Research, Lahore
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Nawaz Sharif Institute of Cancer Treatment and Research in Lahore for oncological treatment, research, and education.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Nawaz Sharif Institute of Cancer Treatment and Research, Lahore as a body corporate with perpetual succession. The Institute is authorized to provide cancer diagnosis and treatment, conduct research, educate medical professionals, and manage funds derived from donations, fees, and investments. It sets up a Board of Governors including government secretaries and private eminences to oversee administration, finance, and quality assurance.

metadata.short_title: The Nazaria-i-Pakistan Foundation (Repeal) Act 2008
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the Nazaria-i-Pakistan Foundation Act, 1997 (XII of 1997).
repeals: Nazaria-i-Pakistan Foundation (Repeal) Ordinance 2008 (VI of 2008)
metadata.one_line: Repeals the Nazaria-i-Pakistan Foundation Act, 1997 and revives the associated Trust.
metadata.summary: This Act repeals the Nazaria-i-Pakistan Foundation Act, 1997. It revives the Nazaria-i-Pakistan Trust which had been dissolved under the repealed Act. All rights, properties, assets, and liabilities of the Foundation are transferred to the revived Trust, while preserving past actions and proceedings.

metadata.short_title: The New Murree Development Authority Act 2004
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of the New Murree Development Authority.
metadata.territorial_extent: such areas as may be notified by the Government from time to time
metadata.one_line: Establishes the New Murree Development Authority for planning and managing a new township near Murree.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the New Murree Development Authority to plan, develop, and manage a new township near Murree. The Authority is a body corporate with powers to acquire property, prepare master plans, and enforce building regulations within notified areas. It consists of ex-officio members from various provincial departments and non-official members appointed by the Government.

metadata.short_title: The Nexis University, Sialkot Act 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Nexis University, Sialkot.
metadata.administering_body: Higher Education Department of the Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Establishes Nexis University, Sialkot as a private sector body corporate in Punjab with defined governance and academic structures.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Nexis University, Sialkot as a private sector institution located in Sialkot. It defines the university's structure, including a Chancellor (Governor of the Punjab), Board of Governors, Academic Council, and various committees for finance and staff selection. The Act outlines the university's functions such as providing instruction, conducting research, holding examinations, and awarding degrees across specified faculties.

name: NEXT INSTITUTE OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY ACT 2025

metadata.short_title: The Next Institute of Science and Technology Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the reconstitution of the Next Institute of Science and Technology.
establishes: Next Institute of Science and Technology
metadata.one_line: This Act reconstitutes the Next Institute of Science and Technology as a private sector body corporate in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Next Institute of Science and Technology Act, 2025 provides for the reconstitution of the Next Institute of Science and Technology in the private sector with its main campus at Multan. The Institute is established as a body corporate with perpetual succession, empowered to acquire property and sue or be sued. It outlines the composition of the Institute, including the Patron, Board of Governors, Rector, and various academic units, while defining their functions and powers.

metadata.short_title: The Nishtar Medical University Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Nishtar Medical University
repeals: The Nishtar Medical University Ordinance, 2017 (VII of 2017)
metadata.one_line: Establishes Nishtar Medical University by upgrading Nishtar Medical College Multan for medical education and research.
metadata.summary: This Act reconstitutes Nishtar Medical College Multan as Nishtar Medical University to provide better medical education and encourage research. It establishes the university as a body corporate with perpetual succession, defining its functions, structure, and governing bodies like the Syndicate and Academic Council. The Act also outlines financial provisions, including the creation of a University Fund, and sets out mechanisms for appeals and indemnity.

metadata.short_title: The Notaries Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for and to regulate the profession of notaries in [the Punjab]
metadata.one_line: Regulates the profession, appointment, registration, and practice of notaries in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for and regulates the profession of notaries in the Punjab. It establishes the power to appoint notaries, maintain registers of their names, issue certificates of practice, and prescribe fees for these services. The document also outlines the functions of notaries, penalties for falsely representing oneself as a notary, and provisions for making rules regarding qualifications and procedures.

metadata.short_title: NUR International University Lahore Act 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of NUR International University Lahore.
metadata.one_line: Establishes NUR International University Lahore in the private sector and defines its structure, functions, and governance.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes NUR International University Lahore as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It outlines the university's functions, including providing instruction, conferring degrees, and maintaining constituent colleges. The legislation details the composition of authorities like the Board of Governors and Academic Council, financial provisions for the University Fund, and rules regarding staff appointments and examinations.

metadata.short_title: The Oaths Act, 1873
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the Law relating to Judicial Oaths, and for other purposes.
repeals: The Repealing Act, 1873 (XII of 1873)
The Repealing Act, 1876 (XII of 1876)
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws relating to judicial oaths, affirmations, and the authority to administer them in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the law regarding judicial oaths and affirmations while repealing previous enactments on official oaths. It authorizes specific courts and persons to administer oaths for evidence and defines who must take them, including provisions for Muslims and non-Muslims. The Act also outlines forms of oaths, procedures for refusal, and ensures that irregularities in administering oaths do not invalidate proceedings.

metadata.short_title: The Official Trustees Act, 1913
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the Law constituting the office of the Official Trustee.
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends the law constituting the office of the Official Trustee in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the laws regarding the Office of the Official Trustee. It establishes the appointment, powers, duties, and liabilities of the Official Trustee for the Province of Punjab. The Act also covers fees, audit procedures, and rules governing the administration of trusts by the Official Trustee.

name: ON-FARM WATER MANAGEMENT AND WATER USERS’ ASSOCIATIONS ORDINANCE, 1981

metadata.short_title: The On-Farm Water Management and Water Users' Associations Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for on-farm water management, conservation and optimum utilization of irrigation water sources and formation of water users' associations in the Province.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
metadata.max_penalty: punished accordingly for obstructing a public servant
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates on-farm water management, conservation, and the formation of registered water users' associations in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the on-farm management, conservation, and optimum utilization of irrigation water sources within the Province of Punjab. It establishes Water Users' Associations as corporate bodies to manage watercourses and outlines the responsibilities of irrigators regarding reconstruction and maintenance. The document grants Field Officers powers to direct repairs, recover costs as land revenue arrears, and punish obstruction of these works.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Citizenship Act, 1951
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for Pakistan Citizenship
metadata.max_penalty: punishable under section 177 of the Pakistan Penal Code
metadata.one_line: An Act providing for the acquisition, deprivation, and status of Pakistan citizenship.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the legal framework for acquiring Pakistani citizenship through birth, descent, migration, naturalization, or incorporation of territory. It defines specific categories of persons deemed citizens at commencement and outlines procedures for registration and certificates of domicile. The legislation also addresses dual nationality restrictions, penalties for fraud regarding citizenship claims, and rules for interpreting terms like 'minor' and 'father'.

name: PAKISTAN COLLEGE OF PHYSICIAN & SURGEONS ORDINANCE, 1962

metadata.short_title: Pakistan College of Physicians and Surgeons Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish a College of Physicians and Surgeons in Pakistan
establishes: Pakistan College of Physicians and Surgeons
metadata.administering_body: Central Government (initial appointments) / Council of the College
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan College of Physicians and Surgeons to promote specialist medical practice and postgraduate training nationwide.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Pakistan College of Physicians and Surgeons as a body corporate with perpetual succession. Its primary functions include promoting specialist medical practice, arranging postgraduate training, conducting examinations for diplomas and fellowships, and facilitating research. The College is governed by a Council comprising Fellows appointed by the Central Government and elected members, with specific provisions for its administration, finances, and legal protections.

name: PAKISTAN DAY MEMORIAL CESS PUNJAB ACT, 1964

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Day Memorial Cess (Punjab) Act, 1964
metadata.long_title: An Act to raise funds for the Pakistan Day Memorial.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab, except the Tribal Areas
metadata.one_line: This Act levies a cess on cinema and race-course tickets to fund the Pakistan Day Memorial in Lahore.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Day Memorial Cess (Punjab) Act, 1964 was enacted to raise funds for the construction of the Pakistan Day Memorial at Lahore. It imposes a specific levy on admission tickets for cinema houses and race-courses within the Punjab province. The proceeds are collected according to rules made by the Provincial Government and credited to the Provincial Consolidated Fund after meeting memorial expenses.

name: PAKISTAN KIDNEY AND LIVER INSTITUTE AND RESEARCH CENTER ACT 2019

metadata.short_title: Pakistan Kidney and Liver Institute and Research Center Act 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Pakistan Kidney and Liver Institute and Research Center.
repeals: Pakistan Kidney and Liver Institute and Research Centre Act, 2014 (Act II of 2015)
establishes: Pakistan Kidney and Liver Institute and Research Center
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Kidney and Liver Institute and Research Center in Punjab for medical care, research, and education.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Pakistan Kidney and Liver Institute and Research Center as a body corporate within the Punjab. The Institute is tasked with providing specialized medical care, conducting research on kidney, liver, bladder, prostate, and pancreatic diseases, and offering medical education and training. It grants the Institute powers to manage funds, acquire property, and coordinate with international institutions while ensuring its administration by a Board of Governors appointed by the Government.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Nursing Council Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend and consolidate the laws relating to registration and training of nurses, midwives and health visitors.
amends: West Pakistan Nursing Services Ordinance, 1959 (W.P. Ordinance No. L of 1959)
repeals: Pakistan Nursing Council Act, 1952 (LIX of 1952)
West Pakistan Nursing Services Ordinance, 1959 (W.P. Ordinance No. L of 1959)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Nursing Council to regulate nursing, midwifery, and health visitor registration and training nationwide.
metadata.summary: This Act amends and consolidates laws regarding the registration and training of nurses, midwives, and health visitors in Pakistan. It establishes the Pakistan Nursing Council as a corporate body with members from various sectors including provincial governments, the armed forces, and professional federations. The Act provides for the recognition of institutions, maintenance of registers, inspection powers, and penalties for unauthorized practice, while repealing previous legislation.

metadata.short_title: Pakistan Penal Code
metadata.long_title: XLV of 1860
metadata.max_penalty: death
metadata.one_line: Defines offences, punishments, and general exceptions applicable throughout Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the substantive criminal law for Pakistan, defining various offences and their corresponding punishments. It outlines general explanations regarding terms like 'person', 'property', and 'good faith', while also detailing exceptions such as private defence and acts done by mistake. The Code applies to citizens and persons in service of Pakistan both within and outside the country.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Rangers Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to constitute a force called the [Pakistan Rangers] for the protection of and maintenance of order in the border areas
metadata.territorial_extent: the Provinces of the Punjab and Sind
repeals: The West Pakistan Border Police Act, 1958
The Sind Rangers Force Act, 1943
metadata.max_penalty: transportation for life or rigorous imprisonment for seven years
metadata.one_line: Constitutes the Pakistan Rangers force for border protection and maintenance of order in Punjab and Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Pakistan Rangers force to protect border areas and maintain order. It defines the roles of officers like the Commandant and Director-General, outlines recruitment conditions, and grants powers to assist police during emergencies. The document also prescribes departmental punishments and repeals previous acts regarding border police forces.

name: PAKISTAN WATER AND POWER DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY ACT, 1958

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Water and Power Development Authority Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the unified and co-ordinated development of the water and power resources of Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan except the Districts of Karachi
repeals: The West Pakistan Water and Power Development Authority Ordinance, 1958
establishes: Pakistan Water and Power Development Authority
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Water and Power Development Authority to develop water and power resources.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Pakistan Water and Power Development Authority to ensure the unified and coordinated development of water and power resources. The Authority is a body corporate with powers to acquire property, frame schemes, and manage finances including the sale of power. It defines key terms such as 'Government' (Federal Government) and 'local body', outlines the constitution of the Authority, and provides for its regulations and financial audits.

metadata.short_title: The Parks and Horticulture Authority Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Parks and Horticulture Authority in the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the district of Lahore but the Government may, by notification, extend it to any other area of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Parks and Horticulture Authority in Lahore to regulate public parks, green belts, and outdoor advertisements.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Parks and Horticulture Authority for the district of Lahore to regulate, develop, and maintain public parks, green belts, and green areas. It grants the Authority powers to manage billboards, sky signs, and outdoor advertisements while promoting open views of the Punjab. The legislation also outlines provisions for maintenance duties, fund management, annual reporting, and penalties for unauthorized use or contravention of orders.

metadata.short_title: The Partnership Act, 1932
metadata.long_title: An Act to define and amend the law relating to partnership
metadata.commencement: 1932-10-01, except section 69 which shall come into force on 1933-10-01
metadata.one_line: Defines partnership law, outlines partner duties/liabilities, and mandates firm registration.
metadata.summary: This Act defines the legal relationship between partners in a business and establishes that partnership arises from contract rather than status. It details the rights and liabilities of partners towards each other and third parties, including rules on agency, authority, and joint liability for wrongful acts. The legislation also provides a comprehensive framework for the registration of firms, the admission or expulsion of partners, and the dissolution and winding up of a firm.

metadata.short_title: The Patents Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to patents in order to give effect in Pakistan to the provisions of the International Convention on Trade Related Intellectual Property Rights 1994, in accordance with its objectives and principles.
repeals: The Patents and Designs Act, 1911 (II of 1911)
metadata.one_line: Amends and consolidates patent law to align with TRIPS 1994, repealing the 1911 Act.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends and consolidates the law relating to patents in Pakistan to comply with the International Convention on Trade Related Intellectual Property Rights 1994. It repeals the Patents and Designs Act, 1911, and establishes a framework for patent applications, examination, grant, and infringement proceedings. The document defines key terms such as novelty and inventive step, sets the patent term at twenty years, and outlines penalties for contraventions.

metadata.short_title: The Payment of Wages Act, 1936
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the payment of wages to certain classes of persons employed in industry.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to five thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Regulates the payment of wages to workers in industry within Punjab, defining establishments and permissible deductions.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the payment of wages to specific classes of persons employed in industry. It defines key terms such as factories, industrial establishments, and plantations, while setting rules for wage periods, timing, and currency. The legislation also outlines permissible deductions from wages, penalties for offenses, and powers granted to inspectors and authorities.

metadata.short_title: The Pharmacy Act, 1967
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish Pharmacy Councils to regulate the practice of pharmacy
establishes: Central Pharmacy Council (Pharmacy Council of Pakistan)
metadata.one_line: Establishes Pharmacy Councils to regulate pharmacy practice and registration across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes Central and Provincial Pharmacy Councils to regulate the practice of pharmacy in Pakistan. It defines the composition of these councils, outlines procedures for registering pharmacists and apprentices, and sets standards for examinations and courses of study. The Act also empowers councils to make bye-laws regarding their functions, finances, and internal management.

name: PIR MEHR ALI SHAH UNIVERSITY OF ARID AGRICULTURE RAWALPINDI ACT, 1995

metadata.short_title: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture University Rawalpindi Act, 1995

repeals: University of Arid Agriculture Rawalpindi Ordinance, 1994 (XVI of 1994)
establishes: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture University Rawalpindi
metadata.one_line: Establishes Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture University Rawalpindi and defines its authorities, officers, and functions.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture University at Rawalpindi to bridge the knowledge gap between arid and irrigated areas. It creates various authorities including the Syndicate, Academic Council, and committees for finance, affiliation, and discipline. The Act also defines the roles of officers such as the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and Registrar, and outlines the university's powers, jurisdiction, and funding mechanisms.

metadata.short_title: The Police Order, 2002
establishes: Capital City District Public Safety Commission
key_definitions: Capital City District Public Safety Commission
metadata.one_line: An Order establishing the organization, duties, and commissions of the police in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Order outlines the constitution, organization, and responsibilities of the police force in Punjab. It establishes various Public Safety Commissions at district, capital city, provincial, and national levels to oversee public safety. The document also creates Police Complaints Authorities for both federal and provincial levels to handle grievances against police officers.

name: POPULATION WELFARE PLANNING PROGRAMME (APPOINTMENT AND TERMINATION) ORDINANCE, 1981

metadata.short_title: The Population Welfare Planning Programme (Appointment and Termination of Service) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the restructuring and reorganization of, and appointment of persons in, the Population Programme
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates the appointment and termination of service for employees in the Population Programme.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the restructuring and reorganization of the Population Programme and governs the appointment and termination of its employees. It defines key terms such as 'appointing authority', 'Board', and 'Council', and establishes procedures for selection by the Federal Public Service Commission or Departmental Selection Committees. The document also outlines rules regarding seniority, terminal benefits upon termination, and grants the Federal Government power to make necessary rules.

metadata.short_title: The Powers-of-Attorney Act, 1882
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law relating to Powers-of-Attorney.
subjects: Validity of Acts Done in Good Faith
metadata.one_line: Amends the law relating to powers-of-attorney regarding execution and payment validity.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the legal framework governing powers-of-attorney in Punjab. It clarifies that a donee may execute instruments in their own name with the donor's authority, treating them as effectual as if executed by the donor. Additionally, it protects third parties making payments or acts in good faith under a power-of-attorney, even if the donor had died or become insolvent without the third party's knowledge.

metadata.short_title: The Prevention of Anti-National Activities Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the more effective prevention of certain anti-national and treasonable activities
repeals: The Prevention of Anti-National Activities Ordinance, 1973 (XXIX of 1973)
key_definitions: secession of a part of the territory of Pakistan from the Federation
metadata.one_line: This Act prevents anti-national activities by declaring associations anti-national, establishing a Tribunal for review, and imposing penalties.
metadata.summary: The Prevention of Anti-National Activities Act, 1974 provides mechanisms to prevent anti-national and treasonable activities by individuals and associations. It empowers the Federal Government to declare associations anti-national after a review by a constituted Tribunal. The Act defines specific acts as anti-national, such as inciting secession or disrupting Pakistan's sovereignty, and establishes penalties for membership in such associations or contravention of orders.

name: PREVENTION OF CORRUPTION ACT (WEST PAKISTAN EXTENSION) ORDINANCE, 1958

metadata.short_title: The Prevention of Corruption Act (West Pakistan Extension) Ordinance, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to extend the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, to the whole of the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan
repeals: The Bahawalpur Prevention of Corruption Act, 1950
key_definitions: Districts of Kalat, Kharan, Mekran and Las Bela
metadata.one_line: Extends the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 to West Pakistan and repeals the Bahawalpur Act.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance extends the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 to the entire Province of West Pakistan. It amends the said Act by substituting references to the Pakistan Penal Code and Code of Criminal Procedure with local laws for specific districts in Kalat, Kharan, Mekran, and Las Bela. Additionally, it repeals the Bahawalpur Prevention of Corruption Act, 1950.

name: PREVENTION OF CRUELTY OF ANIMALS ACT, 1890

metadata.short_title: The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1890
metadata.long_title: An Act for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years and fine which may extend to five hundred rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act prevents cruelty to animals by defining offences, penalties, and powers of search and seizure.
metadata.summary: The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1890 establishes provisions to prevent cruelty towards domestic or captured animals. It defines specific acts as offences, such as overdriving, beating, or selling suffering animals, and prescribes fines and imprisonment for violations. The Act also grants powers for search and seizure, allows for the making of rules regarding animal care and licensing, and includes exceptions for religious rites.

metadata.short_title: The Prevention of Gambling Act, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the prevention of gambling

The West Pakistan Prevention of Gambling Ordinance, 1961
The Punjab Prevention of Gambling Ordinance, 1961
The Sindh Prevention of Gambling Ordinance, 1961

penalty for being found in common gaming-house
