metadata.summary: The Prevention of Gambling Act, 1977 provides for the prevention of gambling across Pakistan. It defines terms such as 'common gaming-house' and 'gaming', and prescribes penalties for owning, keeping, or operating such houses, as well as for being found playing in them. The Act also grants powers to enter and search suspected places and repeals earlier provincial ordinances on gambling.

name: PRICE CONTROL AND PREVENTION OF PROFITEERING AND HOARDING ACT, 1977

metadata.short_title: The Price Control and Prevention of Profiteering and Hoarding Act, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for price control and prevention of profiteering and hoarding.
repeals: The Essential Commodities Act, 1957
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government (via Controller-General of Prices and Supplies)
metadata.one_line: This Act empowers the Federal Government to control prices, prevent profiteering and hoarding of essential commodities across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Price Control and Prevention of Profiteering and Hoarding Act, 1977 provides a legal framework for regulating the prices, production, movement, and distribution of essential commodities in Pakistan. It empowers the Federal Government to issue orders fixing maximum prices and restricting stock possession to ensure equitable availability at fair prices. The Act defines key terms such as 'dealer', 'producer', and 'essential commodity' and outlines penalties for contravention, including false statements and attempts to evade price controls.

metadata.short_title: The Prisoners Act, 1900
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to Prisoners confined by order of a Court.
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws regarding prisoners confined by court order, covering custody, sentence execution, and court attendance.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the law relating to prisoners confined by the order of a Court. It defines key terms such as 'Court' and 'prison', outlines the duties of officers in charge of prisons regarding detention and return of writs, and provides procedures for executing sentences and removing prisoners. The Act also details mechanisms for requiring prisoner attendance in court to give evidence or answer charges, including the service of process and commissions for examination.

metadata.short_title: The Prisons Act, 1894
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law relating to Prisons.
repeals: Bombay Act II of 1874
metadata.one_line: This Act amends the law relating to prisons, defining officers, duties, and offences within the whole of Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Prisons Act, 1894 amends the law relating to prisons in Pakistan and provides rules for their regulation. It defines various prison officers such as the Inspector-General, Superintendent, and Jailer, outlining their specific duties and restrictions on business dealings with prisoners. The Act covers prisoner admission, discipline, food supply, employment, health care, and visits, while also establishing penalties for offences related to prisons and procedures for punishing prison-offences.

name: PRIVATELY MANAGED SCHOOLS AND COLLEGES (TAKING OVER) REGULATION 1972

metadata.short_title: The Privately Managed Schools and Colleges (Taking Over) Regulation, 1972
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: Regulation for the taking over of privately managed schools and colleges by the Central or Provincial Government.
metadata.summary: This Regulation provides for the immediate vesting of all privately-managed colleges and their attached property in the Central or Provincial Government. It restricts owners from closing institutions, transferring property, or changing employment terms without prior permission from the Provincial Government. The text also mandates adherence to government curricula and medium of instruction while granting legal immunity to actions taken in good faith under the Regulation.

name: PRIVATELY MANAGED SCHOOLS AND COLLEGES (TAKING OVER) REGULATION 1972

metadata.short_title: The Privately Managed Schools and Colleges (Taking Over) Regulation, 1972
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: Regulation for the taking over of privately managed schools and colleges by the Central or Provincial Government.
metadata.summary: This Regulation provides for the immediate vesting of all privately-managed colleges and schools in the Central or Provincial Government. It restricts owners from closing institutions, transferring property, or changing employment terms without prior permission from the Provincial Government. The regulation also mandates adherence to government curricula and medium of instruction while granting legal immunity to authorities acting in good faith.

metadata.short_title: The Probation of Offenders Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the release on probation of offenders in certain cases.
metadata.one_line: Provides for the release on probation of offenders and establishes conditions for community service and supervision.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance allows courts to discharge offenders conditionally or place them on probation instead of immediate punishment. It defines the roles of probation officers, sets conditions for community service, and outlines the powers of various courts in Punjab to make these orders. The provisions are designed to rehabilitate offenders as honest citizens while ensuring they remain law-abiding during the probation period.

metadata.short_title: The Prohibition (Enforcement of Hadd) Order, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Order to modify the existing law relating to prohibition of intoxicants so as to bring it in conformity with the injunctions of Islam as set out in the Holy Quran and Sunnah.
repeals: the Prohibition Act, 1977 (XXIV of 1977)
the Baluchistan Prohibition Ordinance, 1978 (Baluchistan Ordinance No. XI of 1978)
the North-West Frontier Province Prohibition Ordinance, 1978 (N.-W.F.P. Ordinance No. VI of 1978)
the Punjab Prohibition Ordinance, 1978 (Punjab Ordinance No. VI of 1978)
the Sind Prohibition Ordinance, 1978 (Sind Ordinance No. IV of 1978)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for life or five years, whipping not exceeding thirty stripes, and fine
metadata.one_line: This Order prohibits the manufacture, sale, and possession of intoxicants in Pakistan to conform with Islamic injunctions.
metadata.summary: The Prohibition (Enforcement of Hadd) Order, 1979 was promulgated by the President to align prohibition laws with Islamic injunctions found in the Holy Quran and Sunnah. It applies to the whole of Pakistan and prohibits the import, export, manufacture, sale, or possession of intoxicants like cannabis, opium, and coca leaf. The Order establishes specific penalties including imprisonment, whipping, and fines, while providing exceptions for non-Muslim foreigners during religious ceremonies and licensed medicinal use.

name: PROHIBITION OF SMOKING AND PROTECTION OF NON-SMOKERS HEALTH ORDINANCE 2002

metadata.short_title: The Prohibition of Smoking and Protection of Non-Smokers Health Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for prohibition of smoking and other tobacco uses in places of public work or use and public service vehicles and to protect the health of non-smokers
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to three months or with a fine which shall not be less than one hundred thousand rupees, or with both
key_definitions: place of public work or use
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance prohibits smoking and tobacco use in public places and vehicles to protect non-smoker health.
metadata.summary: The Prohibition of Smoking and Protection of Non-Smokers Health Ordinance, 2002 was promulgated by the President to address the serious threat posed by smoking to public health and the environment. It prohibits smoking and other tobacco uses in declared places of public work or use and in public service vehicles, while also restricting advertisements and sales to minors. The Federal Government is empowered to declare no-smoking zones, authorize officers to enforce rules, and prescribe guidelines for designated smoking areas where non-smoker protection is ensured.

name: PROTECTION AGAINST HARASSMENT OF WOMEN AT THE WORKPLACE ACT 2010

metadata.short_title: The Protection against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provisions for the protection against harassment of women at the workplace
metadata.one_line: This Act protects women from harassment at the workplace in Punjab by establishing inquiry committees and an Ombudsperson.
metadata.summary: The Protection against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 aims to create a safe working environment for women free from harassment, abuse, and intimidation. It applies to all organizations within the Province of Punjab, including government bodies, private sectors, and civil society associations. The Act establishes mechanisms such as Inquiry Committees and an Ombudsperson to handle complaints, defines various terms related to employment and harassment, and mandates that employers display a Code of Conduct.

name: PROTECTION OF BREAST-FEEDING AND CHILD NUTRITION ORDINANCE, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Protection of Breast-feeding and Child Nutrition Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for protection of breast-feeding and nutrition for infants and young children
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan (adapted for the Province of Punjab)
metadata.repealed_by: Punjab Protection of Breast-Feeding and Child Nutrition (Amendment) Act 2012 (Act XVI of 2012)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which shall not be less than fifty thousand rupees or more than five hundred thousand rupees, or both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance protects breast-feeding and child nutrition by regulating designated products and establishing the Punjab Infant Feeding Board.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance aims to ensure safe and adequate nutrition for infants by promoting breast-feeding and regulating the marketing of breast milk substitutes. It establishes the Punjab Infant Feeding Board to oversee these functions and prohibits specific practices regarding designated products. The law defines key terms such as 'infant' and 'designated product' and prescribes penalties for violations.

name: PROTECTION OF BREAST-FEEDING AND CHILD NUTRITION ORDINANCE, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Protection of Breast-feeding and Child Nutrition Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for protection of breast-feeding and nutrition for infants and young children
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan (adapted for the Province of Punjab)
metadata.repealed_by: Punjab Protection of Breast-Feeding and Child Nutrition (Amendment) Act 2012 (Act XVI of 2012)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which shall not be less than fifty thousand rupees or more than five hundred thousand rupees, or both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance protects breast-feeding and child nutrition by regulating designated products and establishing the Punjab Infant Feeding Board.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance aims to ensure safe and adequate nutrition for infants by promoting breast-feeding and regulating the marketing of breast milk substitutes. It establishes the Punjab Infant Feeding Board to oversee these functions and prohibits specific practices regarding designated products. The law defines key terms such as 'infant' and 'designated product' and prescribes penalties for violations.

metadata.short_title: Protection of Economic Reforms Act, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for furtherance and protection of Economic Reforms
metadata.administering_body: Industries, Commerce, Investment and Skill Department
metadata.one_line: This Act protects economic reforms by ensuring freedom in foreign currency, fiscal incentives, and private sector ownership.
metadata.summary: The Protection of Economic Reforms Act, 1992 was enacted to create a liberal environment for savings and investments. It provides legal protection to various economic reforms introduced since November 7, 1990, including privatization and deregulation. The Act ensures freedom in foreign currency transactions, immunity for foreign currency accounts from tax inquiries, and protection against the compulsory acquisition of private or foreign-owned enterprises.

name: PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLY OF THE PUNJAB PRIVILEGES (REPEAL AND REVIVAL) ACT 2022

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Assembly of the Punjab Privileges (Repeal and Revival) Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab Privileges Act 2022 (XII of 2022) and revive the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab Privileges Act 1972 (II of 1972).
amends: The Provincial Assembly of the Punjab Privileges Act, 2022
metadata.one_line: Repeals the 2022 Privileges Act and revives the 1972 version for the Punjab Assembly.
metadata.summary: This Act serves to repeal the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab Privileges Act, 2022. It simultaneously revives the earlier Provincial Assembly of the Punjab Privileges Act, 1972, treating it as if it had never been repealed. The legislation comes into force immediately upon enactment.

name: PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLY OF THE PUNJAB PRIVILEGES ACT 1972

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Assembly of the Punjab Privileges Act, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for privileges of the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab, its Members and Committees.
metadata.commencement: on the date when the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab Privileges Ordinance, 1972, ceases to operate
metadata.max_penalty: Imprisonment for three months or fine of ten thousand rupees, or both
metadata.one_line: Defines privileges, immunities, and offences related to the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab and its members.
metadata.summary: This Act defines the powers, immunities, and privileges of the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab, its committees, and its members. It grants members freedom from civil or criminal action regarding their official duties, protects them from detention without specific procedures, and outlines the composition and powers of a Judicial Committee to try offences against the House. The Act also establishes VIP status for members, provides for indemnity, and lists various breaches of privilege as criminal offences punishable by imprisonment or fines.

name: PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLY OF THE PUNJAB SECRETARIAT SERVICES (REPEAL AND REVIVAL) ACT 2022

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Assembly of the Punjab Secretariat Services (Repeal and Revival) Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab Secretariat Services Act 2022 and revive the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab Secretariat Services Act 2019.
amends: The Provincial Assembly of the Punjab Secretariat Services Act, 2022
metadata.one_line: This Act repeals the 2022 Secretariat Services Act and revives the 2019 version in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Provincial Assembly of the Punjab enacted this law to address legislative inconsistencies regarding secretariat services. It explicitly repeals the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab Secretariat Services Act, 2022 (Act XI of 2022). Simultaneously, it revives the earlier Provincial Assembly of the Punjab Secretariat Services Act, 2019 (Act IX of 2019), treating it as if it had never been repealed. The Act applies to the whole of the Province of Punjab and came into force immediately upon publication.

name: PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLY OF THE PUNJAB SECRETARIAT SERVICES ACT 2019

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Assembly of the Punjab Secretariat Services Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the recruitment and the conditions of service of persons appointed in the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab Secretariat.
metadata.territorial_extent: all the employees in the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab Secretariat wherever they may be
repeals: The Provincial Assembly of the Punjab Secretariat (Recruitment and Conditions of Service) Rules, 1986
metadata.status_evidence: repealed by the Punjab Laws (Repealing and Removal of Difficulties) Ordinance 2022 (X of 2022), s.3; and published in the Punjab Gazette (Extraordinary), 14.06.2022
metadata.repealed_by: Punjab Laws (Repealing and Removal of Difficulties) Ordinance, 2022
metadata.administering_body: Provincial Assembly of the Punjab Secretariat
metadata.one_line: Regulates recruitment and service conditions for employees in the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab Secretariat.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the recruitment and conditions of service for persons appointed to the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab Secretariat. It defines terms related to appointments, pay scales, promotions, and discipline, while establishing the authority of the Speaker and Finance Committee. The Act also provides mechanisms for appeals, rule-making, and the repeal of previous rules.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Employees' Social Security Ordinance, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to introduce a scheme of Social Security for providing benefits to certain employees or their dependents in the event of sickness, maternity, employment injury or death and for provision of financial benefits and for matters ancillary thereto.
repeals: The Employees' Social Insurance Ordinance, 1962 (XXII of 1962)
metadata.one_line: Establishes a social security scheme for employees providing benefits for sickness, maternity, injury, and death.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance introduces a comprehensive social security scheme for employees in Pakistan. It establishes the Employees' Social Security Institution to manage contributions and provide financial benefits such as sickness, maternity, funeral grants, and disability pensions. The law outlines the powers of the Governing Body, procedures for claiming benefits, medical care provisions, and mechanisms for dispute resolution through Social Security Courts.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Insolvency Act, 1920
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the Law relating to Insolvency [* * *], as administered by Courts having jurisdiction [in the Punjab].
repeals: Act V of 1908
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates and amends the law relating to insolvency proceedings in the Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Provincial Insolvency Act, 1920 consolidates and amends laws regarding insolvency administered by courts in the Punjab. It outlines the constitution of courts, procedures for petitions and adjudication, administration of property by receivers, and penalties for undischarged insolvents. The Act defines key terms such as creditor, debtor, and secured creditor, and establishes mechanisms for compositions, schemes of arrangement, and discharge.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the licensing of drivers and registration of motor vehicles in the Province of West Pakistan and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
repeals: The Motor Vehicles Act, 1939
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates motor vehicles, driver licensing, registration, traffic control, and penalties in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 establishes a comprehensive legal framework for the regulation of motor vehicles in Pakistan. It covers preliminary definitions, licensing requirements for drivers including age limits and medical fitness, and the registration process for all types of vehicles. The Ordinance also grants powers to control transport vehicles through permits, regulates traffic flow with speed limits and parking rules, and defines offences with corresponding penalties. Additionally, it creates specific bodies like the Punjab Road Transport Board and the Claims Tribunal to handle disputes and compensation claims arising from accidents.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Small Cause Courts Act, 1887
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Courts of Small Causes
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates and amends the law relating to the constitution, jurisdiction, and procedure of Courts of Small Causes.
metadata.summary: The Provincial Small Cause Courts Act, 1887 consolidates and amends laws regarding small cause courts. It empowers the Provincial Government to establish these courts and define their local limits. The Act outlines the appointment of judges, the powers of registrars in admitting plaints and passing decrees, and the specific jurisdiction and exclusions applicable to these courts.

metadata.short_title: The Public Gambling (Repeal) Act, 1985
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the Public Gambling Act, 1867 (Act III of 1867).
repeals: The Public Gambling Act, 1867 (Act III of 1867)
metadata.one_line: This Act repeals the Public Gambling Act, 1867 and comes into force immediately.
metadata.summary: The Public Gambling (Repeal) Act, 1985 was enacted to repeal the Public Gambling Act, 1867. It received assent on November 7, 1985, and came into force at once. The Act contains only two sections: one establishing its short title and commencement, and the other effecting the repeal of the earlier legislation.

metadata.short_title: The Public Health (Emergency Provisions) Ordinance, 1944
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make special provisions in regard to public health
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to three months or with fine or with both
metadata.one_line: Empowers the Federal Government to enforce public health measures, supersede local authorities, and make rules during emergencies.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated to make special provisions for preventing the spread of human disease and safeguarding public health during an emergency. It grants the appropriate Government powers to direct local authorities, appoint additional staff, assume superintendence of services, and supersede local bodies that fail to comply with orders. The text also empowers the Government to modify existing rules, make new regulations regarding disease control, and provide legal protection for actions taken in good faith under the Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab (Multan) Timber Market Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provisions for Timber Market, Multan.
repeals: The Punjab (Multan) Timber Market Ordinance, 1972
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: Regulates timber business in Multan by designating a specific market area and prohibiting trade elsewhere.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Timber Market in Multan to regulate the dealing in timber within the municipal limits. It prohibits carrying on timber business outside this designated area, except for furniture manufacturing with hand-saws. The Multan Improvement Trust is authorized to allot sites, determine prices, and prescribe conditions for structures within the market. Penalties are prescribed for contravention of these provisions, while indemnity is provided to government officers acting in good faith.

metadata.short_title: Punjab Aab-e-Pak Authority Act 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Aab-e-Pak Authority.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Aab-e-Pak Authority to provide clean drinking water and manage related infrastructure in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Aab-e-Pak Authority as a body corporate responsible for providing sustainable, clean drinking water to the people of Punjab. The Authority is empowered to construct water filtration plants, conduct surveys on water contamination, and collaborate with local governments and charitable institutions. It also has the power to make rules and frame regulations to ensure quality standards in water provision.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Abolition of Jagirs Act, 1952
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the abolition of Jagirs
repeals: The Punjab Jagirs Act, 1941
metadata.one_line: This Act abolishes all non-military and non-charitable jagirs in the Punjab and repeals the 1941 Jagirs Act.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Abolition of Jagirs Act, 1952 provides for the immediate abolition of all jagirs in the Punjab that are not military or held by religious/charitable institutions. It prohibits the creation of new jagirs after its commencement and terminates all accrued rights associated with existing jagirs without compensation. The Act also grants indemnity against any claims or legal proceedings regarding these abolished rights and repeals the earlier Punjab Jagirs Act, 1941.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Acid Control Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate and control the business of acid in Punjab.
metadata.one_line: Regulates and controls the business of acid in Punjab through licensing, prohibition, and punishment mechanisms.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a comprehensive mechanism to regulate and control the business of acid within the Province of Punjab. It mandates that no person shall carry on the business of acid without a license issued by the Deputy Commissioner, who acts as the licensing authority. The legislation outlines procedures for applying for licenses, renewing them, inspecting business premises, and maintaining records of stock and sales. Furthermore, it prohibits selling acid to persons under eighteen years of age and prescribes punishments for negligence or violations.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Acquisition of Land (Housing) (Repeal) Act, 1985
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the Punjab Acquisition of Land (Housing) Act, 1973 (VIII of 1973).
amends: The Punjab Acquisition of Land (Housing) Act, 1973
repeals: The Punjab Acquisition of Land (Housing) Act, 1973
metadata.one_line: Repeals the Punjab Acquisition of Land (Housing) Act, 1973 and continues related proceedings under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
metadata.summary: This Act repeals the Punjab Acquisition of Land (Housing) Act, 1973 to address issues regarding land acquisition for housing. It ensures that any ongoing acquisition proceedings or compensation assessments under the repealed Act continue and are completed according to its provisions or the Land Acquisition Act, 1894. The legislation allows the Government to drop acquisition schemes at any time and deems references to the repealed Act as references to the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 in other laws.

name: PUNJAB ACQUISITION OF PROPERTY (RESIDENCE OF GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS) ORDINANCE, 1963

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Acquisition of Property (Residence of Government Officials) Ordinance, 1963
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the acquisition of certain property situate in Mauza Mian Mir, District Lahore for use as residence of Government Officials and to validate actions taken under the Martial Law Order No. 115 issued by the Martial Law Administrator, Zone 'B'.
metadata.territorial_extent: the Province of West Pakistan (specifically Mauza Mian Mir, District Lahore)
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on and from the 24th February, 1962
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance acquires property in Lahore for government officials' residence and validates prior martial law actions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the acquisition of specific property in Mauza Mian Mir, District Lahore, to be used as a residence for Government Officials. It validates actions taken under Martial Law Order No. 115 issued on February 24, 1962, which were previously questioned regarding their validity. The Ordinance authorizes the Provincial Government to take immediate possession of the property and pay compensation of ninety-six thousand rupees to the entitled party, deeming the property acquired free from encumbrances.

name: PUNJAB ACQUISITION OF PROPERTY (WAPDA HOUSE) ORDINANCE, 1963

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Acquisition of Property (WAPDA House) Ordinance, 1963
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the acquisition of certain property situate in the revenue estate of Mozang, Lahore, for the purpose of constructing the office of Water and Powers Development Authority and to validate actions taken under the Martial Law Order No. 129 issued by the Martial Law Administrator, Zone 'B'.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from the 29th May, 1962
metadata.one_line: Acquires property in Lahore for WAPDA office and validates prior martial law actions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the acquisition of specific evacuee property located in Mozang, Lahore, to construct an office for the Water and Power Development Authority. It also serves to validate actions taken under Martial Law Order No. 129 issued on May 29, 1962, which were previously questioned regarding their validity. The Ordinance authorizes the Government to take immediate possession of the property, assess compensation through the Chief Settlement Commissioner, and transfer the land to the Authority free from encumbrances.

name: PUNJAB ACQUISITION OF PROPERTY (WAPDA OFFICE) (SECOND) ORDINANCE, 1963

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Acquisition of Property (WAPDA Office) (Second) Ordinance, 1963
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the acquisition of certain properties situate in the revenue estate of Mozang, Lahore, for the purpose of constructing the office of Water and Power Development Authority and to validate actions taken under the Martial Law Orders Nos. 92 and 109 issued by the Martial Law Administrator, Zone 'B'.
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on 19th July, 1961 and 18th January, 1962 respectively
metadata.one_line: Provides for acquiring properties in Lahore for WAPDA office and validates prior Martial Law actions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance facilitates the acquisition of specific evacuee properties in Mozang, Lahore, to construct an office for the Water and Power Development Authority. It validates previous actions taken under Martial Law Orders Nos. 92 and 109 regarding these properties. The document outlines procedures for taking possession, assessing compensation via the Chief Settlement Commissioner, and transferring title to the Authority.

name: PUNJAB ACQUISITION OF PROPERTY (WAPDA OFFICE) ORDINANCE, 1963

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Acquisition of Property (WAPDA Office) Ordinance, 1963
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the acquisition of certain property situate in the revenue estate of Mozang, Lahore, for the purpose of constructing the office of Water and Powers Development Authority and to validate actions taken under the Martial Law Order No. 129 issued by the Martial Law Administrator, Zone 'B'.
metadata.commencement: at once and shall be deemed to have taken effect on and from the 29th May, 1962
metadata.one_line: Provides for acquiring property in Lahore for WAPDA office and validates prior martial law actions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the acquisition of specific property in Mozang, Lahore, to construct an office for the Water and Power Development Authority. It also validates actions taken under Martial Law Order No. 129 issued on May 29, 1962. The property was originally evacuee property acquired by the Government of West Pakistan. The Ordinance authorizes immediate possession, compensation assessment by the Chief Settlement Commissioner, and transfer of the property to the Authority.

name: PUNJAB ADHOC PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE (COMPOSITION AND FUNCTIONS) ORDINANCE, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Adhoc Public Accounts Committee (Composition and Functions) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the constitution of an Adhoc Public Accounts Committee.
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect from 2000-10-20
metadata.administering_body: Secretariat of the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Constitutes an Adhoc Public Accounts Committee for examining government accounts and Auditor General reports in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes an Adhoc Public Accounts Committee to examine the appropriation and other accounts of the Government of the Punjab. It provides for the committee's composition, terms of office, procedure, and specific functions regarding the scrutiny of financial accounts and reports from the Auditor General. The Secretariat of the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab is designated to function as the committee's secretariat.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Administrative Vigilance Commission (Repeal) Ordinance, 1982
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal the Punjab Administrative Vigilance Commission Ordinance, 1979.
repeals: Punjab Administrative Vigilance Commission Ordinance, 1979
metadata.status_evidence: The Punjab Administrative Vigilance Commission Ordinance, 1979 (X of 1979) is hereby repealed.
metadata.one_line: An Ordinance repealing the Punjab Administrative Vigilance Commission Ordinance, 1979 and terminating related appointments.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab to repeal the Punjab Administrative Vigilance Commission Ordinance, 1979. It applies to all appointments made under the repealed Ordinance, which are terminated upon its commencement. The law also empowers the Government to make orders to remove any difficulties arising from the repeal.

name: PUNJAB ADVISORS (SALARY, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) ORDINANCE, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Advisors (Salary, Allowances and Privileges) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for appointment, salary, allowances and privileges of Advisors to the Chief Minister of the Punjab;
metadata.one_line: Provides for appointment, salary, allowances, and privileges of Advisors to the Chief Minister of the Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the appointment, term of office, and financial benefits for Advisors to the Chief Minister of the Punjab. It details specific entitlements including monthly salary, sumptuary allowance, official residence, transport, medical facilities, and leave provisions. The document also outlines rules regarding personal staff, telephone usage, and the maintenance of official property.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Aerial Ropeways Act, 1926
metadata.long_title: An Act to authorize, facilitate, and regulate the construction and working of aerial ropeways in the Punjab.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to fourteen years or fine which may extend to two hundred rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act authorizes, facilitates, and regulates the construction and working of aerial ropeways in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Aerial Ropeways Act, 1926 provides a legal framework for the construction and operation of aerial ropeways within the province. It outlines procedures for obtaining concessions, conducting preliminary investigations, and issuing orders to authorize construction. The Act also establishes the powers of inspectors, regulations regarding rates and working conditions, mechanisms for discontinuance or purchase of ropeways, and specific offences with associated penalties for endangering safety or obstructing operations.

name: PUNJAB AGRICULTURAL DEVELOPMENT AND SUPPLIES CORPORATION ACT, 1973

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Agricultural Development and Supplies Corporation Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of an Agricultural Development and Supplies Corporation in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
repeals: The Punjab Agricultural Supplies Corporation Ordinance, 1973 (Punjab Ordinance No. X of 1973)
establishes: The Punjab Agricultural Development and Supplies Corporation
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Agricultural Development and Supplies Corporation to succeed the business of the defunct West Pakistan Agricultural Development Corporation in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Agricultural Development and Supplies Corporation to increase agricultural production in the Province of the Punjab. It provides for the transfer of assets, liabilities, projects, and employees from the Supply Wing of the defunct West Pakistan Agricultural Development Corporation to the new Corporation. The Act defines the constitution of the Corporation's Board, outlines its financial powers, and repeals the earlier Punjab Agricultural Supplies Corporation Ordinance, 1973.

name: PUNJAB AGRICULTURAL DEVELOPMENT FINANCE CORPORATION (RECOVERY OF ARREARS) ACT, 1958

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Agricultural Development Finance Corporation (Recovery of Arrears) Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide facilities to the Agricultural Development Finance Corporation for recovering its dues.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab, except the Tribal Areas
repeals: The West Pakistan Agricultural Development Finance Corporation (Recovery of Arrears) Ordinance, 1957
metadata.one_line: Provides facilities to the Agricultural Development Finance Corporation for recovering its dues by pledging property.
metadata.summary: This Act provides specific facilities to the Agricultural Development Finance Corporation to recover its outstanding dues. It allows agricultural concerns to pledge, mortgage, hypothecate, or assign movable or immovable property to secure loans advanced by the Corporation. The Corporation is empowered to deal with and recover dues through the disposal of such pledged properties in accordance with the provisions of the Agricultural Development Finance Corporation Act, 1952.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the imposition of a tax on agricultural income in the Punjab.
metadata.one_line: Imposes tax on agricultural income in Punjab and outlines assessment, collection, and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the imposition of a tax on agricultural income within the Province of Punjab. It defines agricultural income derived from land used for agriculture or related processes and establishes the liability of cultivators and receivers of rent-in-kind. The legislation details procedures for assessment, collection, refunds, maintenance of accounts, and penalties for non-compliance or concealment.

name: PUNJAB AGRICULTURAL MARKETING REGULATORY AUTHORITY ACT 2018

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Agricultural Marketing Regulatory Authority Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the systematic growth and transformation of the marketing of agricultural produce.
repeals: The Punjab Agricultural Produce Market Ordinance, 1978 (XXIII of 1978)
metadata.administering_body: Food Safety and Consumer Protection Department
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Agricultural Marketing Regulatory Authority to regulate agricultural produce marketing in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Agricultural Marketing Regulatory Authority to facilitate and regulate the systematic growth of agricultural produce marketing. It defines various roles such as growers, dealers, and commission agents, and provides for the establishment of Market Committees and farmer's markets. The Act outlines powers regarding registration, fees, audits, and penalties for malpractice, while repealing the previous Punjab Agricultural Produce Market Ordinance, 1978.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Agricultural Pests Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to the eradication of agricultural pests in the Province of [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except the Tribal Areas.
metadata.commencement: in such area or areas and from such date or dates as Government may, by notification, specify.
repeals: The North-West Frontier Province Sugarcane (Protection against Pyrilla Pest) Act, 1950
The Sind Boll Worm Act, 1947
The North-West Frontier Province Fruit-Fly (Preventive Measures) Act, 1950
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates laws for eradicating agricultural pests in Punjab, defining powers for inspectors and occupiers.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Agricultural Pests Ordinance, 1959 was promulgated to amend and consolidate laws regarding the eradication of agricultural pests in the Province of Punjab. It defines key terms such as 'agricultural pest', 'occupier', and 'preventive measures', and grants the Government powers to prohibit cultivation methods or crop transport that spread pests. The Ordinance empowers appointed Inspectors to enter land, inspect crops, seize infested produce, and destroy it if necessary. It also outlines penalties for contravention and establishes procedures for appeals and jurisdiction.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Agricultural Produce Markets Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the better regulation of purchase and sale of agricultural produce and the establishment of markets for agricultural produce in the Province of the Punjab.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the purchase and sale of agricultural produce within the Province of the Punjab. It provides for the establishment of markets and Market Committees to administer them. The document outlines procedures for issuing licences, levying fees, defining agricultural produce, and establishing bye-laws for proper administration.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Agricultural Research Board Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Agricultural Research Board and matters ancillary thereto.

metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Agricultural Research Board to conduct agricultural research in the Province of Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Agricultural Research Board as a body corporate with perpetual succession. The Board is responsible for promoting and conducting agricultural research across various subjects including crops, livestock, fisheries, and forestry within the Punjab. It outlines the composition of the Board, its functions, financial management through the Board Fund, and the supervision by the Government.

name: PUNJAB AGRICULTURE, FOOD AND DRUG AUTHORITY ACT 2016

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Agriculture, Food and Drug Authority to conduct forensic examinations and testing of fertilizers, pesticides, food, and drugs. The Authority is empowered to render expert opinions on ingredients and quality, manage a fund, and frame regulations for its operations. It applies throughout the Province of Punjab and came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Agriculturists' Loans Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to the advancement and recovery of taccavi loans for agricultural purposes in the Province of [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except the Tribal Areas.

the West Pakistan Agriculturists' Loans Ordinance, 1958

metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws regarding taccavi loans for agriculture in Punjab and repeals earlier enactments.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the law relating to the advancement and recovery of taccavi loans for agricultural purposes in the Province of Punjab. It empowers the Government to make rules concerning loans for distress relief, land purchase, cattle, seed, and other agricultural purposes, as well as the sale of seed on credit. The Act provides mechanisms for recovering loans, including interest and costs, as arrears of land revenue from borrowers or their sureties. It also defines the liability of joint borrowers among themselves regarding shared loan amounts.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Alienation of Land Act, 1900

metadata.one_line: Amends the law relating to agricultural land in Punjab regarding alienation, mortgages, and benami transactions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the legal framework governing agricultural land in the Punjab. It regulates permanent and temporary alienations of land, requiring Collector sanction for certain transfers and restricting mortgage forms. The legislation also addresses benami transactions intended to evade its provisions and excludes civil courts from specific jurisdictions.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Alternate Dispute Resolution Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for a system of alternate dispute resolution of civil and criminal disputes.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint

section 89-A of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (V of 1908)
clause (iii), Rule 1A, Order X in the First Schedule to that Code
key_definitions: ADR service provider or ADR center
metadata.one_line: Establishes an ADR system for civil and criminal disputes in Punjab with specific timelines and confidentiality rules.
metadata.summary: This Act provides a framework for alternate dispute resolution (ADR) to ensure inexpensive and expeditious justice in both civil and criminal cases within Punjab. It mandates courts to refer eligible cases to accredited ADR persons or centers, setting strict time limits for completion while maintaining confidentiality. The legislation defines key terms like 'ADR person' and 'settlement', establishes an Accreditation Authority and a Director General, and outlines specific types of disputes covered in its schedules.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Animal Health Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the prevention, control, containment and eradication of scheduled animal diseases.
repeals: The Glanders and Farcy Act, 1899
The Dourine Act, 1910
metadata.administering_body: Livestock and Dairy Development Department of the Government
metadata.one_line: Regulates prevention, control, containment and eradication of scheduled animal diseases in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the prevention, control, containment, and eradication of scheduled animal diseases to meet international standards for import and export. It empowers the Government to declare controlled areas, establish check posts, mandate vaccination, and enforce biosecurity measures. The Act defines key terms such as 'scheduled disease' and 'competent officer', establishes a Tribunal for adjudication, and repeals earlier laws regarding glanders and dourine in Punjab.

name: PUNJAB ANIMALS COMPOUND FEEDING STUFF ACT, 1974

metadata.repealed_by: The Punjab Animals Compound Feed and Feed Stuff Ordinance, 2002

metadata.summary: This Act regulates the manufacture and sale of compound feeding stuffs within Punjab. It establishes requirements for licensing, packing, labeling, and quality control while prohibiting adulteration. The legislation empowers appointed inspectors to take samples, conduct analyses, and enforce penalties against violations.

name: PUNJAB ANIMALS FEED STUFF AND COMPOUND FEED ACT 2016

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Animals Feed Stuff and Compound Feed Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate poultry production activities in the Punjab; It is necessary to regulate the manufacture, storage, supply, transport for sale and marketing of feed stuff and compound feed in the Province of the Punjab; to ensure standards of production and quality of feed stuff; to check adulteration and misbranding of poultry and livestock feed stuff and compound feed ingredients; and, to deal with ancillary matters.
repeals: The Punjab Animals Compound Feed and Feed Stuff Ordinance, 2002 (LXVIII of 2002)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years but which shall not be less than one year and with fine which may extend to five hundred thousand rupees but which shall not be less than three hundred thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Regulates manufacture, storage, supply and marketing of animal feed in Punjab to ensure quality and prevent adulteration.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates poultry production activities and the manufacture, storage, supply, transport for sale, and marketing of feed stuff and compound feed in the Province of the Punjab. It aims to ensure production standards, check adulteration and misbranding, and deal with ancillary matters related to animal feed. The Act establishes a Tribunal for cognizance of offences, appoints Feed Inspection Officers and Inspectors, and sets penalties for contraventions.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Animals Slaughter Control Act, 1963
metadata.long_title: An Act to prohibit the slaughter of useful animals and to regulate the slaughter of other animals in the Province of the Punjab.

repeals: Section 43 of the Punjab Laws Act, 1872
metadata.one_line: This Act prohibits slaughtering useful animals and regulates the slaughter of others in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Animals Slaughter Control Act, 1963 was enacted to prohibit the slaughter of useful animals while regulating the slaughter of other animals within the Province of Punjab. It defines key terms such as 'animal', 'carcass', and 'slaughter', and establishes powers for local authorities and gazetted officers regarding entry, search, seizure, and examination in stock yards. The Act also provides for penalties, forfeiture of prohibited meat, rewards to informers, and the framing of rules to give effect to its provisions.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Anti-Corruption Establishment Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the constitution of a special agency for the investigation of certain offences relating to corruption by public servants and for holding preliminary inquiries against such servants in [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except [the Tribal Areas]
repeals: The Sind Prevention of Bribery and Corruption Act, 1950
metadata.one_line: Constitutes a special agency to investigate corruption offences by public servants in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Anti-Corruption Establishment to investigate specific corruption offences committed by public servants. It grants the Director General and members powers of search, arrest, and seizure throughout Punjab for preliminary inquiries. The law defines key terms such as 'public servant' referencing the Pakistan Penal Code and repeals the Sind Prevention of Bribery and Corruption Act, 1950.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Apprenticeship Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to promote, develop and regulate apprenticeship programmes.

metadata.one_line: This Act promotes, develops, and regulates apprenticeship programmes in the Province of Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Apprenticeship Act, 2021 is designed to promote and regulate apprenticeship programs within establishments in the province. It establishes minimum standards for skills training, defining the roles and obligations of both employers and apprentices regarding contracts, training hours, and stipends. The Act empowers a Competent Authority to register contracts and constitutes apprenticeship committees under TEVTA to oversee these functions.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Arms Ordinance, 1965

metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regarding the sale, transport, bearing, and possession of arms in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance consolidates and amends the legal framework concerning the sale, transport, bearing, and possession of arms, ammunition, and military stores within Punjab. It establishes prohibitions on unlicensed activities, regulates licensing for dealers and users, and grants powers to prohibit transport and establish searching posts. The text also defines specific terms like 'arms' and 'ammunition', outlines penalties for offences, and provides mechanisms for search, seizure, and census taking.

name: PUNJAB AUTISM SCHOOL AND RESOURCE CENTRE ACT 2025

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Maryam Nawaz School and Resource Centre for Autism in the Punjab to provide education and support for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder. It creates a corporate body known as the 'Centre' managed by a Board of Governors comprising government officials, experts, parents, and other members. The Act outlines the Board's constitution, business procedures, financial management, audit requirements, and grants immunity to its officers acting in good faith.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Bait-ul-Mal Act, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of a charitable fund to be known as the Punjab Bait-ul-Mal.

metadata.summary: This Act provides for the establishment of a charitable fund known as the Punjab Bait-ul-Mal. It creates a Council to administer the fund, which is financed by government grants and voluntary donations including Sadqaat and Khairat. The Council utilizes the funds for relief of the poor, educational and medical assistance, and other public utility purposes.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Blood Transfusion Safety Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate collection, testing, processing, storage, distribution, issuance, transfusion of human blood, blood components, ensuring health protection and prevention of transfusion transmissible diseases.
repeals: The Punjab Transfusion of Safe Blood Ordinance, 1999 (XXXVI of 1999)
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates blood collection, testing, processing, storage, distribution, and transfusion in Punjab to ensure safety.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Blood Transfusion Safety Act, 2016 was enacted by the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab to regulate all aspects of human blood handling, including collection, testing, processing, storage, distribution, and transfusion. It establishes a dedicated Authority along with various committees to oversee these functions and ensure health protection against transfusion-transmissible diseases. The Act defines key terms related to blood components and donors, sets standards for licensing blood centers and hospital blood banks, and outlines offences and penalties for non-compliance.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Board of Revenue Act, 1957
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the constitution of a Board of Revenue for the Punjab.

metadata.summary: This Act provides for the constitution of a Board of Revenue for the Province of Punjab. The Board is established to exercise superintendence and control over Revenue Officers and Revenue Courts, acting as the controlling authority for land administration and collection. It serves as the highest court of appeal and revision in revenue cases within the province. The Act also outlines the Board's powers, conduct of business, procedures for revision of orders, and validates actions taken under previous ordinances.

It defines the Board's constitution, including members from universities, government departments, and industry. The Board is empowered to recognize institutes for diploma training, conduct examinations, and make rules and regulations. It also outlines the structure of committees, financial management through an auditor, and provisions for officers and legal protection.

metadata.summary: The Punjab Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education Act, 1976 was enacted to reconstitute and establish Boards for Intermediate and Secondary Education in the Punjab. It defines the constitution, jurisdiction, and powers of these Boards, as well as their officers and committees. The Act also outlines procedures for recognizing schools, auditing accounts, and managing funds.

The legislation also defines various offences ranging from mutiny to desertion and outlines the jurisdiction of courts and appeal processes.

metadata.summary: This Act provides for the establishment and regulation of Borstal Institutions within the Punjab province. It outlines the powers of courts to sentence adolescent convicts to detention instead of transportation or rigorous imprisonment, and establishes the roles of a Director and Superintendents. The legislation details procedures for licensing inmates, their release on security, and the specific industrial training and moral influences intended for their reformation.

name: PUNJAB BUS STANDS AND TRAFFIC CONTROL (GUJRANWALA) ORDINANCE, 1963 (XX OF 1963) (REPEAL) ACT 2011

The Center functions as a body corporate with powers to conduct research, develop policies, provide training, and coordinate with international entities to combat extremism. It is funded through government grants, donations, and other sources, with accounts audited annually by the Auditor General of Pakistan.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Charities Act, 2018

It establishes a Charity Commission consisting of Commissioners appointed by the Government to oversee these functions. The Act defines various terms related to charities, trustees, and fund collectors, while also outlining procedures for registration, auditing, and penalties for misapplication of funds.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Child Marriage Restraint Act, 2026

The legislation empowers Courts to issue injunctions against impending marriages and mandates that proceedings prioritize the safety, education, and welfare of the child over customary practices.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Civil Administration Act, 2017

The legislation also creates mechanisms for district accounts, grievance redress through Divisional Boards, and ensures transparency in public office.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962

The document also provides for the preparation of holiday lists, the use of court seals, and the power to frame rules by the High Court with Government approval.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Civil Servants Act, 1974

The Act also provides for the creation of rules by the Governor to carry out its purposes and repeals a previous Ordinance from 1974.

name: PUNJAB CIVILIAN VICTIMS OF TERRORISM (RELIEF AND REHABILITATION) ACT 2016

The legislation defines specific categories of harm, such as death or grievous injury, and sets corresponding grant amounts payable to victims and their families.

name: PUNJAB CO-OPERATIVE SOCIETIES AND CO-OPERATIVE BANKS (REPAYMENT OF LOANS) ORDINANCE, 1966

name: PUNJAB COMMISSION ON THE STATUS OF WOMEN ACT 2014

metadata.summary: This Act establishes community safety measures for buildings and health/fitness centers in the Punjab province. The legislation empowers the Punjab Emergency Service to inspect facilities, issue notices for non-compliance, impose administrative penalties up to one hundred thousand rupees for repeated violations, and seal buildings if necessary.

name: PUNJAB COMPULSORY TEACHING OF THE HOLY QURAN ACT 2018
