metadata.summary: This Act makes the teaching of the Holy Quran compulsory for Muslim students in all educational institutions within the Province of Punjab. It mandates Naazrah Quran (recitation by sight) for levels I to V and translation of the entire Holy Quran for levels VI to XII. The Government of the Punjab is responsible for ensuring implementation through prescribed rules made under this Act.

name: PUNJAB CONFERMENT OF PROPRIETARY RIGHTS ON NON-PROPRIETORS IN ABADI DEH ACT, 1995

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Conferment of Proprietary Rights on Non-proprietors in Abadi Deh Act, 1995
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the conferment of proprietary rights on non-proprietors in the abadi deh.
repeals: The Punjab Conferment of Proprietary Rights on Non-Proprietors in Abadi Deh Ordinance, 1994 (XV of 1994)
metadata.one_line: This Act confers proprietary rights on non-proprietors in abadi deh land within the Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Act provides for the conferment of proprietary rights on non-proprietors residing in the abadi deh of villages in the Punjab. It vests all rights, title, and interest in land under a house owned by a non-proprietor directly into that person free of charge upon the Act's commencement. The legislation establishes mechanisms for resolving disputes through the Collector and allows appeals to the Commissioner within thirty days.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Consolidation of Holdings (Repeal) Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the Punjab Consolidation of Holdings Ordinance, 1960.
repeals: The Punjab Consolidation of Holdings Ordinance, 1960
establishes: Board of Revenue (power to issue instructions)
metadata.one_line: Repeals the Punjab Consolidation of Holdings Ordinance, 1960 and outlines transition for pending consolidation schemes.
metadata.summary: This Act repeals the Punjab Consolidation of Holdings Ordinance, 1960 to facilitate the implementation of land consolidation schemes. It mandates that confirmed schemes be implemented within 365 days by the Collector, while incomplete schemes are transferred to district Collectors under the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967. The Board of Revenue is empowered to issue guidelines and establish digital systems to carry out the Act's purposes.

metadata.short_title: The Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Order to revise, amend and consolidate the law of evidence so as to bring it in conformity with the injunctions of Islam as laid down in the Holy Quran.
repeals: The Evidence Act, 1872
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and revises the law of evidence in Pakistan to conform with Islamic injunctions.
metadata.summary: This Order consolidates and revises the law of evidence applicable in Pakistan. It brings the legal provisions into conformity with the injunctions of Islam as laid down in the Holy Quran. The document repeals the Evidence Act, 1872, and covers topics such as witnesses, admissions, documents, presumptions, and judgments.

metadata.short_title: The Qarshi University, Muridke Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Qarshi University, Muridke.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Qarshi University, Muridke as a private sector body corporate with perpetual succession.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the establishment of the Qarshi University, Muridke in the private sector. It defines the university's structure, including the Chancellor, Board of Governors, and Academic Council, and outlines its functions such as providing instruction, conducting examinations, and awarding degrees. The Act also establishes committees for finance, planning, and selection of staff to manage the university's affairs.

metadata.short_title: The Race Courses Licensing (Repeal) Ordinance, 1985
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal the Race Courses Licensing Act, 1912
repeals: The Race Courses Licensing Act, 1912
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance repeals the Race Courses Licensing Act, 1912 in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Governor of the Punjab promulgated this Ordinance to repeal the Race Courses Licensing Act, 1912. It was issued pursuant to specific Proclamations and Orders regarding the continuance of laws in force. The Ordinance came into force immediately upon its publication.

metadata.short_title: The Rashid Latif Khan University Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Rashid Latif Khan University in Private Sector and to provide for matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto.
metadata.one_line: Establishes Rashid Latif Khan University in the private sector in Lahore with powers to confer degrees and manage faculties.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Rashid Latif Khan University as a body corporate in the private sector located in Lahore. It defines the university's functions, including providing instructions in various sciences and deciding teaching methods. The Act sets up governing bodies such as the Board of Governors, Academic Council, and Selection Board to manage the institution's affairs, appointments, and budget.

metadata.short_title: The Ravi Urban Development Authority Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Ravi Urban Development Authority.
metadata.territorial_extent: such areas as the Government may, in the official Gazette, from time to time notify
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Ravi Urban Development Authority for planning, development, and water rehabilitation in specified areas.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Ravi Urban Development Authority to implement a comprehensive system of planning and development. It aims to improve the quality of life, rehabilitate the Ravi River aquifer, and provide modern civic facilities. The Authority is empowered to levy fees, acquire land, manage infrastructure, and enforce regulations regarding pollution control and beautification within its notified area.

metadata.short_title: The Rawalpindi Medical University Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Rawalpindi Medical University.
repeals: The Rawalpindi Medical University Ordinance, 2017 (V of 2017)
metadata.one_line: Establishes Rawalpindi Medical University to upgrade medical education and research in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act reconstitutes Rawalpindi Medical College as Rawalpindi Medical University to provide better medical education and encourage research. It establishes the university as a body corporate with perpetual succession, defining its functions, structure, and governing bodies like the Syndicate and Academic Council. The Act also sets up financial provisions including a University Fund and outlines mechanisms for appeals and indemnity.

metadata.short_title: The Rawalpindi Women University, Rawalpindi Act 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Rawalpindi Women University, Rawalpindi and for the matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto.
repeals: The Rawalpindi Women University, Rawalpindi Ordinance 2019 (IX of 2019)
metadata.one_line: Establishes Rawalpindi Women University, Rawalpindi and defines its structure, officers, and functions.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Rawalpindi Women University, Rawalpindi as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It outlines the university's incorporation, jurisdiction, fee structures, and the roles of its various authorities including the Syndicate, Academic Council, and Chancellor. The legislation also provides for the transfer of properties and liabilities from the former Government Postgraduate College for Women to the new university.

metadata.short_title: The Reformatory Schools Act, 1897
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law relating to Reformatory Schools and to make further provision for dealing with youthful offenders.
repeals: Section 399 of Act X of 1882
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes Reformatory Schools for youthful offenders under fifteen and outlines their management, inspection, and legal procedures.
metadata.summary: The Reformatory Schools Act, 1897 amends the law regarding institutions for youthful offenders convicted of offences punishable by imprisonment or transportation. It empowers the Provincial Government to establish and maintain these schools, prescribe rules for their operation, and direct courts to send suitable offenders there instead of prison. The Act details the requisites for such schools, including industrial training and sanitary arrangements, while also defining the roles of Superintendents, Committees of Visitors, and Boards of Management in overseeing the welfare and education of inmates.

metadata.short_title: The Registration Act, 1908
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the enactments relating to the Registration of Documents.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan (adapted from India)
repeals: THE SCHEDULE
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine which may extend to five hundred thousand rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws regarding the registration of documents, wills, and fees in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates enactments relating to the registration of documents. It establishes the hierarchy of registering officers, including Inspectors General, Registrars, and Sub-Registrars, and defines their duties and powers. The legislation covers compulsory and optional registration, procedures for presenting documents, fees, penalties for fraud or false statements, and provisions for electronic record systems.

metadata.short_title: The Registration of Foreigners Act, 1939
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the Registration of Foreigners in [Pakistan].
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees or with both (if foreigner); fine which may extend to five hundred rupees (if not a foreigner)
metadata.one_line: Provides for the registration of foreigners entering, present in, or departing from Pakistan and sets penalties for non-compliance.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a legal framework for registering foreigners who enter, reside in, or leave Pakistan. It empowers the Federal Government to make rules requiring foreigners to report their presence, movement, and departure details to prescribed authorities. The Act also defines 'foreigners' as persons not citizens of Pakistan, places the burden of proving non-foreigner status on the individual, and prescribes penalties for contravening these rules.

name: REGULATION OF GENERATION, TRANSMISSION AND DISTRIBUTION OF ELECTRIC POWER ACT, 1997

metadata.short_title: The Regulation of Generation, Transmission and Distribution of Electric Power Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the regulation of generation transmission and distribution of electric power
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority to regulate generation, transmission, and distribution of electric power in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Regulation of Generation, Transmission and Distribution of Electric Power Act, 1997 was enacted to provide a legal framework for regulating the generation, transmission, and distribution of electric power. It establishes the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (NEPRA) as the body empowered to grant licenses, determine tariffs, and oversee industry standards. The Act applies to the whole of Pakistan and came into force immediately upon enactment in December 1997.

name: REGULATION OF MINES AND OIL-FIELDS AND MINERAL DEVELOPMENT [(GOVERNMENT CONTROL)] ACT, 1948

metadata.short_title: The Regulation of Mines and Oil fields and Mineral Development (Government Control) Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provision for certain matters connected with the regulation of mines and oil-fields and minerals developments under government control.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates mines, oil-fields, and mineral development under government control in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the regulation of mines, oil-fields, and mineral developments under government control. It empowers the appropriate Government to make rules regarding licensing, royalties, production control, and pricing. The Act also establishes penalties for breaches of these rules and allows for exemptions from specific provisions.

metadata.short_title: The Repealing (Punjab Loans Limitation) Act, 1923
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the Punjab Loans Limitation Act, 1904.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Provincial Government may, by notification, appoint in this behalf
repeals: The Punjab Loans Limitation Act, 1904
metadata.one_line: This Act repeals the Punjab Loans Limitation Act, 1904 and revives the Limitation Act, 1908 for suits in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Repealing (Punjab Loans Limitation) Act, 1923 was enacted to repeal the Punjab Loans Limitation Act, 1904. It extends to the Province of Punjab and comes into force on a date appointed by the Provincial Government via notification. The Act revives the provisions of the Limitation Act, 1908 for suits previously governed by the repealed 1904 Act, while saving pending suits and existing causes of action from immediate dismissal based on limitation bars.

metadata.short_title: The Restriction of Habitual Offenders (Punjab) Act, 1918
metadata.long_title: An Act for restricting the movements of habitual offenders in the Punjab and for requiring them to report themselves.
metadata.max_penalty: three years imprisonment
metadata.one_line: This Act restricts the movements of habitual offenders in Punjab and requires them to report themselves.
metadata.summary: The Restriction of Habitual Offenders (Punjab) Act, 1918 was enacted to regulate the movements of habitual offenders within the province of Punjab. It empowers Magistrates to pass orders restricting an offender's movements to a specific area, requiring them to report at designated times and places, or both. The Act outlines the procedure for making such orders, including joint proceedings with bonds for good behavior, and specifies penalties for violating these restrictions, which can include imprisonment up to three years.

metadata.short_title: The Revenue Recovery Act, 1890
metadata.long_title: An Act to make better provision for recovering certain public demands.
metadata.one_line: This Act provides mechanisms for Collectors to recover public demands and land revenue arrears from defaulters.
metadata.summary: The Revenue Recovery Act, 1890 establishes procedures for the recovery of certain public demands, specifically focusing on land revenue arrears. It empowers Collectors to issue certificates to other district Collectors regarding defaulters who have property in different districts, allowing for cross-district recovery proceedings. The Act defines key terms such as 'Collector' and 'defaulter', outlines the process for instituting civil suits by persons denying liability, and includes provisions for the sale of a defaulter's immoveable property. It also saves local laws relating to revenue from being impaired by its provisions.

metadata.short_title: Revolution University, Faisalabad Act 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Revolution University, Faisalabad.
metadata.one_line: Establishes Revolution University, Faisalabad in the private sector and defines its structure and functions.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes Revolution University, Faisalabad as a body corporate in the private sector with its campus located in Faisalabad. It outlines the university's composition, including a Chancellor, Board of Governors, Vice-Chancellor, and various academic authorities. The legislation grants the university powers to provide instruction, conduct research, hold examinations, and award degrees across diverse fields such as Islamic Studies, Science, Technology, and Management.

metadata.short_title: The Road Transport Workers Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate the hours of work and other conditions of employment of road transport workers in Pakistan
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan (adapted for the Province of Punjab)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to six months and fine not exceeding ten thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Regulates working hours, rest, and employment conditions for road transport workers in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the hours of work and other employment conditions for road transport workers in Pakistan. It defines key terms such as 'worker', 'employer', and 'vehicle', and sets age limits for drivers and general employees. The law mandates specific rest intervals, weekly rest days, and leave entitlements while establishing penalties for contravention.

metadata.short_title: The Sahara University Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Sahara University in the private sector and to provide for matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto
establishes: Board of Advanced Studies and Research (BASR)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the private Sahara University in Narowal with full academic autonomy under the Punjab Assembly.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sahara University as a body corporate in the private sector located at Narowal. It grants the university academic, financial, and administrative autonomy while defining its structure, including the Board of Governors, Executive Board, and Academic Council. The legislation outlines the composition and functions of various committees responsible for finance, research, and faculty management.

metadata.short_title: The Salar International University Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Salar International University.
metadata.one_line: Establishes Salar International University in the private sector with campuses in Sheikhupura and defines its structure.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Salar International University as a body corporate in the private sector located in Sheikhupura. It outlines the university's functions, including providing instruction across various faculties like Management Sciences, Social Sciences, Law, and Medicine. The legislation also defines the composition and powers of key authorities such as the Board of Governors, Academic Council, and Selection Board.

metadata.short_title: Sale of Goods Act, 1930
metadata.long_title: An Act to define and amend the law relating to the sale of goods
repeals: Act of 1872
metadata.one_line: Defines and amends the law relating to the sale of goods in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act defines and amends the legal framework governing the sale of goods. It applies to the whole of Pakistan and came into force on July 1, 1930. The legislation covers contract formation, property transfer, risk allocation, implied conditions, and remedies for breach of warranty or condition.

metadata.short_title: The Sasti Roti Authority Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Sasti Roti Authority in the Punjab.
metadata.administering_body: Industries, Commerce, Investment and Skill Department
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sasti Roti Authority in Punjab to provide and distribute subsidized tandoori roti.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sasti Roti Authority in the Province of Punjab for the provision and distribution of subsidized tandoori roti to deserving people. The Authority is a body corporate with powers to regulate manufacture, storage, transport, and pricing of sasti roti, as well as to issue licenses and permits. It functions under the supervision of the Government of the Punjab and must submit annual reports to the Provincial Assembly.

metadata.short_title: The Seed Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for controlling and regulating the quality of seeds of various varieties of crops and for matters connected therewith
establishes: Federal Seed Certification and Registration Department
metadata.administering_body: Federal Seed Certification and Registration Department
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the quality of seeds, establishes councils for certification, and sets rules for seed dealers and testing labs.
metadata.summary: The Seed Act, 1976 provides a legal framework to control and regulate the quality of seeds of various crop varieties across Pakistan. It establishes bodies such as the National Seed Council, Provincial Seed Councils, and the Federal Seed Certification and Registration Department to oversee seed certification and registration. The Act defines key terms like 'certified seed' and 'basic seed', regulates the sale of seeds, mandates the registration of growers and dealers, and outlines offences and penalties for non-compliance.

metadata.short_title: The Senate Hill University Act, 2024
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Senate Hill University.
metadata.one_line: Establishes Senate Hill University in the private sector in Punjab with defined governance and academic structures.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Senate Hill University as a body corporate in the private sector located in Lahore. It defines the university's structure, including the Chancellor, Board of Governors, Academic Council, and various faculties. The legislation outlines the university's functions such as providing instruction, conducting research, and managing finances through specific committees.

metadata.short_title: The Settlement Commissioners (Validation of Orders) (Repeal) Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the Settlement Commissioners (Validation of Orders) Act, 1972.
repeals: The Settlement Commissioners (Validation of Orders) Act, 1972
metadata.one_line: Repeals the Settlement Commissioners (Validation of Orders) Act, 1972.
metadata.summary: This Act serves to repeal the Settlement Commissioners (Validation of Orders) Act, 1972. It ensures that any actions or orders previously made under the repealed Act are deemed to have been taken under this new legislation. The law was enacted by the Provincial Assembly of Punjab on June 22, 2012.

metadata.short_title: The Settlement Commissioners (Validation of Orders) Act, 1972
metadata.status_evidence: Repealed by the Settlement Commissioners (Validation of Orders) (Repeal) Act1, 2012
metadata.repealed_by: The Settlement Commissioners (Validation of Orders) (Repeal) Act, 2012
metadata.one_line: An Act to validate orders of Settlement Commissioners in Punjab, later repealed in 2012.
metadata.summary: This Act was enacted to validate specific orders issued by Settlement Commissioners. It applies to the Province of Punjab and was promulgated as Act VI of 1972. The entire legislation has since been repealed by a subsequent Act passed in 2012.

metadata.short_title: The Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the control of Sikh Gurdwaras and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Provincial Government may by notification appoint
repeals: The Sikh Gurdwaras and Shrines Act, 1922
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes a Board and Judicial Commission to control Sikh Gurdwaras in Punjab and provides for dispute resolution.
metadata.summary: The Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925 provides for the control of Sikh Gurdwaras within the Punjab province. It establishes a Board and a Judicial Commission to manage these institutions and resolve disputes regarding their status and property. The Act outlines procedures for petitions concerning gurdwara claims, compensation for hereditary office-holders, and the constitution of management committees.

metadata.short_title: The Societies Registration Act, 1860
metadata.long_title: An Act for the Registration of Literary, Scientific and Charitable Societies.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan (except Scheduled Districts)
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the registration, management, and legal standing of literary, scientific, charitable societies and Deeni Madrassahs.
metadata.summary: The Societies Registration Act, 1860 establishes a legal framework for forming societies through a memorandum of association by seven or more persons. It outlines requirements for registration fees, annual filing of managing body lists, and the vesting of society property in the governing body. The Act also defines the capacity of societies to sue and be sued, procedures for superseding governing bodies, and specific registration mandates for Deeni Madrassahs.

name: SOUTH PUNJAB INSTITUTE OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY DERA GHAZI KHAN ACT 2021

metadata.short_title: The South Punjab Institute of Science and Technology Dera Ghazi Khan Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of South Punjab Institute of Science and Technology Dera Ghazi Khan.
establishes: South Punjab Institute of Science and Technology Dera Ghazi Khan
metadata.one_line: Establishes the South Punjab Institute of Science and Technology Dera Ghazi Khan as a private sector body corporate.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the South Punjab Institute of Science and Technology Dera Ghazi Khan in the private sector within the Province of Punjab. It defines the Institute's functions, including providing instruction in sciences and social sciences, conducting examinations, and awarding degrees. The legislation creates a corporate body with perpetual succession, establishing key governing bodies such as the Board of Directors, Academic Council, and Finance and Planning Committee to manage its affairs.

metadata.short_title: The Specific Relief Act, 1877
metadata.long_title: An Act to define and amend the law relating to certain kinds of Specific Relief.
repeals: enactments repealed by section 2 (specific names not listed in text)
metadata.one_line: Defines and amends the law relating to specific relief obtainable in civil suits including injunctions and specific performance.
metadata.summary: This Act defines and amends the law regarding specific relief in civil suits. It covers recovering possession of property, enforcing contracts through specific performance or damages, rectifying instruments, rescinding contracts, cancelling instruments, granting declaratory decrees, appointing receivers, and issuing injunctions. The Act applies to the whole of Pakistan and came into force on May 1, 1877.

metadata.short_title: The Sports (Development and Control) Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate the development and control of Sports
establishes: Board for the control of Sports in Pakistan
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates the development and control of sports in Pakistan by establishing a Board.
metadata.summary: The Sports (Development and Control) Ordinance, 1962 was promulgated by the President to regulate sports in Pakistan. It establishes a Board with perpetual succession to promote uniform standards of competition comparable to international levels. The Central Government has the power to constitute one or more Boards and determine their name, constitution, powers, and functions. Additionally, the Ordinance grants the Board the exclusive right to make rules for the development and control of sports throughout Pakistan.

name: STAGE CARRIAGES (CANCELLATION OF PERMITS OF ABSENTEES) REGULATION, 1969

metadata.short_title: The Stage Carriages (Cancellation of Permits of Absentees) Regulation, 1969
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or fine or both
metadata.one_line: Regulation cancelling permits of absentee stage carriage owners and requiring surrender of cancelled permits.
metadata.summary: This Martial Law Regulation applies to the whole of Pakistan and cancels permits issued to absentees holding stage carriages. It defines 'absentee' and 'actual owner' for the purpose of determining ownership, which is not conclusive based on registration certificates alone. Cancelled permits must be surrendered within 15 days, and plying a carriage or retaining a permit after cancellation attracts rigorous imprisonment up to three years or a fine.

metadata.short_title: The Stage-Carrriages Act, 1861
metadata.long_title: An Act for licensing and regulating Stage-Carriages
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan; but it shall not apply to carriages ordinarily plying for hire within the limits of any municipality or cantonment or other place in which any law for the regulation of carriages is for the time being in force
repeals: Section 19
metadata.max_penalty: fine not exceeding five hundred rupees or imprisonment if distress not sufficient (Section 18)
metadata.one_line: An Act for licensing and regulating stage-carriages, defining offences and penalties related to their operation.
metadata.summary: This Act provides a legal framework for licensing and regulating stage-carriages used to convey passengers for hire. It defines what constitutes a stage-carriage, outlines the requirements for obtaining a license from a Magistrate, and specifies the details that must be painted on the vehicle. The legislation establishes various penalties for offenses such as operating unlicensed carriages, carrying excess passengers, ill-treating animals, or failing to comply with license conditions. It also grants the Provincial Government the power to make rules regarding license forms, inspection procedures, and stage regulations.

metadata.short_title: The Stage-Carrriages Act, 1861
metadata.long_title: An Act for licensing and regulating Stage-Carriages
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan; but it shall not apply to carriages ordinarily plying for hire within the limits of any municipality or cantonment or other place in which any law for the regulation of carriages is for the time being in force
repeals: Section 19
metadata.max_penalty: fine not exceeding five hundred rupees or imprisonment if distress not sufficient (Section 18)
metadata.one_line: An Act for licensing and regulating stage-carriages, defining offenses and penalties related to their operation.
metadata.summary: This Act provides a framework for licensing and regulating stage-carriages used to convey passengers for hire. It defines what constitutes a stage-carriage, outlines the requirements for obtaining a license from a Magistrate, and specifies the details that must be painted on the carriage. The Act establishes various penalties for offenses such as operating unlicensed carriages, carrying excess passengers, ill-treating animals, or failing to comply with license conditions. It also grants the Provincial Government power to make rules regarding licenses, inspection, and stage regulations.

metadata.short_title: The Stamp Act, 1899
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Stamps.
repeals: Schedule II
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends the law relating to stamp duties on instruments within Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law regarding stamp duties applicable to various instruments in Pakistan. It outlines who is liable for duty, how stamps must be used (adhesive or impressed), and the methods for valuing subject matter for duty purposes. The Act also details procedures for adjudication on unstamped instruments, penalties for non-compliance, and provisions for allowances and refunds.

metadata.short_title: The Sugar Factories Control Act, 1950
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the regulated supply of sugarcane to the sugar factories.
metadata.administering_body: Food Safety and Consumer Protection Department
metadata.one_line: Regulates the supply of sugarcane to sugar factories in Punjab, including pricing, reserved areas, and licensing.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the supply of sugarcane intended for use in sugar factories within the Province of Punjab. It establishes a Sugarcane Control Board to oversee operations and defines specific terms such as 'Cane-grower' and 'Reserved area'. The legislation empowers the Provincial Government to fix minimum prices, declare reserved areas for cane purchase, and license purchasing agents to ensure an orderly supply chain.

metadata.short_title: The Suits Valuation Act, 1887
metadata.long_title: An Act to prescribe the mode of valuing certain suits for the purpose of determining the jurisdiction of Courts with respect thereto.
metadata.commencement: on such dates as the Provincial Government directs (Part I) and on the first day of July, 1887 (Parts II and III)
repeals: section 14 of the Madras Civil Courts Act, 1873
metadata.one_line: Prescribes the mode of valuing certain suits to determine court jurisdiction, particularly regarding land.
metadata.summary: This Act prescribes the method for valuing specific suits to determine the jurisdiction of courts. It empowers the Provincial Government to make rules determining the value of land for jurisdictional purposes and ensures that the relief sought in land-related suits does not exceed the determined land value. The Act applies to both suits relating to land and other suits, with provisions for High Court determination of values where necessary.

metadata.short_title: The Superior University, Lahore, Act, 2004
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the [Superior University], Lahore.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Superior University, Lahore as a private sector body corporate with perpetual succession.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Superior University, Lahore as a private sector institution located in Lahore. It creates a body corporate with perpetual succession to manage faculties, conduct examinations, and award degrees across various disciplines including sciences, engineering, and medical fields. The university is governed by a Board of Governors advised by a Patron, with functions delegated to committees and an Academic Council for academic matters.

metadata.short_title: The Surrender of Illicit Arms Act, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the surrender of illicit arms and improvement and control of the law and order situation
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, on recommendation of the respective Provincial Government, by notification in the official Gazette appoint
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for life and forfeiture of property
metadata.one_line: Provides a legal framework for the surrender of illicit arms to improve law and order in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a mechanism for persons possessing illicit arms to surrender them within a specified timeframe to designated authorities. It defines 'illicit arms' broadly to include various types of firearms, explosives, and containers holding harmful substances. The legislation mandates publicity campaigns, sets out punishments for failure to surrender or present licenses, and provides for the confiscation of seized items.

metadata.short_title: The Suthra Punjab Authority Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Suthra Punjab Authority for management of solid waste, regulation of sanitation services, development of an integrated system for collection, transportation, treatment and safe disposal of waste, promotion of recycling and waste-to-energy initiatives, improvement of rural sanitation and hygiene, protection of public health, to provide every person clean, healthy and sustainable environment and the matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto.
repeals: The Suthra Punjab Authority Ordinance, 2025
metadata.max_penalty: Imprisonment up to two years and fine up to five hundred thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Suthra Punjab Authority to manage solid waste and regulate sanitation services in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Suthra Punjab Authority and its Agency to manage solid waste, regulate sanitation, and promote recycling and waste-to-energy initiatives. It defines the composition of the Authority, including government secretaries and technical experts, and outlines their powers and functions. The Act also sets out offences related to waste disposal and pollution, prescribing fines and imprisonment as penalties.

name: THAL (INCREASE IN VALUE) (VALIDATION OF LEVY OF TAX) ORDINANCE, 1971

metadata.short_title: The Thal (Increase in Value) (Validation of Levy of Tax) Ordinance, 1971
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to validate the levy, charging, collection and realization of the tax under the Punjab Thal (Increase in Value) Act, 1940.
metadata.one_line: Validates the levy and collection of Thal tax under the Punjab Thal Act, 1940.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance validates the levy, charging, collection, and realization of tax under the Punjab Thal (Increase in Value) Act, 1940. It applies to taxes levied in accordance with specific rules before their substitution by a later notification. The law applies specifically to persons subject to Mitakshara law within the Punjab, excluding special customs or wills.

metadata.one_line: Enables executors and administrators to sue or be sued for wrongs committed within one year before a person's death.
metadata.summary: This Act allows executors, administrators, or representatives of deceased persons to maintain actions for pecuniary losses caused by wrongs committed during the deceased's lifetime. It permits such actions if the wrong occurred within one year before death and ensures that recovered damages become part of the personal estate. The Act also prevents suits from abating due to the death of either party, allowing proceedings to continue against or by representatives while permitting a defense based on lack of assets.

key_definitions: Treasure: anything of any value hidden in the soil, or in anything affixed thereto
Collector: (1) an Revenue-officer in independent charge of a district, and (2) any officer appointed by the Provincial Government to perform the functions of a Collector under this Act

Owner: When any person is entitled, under any reservations in an instrument of transfer of any land or thing affixed thereto, to treasure in such land or thing, he shall, for the purposes of this Act, be deemed to be the owner of such land or thing

It also prescribes penalties for failing to give notice or abetting offenses.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated to consolidate and amend the law relating to the consolidation of holdings in the Province of Punjab. It defines key terms such as 'estate', 'Collector', and 'Consolidation Officer' and outlines the procedure for applications, scheme preparation, and confirmation by the Board of Revenue. The document establishes mechanisms for transferring rights, paying compensation, and handling disputes while barring civil court jurisdiction over matters arising under it.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Consumer Protection Act, 2005
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for protection and promotion of the rights and interests of the consumers.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to two years or with fine which may extend to hundred thousand rupees or with both
metadata.administering_body: Industries, Commerce, Investment and Skill Department
metadata.one_line: This Act protects consumer rights regarding defective products and services in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Consumer Protection Act, 2005 establishes a legal framework to protect the rights and interests of consumers within the Province of Punjab. It defines liabilities arising from defective products and faulty services, prohibiting unfair practices such as false representations and bait advertisements. The Act empowers an Authority and Consumer Courts to investigate complaints, order remedies, and impose penalties on manufacturers or service providers who infringe upon consumer rights.

name: PUNJAB CONTROL OF GOONDAS (REMOVAL OF DOUBTS) ORDINANCE, 1972

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Control of Goondas (Removal of Doubts) Ordinance, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to remove certain doubts in regard to the number of Tribunals which can be constituted in every district, under the provisions of the West Pakistan Control of Goondas Ordinance, 1959
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
amends: West Pakistan Control of Goondas Ordinance, 1959
metadata.one_line: Clarifies that 'a Tribunal' under the 1959 Ordinance means one or more Tribunals per district.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab to resolve legal doubts regarding the number of Tribunals that could be constituted in a district. It interprets the term 'a Tribunal' in the West Pakistan Control of Goondas Ordinance, 1959 to mean one or more than one Tribunal. The law applies to the entire Province of Punjab and came into force immediately upon promulgation.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Control of Goondas Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to consolidate and amend the law relating to the control of disorderly persons commonly known as goondas in the Province of [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except the Tribal Areas.
repeals: The Punjab Control of Goondas Act, 1951
The Sind Control of Goondas Act, 1952
The Karachi Control of Disorderly Persons Act, 1952
The Sind Acts Extension to Khairpur District Ordinance, 1959
metadata.max_penalty: Two years' rigorous imprisonment and whipping
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates laws to control disorderly persons (goondas) in Punjab via a Tribunal system.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of West Pakistan to consolidate and amend laws regarding disorderly persons known as goondas in the Province of Punjab. It establishes Tribunals consisting of District Magistrates or empowered Magistrates to conduct inquiries, declare individuals as goondas, and impose special orders such as detention, bond execution, and movement restrictions. The Ordinance outlines specific procedures for summoning witnesses, handling absconders, and appeals against Tribunal orders, while prescribing enhanced punishments under the Pakistan Penal Code for various offences.

name: PUNJAB CONTROL OF NARCOTIC SUBSTANCES ACT 2025

metadata.short_title: Punjab Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for control of narcotic substances, controlled substances and the production, processing, trafficking and transportation of such drugs and substances and the prevention of illicit narcotics related activities.
repeals: Control of Narcotics Substance Act, 1997 (Act No. XXV of 1997)
establishes: Provincial Fund for control of drug abuse
metadata.one_line: An Act to control narcotic substances, prevent illicit activities, establish special courts and create a counter-narcotics force in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the control of narcotic and controlled substances, including their production, processing, trafficking, and transportation. It establishes Special Courts with exclusive jurisdiction over offences under this Act and creates the Punjab Counter Narcotics Force to assist in enforcement. The Act also empowers the Government to amend schedules listing controlled substances and chemicals, and includes provisions for the freezing, tracing, and forfeiture of assets derived from narcotics activities.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Copying Fees Act, 1936
metadata.long_title: An Act to facilitate the recovery of fees payable for copies made or supplied of records in offices under the control of Revenue, Judicial and other officers of Government.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Provincial Government may by notification appoint
metadata.one_line: Facilitates recovery of fees for copies of government records in Punjab as land revenue arrears.
metadata.summary: This Act facilitates the recovery of fees payable for copies made or supplied of records kept in offices under the control of Revenue, Judicial and other officers of Government in the Punjab. It allows unpaid fees to be recovered from applicants as if they were arrear of land revenue, with a proviso exempting pleaders who present applications on behalf of clients. The Act defines 'record' broadly to include documents, plans, maps, or papers attached to any suit, appeal, enquiry, trial, or other proceeding.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Corporation Employees (Special Powers) Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to invest the Governor with certain powers in respect of persons in Corporation service.
metadata.one_line: Invests the Governor of Punjab with powers to remove or revert certain corporation employees without notice.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance empowers the Governor of the Punjab to remove or revert specific persons in Corporation Service appointed between January 1, 1972 and July 5, 1977. It applies to corporate bodies established by the Government of the Punjab and excludes those on deputation from other governments. Affected employees have the right to make a representation or petition for review within fifteen days. Those removed are deemed civil servants for the purposes of the Punjab Service Tribunals Act, 1974.

name: PUNJAB COTTON CONTROL (VALIDATION OF LEVY OF FEES) ORDINANCE, 1971

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Cotton Control (Validation of Levy of Fees) Ordinance, 1971
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to validate the levy, charging, collection and realization of fees from the occupiers of cotton factories run by diesel.
repeals: West Punjab Cotton (Control) Act, 1949
Bahawalpur Cotton (Control) Act, 1949
key_definitions: occupiers of cotton ginning factories run by diesel
metadata.one_line: Validates the levy and collection of fees from occupiers of diesel-run cotton ginning factories in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance validates the levy, charging, collection, and realization of fees imposed on occupiers of cotton ginning factories run by diesel. It applies to fees levied under the West Punjab Cotton (Control) Act, 1949 and the Bahawalpur Cotton (Control) Act, 1949 prior to their amendment in 1961. The Ordinance deems these fees validly collected even if there were omissions or contrary provisions in earlier laws or court orders.

name: PUNJAB COTTON CONTROL (VALIDATION OF TRANSPORTATION FEE) ACT, 1974

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Cotton Control (Validation of Transportation Fee) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to validate the levy, charging, collection and realisation of transportation fee under the West Punjab Cotton (Control) Act, 1949, and the Bahawalpur Cotton (Control) Act, 1949.
repeals: West Punjab Cotton (Control) Act, 1949
Bahawalpur Cotton (Control) Act, 1949
metadata.one_line: Validates the levy and collection of transportation fees under specific 1949 cotton control acts repealed by this Act.
metadata.summary: This Act validates the levy, charging, collection, and realization of transportation fees imposed under the West Punjab Cotton (Control) Act, 1949, and the Bahawalpur Cotton (Control) Act, 1949. It deems these fees validly levied despite any contrary provisions or court orders in those repealed Acts. The Act extends to the whole of the Punjab and provides for the recovery of unpaid fees according to the Punjab Cotton Control Ordinance, 1966.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Cotton Control Ordinance, 1966
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to control over the production, processing and sale of cotton, and other matters incidental thereto.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except the Tribal Areas
repeals: The West Punjab Cotton Control Act, 1949 (IV of 1949)
the Bahawalpur Cotton Control Act, 1949
the Cotton Act, 1952 (Khairpur Act V of 1952)
the Sind Cotton Control Act, 1954 (I of 1954)
metadata.max_penalty: six months imprisonment and fine up to fifteen thousand rupees
metadata.administering_body: Government of Punjab (via Director General of Agriculture, Executive District Officer Agriculture, etc.)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates laws controlling cotton production, processing, and sale in Punjab through licensing and quality standards.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Cotton Control Ordinance, 1966 was promulgated to amend and consolidate laws regarding the control of cotton production, processing, and sale. It establishes a Cotton Control Board and Advisory Committees to oversee these activities. The Ordinance regulates factory licenses, mandates maintenance of registers, prohibits adulteration, and sets standards for cotton bales and pricing.

name: PUNJAB COUNCIL OF THE ARTS ACT, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Council of the Arts, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Council of the Arts.
repeals: Punjab Ordinance No. II of 1975
metadata.administering_body: Department of Information, Culture and Tourism, Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Council of the Arts to promote arts and culture in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Council of the Arts as a body corporate for the patronage and development of arts and culture. It creates a Board of Governors and an Executive Committee to manage the Council's affairs, funds, and activities. The Act also grants powers to take over other cultural bodies and make necessary rules and regulations.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Court Fees (Abolition) Ordinance, 1983
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the abolition of court fee in respect of certain cases.
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on and from the first of August, 1978
metadata.one_line: Abolishes court fees for criminal cases and civil cases involving claims up to twenty-five thousand rupees.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance abolishes the requirement to pay court fees in specific legal proceedings within Punjab. It applies to all criminal cases and civil cases where the subject-matter value or relief claimed does not exceed twenty-five thousand rupees. The abolition covers all stages of the case and includes revenue courts, overriding previous laws like the Court Fees Act, 1870.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Court of Wards Act, 1903
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to the Court of Wards in the Punjab.
repeals: XXVI of 1854
IV of 1872
XII of 1887
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates and amends the law relating to the Court of Wards in the Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Court of Wards Act, 1903 consolidates and amends laws regarding the Court of Wards within the Punjab province. It establishes the constitution, jurisdiction, and powers of the Court of Wards to assume superintendence over the properties and persons of wards (minors). The Act outlines procedures for inquiries, vesting of property, management by guardians or managers, liquidation of liabilities, and the release of wards from wardship.

name: PUNJAB CRIMINAL PROSECUTION SERVICE (CONSTITUTION, FUNCTIONS AND POWERS) ACT 2006

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Criminal Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions and Powers) Act 2006
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish a Criminal Prosecution Service in the Punjab.
metadata.one_line: Establishes an independent Criminal Prosecution Service in Punjab to ensure prosecutorial independence and better coordination.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Criminal Prosecution Service to prosecute criminal cases independently and efficiently within the Province. It defines the constitution, administration, and powers of various prosecutors, including the Prosecutor General. The legislation also outlines the duties of police towards prosecutors, the establishment of a process serving agency, and provisions for rules, indemnity, and overriding other laws.

name: PUNJAB CRIMINAL PROSECUTION SERVICE INSPECTORATE ACT 2018

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Criminal Prosecution Service Inspectorate Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to introduce an effective system of monitoring and inspection of the Punjab Criminal Prosecution Service.
metadata.one_line: Establishes an Inspectorate to monitor and inspect the Punjab Criminal Prosecution Service.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Criminal Prosecution Service Inspectorate to monitor, inspect, and advise on the performance of the prosecution service. It defines the composition of the Inspectorate, including a Director General and Inspectors, and grants powers to summon records from various government agencies. The Inspectorate is required to submit annual reports to the Government and the Provincial Assembly.

name: PUNJAB CURRICULUM AND TEXTBOOK BOARD ACT 2015

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Curriculum and Textbook Board Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Curriculum and Textbook Board.
repeals: The Punjab textbook Board Ordinance, 1962 (XLI of 1962)
the West Pakistan Publication of Books Regulation and Control Ordinance, 1969 (XV of 1969)
the West Pakistan Textbook (Regulation and Control), Ordinance, 1970 (XXVII of 1970)
the Punjab Curriculum Authority Act, 2012 (XXXXIX of 2012)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Curriculum and Textbook Board to formulate curricula, approve textbooks, and conduct educational research in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Curriculum and Textbook Board as a body corporate to manage curriculum formulation, textbook development, and related educational research. The Board consists of ex-officio members representing various government departments and nominated academicians, professionals, and teachers. It has the power to frame regulations, make rules, and produce reference materials while being subject to annual audits by the Auditor General of Pakistan.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Daanish Schools and Centers of Excellence Authority Act 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment and management of the Daanish Schools and Centers of Excellence in the Punjab.
repeals: The Punjab Education Authority Ordinance 1999 (LII of 1999)
establishes: Punjab Daanish Schools and Centers of Excellence Authority
metadata.one_line: Establishes and regulates the management of Daanish Schools and Centers of Excellence in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Daanish Schools and Centers of Excellence Authority to manage schools providing quality education to underprivileged segments of society. The Authority is a body corporate consisting of government officials, assembly members, and a Managing Director, with powers to set curricula, award scholarships, and supervise school discipline. It also provides for financial management, audits, and the dissolution of existing societies related to these schools.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Debtors' Protection Act, 1936
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the more effective protection of debtors in the Punjab.
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the effective protection of debtors in Punjab regarding money-lenders and execution of decrees.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Debtors' Protection Act, 1936 was enacted to modify existing laws and provide better protection for debtors within the province. It specifically addresses issues related to money-lenders and regulates the execution of decrees for the payment of money. The Act defines key terms such as banks, companies, and loans, while establishing exemptions for certain types of property like ancestral land and standing crops from attachment or sale.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Defamation Act, 2024
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provisions in respect of defamation and for matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto.
repeals: Defamation Ordinance, 2002
metadata.one_line: Establishes a Tribunal to handle defamation claims via summary procedure, allowing for damages and account blocking.
metadata.summary: This Act provides specific provisions for handling defamation cases within the Province of Punjab. It establishes a specialized Tribunal to adjudicate claims arising from defamatory statements made through various media, including social media platforms. The Act outlines procedures for filing claims, granting preliminary decrees, and imposing penalties such as damages and mandatory apologies. Additionally, it empowers the Tribunal to direct regulatory authorities to suspend or block social media accounts of defendants found liable.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Departmental Inquiries (Powers) Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to confer powers for compelling attendance of witnesses and production of documents on officers conducting departmental inquiries against Government servants in the Province of Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Punjab, except the Tribal Areas
repeals: The West Pakistan Departmental Inquiries (Powers) Ordinance, 1958
metadata.max_penalty: same penalties to which he would have been liable if he had disobeyed a process issued by the civil court
metadata.one_line: Confers powers on officers to compel witness attendance and document production during departmental inquiries in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act grants specific powers to officers conducting departmental inquiries against government servants in the Province of Punjab. It allows these officers to summon witnesses and compel the production of documents with the same authority as a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. The Act also establishes penalties for anyone who disobeys such processes and repeals the earlier West Pakistan Departmental Inquiries (Powers) Ordinance, 1958.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Essential Articles (Control) Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for regulation of supply, distribution, prices and trade and commerce in respect of certain essential articles.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
repeals: The Punjab Essential Article (Control) Ordinance, 1973
metadata.one_line: Regulates supply, distribution, prices and trade of essential articles in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act provides powers to regulate and control the production, acquisition, prices, storage, movement, supply, distribution, disposal, use or consumption of certain essential articles in the Province of the Punjab. It authorizes the Government to issue notified orders for licensing, fixing prices, prohibiting withholding from sale, and requiring record-keeping for specified items like cement, tea, and fertilizers. The Act also establishes a Controller of Prices and Supplies to exercise these control functions and includes provisions for punishment for contravention.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Fertilizers (Control) Order, 1973
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
metadata.parent_law: Section 3 of the Punjab Essential Articles (Control) Ordinance, 1973
metadata.one_line: An Order by the Governor of Punjab to control fertilizers, fix prices, regulate dealers, and prevent adulteration.
metadata.summary: This Order empowers the Controller to regulate the sale, storage, and movement of fertilizers within the Province of Punjab. It establishes mechanisms for fixing maximum prices, licensing dealers, and requiring importers and producers to submit detailed information regarding consignments and production costs. The document also mandates strict labeling requirements, limits on stock quantities, and provisions for sampling and testing to prevent the sale of adulterated products.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Fertilizers Control Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for regulation and control of fertilizer in the Punjab.
repeals: The Punjab Fertilizers (Control) Order, 1973 (VII of 1973)
Clause (j) of sub-section (2) of section 3 and entry No. 40 of the Schedule to the Punjab Essential Articles (Control) Act, 1973 (XVII of 1973)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months and with fine which may extend to two million rupees but not less than one million rupees
metadata.administering_body: Agriculture Department of the Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates and controls the manufacture, supply, importation, distribution, sale, and quality standards of fertilizers in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Fertilizers Control Act, 2025 establishes a regulatory framework for fertilizers within the province to ensure quality and availability for agriculture. It creates specific roles such as Controllers and Licensing Committees to oversee manufacturing, importing, distribution, and dealership. The Act mandates strict licensing, pricing controls, labeling requirements, and disposal procedures for expired or adulterated products, with severe penalties for violations.

name: PUNJAB INSTITUTE OF TEXTILE TECHNOLOGY CESS ACT 1962

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Institute of Textile Technology Cess Act, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the raising of funds for the establishment and maintenance of the Pakistan Institute of Textile Technology, Lyallpur.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the province of [the Punjab], except the Tribal Areas
metadata.administering_body: Provincial Government of the Punjab (via the Director)
metadata.one_line: This Act levies a cess on textile mills in Punjab to fund the establishment and maintenance of the Pakistan Institute of Textile Technology.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Institute of Textile Technology Cess Act, 1962 provides for the levy of a cess on spindles and power-looms installed in textile mills within the province of Punjab. The funds collected are intended to support the establishment and maintenance of the Pakistan Institute of Textile Technology, Lyallpur (now Faisalabad). The Act establishes a Textile Institutes Fund managed by a Board of Trustees appointed under a Trust Deed, with the Provincial Government overseeing assessment, collection, and expenditure procedures.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Registration of Godowns Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the registration of godowns in the Punjab.
repeals: The Punjab Registration of Godowns Ordinance, 2014 (VIII of 2014)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to three years or fine up to three hundred thousand rupees or both
metadata.administering_body: Food Safety and Consumer Protection Department
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes a registration system for godowns in Punjab to ensure the stable supply of essential articles.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Registration of Godowns Act, 2014 provides for the mandatory registration of godowns used to store essential articles within the province. It empowers the Registering Authority to inspect records and seize goods if provisions are violated or information is incorrect. The Act outlines penalties for contravention, including imprisonment or fines, and establishes an appeal mechanism to the Secretary of the Administrative Department.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Rice (Restrictions on Cultivation) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate the cultivation of rice in the Province of [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except the Tribal Areas.
metadata.max_penalty: fine extending to ten times the land revenue assessment chargeable for the crop or simple imprisonment not exceeding six months or both
metadata.one_line: Regulates rice cultivation in Punjab to prevent water-logging and salinity damage.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the cultivation of rice in the Province of Punjab to check water-logging, salinity, and seepage. It empowers the Board of Revenue to prohibit or restrict rice cultivation in specified areas while allowing cultivators to gather standing crops before restrictions take effect. The Board may also relax these restrictions for land reclamation purposes. Contravention attracts penalties including fines up to ten times the land revenue assessment or imprisonment up to six months.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Seed Corporation Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Seed Corporation.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
establishes: Board of the Punjab Seed Corporation
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Seed Corporation for seed production, procurement, processing, marketing and distribution in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Seed Corporation as a body corporate to handle the production, procurement, processing, marketing, and distribution of seeds within the Province of Punjab. The Corporation is managed by a Board comprising government officials, private sector experts, farmers, and scientists, with powers to borrow money and maintain accounts under commercial procedures. It outlines the financial structure, including sources of funds, budgeting, auditing requirements, and mechanisms for recovering dues through arbitration or land revenue arrears.

name: PUNJAB SEEDS AND FRUIT PLANTS ORDINANCE, 1965

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Seeds and Fruit Plants Ordinance, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for better production and distribution of seeds and fruit plants of high quality in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab, except the Tribal Areas
metadata.commencement: at once for sections 1 and 2; remaining provisions on such dates as Government may notify
metadata.max_penalty: fine not exceeding one thousand rupees; further fine of fifty rupees per day for continued offence
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates the production, certification, and distribution of high-quality seeds and fruit plants in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Seeds and Fruit Plants Ordinance, 1965 was promulgated to ensure better production and distribution of high-quality seeds and fruit plants in the Province of the Punjab. It establishes a system for registering growers, certifying seeds and plants, and setting quality standards for local areas. The competent authority is empowered to inspect crops, seize substandard materials, and impose penalties on unregistered commercial growers or those violating quality norms.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Silkworms (Regulation and Control) Ordinance, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and regulate the production, supply, possession and rearing of silkworms.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates the production, supply, possession and rearing of silkworms in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab to control and regulate the production, supply, possession, and rearing of silkworms. It applies to the whole of the Punjab and comes into force immediately. The law prohibits unauthorized production or possession, allows the government to supply silkworms under specific terms, grants officers powers to enter premises and seize silkworms, and prescribes penalties for contraventions.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Soil Reclamation Act, 1952
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the speedy reclamation and improvement of the areas damaged by Thur and Sem, for preventing further damage and for maximizing agricultural production.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Punjab except the Tribal Areas
establishes: Punjab Land and Water Development Board
metadata.administering_body: Punjab Land and Water Development Board
metadata.one_line: Establishes a board to reclaim land damaged by salt efflorescence in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the speedy reclamation and improvement of areas in Punjab damaged by Thur and Sem. It establishes the Punjab Land and Water Development Board as a body corporate with powers to acquire land, levy fees, and manage funds. The Act outlines procedures for framing schemes, controlling underground water, and includes provisions for compensation if acquisition is delayed.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Tobacco Vend Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to the regulation of retail sale of manufactured tobacco in urban areas in the interest of public health on a uniform basis in the Province of [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except the Tribal Areas.
repeals: The Bombay (District) Tobacco Act, 1933
The Punjab Tobacco Vend Fees Act, 1934
The North-West Frontier Province Tobacco Vend Fees Act, 1938
The Baluchistan Tobacco Vend Fees Regulation, 1942
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to one hundred rupees
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws regulating the retail sale of manufactured tobacco in urban areas of Punjab via licensing.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates legislation regarding the regulation of retail sales of manufactured tobacco in urban areas of Punjab to protect public health. It establishes a licensing system where dealers must obtain a licence from the Collector to sell or keep tobacco for retail sale. The Act defines key terms such as 'manufactured tobacco' and 'urban area', outlines penalties for unlicensed dealing, and grants powers to officers for inspection and investigation.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Vegetable Market (Lahore) Ordinance, 1963
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of a whole-sale vegetable market at Lahore and to validate actions taken under the Martial Law Order No. 121 issued by the Martial Law Administrator, Zone 'B' and the West Pakistan Ordinance No. XXI of 1962.
metadata.territorial_extent: the municipal limits of the Lahore Corporation
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on and from the 27th April, 1962
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: Establishes a wholesale vegetable market in Lahore and validates prior actions taken under martial law.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the establishment of a wholesale vegetable market at Lahore. It validates actions previously taken under Martial Law Order No. 121 and West Pakistan Ordinance No. XXI of 1962 regarding land acquisition and market setup. The document empowers the Commissioner and Lahore Improvement Trust to acquire land, allot sites to dealers, and prohibit vegetable trade outside the designated market.

name: PUNJAB HOLY QURAN (PRINTING AND RECORDING) ACT 2011

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Holy Quran (Printing and Recording) Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to ensure publication of the text of the Holy Quran free from errors of printing and recording and proper disposal of damaged or shaheed copies of the Holy Quran.
repeals: The Publication of Holy Quran (Elimination of Printing and Recording Errors) Act 1973
key_definitions: damaged or shaheed copy of the Holy Quran
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the printing and recording of the Holy Quran in Punjab to prevent errors and manage damaged copies.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Holy Quran (Printing and Recording) Act, 2011 was enacted to ensure the publication of the Holy Quran free from printing and recording errors. It establishes the Punjab Quran Board to authenticate standard copies and supervise error-free production. The Act regulates publishers and recording companies, restricts certain translation practices, and mandates the proper disposal of damaged or sub-standard copies.

name: PUNJAB INSTITUTE OF QURA’N AND SEERAT STUDIES ACT 2014

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Institute of Qura'n and Seerat Studies Act 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish Punjab Institute of Qura'n and Seerat Studies.
establishes: Punjab Institute of Qura'n and Seerat Studies
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Institute of Qura'n and Seerat Studies for research, education, and publications on the Quran and Seerat.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Institute of Qura'n and Seerat Studies in Lahore to conduct research, publish reports, and impart higher education in Islamic fields. The Institute is a body corporate with perpetual succession, managed by a Board of Directors comprising government officials, assembly members, and scholars. It functions through an Academic Council to regulate academic life and maintains a specific fund for its operations.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Waqf Properties Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the proper management and administration of Waqf Properties in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.commencement: on such date as may be notified by the Government in the official Gazette
repeals: Auqaf (Federal Control) Act, 1976
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to rupees twenty five million
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance provides for the management, administration, and regulation of Waqf properties in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Waqf Properties Ordinance, 1979 establishes a framework for the proper management and administration of Waqf properties within the Province of the Punjab. It creates specific roles such as the Chief Administrator, Administrators, and Managers to oversee these properties, regulate leases, and manage income derived from them. The document also outlines powers regarding eviction of wrongfully possessing persons, recovery of rents as land revenue arrears, and the framing of rules to carry out its provisions.

name: PUNJAB DEVELOPMENT OF DAMAGED AREAS ACT, 1952

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Development of Damaged Areas Act, 1952
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the development of damaged areas in the Punjab.
metadata.commencement: immediately after the expiry of the Punjab Development of Damaged Areas Ordinance, 1948 in areas where it was operative; on such date as the Government of the Punjab may specify by notification in other areas
repeals: Punjab Development of Damaged Areas Ordinance, 1948
establishes: Tribunal constituted under the Punjab Town Improvement Act, 1922
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment which may extend to two years or with fine which may extend to Rs. 1,000 or with both
metadata.one_line: Provides for the development of damaged areas in the Punjab through schemes framed by Improvement Trusts.
metadata.summary: This Act provides a legal framework for developing damaged areas within the Punjab province. It empowers Improvement Trusts to frame and execute schemes involving land acquisition, demolition of unfit buildings, and infrastructure improvements like street laying and drainage. The Act establishes a Tribunal to resolve disputes regarding title and compensation calculations, ensuring that affected persons receive fair treatment while facilitating urban redevelopment.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Districts (Reconstitution) Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for alteration of limits of districts and constitution of new districts in the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab, except the Tribal Areas
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance alters district limits and constitutes new districts in Punjab, adapting existing laws accordingly.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the alteration of district limits and the constitution of new districts within the Province of Punjab. It grants the Provincial Government power to alter these limits or create new districts via notification from an appointed date. The document outlines how existing laws apply to newly added areas, ensuring continuity until altered by competent authority, and mandates adaptations where references to specific districts (like Shahpur) are construed as references to new ones (like Sargodha).

name: PUNJAB ENFORCEMENT OF WOMEN'S PROPERTY RIGHTS ACT 2021

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Enforcement of Women's Property Rights Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to protect and secure the rights of ownership of women in the property.
repeals: The Punjab Enforcement of Women's Property Rights Ordinance, 2021 (IX of 2021)
establishes: Ombudsperson (under section 7 of the Protection against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010)
metadata.one_line: This Act protects women's property rights by empowering an Ombudsperson to restore possession and ownership.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Enforcement of Women's Property Rights Act, 2021 is designed to protect and secure the ownership and possession rights of women in property. It establishes a mechanism where women deprived of their property can file complaints with an Ombudsperson for summary enquiry and orders to restore title or possession. The Act empowers the Ombudsperson to direct state functionaries to execute these orders, compensate women for lost rent, and refer complex cases to civil courts, while repealing the previous 2021 Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to levy tax and alter the rate of taxes and duties in the Punjab.
metadata.one_line: This Act levies taxes in the Punjab and amends various revenue, banking, and sales tax laws.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Finance Act, 2010 is an Act to levy tax and alter the rates of taxes and duties in the Punjab. It comes into force on July 1, 2010, and extends to the whole of the Punjab. The Act amends several existing laws including the Stamp Act, 1899, the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967, the Bank of Punjab Act, 1989, the Punjab Sales Tax Ordinance, 2000, and the Punjab Finance Act, 2008. Specifically, it substitutes sections regarding the valuation of immovable property for stamp duty, fixes scales for mutation fees, alters the authorized capital and government shareholding in the Bank of Punjab, and updates sales tax rates and schedules for various services.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Flood Relief Cess Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the levy of flood relief cess in the province of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
repeals: The Punjab Flood Relief Cess Ordinance, 1973 (Punjab Ordinance No. VIII of 1973)
metadata.one_line: This Act levies a flood relief cess on cinema and race course tickets in Punjab for the financial year 1973-74.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Flood Relief Cess Act, 1973 provides for the levy and collection of a specific cess known as the 'Punjab Flood Relief Cess'. This tax applies to all tickets issued for admission to cinema houses and race courses within the Province of the Punjab during the financial year 1973-74. The cess is collected in the same manner as entertainment duty, subject to rules made by the Provincial Government.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Government Dues Recovery Ordinance, 1962
