metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the recovery of Government dues as arrears of land revenue in the Province of [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab] except [the Tribal Areas]
metadata.one_line: Provides for the recovery of government dues as land revenue arrears in Punjab via notification.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance facilitates the recovery of government dues that are treated as arrears of land revenue within the Province of Punjab. It empowers the Provincial Government to issue notifications declaring specific dues recoverable from defaulters under the Revenue Recoveries Act, 1890. The text also grants the Government power to make rules necessary for giving effect to the Ordinance's provisions.

name: PUNJAB GOVERNMENT LANDS (RESUMPTION OF GRANTS AND EXTINGUISHMENT OF RIGHTS) ACT, 1950

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Government Lands (Resumption of Grants and Extinguishment of Rights) Act, 1950
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for resumption of certain grants of [Government] land.
metadata.one_line: This Act empowers the Punjab Government to resume certain land grants made between 1945 and 1947 and extinguish associated rights.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the resumption of specific government land grants made in Punjab between 1945 and 1947 that were deemed contrary to public interest or policy. It authorizes the Government to order the resumption of such grants and extinguish all rights held by grantees, regardless of whether possession was taken or proprietary rights acquired. The Collector is empowered to resume possession immediately upon an order being made, with provisions for limited compensation regarding necessary buildings or trees and refunds for acquisition costs if paid prior to the order.

name: PUNJAB HINDU WOMEN'S RIGHTS TO AGRICULTURAL LAND ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Hindu Women's Rights to Agricultural Land Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to consolidate the Hindu Law governing Hindu Women's rights to agricultural land in the Province of [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except the Tribal Areas.
repeals: The North-West Frontier Province Hindu Women's Rights to Property (Extension to Agricultural Land) Act, 1942
The Hindu Women's Rights to Property (Sind Extension to Agricultural Land) Act, 1943
metadata.one_line: Consolidates Hindu law regarding widows' rights to agricultural land in Punjab and repeals specific extension acts.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance consolidates the Hindu Law governing women's rights to agricultural land within the Province of Punjab. It applies specifically when a Hindu dies intestate, granting widows shares equivalent to sons under the Dayabhag School or customary laws. The document defines limited interests known as Hindu women's estates and clarifies rules for joint family lands while repealing earlier extension acts from NWFP and Sindh.

name: PUNJAB JINNAH ABADIS FOR NON-PROPRIETORS IN RURAL AREAS ACT 1986

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Jinnah Abadis for Non-proprietors in Rural Areas Act, 1986
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend for housing facilities to non-proprietors in the rural areas of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: all rural areas in the Punjab except such rural areas as may be excluded from the operation of this Act through a notification by the Government
amends: The Punjab Housing Facilities for Non-proprietors in Rural Areas Act, 1975
repeals: The Punjab Jinnah Abadis for Non-proprietors in Rural Areas Ordinance, 1986
The Punjab Housing Facilities for Non-proprietors in Rural Areas Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Provides housing facilities and land allotment to non-proprietors in rural areas of Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for granting free land to non-proprietors residing in rural areas of Punjab for constructing houses. It establishes an Allotment Committee to recommend land allotments and grants proprietary rights after construction is completed. The Act also outlines procedures for cancelling allotments due to false information or breach of conditions, re-entry of resumed land, and the liability of acquisition.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Katchi Abadis Act, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provisions for regularisation, development and improvement of Katchi Abadis.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine which may extend to twenty thousand rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the regularization, development, and improvement of Katchi Abadis in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Katchi Abadis Act, 1992 was enacted to regularize, develop, and improve unauthorized settlements known as Katchi Abadis. It establishes a Director-General and Implementation Committees to oversee these functions and creates a dedicated fund for financial management. The Act outlines powers for land acquisition, shifting of occupants, and includes provisions for offences related to obstructing duties or contravening orders.

name: PUNJAB LAND DISPOSITIONS (SAVING OF SHAMILAT) ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Land Dispositions (Saving of Shamilat) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for a uniform interpretation of general expressions with regard to disposition of "Shamilat" lands in the Province of [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except the Tribal Areas.
repeals: The Punjab Land Dispositions (Saving of Shamilat) Act, 1951
metadata.one_line: Provides uniform interpretation for 'Shamilat' lands in Punjab and repeals the 1951 Act.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides a uniform interpretation of general expressions regarding the disposition of 'Shamilat' lands in the Province of Punjab. It defines 'Shamilat' as land described as such in the Record of Rights, regardless of possession by proprietors or others. The law stipulates that Shamilat are not included in any land disposition unless specifically mentioned as the subject matter, overriding contrary laws, usages, or customs. Additionally, it repeals the Punjab Land Dispositions (Saving of Shamilat) Act, 1951.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Land Preservation Act, 1900
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the better preservation and protection of certain portions of the territories of Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Punjab except the Tribal Areas
metadata.one_line: An Act to preserve and protect portions of Punjab territory by regulating land, streams, and prohibiting certain acts.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the better preservation and protection of specific portions of the territories of Punjab. It empowers the Provincial Government to notify areas, regulate or prohibit certain matters within those areas, and take measures regarding the beds of nalahs (streams). The Act includes provisions for inquiries into claims, awarding compensation for restricted rights, making rules for procedure, and imposing penalties for offences.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Land Records Authority Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Land Records Authority for reform and modernization of the system of land records.
repeals: The Punjab Land Records Authority Ordinance, 2016
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Land Records Authority to reform and modernize land records in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Land Records Authority to reform and modernize the system of land records, improve service delivery, and ensure tenure security. The Authority is a body corporate with powers to manage land records, frame policies, and provide efficient services to the public. It includes provisions for the establishment of Arazi Record Centres, financial management, appeals, and the transfer of assets and personnel from the Project Management Unit (PMU) to the new Authority.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Land Revenue (Abolition) Act, 1998
metadata.long_title: An Act to abolish land revenue in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from the date the Punjab Land Revenue (Abolition) Ordinance 1997 stands repealed
repeals: Punjab Land Revenue (Abolition) Ordinance, 1997
metadata.one_line: Abolishes land revenue in Punjab from Rabi 1996-97 while preserving liability for dues due before that period.
metadata.summary: This Act abolishes the charge of land revenue in the Province of Punjab starting from Rabi 1996-97. It explicitly states that no revenue shall be recovered if already assessed for that harvest, though liability for amounts due before that date remains intact under the 1967 Act. The legislation comes into force immediately upon repealing the corresponding Ordinance of 1997.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Land-Revenue in the Province of [the Punjab].
repeals: The Punjab Land-Revenue Act, 1887 (Pb. Act XVII of 1887)
The Sind Revenue Jurisdiction Act, 1876 (Sind Act X of 1876)
The Bombay Land-Revenue Code, 1879 (Bom. Act V of 1879)
The Sind Land Revenue Code, 1879 (Sind Act V of 1879)
The Sind Village Officers Act, 1881 (Sind Act IV of 1881)
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends the law relating to land-revenue assessment, collection, and records in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the laws regarding land revenue in the Province of Punjab. It establishes the framework for assessing land revenue, maintaining records of rights, appointing revenue officers, and collecting arrears through various processes including distress and sale of holdings. The Act also defines the powers and duties of village officers and outlines procedures for appeals and exemptions.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Land Utilization Authority Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of a Land Utilization Authority in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Establishes a Land Utilization Authority in Punjab to manage culturable waste land and provide credit facilities.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Punjab Land Utilization Authority to take control of culturable waste land, survey it, and prepare utilization schemes. The Authority is empowered to execute projects, monitor implementation, and motivate land owners through credit facilities. It constitutes a Board comprising government secretaries, department heads, and non-official members to manage the Authority's affairs.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Lands Improvement Tax Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the levy and collection of tax on certain lands in the Punjab
repeals: The Punjab Lands Improvement Tax Ordinance, 1975 (Punjab Ordinance No. I of 1975)
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the levy and collection of improvement tax on specific lands in the Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Lands Improvement Tax Act, 1975 establishes a tax regime for owners of lands situated in specified local areas within the Punjab. The tax is levied at a rate of Rs. 3.75 per acre per annum for a duration of 12 years and is collected in a manner prescribed by government rules. Arrears of this tax are recoverable as if they were arrears of land revenue, utilizing existing recovery mechanisms. The Act repeals the earlier Punjab Lands Improvement Tax Ordinance, 1975.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Laws Act, 1872
metadata.long_title: An Act for declaring which of certain rules, laws and regulations have the force of law in the Punjab, and for other purposes.
metadata.territorial_extent: the territories comprised in the Punjab
repeals: Regulation I of 1798
Regulation XVII of 1806
Regulation V of 1817
Regulation III of 1818
Regulation XI of 1825
Rules for the conservancy of Forests and Jungles in the Hill Districts of the Punjab Territories
metadata.max_penalty: fine
metadata.one_line: Declares which pre-1872 rules and regulations have force of law in Punjab and establishes local customs.
metadata.summary: This Act declares which specific rules, laws, and regulations made for the Punjab prior to 1872 continue to have the force of law. It establishes that decisions in certain cases regarding personal status shall follow Native law or local customs valid under justice, equity, and good conscience. The Act also empowers the Provincial Government to establish village-watchmen and municipal watchmen and makes rules for their powers, taxation, and penalties for obstruction.

name: PUNJAB LETTERS OF ADMINISTRATION AND SUCCESSION CERTIFICATES ACT 2021

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for an efficacious and speedy mechanism for issuance of Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates.
metadata.commencement: on such dates as the Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: The Punjab Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates Ordinance, 2021 (VIII of 2021)
metadata.one_line: Establishes a mechanism for issuing Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates in Punjab to curb fraud.
metadata.summary: This Act provides an efficacious and speedy mechanism for issuing Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates in the Province of Punjab. It establishes a Succession Facilitation Unit within the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) to process applications from legal heirs. The Act aims to curtail fraud and forgery by streamlining procedures, allowing NADRA or civil courts to issue certificates based on Family Registration Certificates.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Minor Canals Act, 1905
metadata.long_title: An Act to make better provision for the control and management of minor canals in certain areas of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the Divisions of Rawalpindi, Sargodha, Lahore, Multan, Quetta and Kalat except the Tribal Areas
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the control, management, construction, and regulation of minor canals in specific divisions of West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Minor Canals Act, 1905 establishes a legal framework for controlling and managing minor canals in designated areas of West Pakistan. It grants powers to the Collector and Provincial Government regarding canal construction, water supply regulation, and the levying of water-rates. The Act also outlines procedures for acquiring land, resolving disputes, removing obstructions, and imposing penalties for unauthorized activities.

name: PUNJAB MUSLIM PERSONAL LAW (SHARIAT) APPLICATION (REMOVAL OF DIFFICULTIES) ACT, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application (Removal of Difficulties) Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the removal of difficulties of the lawful heirs of last male holders in respect of the limited estates held by refugee females and to protect their rights with respect to the said property.
metadata.commencement: at once but deemed to have taken effect on and from the 15th day of March, 1948
repeals: Punjab Ordinance No. V of 1975
key_definitions: lawful heir of last male holder
metadata.one_line: Removes difficulties regarding property rights of refugee females in Punjab and repeals a 1975 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act addresses legal issues concerning property allotted to refugee females in the Punjab who were erroneously treated as full owners instead of limited owners under custom. It empowers affected persons to challenge decrees or orders treating them as full owners within one year of the Act's commencement and allows for fresh suits regarding alienation or succession. Additionally, it bars claims of adverse possession against lawful heirs of last male holders regarding such property.

name: PUNJAB MUSLIM PERSONAL LAW (SHARIAT) APPLICATION (REMOVAL OF DOUBTS) ORDINANCE, 1972

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application (Removal of Doubts) Ordinance, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make provision for removal of doubts in regard to the termination of limited estates in respect of immovable property held by Muslim females under the Customary Law.
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect from 31st day of December, 1962
amends: West Pakistan Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1962
West Pakistan Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application (Amendment) Act, 1964
metadata.one_line: Removes doubts regarding the termination of limited estates held by Muslim females under customary law in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance addresses legal uncertainties concerning the termination of limited estates held by Muslim females over immovable property under Customary Law. It declares that such limited estates are deemed terminated as of December 31, 1962, regardless of prior laws or court orders. Consequently, any inconsistent decrees, judgments, or pending proceedings are rendered void and must be decided anew based on this provision.

name: PUNJAB NATIONAL CALAMITIES (PREVENTION AND RELIEF) ACT, 1958

metadata.short_title: The Punjab National Calamities (Prevention and Relief) Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the maintenance and restoration of order in areas affected by certain calamities and for the prevention and control of and relief against such calamities.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab, except the Tribal Areas
repeals: The Punjab National Calamities (Prevention and Relief) Act, 1951
the Khairpur National Calamities (Prevention and Relief) Act, 1954
the West Pakistan National Calamities (Prevention and Relief) Ordinance, 1956
metadata.one_line: This Act empowers the government to declare calamity areas, appoint a Relief Commissioner, and requisition resources for relief in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab National Calamities (Prevention and Relief) Act, 1958 provides legal mechanisms to maintain order and provide relief during floods, famines, or other calamities. It allows the Provincial Government to declare affected areas, appoint a Relief Commissioner with specific powers, and requisition property or labor for emergency response. The Act also outlines procedures for compensation, rule-making, and revises previous provincial ordinances.

name: PUNJAB PARTITION OF IMMOVABLE PROPERTY ACT, 2012

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Partition of Immovable Property Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend and reform the law relating to partition of immovable property.
repeals: The Partition Act, 1893 (IV of 1893)
metadata.one_line: This Act amends and reforms the law regarding the partition of non-agricultural immovable property in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Partition of Immovable Property Act, 2012 amends and reforms the legal framework for partitioning jointly owned immovable property in Punjab. It applies to non-agricultural land co-owned by two or more persons and outlines procedures for filing suits, serving notices, and handling mesne profits. The Act establishes mechanisms for internal and open auctions, private settlements, and sets strict time limits for court disposal of cases.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Pre-emption (Removal of Doubts) Ordinance, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make provision for the removal of doubts in regard to the existence of right of pre-emption in respect of the sale of certain properties.
metadata.territorial_extent: the Province of Punjab (specifically Mianwali District or Khushab Tehsil of Sargodha District)
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect from the 7th January, 1972
metadata.one_line: Removes doubts regarding pre-emption rights for specific properties in Mianwali and Sargodha affected by the Chashma Barrage.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance addresses legal uncertainties concerning the right of pre-emption for the sale of specific agricultural lands and immovable properties. It applies exclusively to sales involving persons displaced from Mianwali District due to the construction of the Chashma Barrage, provided certification by the Commissioner of Sargodha Division is obtained. The legislation restores and re-decides any suits or proceedings decided under a conflicting notification issued in November 1971.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Pre-emption Act, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Act to bring in conformity with the injunctions of Islam the law relating to pre-emption.
repeals: The Punjab Pre-emption Act, 1913 (I of 1913)
The Punjab Pre-emption Ordinance, 1991 (IX of 1991)
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the right of pre-emption on immovable property in Punjab to conform with Islamic injunctions.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Pre-emption Act, 1991 re-enacts the law relating to pre-emption to align it with the injunctions of Islam found in the Holy Qur'an and Sunnah. It defines specific categories of persons entitled to pre-emption rights, such as co-owners (Shafi Sharik) and adjacent property owners (Shafi Jar), and outlines the procedures for exercising these rights during a sale of immovable property. The Act overrides other laws and repeals the previous Punjab Pre-emption Act of 1913 and an Ordinance from 1991, while applying standard civil procedure codes to its proceedings.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Privy Purses (Charged Expenditure) Ordinance, 1969
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to declare the expenditure relating to privy purses of Rulers of former States incorporated in the Province of [the Punjab] to be a charge on the Provincial Consolidated Fund.
metadata.one_line: Declares privy purse expenditure for Rulers of former States in Punjab as a charge on the Provincial Consolidated Fund.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance declares that any sums paid by the Federal Government as privy purses to Rulers of former States incorporated into the Province of Punjab are to be charged on the Provincial Consolidated Fund. It applies to payments made under agreements in force between the Federal Government and such Rulers or their successors. The expenditure is reimbursed to the Federal Government out of this specific fund, ensuring that the cost is borne by the province rather than the federal treasury.

name: PUNJAB PROHIBITION OF INTEREST ON PRIVATE LOANS ACT 2022

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Prohibition of Interest on Private Loans Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to prohibit the business and practices of private money-lending and advancing loans and transactions based on interest.
repeals: The Punjab Prohibition of Private Money Lending Act 2007 (VI of 2007)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to ten years and fine not exceeding one million rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act prohibits private money lending and interest-based transactions in Punjab, defining offences and penalties.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Prohibition of Interest on Private Loans Act, 2022 aims to ban the business of private money-lending and any transactions based on interest within the province. It defines key terms such as 'money lender', 'borrower', and 'interest' in accordance with Islamic injunctions found in the Holy Quran and Sunnah. The Act prescribes severe punishments, including imprisonment up to ten years and fines, for those who lend money on interest or abet such activities, while also providing mechanisms for borrowers to recover debts without paying interest.

name: PUNJAB PROTECTION AND RESTORATION OF TENANCY RIGHTS ACT, 1950

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Protection and Restoration of Tenancy Rights Act, 1950
metadata.long_title: An Act to protect and to restore the rights of certain tenants of land in respect of their tenancies.
metadata.territorial_extent: such areas as may be notified by the Provincial Government
metadata.commencement: on such date as may be notified by the Provincial Government
metadata.one_line: This Act protects and restores the rights of tenants in Punjab regarding their tenancies and regulates ejectment procedures.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Protection and Restoration of Tenancy Rights Act, 1950 was enacted by the Governor of the Punjab to protect and restore the rights of specific land tenants. It establishes grounds necessary for the ejectment of tenants, such as failure to pay rent or unfit use of land, and outlines the procedures for restoration of tenancies. The Act empowers Revenue Officers with jurisdiction over these matters, barring civil courts from interfering in their decisions, and allows the Provincial Government to make rules to regulate officer procedures.

name: PUNJAB PROTECTION OF OWNERSHIP OF IMMOVABLE PROPERTY ACT 2025

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Protection of Ownership of Immovable Property Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to protect lawful ownership of immovable property in the Punjab.
repeals: The Punjab Protection of Ownership of Immovable Property Ordinance, 2025
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years but not less than five years or with fine which may extend to ten million rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act protects lawful ownership of immovable property in Punjab by establishing a Tribunal and providing remedies against illegal possession.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Protection of Ownership of Immovable Property Act, 2025 is enacted to protect lawful owners from dispossession and provide effective legal remedies. It establishes the Punjab Property Tribunal and a Scrutiny Committee to resolve disputes expeditiously. The Act defines offences related to illegal possession, prescribes penalties including imprisonment up to ten years or fines up to ten million rupees, and empowers the government to make rules for its implementation.

name: PUNJAB RECOVERY OF COST (COPIES OF ESSENTIAL REVENUE RECORDS) ORDINANCE, 1963

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Recovery of Cost (Copies of Essential Revenue Records) Ordinance, 1963
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the recovery of cost incurred by Government in the preparation and supply of copies of essential revenue records to the Union Councils for public information in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab, except the Tribal Areas
metadata.one_line: Provides for the recovery of costs for supplying copies of essential revenue records to Union Councils in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes a mechanism for recovering the government costs incurred in preparing and supplying copies of essential revenue records. It mandates that these records be made available to Union Councils for public inspection during office hours. The cost is recovered from land revenue payers in proportion to their liability, with the Collector's certificate serving as conclusive proof of the amount due.

name: PUNJAB REDEMPTION AND RESTITUTION OF MORTGAGED LANDS ACT 1964

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Redemption and Restitution of Mortgaged Lands Act, 1964
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to the redemption and restitution of certain mortgages of land in the Province of [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except the Tribal Areas.
metadata.commencement: in such areas and from such dates as Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, direct.
repeals: The Redemption of Mortgages (Punjab) Act, 1913
The Redemption of Mortgages (Punjab) Act, 1913, as applicable to the former State of Bahawalpur
The North-West Frontier Province Redemption of Mortgages Act, 1935
The Punjab Restitution of Mortgaged Lands Act, 1938
The Punjab Restitution of Mortgaged Lands Act, 1938, as applicable to the former State of Bahawalpur
The North-West Frontier Province Restitution of Mortgaged Lands Act, 1950
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws regarding redemption and restitution of mortgaged lands in Punjab via Collector petitions.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the law relating to the redemption and restitution of certain mortgages of land in the Province of Punjab. It establishes a process where a mortgagor can petition the Collector for an order to redeem a mortgage by depositing the due amount, leading to the ejectment of the mortgagee if conditions are met. The Act also provides mechanisms for the restitution of possession for old usufructuary mortgages and outlines the powers of the Collector and Board of Revenue in managing these processes.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Relief of Indebtedness Act, 1934
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the Relief of Indebtedness in the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Punjab (Part I and Parts III-VIII); Part II to such areas as the Provincial Government may direct.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Provincial Government may, by notification, appoint
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to fifty rupees; further fine which may extend to ten rupees for every day after the first during which the breach continues
metadata.administering_body: Provincial Government or the Board of Revenue
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for debt relief, insolvency procedures, and the establishment of Debt Conciliation Boards in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Relief of Indebtedness Act, 1934 aims to amend laws governing relations between debtors and creditors in the Punjab. It establishes Debt Conciliation Boards to attempt amicable settlements between debtors and creditors regarding various types of debts. The Act outlines procedures for applications, verification, and adjudication on the genuineness of debts, while also addressing usurious loans, damdupat limits, and mortgage redemption.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Relief of Indebtedness Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to the relief of indebtedness in the Province of [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except the Tribal Areas.
repeals: The Punjab Relief of Indebtedness Act, 1934
The North-West Frontier Province Petty Zamindars Relief Act, 1936
The North-West Frontier Province Agriculturists Debtors' Relief Act, 1939
The Sind Agriculturists Relief Act, 1940
metadata.one_line: Amends and consolidates laws providing relief to indebted agriculturalists in Punjab by limiting interest and protecting assets.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends and consolidates the law relating to the relief of indebtedness in the Province of Punjab. It defines specific categories of debtors, such as those earning a livelihood mainly by agriculture or whose assets do not exceed five thousand rupees. The document grants courts powers to limit recoverable interest, order payment of decrees by instalments, and exempt certain properties from attachment or sale.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Requisitioned Land (Continuance) Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the continuance of certain powers in relation to requisitioned land.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Punjab, except the Tribal Areas
repeals: The West Pakistan Requisitioned Land (Continuance) Ordinance, 1958
metadata.max_penalty: Penalties under sections 176 and 177 of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860 for failure to furnish information.
metadata.one_line: Continues powers regarding requisitioned land in Punjab and provides for release, acquisition, and compensation.
metadata.summary: This Act ensures that requisitions on immovable property continue even after the expiration of the Defence of India Act, 1939. It empowers the Provincial Government to use or deal with such land, release it from requisition, acquire it through notice, and pay compensation according to the Land Acquisition Act, 1894. The legislation also outlines procedures for obtaining information regarding requisitioned land and protects officials acting in good faith under this Act.

name: PUNJAB SURVEY AND RECTANGULATION OF LANDS ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Survey and Rectangulation of Lands Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the survey and rectangulation of lands.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab, except the Tribal Areas
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Board of Revenue, Punjab may by notification direct
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: Provides for the survey and rectangulation of lands in Punjab, including cost recovery and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the survey and rectangulation of land in any area within the Province of Punjab. It empowers the Board of Revenue to direct such surveys while ensuring that owner's holdings are not reduced as far as possible. The costs of these operations are assessed and recovered from affected persons, though the Provincial Government may remit them. The Ordinance also establishes penalties for obstructing operations, grants indemnity to public servants acting in good faith, and bars civil court jurisdiction over acts done under it.

name: PUNJAB TAUNSA BARRAGE BETTERMENT TAX ORDINANCE, 1971

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Taunsa Barrage Betterment Tax Ordinance, 1971
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the levy of betterment tax on lands irrigated by the Taunsa Barrage Canals.
metadata.territorial_extent: the areas irrigated by the Taunsa Barrage Canals
metadata.commencement: on such date as Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance levies betterment tax on lands irrigated by Taunsa Barrage Canals and outlines payment, recovery, and exemptions.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Taunsa Barrage Betterment Tax Ordinance, 1971 provides for the levy of a specific tax on lands receiving irrigation from the Taunsa Barrage Canals. The tax is payable by land owners, mortgagees, or occupancy tenants depending on the nature of land rights, and can be paid in annual instalments with interest provisions for delays. The Ordinance establishes mechanisms for preparing demand statements, handling objections and appeals to the Commissioner, and empowers the Government to withhold irrigation or remit tax under certain conditions.

name: PUNJAB TENANCY (VALIDATION AND EXTENSION OF PERIOD FOR PAYMENT OF COMPENSATION) ORDINANCE, 1969

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Tenancy (Validation and Extension of Period for Payment of Compensation) Ordinance, 1969
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to validate the amendments made in the Punjab Tenancy (Amendment) Rules, 1953, in respect of extension of the period for payment of compensation by occupancy tenants and to further extend such period.
metadata.one_line: Validates amendments to tenancy rules and extends the period for occupancy tenants to pay compensation.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance validates previous amendments made to the Punjab Tenancy (Amendment) Rules, 1953, regarding the extension of the payment period for compensation. It confirms that these extensions up to June 30, 1960, were valid and deems payments made within that timeframe as legally effective. Furthermore, it extends the deadline for occupancy tenants who failed to pay compensation to acquire proprietary rights in their tenancies.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law relating to the tenancy of land in the Punjab.
metadata.commencement: on such day as the Provincial Government may, by notification, appoint
repeals: Tenancy Act, 1868
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment of either description which may extend to one year or fine or with both
metadata.one_line: Amends the law relating to tenancy of land in Punjab, defining occupancy rights, rent rules, and ejectment procedures.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the law regarding land tenancy in the Punjab province. It establishes rights for occupancy tenants, regulates rent enhancement and reduction, and defines grounds for ejectment. The legislation also covers tenant improvements, compensation mechanisms, and the jurisdiction of Revenue Courts.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Thal (Increase in Value) Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the levy of a tax on lands the value of which has been enhanced due to irrigation from the Thal Canal.
repeals: Punjab Thal (Increase in Value) Act, 1940
metadata.one_line: Levies a tax on lands in Punjab whose value increased due to Thal Canal irrigation.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the levy of a tax on lands in the Punjab whose value has risen or is likely to rise due to irrigation from the Thal Canal. The tax rate does not exceed sixty rupees per acre and is determined by the Board of Revenue. It outlines who must pay the tax, how demands are prepared, and mechanisms for recovery, including withholding irrigation until payment is made.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Trusts Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to revise and modify the law relating to trusts.
repeals: The Trusts Act, 1882 (II of 1882)
metadata.one_line: An Act to revise and modify the law relating to trusts in Punjab, repealing the Trusts Act, 1882.
metadata.summary: This Act revises and modifies the law relating to trusts within the Province of Punjab. It defines key terms such as author, trustee, and beneficiary, and outlines the creation, administration, and extinction of trusts. The legislation establishes a regulator and specific duties for trustees while repealing the Trusts Act, 1882.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Usurious Loans Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to consolidate the law relating to usurious loans in the Province of [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except the Tribal Areas.
repeals: The Usurious Loans Act, 1918
The Punjab Relief of Indebtedness Act, 1934
The Usurious Loans (North-West Frontier Province Amendment) Act, 1935
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws regarding usurious loans in Punjab, allowing courts to reopen transactions with excessive interest.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance consolidates the law relating to usurious loans in the Province of Punjab. It empowers courts to reopen transactions where interest is deemed excessive or the deal was substantially unfair, relieving debtors of liability for such amounts. The provisions apply to suits instituted after its commencement regarding loans made after March 22, 1918, and include specific rules on calculating excessive interest and assessing risk.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Highways Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to consolidate and amend the law relating to highways in the Province of [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except the Tribal Areas.
repeals: The West Punjab Highways Act, 1948
The North–West Frontier Province Ribbon Development Prevention Act, 1946
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws relating to highways, traffic regulation, and penalties in the Province of Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance consolidates and amends the law regarding highways in the Province of Punjab. It establishes Highway Authorities with powers to regulate traffic, manage encroachments, and control vehicle usage. The document also outlines procedures for temporary closures, land acquisition for improvements, and penalties for offences related to highway safety and maintenance.

name: PUNJAB TOLLS ON ROADS AND BRIDGES ORDINANCE, 1962

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Tolls on Roads and Bridges Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to the levy of tolls on public roads and bridges in the Province of [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except [the Tribal Areas]
repeals: The Tolls on Roads and Bridges Act, 1875
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance amends and consolidates laws regarding tolls on roads and bridges in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated to amend and consolidate the law relating to the levy of tolls on public roads and bridges in the Province of Punjab. It grants the Provincial Government powers to set up toll gates, lease out toll collection rights, and impose penalties for non-payment or unlawful levies. The document also repeals the Tolls on Roads and Bridges Act, 1875, while saving previous actions taken under the repealed Act.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Undesirable Cooperative Societies (Dissolution) Act, 1993
metadata.long_title: An Act to prohibit the carrying on of business as financial institutions by Cooperative Societies and to provide for matters ancillary thereto.
repeals: The Punjab Undesirable Cooperative Societies (Dissolution) Ordinance, 1993 (II of 1993)
metadata.one_line: Prohibits cooperative societies from acting as financial institutions and provides for their dissolution.
metadata.summary: This Act prohibits cooperative societies from accepting deposits or functioning as financial institutions. It establishes Cooperatives Boards to investigate, liquidate, and dissolve undesirable societies. The Act empowers these boards to recover hidden assets, cancel agreements, and manage the winding-up process of specified societies.

name: PUNJAB ELECTRICITY (EMERGENCY POWERS) (CONTROL OF SUPPLY) ACT, 1949

metadata.short_title: the Punjab Electricity (Emergency Powers) (Control of Supply) Act, 1949
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the continuance of powers to control the supply, consumption, distribution and use of, and the rates for the supply of electrical energy.
metadata.commencement: immediately on the expiry of the Punjab Electricity (Emergency Powers) Act, 1947
metadata.one_line: This Act empowers the Provincial Government to control electricity supply and consumption in Punjab during emergencies.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Electricity (Emergency Powers) (Control of Supply) Act, 1949 provides powers to the Provincial Government to control the supply, consumption, distribution, and use of electrical energy. It allows for the prohibition or restriction of supply, discontinuance of service under specific circumstances, and fixing rates for energy supply. The Act also outlines penalties for contraventions and defines terms such as 'consumer', 'energy', and 'supplier' by reference to the Electricity Act, 1910.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Electricity (Emergency Powers) Act, 1941
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the protection of the public in cases of emergency.
metadata.max_penalty: fine up to one thousand rupees or imprisonment up to six months or both
metadata.one_line: This Act empowers the Provincial Government to assume control of public electricity services during emergencies.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Electricity (Emergency Powers) Act, 1941 allows the Provincial Government to take possession and control of a public electricity service if there is a likelihood of supply failure or ownership doubt. Upon assuming control, the government manages the undertaking, transfers property, maintains employees' conditions, and keeps accounts. The Act provides for compensation for damages caused by exercising these powers and establishes penalties for non-compliance while barring civil court jurisdiction over matters handled under the Act.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Electricity Act, 1939
metadata.long_title: An Act to explain and amplify section 7 of the Electricity Act, 1910 in its application to the Punjab and to give the Punjab Government the powers of a licensee when it engages in the business of supplying electrical energy.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Electricity Act, 1910 to allow Punjab Government powers and purchase of electricity undertakings.
metadata.summary: This Act explains and amplifies section 7 of the Electricity Act, 1910 specifically for its application in the Punjab. It grants the Punjab Government the powers of a licensee when it engages in supplying electrical energy. The legislation also provides mechanisms for the government to purchase existing electricity undertakings, including notice periods and payment terms.

name: PUNJAB ENERGY EFFICIENCY AND CONSERVATION AGENCY ACT 2025

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Energy Efficiency and Conservation Agency Act 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Energy Efficiency and Conservation Agency.
subjects: National Energy Efficiency and Conservation Act, 2016
Punjab Energy Efficiency and Conservation Program
establishes: Punjab Energy Efficiency and Conservation Agency
metadata.administering_body: Energy Department of the Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Energy Efficiency and Conservation Agency as a designated agency under the NEECA Act, 2016.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Energy Efficiency and Conservation Agency (Agency) to function as a designated agency under the National Energy Efficiency and Conservation Act, 2016. The Agency is a body corporate with powers to recruit staff, appoint inspectors, frame regulations, and manage its Fund. It consists of representatives from various government departments, industry chambers, and universities, with the Secretary to the Government, Energy Department serving as Chairperson.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Power Development Board Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Power Development Board for the implementation of policies of the Government to facilitate the private investors in power sector and to harness the energy generation resources in the Province.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Power Development Board to facilitate private investment in power projects and harness energy resources.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Power Development Board as a body corporate to implement government policies in the energy sector. The Board is tasked with facilitating private investors, coordinating power generation activities, and exploring various energy sources including hydel, coal, solar, and wind. It also issues necessary permissions for water and land use and submits annual reports to the Provincial Assembly.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Environmental Protection Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the protection, conservation, rehabilitation and improvement of the environment, for the prevention and control of pollution, and promotion of sustainable development
metadata.administering_body: Environment Protection and Climate Change Department of the Government
metadata.one_line: An Act to protect the environment in Punjab, control pollution, promote sustainable development, and establish councils and tribunals.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the protection, conservation, rehabilitation, and improvement of the environment within the Punjab province. It establishes the Punjab Environmental Protection Council and the Provincial Environmental Protection Agency to regulate pollution, manage hazardous substances, and conduct environmental impact assessments. The legislation also creates Environmental Tribunals and Magistrates to adjudicate offences and appeals related to environmental violations.

name: PUNJAB PROHIBITION ON MANUFACTURE, SALE, USE AND IMPORT OF POLYTHENE BAGS (BLACK OR ANY OTHER POLYTHENE BAG BELOW FIFTEEN MICRON THICKNESS) ORDINANCE, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Prohibition on Manufacture, Sale, Use and Import of Polythene Bags (black or any other Polythene Bag below fifteen micron thickness) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to prohibit manufacture, sale, use and import of black polythene bags or any other polythene bag below fifteen micron thickness
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to Rs.50,000/- or with both
metadata.one_line: Prohibits manufacture, sale, use, and import of specific polythene bags in Punjab with penalties for violation.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance prohibits the manufacture, sale, use, and import of black polythene bags or any other polythene bag below fifteen micron thickness in the Province of Punjab. It defines key terms such as 'Factory', 'Person', and 'Polythene Bag' to clarify the scope of the ban. Violations are punishable by imprisonment up to three months, a fine up to Rs. 50,000, or both, and are triable by an Environmental Magistrate or specially empowered Judicial Magistrate.

name: PUNJAB DUTY ON EXCESSIVE WASTAGE OF SPIRITS IN DISTILLERIES (VALIDATION) ORDINANCE, 1969

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Duty on Excessive Wastage of Spirits in Distilleries (Validation) Ordinance, 1969
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to validate the levy and recovery of duty on excessive wastage of spirit in distilleries.
metadata.territorial_extent: the districts of Campbellpur, Dera Ghazi Khan, Gujranwala, Gujrat, Jhelum, Jhang, Lahore, Lyallpur, Mianwali, Multan, Muzaffargarh, Rawalpindi, Sahiwal, Sargodha, Sheikhupura and Sialkot
metadata.administering_body: Financial Commissioner, Excise Commissioner, or the Member Board of Revenue
metadata.one_line: Validates the levy and recovery of excise duty on excessive wastage of spirits in Punjab distilleries.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance validates the levy and recovery of duty on excessive wastage of spirits occurring in distilleries within specific districts of Punjab. It deems duties levied before its commencement as valid if they comply with the specified scales under the Punjab Excise Act, 1914. The duty is recoverable as excise revenue payable under the Punjab Excise Act, 1914.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Excise Act, 1914
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law in the Punjab relating to the import, export, transport, manufacture, sale and possession of intoxicating liquor and of intoxicating drugs.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Provincial Government may by notification direct
repeals: The Excise (Spirits) Act, 1863
The Indian Tariff Act, 1894
The Excise Act, 1896
The Excise (Amendment) Act, 1906
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends Punjab law regarding the import, export, manufacture, sale, and possession of intoxicating liquor.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends laws in the Punjab concerning intoxicating liquor and drugs. It covers preliminary definitions, the establishment of excise administration, controls on import/export/transport, licensing for manufacture and sale, duty levies, and powers of officers to inspect and seize goods. The Act also outlines offences, penalties, and procedures for confiscation or compounding of violations.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Act, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Act to enhance the rates of certain taxes and duties in the Province of the Punjab.
amends: The Punjab Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958 (W.P. Act No. XXXII of 1958)
West Pakistan Act No. X of 1958
repeals: Section 11 of the Punjab Finance Act, 1964 (W.P. Act XXXIV of 1964)
metadata.one_line: Enhances tax rates on professions, trades, and duties in Punjab while amending existing taxation acts.
metadata.summary: This Act enhances the rates of certain taxes and duties within the Province of the Punjab. It amends the Punjab Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958, the West Pakistan Entertainments Duty Act, 1958, and the Stamp Act, 1899 to update schedules and definitions. The legislation establishes new tax levies on persons engaged in various professions, trades, and employments within the province.

name: PUNJAB FINANCE ORDINANCE (PROVISIONS RELATING TO HOTEL TAX), 1978

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to levy and enhance the rates of certain taxes and duties, in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance levies and enhances hotel tax rates in Punjab, substituting Section 12 of the 1965 Act.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1978 was promulgated by the Governor to levy and enhance specific taxes and duties within the Province of the Punjab. It substitutes Section 12 of the Punjab Finance Act, 1965, establishing a tax on hotels payable by owners or management at a rate of eight percent of daily charges for occupied lodging units. The Ordinance defines key terms such as 'hotel', 'lodger', and 'lodging unit', while excluding charitable homes and government premises from the tax scope. It also bars suits in civil courts regarding assessments made under this law and empowers the Government to make rules for its implementation.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to levy and enhance the rates of certain taxes and duties in the Province of the Punjab.
amends: Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958
repeals: Section 13 of the Punjab Finance Act, 1964 (W.P. Act No. XXXIV of 1964)
metadata.repealed_by: Punjab Finance (Amendment) Ordinance, 1978 (XIV of 1978)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance levies and enhances taxes on hotels, vehicles, and property in Punjab while amending existing acts.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1978 was promulgated by the Governor to levy and enhance specific tax rates within the Province of the Punjab. It amends several existing Acts regarding urban immovable property tax, entertainments duty, motor vehicle taxation, and hotel taxes. The document also introduces rebates for lump-sum tax payments and establishes fee structures for driving licenses and vehicle registration.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Horse-Race Betting Tax Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to the levy of taxes on horse-race betting in [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except the Tribal Areas.
repeals: The Sind Betting Tax Act, 1938
The Punjab Horse-Race Betting Tax Act, 1950
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates laws regarding taxes on horse-race betting in Punjab, defining terms and levying totalizator and betting taxes.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Horse-Race Betting Tax Act, 1958 is a consolidation act designed to establish a uniform basis for levying taxes on horse-race betting within the Province of Punjab. It defines key terms such as 'backer', 'book-maker', and 'manager' and empowers the Government to levy totalizator tax and betting tax via notifications. The Act outlines duties for management, assessment procedures, exemptions, and penalties for non-compliance, while repealing previous enactments like the Sind Betting Tax Act, 1938 and the Punjab Horse-Race Betting Tax Act, 1950.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Option (Repeal) Ordinance, 1985
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal the Punjab Local Option Act, 1923
repeals: Punjab Local Option Act, 1923
metadata.one_line: An Ordinance promulgated by the Governor of Punjab to repeal the Punjab Local Option Act, 1923.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab on February 23, 1985. It serves to repeal the Punjab Local Option Act, 1923 (V of 1923). The action was taken in accordance with directions from the Federal Shariat Court and relevant constitutional orders.

name: PUNJAB MOTOR VEHICLE TRANSACTION LICENSEES ACT 2015

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Motor Vehicle Transaction Licensees Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to license and regulate the services of the motor vehicle transaction licensees for improved service delivery to the purchasers of motor vehicles.
metadata.max_penalty: simple imprisonment which may extend to six months or fine which may extend to forty thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: This Act licenses and regulates motor vehicle transaction licensees in Punjab to ensure proper registration and service delivery.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Motor Vehicle Transaction Licensees Act, 2015 was enacted by the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab to regulate services provided by motor vehicle dealers acting on behalf of owners for vehicle registration. It establishes a licensing authority within the Excise and Taxation Department to issue licenses subject to specific conditions and disqualifications. The Act mandates that licensees act as withholding agents for fees and taxes, maintain records, and adhere to prescribed service charge rates. It also outlines procedures for renewal, cancellation of licenses due to breaches, recovery of dues, and penalties for offenses including simple imprisonment or fines.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to imposition of tax on Motor Vehicles in [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab] except the Tribal Areas.
repeals: the Punjab Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1924
the North-West Frontier Province Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1936
the Sind Motor Vehicles Tax Act, 1939
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to one hundred rupees
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws for imposing tax on motor vehicles in Punjab, defining rates, licensing, and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the legal framework for levying taxes on motor vehicles within the Province of Punjab. It establishes quarterly tax installments based on vehicle engine capacity and defines the roles of the Government and licensing officers. The legislation outlines obligations for declarations, licensing procedures, exemptions, and specific penalties for non-compliance or unlicensed operation.

name: PUNJAB REAL ESTATE AGENTS AND MOTOR VEHICLES DEALERS (REGULATION OF BUSINESS) ORDINANCE, 1980

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Real Estate Agents and Motor Vehicles Dealers (Regulation of Business) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate the business of real estate agents and motor vehicles dealers in the Province of Punjab.
metadata.max_penalty: six months imprisonment or fine of Rs.5,000 or both
metadata.one_line: Regulates business, registration, and offences related to real estate agents and motor vehicle dealers in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the business of real estate agents and motor vehicles dealers in the Province of Punjab. It mandates registration with a designated authority, sets disqualifications for practitioners, and establishes procedures for obtaining certificates and maintaining records. The document also defines key terms, prescribes penalties for non-compliance, and outlines the appeal process against administrative orders.

name: PUNJAB URBAN IMMOVABLE PROPERTY (VALIDATION OF TAX) ACT, 1976

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Urban Immovable Property (Validation of Tax) Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to validate the levy, charging, collection and realization of property tax under the Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1940 (since repealed) and the Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958.
amends: Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1940
Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958
metadata.one_line: Validates the levy and collection of property tax under specific Punjab Acts for extended rating areas.
metadata.summary: This Act validates the levy, charging, collection, and realization of property tax under the Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1940 and the 1958 Act. It deems certain extended areas within local authority limits to have always been part of rating areas and urban areas for tax purposes. Any unpaid or refunded tax from these extended areas is deemed validly levied and recoverable under the provisions of the 1958 Act.

name: PUNJAB URBAN IMMOVABLE PROPERTY TAX ACT, 1958

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to the levy of a tax on Urban Immovable Property in the Province of [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Punjab, except the Tribal Areas
repeals: Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1948
key_definitions: members of the family of the owner
metadata.administering_body: Excise, Taxation and Narcotics Control Department
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws for levying tax on urban immovable property in Punjab, defining authorities and collection mechanisms.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the legal framework for levying taxes on urban immovable properties within the Province of Punjab. It establishes specific assessing authorities, including Collectors and Commissioners, to manage valuation, assessment, and collection processes. The legislation outlines exemptions, appeal procedures, penalties for default, and mechanisms for recovering unpaid dues from tenants.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Act, 1985
metadata.long_title: An Act to make certain provisions in relation to taxation in the Province of the Punjab
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
repeals: Gift Tax Act, 1963
metadata.one_line: Amends Punjab motor vehicle and finance acts while repealing the Federal Gift Tax Act, 1963.
metadata.summary: This Act makes specific provisions regarding taxation in the Province of the Punjab. It amends sections of the Punjab Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958, and the Punjab Finance Act, 1973 to allow for annual or lumpsum tax levies on motor vehicles. Additionally, it repeals the Federal Gift Tax Act, 1963.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Act, 1986
metadata.long_title: An Act to continue and levy certain taxes and fees in the Province of the Punjab
metadata.territorial_extent: whole of the Province of the Punjab
repeals: section 16 of Act IX of 1963
key_definitions: immovable property in an urban area
metadata.one_line: Continues and levies certain taxes and fees in Punjab while amending stamp duty rules.
metadata.summary: This Act continues and levies specific taxes and fees within the Province of the Punjab. It amends the Stamp Act, 1899 to introduce new valuation methods for urban land and adjust duty rates for conveyances and exchanges of property. Additionally, it repeals section 16 of the Punjab Finance Act, 1963.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Act, 1998
metadata.long_title: An Act to levy and enhance the rates of certain taxes, duties and fees in the Punjab.
amends: The Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958 (V of 1958)
The Punjab Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958 (XXXII of 1958)
The Punjab Real Estate Agents and Motor Vehicles Dealers (Regulation of Business) Ordinance, 1980 (VI of 1980)
key_definitions: proprietary rights transferred by Development Authority or Housing Authority
metadata.one_line: This Act levies and enhances taxes, duties, and fees in the Punjab while amending several existing provincial statutes.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Finance Act, 1998 was enacted to levy and enhance rates of certain taxes, duties, and fees within the province. It applies to the whole of the Punjab and came into force on July 1, 1998. The Act amends various existing laws including the Stamp Act, Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, and others to update tax rates, definitions, and recovery mechanisms.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Act, 1999
metadata.long_title: An Act to reduce the rates of stamp duty and revise certain taxes in the Punjab.
metadata.one_line: This Act reduces stamp duty rates and revises tax rates for companies in the Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Finance Act, 1999 was enacted to reduce the rates of stamp duty and revise certain taxes within the province of Punjab. It amends the Stamp Act, 1899 by substituting specific monetary values related to agricultural land, immovable property in urban areas, and other cases. Additionally, it revises tax rates for companies registered under the Companies Ordinance, 1984, based on their paid-up capital.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Act, 2003
metadata.long_title: An Act to enhance, reduce and rationalize certain taxes, fees and duties in the Province of the Punjab.
amends: The Punjab Entertainments Duty Act, 1958 (X of 1958)
The Punjab Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958 (XXXII of 1958)
metadata.one_line: Amends various provincial acts to enhance, reduce and rationalize taxes, fees and duties in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends several existing laws to adjust tax rates and definitions within the Province of the Punjab. It specifically targets stamp duties, entertainment duties on vehicles, motor vehicle taxation schedules, and provisions regarding import/export goods. metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to levy, enhance and rationalize certain taxes and duties in the Province of the Punjab.
amends: Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958
metadata.one_line: An Ordinance to levy, enhance and rationalize taxes in Punjab by amending four existing Acts.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab to further levy, enhance, and rationalize certain taxes and duties within the province. It achieves this objective by amending four specific acts: the Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958; the Punjab Entertainments Duty Act, 1958; the Punjab Finance Act, 1964; and the Punjab Finance Act, 1973. The amendments introduce tax relief for widows, disabled persons, and minor orphans regarding immovable property, adjust entertainment duty rates for cinema houses over a five-year period, redefine the term 'licensee' in relation to electric power generation, and update tax rates in the Sixth Schedule of the 1973 Finance Act.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to rationalize certain taxes, fees and duties in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.one_line: Rationalizes taxes, fees and duties in Punjab by amending various existing Acts.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab to rationalize certain taxes, fees, and duties within the province. It achieves this objective by amending six specific pieces of legislation, including the Stamp Act, Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, and Finance Acts from 1973 and 1977. The amendments primarily involve updating fee schedules for vehicle registration, duplicate certificates, and professional licenses, as well as adjusting tax rates for various machinery and vehicles.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1969
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to continue and levy certain taxes, cesses and surcharges in the Province of [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], excluding the Tribal Areas
metadata.commencement: on and from the first day of July, 1969
amends: section 5 of W.P. Act X of 1958
metadata.max_penalty: penalty not exceeding the amount of the tax payable
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance continues and levies specific taxes, surcharges, and stamp duties in the Province of Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1969 was promulgated to continue and levy certain taxes, cesses, and surcharges in the Province of Punjab. It imposes a surcharge on agricultural income tax in specific districts, levies cinema tax based on class, and adds surcharges on motor vehicle and railway fares. The document also amends existing Stamp Acts and regulations regarding administration bonds and adoption deeds.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1970
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to continue and levy certain taxes, cesses and surcharges in the new Province of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the new Province of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance continues and levies specific taxes, cesses, and surcharges in the new Province of Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1970 was promulgated by the Governor to continue and levy certain taxes, cesses, and surcharges in the newly formed Province of Punjab. It imposes a surcharge on agricultural income tax in specific districts, levies cinema tax based on class, adds surcharges on motor vehicle tax, and introduces a tax on railway fares and freights until June 30, 1971. The Ordinance applies existing laws for assessment and collection procedures where applicable and bars suits in civil courts regarding assessments made under it.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1971
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to continue and levy certain taxes, fees and surcharges in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab, except the Islamabad Capital Territory
amends: Bahawalpur State Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1949
West Pakistan Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958
repeals: Section 10 of the West Pakistan Finance Act, 1965 (W.P. Act I of 1965)
metadata.repealed_by: Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1980 (VIII of 1980)
metadata.max_penalty: penalty not exceeding the amount of the tax payable
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance continues and levies various taxes, fees, and surcharges in Punjab for the financial year 1971-72.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1971 was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab to continue and levy specific taxes, fees, and surcharges within the province. It imposes surcharges on agricultural income tax in certain districts, levies cinema tax based on class, and enhances motor vehicle taxes and registration fees. The document also amends existing acts regarding entertainment duty and electricity duty while repealing a specific section of the West Pakistan Finance Act, 1965.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to streamline, levy and enhance the rates of certain taxes and duties in the Province of the Punjab.
amends: Seventh Schedule of W.P. Act IX of 1963
Punjab Finance Act 1964 (W.P. Act XXXIV of 1964)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance streamlines and enhances tax rates in Punjab, amending existing finance acts and schedules.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1980 was promulgated by the Governor to streamline, levy, and enhance specific taxes and duties within the Province of the Punjab. It comes into force on July 1, 1980, and amends several existing finance acts and ordinances from 1963, 1971, 1978, and 1964 by substituting new entries in their schedules regarding vehicle registration fees and electricity duties. The Ordinance also establishes procedures for assessment and collection while barring suits in civil courts to challenge these levies.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to streamline the rates of certain taxes and duties in the Province of the Punjab
amends: The Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958 (W.P. Act No. V of 1958)
The Punjab Entertainments Duty Act, 1958 (W.P. Act X of 1958)
The Punjab Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958 (W.P. Act No. XXXII of 1958)
key_definitions: Disabled person: a person who is permanently incapacitated to earn his livelihood.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance streamlines tax rates and amends three specific Punjab Acts regarding property, entertainment, and vehicle taxes.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1981 was promulgated by the Governor to streamline various tax rates within the Province of the Punjab. It amends the Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958, to adjust tax rates for owner-occupied properties and introduce exemptions for widows, disabled persons, minors, and newly constructed residential houses. Additionally, it modifies the Punjab Entertainments Duty Act, 1958, regarding stage dramas and amends the Punjab Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958, by updating seating capacity entries in the Schedule.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Financial Advisory Services Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Punjab Financial Advisory Services.
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the Punjab Financial Advisory Services Authority to provide financial and management advisory services in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Financial Advisory Services Act, 2025 establishes a body corporate known as the Punjab Financial Advisory Services. The Authority is constituted by a Board comprising government secretaries, assembly members, private sector experts, and the Chief Executive Officer. Its primary function is to offer high-quality financial and management advisory support to various entities within the province. The Act outlines the Authority's powers, funding mechanisms, rule-making authority, and procedures for appeals and indemnity.

name: PUNJAB GENERAL PROVIDENT INVESTMENT FUND ACT 2009

metadata.short_title: The Punjab General Provident Investment Fund Act, 2009
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Punjab General Provident Investment Fund to generate revenue for the discharge of the liabilities of the General Provident Fund.
establishes: General Provident Investment Fund Management Committee
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab General Provident Investment Fund to generate revenue for the General Provident Fund liabilities.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab General Provident Investment Fund as a body corporate with perpetual succession. The fund is managed by a Management Committee which formulates investment policies and invests assets from a Reserve Fund created by the Government. The Act defines key terms such as 'family' and 'financial year', outlines the powers of the committee, and includes provisions for conflict of interest management and annual reporting to the Provincial Assembly.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Infrastructure Development Cess Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to levy and collect infrastructure development cess on transportation of goods manufactured, produced or consumed in, imported into or exported out of the Punjab.
metadata.max_penalty: ten times the cess leviable on such goods
metadata.one_line: This Act levies and collects an infrastructure development cess on goods transported in, into, or out of Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Infrastructure Development Cess Act, 2015 establishes a levy on the transportation of goods manufactured, produced, consumed, imported, or exported within the province. The collected funds are deposited into the Provincial Consolidated Fund to support infrastructure maintenance and development. The Act defines liable persons, sets payment procedures, outlines exemptions, and prescribes penalties for evasion or obstruction of officers.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Pension Fund Act, 2007
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of a Fund to generate revenue for the discharge of the pension liabilities of the Government.
metadata.territorial_extent: whole of the Province of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Establishes a pension fund for the Government of Punjab to manage and discharge its pension liabilities.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Pension Fund to generate revenue for discharging the pension liabilities of the Government. It creates a Management Committee responsible for the administration of the Fund, which includes both official members from the government and non-official members from the private sector. The Act outlines the powers and functions of the committee, rules regarding investments, conflict of interest provisions for members, and requirements for submitting annual reports to the Provincial Assembly.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Public Financial Management Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate financial affairs in the public sector and matters relating to the Provincial Consolidated Fund and Public Account of the Province.
metadata.one_line: Regulates financial affairs in the Punjab public sector, budgeting, debt management, and public investments.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates financial affairs in the public sector of the Punjab to ensure comprehensive, efficient, transparent, and sustainable management. It establishes frameworks for medium-term planning, fiscal risk management, debt limits, and public investment monitoring. The legislation also defines key terms like 'appropriation' and 'financial propriety', creates specific units such as the Public Financial Management Unit and Debt Management Unit, and mandates internal controls and financial reporting mechanisms.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Revenue Authority Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Punjab Revenue Authority.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may, by notification, specify
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Revenue Authority to reform taxation and promote fiscal compliance in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Revenue Authority as a body corporate to modernize the taxation system and assist taxpayers. It defines the composition, powers, and functions of the Authority, including its Chairperson, Secretary, and Advisory Council. The legislation also provides for the administration of various taxes, financial provisions, an appellate tribunal, and rules regarding staff and delegation of powers.

name: PUNJAB SALES TAX ON SERVICES ACT 2012

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the levy of a tax on services provided, rendered, initiated, received, originated, executed or consumed in the Punjab.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may, by a notification in the official Gazette, specify
metadata.one_line: This Act levies a tax on services provided or consumed in the Punjab and outlines registration, payment, and penalty procedures.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act, 2012 provides for the levy of tax on services provided, rendered, initiated, received, originated, executed, or consumed within the Punjab. It establishes definitions for terms like 'active taxpayer' and 'resident', outlines registration requirements, and details the calculation of tax value based on open market price. The Act also covers procedures for assessment, appeals, recovery of arrears, and penalties for non-compliance.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Secretariat Allowance (Withdrawal) Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the withdrawal of the Secretariat Allowance.
repeals: The Punjab Secretariat Allowance (Withdrawal) Ordinance, 1997 (XXXIV of 1997)
metadata.one_line: This Act withdraws the Secretariat Allowance for Punjab government employees and repeals a related Ordinance.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Secretariat Allowance (Withdrawal) Act, 1997 provides for the withdrawal of the Secretariat Allowance paid to all Secretariat employees in the Punjab Government. It declares that the previous letter providing this allowance was discriminatory and deemed never to have been issued, while ensuring that allowances already paid are not recoverable.
