The Act also repeals the Punjab Secretariat Allowance (Withdrawal) Ordinance, 1997.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Food Authority Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the safety and standards of food and for establishment of the Punjab Food Authority.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may, by notification, specify
repeals: The Punjab Pure Food Ordinance, 1960 (VII of 1960)
The Punjab Food Safety and Standards Authority Ordinance, 2011 (I of 2011)
establishes: Food Safety and Consumer Protection Department
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year but which shall not be less than six months and fine which may extend to one million rupees but which shall not be less than one hundred thousand rupees
metadata.administering_body: Food Safety and Consumer Protection Department
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Food Authority to ensure food safety, set standards, license businesses, and penalize violations.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Food Authority to protect public health by ensuring the safety and standards of food. It defines various terms related to food, consumer rights, and business operations. The Authority is empowered to issue licenses, conduct inspections, recall unsafe food, and impose penalties for offenses such as selling adulterated or substandard food.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Foodstuffs (Control) Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the continuance of powers to control the supply and distribution of, and trade and commerce in foodstuffs.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Punjab, except the Tribal Areas
repeals: The Bahawalpur Foodgrains Control Act, 1947
The Bahawalpur Control of Essential Supplies Commodities Act, 1948
The West Pakistan Foodstuffs (Control) Ordinance, 1957
metadata.one_line: This Act empowers the Punjab Government to control the supply, distribution, and trade of foodstuffs through orders, licenses, and tribunals.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Foodstuffs (Control) Act, 1958 provides the legal framework for the Provincial Government of the Punjab to regulate the supply, distribution, and movement of essential food items. It grants powers to issue orders regarding storage, transport, pricing, and licensing to ensure equitable availability at fair prices. The Act establishes tribunals for trial of offences and includes provisions for penalties, presumptions regarding official orders, and the protection of actions taken in good faith under the Act.

name: PUNJAB PRICE CONTROL OF ESSENTIAL COMMODITIES ACT 2024

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Price Control of Essential Commodities Act, 2024
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for price control of essential commodities in the Punjab.
repeals: The Punjab Price Control of Essential Commodities Ordinance 2023 (V of 2024)
metadata.administering_body: Food Safety and Consumer Protection Department
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes a Price Control Council to fix prices of essential commodities in Punjab and penalize profiteering.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Price Control of Essential Commodities Act, 2024 provides a mechanism for fixing prices of essential commodities within the province. It establishes a Price Control Council comprising various government ministers, department heads, and experts to monitor markets and issue orders. The Act defines key terms such as 'essential commodity' and 'dealer', outlines penalties for selling without permits, and repeals the previous 2023 Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Firewood and Charcoal (Restriction) Act, 1964
metadata.long_title: An Act to prohibit and regulate the burning of firewood and charcoal in factories, brick-kilns, lime-kilns and other specified places in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab, except the Tribal Areas
metadata.commencement: at once for sections 1 and 2; remaining provisions on such date as may be specified by Government
metadata.max_penalty: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to thirty days or with fine upto five hundred rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act prohibits and regulates the burning of firewood and charcoal in specified places within Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Firewood and Charcoal (Restriction) Act, 1964 was enacted to prohibit and regulate the burning of firewood and charcoal in factories, brick-kilns, lime-kilns, and other specified places in the Province of Punjab. It defines key terms such as 'factory', 'firewood', and 'Forest Officer' and outlines specific restrictions on burning, including exceptions for earthen-wares and personal use. The Act prescribes penalties for contravention, including simple imprisonment up to thirty days or a fine of up to five hundred rupees, and grants powers to Forest Officers to arrest offenders and seize firewood.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Fisheries Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to fisheries in the Province of [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except [the Tribal Areas]
repeals: The Punjab Fisheries Act, 1914
The Bahawalpur States Fisheries Act, 1951
metadata.max_penalty: fine not exceeding fifty rupees; composition up to five thousand rupees for certain offences
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates and amends the law relating to fisheries in Punjab, defining offences, licensing, and penalties.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Fisheries Ordinance, 1961 was promulgated to amend and consolidate laws regarding fisheries in the Province of Punjab. It establishes the Director General of Fisheries and defines various terms related to fish, water, and fishing equipment. The document outlines powers for issuing permits, protecting fish sanctuaries, and imposing penalties for offences such as using prohibited nets or destroying fish by poisoning.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Forest (Sale of Timber) Act, 1913
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the control of the sale of timber and the establishment of sale depots for such timber in the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: such local areas as the Provincial Government may by notification direct
metadata.commencement: on such day as the Provincial Government directs
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to six months or fine up to Rs. 500 or both
metadata.one_line: This Act controls timber sales and establishes sale depots in the Punjab, allowing rules to be made by the Provincial Government.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Forest (Sale of Timber) Act, 1913 provides for the control of timber sales and the establishment of sale depots within the Punjab. It empowers the Provincial Government to make rules regulating these activities, including defining sale depots, levying registration fees, and maintaining registers. The Act applies Chapter X of the Forest Act, 1927 to infringements of its rules and provides indemnity for public servants acting in good faith.

name: PUNJAB PLANTATION AND MAINTENANCE OF TREES ACT, 1974

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Plantation and Maintenance of Trees Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for plantation and maintenance of trees in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
metadata.max_penalty: rupee one per tree
metadata.administering_body: Forestry and Wildlife Department, Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: This Act mandates planting and maintaining three trees per acre in Punjab with penalties for non-compliance.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Plantation and Maintenance of Trees Act, 1974 was enacted to promote tree plantation and maintenance within the Province of the Punjab. It requires occupiers of land to plant and maintain three trees per acre, with provisions for the Department to plant trees if the occupier fails to comply. The Act defines key terms such as 'Department', 'Government', 'land', and 'occupier', and establishes penalties not exceeding one rupee per tree for contravention, recoverable as land revenue.

name: PUNJAB WILDLIFE (PROTECTION, PRESERVATION, CONSERVATION AND MANAGEMENT) ACT, 1974

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Wildlife (Protection, Preservation, Conservation and Management) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the protection, preservation, conservation and management of wildlife in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
repeals: Punjab Ordinance No. XX of 1973
establishes: Punjab Protected Areas and Wildlife Management Board
metadata.one_line: This Act protects, preserves, conserves and manages wildlife in Punjab through a Board, licensing, and penalties.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Wildlife (Protection, Preservation, Conservation and Management) Act, 1974 was enacted to regulate the protection and management of wildlife within the Province of the Punjab. It establishes a Board to oversee these functions and creates specific offences related to hunting, cruelty to animals, and unauthorized possession or trade of wildlife. The Act provides for the issuance of licenses, permits, and certificates, while also defining protected species in schedules and outlining penalties for violations.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Economic Research Institute Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Economic Research Institute as a statutory body.
establishes: Board of the Punjab Economic Research Institute
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Economic Research Institute as a statutory body to conduct economic research and advise government.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Punjab Economic Research Institute as a statutory body with perpetual succession. The Institute is tasked with conducting research in economics, demography, and socio-economic problems, providing advice on modern research techniques, and assisting national and international agencies. It creates a Board for administration and management, defines the roles of officers and employees as public servants, and grants powers to make rules and regulations.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Educational Institutions (Reconstitution) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to reconstitute certain educational Institutions in the Punjab.
repeals: Statutes, Regulations and Rules of the Institutions
metadata.one_line: This Act reconstitutes educational institutions in Punjab to improve governance and grant them academic, financial, and administrative autonomy.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Educational Institutions (Reconstitution) Act, 2021 was enacted by the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab to reconstitute specific educational institutions within the province. Its primary purpose is to enhance the quality of education by granting these institutions academic, financial, and administrative autonomy. The Act establishes a Board of Governors for each institution, comprising government officials, academicians, alumni, and other members, which holds management and control powers. It also creates a Management Committee and defines the roles of the President and Principal, while repealing previous statutes, regulations, and rules to facilitate this new governance structure.

name: PUNJAB GOVERNMENT EDUCATIONAL AND TRAINING INSTITUTIONS ORDINANCE, 1960

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Government Educational and Training Institutions Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish Boards of Governors for Government Educational and Training Institutions in the Punjab.
metadata.commencement: such date as may be notified by Government
metadata.one_line: Establishes Boards of Governors to manage government educational and training institutions in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes Boards of Governors for government educational and training institutions in the Punjab to ensure their efficient management and control. The Board is a body corporate with perpetual succession, empowered to acquire property, enter contracts, and manage the institution's affairs. It defines the composition of the Board, including provisions for official and non-official members, and outlines powers regarding property, funds, accounts, and personnel.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Higher Education Commission Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Punjab Higher Education Commission.
repeals: The Punjab Higher Education Commission Ordinance, 2014 (XV of 2014)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Higher Education Commission and defines its powers, composition, and functions.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Higher Education Commission to promote higher education, research, and development within the province. It defines the Commission as a body corporate with perpetual succession, appoints a Chairperson and various members including representatives from universities and industry, and outlines its administrative and financial functions. The Act also provides for the making of regulations, indemnity for officials acting in good faith, and repeals the previous Ordinance from 2014.

name: PUNJAB KINNAIRD COLLEGE FOR WOMEN, LAHORE, ORDINANCE 2002

metadata.short_title: The Kinnaird College for Women, Lahore Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to reconstitute and reorganize the Kinnaird College for Women, Lahore.
establishes: Kinnaird College for Women, Lahore (as a body corporate)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance reconstitutes and reorganizes the Kinnaird College for Women, Lahore as a body corporate.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab to reconstitute and reorganize the Kinnaird College for Women, Lahore. It establishes the College as a body corporate with perpetual succession and defines the composition and powers of its Board of Governors. The document outlines the administrative functions of the Board, the management of the College fund, and provisions for rules and regulations to govern the institution's affairs.

name: PUNJAB PRIVATE COLLEGES (MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL) ORDINANCE, 1970

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Private Colleges (Management and Control) Ordinance, 1970
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for control over and management of private colleges in [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except the Tribal Areas
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance establishes a Governing Body to manage and control private colleges in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the control and management of private colleges located in the Province of Punjab, excluding Tribal Areas. It mandates the establishment of a Governing Body for each college to streamline administration and regulate teacher service conditions. The document defines key terms such as 'Private college', 'Governing Body', and 'competent authority', and outlines the powers, duties, and composition of these bodies.

name: PUNJAB PRIVATE EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS (PROMOTION AND REGULATION) ORDINANCE, 1984

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Private Educational Institutions (Promotion and Regulation) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the promotion and regulation of private educational institutions.
repeals: The Punjab Registration of Unrecognized Educational Institutions Ordinance, 1962 (W. P. XI of 1962)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates private educational institutions in Punjab through registration, district committees, and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the promotion and regulation of privately managed educational institutions within the Province of Punjab. It mandates that all such institutions must be registered with a designated Registering Authority before commencing business. The law establishes District Committees to oversee schools and outlines procedures for inspection, cancellation of registration, appeals, and penalties for non-compliance or failure to meet prescribed conditions.

name: PUNJAB UNIVERSITIES AND BOARDS OF INTERMEDIATE AND SECONDARY EDUCATION MALPRACTICES ACT, 1950

metadata.short_title: The Universities and Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education Malpractices Act, 1950
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the eradication of malpractices in connection with examinations held by the Universities and Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab, except the Tribal Areas
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and with fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees
key_definitions: premature disclosure of a question or question paper
metadata.one_line: This Act eradicates malpractices in university and board examinations by defining offences and penalties for employees.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the eradication of malpractices connected with examinations held by Universities and Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education. It defines specific terms such as 'candidate', 'examiner', and 'answer book' to clarify the scope of offenses. The legislation establishes punishments including imprisonment up to three years and fines up to fifty thousand rupees for various acts of malpractice, while also granting privileges regarding unpublished records and official information held by employees.

name: PUNJAB UNIVERSITIES REMOVAL OF UNDESIRABLE GOVERNMENT SERVANTS ORDINANCE, 1962

metadata.short_title: The Punjab (Universities) Removal of Undesirable Government Servants Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the termination of the services of undesirable Government servants serving in Universities and other educational institutions in [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of [the Punjab] except [the Tribal Areas]
metadata.commencement: immediately after the Martial Law Order No. 124, issued by Martial Law Administrator, Zone 'B', ceases to operate
metadata.one_line: Provides for the termination of services of undesirable government servants in Punjab universities and educational institutions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance allows the Governor to terminate the services of any government servant serving in a university or other educational institution if deemed undesirable. It applies to the whole of Punjab except the Tribal Areas and comes into force once specific Martial Law orders cease. The Governor may direct payment of specified pension or Provident Fund amounts upon termination.

name: PUNJAB DESTITUTE AND NEGLECTED CHILDREN ACT 2004

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Destitute and Neglected Children Act, 2004
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law for the rescue, protective custody, care and rehabilitation of destitute and neglected children in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.commencement: at once but shall take effect in such areas and from such date as the Government may, by notification, specify
repeals: The Punjab Children Ordinance, 1983 (XXII of 1983)
The Punjab Youthful Offenders Ordinance, 1983 (XXIII of 1983)
The Punjab Supervision and Control of Children Homes Act, 1976 (XVI of 1976)
establishes: Destitute and Neglected Children's Welfare Fund
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws for rescuing, protecting, and rehabilitating destitute and neglected children in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates existing laws regarding the rescue, protective custody, care, and rehabilitation of destitute and neglected children in the Province of Punjab. It establishes a Child Protection and Welfare Bureau with a Board of Governors to manage child protection institutions and courts. The legislation defines specific offences related to children, such as unauthorized custody and employing them for begging, while repealing previous Ordinances and Acts on similar subjects.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Emergency Service Act, 2006
metadata.long_title: An Act for the establishment of the Punjab Emergency Service to deal with emergencies.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
metadata.max_penalty: simple imprisonment for six months or with fine not exceeding rupees fifty thousand or with both
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Emergency Service to handle emergencies, rescue operations, and medical treatment within Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Emergency Service to maintain preparedness for emergencies and provide timely rescue and medical treatment. It defines the powers of the Service, including coordinating with other agencies and establishing community response teams. The Act also outlines the appointment of officers, regulations for emergency vehicles, and penalties for offenses such as false calls or obstruction.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Forensic Science Agency Act, 2007
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Punjab Forensic Science Agency for forensic examination of documents, materials, equipment, impressions or other objects.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Forensic Science Agency to conduct forensic examinations and render expert opinions for courts.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Forensic Science Agency to examine forensic materials and provide expert opinions to courts, tribunals, or authorities. The Agency is headed by a Director General appointed by the Government of the Punjab and consists of experts and officials. It functions to maintain records, promote forensic awareness, and ensure the proper collection and preservation of forensic material. The Act also outlines offences for rendering false opinions and provides mechanisms for appeals and re-examination.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Forensic Science Authority Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Punjab Forensic Science Authority for forensic examination of documents, materials, equipment, impressions or other objects; for scientific opinion on different types of evidential material referred to it by the investigating agencies or any other authorized authority for forensic and tendering its expert opinion thereon and for the matters ancillary thereto and connected therewith.
repeals: The Punjab Forensic Science Agency Act, 2007 (XII of 2007)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Forensic Science Authority to provide forensic examination and expert opinions on evidential materials.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Forensic Science Authority as a body corporate to conduct forensic examinations of various materials and provide scientific opinions. The Authority consists of government secretaries, police officials, and experts in fields like audio-visual analysis, computer forensics, and molecular sciences. It empowers the Authority to absorb existing forensic facilities and employees from the Punjab Forensic Science Agency while repealing the previous 2007 Act.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab High Security Zones (Establishment) Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for declaring of high security zones and designated areas to regulate public gatherings and prohibiting of activities prejudicial to safety and security of general public in the Punjab.
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment for a term not less than one year and not more than three years and fine up to rupees five hundred thousand
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes high security zones in Punjab to regulate public gatherings and prohibit activities prejudicial to public safety.
metadata.summary: The Punjab High Security Zones (Establishment) Act, 2026 provides for the declaration of high security zones and designated areas within the province. It regulates public gatherings by requiring prior permission for events in designated areas and prohibiting all gatherings in high security zones. The Act establishes Provincial and District Intelligence Committees to recommend zone declarations and manage applications, while prescribing punishments for violations including imprisonment and fines.

name: PUNJAB INFORMATION OF TEMPORARY RESIDENTS ACT 2015

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Information of Temporary Residents Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for sharing of information of tenants and other temporary residents.
repeals: The Punjab Information of Temporary Residents Ordinance, 2015 (II of 2015)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to six months and fine between ten thousand and one hundred thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act mandates landlords and hotels to share tenant/guest information with police to combat terrorism.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Information of Temporary Residents Act, 2015 establishes a legal framework for sharing information about tenants and guests with the police. It requires property dealers, landlords, and hotel managers to report details of occupants within specific timelines using computerized national identity cards or passports. The Act aims to develop a database to prevent terrorism and other crimes while defining penalties for non-compliance.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Juvenile Smoking Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to prevention of smoking of tobacco by juveniles in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab, except the Tribal Areas
repeals: The Punjab Juvenile Smoking Act, 1918
The Punjab Juvenile Smoking Act, 1918, as applicable to the former State of Bahawalpur
The North-West Frontier Province Juvenile Smoking Act, 1933
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to six months or fine which may extend to five thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance prevents tobacco sales to juveniles in Punjab, defines offences and penalties, and repeals earlier acts.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends and consolidates laws preventing juvenile smoking in the Province of the Punjab. It prohibits selling or giving tobacco to persons under eighteen years of age and prescribes fines, licence suspension, and imprisonment for violations. The law also empowers authorities to seize tobacco smoked by juveniles in public places and requires government publicity before enforcement.

name: PUNJAB LAND PRESERVATION (EXTENSION TO DERA GHAZI KHAN EXCLUDED AREA) REGULATION, 1959

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Land Preservation (Extension to Dera Ghazi Khan Excluded Area) Regulation, 1959
metadata.long_title: A Regulation to extend the provisions of the Punjab Land Preservation Act, 1900, to the Dera Ghazi Khan Excluded Area in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the Dera Ghazi Khan Excluded Area declared to be an excluded area in the Ministry of States and Frontier Region's Notification No. D-2162-F/50, dated the 17th April, 1950.
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Land Preservation Act, 1900
metadata.one_line: Extends the Punjab Land Preservation Act, 1900 to the Dera Ghazi Khan Excluded Area in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Regulation extends the provisions of the Punjab Land Preservation Act, 1900 to the Dera Ghazi Khan Excluded Area. It was promulgated by the Governor of West Pakistan on September 12, 1959, for the purposes of peace and good government in that area. The regulation applies specifically to the territory declared as an excluded area in a 1950 notification.

name: PUNJAB MAINTENANCE OF PUBLIC ORDER ORDINANCE, 1960

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to preventive detention and control of persons and publications connected with the maintenance of public order in the Punjab.
repeals: Baluchistan Public Safety Regulation, 1947
Baluchistan States Union Public Safety Regulation
Bahawalpur State Public Security Act, 1944
North-West Frontier Province Public Safety Act, 1948
Punjab Public Safety Act, 1949
Khairpur Public Order and Detention Khairpur Act, 1954
Sind State Prisoners Regulation, 1827
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates laws regarding preventive detention and control of persons/publications to maintain public order in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends and consolidates laws concerning preventive detention and the control of persons and publications for reasons connected with public safety and order in the Punjab. It grants powers to arrest, detain, and control suspected persons, regulate publications, issue search warrants, and establish a Review Board for detention cases. The document also repeals several earlier state-level public safety acts and regulations from various provinces.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Marriage Functions Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate marriage functions and other related ceremonies.
repeals: The Marriage Functions (Prohibition of Ostentatious Displays and Wasteful Expenses) Ordinance, 2000 (II of 2000)
The Punjab Marriage Functions Ordinance, 2015 (VI of 2016)
metadata.max_penalty: simple imprisonment up to one month and fine between fifty thousand rupees and two million rupees
metadata.one_line: Regulates marriage functions in Punjab by restricting waste, fireworks, and late-night celebrations.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates marriage functions and related ceremonies within the Province of Punjab. It prohibits ostentatious displays such as street decorations, fireworks, and dowry exhibitions, while also limiting food servings to one dish per person. The legislation mandates that marriage functions conclude by 10:00 pm and establishes committees for enforcement.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Military Transport Act, 1916
metadata.long_title: An Act to make better provision for the Impressment of Animals, Vehicles, Boats and Gear in the Punjab for the purposes of Military Transport.
repeals: The Punjab Military Transport Animals Act, 1903
key_definitions: Vehicles (includes doolies, dandies, jhampans and palkies)
Collector (includes persons appointed by Federal Government or Deputy Commissioner)
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the impressment of animals and vehicles in Punjab for military transport purposes.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Military Transport Act, 1916 makes better provision for impressing animals, vehicles, boats, and gear in the Punjab for military transport. It applies to all such items whether for service within or outside Pakistan limits and covers impressment for hire or purchase. The Act empowers the Federal Government to appoint officers, make rules for enumeration, declare emergencies, fix compensation, and prescribe penalties for offences.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Prevention of Gambling Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the prevention of gambling.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
repeals: W.P. Ordinance No.I of 1961
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance prevents gambling in Punjab by defining offenses, penalties, and police powers to search and seize gaming instruments.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Prevention of Gambling Ordinance, 1978 was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab to prevent gambling activities within the province. It defines terms such as 'common gaming house' and 'gaming', which includes wagering or betting on horses or figures. The document establishes penalties for owning gaming houses, being found in them, or gaming in public and private places, with enhanced punishments for subsequent offenses. It also grants police officers powers to arrest, search, and seize instruments of gaming without a warrant in specific cases.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Prevention of Hoarding Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the prevention of hoarding in respect of certain articles.
repeals: The Punjab Prevention of Hoarding Ordinance, 2020 (VI of 2020)
metadata.max_penalty: simple imprisonment up to three years and fine equivalent to fifty percent of the value of the articles involved or fine up to rupees one million
metadata.one_line: This Act prevents hoarding of essential articles during the COVID-19 pandemic in Punjab, defining offences and penalties.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Prevention of Hoarding Act, 2020 was enacted to prevent hoarding of specific essential articles during the COVID-19 pandemic in the province of Punjab. It defines 'hoarding' as stocking excess quantities or accumulating goods without offering them for sale despite consumer demand. The Act empowers officers to search premises without a warrant, seize contraband, and auction seized items, with proceeds going to the accused if acquitted or the government exchequer if convicted.

name: PUNJAB PRIVATE SECURITY COMPANIES (REGULATION AND CONTROL) ORDINANCE, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Private Security Companies (Regulation and Control) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for regulation, licensing and control of private security companies in the Province of Punjab.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates, licenses, and controls private security companies and their employees in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Private Security Companies (Regulation and Control) Ordinance, 2002 was promulgated by the Governor to regulate and control private security companies in the Province of Punjab. It establishes a licensing system for companies wishing to engage in the business of providing security guards or arrangements for the protection of persons or property. The Ordinance defines key terms such as 'Private Security Company' and 'security guard', prohibits employees from wearing uniforms akin to armed forces, and outlines procedures for granting licenses, registration, and penalties for non-compliance.

name: PUNJAB PROBATION AND PAROLE SERVICE ACT 2019

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Probation and Parole Service Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Punjab Probation and Parole Service in the Punjab.
repeals: The Punjab Probation and Parole Service Ordinance, 2019
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Probation and Parole Service to manage offenders on probation or parole within the province.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes an effective and efficient Punjab Probation and Parole Service to assess and manage offenders released on probation or parole. It creates a structured service headed by a Director General, supported by a Board of Management and a Parole Board, to ensure better coordination in the criminal justice system. The legislation outlines the functions of officers, training requirements, reporting mechanisms, and repeals the previous Ordinance from 2019.

name: PUNJAB PROHIBITION OF SMOKING IN CINEMA HOUSES ORDINANCE, 1960

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Prohibition of Smoking in Cinema Houses Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to prohibit smoking in cinema houses in the Province of [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except the Tribal Areas.
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to one hundred rupees
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance prohibits smoking in cinema houses in Punjab and sets penalties for violations.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated to prohibit smoking in cinema houses within the Province of Punjab. It defines key terms such as 'cinema house' and 'management', and establishes penalties including fines up to one hundred rupees and arrest without warrant for offenders. The Ordinance also grants powers to the Executive District Officer to exempt specific cinema houses and allows the Government to make rules for its implementation.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Qaumi Razakars Ordinance, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to consolidate the law relating to Qaumi Razakars in the Province of [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except the Tribal Areas
repeals: the Sind Home Guards Act, 1948
the West Punjab Qaumi Razakars Act, 1949
the North-West Frontier Qaumi Razakars Act, 1952
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to fifty rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates laws regarding Qaumi Razakars in Punjab, defining their duties, powers, and repealing earlier acts.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated to consolidate existing laws relating to Qaumi Razakars in the Province of Punjab. It establishes the constitution, duties, and control mechanisms for these bodies under the Deputy Commissioner's supervision. The document also outlines penalties for neglecting duty, legal protections for members, and repeals three earlier enactments related to Home Guards and Qaumi Razakars in different regions.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Rented Premises Act, 2009
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the relationship of landlord and tenant in respect of rented premises.
repeals: The Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Ordinance, 1959 (VI of 1959)
The Punjab Rented Premises Ordinance 2007 (XXI of 2007)
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates landlord-tenant relationships in Punjab, establishes Rent Tribunals, and repeals earlier rent restriction laws.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Rented Premises Act, 2009 is enacted to regulate the relationship between landlords and tenants regarding rented premises. It mandates written tenancy agreements registered with a Rent Registrar and establishes Rent Tribunals for expeditious dispute resolution. The Act defines key terms like 'rent' and 'premises', outlines grounds for eviction, and repeals the Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Ordinance, 1959 and the Punjab Rented Premises Ordinance, 2007.

name: PUNJAB REQUISITIONING OF MOTOR VEHICLES (TEMPORARY POWERS) ORDINANCE, 1970

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Requisitioning of Motor Vehicles (Temporary Powers) Ordinance, 1970
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for requisitioning of Motor Vehicles.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance empowers District Officers to requisition motor vehicles for public purposes in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides temporary powers for the requisitioning of motor vehicles within the Punjab for any public purpose. It grants authority to District Officers (Revenue) to order the use of vehicles, conduct searches and seizures, and manage related permits and payments. The document outlines procedures for appeals to the Government of the Punjab, compensation claims, and protections against legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under this Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Safe Cities Authority Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Punjab Safe Cities Authority.
repeals: Punjab Safe Cities Authority Ordinance, 2015 (XVI of 2015)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Safe Cities Authority to manage IC3 systems for safety and security in Punjab cities.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Safe Cities Authority to construct, develop, and maintain integrated command, control, and communication (IC3) systems. The Authority is responsible for ensuring the safety and security of people in major cities of Punjab, starting with Lahore. It grants the Authority powers to manage facilities, enter contracts, and oversee infrastructure while defining its composition and functions.

name: PUNJAB SECURITY OF VULNERABLE ESTABLISHMENTS ACT 2015

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Security of Vulnerable Establishments Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for effective security arrangements of vulnerable establishments.
repeals: The Punjab Shops and Establishments (Security) Act, 1999
The Punjab Security of Vulnerable Establishments Ordinance, 2015
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to six months and fine which shall not be less than fifty thousand rupees but shall not exceed one hundred thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes security committees and procedures to protect vulnerable establishments from terrorism and crime.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Security of Vulnerable Establishments Act, 2015 provides for effective security arrangements at vulnerable establishments to prevent acts of terrorism and other crimes. It constitutes a Security Advisory Committee in each sub-division to identify, inspect, and advise managers on necessary security measures. The Act empowers the District Coordination Officer to declare establishments as vulnerable, issue advice, and impose penalties for non-compliance, including sealing establishments and conducting summary trials.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Sentencing Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to lay down factors to be considered by courts while passing sentences to improve consistency in sentencing.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may, by Notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes a Sentencing Council and lays down factors for courts to ensure consistency in sentencing within Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Sentencing Act, 2019 was enacted by the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab to improve consistency in sentencing by defining specific aggravating and mitigating factors. It establishes a Sentencing Council responsible for publishing guidelines that courts must consider when imposing sentences. The Act applies to cases involving imprisonment but excludes capital punishment cases, covering various offences including those related to terrorism and public order.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Shops and Establishments (Security) Act, 1999
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the security of establishments in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.status_evidence: which is repealed by the Punjab Security of Vulnerable Establishments Ordinance 2015 (I of 2015), w.e.f. 8.1.2015, s.20
metadata.repealed_by: The Punjab Security of Vulnerable Establishments Ordinance, 2015
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the security of shops and establishments in Punjab but was repealed by an Ordinance in 2015.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Shops and Establishments (Security) Act, 1999 was passed by the Punjab Assembly to regulate security measures for establishments. It outlines provisions regarding security, penalties, rules, and repeal. The entire Act was repealed by the Punjab Security of Vulnerable Establishments Ordinance, 2015, effective January 8, 2015.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Sound Systems (Regulation) Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate and control use of sound systems in the Punjab.
repeals: The Punjab Regulation of Loudspeakers and Sound Amplifiers Ordinance, 1965 (II of 1965)
The Punjab Sound Systems (Regulation) Ordinance, 2015 (V of 2015)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to six months and fine between twenty five thousand and one hundred thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates and controls the use of sound systems in Punjab to prevent public nuisance and disorder.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Sound Systems (Regulation) Act, 2015 was enacted to regulate and control the use of sound systems within the Province of Punjab. It prohibits the use of loudspeakers that generate unnecessary noise or disturb public peace, particularly near places of worship, hospitals, and educational institutions. The Act empowers police officers to inspect sound systems, seize equipment used in offences, and imposes penalties including imprisonment and fines for violations.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Special Protection Unit Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the constitution of Special Protection Unit in the Police.
repeals: The Punjab Special Protection Unit Ordinance, 2015 (XXIII of 2015)
metadata.one_line: Constitutes a Special Protection Unit in the Punjab Police to provide dedicated security to foreigners, important persons and premises.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the constitution of the Special Protection Unit within the Police of the Province of Punjab. The Unit is designed to offer dedicated security services to foreigners, important persons, and specific premises notified by the Provincial Police Officer. It outlines the ranks, terms of service, recruitment criteria, pay structures, and financial arrangements for providing these security services, including fees payable by organizations utilizing the Unit.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Strategic Coordination Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Provincial Security Council and Punjab Strategic Coordination Board.
repeals: The Punjab Strategic Coordination Ordinance, 2014 (IX of 2014)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Provincial Security Council and Board to formulate security policy and coordinate counter-terrorism efforts in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Provincial Security Council and the Provincial Strategic Coordination Board to manage security and counter-terrorism matters in Punjab. The Council includes high-ranking officials like the Chief Minister and Home Minister, while the Board assists in policy formulation and monitors agency performance. The legislation grants powers to obtain information, appoint specialists, and make rules for its implementation.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Suppression of Prostitution Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to the suppression of prostitution in the Province of [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except the Tribal Areas.
repeals: the Punjab Suppression of Immoral Traffic Act, 1935
the Punjab Suppression of Immoral Traffic Act, 1935, as applicable to the former State of Bahawalpur
the North-West Frontier Province Anti-Prostitution and Suppression of Brothels Act, 1937
the Sind Prevention of Prostitution Act, 1951
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years and fine which may extend to one thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates laws to suppress prostitution in Punjab, defining offenses and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends and consolidates the law regarding the suppression of prostitution in the Province of Punjab. It defines key terms such as brothel, prostitute, and public place, while establishing punishments for keeping brothels, soliciting, and living on earnings of prostitution. The document also grants powers to arrest without warrant and enter premises, repeals previous acts related to immoral traffic, and applies to the whole of Punjab except Tribal Areas.

name: PUNJAB TENDOO LEAVES (PROHIBITION ON POSSESSION AND USE IN THE BORDER-BELT) ACT, 1974

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Tendoo Leaves (Prohibition on Possession and Use in the Border-Belt) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for prohibition on the possession and use of tendoo leaves in the border-belt of the Province of the Punjab.
repeals: The Punjab Tendoo Leaves (Prohibition on Possession and Use in the Border-Belt) Ordinance, 1973
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: Prohibits possession and use of tendoo leaves and bidi manufacture in Punjab's border-belt with penalties.
metadata.summary: This Act prohibits the possession and use of tendoo leaves within a ten-mile border-belt area inside the Province of the Punjab. It specifically bans the manufacture of bidi in this restricted zone and imposes severe penalties, including imprisonment up to three years or fines up to ten thousand rupees, for violations. The legislation also grants police and authorized officers powers to seize contraband, search premises (subject to warrant constraints), and hold company officials criminally liable unless they prove lack of knowledge or due diligence.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Tribunals of Inquiry Ordinance, 1969
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the appointment of Tribunals of Inquiry and for vesting such Tribunals with certain powers.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except the Tribal Areas
metadata.one_line: Provides for the appointment and powers of Tribunals of Inquiry in the Province of Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the framework for appointing Tribunals, Commissions, or Committees of Inquiry to investigate matters of public importance. It vests these bodies with the powers of a civil court, including summoning witnesses, receiving evidence, and seizing documents. The Ordinance also grants additional powers such as ordering police investigations and provides legal protection for actions taken in good faith by the Tribunal or Government.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Vagrancy Ordinance, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to vagrancy in the Province of [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except the Tribal Areas.
metadata.commencement: on such date or dates as Government may, by notification, direct.
repeals: The Sind Vagrancy Act, 1947
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates laws on vagrancy in Punjab, establishing welfare homes and defining offences related to soliciting alms.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends and consolidates the law relating to vagrancy in the Province of Punjab. It establishes welfare homes for the detention and training of vagrants and defines specific terms such as 'vagrant', 'organizer', and 'public place'. The document outlines the powers of police officers, duties of managers, and procedures for trial and sentence. It also repeals the Sind Vagrancy Act, 1947.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Vigilance Committees Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the constitution of Vigilance Committees.
repeals: The Punjab Vigilance Committees Ordinance, 2016 (I of 2016)
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes Vigilance Committees at District, Sub-divisional and Union Council levels to ensure watch and ward systems.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Vigilance Committees Act, 2016 provides for the constitution of Vigilance Committees at District, Sub-divisional, and Union Council or Municipal Committee levels. These committees are designed to ensure an effective watch and ward system and deal with ancillary matters related to local security. The Act defines the composition of these committees, outlines their functions such as monitoring subversive activities and hate literature, and establishes mechanisms for meetings, logistic support, and member conduct.

name: PUNJAB WAQF, TRUSTS AND COOPERATIVE SOCIETIES (MONITORING) ACT 2026

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Waqf, Trusts and Cooperative Societies (Monitoring) Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to monitor and oversee the regulation of waqf, trusts and cooperative societies in Punjab.
establishes: Punjab Waqf, Trusts and Cooperative Societies Commission
metadata.one_line: Establishes a Commission to monitor and oversee waqf, trusts, and cooperative societies in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Waqf, Trusts and Cooperative Societies Commission to monitor and regulate waqf, trusts, and cooperative societies within the province. The Commission is tasked with implementing beneficial ownership regimes, coordinating on anti-money laundering measures, and reviewing relevant departmental policies. It possesses powers to conduct enquiries, recommend the cancellation of registrations for violations, and frame rules or regulations to carry out its purposes.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Witness Protection Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to protect witnesses and other persons connected with certain criminal proceedings.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years but which shall not be less than thirty days and with fine which may extend to rupees five million but which shall not be less than rupees one hundred thousand
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes a Witness Protection Board and Units to protect witnesses in terrorism, sexual offence, or serious criminal cases.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Witness Protection Act, 2018 provides measures to protect witnesses and other persons connected with the investigation, prosecution, and trial of specific criminal proceedings. It applies to cases involving terrorism, sexual offences, or other serious offences punishable by death, life imprisonment, or over seven years. The Act establishes a Witness Protection Board and Units to frame policies, oversee implementation, and provide protection measures such as relocation, change of identity, and close protection services.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Development of Cities Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the development of cities in the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
repeals: Punjab Ordinance No. XI of 1976
metadata.one_line: Establishes a system for city planning and development in Punjab, creating an Authority with powers to execute schemes and levy fees.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a comprehensive system for planning and developing cities within the Province of Punjab. It creates an integrated Authority responsible for improving housing, infrastructure, traffic, health, and waste disposal. The Authority is empowered to prepare execution schemes, levy betterment fees, acquire land, and enforce regulations regarding building lines and public amenities.

name: PUNJAB HOUSING AND TOWN-PLANNING AGENCY ORDINANCE, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Housing and Town-Planning Agency Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for establishment of the Punjab Housing and Town-Planning Agency.
establishes: Punjab Housing and Town Planning Agency
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Housing and Town Planning Agency to provide shelter and ensure systematic urban growth in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Punjab Housing and Town Planning Agency as a body corporate to provide shelter to the shelterless and establish a comprehensive town planning system. It defines the composition of the Agency, its powers to prepare schemes, acquire land, and manage finances through a dedicated fund. The document also outlines penalties for offences, procedures for recovery of dues, and provisions regarding government servants serving within the Agency.

name: PUNJAB PUBLIC UTILITIES INFRASTRUCTURE PROTECTION ACT 2026

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Public Utilities Infrastructure Protection Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for prevention of theft, unauthorized removal, damage, repair and maintenance of public utilities infrastructure in Punjab.
repeals: The Punjab Public Utilities Infrastructure Protection Ordinance, 2026 (IV of 2026)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to three years or fine up to ten million rupees
metadata.one_line: An Act to prevent theft, unauthorized removal, and damage to public utilities infrastructure in Punjab with strict penalties.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a legal framework to prevent the theft, unauthorized removal, and wilful damage of public utilities infrastructure within Punjab. It defines specific offences regarding scrap dealers and re-rolling plants, mandating that such items must be deformed before purchase to prevent reuse. The legislation empowers designated authorities to inspect premises, seize property, and seal locations while providing for whistle-blower rewards and expedited trials.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Saaf Pani Authority Act, 2024
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of the Punjab Saaf Pani Authority.
repeals: The Punjab Aab-e-Pak Authority Act, 2019
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Saaf Pani Authority to provide safe drinking water in Punjab by re-constituting the previous authority.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Saaf Pani Authority to ensure the availability of safe drinking water for people in Punjab. It re-constitutes the existing Punjab Aab-e-Pak Authority as the new entity with powers to manage water filtration and purification plants. The Authority is empowered to conduct surveys, design infrastructure, issue licenses, and make rules or regulations necessary for its functions.

name: PUNJAB WATER AND SANITATION AUTHORITY ACT 2025

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Water and Sanitation Authority Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of the Punjab Water and Sanitation Authority.
repeals: Lahore Development Authority Act, 1975 (XXX of 1975)
Punjab Development of Cities Act, 1976 (XIX of 1976)
Punjab Water Act, 2019 (XXI of 2019)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Water and Sanitation Authority to manage water supply, sanitation, and groundwater conservation in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Water and Sanitation Authority as a body corporate to develop, operate, and maintain water supply and sanitation systems. It also creates the Al-Jazari Water and Sanitation Academy for training purposes. The Authority is composed of government representatives, agency heads, technical experts, and has powers over fees, groundwater control, and rule-making.

name: PUNJAB SIKH ANAND KARAJ MARRIAGE ACT 2018

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Sikh Anand Karaj Marriage Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for solemnization and registration of Sikh marriages.
repeals: The Anand Marriage Act, 1909 (VII of 1909)
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Regulates solemnization, registration, and dissolution of Sikh Anand Karaj marriages in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the solemnization and registration of Sikh marriages known as Anand Karaj within the Province of Punjab. It mandates that all such marriages be registered by an authorized Anand Karaj Registrar within thirty days and establishes a procedure for dissolving marriages through an Arbitration Council if reconciliation fails. The Act also repeals the application of the Anand Marriage Act, 1909, to the Punjab.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Industrial Development Board Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of an Industrial Development Board in the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
repeals: The Punjab Industrial Development Board Ordinance, 1973 (Punjab Ordinance No. XI of 1973)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Industrial Development Board to manage and run public sector industries in the Province.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Industrial Development Board to establish, manage, control, and run industries in the public sector within the Province of Punjab. The Board is a body corporate with perpetual succession, headed by a Chairman and Managing Director appointed by the Government. It possesses powers to acquire property, maintain accounts, make rules and regulations, and dispose of assets upon winding up.

name: PUNJAB INDUSTRIES (CONTROL ON ESTABLISHMENT AND ENLARGEMENT) ORDINANCE, 1963

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Industries (Control on Establishment and Enlargement) Ordinance, 1963
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the organized and planned growth of industries in [the Punjab].
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except the Tribal Areas
metadata.commencement: at once for sections 1 and 2; remaining provisions on such dates as the Government may specify by notification
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates the organized growth of industries in Punjab by requiring government permission for new establishments or enlargements.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Industries (Control on Establishment and Enlargement) Ordinance, 1963 was promulgated to ensure the organized and planned growth of industries within the Province of Punjab. It mandates that no person shall establish or enlarge an industrial undertaking without previous written permission from the Government. The Ordinance defines key terms such as 'industrial undertaking' based on worker numbers and grants powers to the Director for information gathering and entry. It establishes penalties for contravention, including imprisonment up to one year or fines, and provides mechanisms for revision and appeal to the Government.

name: PUNJAB PREVENTION OF SPECULATION IN ESSENTIAL COMMODITIES ACT 2021

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Prevention of Speculation in Essential Commodities Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the prevention of speculation in essential commodities.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months and fine which may extend to one hundred thousand rupees
metadata.administering_body: Director General Industries, Prices, Weights and Measures, Punjab
metadata.one_line: This Act prevents speculation in essential commodities to curb artificial price hikes and profiteering in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Prevention of Speculation in Essential Commodities Act, 2021 aims to prevent speculation in essential commodities to curb artificial price hikes and profiteering. It applies to the whole of Punjab and defines key terms such as 'essential commodity', 'dealer', and 'speculation' which includes wagering or betting. The Act empowers authorized officers to verify stocks, register delivery orders, seize unlifted commodities, and impose penalties including imprisonment up to six months and fines up to one hundred thousand rupees for contraventions.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Skills Development Authority Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Punjab Skills Development Authority.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify
metadata.max_penalty: rupees five hundred thousand
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Skills Development Authority to promote and regulate technical education and vocational training in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Skills Development Authority to promote and regulate the technical education and vocational training sector in the Punjab. The Authority is a body corporate with powers to enter contracts, acquire property, and sue or be sued, subject to government approval for immovable property disposal. It defines its composition, including ex officio members from various departments and non-official members appointed by the Government, along with their terms and disqualifications. The Act outlines the Authority's functions, delegation of powers, financial management through a fund, audit requirements, and mechanisms for imposing administrative penalties for non-compliance with standards.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Small Industries Corporation Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of a Small Industries Corporation in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
repeals: The Punjab Ordinances Temporary Enactment Act, 1973
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Small Industries Corporation to succeed the defunct West Pakistan Small Industries Corporation and promote small industries in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Small Industries Corporation to succeed the business and properties of the defunct West Pakistan Small Industries Corporation. It provides for the corporation's constitution, management, powers, duties, and functions, including granting loans and managing industrial estates. The Act also outlines financial provisions, rules-making powers, and repeals the temporary enactment that passed the 1972 Ordinance.

name: PUNJAB STATE AID TO INDUSTRIES ACT, 1935

metadata.short_title: The Punjab State Aid to Industries Act, 1935
metadata.long_title: An Act to encourage the development of industries in the Punjab by the grant of State aid.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Provincial Government may by notification, appoint
repeals: The Punjab Industrial Loans Act, 1923
metadata.one_line: This Act encourages industrial development in Punjab through state aid, loans, and machinery supply via a Board of Industries.
metadata.summary: The Punjab State Aid to Industries Act, 1935 establishes a Board of Industries to regulate and grant state aid for industrial purposes within the Punjab. It provides mechanisms for loans, hire-purchase systems for machinery, subsidies, and government guarantees. The Act outlines procedures for applications, security requirements, repayment terms, and penalties for defaults, while also empowering the Provincial Government to make rules and control aided industries.

name: PUNJAB TECHNICAL EDUCATION AND VOCATIONAL TRAINING AUTHORITY ACT 2010

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to reorganize the Punjab Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority.
repeals: The Punjab Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority Ordinance, 1999
establishes: Punjab Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority
metadata.administering_body: Industries, Commerce, Investment and Skill Department
metadata.one_line: This Act reorganizes the Punjab Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority and repeals the 1999 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority Act, 2010 was enacted to reorganize the existing technical education authority in the Province. It establishes a body corporate with specific functions including providing technical education, maintaining institutions, and regulating training facilities. The Act defines the composition of the Authority, outlines its powers to frame rules and regulations, and provides for appeals to the Government. Finally, it repeals the Punjab Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority Ordinance, 1999, ensuring a smooth transition of assets and employees.

name: PUNJAB TIANJIN UNIVERSITY OF TECHNOLOGY LAHORE ACT 2018

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Tianjin University of Technology Lahore Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act for the establishment of Punjab Tianjin University of Technology Lahore.
repeals: The Punjab Tianjin University of Technology Lahore Ordinance, 2017 (XVI of 2017)
establishes: Punjab Tianjin University of Technology Lahore
metadata.one_line: Establishes Punjab Tianjin University of Technology Lahore and provides for its incorporation, governance, and functions.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Tianjin University of Technology Lahore as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It outlines the university's structure, including the Chancellor, Vice Chancellor, Syndicate, and Academic Council, while defining their respective powers and duties. The legislation also covers financial provisions, faculty appointments, student fees, and the transition of existing government institutes into the new university entity.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Undesirable Companies Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to prohibit the registration of companies for carrying on business for certain undesirable purposes and to provide for the winding up and dissolution of such companies.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab, except the Triable Areas.
metadata.commencement: on and after the commencement of this Ordinance
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine or with both
metadata.one_line: Prohibits registration of companies carrying on undesirable businesses in Punjab and provides for their winding up.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance prohibits the registration of any association or body intending to carry on business for specified undesirable purposes within the Province of Punjab. It mandates the cessation of functioning, preservation of assets, and submission of statements for existing undesirable companies. The text outlines powers for the registrar to call for information, inspect documents, seize assets, and take over management, while also defining offences and penalties for contravention.

name: PUNJAB WEIGHTS AND MEASURES (INTERNATIONAL SYSTEM) ENFORCEMENT ACT, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Weights and Measures (International System) Enforcement Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the enforcement of weights and measures (based on International System) and to regulate the use thereof and to provide for matters connected therewith in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Punjab
metadata.commencement: on such date as Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: West Pakistan Weights and Measures Ordinance, 1965
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to one thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Enforces weights and measures based on the International System in Punjab, regulating trade and imposing penalties for violations.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the enforcement and regulation of weights and measures based on the International System within the Province of Punjab. It establishes a framework involving Controllers and Inspectors to verify standards, stamp instruments, and inspect commercial transactions. The legislation prohibits the use of non-standard weights, demands for incorrect quantities, and the sale of un-stamped measures, while prescribing penalties for breaches and empowering the Government to make necessary rules.

name: PUNJAB INSTITUTE OF LANGUAGE, ART AND CULTURE ACT 2004

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Institute of Language, Art and Culture Act, 2004
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Institute of Language, Art and Culture.
repeals: Societies Registration Act (Act XXI of 1860)
establishes: Punjab Institute of Language, Art and Culture
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Institute of Language, Art and Culture to promote Punjabi language, art, and culture in the province.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Institute of Language, Art and Culture as a body corporate with perpetual succession. The Institute is responsible for promoting the Punjabi language, art, and culture through research, library development, and cultural projects. It defines the composition of its Board of Governors, including the Chief Minister and various Secretaries, and outlines its functions such as preserving folk arts and facilitating international collaboration.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Journalists Housing Foundation Act, 2004
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Journalists Housing Foundation.
metadata.commencement: at once but shall take effect on such date as may be notified by the Government in the official Gazette
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Journalists Housing Foundation to allot plots for house construction on a no-profit-no-loss basis.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Journalists Housing Foundation to introduce schemes for allotting plots for house construction on a no-profit, no-loss basis. The Foundation is a body corporate with perpetual succession, empowered to acquire land, develop housing schemes, and manage funds derived from government grants, donations, and fees. A Board of Directors comprising the Chief Minister, Information Minister, Secretary to Government, and nominated Assembly members oversees the foundation, while a Managing Committee handles day-to-day operations including plot allocation and budget management.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Special Premises (Preservation) Ordinance, 1985
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the preservation of certain premises in the Punjab.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to one year or with fine or with both
metadata.one_line: Preserves historical, cultural, and architectural premises in Punjab by regulating alterations, demolition, and restoration.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the preservation of specific premises in the Punjab that hold historical, cultural, or architectural value. It establishes Committees to regulate alterations, prevent unauthorized demolition, and oversee restoration efforts. The law also restricts advertising near these sites and allows for compulsory acquisition if a premise is in danger of decay.

name: PUNJAB TRANSPARENCY AND RIGHT TO INFORMATION ACT 2013

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Transparency and Right to Information Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for transparency and freedom of information in the Punjab.
repeals: The Punjab Transparency and Right to Information Ordinance, 2013
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the Punjab Information Commission to ensure transparency and freedom of information in the Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Transparency and Right to Information Act, 2013 provides for transparency and freedom of information within the Punjab province. It establishes the Punjab Information Commission to oversee access to public information held by various government bodies and local governments. The Act mandates proactive disclosure of specific categories of information by public bodies and outlines procedures for citizens to request information, including internal review mechanisms and penalties for non-compliance.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Flood Plain Regulation Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate construction in the flood plains in the Punjab.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to thirty days and fine up to two hundred thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Regulates construction in Punjab flood plains, designates areas, and establishes committees for approval and review.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates construction activities within designated flood plains in the Punjab to ensure flood mitigation and water resource development. It empowers the Government to declare flood plains and appoints Canal Officers responsible for granting or rejecting construction permissions based on committee reviews. The legislation outlines procedures for applications, defines specific offences with associated penalties, and establishes a Review Board to handle appeals against officer orders.

name: PUNJAB IRRIGATION, DRAINAGE AND RIVERS ACT 2023

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Irrigation, Drainage and Rivers Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provisions for management and control of irrigation, drainage and rivers in the Punjab.
repeals: Canal and Drainage Act, 1873 (VIII of 1873)
Punjab Soil Reclamation Act, 1952 (XXI of 1952)
metadata.one_line: This Act manages and controls irrigation, drainage, and rivers in Punjab while repealing older canal acts.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Irrigation, Drainage and Rivers Act, 2023 establishes a comprehensive framework for managing water resources, canals, and rivers within the province. It vests natural water in the Government, defines the powers of Canal Officers, and sets standards for irrigation schemes, drainage construction, and flood control measures. The Act also repeals the Canal and Drainage Act, 1873, and the Punjab Soil Reclamation Act, 1952, while preserving existing rights and liabilities acquired under those repealed laws.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Water Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to comprehensively manage and regulate water resources in the Punjab in the interest of conservation and sustainability.
repeals: The Lahore Development Authority Act, 1975 (XXX of 1975)
The Punjab Development of Cities Act, 1976 (XIX of 1976)
metadata.one_line: This Act comprehensively manages and regulates water resources in Punjab for conservation and sustainability.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Water Act, 2019 establishes a framework for managing water resources within the province to ensure conservation and sustainability. It creates two main bodies: the Punjab Water Resources Commission and the Punjab Water Services Regulatory Authority, which oversee various aspects of water supply and sewerage services. The Act regulates water undertakers, issues licenses for abstraction and disposal, sets quality standards, and provides mechanisms for enforcement during droughts or in cases of contamination.

metadata.short_title: Punjab Domestic Workers Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the regulation of employment of domestic workers in Province of the Punjab.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for one month or fine up to Rs. 50,000
metadata.one_line: Regulates employment, rights, and welfare of domestic workers in Punjab while prohibiting child labour.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the employment of domestic workers in the Province of Punjab to protect their rights and ensure their welfare. It prohibits bonded labor, discrimination, and child employment under age 15, while establishing a Welfare Fund and mechanisms for dispute resolution. The legislation also defines wages, leave entitlements, maternity benefits, and outlines penalties for employers who violate these provisions.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Fair Price Shops (Factories) Ordinance, 1971
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of fair price shops in certain factories in the Punjab.
metadata.commencement: on such date, in such areas and shall apply to such factories or class of factories as Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify in that behalf
metadata.max_penalty: double the punishment provided for such offence under this Ordinance on second conviction
metadata.one_line: Establishes fair price shops in Punjab factories to sell essential articles at cheaper rates to workers.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the establishment and maintenance of fair price shops within specific factories in the Punjab. It mandates employers to maintain sufficient stocks of essential articles like wheat, pulses, and sugar for their workers. The law establishes a Managing Committee to determine monthly quotas and appoints Inspectors to oversee compliance with fair pricing and stock requirements.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Home-based Workers Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for protection of rights of home-based workers.
metadata.one_line: An Act to protect the rights of home-based workers in Punjab by establishing a welfare fund and regulating employment conditions.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the protection of rights for home-based workers in the Province of Punjab. It establishes a Home-based Workers Welfare Fund and defines key terms such as 'home-based worker', 'employer', and 'contractor'. The legislation outlines employer obligations regarding wages, medical treatment, travel costs, and contract termination, while also providing mechanisms for dispute settlement.
