metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Punjab, except the Tribal Areas
metadata.commencement: at once for sections 1 and 2; other provisions on dates specified by Government notification
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance transfers control of High Schools from Local Councils to the Government in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the taking over of High Schools maintained by District Councils and Town Committees in Punjab by the Provincial Government. It mandates the transfer of staff, assets, funds, and liabilities from the Local Councils to the Government while defining specific financial contributions required from the councils. The Ordinance also grants the Government power to make rules and except certain schools from its provisions via notification.

name: PUNJAB SEIZED AND FREEZED INSTITUTIONS (MADAARIS AND SCHOOLS) ACT 2019

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Seized and Freezed Institutions (Madaaris and Schools) Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Madaaris and Schools Management Board in the Punjab.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify
repeals: The Punjab Seized and Freezed Institutions (Madaaris and Schools) Ordinance, 2019
metadata.one_line: Establishes a Board to manage seized madaaris and schools in Punjab and mainstream their students.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Madaaris and Schools Management Board to efficiently manage institutions seized under UN Security Council orders. The Board is empowered to recruit staff, formulate budgets, acquire property, and ensure the mainstreaming of students from these institutions. It creates a Directorate to manage properties and student affairs, while exempting its employees from certain provincial civil servant acts.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Text-Book Board Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Text-Book Board.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the province of the Punjab, except the Tribal Areas
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Text-Book Board to produce textbooks, conduct research, and manage school education in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Punjab Text-Book Board as a body corporate to produce text books, supplementary reading material, and guide books for teachers. It defines the Board's constitution, including a Chairman and Directors appointed by the Government, and outlines its powers regarding curriculum research and scheme framing. The Board is deemed a local authority for borrowing money and must maintain accounts audited annually by government-appointed Auditors.

name: PUNJAB EMPLOYEES EFFICIENCY, DISCIPLINE AND ACCOUNTABILITY ACT 2006

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Employees Efficiency, Discipline and Accountability Act, 2006
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for proceedings against the employees in government and corporation service in relation to their efficiency, discipline and accountability.
repeals: The Punjab Removal from Service (Special Powers) Ordinance, 2000
metadata.one_line: Provides for proceedings against government and corporation service employees regarding efficiency, discipline, and accountability.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a framework for initiating proceedings against employees in government and corporation service concerning their efficiency, discipline, and accountability. It defines key terms such as 'competent authority' and 'corruption', outlines the procedure for inquiries, and specifies penalties for misconduct. The Act applies to current and retired employees, provided proceedings are initiated within specific timeframes after retirement.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Enforcement and Regulation Act, 2024
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of the Punjab Enforcement and Regulatory Authority and to prescribe procedures for efficient and effective implementation and enforcement of special laws throughout Punjab.
metadata.commencement: on such date and apply to such area as the Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify
metadata.one_line: Establishes an overarching provincial enforcement authority in Punjab to streamline regulatory compliance and enforce special laws.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Enforcement and Regulatory Authority to oversee the implementation and enforcement of special laws throughout the province. It creates District Enforcement and Regulatory Boards, defines the composition and powers of the Authority, and outlines procedures for handling encroachments, public nuisances, and administrative penalties. The legislation aims to improve coordination between existing regulatory agencies, designate lead regulators where necessary, and provide mechanisms for whistle-blower protection and grievance redressal.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Essential Services (Maintenance) Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the maintenance of certain essential services.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab, except the Tribal Areas
repeals: The North-West Frontier Province Essential Services (Maintenance) Act, 1946
The West Pakistan Essential Services (Maintenance) Ordinance, 1957
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year and a fine
metadata.one_line: Provides for the maintenance of essential services in Punjab by regulating employment, wages, and imposing penalties for disobedience.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the maintenance of certain essential services within the Province of Punjab. It defines key terms such as 'employment' and 'essential service', and applies to all government employments, local authority services, transport, or civil defence. The Act empowers the Government to order persons in these employments to remain in specified areas and regulates their wages and conditions. It establishes offences for disobedience, abandonment of employment, or unauthorized departure from specified areas, prescribing penalties including imprisonment up to one year and fines.

name: PUNJAB ESTABLISHMENT OF SPECIAL COURTS (OVERSEAS PAKISTANIS PROPERTY) ACT 2025

metadata.short_title: Punjab Establishment of Special Courts (Overseas Pakistanis Property) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish special courts for adjudication of petition in respect of immovable properties of overseas Pakistanis.
metadata.one_line: Establishes special courts in Punjab to adjudicate petitions regarding immovable properties of overseas Pakistanis.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes special courts within the Punjab province specifically for handling petitions related to the immovable properties of overseas Pakistanis. It defines key terms such as 'Overseas Pakistani' and outlines procedures for filing petitions, including e-filing capabilities managed by the Lahore High Court. The Act grants these special courts exclusive jurisdiction over disputes involving overseas Pakistanis, provides for the appointment of judges with specific qualifications, and details the powers regarding execution of decrees and appeals.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Film City Authority Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of the Punjab Film City Authority for promotion, development, regulation and facilitation of the cinema and motion picture industry in the Punjab.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Film City Authority to regulate and promote the cinema industry in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Film City Authority as a body corporate to promote, develop, and regulate the cinema and motion picture industry in the Punjab. The Authority is composed of various members including film professionals, experts, and government nominees, with powers to manage funds, acquire property, and frame regulations. It provides mechanisms for financial management, annual reporting, recovery of dues, and grants immunity from legal proceedings for acts done in good faith.

name: PUNJAB GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES WELFARE FUND ORDINANCE, 1969

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Government Employees Welfare Fund Ordinance, 1969
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish a Welfare Fund for the relief and security of the employees of the [the] Punjab Government and their families.
metadata.commencement: on such date as Government may, by notification, appoint in this behalf
metadata.one_line: Establishes a welfare fund for the relief and security of Punjab Government employees and their families.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes a Welfare Fund to provide relief and security for employees of the Punjab Government and their families. It creates two parts of the fund, one for gazetted servants and one for non-gazetted servants, funded by contributions from employees and the government. The Ordinance also sets up Welfare Boards with specific powers to administer the fund and arrange insurance coverage for employees.

name: PUNJAB GOVERNMENT SERVANTS BENEVOLENT FUND ORDINANCE, 1960

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Government Servants Benevolent Fund Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to constitute a Benevolent Fund for relief of Government servants and their families.
metadata.commencement: on such date as Government may, by notification, appoint
metadata.one_line: Constitutes a Benevolent Fund to provide financial relief to government servants and their families in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes a Benevolent Fund specifically for the relief of Government servants and their families in the Province of Punjab. The Fund is divided into two parts for gazetted and non-gazetted servants, financed by compulsory contributions, government grants, donations, and investment income. It authorizes the use of funds to provide financial assistance to families of deceased servants, those invalided out of service, and for special cases, in addition to existing pensions or gratuities.

name: PUNJAB GOVERNMENT SERVANTS HOUSING FOUNDATION ACT 2004

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Government Servants Housing Foundation Act, 2004
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Housing Foundation for the Government servants.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
metadata.commencement: at once but shall take effect on such date as may be notified by the Government in the official Gazette
metadata.one_line: Establishes a foundation to provide houses or plots on no profit no loss basis to Government servants in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Government Servants Housing Foundation to provide housing schemes for government servants and their families. The Foundation is a body corporate with a Board of Directors comprising civil servants and other appointed members. It manages the collection of contributions, maintenance of accounts, and disposal of houses or plots at retirement or upon death during service.

name: PUNJAB MINISTERS (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) ACT, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the salaries, allowances and privileges of the Ministers of the Punjab.
metadata.commencement: at once but deemed to have taken effect on and from the first day of March, 1975
repeals: The Punjab Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Order, 1972
The Punjab Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Ordinance, 1975
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the salaries, allowances, and privileges of Ministers of the Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the framework for the salaries, allowances, and privileges applicable to Ministers of the Punjab. It defines specific monetary amounts for basic salary, equipment allowance, sumptuary allowance, and various travel and medical benefits. The legislation also outlines provisions for official residence, personal staff, leave, and discretionary grants, while repealing previous orders and ordinances on the same subject.

name: PUNJAB OFFICE OF THE OMBUDSMAN ACT 1997

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Office of the Ombudsman Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the office of Ombudsman in the Province of the Punjab.
repeals: The Punjab Office of the Ombudsman Ordinance 1997 (XIV of 1997)
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Province of Punjab
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Office of Ombudsman in Punjab to protect citizens' rights and redress maladministration.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the office of the Provincial Ombudsman for the Punjab to protect people's rights, ensure adherence to the rule of law, and rectify injustice caused by maladministration. It defines maladministration to include acts contrary to law, arbitrary decisions, corruption, and inefficiency. The Ombudsman is appointed by the Government, holds office for a fixed term, and possesses powers to investigate complaints, enter premises, and recommend remedies.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Overseas Pakistanis Commission Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for reconstitution of the Punjab Overseas Pakistanis Commission.
repeals: The Punjab Overseas Pakistanis Commission Act, 2014
The Punjab Overseas Pakistanis Commission Ordinance, 2020
metadata.max_penalty: disciplinary action against the delinquent public servant
metadata.one_line: Reconstitutes the Punjab Overseas Pakistanis Commission to handle grievances of Overseas Pakistanis regarding Government Agencies.
metadata.summary: This Act reconstitutes the Punjab Overseas Pakistanis Commission to receive and redress grievances of Overseas Pakistanis relating to Government Agencies. The Commission consists of the Chief Minister as Chairperson, various government officials, Assembly members, and private sector nominees. It functions by reviewing reports, nominating council members, notifying committees, and referring complaints to concerned offices. The Act also establishes Special Courts for speedy trials and provides mechanisms for implementing recommendations and taking disciplinary action against delinquent public servants.

name: PUNJAB PREVENTION OF CONFLICT OF INTEREST ACT 2019

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Prevention of Conflict of Interest Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Punjab Prevention of Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commission; It is necessary to establish principles of conflict of interest for public office holders and the related post-employment matters; to prevent and minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the private interests and public duties of public office holders; to provide for the resolution of those conflicts in the public interest should they arise; to establish an independent Commission with the mandate to determine the measures necessary to avoid conflict of interest; to determine whether a contravention of the Act has occurred; to encourage experienced and competent persons to seek and accept public office; to facilitate interchange between the private and public sector; and, not to deny equal opportunities to relatives of public office holder, as the relatives cannot be barred from legal business activities, and, for matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto
metadata.commencement: on such date as Government may, by notification in the official Gazette specify
establishes: Punjab Prevention of Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commission
metadata.max_penalty: rupees five hundred thousand
metadata.one_line: Establishes an independent Commission to prevent conflict of interest for public office holders in Punjab and sets penalties for violations.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Prevention of Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commission to regulate conflicts between private interests and public duties. It defines 'public office holder' broadly, including provincial ministers and civil servants, and mandates specific duties such as recusal and summary statements. The Commission has powers to issue compliance orders, investigate violations, and impose penalties up to five hundred thousand rupees or declare contracts void.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Procurement Regulatory Authority Act, 2009
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Procurement Regulatory Authority in the Punjab.
repeals: The Punjab Procurement Regulatory Authority Ordinance, 2007 (XIX of 2007)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Procurement Regulatory Authority in Punjab to regulate public sector procurement.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Procurement Regulatory Authority to regulate the procurement of goods, services, and works in the public sector within the province. It defines key terms such as 'corrupt practice' and 'procuring agency' and outlines the functions, powers, and governance structure of the Authority, including its Board and Managing Director. The Act also provides for the maintenance of funds, audit procedures, ethical considerations, and mechanisms for blacklisting and exemptions.

name: PUNJAB PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION EXAMINATION REFORMS ACT, 1977

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Public Service Commission Examination Reforms Act, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the eradication of malpractices in connection with examinations held by the Punjab Public Service Commission.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to rupees one thousand, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act eradicates malpractices in Punjab PSC examinations and defines offences with penalties.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Public Service Commission Examination Reforms Act, 1977 aims to eliminate malpractices in examinations conducted by the Punjab Public Service Commission. It defines key terms such as candidate, examiner, and answer-book, and lists specific offenses like impersonation, premature disclosure of questions, and falsification of results. The Act prescribes punishments including rigorous imprisonment up to one year or fines for these offenses and establishes procedures regarding court evidence and police cognizance.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal and, with certain modifications, re-enact the Punjab Public Service Commission Act, 1974.
amends: The Punjab Public Service Commission Act, 1974
repeals: The Public Service Commission Act, 1974 (1 of 1974)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance repeals and re-enacts the Punjab Public Service Commission Act, 1974 with modifications.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab to repeal and re-enact the Punjab Public Service Commission Act, 1974. It establishes the composition, terms of office, and functions of the Punjab Public Service Commission. The document outlines procedures for recruitment examinations, advice to the government, and rules regarding the removal of members from office.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Regularization of Service Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for appointment on regular basis.
metadata.territorial_extent: whole of Province of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Provides for the regularization of contract employees in the Government of the Punjab on a regular basis.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the appointment on a regular basis of certain employees serving on contract in the Government of the Punjab. It applies to all persons employed on contract who have completed three years of continuous service before or after the commencement of the Act. The Act establishes Scrutiny Committees to verify eligibility and qualifications, outlines procedures for regularization, determines seniority based on continuous service and age, and sets out mechanisms for appeals and reviews.

name: PUNJAB REQUISITIONING OF IMMOVABLE PROPERTY (TEMPORARY POWERS) ACT, 1956

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Requisitioning of Immovable Property (Temporary Powers) Act, 1956
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the requisitioning of immovable property.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Punjab except the Special Areas
repeals: The Sind Crown Servants (House Accommodation) Act, 1947
The Sind (Requisition of Land) Act, 1947
The North-West Frontier Province Premises (Requisition and Eviction) Act, 1953
The Bahawalpur Requisitioning of Immovable Property (Temporary Powers) Act, 1955
The Punjab Requisitioning of Immovable Property (Temporary Powers) Ordinance, 1955
subjects: Legal protection for actions taken under the Act
metadata.one_line: This Act empowers the Provincial Government to requisition immovable property for government use with provisions for compensation and exemptions.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Requisitioning of Immovable Property (Temporary Powers) Act, 1956 provides legal authority for the Provincial Government to requisition buildings for the use of federal or provincial officers, offices, or education institutions. It outlines procedures including notice periods, hearing opportunities for owners, and specific exemptions for religious worship sites, cantonments, evacuee properties, and residential houses occupied by owners. The Act also establishes principles for assessing compensation, powers to obtain information, and legal protections against suits for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

name: PUNJAB RIGHT TO PUBLIC SERVICES ACT, 2019

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Right to Public Services Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for delivery of public services to the people within the stipulated time limit.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
establishes: Punjab Right to Public Services Commission
metadata.one_line: This Act ensures delivery of public services within stipulated time limits and establishes a commission to oversee compliance.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Right to Public Services Act, 2019 provides eligible persons in Punjab with the right to access public services within specified time limits. It defines various authorities and officers responsible for service delivery and establishes the Punjab Right to Public Services Commission to enforce these provisions. The Act outlines mechanisms for appeals, compensation for delays, penalties for non-compliance, and powers for e-governance implementation.

name: PUNJAB SPECIAL ASSISTANTS (SALARY, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) ORDINANCE, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Special Assistants (Salary, Allowances and Privileges) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for appointment, salary, allowances and privileges of Special Assistants to the Chief Minister of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Provides for appointment, salary, allowances and privileges of Special Assistants to the Chief Minister of the Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the appointment, term of office, salary, and various allowances for Special Assistants appointed by the Chief Minister of the Punjab. It details entitlements regarding official residence, transport, medical facilities, leave, and personal staff. The document also outlines rules for maintenance costs, travelling allowances, and the power to make further rules.

name: PUNJAB SUBORDINATE JUDICIARY SERVICE TRIBUNAL ACT 1991

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Subordinate Judiciary Service Tribunal Act, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Subordinate Judiciary Service Tribunal.
repeals: Punjab Subordinate Judiciary Service Tribunal Ordinance, 1991 (XVIII of 1991)
metadata.one_line: Establishes a tribunal for the subordinate judiciary of Punjab to handle service terms and disciplinary matters.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Subordinate Judiciary Service Tribunal to adjudicate matters regarding the terms, conditions, and discipline of members of the subordinate judiciary under the administrative control of the Lahore High Court. The Tribunal consists of three judges nominated by the Chief Justice of the Lahore High Court and has exclusive jurisdiction over such service-related disputes. It possesses the powers of a civil court for conducting appeals, including enforcing attendance and examining witnesses, while excluding certain departmental decisions from its appellate scope.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab [Service] Tribunals Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of [Service] Tribunals to exercise jurisdiction regarding matters relating to the terms and conditions of service in respect of services of the Province of the Punjab.
repeals: Punjab Ordinance No. V of 1974
metadata.one_line: Establishes Service Tribunals in Punjab to adjudicate disputes regarding civil servants' terms and conditions of service.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes Service Tribunals within the Province of Punjab to exercise exclusive jurisdiction over matters relating to the terms and conditions of service for civil servants. The tribunals consist of a Chairman and Members appointed by the Governor, with specific qualifications required for each position. The Act outlines procedures for appeals, the composition of benches, and the powers of the tribunals, while also defining key terms such as 'civil servant' and excluding certain categories like workers or those on contract.

name: PUNJAB SKILLS DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP AUTHORITY ACT 2026

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Skills Development and Entrepreneurship Authority Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Punjab Skills Development and Entrepreneurship Authority.
repeals: The Punjab Board of Technical Education Ordinance, 1962 (XXXIX of 1962)
The Punjab Vocational Training Council Act, 1998 (VII of 1998)
The Punjab Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority Act, 2010 (X of 2010)
The Punjab Skills Development Authority Act, 2019 (VI of 2019)
establishes: Punjab Skills Development and Entrepreneurship Authority
Punjab Technical Education and Vocational Training Agency
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Skills Development and Entrepreneurship Authority to regulate technical and vocational education in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Skills Development and Entrepreneurship Authority to promote and regulate technical, vocational, skills development, education, and training. It creates various agencies for monitoring institutes, assessing students, and certifying them in technical and vocational fields. The Act also repeals previous legislation related to technical education and vocational training in Punjab to consolidate these functions under the new Authority.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Ehsaas Programme Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of the Punjab Ehsaas Programme.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Ehsaas Programme as an umbrella social protection and poverty alleviation initiative.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Ehsaas Programme as a body corporate to serve as an umbrella for social protection and poverty alleviation in the province. It aims to reform existing initiatives, optimize resource utilization, and utilize modern technology to ensure transparency and merit-based delivery. The Act defines key terms such as the Ehsaas Council and implementing agencies, outlines governance structures including a Chief Executive Officer, and provides mechanisms for grievance redressal and annual auditing.

name: PUNJAB EMPOWERMENT OF PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES ACT 2022

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to promote and ensure effective inclusion of persons with disabilities in the community and to protect their rights.
repeals: The Disabled Persons (Employment and Rehabilitation) Ordinance, 1981
establishes: Fund for rehabilitation of persons with disabilities
metadata.administering_body: Social Welfare and Bait-ul-Maal Department of the Government
metadata.one_line: This Act promotes inclusion, protects rights, and establishes councils for persons with disabilities in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2022 aims to ensure the effective inclusion of persons with disabilities in the community and protect their rights. It establishes a Council, District Welfare and Rehabilitation Units, and an Assessment Board to oversee rehabilitation and employment matters. The Act grants specific rights regarding accessibility, education, healthcare, and political participation while repealing the earlier 1981 Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Panah Gah Authority Act 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Punjab Panah Gah Authority.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Panah Gah Authority to provide temporary shelter and relief for shelterless persons in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Panah Gah Authority to create a comprehensive system for protecting and relieving shelterless persons. The Authority is empowered to establish, maintain, monitor, and operate Panah Gahs (places for temporary stay) across the province. It also defines the composition of the Authority, its powers to accept donations, frame regulations, and submit annual performance reports to the Government.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Senior Citizens Welfare Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the well-being, comfort and dignity of the senior citizens residing in the Punjab.
metadata.one_line: Establishes a council and fund to ensure the well-being, comfort, and dignity of senior citizens in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the well-being, comfort, and dignity of senior citizens residing in the Punjab. It establishes the Punjab Senior Citizens Welfare Council as a body corporate with perpetual succession and creates the Punjab Senior Citizens Welfare Fund to support their needs. The Council is composed of government secretaries, assembly members, philanthropists, and other officials who will formulate policies, conduct research, and manage funds to assist indigent senior citizens.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Women Protection Authority Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act for the establishment of the Punjab Women Protection Authority.
repeals: The Punjab Women Protection Authority Ordinance, 2017 (II of 2017)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Women Protection Authority to protect women against violence in the province.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Women Protection Authority as a body corporate to oversee protection, relief, and rehabilitation systems for women facing violence. The Authority is headed by a Chairperson and consists of ex-officio members from government departments and nominated non-official members. It possesses powers to establish protection centers, monitor administration, and implement policies while maintaining its own fund and accounts under the supervision of the Auditor General.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Health Foundation Act, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Health Foundation.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
repeals: The Punjab Health Foundation Ordinance, 1992 (XXXV of 1992)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Health Foundation to promote and finance health sector development in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Health Foundation as a body corporate to promote, develop, and finance the health sector in the Province of Punjab. The Foundation is managed by a Board of Directors appointed by the Government and includes functions such as establishing health institutions, providing grants and loans to private health providers, and assisting in population welfare programs. It creates a dedicated Fund for these activities and provides immunity to its employees and directors while repealing the earlier 1992 Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Healthcare Commission Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to improve quality of healthcare services and ban quackery in the Punjab in all its forms and manifestations.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Healthcare Commission to improve healthcare quality and ban quackery in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Healthcare Commission to regulate healthcare services and ban quackery within the province. It provides for the registration and licensing of healthcare establishments, sets standards for service delivery, and outlines procedures for inspection and enforcement. The Commission is empowered to make regulations regarding facility standards, staff qualifications, and pricing, while also defining offences related to medical negligence and obstruction.

name: PUNJAB MEDICAL AND HEALTH INSTITUTIONS ACT, 2003

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Medical and Health Institutions Act, 2003
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment and management of Medical and Health Institutions in the Punjab.
repeals: The Punjab Medical and Health Institutions Ordinance, 2002 (VIII of 2002)
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes and regulates Medical and Health Institutions in Punjab through a Board of Management.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Medical and Health Institutions Act, 2003 provides for the establishment and efficient management of medical and health institutions within the province. It creates a Board of Management to oversee these institutions, defining their composition, powers, and administrative functions. The Act also outlines provisions for funding, auditing, annual reporting, and the appointment of key officers like the Principal and Medical Superintendent.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Medical Teaching Institutions (Reforms) Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to improve medical education and enhance effectiveness, efficiency and responsiveness of healthcare services.
repeals: The Punjab Medical Teaching Institutions (Reforms) Ordinance, 2019
metadata.one_line: This Act reforms medical teaching institutions in Punjab to improve education and healthcare service effectiveness.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Medical Teaching Institutions (Reforms) Act, 2020 was enacted by the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab to improve medical education and enhance the efficiency of healthcare services. It establishes a Provincial Policy Board and Boards of Governors for various institutions, defining their functions, composition, and powers. The Act creates bodies corporate for medical teaching institutions, outlines management structures including Deans and Directors, and sets provisions for finance, audit, and personnel.

name: PUNJAB REPRODUCTIVE, MATERNAL, NEO-NATAL AND CHILD HEALTH AUTHORITY ACT 2014

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Reproductive, Maternal, Neo-natal and Child Health Authority Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Reproductive, Maternal, Neo-natal and Child Health Authority.
establishes: Punjab Reproductive, Maternal, Neo-natal and Child Health Authority
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Reproductive, Maternal, Neo-natal and Child Health Authority to manage primary healthcare and family planning affairs.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Reproductive, Maternal, Neo-natal and Child Health Authority to provide a legal framework for managing national programs on primary healthcare and family planning in Punjab. The Authority is managed by a Board of Governors comprising government officials, assembly members, and civil society representatives. It grants the Authority corporate status, defines its powers regarding assets and agreements, and outlines procedures for audits, annual reporting, and immunity from legal proceedings.

name: PUNJAB SAFE MEDICAL SUPPLIES AUTHORITY ACT 2018

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Safe Medical Supplies Authority Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish an Authority for procuring drugs and medical equipment and providing them to the public health facilities in the Punjab
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may, by notification, specify
metadata.max_penalty: five hundred thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Establishes an Authority to procure quality drugs and medical equipment for equitable distribution to public health facilities in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Safe Medical Supplies Authority to ensure the procurement of quality drugs and medical equipment. The Authority is responsible for their effective administration and prompt, equitable distribution to public health facilities across the Punjab. It defines the composition of the Authority, categorizes storage premises, and outlines mechanisms for fund management, audits, and administrative penalties for non-compliance.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Masstransit Authority Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Punjab Masstransit Authority.
repeals: The Punjab Metrobus Authority Act, 2012 (LVI of 2012)
The Punjab Masstransit Authority Ordinance, 2015 (XIII of 2015)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Masstransit Authority to manage mass transit systems in Punjab cities.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Masstransit Authority as a body corporate to construct, operate, and maintain mass transit systems in major cities of Punjab. It defines the composition of the Authority, including ex officio members and nominated representatives from the private sector and legislature. The Act outlines the Authority's functions regarding ancillary facilities, fare collection, and service provider management while granting immunity for actions taken in good faith.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Road Safety Authority Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for road safety in the Punjab.
repeals: provisions of the Ordinance listed in the Schedule appended to this Act
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Road Safety Authority to ensure safe road design, vehicles, trained drivers, and post-accident management in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Road Safety Authority to ensure road safety by adopting best international practices. It covers safe road design, vehicle safety, driver training, and post-accident management within the Province of Punjab. The Authority is a body corporate with specific composition including government secretaries, police representatives, and industry experts. The Act empowers the Authority to frame regulations and rules regarding vehicle classification, driver testing, and road safety inspections.

name: PUNJAB ROAD TRANSPORT BOARD REMOVAL OF UNDESIRABLE EMPLOYEES ORDINANCE, 1965

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Road Transport Board (Punjab) Removal of Undesirable Employees Ordinance, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the termination of services of undesirable employees of the Punjab Road Transport Board.
metadata.one_line: Provides for termination of services of undesirable employees of the Punjab Road Transport Board with appeal rights.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance allows the appropriate authority to terminate the services of undesirable employees of the Punjab Road Transport Board if it is expedient in the public interest. It defines key terms such as 'employee' and 'appropriate authority', outlines the procedure for termination including a reasonable opportunity to show cause, and provides for appeals to Government within fifteen days. The Ordinance also grants protection from legal proceedings against government officers acting in good faith under its provisions.

name: PUNJAB FAIR REPRESENTATION OF WOMEN ACT 2014

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Fair Representation of Women Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend certain laws of the Punjab for purposes of fair representation of women in decision-making process and their empowerment.
amends: The Punjab Government Educational and Training Institution Ordinance, 1960
The Punjab Government Servants Benevolent Fund Ordinance, 1960
The Punjab Board of Technical Education Ordinance, 1962
The Provincial Employees' Social Security Ordinance, 1965
The Punjab Social Services Board Ordinance, 1970
The Punjab Fair Price Shops (Factories) Ordinance, 1971
The University of the Punjab Act, 1973
The University of Agriculture Faisalabad Act, 1973
The Government College Women University Faisalabad Act, 2012
The Government College Women University Sialkot Act, 2012
The Government Sadiq College Women University Bahawalpur Act, 2012
metadata.one_line: Amends various Punjab laws to ensure at least one-third women representation in decision-making bodies.
metadata.summary: This Act amends specific laws of the Punjab to ensure fair representation of women in decision-making processes. It mandates minimum percentages or numbers of female members, trustees, and officers across various boards, institutions, and authorities. The amendments apply to existing ordinances and acts governing education, social security, wages, and technical bodies within the province.

name: PUNJAB PROTECTION OF WOMEN AGAINST VIOLENCE ACT 2016

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Protection of Women against Violence Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish an effective system of protection, relief and rehabilitation of women against violence.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may, by notification, specify
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab, Social Welfare and Bait-ul-Maal Department
metadata.one_line: Establishes a protection system for women victims of violence in Punjab including committees, centers, and relief orders.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes an effective system to protect, provide relief, and rehabilitate women against violence in the province of Punjab. It creates District Women Protection Committees, Protection Centres, and shelter homes to assist aggrieved persons facing domestic violence, sexual violence, or other forms of abuse. The legislation empowers Courts to issue interim, protection, residence, and monetary orders to ensure safety and financial support for victims.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Women Hostels Authority Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate women hostels established in the private sector.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may, by notification, appoint
metadata.one_line: Establishes an Authority to regulate women hostels in the private sector within Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Women Hostels Authority to regulate women hostels established in the private sector within the Province of Punjab. The Authority aims to provide safe and standard accommodation facilities to women by regulating these establishments and handling ancillary matters. It defines the composition, powers, and functions of the Authority, including provisions for hostel inspection, registration, hygiene standards, and dispute resolution mechanisms.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Heritage Foundation Act, 2005
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Punjab Heritage Foundation in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
repeals: The Tajdeed-e-Lahore Board Ordinance, 2002 (LXII of 2002)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Heritage Foundation to conserve and rehabilitate heritage sites in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Heritage Foundation within the Province of Punjab to conserve, maintain, and rehabilitate local heritage. It creates a permanent fund supported by grants and voluntary contributions for these purposes. The management is vested in a Board of Governors comprising government officials and nominated members, with powers to approve projects and manage assets.

name: PUNJAB HISTORICAL MOSQUES AND SHRINES FUND CESS ORDINANCE, 1960

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Historical Mosques and Shrines Fund Cess Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the raising of funds for the repair, maintenance and endowment of mosques and shrines of historical importance in the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab, except the Tribal Areas
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance imposes a cess on land revenue and urban immovable property tax to fund the repair and maintenance of historical mosques and shrines in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Historical Mosques and Shrines Fund Cess Ordinance, 1960 establishes a mechanism to raise funds for the repair, maintenance, and endowment of historically significant mosques and shrines in the Punjab. It imposes a specific cess on land revenue and urban immovable property tax payable by Muslims within the province. The collected funds are managed under a designated authority and used to cover operational expenses, salaries, and construction or restoration costs. The Ordinance also empowers the Government to make rules regarding the collection of the cess and the administration of the fund.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Vocational Training Council Act, 1998
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Vocational Training Council.
repeals: The Punjab Vocational Training Council Ordinance, 1998 (XXII of 1998)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Vocational Training Council to regulate vocational training institutes in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the establishment of the Punjab Vocational Training Council as a body corporate with perpetual succession. The Council is responsible for setting up, administering, and regulating Vocational Training Institutes across the country. It outlines the constitution of the Council, including ex-officio members from government departments and private sector representatives, along with provisions for its fund, budget, and powers to make rules and regulations.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Zakat and Ushr Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provisions relating to assessment, collection and disbursement of Zakat and Ushr in the Punjab.
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab, Zakat and Ushr Department
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the assessment, collection, and disbursement of Zakat and Ushr in the Province of Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Zakat and Ushr Act, 2018 establishes a legal framework for assessing and collecting Zakat and Ushr specifically within the Punjab province. It creates three tiers of administrative bodies: the Punjab Zakat and Ushr Council, District Committees, and Local Committees to manage these funds. The Act defines specific rates for agricultural produce and livestock, outlines deduction mechanisms from financial assets, and mandates that these funds be disbursed through banks or post offices to eligible recipients.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Vegetable Market (Lahore) (Repeal) Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the Punjab Vegetable Market (Lahore) Ordinance, 1963.
repeals: The Punjab Vegetable Market (Lahore) Ordinance, 1963
metadata.one_line: Repeals the Punjab Vegetable Market (Lahore) Ordinance, 1963 as its objectives are fulfilled.
metadata.summary: This Act repeals the Punjab Vegetable Market (Lahore) Ordinance, 1963 because the original Ordinance's objectives have been achieved. It ensures that any actions taken under the repealed Ordinance remain valid despite the repeal. The Act comes into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: Punjab Finance Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize the structure of sales tax on services in Punjab.
amends: Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act, 2012
metadata.max_penalty: up to one million rupees; sealing of business premises for up to one month in case of three acts of commission or omission
metadata.one_line: This Act amends the Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act, 2012 to rationalize sales tax structure and define tax-free services in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Finance Act, 2025 was enacted by the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab to rationalize the structure of sales tax on services within the province. It amends the Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act, 2012 by inserting new sections, substituting existing clauses, and defining specific categories of tax-free services such as healthcare, education, and public transport provided by government bodies. The Act also updates penalty structures for non-compliance with digital payment requirements and revises tax rates for various service sectors.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Horticulture Authority Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of the Punjab Horticulture Authority.
repeals: The Parks and Horticulture Authority Act, 2012 (XLVII of 2012)
sub-sections (2) to (6) of section 10 of the Lahore Development Authority Act, 1975 (XXX of 1975)
section 28 and section 29 of the Lahore Development Authority Act, 1975 (XXX of 1975)
clause (xvi) of sub-section (2) of section 7 of the Punjab Development of Cities Act, 1976 (XIX of 1976)
sub-section (2) of section 27 of the Punjab Development of Cities Act, 1976 (XIX of 1976)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Horticulture Authority to regulate public parks, green belts, and advertisements in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Horticulture Authority to regulate, develop, and maintain public parks, green belts, and green areas within the province. It also governs the installation of billboards, sky signs, and outdoor advertisements, as well as the maintenance of these green spaces. The Act defines various terms related to land use and advertising, sets up an Agency structure for specific districts, and repeals previous legislation regarding parks and horticulture authorities.

name: PUNJAB PRIMARY AND SECONDARY HEALTHCARE SERVICES ACT 2025

metadata.short_title: Punjab Primary and Secondary Healthcare Services Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide the mechanism for provision of healthcare services, as well as operation and management of primary and secondary healthcare facilities
establishes: Maryam Nawaz Community Health Services Programme
metadata.administering_body: Health and Population Department, Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Establishes a framework for primary and secondary healthcare services, facilities, and digital systems in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act provides a mechanism for delivering primary and secondary healthcare services across Punjab through a structured network of clinics, hospitals, and community health inspectors. It establishes specific facility types including Maryam Nawaz Health Clinics and Hospitals, outlines the hiring of health managers via outsourcing, and mandates digitalization of records and referral systems. The legislation defines key roles such as Community Health Inspectors and medical practitioners, grants powers to the Department for rule-making, and ensures legal indemnity for officials acting in good faith.

name: PUNJAB PUBLIC AWARENESS AND DISSEMINATION OF INFORMATION ACT 2025

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Public Awareness and Dissemination of Information Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to disseminate public awareness regarding Government projects, initiatives, programs and policies for ensuring access to information, participation of public and transparency in respect thereof.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have come into force from the 1st January 2024
metadata.administering_body: Information and Culture Department of the Government
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates public awareness campaigns regarding government projects to ensure transparency and public participation in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Public Awareness and Dissemination of Information Act, 2025 establishes a framework for disseminating information about government projects, initiatives, programs, and policies. It empowers the Government or public bodies to launch public awareness campaigns through various advertising agencies including digital media, television, and print. The Act defines eligibility criteria for advertising agencies, outlines parameters for campaigns such as project funding and timelines, and sets up complaint redressal forums with the Director General as the primary decision-maker.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Public Private Partnership Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for promotion of Public Private Partnerships in Punjab.
repeals: The Punjab Public Private Partnership Act, 2019
metadata.one_line: Establishes an Authority to promote and regulate Public Private Partnerships in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the promotion of Public Private Partnerships (PPPs) within the Province of Punjab. It establishes a dedicated Authority, defines key terms related to bidding and contracts, and outlines the functions of implementing agencies. The legislation includes provisions for risk management, transparency, dispute resolution, and financial mechanisms like viability gap funds, while repealing the previous 2019 Act.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Sahulat Bazaars Authority Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Punjab Sahulat Bazaars Authority.
metadata.administering_body: Food Safety and Consumer Protection Department
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Sahulat Bazaars Authority to regulate Sahulat Bazaars and supply essential commodities in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Sahulat Bazaars Authority to launch, construct, monitor, regulate, and maintain Sahulat Bazaars across Punjab. The Authority is empowered to supply essential commodities at notified rates and create business opportunities for entrepreneurs. It defines the composition of the Authority, its powers regarding land acquisition, fund management, and rule-making, while providing indemnity to its officials.

metadata.short_title: Punjab Spatial Planning Authority Act 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Punjab Spatial Planning Authority.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Spatial Planning Authority to regulate land use and ensure balanced growth through spatial planning.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Spatial Planning Authority as a body corporate to oversee balanced growth and sustainable development in the province. The Authority is responsible for preparing master plans, regional plans, and district zoning structures while harmonizing laws related to land use. It includes members from various provincial departments and empowers the Authority to frame regulations and make rules for its operations.

metadata.short_title: Punjab Specialized Medical Institutions Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to improve medical education, responsiveness and quality of clinical care for patients in an effective, efficient and accountable manner.
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes Specialized Medical Institutions in Punjab to improve medical education and clinical care quality.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Specialized Medical Institutions Act, 2025 was enacted by the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab to enhance medical education, responsiveness, and the quality of clinical care. It empowers the Government to notify specific medical colleges or teaching hospitals as Specialized Medical Institutions, which shall function as bodies corporate with perpetual succession. The Act establishes a Board of Governors comprising government secretaries, the Dean, and private sector members to administer the affairs of these institutions. Key mechanisms include the constitution of a Search and Nomination Committee for appointments, strict budgetary controls audited by the Auditor General, and the power to frame regulations and rules for effective healthcare management.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Thalassemia Prevention Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provisions for the control and prevention of Thalassemia and other genetic orders.
metadata.administering_body: Specialized Healthcare and Medical Education Department
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes an Advisory Council to control and prevent Thalassemia in Punjab through testing, counseling, and regulation.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Thalassemia Prevention Act, 2025 is enacted to control and prevent Thalassemia and other genetic disorders within the province. It establishes an Advisory Council comprising government officials, health experts, and educational representatives to oversee genetic counseling, testing facilities, and data management. The Act empowers the Council to regulate laboratories, set test rates, and ensure quality control while mandating early diagnosis and prevention measures for students and the general public.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Privatization Board (Repeal) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the Punjab Privatization Board Act 2010
repeals: The Punjab Privatization Board Act, 2010
metadata.status_evidence: The Punjab Privatization Board Act 2010 (IV of 2010) is hereby repealed.
metadata.administering_body: Colonies Department, Board of Revenue, Punjab
metadata.one_line: Repeals the Punjab Privatization Board Act 2010 and transfers its assets and staff to the Colonies Department.
metadata.summary: This Act repeals the Punjab Privatization Board Act 2010. It provides for the immediate transfer of all properties, moveable assets, employees, and ongoing proceedings from the defunct Privatization Board to the Colonies Department, Board of Revenue, Punjab.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Protected Areas Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the protection, preservation, conservation and management of ecologically important areas.
repeals: Punjab Wildlife (Protection, Preservation, Conservation and Management) Act, 1974
metadata.administering_body: Forestry, Wildlife and Fisheries Department of the Government
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the protection, preservation, conservation and management of ecologically important areas in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Protected Areas Act, 2020 establishes a legal framework to protect, preserve, conserve, and manage ecologically important areas within the province. It empowers the Government to declare various categories of protected areas, including national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, and wetlands, and sets out functions for management authorities. The Act also defines key terms, outlines offences related to these areas, and repeals specific sections of the 1974 Wildlife Protection Act.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to levy, alter and rationalize certain taxes and duties in the Punjab.
amends: The Punjab Revenue Authority Act, 2012 (XLIII of 2012)
metadata.one_line: This Act levies and rationalizes taxes in Punjab while amending the Stamp Act 1899 and Punjab Revenue Authority Act 2012.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Finance Act 2018 was enacted to levy, alter, and rationalize certain taxes and duties within the province of Punjab. It comes into force on November 1, 2018, and applies to the whole of Punjab. The Act primarily functions as an amendment instrument, updating schedules in the Stamp Act 1899 regarding stamp duties on various instruments like contracts, insurance policies, and deeds, while also amending sections of the Punjab Revenue Authority Act 2012.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Power Development Board Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Power Development Board for the implementation of policies of the Government to facilitate the private investors in power sector and to harness the energy generation resources in the Province.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Power Development Board to facilitate private investment in power projects and harness energy resources.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Power Development Board as a body corporate to implement government policies in the energy sector. The Board is tasked with facilitating private investors, coordinating power generation activities, and exploring various energy sources including hydel, coal, solar, wind, and biomass. It also manages funds, audits accounts, and issues necessary permissions for water and land use related to power projects.

name: PUNJAB REVISION OF EMOLUMENTS OF PUBLIC REPRESENTATIVES ACT 1995

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Revision of Emoluments of Public Representatives Act, 1995
metadata.long_title: An Act to revise the salaries and other emoluments of the holders of representative offices relating to the Punjab.
amends: The Punjab Provincial Assembly (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges of Members) Act, 1974
The Punjab Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
The Punjab Provincial Assembly Speaker (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Revises salaries and allowances for Punjab public representatives including members, ministers, and the deputy speaker.
metadata.summary: This Act revises the salaries, allowances, and privileges of holders of representative offices in the Punjab. It amends existing legislation governing the emoluments of Provincial Assembly members, Ministers, and the Deputy Speaker. The amendments update specific monetary figures for daily allowances, travel fares, sumptuary allowances, and other benefits to reflect revised rates.

metadata.short_title: The Land Acquisition (West Pakistan Amendment) Ordinance, 1969
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, in its application to the Province of West Pakistan
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan, except the Tribal Areas
repeals: the Land Acquisition (N.W.F.P. Amendment) Act, 1947
the Land Acquisition (N.W.F.P. Amendment) Act, 1952
the Land Acquisition (Punjab Amendment) Act, 1952
the Land Acquisition (Punjab Amendment) Act, 1954
the Land Acquisition (Bahawalpur State Amendment) Act, 1954
the Land Acquisition (West Pakistan Amendment) Act, 1958
metadata.one_line: Amends the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 for West Pakistan and repeals earlier provincial amendments.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 to apply specifically to the Province of West Pakistan. It repeals several previous amendment acts related to N.W.F.P., Punjab, Bahawalpur, and the previous West Pakistan amendment. The text modifies various sections regarding public notices, court jurisdiction, compensation procedures, and restrictions on land transfers by companies.

metadata.short_title: The Land Acquisition (West Pakistan Amendment) Act, 1969
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 in its application to the Province of West Pakistan
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan except the Tribal Areas
metadata.one_line: Amends the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 regarding interest rates and waiver rights in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 specifically for its application to the Province of West Pakistan. It substitutes the rate of interest on excess compensation from six percent to eight percent compound interest and adds a proviso preventing land owners from waiving this right via agreement. The amendments apply to sections 28 and 34 of the 1894 Act, excluding the Tribal Areas.

metadata.short_title: The Land Acquisition (West Pakistan Amendment) Ordinance, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, in its application to the Province of West Pakistan
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan, except the Tribal Areas
metadata.parent_law: The Land Acquisition Act, 1894
key_definitions: said Act (referring to the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 in its application to West Pakistan)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 for West Pakistan by substituting Provincial Government for Commissioner and adding public purpose clauses.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 specifically for its application to the Province of West Pakistan. It substitutes 'Provincial Government' for 'Commissioner' in relevant sections and adds a new clause regarding land acquisition for company works serving a public purpose. The Ordinance extends to the whole of West Pakistan except the Tribal Areas and came into force immediately upon promulgation by the Governor.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967 to align with the Punjab Land Records Authority Act 2017.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967 to harmonize it with the Punjab Land Records Authority Act 2017. It introduces new clauses regarding the Arazi Record Centre and updates references from Service Centre Officials to the Arazi Record Centre throughout the parent Act. The legislation also modifies provisions related to fees for computerized land records and reporting requirements for land acquisitions.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Drugs (Amendment) Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Drugs Act, 1976, in its application to Province of the Punjab, for control and eradication of spurious, adulterated and substandard drugs.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Drugs Act, 1976 to strengthen control over spurious and substandard drugs in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Drugs Act, 1976 specifically for its application to the Province of Punjab. Its primary purpose is to address the increasing menace of spurious, adulterated, and substandard drugs by updating enforcement mechanisms and monitoring systems. The legislation introduces new provisions for Provincial Drugs Monitoring Teams, establishes independent inspection powers, and defines specific terms like 'Notified Drugs Laboratory' and 'sub-standard drug'. It also grants the Provincial Government powers to delegate functions and imposes stricter penalties.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend certain laws of the Punjab to harmonize them with the Local Government system envisaged under Punjab Local Government Act 2013.
amends: The Punjab Prohibition of Smoking in Cinema Houses Ordinance, 1960
Punjab Tolls on Roads and Bridges Ordinance, 1962
The Punjab Recovery of Cost (Copies of Essential Revenue Records) Ordinance, 1963
The Punjab Autonomous Bodies Immovable Property (Ejectment of Unauthorized Occupants) Ordinance, 1965
The Punjab Acquisition of Land (Housing) (Repeal) Act, 1985
The Lahore Ring Road Authority Act, 2011
The Parks and Horticulture Authority Act, 2012
The Punjab Security of Vulnerable Establishments Act, 2016
repeals: The Punjab Acquisition of Land (Housing) (Repeal) Act, 1985
metadata.one_line: Amends various Punjab laws to align administrative terms with the Punjab Local Government Act 2013.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends specific laws of the Punjab to harmonize them with the local government system established under the Punjab Local Government Act 2013. It substitutes terms like 'Executive District Officer' with 'Commissioner' or 'Deputy Commissioner' and updates definitions of local authorities and urban areas across multiple statutes. The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor because the Provincial Assembly was not in session, taking immediate effect upon promulgation.

name: INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY OF THE PUNJAB ORDINANCE 2015

metadata.short_title: The Infrastructure Development Authority of the Punjab Ordinance, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for founding Infrastructure Development Authority of the Punjab.
repeals: The Punjab Highways Authority Act, 1989 (V of 1989)
establishes: Infrastructure Development Authority of the Punjab
metadata.max_penalty: Five thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Infrastructure Development Authority of the Punjab for planning and maintaining infrastructure in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Infrastructure Development Authority of the Punjab to plan, design, construct, and maintain infrastructure within the province. It defines the composition of the Authority, including ex-officio members like the Chief Minister and various Secretaries, as well as appointed technical experts. The document outlines the Authority's functions, financial management, powers regarding land acquisition and ejection of unauthorized occupants, and specifies offences related to road usage with associated fines.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Development of Cities (Amendment) Ordinance, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Development of Cities Act, 1976.
amends: The Punjab Development of Cities Act, 1976
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Development of Cities Act, 1976 to update definitions, authority composition, and local government references.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Development of Cities Act, 1976 to align it with newer local government legislation. It updates definitions within the Act, alters the composition of the Authority to include specific government representatives, and substitutes references to the Punjab Local Government Act 2013. The document also omits certain sections and words related to City Districts and modifies provisions regarding land acquisition and offences.

metadata.short_title: The Lahore Development Authority (Amendment) Ordinance, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Lahore Development Authority Act, 1975.
metadata.parent_law: The Lahore Development Authority Act, 1975
establishes: Commission on issues on issues of bona fide purchasers, illegal schemes and illegal constructions
metadata.one_line: Amends the Lahore Development Authority Act, 1975 to expand jurisdiction and establish a commission for illegal constructions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Lahore Development Authority Act, 1975 to extend its jurisdiction from the metropolitan area of Lahore to the entire area of Lahore Division. It substitutes various definitions and sections within the parent Act to align with the new territorial scope. Additionally, it establishes a Commission to address issues regarding bona fide purchasers, illegal schemes, and illegal constructions, providing mechanisms for regularization and recommendations on fines or demolition.

name: PUNJAB PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP FOR INFRASTRUCTURE ACT 2010

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Public-Private Partnership for Infrastructure Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to create an enabling environment for private sector participation in infrastructure development in the Punjab through public-private partnership projects.
repeals: The Punjab Public Private Partnership Act, 2014
metadata.status_evidence: This Act was passed by the Punjab Assembly on 12 July 2010; assented to by the Governor of the Punjab on 19 July 2010; and published in the Punjab Gazette (Extraordinary), dated 20 July 2010, pages 203-215, and repealed by the Punjab Public Private Partnership Act, 2014 (IX of 2014), w.e.f. 29.5.2014
metadata.repealed_by: The Punjab Public Private Partnership Act, 2014
metadata.one_line: Establishes a framework for public-private partnerships to develop infrastructure in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act creates an enabling environment for private sector participation in infrastructure development within the Province of Punjab. It establishes institutional arrangements including a PPP Steering Committee, a PPP Cell, and a Risk Management Unit to oversee projects. The legislation outlines a comprehensive project delivery process covering identification, approval, bidding, agreement negotiation, implementation, and termination, while defining various partnership models such as BOT, BOOT, and MC.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the constitution, powers and functions of local governments in the Province of the Punjab and matters connected therewith.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the framework for local governments, councils, and administration in Punjab with defined powers and functions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the structure, composition, and functions of local governments at various levels including District, Tehsil, Town, Union, Village, and Neighbourhood Councils within the Province of Punjab. It defines the roles of Nazims, councils, and administrative officers while outlining fiscal mechanisms, decentralization processes, and dispute resolution through Musalihat Anjuman. The law also sets up the Provincial Finance Commission to oversee fiscal transfers and ensures local governments operate within a provincial framework.

metadata.short_title: The Companies Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to consolidate and amend the law relating to companies.
repeals: The Companies Act, 1956
establishes: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
metadata.max_penalty: Imprisonment and fine (specific amounts not stated in excerpts)
metadata.administering_body: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends the law relating to companies, covering incorporation, shares, prospectus, and winding up.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance consolidates and amends the law relating to companies in Pakistan. It covers preliminary matters, court jurisdiction, the Securities and Exchange Commission, company incorporation, share capital, prospectus regulations, and winding up procedures. The text also includes provisions for non-banking finance companies and amendments to previous ordinances.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Small Cause Courts Act, 1887
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Courts of Small Causes
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates and amends the law relating to Courts of Small Causes in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Provincial Small Cause Courts Act, 1887 establishes Courts of Small Causes within the territories under the administration of the Provincial Government. It defines their jurisdiction, outlines the appointment of judges and registrars, and details the procedure for admitting plaints, passing decrees, and executing them. The Act also specifies suits excluded from the cognizance of these courts and provides for appeals and revisions against their orders.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Development of Cities (Amendment) Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Development of Cities Act, 1976.
amends: The Punjab Development of Cities Act, 1976
repeals: The Lahore Development of Cities (Amendment) Ordinance, 2014
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Development of Cities Act, 1976 to update definitions, authority composition, and repeal a specific ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Development of Cities Act, 1976 to align it with newer local government legislation. key_definitions: immovable property paying revenue to Government
metadata.one_line: Amends the Partition Act, 1893 by substituting 'the Punjab' for 'Pakistan' and defining agricultural land.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Partition Act, 1893 to align its provisions with the current context of the Province. It substitutes the word 'Pakistan' with 'the Punjab' in section 1, sub-section (2) of the 1893 Act. Additionally, it replaces the phrase 'immovable property paying revenue to Government' with 'agricultural land' in section 1, sub-section (4). The Act was passed by the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab and came into force immediately upon enactment.

name: THE WEST PAKISTAN BORDER AREA REGULATION 1959 (PUNJAB AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1981

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Border Area Regulation 1959 (Punjab Amendment) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the West Pakistan Border Area Regulation 1959 (MLR-9 of 1959)
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
amends: The West Pakistan Border Area Regulation 1959 (MLR-9 of 1959)
metadata.one_line: Amends the West Pakistan Border Area Regulation 1959 to apply specific terms and powers to the Province of Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the West Pakistan Border Area Regulation 1959 specifically for its application to the Province of Punjab. It substitutes various definitions within the original Regulation, such as 'West Pakistan' becoming 'the Province of the Punjab', and updates references to rehabilitation schemes and property types. The text also modifies the composition of committees handling land matters and clarifies procedures for surrendering unauthorized occupation of state or evacuee property.

metadata.short_title: The Land Reforms (Punjab Amendment) Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Land Reforms Regulation, 1972
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
repeals: Punjab Ordinance Temporary Enactment Act, 1973
metadata.one_line: Amends the Land Reforms Regulation, 1972 regarding land ceilings, transfers, and civil service ownership in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Land Reforms Regulation, 1972 (M.L.R. No. 115) to further regulate land ownership and transfer in the Province of Punjab. It introduces specific provisions restricting gifts of land by certain persons while exempting transfers to heirs or widowed sisters, and sets limits on additional land acquisition for owners of tractors or tubewells. The Act also modifies rules regarding joint holding partitions, civil service land eligibility, and validates actions taken under a previous Ordinance.

name: CANAL AND DRAINAGE (WEST PAKISTAN SECOND AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1970

metadata.short_title: The Canal and Drainage Act (West Pakistan Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1970
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Canal and Drainage Act, 1873, in its application to the Province of West Pakistan
metadata.parent_law: Canal and Drainage Act, 1873
metadata.one_line: Amends the Canal and Drainage Act, 1873 regarding cost allocation and rates for lands in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Canal and Drainage Act, 1873 specifically as it applies to the Province of West Pakistan. It omits certain words from section 57 regarding cost statements and substitutes a new section 59 concerning annual rates on benefitted lands. The amendment allows for charges on land owners based on rules made by the Provincial Government, with a proviso exempting agricultural land from rates for the first two harvests after scheme completion.

name: PUNJAB SOIL RECLAMATION (WEST PAKISTAN AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1964
