metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Soil Reclamation Act, 1952 to apply to West Pakistan and updates board composition.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Soil Reclamation Act, 1952 to extend its application to the whole of West Pakistan. It substitutes references to 'Punjab' with 'West Pakistan', renames the governing body to the West Pakistan Land and Water Development Board, and updates definitions related to irrigation and land reclamation. The Ordinance also ensures the continuance of actions taken by the previous Soil Reclamation Board.

metadata.short_title: Pakistan Penal Code
metadata.long_title: XLV of 1860
metadata.max_penalty: death
metadata.one_line: The Pakistan Penal Code defines offences, punishments, and general exceptions applicable throughout Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act serves as the primary criminal code for Pakistan, defining various offences and their corresponding punishments. It establishes general explanations regarding terms like 'person', 'offence', and 'good faith', while also outlining exceptions such as private defence and acts done by children or persons of unsound mind. The Code applies to citizens and service members both within and beyond Pakistan's borders.

metadata.short_title: Zakat and Ushr Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make provisions relating to the assessment, collection and disbursement of Zakat and Ushr
establishes: Tehsil, Taluqa or Sub-divisional Zakat and Ushr Committee
metadata.administering_body: Secretary, Religious Affairs, Zakat and Ushr Division, Government of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance provides for the assessment, collection, and disbursement of Zakat and Ushr in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Zakat and Ushr Ordinance, 1980 establishes the legal framework for assessing and collecting Zakat and Ushr from Muslim citizens in Pakistan. It creates various administrative bodies including Central and Provincial Zakat Councils to oversee the collection and disbursement of funds to assist the needy. The Ordinance specifies rates for livestock and other assets according to Shariah principles and allows for exemptions or declarations by individuals who do not believe they are obligated to pay.

name: PUNJAB AGRICULTURE, FOOD AND DRUG AUTHORITY ORDINANCE 2016

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Agriculture, Food and Drug Authority Ordinance, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish the Punjab Agriculture, Food and Drug Authority for forensic examination and testing of fertilizer, pesticide, food and drug.
establishes: Punjab Agriculture, Food and Drug Authority
metadata.max_penalty: five hundred thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Agriculture, Food and Drug Authority for forensic testing of fertilizers, pesticides, food, and drugs.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Punjab Agriculture, Food and Drug Authority to conduct forensic examinations and quality testing of fertilizers, pesticides, food, and drugs. The Authority is a body corporate comprising ex-officio members from various government departments and appointed experts. It has the power to render expert opinions on ingredients and quality, maintain records, and frame regulations. The Ordinance also defines offences related to its functions, establishes an appeal mechanism to the Lahore High Court, and outlines procedures for fund management and annual performance reporting.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Seed Corporation (Amendment) Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Seed Corporation Act, 1976.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Seed Corporation Act, 1976 regarding board composition and management appointments.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Seed Corporation Act, 1976 to update the composition of the Board and the appointment process for the Managing Director. It substitutes specific sections to replace references to the Government with the Chief Minister and adjusts the number of members in certain subsections. The changes include adding new categories of board members from the private sector, universities, and farming communities, while ensuring representation for women.

name: PUNJAB PRICE CONTROL OF ESSENTIAL COMMODITIES (AMENDMENT) ACT 2025

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Price Control of Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act, 2025

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Price Control of Essential Commodities Act, 2024 to update the composition of the Price Control Council. It substitutes specific members in section 3, adding various government secretaries and representatives while defining the Directorate General as the council's secretariat. Additionally, it modifies section 5 to replace a department name with 'Price Control and Commodities Management Department'.

name: THE PREVENTION OF ANTI-NATIONAL ACTIVITIES ACT, 1974

metadata.short_title: The Prevention of Anti-National Activities Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the more effective prevention of certain anti-national and treasonable activities
repeals: The Prevention of Anti-National Activities Ordinance, 1973 (XXIX of 1973)
key_definitions: secession of a part of the territory of Pakistan from the Federation
metadata.one_line: This Act prevents anti-national activities by declaring associations anti-national, establishing a Tribunal for inquiry, and imposing penalties.
metadata.summary: The Prevention of Anti-National Activities Act, 1974 provides mechanisms to prevent anti-national and treasonable activities within Pakistan. It empowers the Federal Government to declare associations as anti-national after a review by a constituted Tribunal. The Act defines specific acts constituting anti-national activities, such as inciting secession or disrupting national unity, and establishes penalties for membership in such associations or contravention of orders.

metadata.short_title: The Anti-terrorism Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the prevention of terrorism, sectarian violence and for speedy trial of heinous offences;
metadata.one_line: Provides for prevention of terrorism, sectarian violence, and speedy trial of heinous offences via Anti-terrorism Courts.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes Anti-terrorism Courts to ensure the speedy trial of heinous offences related to terrorism and sectarian violence. It defines key terms such as armed forces, civil armed forces, and explosives, and grants powers for forfeiture of property and proscription of organizations involved in terrorism. The legislation also incorporates various international conventions regarding aviation safety and hostage-taking into its framework.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Industrial Relations (Amendment) Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Industrial Relations Act 2010.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Industrial Relations Act 2010 regarding union formation, appeals, and procedural figures.
metadata.summary: This Act serves to amend specific sections of the Punjab Industrial Relations Act 2010. It allows workers to form associations without prior authorization, modifies appeal procedures in Labour Courts, and updates a numerical figure in section 12. The legislation came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Vigilance Committees Ordinance, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the constitution of Vigilance Committees.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance establishes Vigilance Committees at District, Sub-divisional and Union Council levels to ensure security and watch systems.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Vigilance Committees Ordinance, 2016 provides for the constitution of Vigilance Committees at District, Sub-divisional, and Union Council levels. These committees are designed to ensure an effective watch and ward system and deal with ancillary matters related to local security. The Ordinance outlines the specific composition, functions, meeting schedules, and logistical support required for these committees, while also defining terms such as 'proscribed organization' and establishing mechanisms to handle sectarianism and subversion.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Waqf Properties (Amendment) Act, 2026

metadata.administering_body: Government, Auqaf and Religious Affairs Department

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Waqf Properties Ordinance, 1979 to update definitions and appointment procedures for the Chief Administrator of Auqaf. It designates the Secretary to the Government, Auqaf and Religious Affairs Department as the Chief Administrator and vests waqf properties in him. The Act also mandates that no person shall be appointed unless they are a Muslim.

metadata.short_title: The Charitable Funds (Regulation of Collections) Act, 1953
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the regulation, administration and accounting of collections of charitable donations and for the prevention of frauds.

metadata.one_line: Regulates the collection and administration of charitable donations to prevent fraud.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the regulation, administration, and accounting of collections of charitable donations. It aims to prevent frauds associated with such collections by defining private and charitable funds, promoters, collectors, and recipients. The legislation mandates declarations for collections, requires sanctioning authority approval, and establishes penalties for contraventions.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Punjab Tourism, Culture and Heritage Authority to promote travel, tourism, and the preservation of heritage, landscape, and culture in the Punjab. It defines the composition of the Authority, including members from various government departments and local bodies, and outlines its functions such as managing specified areas and conserving properties. The document also creates a Tourism Squad for security and assistance at tourist destinations and provides for offences, penalties, and administrative procedures like rules and regulations.

metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Tourism, Culture and Heritage Authority to promote tourism and heritage in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Tourism, Culture and Heritage Authority to promote travel, tourism, and the preservation of heritage, landscape, and culture within the Punjab. The Authority is a body corporate with specific powers to enter contracts and manage property, composed of ex-officio members including the Chief Minister and various Secretaries, as well as nominated experts. It functions in collaboration with concerned government departments to develop eco-tourism, frame regulations for housing projects, and provide facilities for tourists. Additionally, the Act creates a Tourism Squad to ensure security and assist visitors, while providing indemnity to Authority members acting in good faith.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Disposal of Land by Development Authorities (Regulation) Act, 1998. It updates the definition of 'Development Authority' to include specific bodies like the Lahore Development Authority and others notified by the Government. Furthermore, it revises Section 4 to specify new percentages for land disposal via open auction or allotment by ballot for defence personnel, police, government servants, minorities, and destitutes based on plot size.

metadata.short_title: Namal Institute Mianwali Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Namal Institute Mianwali.

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Namal Institute Mianwali as a body corporate in the private sector located at Mianwali. The Institute is authorized to provide instruction in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Sciences, and other non-medical branches approved by the Board and Patron. It creates various governing bodies including the Board of Governors, Academic Council, Selection Board, and Finance and Planning Committee to manage its academic, administrative, and financial affairs.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government Act, 2019
repeals: The Punjab Local Government Act, 1995
metadata.one_line: An Act to provide for the constitution, functioning, elections, and responsibilities of local governments in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the framework for local governments in Punjab, defining their structure, composition, and functions. It outlines procedures for elections, including the role of the Election Commission and Tribunals, and details the duties of various functionaries like councillors and Chief Officers. The legislation also covers joint authorities, public service delivery standards, and includes provisions for offences and penalties related to local governance.

metadata.short_title: Rawalpindi Medical University Ordinance, 2017

metadata.summary: This Ordinance reconstitutes Rawalpindi Medical College into Rawalpindi Medical University to upgrade medical education and encourage research. It establishes the university as a body corporate with perpetual succession, defining its functions, internal authorities like the Syndicate and Academic Council, and financial provisions including the University Fund. The law also outlines the appointment of officers, governance structures, and mechanisms for appeals and indemnity.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Land Records Authority Ordinance, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Land Records Authority for reform and modernization of the system of land records.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Punjab Land Records Authority to reform and modernize the system of land records. It aims to improve service delivery, ensure long-lasting tenure security, and handle ancillary matters related to land management. The Authority is a body corporate with powers to manage land records, frame policies, and advise the Government on modernization. It also provides for the transfer of assets, staff, and functions from the existing Project Management Unit (PMU) to the new Authority.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Compulsory Primary Education Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for compulsory primary education in the Province of the Punjab.
repeals: The Punjab Primary Education Ordinance, 1962 (XXIX of 1962)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to one month or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act mandates compulsory primary education for children aged five to ten in Punjab and establishes authorities to enforce attendance.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Compulsory Primary Education Act, 1994 provides for compulsory primary education for all children between the ages of five and ten years in the Province of the Punjab. It defines key terms such as 'child', 'parent', 'primary school', and 'primary education' to clarify the scope of the law. The Act empowers the Government to constitute School Attendance Authorities responsible for ensuring every child attends a primary school, even if parents fail to do so without reasonable excuse. Offences are established for parents or employers who fail to comply with attendance orders after receiving warnings, punishable by fines and imprisonment.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance consolidates and amends the law relating to the preparation and sale of foods in the province of Punjab. It prohibits the sale of adulterated, misbranded, or unwholesome food and establishes requirements for licenses, inspections, and analysis by appointed officials. The document outlines various offences related to false warranties, mixing food, and unsanitary conditions, along with corresponding penalties and procedures for prosecution.
