metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Local Government Act, 2019.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Punjab other than the areas notified as cantonments under the Cantonments Act, 1924 (II of 1924), or the Cantonments Ordinance, 2002 (CXXXVII of 2002), and such other areas under active possession and direct control of the Armed Forces of Pakistan
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Local Government Act, 2019
repeals: The Village Panchayats and Neighbourhood Councils Act, 2019
metadata.status_evidence: This Ordinance was Promulgated by Governor of the Punjab on 03 February 2021; and was published in the Punjab Gazette (Extraordinary), dated: 03 February 2021, pp. 5545-5615; and was repealed on 03.05.2021 at the expiration of its period in terms of Article 128 of the Constitution
metadata.repealed_by: Article 128 of the Constitution (at the expiration of its period)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Local Government Act, 2019 to establish an effective local government system and abolish certain town committees.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Local Government Act, 2019 to empower decision-making at the grassroots level and improve service delivery. It abolishes Town Committees with populations under fifty thousand in Metropolitan Corporations and merges their areas into Tehsil Councils. The document also defines terms like 'bye-laws' and 'Chief Officer', amends various sections of the parent Act, and repeals the Village Panchayats and Neighbourhood Councils Act, 2019.

metadata.short_title: The Times Institute, Multan (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Times Institute, Multan Act 2020.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Times Institute, Multan Act 2020 to rename it as Times University and update governance structures.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Times Institute, Multan Act 2020 to change the institution's name from 'Times Institute' to 'Times University'. It updates various sections regarding the establishment of faculties, appointment of the Vice Chancellor, composition of the Board, and restrictions on opening sub-campuses. The legislation also adds a new section granting emergency powers to the Chief Executive.

name: PUNJAB AUTONOMOUS BODIES IMMOVABLE PROPERTY (EJECTMENT OF UNAUTHORIZED OCCUPANTS) ORDINANCE, 1965

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Autonomous Bodies Immovable Property (Ejectment of Unauthorized Occupants) Ordinance, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for summary ejectment of unauthorized occupants of immovable property vesting in autonomous bodies.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of [the Punjab], except the Tribal Areas
metadata.one_line: Provides for summary ejectment of unauthorized occupants from property owned by autonomous bodies in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides a legal framework for the summary ejectment of unauthorized occupants from immovable property vested in autonomous bodies. It defines key terms such as 'autonomous body' and 'unauthorized occupant' to clarify who is covered under the law. The document establishes an appellate mechanism for challenging eviction orders and allows for the requisition of police assistance to carry out evictions. Additionally, it bars civil courts from passing injunctions restraining autonomous bodies from executing eviction orders under this Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Civil Administration Ordinance, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to institute a comprehensive system of civil administration in the Punjab for efficient administration and improved service delivery to the people.
metadata.commencement: on and from the day the Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 2001 (XIII of 2001) is repealed
metadata.one_line: Institutes a comprehensive system of civil administration in Punjab for efficient governance and service delivery.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes a comprehensive system of civil administration across the Punjab to ensure efficient administration and improved service delivery. It defines the roles, functions, and powers of Commissioners, Deputy Commissioners, and Assistant Commissioners within Divisions, Districts, and Tehsils. The document also creates mechanisms for coordination, transparency, grievance redress through Divisional Boards, and financial accountability via District Accounts.

name: PUNJAB IMMOVABLE PUBLIC PROPERTIES (REMOVAL OF ENCROACHMENT) ORDINANCE 2022

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Immovable Public Properties (Removal of Encroachment) Ordinance, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for removal of encroachment from public properties.
repeals: The Punjab Autonomous Bodies Immovable Property (Ejectment of Unauthorized Occupants) Ordinance, 1965
The Punjab Government Lands and Buildings (Recovery of Possession) Ordinance, 1966
metadata.status_evidence: This Ordinance was Promulgated by Governor of the Punjab on 17 January 2022; and was published in the Punjab Gazette (Extraordinary), dated: 19 January 2022, pp. 3641-3646; and was repealed on 18.04.2022 at the expiration of its period in terms of Article 128 of the Constitution of Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab / Board of Revenue, Punjab
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance provides for the removal of encroachments from public properties in Punjab through eviction and demolition.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab to address the immediate need for removing encroachments from public properties when the Provincial Assembly was not in session. It defines key terms such as 'unauthorized occupant' and 'public property', and establishes a procedure involving show cause notices, personal hearings, and orders for vacation and removal of structures. The Ordinance empowers authorized officers to direct unauthorized occupants to vacate land and remove structures, while also creating Enforcement Squads under the Board's control to execute these duties.

metadata.short_title: Protection of Economic Reforms Act, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for furtherance and protection of Economic Reforms
metadata.one_line: This Act protects economic reforms by ensuring freedom in foreign currency, banking secrecy, and investment security across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Protection of Economic Reforms Act, 1992 was enacted to create a liberal environment for savings and investments in Pakistan. It provides legal protection to various economic reforms introduced since November 7, 1990, including privatization and deregulation. The Act overrides conflicting provisions in other laws regarding foreign exchange, taxation, and customs to ensure the continuity of these reforms.

metadata.short_title: The University of Murree Ordinance, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the University of Murree.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the University of Murree and provides for its incorporation, functions, finances, and governance structure.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the University of Murree in the public interest to provide instruction in geology, geography, forestry, and other branches of learning. It incorporates the University as a body corporate with perpetual succession, defining its powers to award degrees, conduct research, and manage property. The document outlines the composition of the University, including the Chancellor, Vice Chancellor, and Syndicate, while also setting up the University Fund and mechanisms for appeals and indemnity.

metadata.short_title: Faisalabad Medical University Ordinance 2017
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of Faisalabad Medical University
establishes: Board of Advanced Studies and Research
metadata.one_line: Establishes Faisalabad Medical University to upgrade medical education and research in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance reconstitutes Punjab Medical College Faisalabad as Faisalabad Medical University to improve medical education and research. It establishes a corporate body with perpetual succession, defining its structure including the Chancellor, Vice Chancellor, Syndicate, and Academic Council. The document outlines functions such as imparting medical knowledge, conducting examinations, awarding degrees, managing finances, and regulating staff appointments and student access.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Drugs (Amendment) Ordinance, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Drugs Act, 1976.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment of ten years and fine of five million rupees
metadata.one_line: Amends the Drugs Act, 1976 to strengthen penalties for spurious drugs and improve enforcement mechanisms in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Drugs Act, 1976 to address the menace of spurious drugs through stricter penalties and improved enforcement. It introduces new definitions for foreign drug authorities, modifies licensing suspension powers, and adjusts timelines for investigations and appeals. The amendments also clarify the roles of Provincial Quality Control Boards and Drug Courts in prosecuting drug-related offences.

metadata.short_title: NUR International University Lahore Ordinance 2014
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of NUR International University Lahore.
metadata.one_line: Establishes NUR International University Lahore in the private sector with its campus in Lahore.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes NUR International University Lahore as a body corporate in the private sector located in Lahore. It defines the university's structure, including the Chancellor, Board of Governors, and Academic Council, and outlines its functions such as providing instruction, conducting examinations, and awarding degrees. The document also sets out provisions for financial management, faculty appointments, and the making of statutes and regulations to govern the university's administration.

name: PUNJAB CURRICULUM AND TEXTBOOK BOARD ORDINANCE 2014

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Curriculum and Textbook Board Ordinance, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Curriculum and Textbook Board.
repeals: The Punjab Textbook Board Ordinance, 1962 (XLI of 1962)
the West Pakistan Publication of Books Regulation and Control Ordinance, 1969 (XV of 1969)
the West Pakistan Textbook (Regulation and Control) Ordinance, 1970 (XXVII of 1970)
the Punjab Curriculum Authority Act 2012 (XXXXIX of 2012)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Curriculum and Textbook Board to formulate curricula, develop textbooks, and regulate educational materials in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Punjab Curriculum and Textbook Board as a body corporate to manage curriculum formulation, textbook development, and publication for classes I to XII. The Board consists of ex officio members from various government departments and appointed academicians, with specific powers delegated while retaining certain functions like policy decisions and budget approval with the Government. It repeals previous ordinances and acts related to textbooks in Punjab and provides for rules, regulations, audits, and penalties for offenses committed under its provisions.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government (Second Amendment) Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Local Government Ordinance 2001.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Local Government Ordinance 2001 regarding budget allocation, accounts committees, and election timelines.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Local Government Ordinance 2001 to update provisions on budget allocation for Citizen Community Boards and modify the powers of local governments. It establishes an Ad hoc Accounts Committee consisting of Provincial Assembly members and officials to audit local government finances. The Act also designates the District Coordination Officer, sets timelines for holding elections, and specifies that the new section remains in force until the next election.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Katchi Abadis (Amendment) Act, 2009
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Katchi Abadis Act, 1992.
repeals: The Punjab Katchi Abadis (Amendment) Ordinance, 2007
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Katchi Abadis Act, 1992 regarding definitions, committees, and surcharges.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Katchi Abadis Act, 1992 to update definitions of 'Government' and 'Governmental Agency'. It establishes Implementation Committees for districts and substitutes various references to local authorities with Governmental Agencies. The Act also introduces provisions for surcharges on misappropriation of funds and repeals the Punjab Katchi Abadis (Amendment) Ordinance, 2007.

name: PUNJAB GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES WELFARE FUND (AMENDMENT) ACT 2009

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Government Employees Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2009
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Government Employees Welfare Fund Ordinance, 1969.
amends: The Punjab Government Employees Welfare Fund Ordinance, 1969
repeals: The Punjab Government Employees Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance 2007 (XXII of 2007)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Government Employees Welfare Fund Ordinance, 1969 regarding definitions, boards, contributions, and assurance sums.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Government Employees Welfare Fund Ordinance, 1969 to update definitions of government servants and establish specific welfare boards. It modifies contribution rules for active and retired employees and adjusts assured amounts based on basic scales. The Act also repeals a previous 2007 amendment ordinance and validates actions taken under it.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to reconstitute the [Medical and Dental] Council in Pakistan.
key_definitions: house job or foundation year or internship
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance reconstitutes the Medical and Dental Council to regulate medical and dental professions in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the President to consolidate laws regarding the registration of medical practitioners and dentists. It establishes the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council as a body corporate with perpetual succession to set uniform minimum standards for qualifications. The document outlines the Council's powers to recognize institutions, maintain registers of practitioners, certify qualifications, and impose penalties for fraudulent representation or practicing without registration.

name: PAKISTAN COLLAGE OF PHYSICIANS AND SURGEONS ORDINANCE, 1962

metadata.short_title: Pakistan College of Physicians and Surgeons Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish a College of Physicians and Surgeons in Pakistan
establishes: Pakistan College of Physicians and Surgeons
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan College of Physicians and Surgeons to promote specialist practice and postgraduate training.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Pakistan College of Physicians and Surgeons to maintain high principles of the medical profession and promote specialist practice. It creates a corporate body with a Council consisting of Fellows appointed by the Central Government, elected by Fellows, or admitted after passing examinations. The College functions include arranging postgraduate training, conducting examinations for diplomas, providing research facilities, and organizing scientific discussions among physicians and surgeons across Pakistan.

metadata.short_title: The Sports (Development and Control) Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate the development and control of Sports
establishes: Board for the control of Sports in Pakistan
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates sports development and control across Pakistan by establishing a Board with rule-making powers.
metadata.summary: The Sports (Development and Control) Ordinance, 1962 was promulgated by the President to regulate the development and control of sports in Pakistan. It establishes one or more Boards constituted by the Central Government to promote uniform standards of competition comparable to international levels. The Ordinance grants these Boards the power to make rules and regulations for carrying their objects into effect, while defining 'Sports' to include a wide range of activities like hockey, football, and cricket.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Nursing Council Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend and consolidate the laws relating to registration and training of nurses, midwives and health visitors.
amends: The Pakistan Nursing Council Act, 1952 (LIX of 1952)
West Pakistan Nursing Services Ordinance, 1959 (W.P. Ordinance No. L of 1959)
repeals: The Pakistan Nursing Council Act, 1952 (LIX of 1952)
West Pakistan Nursing Services Ordinance, 1959 (W.P. Ordinance No. L of 1959)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Nursing Council to regulate nursing registration, training, and recognition of institutions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends and consolidates laws regarding the registration and training of nurses, midwives, and health visitors. It establishes the Pakistan Nursing Council with specific members from various sectors including the Federal Government, Provincial Governments, and professional bodies. The Act provides for the maintenance of a register, recognition of institutions, and penalties for employing unregistered personnel.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Drugs (Amendment) Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Drugs Act, 1976.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Drugs Act, 1976 to include cosmetics under regulation and establish a licensing board.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Drugs Act, 1976 to extend its regulatory scope from drugs to include cosmetics. It addresses the menace of adulterated and sub-standard cosmetics by ensuring efficacy and safety standards. The legislation establishes a Provincial Licensing and Registration Board to regulate manufacturing, sale, and distribution, requiring licenses for operators and registration with clearance certificates. It introduces specific definitions for cosmetic articles, businesses, and counterfeit products while mandating strict penalties for violations.

name: PUNJAB VILLAGE PANCHAYATS AND NEIGHBOURHOOD COUNCILS ACT, 2019

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Village Panchayats and Neighbourhood Councils Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the constitution, powers and duties of village panchayats and neighbourhood councils in the Province of Punjab.
metadata.max_penalty: Imprisonment for default of payment of penalties; specific penalties for disobedience of orders and infringement of by-laws are prescribed in Chapter VIII.
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes village panchayats and neighbourhood councils in Punjab, defining their constitution, powers, duties, elections, and penalties for misconduct.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Village Panchayats and Neighbourhood Councils Act, 2019 provides the legal framework for establishing common assemblies, panchayats, and neighbourhood councils within the Province of Punjab. It outlines their territorial jurisdiction, powers to manage local funds, conduct elections, and perform administrative duties. The Act also details the code of conduct for members, procedures for handling misconduct, and penalties for non-compliance with orders or by-laws.

name: PUNJAB IRRIGATION AND DRAINAGE AUTHORITY ACT, 1997

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Irrigation and Drainage Authority Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Irrigation and Drainage Authority.
repeals: The Punjab Irrigation and Drainage Authority Ordinance, 1997 (XX of 1997)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Irrigation and Drainage Authority to manage irrigation, drainage, and flood control systems in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Irrigation and Drainage Authority as a body corporate to streamline the province's irrigation and drainage system. The Authority is responsible for managing water supplies, ensuring drainage effluent conveyance, and maintaining infrastructure like tube-wells and reservoirs. It also sets up Area Water Boards and Farmers Organizations to involve beneficiaries in management and achieve financial self-sufficiency within a specified period.

metadata.short_title: The Minimum Wages Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the regulation of minimum rates of wages for workers employed in certain industrial undertakings and for matters ancillary thereto
metadata.max_penalty: fine not exceeding ten thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Regulates minimum wages for workers in specific industrial undertakings within Punjab and establishes Minimum Wages Boards.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the minimum rates of wages for workers employed in certain industrial undertakings. It establishes Minimum Wages Boards to recommend and fix wage rates, defines key terms such as 'worker' and 'employer', and prohibits paying wages below the declared minimum rate. The document also outlines the powers of these boards to collect information and the rules governing their proceedings.

metadata.short_title: The Workers' Welfare Fund Ordinance, 1971
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of a Workers' Welfare Fund
metadata.one_line: Establishes a Workers' Welfare Fund to provide residential accommodation and facilities for workers across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Workers' Welfare Fund to provide residential accommodation and other facilities for workers. It defines the constitution of the Governing Body and Workers Welfare Boards responsible for managing the fund. The law applies to various industrial establishments, including factories, mines, public transport services, and others declared by the Federal Government.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Khal Panchayat Ordinance, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of Khal Panchayats.
metadata.territorial_extent: the areas in which canal irrigation system is maintained by the Government
repeals: The Punjab Irrigation and Drainage Authority Act, 1997
metadata.status_evidence: [Repealed by the Punjab Khal Panchayat Act 2019 (XXV of 2019), w.e.f. 13.12.2019, s.24]
metadata.repealed_by: The Punjab Khal Panchayat Act, 2019
metadata.one_line: Establishes Khal Panchayats for canal irrigation areas and creates the Punjab Khal Panchayat Authority to manage water distribution.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes Khal Panchayats for every water course in areas with a government-maintained canal irrigation system. It creates the Punjab Khal Panchayat Authority, a body corporate responsible for managing affairs, funds, and personnel. The document outlines the functions of Khal Panchayats, including mediating disputes between farmers regarding equitable water distribution and enforcing warabandi schedules.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Medical Teaching Institutions (Reforms) Ordinance, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to improve medical education and enhance effectiveness, efficiency and responsiveness of healthcare services.
metadata.status_evidence: 1This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab on 27 August 2019; and was published in the Punjab Gazette (Extraordinary), dated: 02 September 2019, pp. 689-706, and repealed by the Punjab Medical Teaching Institutions (Reforms) Act 2020 (II of 2020), w.e.f. 19.03.2020, s.33; and published in the Punjab Gazette (Extraordinary), pp. 3817-3828.
metadata.repealed_by: The Punjab Medical Teaching Institutions (Reforms) Act, 2020
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance establishes a framework for reforming medical teaching institutions in Punjab to improve education and healthcare.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Medical Teaching Institutions (Reforms) Ordinance, 2019 was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab to improve medical education and enhance the effectiveness of healthcare services. It establishes a Provincial Policy Board and Boards of Governors for various institutions to oversee their functioning. The Ordinance defines key terms such as Medical Faculty and Clinical Faculty, outlines the objectives of these institutions, and provides powers for making rules and regulations.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Panah Gah Authority Ordinance, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish the Punjab Panah Gah Authority.
metadata.status_evidence: This Ordinance was Promulgated by Governor of the Punjab on 13 January 2021; and was published in the Punjab Gazette (Extraordinary), dated: 13 January 2021, pp. 4811-4818; and was extended for a further period of 90 days w.e.f. 13 April 2021 by the resolution dated: 04 February 2021 passed by Provincial Assembly of the Punjab; and was repealed on 11.07.2021 at the expiration of its extended period in terms of Article 128 of the Constitution of Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Panah Gah Authority to provide temporary shelter for shelterless persons in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Punjab Panah Gah Authority to create a comprehensive system for protecting and relieving shelterless persons. The Authority is empowered to establish, maintain, and operate Panah Gahs (temporary shelters) across the province. It defines the composition of the Authority, its powers regarding property acquisition and donations, and mandates regular audits and annual reporting to the Government.

name: NATIONAL COLLEGE OF BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION & ECONOMICS, LAHORE (AMENDMENT) ACT 2021

metadata.short_title: The National College of Business Administration & Economics, Lahore (Amendment) Act 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the National College of Business Administration & Economics, Lahore Ordinance, 2002.
metadata.parent_law: The National College of Business Administration & Economics, Lahore Ordinance, 2002
amends: The National College of Business Administration & Economics, Lahore Ordinance, 2002
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2002 Ordinance governing National College of Business Administration & Economics, Lahore.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the National College of Business Administration & Economics, Lahore Ordinance, 2002 to update its governance structure and scope. It adds a new definition for 'Company' as Alhamra Education (Private) Limited and omits an old clause regarding social sciences subjects. The legislation also expands the college's campuses in Multan, Rahim Yar Khan, and Bahawalpur as sub-campuses and restructures the Board of Governors to include specific representatives from the Provincial Assembly and other bodies.

name: NATIONAL COLLEGE OF BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION & ECONOMICS, LAHORE (AMENDMENT) ACT 2025

metadata.short_title: National College of Business Administration & Economics, Lahore (Amendment) Act 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the National College of Business Administration & Economics, Lahore Ordinance, 2002.
metadata.parent_law: National College of Business Administration & Economics, Lahore Ordinance, 2002
amends: National College of Business Administration & Economics, Lahore Ordinance, 2002
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2002 Ordinance to rename the institution Alhamra University and update its academic structure.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the National College of Business Administration & Economics, Lahore Ordinance, 2002 to rename the institution as Alhamra University. It updates definitions for 'Institute' to 'University', expands faculty options, and establishes an Academic Council as the principal academic body. The Act also restricts sub-campus openings for ten years and modifies provisions regarding teaching methods and Rector appointments.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Pure Food (Amendment) Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Pure Food Ordinance, 1960.
repeals: The Punjab Pure Food (Amendment) Ordinance, 2015
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for life and fine of three million rupees
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Pure Food Ordinance, 1960 to strengthen enforcement and penalties for food adulteration.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Pure Food Ordinance, 1960 to provide for more effective law enforcement and rationalization of punishments. It updates definitions for local authorities and inspectors, grants powers to seal premises containing unsafe food, and introduces electronic evidence generation during inspections. The Act also substitutes sections regarding penalties for selling adulterated food, manufacturing substandard products, and operating under unhygienic conditions, while repealing the 2015 Amendment Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Food Authority (Amendment) Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Food Authority Act 2011.
repeals: The Punjab Food Authority (Amendment) Ordinance, 2015
subjects: Performance audits of the Food Authority
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years and fine which may extend to two million rupees
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Food Authority Act 2011 regarding food categorization, penalties, and repeals a 2015 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Food Authority Act 2011 to enhance punishments for selling adulterated food and introduce categorization of food business premises. It inserts new sections defining offences by large-scale manufacturers and establishes mechanisms for periodical reports and performance audits by the Government. The Act also repeals the Punjab Food Authority (Amendment) Ordinance, 2015.

name: PUNJAB BOILERS AND PRESSURE VESSELS (AMENDMENT) ACT 2013

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Boilers and Pressure Vessels (Amendment) Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Boilers and Pressure Vessels Ordinance 2002.
metadata.parent_law: Boilers and Pressure Vessels Ordinance, 2002
establishes: Provincial Boilers and Pressure Vessels Safety Board
metadata.administering_body: Industries Department of the Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Amends the Boilers and Pressure Vessels Ordinance 2002 to transfer enforcement powers to the Punjab government.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Boilers and Pressure Vessels Ordinance, 2002 to align its provisions with the Government of the Punjab. It substitutes references to the Federal Government and Pakistan with the Punjab Government throughout the Ordinance. The Act establishes a Provincial Boilers and Pressure Vessels Safety Board and an Ad hoc Technical Committee to regulate safety standards within the province.

name: PUNJAB REVISION OF EMOLUMENTS OF PUBLIC REPRESENTATIVES ACT 2006

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Revision of Emoluments of Public Representatives Act, 2006
metadata.long_title: An Act to revise the emoluments of the holders of the representative offices of the Province of the Punjab.
amends: The Punjab Provincial Assembly Speaker (Salary, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
The Punjab Provincial Assembly Deputy Speaker (Salary, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
The Punjab Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
The Punjab Parliamentary Secretaries (Salary, Allowances and Privileges) Ordinance, 2002
The Punjab Provincial Assembly (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges of Members) Act, 1974
metadata.one_line: Revises salaries, allowances, and accommodation privileges for public representatives in the Punjab Province.
metadata.summary: This Act revises the emoluments of holders of representative offices in the Province of Punjab. It amends five existing Acts and one Ordinance to update salary figures, car allowances, residence provisions, and death compensation benefits. The amendments apply to the Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Ministers, Parliamentary Secretaries, and Assembly Members.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2005
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance 1965.
repeals: The Provincial Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Ordinance, 2005
metadata.administering_body: Government of Punjab / Provincial Transport Authority
metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 regarding stage carriage permits and regulations in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to regulate stage carriages on specified routes within Punjab. It empowers the Government to conduct surveys, declare specified routes, and determine technical specifications for vehicles and permit numbers. The Act also introduces penalties for non-compliance, including forfeiture of guarantees and suspension of permits, while repealing a previous 2005 Amendment Ordinance.

name: PUNJAB PRIVATE SECURITY COMPANIES (REGULATION AND CONTROL) (AMENDMENT) ACT 2004

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Private Security Companies (Regulation and Control) (Amendment) Act, 2004
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Private Security Companies (Regulation and Control) Ordinance, 2002.
amends: The Punjab Private Security Companies (Regulation and Control) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2002 Ordinance to prohibit cash-in-transit without a No Objection Certificate.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Private Security Companies (Regulation and Control) Ordinance, 2002. It adds a new section 5-A which prohibits private security companies from undertaking the transit of cash or valuable articles unless a specific No Objection Certificate is issued by the Licensing Authority. The Act came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Allopathic System (Prevention of Misuse) Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to prevent the misuse of the allopathic system of medicine and to provide for matters connected therewith.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to one year or with fine not exceeding two thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: Prevents misuse of the allopathic system by regulating titles, degrees, surgeries, drug prescriptions, and medicine sales.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance prevents the misuse of the allopathic system of medicine by restricting the use of the title 'doctor' and medical degrees to registered practitioners. It prohibits unqualified persons from performing surgical operations (except minor procedures) and restricts the prescription of certain drugs and the sale of patent medicines without proper labeling. The Central Government is empowered to make rules, while penalties for contravention include imprisonment up to one year or a fine not exceeding two thousand rupees.

metadata.short_title: The Companies Profits (Workers Participation) Act, 1968
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for participation of workers in the profits of companies and for matters ancillary thereto
repeals: Companies Act, 1913 (VII of 1913)
metadata.one_line: Provides for worker participation in company profits through a dedicated fund managed by a Board of Trustees.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a framework for workers to participate in the profits of companies operating in Pakistan. It mandates the creation of a Workers Participation Fund, where companies contribute a percentage of their net profits. The fund is managed by a Board of Trustees responsible for distributing benefits to eligible workers based on a defined scheme. The Act also outlines provisions for dispute resolution, tax treatments for both the fund and workers, and allows for the delegation of management to financial institutions like the Investment Corporation of Pakistan.

metadata.short_title: The Foreigners Act, 1946
metadata.long_title: An Act to confer upon the Federal Government Certain powers in respect of foreigners.
repeals: The Foreigners Act, (1864), (111 of 1864)
The Foreigners Act, 1940, (II of 1940)
The Foreigners Act (Amendment) Ordinance, 1946, (Ord. XXI of 1946)
metadata.one_line: Confers powers on the Federal Government regarding entry, presence, and departure of foreigners in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Federal Government to regulate the entry, presence, and departure of foreigners into Pakistan. It provides for the detention of internees, the determination of nationality, and the registration of illegal immigrants. The Act also outlines penalties for contraventions and establishes an Aliens Registration Authority to manage foreigner registrations.

metadata.short_title: The Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Order to revise, amend and consolidate the law of evidence so as to bring it in conformity with the injunctions of Islam as laid down in the Holy Quran.
repeals: The Evidence Act, 1872
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and revises the law of evidence in Pakistan to conform with Islamic injunctions.
metadata.summary: This Order consolidates and revises the law of evidence applicable in Pakistan. It brings the legal framework into conformity with the injunctions of Islam as laid down in the Holy Quran. The document repeals the Evidence Act, 1872, and covers topics such as witnesses, admissions, confessions, documentary evidence, and judicial notice.

metadata.short_title: Punjab Local Government (Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Local Government Act, 2019.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Punjab other than the areas notified as cantonments under the Cantonments Act, 1924 (II of 1924), or the Cantonments Ordinance, 2002 (CXXXVII of 2002), and such other areas under active possession and direct control of the Armed Forces of Pakistan that may be notified by the Government for this purpose
amends: Village Panchayats and Neighbourhood Councils Act, 2019 (Act XIV of 2019)
repeals: section 242 of the Punjab Local Government Act, 2019
Village Panchayats and Neighbourhood Councils Act, 2019 (Act XIV of 2019)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Local Government Act, 2019 to establish neighbourhood councils and modify local government structures.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Local Government Act, 2019 to empower grassroots decision-making and improve service delivery. It establishes Neighbourhood Councils for each neighbourhood and Town Councils by combining neighbourhoods in Metropolitan Corporations. The legislation also repeals the Village Panchayats and Neighbourhood Councils Act, 2019, and amends various sections regarding definitions, local government composition, and bye-laws.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Shops and Establishments (Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Shops and Establishments Ordinance, 1969
amends: The Punjab Shops and Establishments Ordinance, 1969
metadata.administering_body: Deputy Chief Inspector of the area concerned
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Shops and Establishments Ordinance, 1969 regarding working hours, adolescent employment, and definitions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Shops and Establishments Ordinance, 1969 to update definitions of adolescents and adults, restrict working hours, and regulate the employment of minors. It expands the scope of establishments covered to include various commercial and service sectors while introducing welfare measures for employees. The amendments also modify provisions regarding wage payment, inspection authorities, and registration requirements.

name: UNIVERSITY OF SOUTH ASIA, LAHORE (AMENDMENT) ACT 2021

metadata.short_title: The University of South Asia, Lahore (Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the University of South Asia Lahore Act 2005.
amends: The University of South Asia Lahore Act, 2005
metadata.one_line: Amends the University of South Asia Lahore Act 2005 regarding faculties, governance, and affiliation rules.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the University of South Asia Lahore Act 2005 to update its structure and regulations. It introduces new faculties such as Food and Culinary Sciences and Engineering, modifies the appointment terms for the Vice Chancellor, and sets restrictions on opening sub-campuses or affiliating institutions for ten years. The legislation also validates previous amendments made by this Act from its commencement date.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Shops and Establishments (Amendment) Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Shops and Establishments Ordinance, 1969
amends: The Punjab Shops and Establishments Ordinance, 1969
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Shops and Establishments Ordinance, 1969 regarding definitions, working hours, and registration forms.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Shops and Establishments Ordinance, 1969 to update definitions for adolescents and adults and expand the scope of establishments covered. It modifies provisions regarding daily and weekly working hours, overtime rules, and the authority responsible for wage payments. The legislation also revises registration forms and schedules to include new categories like IT companies and private clinics while updating employer declaration requirements.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government (Amendment) Act, 2005
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 2001.
repeals: The Punjab Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 2005
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 2001 regarding elections, misconduct, and health offences.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 2001 to update references to other laws and redefine terms like 'misconduct'. It introduces provisions for dissolving councils upon election announcements and adds specific offences related to food adulteration. The Act also includes schedules for reporting complaints, search warrants, and compounding of cases by inspectors.

name: PUNJAB INFECTIOUS DISEASES (PREVENTION AND CONTROL) ORDINANCE 2020

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Infectious Diseases (Prevention and Control) Ordinance, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for prevention and control of infectious diseases in the Punjab and matters ancillary and connected thereto.
repeals: The Punjab Epidemic Diseases Act, 1958
metadata.status_evidence: [Repealed by the Punjab Infectious Diseases (Prevention and Control) Act 2020 (XIII of 2020), w.e.f. 11.08.2020, s.32]
metadata.repealed_by: The Punjab Infectious Diseases (Prevention and Control) Act, 2020
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance provides for the prevention and control of infectious diseases in Punjab through restrictions, duties, and penalties.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Infectious Diseases (Prevention and Control) Ordinance, 2020 was promulgated by the Governor to address immediate threats from infectious diseases while the Provincial Assembly was not in session. It empowers the Secretary to declare infection threats, impose duties on medical practitioners, restrict gatherings, and manage potentially infectious persons. The Ordinance establishes offences for non-compliance with directions and includes provisions for confidentiality and rule-making.

metadata.short_title: The Canal and Drainage (Amendment) Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Canal and Drainage Act, 1873.
establishes: Board consisting of Superintending Canal Officers
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1873 Act to improve canal development, charge recovery, and judicial jurisdiction in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Canal and Drainage Act, 1873 to encourage participatory canal development and establish an effective mechanism for recovering charges. It grants revisional jurisdiction to a Board of Superintending Canal Officers and ousts civil court jurisdiction over specific proceedings under the parent Act. Additionally, it makes certain offences cognizable and non-bailable while introducing provisions for disciplinary action against officers acting with bad intention or gross negligence.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Public Private Partnership Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to foster an enabling environment for private sector participation in development in the Punjab through public private partnership.
repeals: The Punjab Public Private Partnership for Infrastructure Act, 2010
The Punjab Public Private Partnership Ordinance, 2014
metadata.one_line: Establishes a framework for public private partnerships in infrastructure sectors across Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act creates an enabling environment for private sector participation in development projects within the Punjab province. It establishes institutional arrangements including a PPP Steering Committee, a PPP Cell, and a Risk Management Unit to oversee project delivery. The legislation outlines a comprehensive process for identifying, approving, and implementing PPP projects across various sectors such as health, education, power, and roads.

metadata.short_title: The Employment of Children (Amendment) Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Employment of Children Act, 1991.
key_definitions: said Act (refers to Employment of Children Act, 1991)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Employment of Children Act, 1991 to apply it exclusively to the Province of Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Employment of Children Act, 1991 to restrict its application to the Province of Punjab. It substitutes references to 'Pakistan' and 'Federal Government' with 'the Punjab' and 'Government of the Punjab'. The Act also omits various federal references and specific sections from the parent Act to align it with provincial jurisdiction.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Workers' Children (Education) (Amendment) Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Workers' Children (Education) Ordinance, 1972.
key_definitions: worker (as defined in section 2 of the Punjab Industrial Relations Act 2010)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Workers' Children (Education) Ordinance, 1972 to restrict scope to Punjab workers and update definitions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Workers' Children (Education) Ordinance, 1972 to align its provisions with the jurisdiction of the Province of Punjab. It substitutes references to 'Pakistan' with 'the Punjab', defines 'Government' as the Government of the Punjab, and updates the definition of a worker to reference the Punjab Industrial Relations Act 2010. Additionally, it omits specific wage thresholds and the word 'Provincial' from various sections of the said Ordinance.

name: PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOMES (AMENDMENT) ACT 2003

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Supervision and Control of Children Homes (Amendment) Act, 2003
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Supervision and Control of Children Homes Act 1976 (XVI of 1976).
amends: The Punjab Supervision and Control of Children Homes Act, 1976
metadata.one_line: Amends Section 4 of the Punjab Supervision and Control of Children Homes Act 1976 to include women members.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Supervision and Control of Children Homes Act 1976. It specifically modifies Section 4, clause (g) of the 1976 Act. The amendment inserts a requirement for at least four women members in the relevant body.

name: THE PUNJAB DESTITUTE AND NEGLECTED CHILDREN (AMENDMENT) ACT 2017

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Destitute and Neglected Children (Amendment) Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Destitute and Neglected Children Act 2004.
amends: The Punjab Destitute and Neglected Children Act, 2004
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for seven years and fine up to three hundred thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2004 Act to register organizations, define new offences like rag picking, and increase penalties for child exploitation.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Destitute and Neglected Children Act, 2004 to strengthen protections for vulnerable children. It introduces requirements for organizations managing child accommodation to register with the Bureau within 120 days. The legislation defines new categories of neglected children, such as those at risk due to disability or born in jail, and adds specific offences regarding rag picking and selling goods for begging. Furthermore, it significantly increases penalties for unauthorized custody and other forms of child exploitation.

name: PUNJAB RESTRICTION ON EMPLOYMENT OF CHILDREN ORDINANCE 2016

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Restriction on Employment of Children Ordinance, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to prohibit the employment of children and to restrict the employment of adolescents in certain occupations and processes.
repeals: The Employment of Children Act, 1991 (V of 1991)
metadata.one_line: Prohibits child employment and restricts adolescent hazardous work in Punjab, repealing the 1991 Act.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance prohibits the employment of children and restricts adolescents from performing hazardous work in specific occupations. It establishes a Provincial Committee on Child Labour to advise on eradication measures and sets limits on working hours and weekly holidays for adolescents. The law applies throughout Punjab and repeals the Employment of Children Act, 1991.

metadata.short_title: The Employment (Record of Services) (Amendment) Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Employment (Record of Services) Act, 1951.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Employment (Record of Services) Act, 1951 to apply it specifically to the Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Employment (Record of Services) Act, 1951 to restrict its application to the Province of Punjab. It substitutes 'Pakistan' with 'the Punjab' and omits references to 'Provincial' government throughout the amended sections. Additionally, it redefines 'Government' to mean the Government of the Punjab and adjusts certain monetary figures in the original Act.

metadata.short_title: The Ehtram-e-Ramazan Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for measures observe the sanctity of the month of Ramazan
metadata.max_penalty: six months imprisonment or fine up to fifty thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: Prohibits eating and serving food in public places during Ramazan fasting hours in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides measures to observe the sanctity of the month of Ramazan. It prohibits persons obligated to fast from eating, drinking, or smoking in public places and forbids proprietors from serving eatables to such persons during fasting hours. The law also mandates the closure of cinema houses and theatres from sunset until three hours thereafter. Offences are punishable by imprisonment up to six months or fines up to fifty thousand rupees.

metadata.short_title: The Juvenile Justice System Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for protection of the rights of children involved in criminal litigation
metadata.one_line: Establishes juvenile courts and provides for the protection, legal assistance, and rehabilitation of children involved in criminal litigation.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes a framework to protect the rights of children involved in criminal litigation and facilitate their rehabilitation. It mandates the creation of specialized juvenile courts with exclusive jurisdiction over cases involving child offenders, ensuring separate trials from adults. The law provides for state-funded legal assistance, defines specific protections against corporal punishment or death penalties for children, and outlines procedures for probation and appeals.

metadata.short_title: Punjab Home-based Workers Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for protection of rights of home-based workers.
metadata.one_line: This Act protects the rights, welfare, and employment conditions of home-based workers in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Home-based Workers Act, 2021 provides legal protection for home-based workers who perform work from their homes. It defines key terms such as 'home-based worker', 'employer', and 'contractor' to regulate their employment relationships. The Act grants entitlements including sickness benefits, maternity benefits, medical care, and employment injury benefits to secured home-based workers. Furthermore, it prohibits the employment of children under fifteen years and restricts child labour between fifteen and eighteen years in prohibited sectors.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Shops and Establishments (Amendment) Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the West Pakistan Shops and Establishments Ordinance, 1969.
amends: The West Pakistan Shops and Establishments Ordinance, 1969
key_definitions: daycare room (for under-six years old children)
metadata.one_line: Amends the West Pakistan Shops and Establishments Ordinance, 1969 to apply it to the Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the West Pakistan Shops and Establishments Ordinance, 1969 to adapt its provisions specifically for the Province of Punjab. Key changes include substituting references from 'West Pakistan' to 'the Punjab', defining 'Government' as the Government of the Punjab, and introducing a requirement for daycare rooms in establishments employing twenty-five or more women. The Act also updates penalties, court jurisdictions, and administrative codes to align with Punjab-specific laws.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Sales Tax Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for levy of sales tax on services rendered or provided in the Province of the Punjab and for matters ancillary thereto or connected therewith
repeals: Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act 2012 (XLII of 2012)
metadata.status_evidence: Repealed by the Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act 2012 (XLII of 2012), published in the Punjab Gazette (Extraordinary), dated: 27 June 2012, pp. 41901-35, s.87.
metadata.repealed_by: Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act 2012 (XLII of 2012)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance levies sales tax on various services rendered in the Province of Punjab at a rate of sixteen per cent.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Sales Tax Ordinance, 2000 was promulgated by the Governor to levy sales tax on specific services provided within the Province of Punjab. It applies to sectors including hotels, telecommunication, banking, insurance, and courier services, charging a tax rate of sixteen per cent on the value of taxable services. The Ordinance incorporates provisions from the Sales Tax Act, 1990 regarding payment, registration, records, enforcement, and penalties. Although promulgated as an Ordinance due to the suspension of the Provincial Assembly, it was later repealed by the Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act 2012.

metadata.short_title: The Factories (Amendment) Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Factories Act, 1934.
metadata.max_penalty: ten thousand rupees
metadata.administering_body: Government of Punjab or an authority notified by the Government
metadata.one_line: Amends the Factories Act, 1934 to update definitions, penalties, and provisions regarding child labour and factory operations in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Factories Act, 1934 to modernize definitions of machinery and manufacturing processes while clarifying the status of clerical workers. It updates penalties for non-compliance, specifically increasing fines for failure to register factories and removing references to obsolete sections regarding child employment. The amendments also adjust age limits and procedural requirements for factory inspections and registrations across Punjab.

metadata.short_title: The Factories (Amendment) Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Factories Act 1934.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Factories Act 1934 to apply specifically to Punjab and enhance penalties for offences.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Factories Act, 1934 to restrict its application to the Province of Punjab by replacing references to 'Pakistan' and 'Provincial Legislature'. It updates various sections regarding fines, penalties, and definitions, including substituting the Employment of Children Act, 1938 with the 1991 version. The Act also enhances penalties for repeat offenders in government factories and extends the Act's application to all government-controlled factories.

name: THE PUNJAB PROHIBITION OF CHILD LABOUR AT BRICK KILNS ORDINANCE 2016

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Prohibition of Child Labour at Brick Kilns Ordinance, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the prohibition of child labour and regulation of labour at the brick kilns in the Punjab.
metadata.max_penalty: simple imprisonment up to six months and fine up to five hundred thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance prohibits child labour and regulates working conditions at brick kilns in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance aims to protect children from hazardous environments at brick kilns by prohibiting their employment. It mandates written contracts for all workers, limits cash advances to six times the wage, and establishes District Labour Committees and inspectors to enforce these rules. Occupiers who violate provisions face imprisonment and fines, while specific presumptions are made regarding child presence during school hours.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Undesirable Cooperative Societies (Dissolution) (Amendment) Act 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Undesirable Cooperative Societies (Dissolution) Act, 1993.
amends: The Punjab Undesirable Cooperative Societies (Dissolution) Act, 1993
repeals: The Punjab Undesirable Cooperative Societies (Dissolution) (Amendment) Ordinance 2020
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1993 Act to direct surplus assets of dissolved societies toward public or charitable uses and repeals a 2020 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Undesirable Cooperative Societies (Dissolution) Act, 1993 to ensure that surplus assets from wound-up societies are used for public or charitable purposes rather than distributed among members. It inserts a new section 15-A into the 1993 Act, allowing these assets to be placed with the Punjab Provincial Cooperatives Bank Limited pending approval by the Government. The Act also repeals the Punjab Undesirable Cooperative Societies (Dissolution) (Amendment) Ordinance 2020.

metadata.short_title: The Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Co-operative Societies Act, 1925.
repeals: The Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Ordinance, 2020
metadata.max_penalty: rupees one million
metadata.one_line: Amends the Co-operative Societies Act, 1925 to update definitions, membership rules, merger provisions, and penalties for societies in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Co-operative Societies Act, 1925 to align terminology with the Government of the Punjab and update jurisdictional references. It modifies registration requirements for different types of societies, including housing and producers' societies, and introduces new provisions regarding mergers and member expulsion. The legislation also updates penalty structures for offences and clarifies appeal processes to the Secretary Cooperatives.

metadata.short_title: The Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Ordinance, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Co-operative Societies Act, 1925.
metadata.status_evidence: This Ordinance was promulgated by Governor of the Punjab on 13 July 2020; and was published in the Punjab Gazette (Extraordinary), dated: 13 July 2020, pp. 181-185; and repealed by the Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Act 2020 (XIX of 2020), w.e.f. 11.08.2020, s.24; and published in the Punjab Gazette (Extraordinary), pp. 585-588.
metadata.repealed_by: The Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2020
metadata.max_penalty: rupees one million
metadata.one_line: Amends the Co-operative Societies Act, 1925 to update definitions and procedures for societies in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Co-operative Societies Act, 1925 to replace references to 'Provincial Government' with 'Government' and 'West Pakistan' with 'Punjab'. It updates membership requirements, merger provisions, and penalties for offences. The document also substitutes specific sections to clarify the role of the Secretary Cooperatives and adjust appeal processes.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Undesirable Cooperative Societies (Dissolution) (Amendment) Ordinance, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Undesirable Cooperative Societies (Dissolution) Act, 1993.
amends: The Punjab Undesirable Cooperative Societies (Dissolution) Act, 1993
metadata.status_evidence: and repealed by the Punjab Undesirable Cooperative Societies (Dissolution) (Amendment) Act 2020 (XVIII of 2020), w.e.f. 11.08.2020, s.3
metadata.repealed_by: The Punjab Undesirable Cooperative Societies (Dissolution) (Amendment) Act, 2020
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1993 Act to direct surplus assets of dissolved societies toward public or charitable purposes.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Undesirable Cooperative Societies (Dissolution) Act, 1993 to address the disposal of surplus assets from wound-up societies. It mandates that after meeting liabilities, such assets must be devoted to public utility or charitable purposes rather than being divided among members. The provision allows placing these assets with the Punjab Provincial Cooperatives Bank Limited pending government approval for specific uses.

name: WEST PAKISTAN PUBLICATION OF TEXTBOOKS (REGULATION AND CONTROL) ORDINANCE, 1970

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Publication of Textbooks (Regulation and Control) Ordinance, 1970
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the regulation and control of printing, publication and sale of textbooks and works published by or under the authority of the West Pakistan Textbook Board.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment of either description which may extend to one year or with fine or both
metadata.one_line: Regulates and controls the printing, publication, and sale of textbooks in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the regulation and control of the printing, publication, and sale of textbooks published by or under the authority of the West Pakistan Textbook Board. It prohibits any person from printing, publishing, or selling such textbooks without specific permission from the Board and prescribes fees for applications. The document establishes offences for contravention, allowing for imprisonment up to one year or fines, and provides mechanisms for forfeiture of illegal copies and exemption by notification.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Mineral Development Corporation (Amendment) Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Mineral Development Corporation Act 1975.
amends: The Punjab Mineral Development Corporation Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Amends section 5 of the Punjab Mineral Development Corporation Act 1975 regarding departmental appointments.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Mineral Development Corporation Act 1975 to update provisions within Section 5. Specifically, it substitutes a clause in subsection (1) concerning the rank and designation of the Secretary to the Government, Mines and Minerals Department. The amendment clarifies that the relevant authority must be the Secretary or a nominee not below the rank of Deputy Secretary.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government (Amendment) Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Local Government Act 2013.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Local Government Act 2013 regarding membership bars, dissolution provisions, and presiding officers.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Local Government Act 2013 to remove restrictions on double membership in specific cases. It also omits provisions concerning the dissolution of local governments to strengthen their security. Additionally, it empowers Deputy Mayors or Vice Chairmen to preside over meetings of various local government bodies.

name: PUNJAB URBAN IMMOVABLE PROPERTY TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT 2017

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax (Amendment) Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may, by notification, specify
amends: The Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1958 Property Tax Act to align with the 2013 Local Government Act regarding tax rates and urban area definitions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958 to harmonize its provisions with section 116 of the Punjab Local Government Act, 2013. It substitutes definitions for 'urban area' in Section 2 and modifies tax levies in Section 3 to allow higher rates under the 2013 Act. The amendments apply to Metropolitan Corporations, Municipal Corporations, Municipal Committees, and rural Union Councils with urban characteristics within Punjab.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Punjab Local Government Act 2013.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Local Government Act 2013 regarding reserved seats, election methods, and technocrat definitions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Local Government Act 2013 to align the election system for reserved seats with proportional representation based on political party lists. It redefines a 'technocrat' as requiring specific educational qualifications and experience. The document also changes election methods for Mayors, Chairmen, and other officials to open division rather than voting by existing chairmen, and establishes procedures for filling vacant reserved seats.

name: THE PUNJAB LOCAL GOVERNMENT (THIRD AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE 2016

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Punjab Local Government Act, 2013.
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Local Government Act, 2013
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Local Government Act, 2013 regarding council composition and technocrat definitions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Local Government Act, 2013 to update definitions and compositions for various local government bodies. It introduces specific requirements for 'technocrats' with defined educational and experience criteria. The text also revises the number of reserved seats for women, peasants, workers, youth, and non-Muslims in Union Councils and higher municipal bodies. Additionally, it adjusts the rules for Vice Chairmen and Deputy Mayors performing functions during absences and modifies membership numbers based on population.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Local Government Act, 2013.
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Local Government Act, 2013
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Local Government Act, 2013 regarding Union Council composition, elections, and finance commission representation.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Local Government Act, 2013 to address reserved seats in Union Councils via indirect elections. It establishes representation for local governments in the Punjab Finance Commission and modifies nomination processes for various local bodies. The text also omits specific sections and inserts transitional arrangements until new Union Councils are notified.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Local Government Act 2013.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Local Government Act 2013 regarding election procedures and non-Muslim representation.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Local Government Act, 2013 to facilitate immediate legislative action when the Provincial Assembly is not in session. It modifies sections concerning Union Councils, District Councils, Municipal Corporations, and Municipal Committees to adjust membership composition for non-Muslim representatives. Additionally, it updates provisions related to election schedules, polling station establishment, and the appointment of returning officers by the Election Commission.

name: DERA GHAZI KHAN DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY ACT 1991

metadata.short_title: The Dera Ghazi Khan Development Authority Act, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Dera Ghazi Khan Development Authority.
repeals: The Dera Ghazi Khan Development Authority Ordinance, 1991 (X of 1991)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Dera Ghazi Khan Development Authority for urban development and repeals a corresponding Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Dera Ghazi Khan Development Authority to oversee the development of the Revenue Division of Dera Ghazi Khan. The Authority is empowered to prepare schemes, acquire property, levy betterment fees, and regulate land use within its notified jurisdiction. It defines key terms such as 'Government' (meaning Government of the Punjab) and grants immunity to its members and employees for acts done in good faith.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government (Fifth Amendment) Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Local Government Act 2013.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on 18 October 2016
repeals: The Punjab Local Government (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 2016
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Local Government Act, 2013 regarding council composition and repeals a 2016 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Local Government Act, 2013 to update the composition of Union Councils, District Councils, and Municipal bodies. It introduces specific requirements for technocrat, peasant, worker, youth, and non-Muslim members while adjusting deputy mayor counts based on population. The Act also clarifies succession procedures for chairmen and mayors when absent and repeals the Punjab Local Government (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 2016.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government (Fourth Amendment) Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Local Government Act 2013.
subjects: Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Local Government Act 2013 to allow rural Union Councils with urban characteristics to levy property tax.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Local Government Act, 2013 to empower specific rural Union Councils with urban characteristics to levy property tax. It substitutes a subsection in section 116 of the 2013 Act to mandate that such councils levy property tax according to the Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958 if they have not determined their own rates. The legislation applies throughout the Province of Punjab and came into force immediately upon publication.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government (Second Amendment) Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Local Government Act 2013.
repeals: The Punjab Local Government (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2016
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2013 Local Government Act regarding reserved seats, election methods, and definitions for Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Local Government Act, 2013 to align reserved seat elections with proportional representation systems. It updates the definition of a 'technocrat' and changes election procedures for various local government bodies to use open division or party lists. The legislation also repeals the earlier Second Amendment Ordinance of 2016.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government (First Amendment) Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Local Government Act 2013.
repeals: The Punjab Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 2016
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Local Government Act 2013 to create zones, increase marginalized representation, and update meeting presiding rules.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Local Government Act 2013 to empower the Government to divide Metropolitan and Municipal Corporations into zones for better service delivery. It rationalizes the representation of marginalized segments by increasing the number of worker, peasant, and technocrat members in local governments. The legislation also enhances the number of Deputy Mayors and Vice Chairmen, updates provisions for presiding over meetings in the absence of the Mayor or Chairman, and repeals a previous 2016 Ordinance.

metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Punjab Local Government Act 2013 to define local areas such as Metropolitan Corporations and District Councils. It substitutes sections concerning the demarcation of local governments, the delimitation of Union Councils and wards by the Election Commission, and the preparation of electoral rolls. The Act also repeals the earlier Punjab Local Government (Second Amendment) Ordinance 2014.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Local Government Act 2013 to clarify definitions of wards and Union Councils. It establishes rules for ward delimitation, composition of local bodies including reserved seats for women, peasants, workers, youth, and non-Muslim members. The Act also introduces a declaration regarding the finality of Prophethood for candidates and repeals four previous Ordinances amending the same Act.

metadata.short_title: The Women University Multan (Amendment) Act, 2012

It establishes the university as a body corporate with perpetual succession and defines its structure, including the Chancellor, Vice Chancellor, and Authority members. The Act also provides for the transfer of property, affiliation of colleges, opening of sub-campuses, and the absorption of existing government employees into the university service.

metadata.short_title: The Stamp (Punjab Amendment) Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Stamp Act, 1899, in its application to the Province of the Punjab

metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Stamp Act, 1899 specifically for its application to the Province of the Punjab. It adds new clauses defining 'Public Office' and 'Public Officer' to include various government bodies, local authorities, statutory corporations, commercial concerns with over twenty employees, registered companies, and cooperative societies. The Act also repeals the earlier Stamp (Punjab Amendment) Ordinance, 1973.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Prevention of Hoarding Ordinance, 2020

metadata.one_line: This Ordinance prevents hoarding of essential items during the COVID-19 pandemic in Punjab with penalties for offenders.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Prevention of Hoarding Ordinance, 2020 was promulgated by the Governor to prevent hoarding of essential articles during the COVID-19 pandemic when the Provincial Assembly was not in session. It defines specific offences related to stocking excess quantities or failing to sell demanded goods, granting officers powers to search premises without a warrant and auction seized items. The Ordinance establishes penalties including imprisonment and fines for dealers, corporations, and those providing false information, while overriding other laws to ensure immediate action.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Commercial Courts Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of Commercial Courts in the Punjab.

metadata.summary: This Act establishes Commercial Courts within the Province of Punjab to facilitate the speedy resolution of commercial disputes. It defines specific entities such as domestic and foreign companies, firms, and commercial disputes involving claims of five hundred thousand rupees or more. The Act creates a Secretariat to maintain records and train judges, while empowering the Government to appoint judges and establish courts across various districts.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes a framework for Commercial Courts within the Province of Punjab to handle commercial disputes efficiently. It defines specific types of commercial disputes, including those involving domestic and foreign companies or firms with a claim value of at least five hundred thousand rupees. The document outlines the powers of these courts, the appointment of judges, the establishment of a Secretariat, and provisions for appeals and alternative dispute resolution.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 to update specific provisions applicable in the Province of Punjab. It introduces changes regarding the substitution of court names, omission of certain sections, adjustments to cost limits, and modifications to appeal and revision procedures. metadata.short_title: The Punjab Drugs (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2015

It substitutes references to the 'Federal Government' with 'Provincial Government' within section 31 of the said Act. The Ordinance transfers all powers exercisable by the Federal Government concerning existing Drug Courts in Punjab to the Provincial Government immediately upon commencement.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Food Authority Act 2011 to improve the categorization of food business premises based on adherence to standards. It enhances punishments for selling adulterated or substandard food, introducing stricter penalties for large-scale manufacturers. The document also inserts provisions for periodic reports by the Authority and establishes a bar on civil court jurisdiction over proceedings under the Act.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Pure Food (Amendment) Ordinance, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Pure Food Ordinance, 1960.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Pure Food Ordinance, 1960 to ensure more effective law enforcement and rationalize punishments. It introduces new definitions for local authorities and directors, mandates the use of electronic devices for generating evidence during inspections, and establishes stricter penalties for selling adulterated or unsafe food. The text also adds provisions for sealing premises by inspectors and conducting annual performance audits by the Government.

It specifies which persons are required to take oaths, such as witnesses and interpreters, while exempting children under twelve or accused persons examined as defense witnesses. The Act provides forms for oaths based on religious persuasion, authorizes courts to tender specific oaths, and ensures that evidence is not invalidated by irregularities in the administration of oaths.

The Act defines specific terms, outlines the composition and functions of the councils, sets standards for teaching institutions, and prescribes penalties for unregistered practice or misconduct.
