It empowers authorised officers to enter premises, evict occupants, demolish unauthorized structures, and recover costs or arrears as land revenue. The legislation also bars civil courts from granting injunctions against such recovery actions and provides indemnity for officials acting in good faith.

It substitutes sections on the commission's makeup, specifying requirements for members from various sectors like the judiciary and armed forces, while setting age limits at sixty-five years. The Act also defines terms of office as three years without reappointment and omits a specific section from the original ordinance.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Local Government Act, 2013 to ensure local governments provide designated landfill sites for solid waste disposal. It introduces penalties for illegal dumping, including warnings for first-time offenders and imprisonment with fines for repeat offenses within a year. The amendment also mandates that local governments maintain these sites according to bylaws until proper facilities are established.

It substitutes references to 'West Pakistan' with 'the Punjab' in the long title, preamble, and section 1, while replacing 'Deputy Commissioner' with 'District Coordination Officer' in section 2. Additionally, it omits section 5 of the original 1958 Act.

metadata.summary: This Act consolidates legislation regarding the prevention of dangerous epidemic diseases within the Province of Punjab. It grants the Provincial Government authority to prescribe temporary regulations, inspect travellers, and segregate suspected cases when ordinary laws are insufficient. The Act also defines penalties for disobedience of orders and provides legal protection to persons acting in good faith under its provisions.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Evacuee Property and Displaced Persons Laws (Repeal) Act, 1975 to modify definitions and procedures regarding property disposal. It transfers pending proceedings to a newly constituted 'Full Board' of the Board of Revenue for final disposal. The Act also provides mechanisms to cancel fraudulent land allotments and abates certain pending proceedings while retaining others involving post-1974 contraventions.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Animals Slaughter Control Act, 1963 to provide a more effective system for regulating and monitoring animal slaughter. It updates definitions for terms such as 'carcass', 'local authority', and 'useful animal' while restricting slaughter days and prohibiting the sale of meat from haram or diseased animals. The legislation also introduces provisions for forfeiture of contraband meat, rewards for informers, and mandatory annual performance audits by the Government.

metadata.short_title: The Electricity (Amendment) Ordinance, 1979

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Electricity Act, 1910 to update definitions of premises ownership and expand licensee powers for entering premises and removing fittings. It establishes procedures for discontinuing supply due to non-payment or safety violations, including specific conditions for domestic consumers. The text also outlines dispute resolution mechanisms involving Electric Inspectors and the Provincial Government regarding charges and service line costs.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Electricity Act, 1910 to update provisions concerning licensee entry rights, notice periods for supply discontinuance, and definitions of energy theft. It introduces new penalties for installing devices to abstract energy dishonestly and clarifies the role of the Electric Inspector in resolving disputes between licensees and consumers. The amendments apply specifically to the Province of Punjab and come into force immediately upon promulgation.

metadata.summary: This Act establishes a legal framework for registering foreigners who enter, reside in, or leave Pakistan. It empowers the Federal Government to make rules requiring foreigners to report their presence, movement, and departure details to prescribed authorities. The Act also mandates that hotels and vessel/aircraft operators report foreigner information and places the burden of proving non-foreigner status on the individual.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Explosives Act 1884 to adapt it for provincial administration in Punjab. It substitutes references to the Federal Government with the Government of the Punjab and changes the definition of 'import' to include bringing explosives into the province by land, air, or river. The Ordinance also omits Section 15 of the original Act and transfers enforcement duties from armed forces rules to persons employed under the provincial government.

The Act also omits section 15 of the original 1884 Act and repeals a previous Ordinance on the same subject.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sugar Factories (Control) Act, 1950 to ensure timely and transparent payments to cane growers. The Act also clarifies that offences under the parent Act are cognizable upon report by the Cane Commissioner and are bailable.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sugar Factories (Control) Act, 1950 to ensure timely and transparent payments to cane growers. It introduces new definitions for Cane Purchase Receipts, mandates specific crushing timelines, and regulates interactions between factory occupiers, cane growers, and cooperative societies. The legislation also updates penalty structures for contraventions and repeals two previous Ordinances from 2020.

It establishes a Review Board consisting of judges to oversee detentions exceeding three months and introduces provisions for prohibiting the entry of publications prejudicial to public order. It prohibits decorating public streets with lights, using explosives or fireworks, displaying dowry, and serving more than one dish to participants. The law also mandates that marriage functions in public places conclude by 10:00 pm and establishes committees for enforcement.

metadata.short_title: The Forest (Amendment) Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Forest Act, 1927.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Forest Act, 1927 to introduce provisions regarding reserved and protected forests. It empowers the Government to declare such forests as no longer reserved or protected if they are required for projects of national importance undertaken by the Federal Government or the Provincial Government. The amendments allow these declarations to be made on specific terms and conditions prescribed by the Government.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Forest Act, 1927 to provide mechanisms for using reserved or protected forest land for national projects of strategic importance. It allows the Government, with Provincial Cabinet approval, to declare such forest land no longer reserved or protected if a suitable substitute plant-able land is provided and funds are secured for its maintenance. The amendments apply specifically to the Province of Punjab.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Forest (Amendment) Act, 2016

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Forest Act, 1927 to facilitate better utilization of wasteland through the establishment of forest companies. It introduces provisions for public private partnerships where the Government assigns forest land or wasteland to these companies for development. The Act outlines procedures for inviting eligible applicants, managing afforestation plans, and ensuring government oversight through monitoring committees.

It introduces provisions for public-private partnerships where the Government assigns forest land or wasteland to these companies for development and afforestation. The Ordinance outlines eligibility criteria for applicants, procedures for partnership agreements, and requirements for profit deposit and record maintenance by forest companies.

It allows the Government, with Provincial Cabinet approval, to declare such forests no longer reserved or protected if specific conditions regarding substitute land and afforestation are met. The legislation applies to the Province of Punjab and came into force immediately upon promulgation by the Governor.

The law sets out penalties for employers who fail to comply with these wage standards and outlines deductions for housing and transport allowances.

metadata.summary: The Punjab Enforcement of Women's Property Rights Ordinance, 2021 was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab to protect and secure women's ownership rights against harassment, coercion, force, or fraud. It establishes an Ombudsperson with powers to conduct summary enquiries, restore possession or title to property, and award rent compensation when proceedings in a court are not pending. The Ordinance allows for references to Civil Courts for intricate adjudication and mandates the appointment of necessary officers by the Government of the Punjab.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government (Sixth Amendment) Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Local Government Act 2013.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Local Government Act, 2013 to grant local governments the power to sell immovable properties through public auction after obtaining prior approval from the Government. It also allows for the leasing of immovable properties and the transfer of movable properties via public auction. The provisions ensure that occupants have a first right of refusal upon payment of outstanding dues when selling property.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 2001 to grant local governments specific powers regarding their property. It allows them to sell immovable property through public auction after obtaining prior approval from the Government and ensures occupants have a right of refusal if dues are paid. Additionally, it authorizes the granting of leases for up to fifteen years with potential extensions and permits the transfer of movable properties.

The company is empowered to fix fares, manage routes, and advise on public policy matters regarding urban transport.

It substitutes and omits certain sections of the original Act to include new categories of offences punishable by whipping. These offences include assault on women, throwing substances at persons, disfiguring males, rape, robbery, dacoity, and specific cattle-related crimes.

It grants the Government of the Province the power to dissolve the governing body of a registered society and reconstitute or reorganize it. The government may entrust management of the society's affairs to the new governing body subject to conditions deemed fit. This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of West Pakistan on April 12, 1962.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Societies Registration Act, 1860 to specifically regulate religious institutions known as Deeni Madrassahs. It mandates that such institutions must be registered as societies, submit annual activity reports and audited accounts to the Registrar, and prohibits teaching militancy or sectarian hatred. The Act also repeals the earlier Societies Registration (Amendment) Ordinance, 2005.

It substitutes various terms within the original Act to reflect the new name and broader scope, including ring roads, strategic roads, and economic corridors. The legislation also introduces new definitions for key terms and adds provisions regarding fines, fees, and penalties for traffic violations.

It updates various sections to reflect new entities like development authorities and cooperative housing societies, while introducing specific definitions for electronic transactions and multi-storey buildings. The legislation also adjusts stamp duty rates and exemptions, particularly for transfers by public offices and auction allotments.

metadata.one_line: This Act prevents the spread of dourine by regulating horse registration and empowering inspectors and veterinary practitioners.
metadata.summary: The Dourine Act, 1910 provides for the prevention of the spread of dourine among horses. It establishes a system for registering entire horses used for breeding purposes and appoints inspectors and veterinary practitioners to enforce these regulations. The Act grants powers to inspect horses, order their segregation or destruction if infected, and provides for compensation to owners whose horses are destroyed or castrated. Appeals against decisions regarding compensation can be made to committees constituted by the Provincial Government.

name: PUNJAB TRANSFUSION OF SAFE BLOOD ORDINANCE 1999

metadata.one_line: Regulates safe blood transfusion, establishes an Authority, registers blood banks, and sets penalties for contravention in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the transfusion of safe and healthy blood free from viruses and infective agents. It establishes the Punjab Blood Transfusion Authority to register blood banks, issue licenses, and ensure bio-safety measures are followed. The law also creates District Safe Blood Transfusion Committees for awareness and voluntary donations, while prescribing penalties for contravention.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Trusts Act, 2020 to broaden the scope of trusts covered by replacing 'natural' with 'any' in various sections. It introduces a new definition for 'specialized trust' encompassing collective investment schemes, pension funds, and other financial vehicles regulated under the Anti-Money Laundering Act, 2010. The legislation mandates registration for all trusts and requires No Objection Certificates from regulators for specialized trusts to function legally.

It specifically targets six existing Ordinances from 2002 and three Acts from 2013, which establish various Government Colleges as universities. The primary mechanism involves substituting specific expressions in the long titles, preambles, and sections of these parent laws to reflect updated nomenclature, such as changing 'Government College University' to 'Government College... as the University'. The Act comes into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to increase fines for non-display of security featured or vanity number plates.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to prescribe higher penalties for failing to display a security featured number plate or a vanity plate on a motor vehicle. It inserts a new entry into the Twelfth Schedule of the Ordinance specifying increased fines for motorcycles, public service vehicles, and private cars/jeeps. The Act was passed by the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab and assented to by the Governor on February 15, 2018.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965.
metadata.parent_law: The Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965
metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to increase fines for non-display of security or vanity plates.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to prescribe higher penalties for failing to display security featured or vanity number plates on motor vehicles. It specifically inserts a new entry into the Twelfth Schedule of the Ordinance detailing fines ranging from Rs. 1000 to Rs. 5000 depending on the vehicle type. The Act applies to motorcycles, cars, jeeps, public service vehicles, and private carriers within Punjab.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles (Second Amendment) Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965.
metadata.parent_law: The Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965
metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to allow applications for personalized vanity plates.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to introduce provisions regarding personalized vanity plates. It allows vehicle owners to submit applications to the registering authority for allocation of these plates linked with a particular registration mark. The Act mandates that owners must display these plates on their motor vehicles and leaves specifications for issuance to be prescribed.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify
metadata.one_line: Amends section 44 of the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 regarding school buses and Metrobus operations.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to update exemptions in Section 44. Specifically, it adds school buses and buses operated under the Punjab Metrobus Authority to the list of exempted vehicles. It also clarifies exemptions for trailers used for purposes other than carrying goods for hire or reward when drawn by a vehicle with limited passenger capacity.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance 1965.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance 1965 by substituting a new schedule of violations and fines.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance 1965 to update penalties for traffic violations. It substitutes the Twelfth Schedule of the Ordinance with a comprehensive list of offenses ranging from speeding to mobile phone usage while driving. The new schedule specifies distinct fine amounts for motorcycles, cars/jeeps, and public service vehicles for each violation.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to require fitness certificates for motor cars in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to extend the mandatory fitness certificate regime from transport vehicles to private motor cars. It inserts a new section 39-A requiring motor cars listed in the Fifteenth Schedule to carry a valid certificate of fitness issued by the prescribed authority. The amendment also updates Form I and adds the Fifteenth Schedule to specify validity periods based on vehicle category and age, aiming to enhance road safety and improve air quality.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 for the purposes of registering and regulating the electric and hybrid vehicles, and for the ancillary matters.
amends: The Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 (XIX of 1965)
key_definitions: vehicle propelled mechanically or electrically either partially or completely
metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to regulate electric and hybrid vehicles in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to facilitate the registration and regulation of electric and hybrid vehicles in the Province of Punjab. It substitutes specific definitions regarding mechanically propelled vehicles to include electrically or hybrid-propelled ones. The legislation also updates registration forms and procedures for vehicle transfers and cancellations based on false information.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 regarding fitness certificates for motor cars.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to insert a new section on fitness certificates for motor cars. It updates Form I in the First Schedule to include specific vehicle categories and extends applicability beyond transport vehicles only. The Act also adds a Fifteenth Schedule detailing validity periods for different engine capacities.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965.
subjects: Punjab Motor Vehicle Transaction Licensees Act 2015
key_definitions: vehicle propelled mechanically or electrically either partially or completely
metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to regulate electric and hybrid vehicles in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to facilitate the registration and regulation of electric and hybrid vehicles. It updates definitions regarding mechanically propelled vehicles and modifies sections concerning document submission, registration marks, transfer cancellations, suspension orders, and application forms. The amendments also allow applications for registration through licensees under the Punjab Motor Vehicle Transaction Licensees Act 2015.

metadata.short_title: Provincial Motor Vehicles (First Amendment) Act 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965.
repeals: Provincial Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Ordinance 2025
metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to introduce e-traffic systems and penalty mechanisms.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to incorporate definitions for an e-traffic management system and the Punjab Safe Cities Authority. It establishes procedures for recording traffic violations electronically, issuing e-tickets, and recovering fines through vehicle impoundment or auction if unpaid. The Act also repeals the Provincial Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Ordinance 2025.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles (Third Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965.
metadata.one_line: Amends section 24 of the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 regarding vehicle registration and fees.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to update provisions related to motor vehicle registration. It requires owners or keepers of registered vehicles residing in the Province to register them with any registering authority within the Province. Additionally, it grants the Government the power to impose an additional fee as prescribed.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965.
metadata.max_penalty: fine up to rupees two thousand or cancellation of permit/licence
metadata.administering_body: Provincial Transport Authority / Regional Transport Authority
metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to regulate TNCs, permits for CVH/PVH, and impose penalties.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to introduce regulations for Commercial Vehicles for Hire (CVH) and Private Vehicles for Hire (PVH) operated through Digital Platforms for Passenger Transportation (DPPT). It establishes licensing requirements for Transportation Network Companies (TNCs), mandates permits for vehicle operation, and defines specific terms related to drivers and platforms. The Act also introduces penalties for violations regarding permits and TNC responsibilities, including fines up to two thousand rupees or licence cancellation.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles (Second Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or fine up to Rs. 40,000, or both
metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to include motor cycles and increase penalties for overloading.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to incorporate motor cycles into various sections and schedules. It significantly increases fines for vehicle overloading based on the percentage of excess weight and the number of axles. Additionally, it reduces the time limit for certain offences from six months to one month and updates references regarding fitness certificates.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965.
metadata.parent_law: The Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965
metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to allow 16-year-olds to drive small motorcycles with a permit.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to introduce provisions for juvenile driving permits. It allows persons aged sixteen or older to drive motor cycles up to 125 cc or equivalent electric motor cycles if they hold a specific permit issued by the licensing authority. Additionally, the Act omits certain words and sub-sections from section 89-B of the Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Waqf Properties (Amendment) Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Waqf Properties Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to five years and fine up to three times the amount of income derived from the waqf property or twenty-five million rupees
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Waqf Properties Ordinance, 1979 regarding registration, beneficial ownership, and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Waqf Properties Ordinance, 1979 to incorporate definitions related to anti-money laundering and beneficial ownership. It mandates the registration of waqf properties within ninety days and establishes penalties for non-compliance or wrongful possession. The legislation also requires reporting entities to disclose status and allows the Chief Administrator to provide information on waqf assets.

name: PUNJAB PROHIBITION OF KITE FLYING (AMENDMENT) ACT 2025

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Prohibition of Kite Flying (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Prohibition of Kite Flying Ordinance, 2001.
amends: The Punjab Prohibition of Kite Flying Ordinance, 2001
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Prohibition of Kite Flying Ordinance, 2001 regarding definitions, trial procedures, and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Prohibition of Kite Flying Ordinance, 2001 to update definitions of 'child' and 'guardian'. It modifies trial procedures for offenders and adjusts penalties for manufacturing or transporting kites. The Act also omits specific sections related to children's offenses and updates recovery mechanisms for fines.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Protected Areas (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Protected Areas Act 2020.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Protected Areas Act 2020 to incorporate ecotourism provisions and strengthen penalties.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Protected Areas Act 2020 to introduce specific definitions regarding ecotourism and wildlife boards. It inserts a new section on sustainable ecotourism practices that benefit local communities while conserving natural heritage. The legislation also strengthens administrative oversight by substituting the Director General, Wildlife and Parks for previous departments and increases penalties for contraventions.

name: LAHORE COLLEGE FOR WOMEN UNIVERSITY, LAHORE (AMENDMENT) ACT 2004

metadata.short_title: The Lahore College for Women University, Lahore (Amendment) Act 2004
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Lahore College for Women University, Lahore Ordinance, 2002.
amends: The Lahore College for Women University, Lahore Ordinance, 2002
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2002 Ordinance to appoint the Education Minister as Pro-Chancellor and define Chancellor's powers.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Lahore College for Women University, Lahore Ordinance, 2002 to update its governance structure. It designates the Minister for Education of the Government of the Punjab as the Pro-Chancellor and outlines their duties. Additionally, it clarifies the Chancellor's functions by aligning them with the Governor's powers under Article 105 of the Constitution and adds three women members from the Provincial Assembly to the university body.

name: FATIMA JINNAH WOMEN UNIVERSITY, RAWALPINDI (AMENDMENT) ACT 2004

metadata.short_title: The Fatima Jinnah Women University, Rawalpindi (Amendment) Act 2004
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Fatima Jinnah Women University, Rawalpindi Ordinance, 1999.
amends: The Fatima Jinnah Women University, Rawalpindi Ordinance, 1999
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1999 Ordinance to define the Chancellor's functions as equivalent to a Provincial Governor.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Fatima Jinnah Women University, Rawalpindi Ordinance, 1999 by adding a new sub-section to section 8. The amendment stipulates that in performing his functions under the Ordinance, the Chancellor must act and be bound in the same manner as the Governor of a Province acts under Article 105 of the Constitution. The Act came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Women Protection Authority (Amendment) Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Women Protection Authority Act 2017.
amends: The Punjab Women Protection Authority Act, 2017
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2017 Act to add perks for the Chairperson and travelling allowance for members.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Women Protection Authority Act, 2017 by inserting two new subsections into section 3. The amendments specify that the Chairperson shall receive perks and privileges determined by the Government and that members shall receive a travelling allowance for attending meetings as determined by the Authority. It came into force immediately upon publication.

name: PROTECTION AGAINST HARASSMENT OF WOMEN AT THE WORKPLACE (AMENDMENT) ACT 2021

metadata.short_title: The Protection against Harassment of Women at the Workplace (Amendment) Act 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Protection against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act 2010
amends: Protection against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act 2010
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2010 Act to define Ombudsperson tenure and resignation procedures.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Protection against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act 2010 by adding subsections to section 7. It specifies that the Ombudsperson holds office for four years without eligibility for extension or re-appointment. Additionally, it allows the Ombudsperson to resign by writing addressed to the Governor. The Act came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Women Protection Authority Ordinance, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance for the establishment of the Punjab Women Protection Authority.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Women Protection Authority to protect women against violence in the province.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Punjab Women Protection Authority to provide a comprehensive system for the protection, relief, and rehabilitation of women against violence. The Authority is a body corporate with powers to establish protection centers, monitor the administration, and execute government policies regarding women's safety. It defines the composition of the Authority, including ex-officio members from various departments and nominated non-official members, along with their qualifications and tenure.

name: PUNJAB COMMISSION ON THE STATUS OF WOMEN (AMENDMENT) ACT 2022

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Commission on the Status of Women (Amendment) Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Commission on the Status of Women Act 2014.
amends: The Punjab Commission on the Status of Women Act, 2014
subjects: Commission on the Status of Women
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2014 Act by omitting subsection (3) of section 4 regarding the Commission.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Commission on the Status of Women Act, 2014. It specifically directs the omission of subsection (3) from section 4 of the original 2014 legislation. The amendment was passed by the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab and received assent from the Governor on October 21, 2022, coming into force immediately upon publication.

name: GHAZI UNIVERSITY, DERA GHAZI KHAN (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE 2015

metadata.short_title: Ghazi University, Dera Ghazi Khan (Amendment) Ordinance 2015
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Ghazi University, Dera Ghazi Khan Act 2012.
metadata.parent_law: Ghazi University, Dera Ghazi Khan Act 2012
amends: Ghazi University, Dera Ghazi Khan Act 2012
metadata.one_line: Amends the Ghazi University Act 2012 to mandate female representation in faculty and leadership roles.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Ghazi University, Dera Ghazi Khan Act 2012 to enhance gender inclusivity within the institution. It substitutes the term 'woman' with 'person' in section 11 while inserting specific requirements for female principals, lecturers, persons, and experts in various clauses of sections 21 and 26. The amendments ensure that at least one female principal, three female lecturers, one female person, two female experts, one female individual, and one female expert are included in the respective categories.

name: GHAZI UNIVERSITY, DERA GHAZI KHAN (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE 2015

metadata.short_title: The Ghazi University, Dera Ghazi Khan (Amendment) Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Ghazi University, Dera Ghazi Khan Act 2012.
amends: The Ghazi University, Dera Ghazi Khan Act, 2012
repeals: The Ghazi University, Dera Ghazi Khan (Amendment) Ordinance, 2015
metadata.one_line: Amends the Ghazi University Act 2012 to mandate female representation in staff and leadership roles.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Ghazi University, Dera Ghazi Khan Act 2012 to substitute the word 'woman' with 'person' in section 11. It further inserts requirements for female principals, lecturers, persons, and experts into sections 21 and 26 of the said Act. The Ordinance promulgated on June 26, 2015, is repealed by this Act.

name: GHAZI UNIVERSITY, DERA GHAZI KHAN (AMENDMENT) ACT 2015

metadata.short_title: The Ghazi University, Dera Ghazi Khan (Amendment) Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Ghazi University, Dera Ghazi Khan Act 2012.
amends: The Ghazi University, Dera Ghazi Khan Act, 2012
repeals: The Ghazi University, Dera Ghazi Khan (Amendment) Ordinance, 2015
metadata.one_line: Amends the Ghazi University Act 2012 to mandate female representation in staff and leadership roles.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Ghazi University, Dera Ghazi Khan Act 2012 to ensure gender inclusivity within the university's administration and faculty. Specifically, it substitutes 'woman' with 'person' in one section while inserting requirements for female principals, lecturers, experts, and other staff members in various clauses. Additionally, it repeals a previous Amendment Ordinance from 2015.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Public Service Commission (Amendment) Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act, further to amend the Punjab Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1978.
amends: The Punjab Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1978
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1978 Ordinance regarding PSC member terms and female candidate qualifications.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1978 to update provisions on member appointments and candidate qualifications. It extends eligibility for women from both public and private sectors with qualifications prescribed by government rules. Additionally, it modifies the term of office for PSC members to three years without reappointment eligibility, allowing a residual period appointment as Chairman if not less than six months.

metadata.short_title: Agricultural Pesticide Rules, 1973
metadata.parent_law: Agricultural Pesticides Ordinance, 1971 (II of 1971)
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the registration, manufacture, sale, labeling, and safety precautions regarding agricultural pesticides in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the framework for the registration and licensing of agricultural pesticides, including procedures for application, testing, and renewal. They specify conditions for storage, labeling, and advertising, as well as the duties of inspectors and government analysts. The document also details first aid measures and antidotes for various types of pesticide poisoning.

name: CRITERIA FOR FUNDING TO ATTEND WORKSHOPS SEMINARS CONFERENCES

metadata.short_title: PARB Regulation (Holding of workshops)
metadata.one_line: Sets criteria and procedures for PARB funding of agricultural research workshops and conferences.
metadata.summary: This notification establishes the eligibility criteria and funding procedures for organizing scientific conferences, workshops, and seminars under the Punjab Agricultural Research Board. It specifies that events must be arranged by Punjab-based or HEC-recognized institutions and relate to high-priority research themes. The document outlines merit criteria for funding approval, including expenditures borne by organizers, number of foreign delegates, and expected participants, with a maximum limit of five sponsored foreign delegates per conference.

name: CRITERIA FOR FUNDING TO ORGANIZE SCIENTIFIC CONFERENCES

metadata.short_title: PARB Regulation (Travel Grant)
metadata.one_line: Sets criteria for PARB funding to attend scientific conferences abroad.
metadata.summary: This regulation outlines the eligibility, funding, and merit criteria for scientists from public sector agricultural research or educational institutions in Punjab to receive funding for attending international conferences. Funding covers economy class air tickets, registration fees, visa fees, and per diem charges, subject to specific conditions regarding previous fund usage and presentation type. The Executive Committee approves applications based on a monthly share of the total allocation.

name: DIRECTORATE OF FLORICULTURE (TRAINING & RESEARCH), PUNJAB, LAHORE SERVICES RULES, 1996

metadata.short_title: The Directorate of Floriculture (Training & Research), Punjab, Lahore Services Rules, 1996
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Civil Servants Act, 1974 (VIII of 1974)
metadata.administering_body: Agriculture Department, Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Governor of Punjab regarding recruitment, qualifications, and promotion for staff in the Directorate of Floriculture.
metadata.summary: These rules were made by the Governor of the Punjab under the Punjab Civil Servants Act, 1974 to regulate the Directorate of Floriculture (Training & Research). They specify the method of recruitment, minimum educational qualifications, age limits, and experience requirements for various gazetted and non-gazetted posts. The rules also outline the basis for promotion on seniority-cum-fitness and initial recruitment percentages for different functional groups within the department.

name: i. UAF Pay Scales and Allowances Sstatutes 2005

metadata.short_title: The University of Agriculture Faisalabad Employees (Revised Basic Pay Scales, Allowances and Pension) (BS-1 to 22) Statutes, 2005

amends: The University of Agriculture Faisalabad Employees (Revised Basic Pay Scales and Fringe Benefits) (BS.1-22) Statutes, 2001
metadata.one_line: Statutes revising pay scales, allowances, and pension for University of Agriculture Faisalabad employees effective July 1, 2005.
metadata.summary: This notification approves revised basic pay scales, allowances, and pension statutes for the University of Agriculture Faisalabad. It applies to all existing employees as of June 30, 2005, replacing the 2001 statutes. The document details specific rates for house rent, medical, conveyance, and other special allowances, along with qualification pay and senior post allowances. An option is provided for existing employees to choose between the old or new scales within 60 days.

name: ii. UAF Pay Scales and Allowances Statutes, 2007

metadata.short_title: The University of Agriculture Faisalabad Employees (Revised Basic Pay Scales and Allowances) (BS 1 To 22) Statutes, 2007

amends: The University of Agriculture Faisalabad Employees (Revised Basic Pay Scales, Allowances and Pension) (BS 1-22) Statutes, 2005
metadata.one_line: Statutes revising basic pay scales and allowances for University of Agriculture Faisalabad employees effective July 1, 2007.
metadata.summary: These Statutes revise the basic pay scales and allowances for employees of the University of Agriculture Faisalabad. They apply to existing employees and contract employees as of June 30, 2007, fixing their pay in the new revised scales effective July 1, 2007. The document details annual increments, special allowances, dearness allowance freezes, and general modifications to previous statutes.

name: iii. UAF Pay Scales and Allowances Statutes, 2008

metadata.short_title: The University of Agriculture Faisalabad Employees (Revised Basic Pay Scales and Allowances) (BPS-1 to 22) Statutes, 2008

amends: The University of Agriculture Faisalabad Employees (Revised Basic Pay Scales and Allowances) (BS-1 to 22) Statutes, 2007
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab, Agriculture Department
metadata.one_line: Revises basic pay scales and allowances for University of Agriculture Faisalabad employees effective July 1, 2008.
metadata.summary: This document revises the revised basic pay scales and allowances for employees of the University of Agriculture, Faisalabad. It applies to existing employees and contract employees as of June 30, 2008, adjusting their pay to new scales effective July 1, 2008. The statutes detail specific rates for conveyance, medical, and other allowances, along with annual increment conditions.

metadata.short_title: Postgraduate GPA and CGPA Regulations
amends: Statute and Regulations relating to MSc (Hons)/MPhil/MS
metadata.one_line: Regulates postgraduate GPA and CGPA requirements for various degrees in Punjab universities.
metadata.summary: These regulations establish the Grade Point Average (GPA) and Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) scales for Master of Arts, Master of Science, M.Sc. (Hons.), M.Phil., M.S., MBA, and Doctor of Philosophy programs. They specify minimum CGPA thresholds required to remain on roll, qualify for degree awards, or repeat courses. The rules also outline conditions under which admission is cancelled if students fail to meet specific GPA standards at the end of academic years.

name: PROCEDURE FOR FUNDING OF CGS PROJECTS BY PARB

metadata.short_title: PARB Regulation (Funding Procedure)
metadata.one_line: Regulates the procedure for funding research projects by the Punjab Agricultural Research Board.
metadata.summary: This regulation outlines the procedure for identifying priority research areas and soliciting proposals from public sector organizations. It details the scrutiny process involving Technical Working Groups, selection criteria based on scientific competence, and financial arrangements including block allocations and honorariums. The document also establishes administrative powers for the Chief Executive regarding fund release, project modification, and audit.

name: Punjab Agricultural Development & Supplies Corporation Employees Gratuity Regulations 1980

metadata.short_title: PAD&SC Employees Gratuity Regulations, 1980
metadata.parent_law: Punjab Agricultural Development & Supplies Corporation Act, 1973 (Punjab Act No.XXI of 1973)
metadata.one_line: Regulations governing gratuity eligibility, rates, and payment procedures for PAD&SC employees in Punjab.
metadata.summary: These Regulations provide a lump-sum grant (gratuity) to employees of the Punjab Agricultural Development & Supplies Corporation holding non-pensionable posts. Eligibility is based on completing 10 years of qualifying service or specific events like death or abolition of post, with rates varying by years of service. The document defines terms such as 'Family', 'Misconduct', and 'Qualifying Service', outlines nomination procedures for death benefits, and establishes a separate gratuity fund.

name: PUNJAB AGRICULTURAL DEVELOPMENT & SUPPLIES CORPORATION EMPLOYEES SERVICE RULES 1982

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Agricultural Development & Supplies Corporation Employees Service Rules, 1982

metadata.administering_body: Agriculture Department, Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Rules governing service conditions, recruitment, and benefits for employees of the Punjab Agricultural Development & Supplies Corporation.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the terms and conditions of service for employees of the Punjab Agricultural Development & Supplies Corporation. They cover classification of posts, appointment procedures, probationary periods, pay scales, gratuity, suspension, punishment, and retirement. The rules also define key terms such as 'Duty', 'Pay', and 'Competent Authority' and specify eligibility criteria including Pakistani nationality.

name: PUNJAB AGRICULTURAL PRODUCE MARKETS (MARKET COMMITTEES PROVINCIAL FUND) RULES, 1980

metadata.summary: These rules were made by the Governor of the Punjab to constitute a Board for managing the Market Committees Provincial Fund. The Board comprises a Chairman, government officers, and representatives from various classes of market committees. It empowers the Board to undertake development projects, invest funds, organize modern markets, and supervise market committees, with provisions for financial contributions, audits, and suspension if necessary.

metadata.short_title: Punjab Agricultural Research Board Rules 2009
metadata.parent_law: Punjab Agricultural Research Board Act, 1997 (XIV of 1997)
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab, Agriculture Department
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of the Punjab to regulate the Punjab Agricultural Research Board under the 1997 Act.
metadata.summary: These rules were promulgated by the Government of the Punjab in exercise of powers under section 12 of the Punjab Agricultural Research Board Act, 1997. They establish the composition of the Board and its committees, define key terms related to research and stakeholders, and outline the Board's functions regarding research planning, funding, and collaboration. The rules also detail financial management, including budget preparation, audit responsibilities, and procurement procedures for the Board.

name: PUNJAB AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH BOARD SERVICE RULES 2009

metadata.short_title: Punjab Agricultural Research Board Service Rules 2009
metadata.parent_law: Punjab Agricultural Research Board Act 1997 (XIV of 1997)

metadata.summary: These rules are made under section 12 of the Punjab Agricultural Research Board Act 1997 to regulate the service of the Board. They define key terms, specify nomenclatures and recruitment methods for various posts, and outline procedures for performance evaluation, incentives, compensatory leaves, and gratuity benefits. The rules apply to employees appointed in the service of the Board under section 9 of the Act.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Agricultural Produce Markets (General) Rules, 1979
metadata.parent_law: Section 35 of the Punjab Agricultural Produce Markets Ordinance, 1978 (Punjab Ordinance No. XXIII of 1978)
metadata.max_penalty: one hundred rupees for each breach
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Governor of Punjab to regulate agricultural produce markets, licences, fees, and market committees under the 1978 Ordinance.

The rules also outline processes for site inspections, confidentiality requests, and modifications to existing licenses, ensuring a structured approach to regulatory oversight in the electricity sector.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Electricity Duty Rules, 2012

It sets specific targets for banning single-use plastics, raising public awareness, and implementing Extended Producer Responsibility projects. The rules specify that charges are calculated based on pollution levels multiplied by actual production and applicable rates, payable biannually to the Government Treasury or National Bank of Pakistan.

They specify conditions such as keeping packages sealed during transit and delivering consignments directly to designated offices for inspection. The rules also outline application forms, authority requirements for removal from bonded warehouses, and fee exemptions.

metadata.short_title: The Entertainments Duty Rules, 1958
metadata.parent_law: Entertainments Duty Act, 1958
repeals: The Sind Entertainments Duty Act, 1923
The Punjab Entertainments Duty Act, 1936
The North West Frontier Province Entertainments Duty Act, 1937
The Baluchistan Entertainments Duty Regulation, 1942 (1 to 1942)
The Khairpur Entertainments Duty Act, 1945
The Bahawalpur State Entertainment Duty Act, 1948
The West Pakistan Entertainments Duty Act, 1957
key_definitions: Deputy District Officer/Excise and Taxation Officer
metadata.administering_body: Government (via Treasury Officers, Collector, Deputy District Officer)
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Provincial Government to regulate entertainments duty, stamps, tickets, and refunds under the Entertainments Duty Act, 1958.
metadata.summary: These rules were made by the Provincial Government in exercise of powers under Section 11 of the Entertainments Duty Act, 1958. They govern the supply, purchase, and issue of duty stamps for entertainments, including specific provisions for press representatives and military personnel. The rules establish procedures for ticketing, refunds of unused or damaged stamps, inspection of accounts, and the recovery of unpaid duties.

metadata.short_title: the Matches (Excise Duty) Rules, 1934
metadata.parent_law: Matches (Excise Duty) Order, 1934
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Governor in Council regarding appeals and search powers for matches under the Matches (Excise Duty) Order, 1934.
metadata.summary: These rules were promulgated on October 12, 1934, by the Governor in Council to regulate appeals against Collector orders and define search powers. They allow Excise officers above the rank of Jamadar or peon, and Police officers above the rank of Constable, to search for and seize illegally imported or manufactured matches. The rules also specify that time spent obtaining an authenticated order is excluded from limitation periods.

name: PUNJAB EDUCATION CESS ON CLUBS RULES 2011

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Education Cess on Clubs Rules, 2011
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Finance Act, 2011 (XV of 2011)
metadata.administering_body: Excise & Taxation Department of the Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Governor of Punjab to levy and collect education cess on clubs under the Punjab Finance Act, 2011.
metadata.summary: These rules empower the Assessing Authority to assess and collect an education cess from clubs operating in Punjab. Clubs are required to submit monthly returns accompanied by payment receipts within seven days of the month's close. The rules outline procedures for assessment, record maintenance, recovery of dues as arrears of land revenue, and the process for filing appeals to the Collector.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Excisable Articles Confiscation Orders
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Excise Act, 1914
repeals: Financial Commissioner's notification No.19, dated the 18th January, 1915
metadata.one_line: Orders the disposal and destruction of confiscated excisable articles by collectors.
metadata.summary: These orders delegate powers to Commissioners and Collectors regarding the revision of orders passed by subordinate Excise Officers. They provide specific rules for the disposal of articles confiscated under sections 78 and 79 of the Punjab Excise Act, 1914. Confiscated liquors and hemp drugs must be destroyed, while other items may be sold as directed by the Collector, with proceeds credited to the Excise Department.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Excise Barrier Rules, 1931
metadata.one_line: Rules empowering the Excise Commissioner to establish outposts for preventing smuggling and conducting vehicle searches.
metadata.summary: These rules authorize the Excise Commissioner to establish excise outposts on roads or ferries to prevent the smuggling of excisable articles or opium. Drivers must stop their vehicles or animals at these outposts for search by an excise officer before proceeding. Complaints regarding wrongful detention are to be recorded in a specific book submitted monthly to the District Magistrate.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Farm Houses Tax Rules, 2012
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Finance Act, 2011 (XV of 2011)
metadata.administering_body: Excise & Taxation Department, Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Governor of Punjab to levy and collect tax on farm houses under the Punjab Finance Act 2011.
metadata.summary: These rules provide the framework for assessing and collecting tax on farm houses within the Province of Punjab. They define key terms such as 'farm owner' and 'Assessing Authority', outlining the duties of officials in inspecting properties and maintaining records. The document establishes procedures for filing returns, issuing notices for non-compliance, determining tax amounts, and recovering unpaid taxes as arrears of land revenue.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Liquor License Rules, 1932
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the grant, renewal, and conditions of licenses for the sale and manufacture of various types of liquor in Punjab.
metadata.summary: These rules classify different types of liquor licenses, including those for foreign liquor, country spirit, and denatured spirit, specifying the authorities empowered to grant them. They regulate the conditions under which licenses are issued to individuals, companies, societies, or partnerships, ensuring compliance with local restrictions and provincial government notifications. The document also details specific regulations for manufacturing country fermented liquor for home consumption or special occasions, as well as procedures for reducing country spirit and producing vinegar.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Manufactured Drugs Rules, 1932
metadata.territorial_extent: all the territories for the time being administered by the Governor of the Punjab in Council
metadata.parent_law: Dangerous Drugs Act, 1930 (II of 1930)
repeals: Punjab Government Notification No. 1161-E. & S., dated 16th February 1931
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the manufacture, possession, and transport of medicinal opium and morphine derivatives in Punjab.
metadata.summary: These rules were made by the Punjab Government under the Dangerous Drugs Act, 1930 to regulate the manufacture of medicinal opium and preparations containing morphine or cocaine. They define key terms such as licensed druggists, medical practitioners, and opium alkaloidal derivatives, and specify who may manufacture these substances based on their licenses and professional status. The rules also cover the inter-provincial import, export, transport, possession, and sale of manufactured drugs, while establishing an appeal mechanism to the Financial Commissioner for orders made by Excise Officers.

name: PUNJAB MOTOR VEHICLE TRANSACTION LICENSEES RULES 2015

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Motor Vehicle Transaction Licensees Rules, 2015
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Motor Vehicle Transaction Licensees Act, 2015
metadata.administering_body: Excise & Taxation Department, Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Governor of Punjab to regulate licensing of motor vehicle transaction licensees under the Act of 2015.
metadata.summary: These rules are made in exercise of powers under Section 12 of the Punjab Motor Vehicle Transaction Licensees Act, 2015. They establish eligibility criteria for applicants, define the role of the licensing authority, and outline procedures for license application, renewal, and permit issuance for staff. The rules also mandate record maintenance, fee structures, and training requirements for licensees.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Motor Vehicles Rules, 1969
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Punjab except the Tribal Areas
metadata.parent_law: West Pakistan Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965
repeals: Punjab Motor Vehicles Rules, 1940
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Governor of West Pakistan to regulate motor vehicles in Punjab, superseding earlier rules.
metadata.summary: These rules were promulgated by the Governor of West Pakistan on September 1, 1969, under specific sections of the West Pakistan Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965. They apply to the whole of Punjab except the Tribal Areas and come into force immediately. The document supersedes the Punjab Motor Vehicles Rules, 1940, and defines terms such as 'articulated vehicle', 'Forwarding Agent', and 'Motor Vehicles Examiner'. It establishes licensing authorities (Superintendent of Police), outlines fee payment procedures, and sets regulations for vehicle registration marks and colors.

name: PUNJAB OPIUM CONFISCATION AND REWARDS ORDERS, 1934

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Opium Confiscation and Rewards Orders
metadata.parent_law: The Opium Act, 1878 (I of 1878)
metadata.one_line: Rules regarding the disposal of confiscated opium and payment of rewards under the Opium Act, 1878.
metadata.summary: These orders were made by the Punjab Government in exercise of powers under the Opium Act, 1878. They govern the delivery of confiscated items to district Collectors and their destruction under the Collector's orders. The document also establishes a framework for granting rewards for information regarding opium offences, specifying limits based on the authority granting the reward.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Paddy Husking Tax Rules, 1978
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1978
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Governor of Punjab to levy and administer tax on paddy husking in rice mills.
metadata.summary: These rules empower the Governor of the Punjab to impose a tax on owners or occupants of rice husking mills. They define key terms such as 'Assesse' and establish the roles of the District Excise & Taxation Officer and the Director, Excise & Taxation. The rules mandate the maintenance of specific registers, the filing of monthly returns, and the deposit of tax within seven days of the month's close. Furthermore, they outline procedures for appeals against orders, inspections of stocks and books, and the imposition of penalties.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Prohibition (Enforcement of Hadd) Rules, 1979
metadata.parent_law: The Prohibition (Enforcement of Hadd) Order, 1979
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab, Excise and Taxation Department
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Governor of Punjab to enforce the Prohibition (Enforcement of Hadd) Order, 1979.
metadata.summary: These rules were promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab in exercise of powers under the Prohibition (Enforcement of Hadd) Order, 1979. They define key terms such as 'Order', 'Authorized Medical Officer', and 'Licence' regarding intoxicants and opium. The rules outline the powers of various excise officers, procedures for medical examinations to detect intoxication, limits on detention, and disposal of seized articles.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Restaurant (Consumption of Liquor) Rules, 1939
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Excise Act, 1914
metadata.one_line: Rules regulating the consumption of liquor in restaurants in Punjab via exemption certificates.
metadata.summary: These rules were made by the Governor of Punjab under the Punjab Excise Act, 1914 to regulate liquor consumption in restaurants. They establish a system where proprietors can apply for exemption certificates from the Collector to sell liquor in restricted areas. The rules define specific terms like 'restaurant' and 'exemptee', set operating hours based on seasons, and impose conditions regarding cleanliness, public order, and prohibition of sales to minors or bad characters.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Sugar (Excise Duty) Rules, 1935
metadata.parent_law: Sugar (Excise Duty) Order, 1934
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Governor in Council regarding appeals and search powers for sugar excise duty in Punjab.
metadata.summary: These rules were made under the Sugar (Excise Duty) Order, 1934, to regulate appeals from Collectors to Commissioners and the Financial Commissioner. They grant specific Excise and Police officers the power to search for illegally imported or manufactured sugar and to seize such goods. The rules define the hierarchy of authority for reviewing cases and passing final orders.

name: THE PUNJAB BHANG IMPORT EXPORT TRANSPORT AND POSSESSION ORDERS

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Bhang Import, Export, Transport and Possession Orders
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Excise Act, I of 1914
repeals: Punjab Government notification No.890, dated 29th June 1915
metadata.one_line: Regulates the import, export, transport and possession of bhang in Punjab under the Punjab Excise Act.
metadata.summary: These orders regulate the import, export, transport, and possession of bhang within the Province of Punjab. They define specific conditions for licensed sellers to import or export bhang from other provinces, including permit requirements, duty payments, and quantity limits. The rules also govern government transit by post and establish restrictions on non-licensed possession.

name: The PUNJAB BONDED SPIRIT WAREHOUSE RULES

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Bonded Spirit Warehouse Rules
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Excise Act, 1914
metadata.one_line: Rules governing bonded spirit warehouses in Punjab, defining registers and applying distillery rules.
metadata.summary: These rules define the Punjab Bonded Spirit Warehouse Rules and establish their application to bonded spirit warehouses. They specify that certain sections of the Punjab Distillery Rules apply mutatis mutandis to these warehouses. The rules mandate the maintenance of specific registers by the Officer-in-charge, including general registers, store vats lists, employment lists, inspection diaries, and various forms for tracking spirit receipt, issue, bottling, and duty payment.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Brewery Rules, 1932
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Excise Act, 1 of 1914
metadata.administering_body: Excise and Taxation Department, Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Rules governing licensing, security deposits, and operations for breweries in Punjab.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the framework for obtaining licenses to operate a brewery in Punjab. They define key terms related to brewing processes and equipment, set requirements for security deposits and staff establishment, and regulate the supply of beer to licensed vendors.

name: THE PUNJAB CHARAS IMPORT EXPORT TRANSPORT AND POSSESSION ORDERS

repeals: Punjab Government notification no. 449, dated 19th march 1915
metadata.one_line: Regulates the import, export, transport and possession of charas in Punjab under the Punjab Excise Act.
metadata.summary: These orders regulate the import, export, transport, and possession of charas within the Punjab. They define terms like 'import' and 'export' based on the Dangerous Drugs Act, 1930, and restrict movement to bonded warehouses or licensed vendors. The rules specify conditions for obtaining passes from the Financial Commissioner and limit possession quantities for non-licensed persons.

name: THE PUNJAB CHARAS PERMIT AND PASS RULES

metadata.summary: These rules were promulgated on November 13, 1935, by the Financial Commissioner of Punjab. The document establishes a framework for issuing permits and passes related to charas within the province.

Financial Commissioner's Notification No. 50, dated the 19th March, 1915

metadata.summary: These rules were made by the Financial Commissioner of Punjab to establish bonded warehouses for the deposit of charas. They outline the management of these warehouses, including the appointment of officers and the maintenance of daily and personal registers for deposits and removals. The rules also specify procedures for transferring charas between warehouses within two years of registration and the marking of packages upon entry into Punjab.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Chemical Works Rules
metadata.parent_law: Punjab Excise Act, 1914
metadata.administering_body: Excise and Taxation Department, Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the manufacture, storage, and licensing of medicinal preparations containing alcohol in Chemical Works.
metadata.summary: These rules define terms related to chemical works for manufacturing medicinal preparations containing alcohol. They establish requirements for obtaining licenses, including application details, security deposits, and annual fees. The rules also outline conditions for inspections, stock disposal upon business closure, and the Excise Commissioner's power to amend the rules.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Distillery Rules
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Excise Act, 1 of 1914
metadata.administering_body: Excise and Taxation Department, Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the grant, conditions, and revocation of licenses for distilleries in Punjab.
metadata.summary: These rules provide the framework for granting licenses to operate distilleries within the Province of Punjab. They define specific technical terms related to spirit production, such as wash, low wines, and rectified spirit. The rules outline the application process, security deposit requirements, and the powers of the Excise Commissioner regarding license cancellation or forfeiture.

name: THE PUNJAB EXCISE BEER BOTTLES RULES 1943 APPENDIX

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Excise Beer Bottles Rules
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Act, 1914
repeals: The Punjab Beer Bottles Rules
metadata.one_line: Regulates the storage, transport, and sale of beer bottles in Punjab under excise licensing.
metadata.summary: These rules define specific terms related to beer bottles, breweries, and licensed vendors within Punjab. They establish strict limits on the possession and storage of empty bottles for various categories of persons, including authorized agents and permit holders. The document also prohibits the export of empty bottles from Punjab and restricts transportation to licensed entities, while exempting lawfully filled bottles and small quantities for domestic use.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Excise Bottles Rules
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Excise Act, 1914
amends: Punjab Excise Bottles Rules (No.1178-Ex., dated the 24th February 1942)
key_definitions: licensed vendor of foreign liquor or country spirit
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the use, sale, storage, and export of excise bottles in Punjab under the Punjab Excise Act, 1914.
metadata.summary: These rules substitute the existing Punjab Excise Bottles Rules promulgated on February 24, 1942. They regulate the use of excise bottles strictly for bottling spirit under a license granted by the Punjab Excise Act, 1914. The rules impose limits on the possession and storage of excise bottles by licensed vendors and authorized agents, while prohibiting their sale to unauthorized persons or export without specific orders. Exceptions are made for lawfully filled liquor and domestic household use.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Excise Fiscal Orders
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Excise Act, 1 of 1914
metadata.administering_body: Excise and Taxation Department, Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: The Punjab Excise Fiscal Orders set rates of duty on spirits, beer, bhang, and medicinal preparations in Punjab.
metadata.summary: These orders establish the rates of excise duty leviable on various types of spirit, sweets, beer, and medicinal preparations manufactured or sold in the Punjab. They define specific duties for plain country spirit, rectified spirit, and other sorts, while providing exemptions for certain medicinal preparations and bhang under specific conditions. The document also outlines rules regarding wastage scales, transport passes for liquor moving between districts, and price fixes for excise opium.

name: THE PUNJAB EXCISE GRANT OF REWARD INFORMERS AND OTHER PERSONS RULES 1966

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Excise (Grant of Reward Informers and Other Persons) Rules, 1966
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Excise Act, 1 of 1914
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab, Excise and Taxation Department
metadata.one_line: Rules empowering designated authorities to grant rewards to informers under the Punjab Excise Act, 1914.
metadata.summary: These rules empower specific authorities within the Excise & Taxation department to grant financial rewards to officers, informers, and other persons for assistance under the Punjab Excise Act, 1914. The rules specify monetary limits for different officials, allow for disbursement without the payee's attendance, and authorize the Excise Commissioner to issue directions on procedure and accounts verification. They were promulgated by the Provincial Government in exercise of powers conferred by section 58 of the Punjab Excise Act.

name: THE PUNJAB EXCISE POWERS AND APPEAL ORDERS

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Excise Powers and Appeal Orders
metadata.parent_law: Punjab Excise Act 1 of 1914

metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab, Excise and Taxation Department
metadata.one_line: This order defines classes of excise officers and their powers regarding seizure, arrest, and licensing under the Punjab Excise Act.
metadata.summary: This document establishes three classes of Excise Officers (1st, 2nd, and 3rd class) and lists the specific personnel belonging to each group. It details the powers granted to these officers, including the authority to seize intoxicants, search persons and vehicles, and arrest individuals suspected of offences related to liquor, opium, or dangerous drugs. The order also outlines restrictions on licensing shops in villages and towns and designates the Director General Excise and Taxation Punjab as an Excise Commissioner.

name: THE PUNJAB HEMP CULTIVATION AND BHANG PERMIT AND PASS RULES
