metadata.one_line: Rules governing hemp cultivation for religious institutions and permits for bhang transport in British India.
metadata.summary: These rules regulate the cultivation of hemp plants by managers or heads of temples, dharamsala, or similar religious institutions. They grant special licenses subject to specific conditions regarding land usage, consumption limits, and prohibitions on sale. The document also establishes procedures for obtaining permits and passes for the inter-provincial import, export, and transport of bhang, including requirements for duty payment and route adherence.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Hotel Tax Rules, 1992
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Finance Act, 1965 (W.P. Act I of 1965)
metadata.administering_body: Excise and Taxation Department, Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Punjab to levy and collect hotel tax under the Punjab Finance Act, 1965.
metadata.summary: These rules were promulgated by the Government of the Punjab in exercise of powers conferred by the Punjab Finance Act, 1965. They establish procedures for hotel owners to submit monthly tax statements, undergo verification of lodging units, and maintain specific registers. The rules also outline processes for assessing tax, issuing demand notices, and handling appeals or refunds.

name: THE PUNJAB IMPORT AND POSSESSION OF GANJA ORDERS

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Import and Possession of Ganja Orders
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Excise Act, 1914 (I of 1914)
metadata.one_line: Prohibits the import and possession of ganja within Punjab under the Punjab Excise Act, 1914.
metadata.summary: This Order prohibits the import and possession of ganja or any preparation thereof within the Punjab. It is issued by the Government of the Punjab in exercise of powers conferred by sections 24(4) and 17(a) of the Punjab Excise Act, 1914. The prohibition applies to the whole of Pakistan as per the jurisdiction derived from the enacting authority.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Intoxicants Confiscation Rules
metadata.number: Notification No. 5509-E&S dated 19.10.1932 (revised) / Notification 2002-2003/323-Excise & Taxation (P) I
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Excise Act, 1914
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the confiscation, disposal, and sale of illicit liquor and hemp drugs in Punjab.
metadata.summary: These rules were promulgated by the Government of the Punjab under the powers of the Punjab Excise Act, 1914. They establish procedures for handing over confiscated articles to the Collector and disposing of them based on their nature and fitness for consumption. Illicit liquor and unfit hemp drugs are to be destroyed, while fit items may be sold or disposed of as directed by the Excise Commissioner. Proceeds from sales are credited to the Provincial Excise Department.

name: THE PUNJAB INTOXICANTS LICENSE AND SALE ORDERS

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Intoxicants License and Sale Orders
metadata.one_line: Sets limits on retail possession of intoxicants, licensing periods, localities, and restrictions on sales to specific persons in Punjab.
metadata.summary: These Orders regulate the retail sale of intoxicants in the Province of Punjab by defining maximum possession limits for various types of liquor. They establish rules regarding the duration of licenses, the localities where shops may be licensed, and the number of shops permitted in an area. The document further prohibits the sale of liquor to soldiers, police officers, intoxicated persons, and others, while also restricting the employment of individuals with infectious diseases by license holders.

name: THE PUNJAB LIQUOR IMPORT EXPORT TRANSPORT AND POSSESSION ORDERS

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Liquor Import, Export, Transport and Possession Orders
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Excise Act
metadata.administering_body: Excise and Taxation Department, Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Regulates import, export, transport, and possession of liquor in Punjab with specific duties and exceptions.
metadata.summary: These orders regulate the import, export, transport, and possession of various types of liquor within the Province of Punjab. They establish conditions for duty payment, define exceptions for private consumption and medicinal use, and outline procedures for exporting spirits from licensed distilleries. The document also prohibits the import of country fermented liquor and denatured spirit from Kashmir while allowing rectified spirit imports under specific bonded conditions.

name: THE PUNJAB LIQUOR PERMIT AND PASS RULES

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Liquor Permit and Pass Rules
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Excise Act (1 of 1914)
metadata.one_line: Rules governing permits and passes for importing, exporting, and transporting liquor and spirit in Punjab under the Punjab Excise Act.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the procedure for obtaining permits and passes required for importing, exporting, or transporting country spirit, rectified spirit, denatured spirit, and medicinal preparations containing spirit within Pakistan. They specify that passes granted in other provinces or NWFP are deemed valid under Punjab law if they cover specific consignments. The rules also detail requirements for bonded exports of medicinal preparations to other provinces, including bond execution, duty payment conditions, and waste allowances. Additionally, they outline the process for educational institutions to obtain permits for importing spirit for research or teaching purposes, including storage limits and usage restrictions.

name: THE PUNJAB PROFESSIONS AND TRADES TAX RULES 1977

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Professions and Trades Tax Rules, 1977
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Finance Act, 1977 (Act XV of 1977)
key_definitions: District Officer / Director, Excise and Taxation
District Officer/ Excise and Taxation Officer
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Governor of Punjab to levy and collect tax on professions and trades under the Punjab Finance Act, 1977.
metadata.summary: These rules empower the District Officer/ Director, Excise and Taxation to assess and collect tax payable under Section 3 of the Punjab Finance Act, 1977. They define key terms such as 'Tax', 'Principal Officer', and 'Treasury' and establish procedures for filing statements, paying tax, appealing orders, and maintaining registers. The rules also specify how tax is deducted from salaries of government servants and other public bodies.

name: THE PUNJAB SPIRITUOUS PREPARATIONS BONDED WAREHOUSE RULES

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Spirituous Preparations Bonded Warehouse Rules
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Excise Act, I of 1914
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the licensing, operation, supervision, and duty payment for spirituous preparations in bonded warehouses in Punjab.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the framework for private bonded warehouses in Punjab for storing medicinal and other spirituous preparations imported under bond. They outline the application process for licenses, daily operating hours, security requirements, and procedures for receiving and issuing goods. The rules also define allowances for transit loss, responsibilities regarding fire or theft, and conditions under which a license may be revoked.

name: THE PUNJAB SUPPLY AND SALE OF HEMP DRUGS RULES

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Supply and Sale of Hemp Drugs Rules
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the licensing, fees, and conditions for wholesale and retail sale of hemp drugs in Punjab.
metadata.summary: These rules establish four kinds of licenses for the vend of hemp drugs, distinguishing between wholesale and retail categories. They specify fee structures, requiring wholesale fees to be paid in advance while retail fees are fixed by auction or tender. The rules impose strict conditions on licensees regarding stock maintenance, minimum sale quantities, prohibited substances like chloral hydrate, and restrictions on holding licenses for spirits or opium.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Sweets (Manufacture) Rules, 1939
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Excise Act, 1914
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the manufacture, licensing, inspection, and labeling of sweets in Punjab under the Punjab Excise Act.
metadata.summary: These rules regulate the manufacture of sweets defined as fermented fruit or sugar mixtures without distillation. They establish a licensing system administered by the Financial Commissioner, requiring detailed entries of premises and utensils. The rules mandate strict labeling, record-keeping via entry books, and prohibit mixing foreign wine beyond specific proportions or adding excessive proof spirit.

name: THE PUNJAB URBAN IMMOVABLE PROPERTY TAX RULES 1958

The Sind Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1948
The North West Frontier Province Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1948

metadata.summary: These rules were promulgated on December 29, 1958, by the Government of West Pakistan to establish procedures for assessing and collecting urban immovable property tax. They define the powers of the Assessing Authority, including entering premises and examining documents, and outline duties such as preparing valuation lists and maintaining registers. The rules also specify mechanisms for filing objections, claiming exemptions based on bona fide residence, and recovering taxes or penalties as arrears of land revenue.

name: THE REAL ESTATE AGENTS AND MOTOR VEHICLES DEALERS (REGULATION OF BUSINESS) RULES 1980

metadata.short_title: The Real Estate Agents and Motor Vehicles Dealers (Regulation of Business) Rules, 1980
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Real Estate Agents and Motor Vehicles Dealers (Regulation of Business) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.administering_body: Excise and Taxation Department, Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Governor of Punjab to regulate the business of real estate agents and motor vehicles dealers.
metadata.summary: These rules were promulgated under the Punjab Real Estate Agents and Motor Vehicles Dealers (Regulation of Business) Ordinance, 1980 to regulate the business of real estate agents and motor vehicles dealers in the Province of Punjab. The document establishes procedures for registration and renewal of certificates, requiring a security deposit and prescribed fees. It sets maximum limits on commissions and remuneration chargeable by agents and dealers for various transactions. Additionally, it outlines the process for appeals against orders of the registering authority to the Director, Excise & Taxation.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Opium Rules, 1956
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of West Pakistan except the district of Khairpur
metadata.parent_law: The Opium Act, 1878

metadata.administering_body: Excise and Taxation Department, Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Rules regulating the possession, transport, import, export, sale, and licensing of opium in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: These rules regulate the possession, transport, import, export, and sale of opium and poppy-heads within the Province of West Pakistan. They define specific terms such as 'Pure Opium' and 'Excise Opium', establish licensing requirements for retail and wholesale sales, and set conditions for the registration of addicts. The rules also outline procedures for transit by post, disposal of confiscated items, and the granting of rewards for information.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Electricity Duty Rules, 1964
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan (except Tribal Areas in Balochistan)

metadata.summary: These rules prescribe the manner for levying and collecting electricity duty on energy consumed by consumers and licensees. They define key terms such as 'Consumer', 'Energy', and 'Licensee', and establish rates for various uses including residential, industrial, and agricultural purposes. The rules also provide for exemptions, the keeping of accounts, inspection powers, and penalties for non-payment or failure to comply with metering requirements.

name: PUNJAB MEDIUM-TERM FISCAL FRAMEWORK AND BUDGET STRATEGY RULES 2023

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Medium-term Fiscal Framework and Budget Strategy Rules, 2023
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Public Financial Management Act, 2022
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the preparation, submission, and approval of Punjab's medium-term fiscal framework and budget strategy.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the procedures for preparing and approving the Medium-term Fiscal Framework and Budget Strategy in Punjab. They define key terms such as 'Budget Strategy' and 'Federal Divisible Pool' and set up specific committees including the Fiscal Discipline Committee, Joint Priorities Committee, and Resource Mobilization Committee to oversee the process. The document outlines a detailed timeline for reviewing estimates, setting expenditure ceilings, and finalizing the strategy paper before submission to the Government.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Pension Fund Rules, 2007
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Pension Fund Act, 2007 (I of 2007)
metadata.administering_body: Finance Department, Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Governor of Punjab to regulate the management and investment of the Punjab Pension Fund under the Act.
metadata.summary: These rules are made by the Governor of the Punjab in exercise of powers under the Punjab Pension Fund Act, 2007. They establish the preliminary definitions, general obligations, and restrictions on the Fund's investments. The rules outline the powers of the Management Committee regarding asset administration and investment policies.

name: PUNJAB RESTAURANT INVOICE MONITORING SYSTEM RULES 2015

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Restaurant Invoice Monitoring System Rules, 2015

metadata.summary: These rules empower the Punjab Revenue Authority to monitor restaurants by installing specific hardware and software systems for real-time invoice tracking. The rules mandate access for verification, installation of devices like cash registers, and the use of video vigilance systems including CCTV. Restaurants are required to comply with invoicing formats, allow surprise inspections, and face penalties for system damage or tax fraud. Additionally, an incentive scheme rewards customers who report taxable services worth over 1000 rupees.

name: PUNJAB REVENUE AUTHORITY (MEMBERS AND SECRETARY) RULES 2016

metadata.summary: These rules were made by the Governor of the Punjab under the Punjab Revenue Authority Act 2012 to regulate the appointment of members and the Secretary. They specify eligibility criteria based on service rank and experience, set a term of three years extendable to five years, and define the administrative responsibilities of the Secretary regarding meetings and reports. The rules also outline the distribution of work among members and procedures for re-appointment.

name: PUNJAB SALES TAX ON SERVICES (ADJUDICATION AND APPEALS) RULES 2012

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Sales Tax on Services (Adjudication and Appeals) Rules, 2012
metadata.parent_law: Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act 2012 (XLIII of 2012)
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Punjab Revenue Authority under the Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act 2012 regarding adjudication and appeals procedures.
metadata.summary: These rules were promulgated by the Punjab Revenue Authority in exercise of powers under section 76 of the Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act 2012. They govern the process for issuing show cause notices, conducting adjudication proceedings, and handling appeals to the Commissioner (Appeals). The document outlines principles of natural justice, procedures for summary adjudication, and formats for filing references to the High Court.

name: PUNJAB SALES TAX ON SERVICES (ADJUSTMENT OF TAX) RULES 2012

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Sales Tax on Services (Adjustment of Tax) Rules, 2012
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act, 2012 (XLIII of 2012)
metadata.one_line: Rules governing input tax adjustment, credit/debit notes, and refunds for exported taxable services under the Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act, 2012.
metadata.summary: These rules provide a framework for registered persons to deduct or adjust input tax paid on goods and services used in providing taxable services. They specify conditions under which input tax adjustments are admissible, including apportionment for non-taxable services and restrictions on capital goods or entertainment items. The document also outlines procedures for issuing credit and debit notes, handling supplementary invoices, and managing refunds for exported services.

name: PUNJAB SALES TAX ON SERVICES (AUDIT) RULES 2012

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Sales Tax on Services (Audit) Rules, 2012
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act, 2012 (XLIII of 2012)
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Punjab Revenue Authority to regulate departmental and special audits under the Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act, 2012.
metadata.summary: These rules empower the Commissioner of the Punjab Revenue Authority to conduct departmental and special audits of registered persons. The rules outline procedures for selecting auditees based on risk factors, conducting pre-audit reviews, and preparing standardized audit reports. They also provide mechanisms for voluntary tax payments during audits and allow for the conversion of an audit into an investigation if tax fraud is observed.

name: PUNJAB SALES TAX ON SERVICES (AUTHORIZED REPRESENTATIVES) RULES 2012

metadata.summary: The Punjab Sales Tax on Services (Authorized Representatives) Rules, 2012 specify the categories of persons authorized to represent a taxpayer before the Punjab Revenue Authority or its appellate bodies. The document details the procedure for appointing an authorized representative via a letter of authorization and lists specific disqualifications such as criminal convictions or dismissal from service. Furthermore, it outlines the professional responsibilities and code of ethics that authorized representatives must adhere to, including prohibitions on fraud, dishonesty, and misleading conduct.

name: PUNJAB SALES TAX ON SERVICES (COMPUTERIZED SYSTEM) RULES 2012

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Sales Tax on Services (Computerized System) Rules, 2012

metadata.summary: These rules were made under the Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act, 2012 to establish a computerized system for filing returns. They define the responsibilities of authorized users regarding security and confidentiality of business information. The rules also appoint e-intermediaries with professional experience and regulate the use of electronic invoicing systems.

name: PUNJAB SALES TAX ON SERVICES (ENFORCEMENT) RULES 2014

metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Punjab Revenue Authority to enforce the Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act, 2012.
metadata.summary: These rules empower officers of the Punjab Revenue Authority to visit business premises, access records, and seal premises involved in non-compliance with sales tax obligations. The document defines key terms such as 'business premises' and 'enforcement', outlines procedures for sealing and de-sealing locations, and grants powers for arrest and detention regarding tax liabilities. It also establishes protocols for coordinating with Chambers of Commerce and handling cases involving tampering with seals or obstruction of duties.

name: PUNJAB SALES TAX ON SERVICES (FILING OF RETURNS) RULES 2012

The document details the step-by-step process for generating forms, verifying data, making payments through designated banks, and obtaining acknowledgments.

name: PUNJAB SALES TAX ON SERVICES (RECOVERY) RULES 2012

They establish procedures for referring officers to issue certificates detailing defaulter information and properties, which are then used by nominated recovery officers to attach and sell assets. The rules specify measures such as maintaining registers, prohibiting officer bidding at sales, and defining the order of utilizing sale proceeds to cover costs, tax dues, other government liabilities, and finally returning any balance to the defaulter.

name: PUNJAB SALES TAX ON SERVICES (REGISTRATION AND DE-REGISTRATION) RULES 2012

They establish procedures for applying for registration, including electronic or manual applications via prescribed forms, and outline requirements for displaying registration numbers on invoices and correspondence. The rules also detail processes for suspension or cancellation due to tax fraud, revival of cancelled registrations, and automatic registration for existing federal taxpayers.

The rules cover various sectors including financial services, insurance, shipping agents, and advertising, detailing scope, registration requirements, taxable values, record-keeping, and audit obligations. They also address franchise arrangements, preventing double taxation, and establishing penalties for defaulters.

The rules also outline the filing requirements for monthly returns by withholding agents and registered service providers.

The rules define key terms such as 'food business' and 'contact material', mandate licensing for food trades, and outline the duties of the Food Authority and Food Inspectors. It defines specific terms such as 'producer', 'wholesale dealer', and 'retail dealer' based on transaction quantities. The Order mandates that no person shall engage in the purchase, sale, or storage of specified foodgrains without a license issued by the Licensing Authority, with exceptions for producers and retail undertakings in wheat and wheat atta.

name: ESTABLISHMENT OF SAWPITS, SAWMILL, CHARCOAL KILN, TIMBER OR FIREWOOD DEPOT RULES 2013

metadata.summary: These rules establish a mandatory registration system for depots, sawpits, sawmills, and charcoal kilns located within five miles of forest boundaries. They define specific terms related to timber and processing facilities, requiring applicants to submit applications with identity cards and a security deposit. The rules also prescribe the maintenance of detailed registers for receipts and sales, restrict operating hours to daylight, and grant Forest Officers powers to refuse registration or seize materials in case of offences.

metadata.short_title: Private Wildlife Breeding Farm Rules 2016

They establish a licensing system managed by the competent authority, requiring specific land sizes, boundary demarcation, and maintenance of records including mortality reports and micro-chipping. The rules also outline procedures for inspection, disease reporting, surplus stock sales, and the repeal of the previous 2008 rules.

The rules mandate licensing, fee payments, strict record-keeping including mortality reports, and the use of tags or micro-chips for all animals. Additionally, they outline government responsibilities such as providing technical assistance, inspecting farms every three months, and selling surplus stock to owners.

The rules outline requirements for applications, management plans, and agreements, while also providing mechanisms for cancellation of notifications and appeals to a Board.

The rules outline procedures for election, fund sharing, account maintenance, and the cancellation of conservancy. Additionally, they provide fee schedules for hunting permits and repeal previous rules regarding ungulate conservation.

The rules also define the hierarchy of officers authorized to sanction rewards and establish scrutiny committees for high-value reward cases.

metadata.short_title: Punjab Forest Transit Rules, 2013

The rules set up specific committees, including a scrutiny committee and an implementation committee, to manage the selection of project areas, evaluation of proposals, drafting of agreements, and monitoring of projects throughout their cycle.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Protected Areas Rules, 2022

The rules cover management plans, hunting permits with specific fees and auction processes, fishing rights, mining permissions, and special provisions for research and dignitaries.

The document outlines eligibility criteria for offenders, procedures for granting licenses, and mechanisms for revoking licenses if conditions are breached.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Notaries Rules, 1965
metadata.parent_law: Notaries Ordinance, 1961 (XIX of 1961)
metadata.one_line: These rules govern the appointment, qualifications, fees, and practice of notaries in West Pakistan under the Notaries Ordinance, 1961.
metadata.summary: The West Pakistan Notaries Rules, 1965 establish the framework for appointing notaries public within West Pakistan. They specify eligibility criteria such as prior appointment by the Master of Faculties in England or five years of legal practice, along with age limits. The rules detail the application process, fees for certificates and services, and procedures for extending areas of practice. Additionally, they outline requirements for seals, offices, and forms used in notarial work.

metadata.short_title: Notification No. SO (MP) 9-1-G/2008 (P)
metadata.parent_law: Prisons Act 1894
metadata.one_line: Amends Pakistan Prisons Rules, 1978 regarding religious examinations and prisoner funeral participation.
metadata.summary: This notification amends the Pakistan Prisons Rules, 1978 under the powers of the Prisons Act 1894. It inserts provisions for examining convicts on religious texts and establishes a committee involving district officials and religious representatives. Additionally, it allows well-behaved prisoners to attend funerals of relatives with police escort and clarifies the roles of Deputy Inspectors-General.

name: NOTIFICATION REGARDING PUNJAB WITNESS PROTECTION RULES, 2019

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Witness Protection Rules, 2019
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Witness Protection Act, 2018 (XXI of 2018)
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab, Home Department
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Governor of Punjab to establish Witness Protection Units and define procedures for witness protection under the 2018 Act.
metadata.summary: These rules were made by the Governor of the Punjab in exercise of powers under Section 17 of the Punjab Witness Protection Act, 2018. They establish two distinct Witness Protection Units (Unit-I for terrorism and Unit-II for serious offences) within the Punjab police structure. The rules define key terms, outline risk assessment procedures, specify the composition and functions of the units, and provide for funding and review mechanisms.

name: Notification Superior Class Jail Facilities to a Prisoner in the Punjab

metadata.short_title: Notification NO.SO(R&P)4-24/10(Part-1)
metadata.parent_law: Prisons Rules, 1983
metadata.administering_body: Home Department, Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Allows superior class jail facilities in Punjab for eligible prisoners meeting specific criteria and excluding those with serious offences.
metadata.summary: This notification directs that superior class jail facilities may be allowed to prisoners in the Punjab under Prisons Rules, 1983. Eligibility requires the prisoner to be a casual offender holding a graduate degree, maintaining a superior mode of living, and owning significant land or assets. The facilities are not a right and are initially granted on a provisional basis for up to three months, subject to extension based on good conduct. Certain prisoners, including habitual criminals, those with heinous offences like terrorism or rape, and those involved in financial crimes, are explicitly excluded from these facilities.

metadata.parent_law: Police Order 2002
metadata.administering_body: Police Department, Government of the Punjab

metadata.summary: This notification approves the recruitment criteria, pay scales, ranks, and terms of service for members of the Punjab Highway Patrol. It outlines promotion authorities, training requirements, and administrative powers for the force. The document also details grievance redressal mechanisms and leave entitlements based on existing rules.

metadata.short_title: West Pakistan Probation of Offenders Rules, 1961
metadata.parent_law: Probation of Offenders Ordinance, 1960(XLV of 1960)
metadata.administering_body: Department of Reclamation and Probation, West Pakistan
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Governor of West Pakistan to regulate probation officers, case committees, and probation orders under the 1960 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: These rules were promulgated by the Governor of West Pakistan in exercise of powers under the Probation of Offenders Ordinance, 1960. They establish the structure for the Probation Department, defining roles for the Officer-in-Charge, Assistant Directors, and Chief Probation Officers. The document sets strict eligibility criteria for Probation Officers, including age limits and educational requirements in Sociology or Social Work. It also outlines the duties of officers, the constitution of Case Committees, and the standard forms for probation orders and bonds.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Arms Rules, 2014

metadata.summary: These rules provide the framework for issuing, renewing, and managing arms licenses within the Province of Punjab. They establish eligibility criteria for natural and legal persons, categorize businesses based on size, and define procedures for application, fee payment, and license transfer. The rules also outline powers for suspension or cancellation of licenses and repeal the previous Arms Rules of 1924.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Censorship of Films Rules, 2013
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Motion Pictures (Amendment) Act, 2012
repeals: The Censorship of Film Rules, 1980
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab, Information and Culture Department
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Governor of Punjab to regulate the censorship and certification of films for public exhibition.
metadata.summary: These rules were promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab in exercise of powers under the Punjab Motion Pictures (Amendment) Act, 2012. They establish the Punjab Film Censor Board, define its structure including centers and panels, and outline procedures for appointing members and staff. The document details requirements for film certification applications, fee structures for local and imported films, rating classifications, and mechanisms for appeals.

metadata.summary: These rules establish the District Public Safety and Police Complaints Commission under the Police Order, 2002. They define the Commission's functions, meeting procedures, decision-making processes, and the roles of its members and secretary. The document also outlines mechanisms for fact-finding inquiries, annual policing plans, and cooperation with citizen police liaison committees.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Juvenile Justice System Rules, 2002

metadata.summary: These Rules were framed under the Juvenile Justice System Ordinance, 2000, to provide for the establishment and maintenance of Borstal Institutions in every district of Punjab. They outline procedures for the admission, accommodation, medical care, and training of juveniles detained in these institutions. The document also establishes standards for legal assistance, discipline, psychological development, and the release of juveniles upon court order.

metadata.summary: The document establishes recruitment rules for miscellaneous posts within the Punjab Police Department. The rules come into force immediately and govern appointments by promotion or initial recruitment based on seniority cum fitness.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Police Promotion Rules, 1934
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the organization, establishment, buildings, clothing, equipment, and allowances of the Punjab Police force.
metadata.summary: These Rules establish the organizational structure and hierarchy of the Punjab Police, defining the roles of officers from the Inspector General down to Sub-Inspectors. They detail the permanent and additional police establishment, including procedures for recruitment, pay grades, and duties. The document also covers regulations regarding police buildings, uniform specifications, equipment maintenance, contingent expenditure management, and the powers and duties of town watchmen.

metadata.short_title: Punjab Prisons Rules, 1978

metadata.summary: These rules regulate the establishment and management of prisons within the Province of Punjab. They define key terms such as 'Prison', 'criminal prisoner', and 'habitual criminal' based on relevant Acts like the Prisons Act, 1894. The document outlines procedures for calculating sentence periods, including time spent on bail or parole, and provides guidelines for classifying habitual criminals.

metadata.summary: These rules were made under the Punjab Private Security Companies (Regulation and Control) Ordinance, 2002, to regulate the licensing, employment, and training of private security companies in Punjab. They establish procedures for granting licenses, verifying company antecedents, setting employee qualifications, and managing arms possession. The rules also outline fees for registration and licensing, performance reporting requirements, and provisions for the welfare of employees.

name: PUNJAB PROTECTION OF VULNERABLE PERSONS RULES 2015

metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab, Home Department
metadata.one_line: Rules establishing a Board and Unit to protect vulnerable persons in proceedings under the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the Punjab Protection of Vulnerable Persons Board and a Protection Unit within the Counter Terrorism Department. They define vulnerable persons as witnesses, judges, prosecutors, counsel, accused, and others involved in proceedings under the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 who require protection. The Unit is empowered to formulate programmes, regulate admission to protection schemes, determine security measures, establish safe houses, and provide financial assistance to prosecution witnesses.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Witness Protection Rules, 2019

metadata.summary: The Punjab Witness Protection Rules, 2019 were made by the Governor of the Punjab under the powers of the Punjab Witness Protection Act, 2018. They establish two distinct Witness Protection Units (Unit-I for terrorism offences and Unit-II for serious offences) within the Punjab Police structure. The rules define key terms such as 'protected person' and 'assisted witness', outline the composition and functions of the Units including risk assessment procedures, and detail the criteria for granting protection measures. Additionally, they provide for the allocation of funds by the Government and a mechanism for reviewing decisions made by the Units.

metadata.short_title: Section 08 of Pakistan Citizenship Rules, 1952
metadata.parent_law: Pakistan Citizenship Act, 1952
metadata.one_line: Sets out procedures for applying for citizenship by birth via a magistrate and provincial government.
metadata.summary: This rule outlines the process for a person to claim citizenship by birth under Section 04 of the Act. Applicants must submit Form 'B' in duplicate to a first-class magistrate in their district of birth, accompanied by a valid birth certificate and an oath statement from parents or guardians if under 21. The magistrate conducts an inquiry and recommends granting a Certificate in Form R-1 to the Provincial Government, which then passes final orders.

metadata.short_title: Pakistan Citizenship Rules, 1952
metadata.parent_law: Pakistan Citizenship Act, 1952
metadata.one_line: Sets procedures for citizenship applications by descent via Provincial and Federal Governments.
metadata.summary: This rule outlines the process for individuals claiming citizenship by descent under Section 05 of the Pakistan Citizenship Act, 1952. Applicants must submit Form 'B' in triplicate to the Provincial Government where they have their domicile of origin. The application requires a parent's citizenship certificate and additional documents if the parent is a citizen by descent only, such as birth registration certificates or proof of government service.

name: THE PUNJAB PUBLIC ORDER DETENUE RULES, 1979

metadata.summary: These rules provide for the administration of persons detained in custody under the West Pakistan Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960. They cover definitions, classification into better or ordinary classes, provisions for diet, clothing, and furniture, as well as regulations regarding funds, interviews, searches, and transfers. The rules also supersede the earlier West Pakistan Maintenance of Public Order Detenu Rules, 1962.

metadata.summary: This Order is made by the Federal Government under the United Nations (Security Council) Act, 1948 to enforce UN Security Council resolutions. It designates a specific authority within the Foreign Affairs Division to seek assistance from federal and provincial agencies for compliance. The Order imposes severe penalties, including fines up to one million rupees for willful non-compliance by individuals or companies, and up to five hundred thousand rupees for responsible officers.

The rules define various branch services such as Wardens, Rescue, Control and Communication, Casualty, Fire, and Training services, and outline the appointment process and responsibilities of the Civil Defence Controller.

metadata.summary: These rules were made by the Governor of West Pakistan to regulate shops and establishments within the province. They supersede previous rules from Punjab, Sind, and N.W.F.P. The document outlines procedures for choosing weekly holidays, fencing machinery, granting casual leave, maintaining employment registers, and displaying notices. It also defines key terms like 'Ordinance' and 'Section' and assigns duties to inspectors.

They establish a Workman's Compensation Fund for cases where no dependants exist after two years. The rules also define the roles of Commissioners, outline examination procedures, and specify scales for costs and fees applicable in West Pakistan.

metadata.summary: These rules were framed by the Central Government under the Workmen Compensation Act, 1923 to regulate the transfer of compensation sums. They define the roles of authorized officers and Commissioners in transferring funds to persons residing abroad or receiving foreign awards within Pakistan. The rules also cover the administration, reporting, and return of undisbursed sums received from transferring authorities.

metadata.short_title: The Official Trustee's (Punjab) Rules, 1914
metadata.long_title: Whereas the Governor-General in Council, in exercise of the Powers conferred by Section 31 of the Official Trustee's Act, 1913 (II of 1913) has been pleased, by Notification No. 1824-C, dated March 13, 1914 to remove the Punjab, North-West Frontier Province, and the Province of Delhi, from the presidency of Bengal, and to constitute them into the Province of the Punjab for the purposes of the said Act, and further to declare that the duties of Government under the Official Trustees Act, 1913 (II of 1913), to make the following rules for the Province of the Punjab, as constituted by the notification referred to above

metadata.summary: These rules were made by the Governor-General in Council under the powers of Section 31 of the Official Trustee's Act, 1913. They apply specifically to the Province of the Punjab and cover the administration of trusts, including religious and business trusts. The document prescribes fees for the Official Trustee, outlines methods for fee reduction and remission, details the valuation of property for fee calculation, and mandates specific registers for investments, immovable property, and mortgages.

name: PUNJAB LETTERS OF ADMINISTRATION AND SUCCESSION CERTIFICATES RULES 2021

metadata.summary: These rules were made under the Punjab Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates Act, 2021 to regulate the application process for Letters of Administration or Succession Certificates. They outline requirements for applications, including death certificates, heir lists, and authorization forms, as well as procedures for summary enquiries and public notice publication. The rules also cover fees, costs, bio-metric verification of legal heirs, and the issuance of duplicate or amended certificates.

metadata.short_title: Animal Birth Control (Dogs) Policy 2021
metadata.one_line: A policy to control stray dog populations in Punjab through sterilization, responsible ownership, and monitoring committees.
metadata.summary: This notification establishes the Animal Birth Control (Dogs) Policy 2021 to address issues related to stray dogs in Punjab. The policy aims to reduce dog populations and rabies incidents while promoting responsible dog ownership and animal welfare. It creates specific committees at provincial, district, and tehsil levels for implementation and monitoring, defining roles for local governments, NGOs, and healthcare departments.

name: Prevention of cruelty to animal rules, 1961

metadata.short_title: Prevention of cruelty to animal rules, 1961
metadata.one_line: Rules regulating the prevention of cruelty to animals through licensing farriers and restricting animal usage.
metadata.summary: These rules establish a framework for preventing cruelty to animals by recognizing societies dedicated to this cause. They mandate that farriers must be licensed by recognized societies and specify conditions for such licenses, including fees. The rules also impose restrictions on the use of bits or harnesses, limit draught hours for buffaloes based on seasons, restrict loading weights, and set age limits for animals in yoke.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Animal Health Rules, 2021
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Animal Health Act, 2019 (XXXII of 2019)
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Governor of Punjab to control scheduled diseases, identify animals, and manage quarantine under the Punjab Animal Health Act 2019.
metadata.summary: These rules were promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab in exercise of powers under section 29 of the Punjab Animal Health Act 2019. They establish mechanisms for controlling scheduled diseases through vaccination, identification, and traceability systems within the province. The rules define controlled areas, buffer zones, and quarantine units managed by the Chief Veterinary Officer and authorized officers. Additionally, they prescribe forms for vaccination certificates, postmortem examinations, and entry permits for animals entering or exiting controlled areas.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Animals Slaughter Controls Rules, 1965
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Animals Slaughter Control Act, 1963

metadata.summary: These rules were made by the Governor of West Pakistan under the Punjab Animals Slaughter Control Act, 1963. They specify permitted hours for animal slaughter in licensed houses or default times if none are fixed. The rules also dictate procedures for disposing of seized animals via auction or burning/burying unfit carcasses under veterinary supervision.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Dourine Rules, 1952
metadata.parent_law: Dourine Act, 1910

metadata.one_line: Rules framed under the Dourine Act, 1910 regarding inspections, appeals, and penalties for dourine disease in Punjab.
metadata.summary: These rules were framed under section 14 of the Dourine Act, 1910 to regulate procedures related to dourine disease control in Punjab. They specify restrictions on entry and search times, requirements for owners during inspections, compensation limits for destroyed mares, and the composition of the appeals committee. The rules also outline notice procedures for hearings and establish a fine of up to fifty rupees for breaching Rule 3.

name: PUNJAB LIVESTOCK AND DAIRY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT (PARA-VETERINARY STAFF) SERVICE RULES 2021

metadata.summary: These rules are made by the Governor of the Punjab under the Punjab Civil Servants Act, 1974. They establish the short title and immediate commencement of the regulations governing para-veterinary staff. The document specifies that recruitment methods, qualifications, age limits, and other incidental matters for these posts are detailed in the appended Schedule.

metadata.summary: These rules were made by the Governor-General of West Pakistan to deal with cases of South African Horse Sickness. They supersede earlier Punjab notifications and apply under Article 19 of President's Order No. 1 of 1970 in Punjab, Sind, N.W.F.P., and Baluchistan. The rules define key terms, mandate immediate reporting and isolation of diseased horses, prescribe strict disinfection and destruction procedures, grant licenses for removal, and provide compensation for destroyed animals.

metadata.summary: This notification sets out the Standards and Procedures for Breeding Animals in Punjab, effective immediately. It outlines protocols for performance recording, progeny testing, artificial insemination, and animal identification under the authority of the Livestock Breeding Service Authority. The document also includes specific guidelines for Foot and Mouth Disease testing, quarantine, vaccination schedules, and semen management during outbreaks.

metadata.short_title: Forms for Building Applications
metadata.one_line: Provides standardized application forms and specifications for building permits in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This document establishes the specific forms required to apply for permission to execute building works, including new construction, alterations, and additions. It outlines the necessary supporting documents such as title deeds, architectural plans, and stability certificates depending on the type of work. The rules also specify safety precautions, utility service protections, and fire safety requirements that must be adhered to during construction.

name: PUNJAB LOCAL GOVERNMENT (DELIMITATION OF NEIGHBOURHOODD COUNCILS AND VILLAGE COUNCILS) RULES 2022

They establish population criteria for urban and rural areas, define the functions of the delimitation committee, and outline procedures for filing objections. The rules also specify the validity period of the final lists and provide forms for official use.

metadata.summary: These rules provide a comprehensive framework for conducting local government elections in Punjab. They cover preliminary matters such as definitions and political party enlistment, detailed procedures for polling including the use of EVMs, management of election expenses, and the declaration of results. The document also establishes specific forms and affidavits that candidates must submit regarding their assets and liabilities.

metadata.summary: These rules provide the legal framework for reporting and registering births and deaths within the Province of Punjab. They specify the timelines for registration, required documents, applicable fees, and procedures for late registration or issuing duplicate certificates. The rules also define key terms such as 'abandoned child' and 'foreigner', and empower various departments to report births.

The document outlines procedures for fees, penalties for illegal development, and mechanisms for managing mortgaged plots to ensure completion of public amenities.

name: PUNJAB REGISTRATION OF CHRISTIAN DIVORCE RULES 2024

metadata.summary: The Punjab Registration of Christian Divorce Rules, 2024 provide a framework for applicants to register divorce decrees issued under the Divorce Act. The process involves submitting an application with specific documents to the Secretary of the concerned Union Council after a six-month waiting period or the dismissal of any appeal. The application is reviewed by the Assistant Director within three days, who may accept or reject it, with provisions for appeal to the Deputy Director if rejected. Upon acceptance, a Registration Certificate is issued jointly signed by the Assistant Director and the Secretary Union Council.

metadata.summary: These rules provide a framework for protecting heritage properties and declaring them within the Walled City of Lahore. They empower the Walled City of Lahore Authority to declare buildings, structures, or lands as heritage properties based on specific grounds like architectural value or historical association. The process includes consulting the Heritage Conservation Board, serving notices of intention, allowing for public objections, and holding hearings before a final declaration is made.

The rules also set construction standards, water pressure requirements, lighting provisions, and duties regarding attendants and locker rooms.

metadata.short_title: The Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1926

They mandate specific forms for reporting output, accidents, and employment details to the District Magistrate and Chief Inspector. The text also includes detailed provisions for handling explosives, managing unsafe working places, and reporting fatal or serious accidents.

They establish a Rescue Station Committee comprising representatives from the Chief Inspector of Mines, Industries, Mine Owners, Institute of Mining Engineers, and workers. The rules define procedures for rescue operations, equipment maintenance, excise duty assessment on coal despatches, and the constitution of rescue corps.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Miners Training Institutions Regulations, 1999

They mandate that private institutes must be registered by the Government on the recommendations of the Mining Board. The text outlines the roles of the Mining Board and Chief Inspector in supervising syllabi, admissions, fees, staff strength, and practical training.

They establish principles for fair and transparent agreements and define specific competitive bidding procedures, such as single-stage two-envelope or three-envelope methods. The rules also set timeframes for inviting tenders, conducting pre-qualification, evaluating technical and financial proposals, and issuing bidding documents.

metadata.summary: These temporary regulations empower the Health Inspector to direct owners and occupiers in Punjab to take immediate measures against mosquito breeding, such as removing water containers and clearing drains. The regulations outline specific duties for premises owners, including maintaining cisterns and draining artificial ponds, while also addressing safety measures in educational institutions. A Health Inspector is authorized to enter premises for inspection and may require pesticide spraying or execute necessary works if compliance is neglected. The regulations were intended to remain in force only until November 30, 2011, after which they were repealed.

The amendments were enacted by the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab and came into force immediately upon assent.

metadata.short_title: The Stamp (Amendment) Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Stamp Act, 1899.
repeals: The Stamp (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026
metadata.one_line: Amends the Stamp Act, 1899 to define assignable deeds and adjust stamp duty rates in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Stamp Act, 1899 to introduce a definition for 'assignable deed' regarding the assignment of rights in immovable property. It inserts new entries into Schedule-I to levy specific stamp duties on such assignments within or beyond twelve months. Additionally, the Act repeals the Stamp (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026 and substitutes certain figures in existing articles of the parent Act.

metadata.short_title: The University of Lahore (Amendment) Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the University of Lahore Ordinance, 2002.
metadata.one_line: Amends the University of Lahore Ordinance, 2002 to add new faculties and expand campus and program offerings.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the University of Lahore Ordinance, 2002 to update its scope and administrative powers. It adds Agriculture and Veterinary Sciences as new branches of knowledge and allows for offshore campuses. The amendment also facilitates online learning, joint degree programs, and the establishment of various research and training centers within and outside Pakistan.

metadata.short_title: Anti-terrorism (Punjab Amendment) Act 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Anti-terrorism Act, 1997.
metadata.parent_law: Anti-terrorism Act, 1997 (XXVII of 1997)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Anti-terrorism Act, 1997 regarding detention inquiries and their duration in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends section 11EEEE of the Anti-terrorism Act, 1997 to modify provisions concerning detention orders issued by armed forces. It establishes that inquiries for such detentions must be conducted by a joint investigation team comprising police, intelligence, civil armed forces, and other law enforcement agencies. The amended provisions remain in force for a period of two years from the commencement of this Act.

metadata.short_title: Companies Profits (Workers Participation) (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Companies Profits (Workers Participation) Act, 1968.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Companies Profits (Workers Participation) Act, 1968 by substituting 'Government' with 'Institution' in several sections.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Companies Profits (Workers Participation) Act, 1968 to align references from 'Government' to the Employees' Social Security Institution. It inserts a definition for 'Institution' in section 2 and modifies sections 5, 6, 7, and 8A of the parent Act. The amendments grant the Institution rights regarding recovery charges and establish its role in determining such charges via a Committee.

metadata.short_title: Drugs (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Drugs Act, 1976.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Drugs Act, 1976 to define the composition and quorum of Drug Courts in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends section 31 of the Drugs Act, 1976 to specify the composition of Drug Courts. It establishes that a Drug Court consists of a Chairperson appointed from the judiciary and two members with fifteen years of pharmaceutical or medical experience. The Act also defines the quorum requirements for deciding matters other than final hearings.

metadata.short_title: The Lahore Leads University (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Lahore Leads University Act, 2011.
metadata.administering_body: The Board of the Lahore Leads University
metadata.one_line: Amends the Lahore Leads University Act, 2011 to update governance, faculties, and operational provisions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Lahore Leads University Act, 2011 to expand the university's educational scope and governance structure. It adds new clauses regarding constituent colleges, teaching methods, and international partnerships while updating the Board's composition and powers. The legislation also revises the appointment terms for the Vice Chancellor and modifies the Statutes and Regulations framework.

metadata.short_title: The Notaries (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Notaries Ordinance, 1961.
metadata.parent_law: The Notaries Ordinance, 1961
metadata.one_line: Amends the Notaries Ordinance, 1961 to restrict jurisdiction and powers to the Punjab Province.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Notaries Ordinance, 1961 to limit its application from Pakistan to the Punjab province. It substitutes references to the Provincial Government with the Secretary of the Home Department or authorized officers. The Act also increases fines for offences and omits specific sections from the original Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Probation of Offenders (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Probation of Offenders Ordinance, 1960.
metadata.parent_law: Probation of Offenders Ordinance, 1960
metadata.administering_body: Deputy Commissioner of the District concerned
metadata.one_line: Amends the Probation of Offenders Ordinance, 1960 to introduce community service and adjust jurisdiction.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Probation of Offenders Ordinance, 1960 to restrict its application to the Punjab. It introduces 'community service' as a form of unpaid work beneficial to the community and mandates supervision by the Deputy Commissioner. The Act also updates court considerations for probation orders and adjusts penalty durations in the original ordinance.

metadata.short_title: Provincial Employees' Social Security (Amendment) Act 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Provincial Employees' Social Security Ordinance, 1965.
metadata.parent_law: Provincial Employees' Social Security Ordinance, 1965
metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Employees' Social Security Ordinance, 1965 to add financial benefits for purchasing essential commodities.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Employees' Social Security Ordinance, 1965 by updating its long title and preamble. It inserts a new section 43-A allowing secured persons to receive financial benefits for purchasing essential commodities. These benefits are subject to government approval and fund availability, with specific outlets notified by the Government.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Alternate Dispute Resolution (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Alternate Dispute Resolution Act 2019.
amends: The Punjab Alternate Dispute Resolution Act, 2019
metadata.administering_body: Authority established under the Punjab Alternate Dispute Resolution Act, 2019
metadata.one_line: Amends sections 11, 21, and 21-A of the Punjab Alternate Dispute Resolution Act, 2019 regarding mediation judges and appointments.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Alternate Dispute Resolution Act, 2019 to update provisions on mediator judges and expert nominations. It modifies section 11 to include mediator judges nominated by the Lahore High Court. Additionally, it alters appointment procedures for experts and the Director General of the Authority in sections 21 and 21-A.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Arms (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Arms Ordinance, 1965.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for seven years and fine not less than two million rupees
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Arms Ordinance, 1965 to regulate gun shooting clubs and increase penalties for unlicensed arms activities.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Arms Ordinance, 1965 to introduce regulations regarding gun shooting clubs and substitute various administrative terms like 'Government' with 'Secretary'. It expands the scope of prohibited activities to include the running of gun shooting clubs without a license. The Act significantly increases penalties for offences related to possessing or carrying non-prohibited and prohibited bore weapons, as well as military stores.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Consumer Protection (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Consumer Protection Act, 2005.
key_definitions: buys or obtains on lease any product
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Consumer Protection Act, 2005 regarding definitions, penalties, and consumer court designations.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Consumer Protection Act, 2005 to update definitions related to transactions and commercial purposes. It revises penalty structures for violations and redesignates District Judges as Consumer Courts. The amendments also address the transfer of cases from defunct courts and clarify the scope of consumer protection for self-employed individuals.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Judicial Academy (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Judicial Academy Act, 2007.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Judicial Academy Act, 2007 to update definitions, functions, and provisions regarding rules and regulations.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Judicial Academy Act, 2007 to clarify definitions regarding rules and regulations. It updates the Board's functions to include policy formulation, international standard setting, and committee constitution. The legislation also allows for the establishment of sub-campuses and grants the Board power to frame regulations.

name: PUNJAB LETTERS OF ADMINISTRATION AND SUCCESSION CERTIFICATES (AMENDMENT) ACT 2025

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates (Amendment) Act, 2025

amends: The Punjab Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates Act, 2021
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates Act 2021 to include civil courts and omit section 10.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates Act 2021 to reduce hardship for people in Punjab. It inserts 'or a civil court' into Section 3 and mandates following the Succession Act 1925 procedure for civil courts. Additionally, it omits Section 10 of the original Act.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Public Representatives' Laws (Amendment) Act 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the laws relating to the public representatives of the Province of the Punjab

The Punjab Provincial Assembly Speaker (Salary, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
The Punjab Provincial Assembly Deputy Speaker (Salary, Allowances and Privileges) Act 1975
metadata.one_line: Amends salary and allowance provisions for Ministers, Speaker, and Deputy Speaker in three specific Punjab Acts.
metadata.summary: This Act amends three existing laws relating to the salaries, allowances, and privileges of public representatives in the Province of the Punjab. It substitutes specific monetary amounts with a reference to 'the same as his salary' for the Minister, the Speaker, and the Deputy Speaker. The amendments apply immediately upon the commencement of the Punjab Revision of Salaries of Public Representatives Act 2024.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Road Safety Authority (Amendment) Act, 2025

amends: The Punjab Road Safety Authority Act, 2023
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Road Safety Authority Act 2023 regarding appointments, budget, funds, and audit.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Road Safety Authority Act 2023 to update provisions on employee appointments, budget approval processes, and financial reporting. It establishes a specific Fund for the Authority detailing sources of income including government grants and property disposal proceeds. The amendments also introduce new sections regarding the preparation of budgets, maintenance of accounts, and the conduct of audits by the Auditor General of Pakistan.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Vagrancy (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Vagrancy Ordinance, 1958.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment of ten years and fine up to two million rupees
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Vagrancy Ordinance, 1958 to include transgender persons and define organizers regarding vagrancy.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Vagrancy Ordinance, 1958 to expand definitions and penalties related to organizing or employing persons for vagrancy. It specifically includes transgender persons within the definition of 'person' and introduces stricter punishments for soliciting alms from children or using them as exhibits. The amendments also clarify jurisdiction and bail provisions for offences under the Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: Stamp (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Stamp Act, 1899.
metadata.administering_body: Board of Revenue / Chief Revenue Authority
metadata.one_line: Amends the Stamp Act, 1899 regarding valuation appeals, terminology, refunds, and revenue board references.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Stamp Act, 1899 to improve legal procedures and administrative clarity within Punjab. It substitutes provisions in section 27-A to define appeal processes for valuation tables and restricts reviews by District Collectors. Additionally, it inserts a new section 50-A allowing refunds for specific circumstances like detention or absence from the country, and amends sections 48 and 73 to update terminology and include the Board of Revenue.

metadata.short_title: The Police Order (Punjab Amendment) Act, 2024
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Police Order, 2002.
repeals: The Police Order (Amendment) Ordinance, 2023
metadata.one_line: Amends the Police Order 2002 to establish Organized Crime Units in every District and repeals a previous amendment ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Police Order, 2002 by inserting Article 18B to establish an Organized Crime Unit in every District of Punjab. The new unit is tasked with handling specific serious cases such as kidnapping for ransom, extortion, dacoity, robbery, and trafficking of narcotic drugs. It defines the leadership structure for these units based on district type and grants powers to officers posted within them. Additionally, the Act repeals Rule 21.35 of the Police Rules, 1934 and supersedes The Police Order (Amendment) Ordinance, 2023.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Alternate Dispute Resolution (Amendment) Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Alternate Dispute Resolution Act 2019.
amends: The Punjab Alternate Dispute Resolution Act, 2019
key_definitions: ADR service provider or ADR center
metadata.administering_body: Law and Parliamentary Affairs Department of the Government
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Alternate Dispute Resolution Act 2019 regarding definitions, timelines, and the Authority structure.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Alternate Dispute Resolution Act 2019 to update definitions, timelines for proceedings, and the composition of the Accreditation Authority. It establishes the Director General's appointment process and clarifies the status of Authority members as public servants. The legislation also modifies sections related to court returns, service providers, and the schedule regarding ownership.

name: PUNJAB GENERAL PROVIDENT INVESTMENT FUND (AMENDMENT) ACT 2023

metadata.one_line: Amends section 9 of the Punjab General Provident Investment Fund Act 2009 to increase financial limits.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab General Provident Investment Fund Act 2009 to update specific financial clauses. It substitutes the phrase 'more than seventy-five' with 'up to one hundred' in section 9, clause (d) of the parent Act. The legislation was passed by the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab and received assent on January 23, 2023.

metadata.short_title: The University of Gujrat (Amendment) Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the University of Gujrat Act, 2004.
key_definitions: the Act (referring to the University of Gujrat Act, 2004)
metadata.one_line: Amends the University of Gujrat Act, 2004 to restore properties and status to specific colleges.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the University of Gujrat Act, 2004 to reverse previous transfers of assets and liabilities. It restores the status and premises of Government College Gujrat and several women's colleges that existed before the original Act. The legislation ensures that properties and rights transferred to the University are returned to the said colleges.

name: PUNJAB INDUSTRIES (CONTROL ON ESTABLISHMENT AND ENLARGEMENT) (AMENDMENT) ACT 2022

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Industries (Control on Establishment and Enlargement) (Amendment) Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Industries (Control on Establishment and Enlargement) Ordinance, 1963.
amends: The Punjab Industries (Control on Establishment and Enlargement) Ordinance, 1963
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1963 Punjab Industries Ordinance to allow government exemptions and regularization of past contraventions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Industries (Control on Establishment and Enlargement) Ordinance, 1963. It empowers the Government to exempt industrial undertakings from specific provisions or regularize past contraventions upon payment of determined requitals. The amendment also allows such undertakings to apply for these exemptions within six months of the Act's commencement.

name: PUNJAB MINISTERS (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) (AMENDMENT) ACT 2022

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Act 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975.
amends: The Punjab Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1975 Act to grant lifetime security to former Chief Ministers serving at least six months after 2002.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975 by substituting a new section regarding perks and privileges. It grants lifetime suitable and adequate security to any person who held the office of Chief Minister of Punjab for at least six months after the general elections of 2002 under Article 130 of the Constitution. The amendment applies specifically to former Chief Ministers meeting these criteria.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Regularization of Service (Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Regularization of Service Act 2018.
amends: The Punjab Regularization of Service Act, 2018
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Regularization of Service Act 2018 to allow the Chief Minister to regularize contract employees without Commission reference.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Regularization of Service Act, 2018 to introduce a proviso regarding the regularization of services for contract employees. It empowers the Chief Minister to specify posts and regularize these employees in the public interest, even if it involves relaxing relevant rules without reference to the Commission. The amendment was enacted by the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab on January 12, 2022, and came into force immediately upon publication.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Civil Servants (Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Civil Servants Act, 1974.
repeals: The Punjab Civil Servants (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Civil Servants Act, 1974 regarding retirement age and service years while repealing a prior Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Civil Servants Act, 1974 to modify provisions related to the retirement of civil servants. Specifically, it substitutes clause (ii) of section 12 to define retirement conditions based on age or years of service. The legislation also repeals the Punjab Civil Servants (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021.

name: PUNJAB COMPULSORY TEACHING OF THE HOLY QURAN (AMENDMENT) ACT 2021

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Compulsory Teaching of the Holy Quran (Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Compulsory Teaching of the Holy Quran Act 2018.
amends: The Punjab Compulsory Teaching of the Holy Quran Act, 2018
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2018 Act to define 'compulsory teaching' and 'Naazrah Quran'.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Compulsory Teaching of the Holy Quran Act 2018 by inserting a new definition for 'compulsory teaching' and substituting the definition of 'Naazrah Quran'. It clarifies that compulsory teaching refers to the Holy Quran as a separate subject and defines Naazrah Quran as reading with correct pronunciation while sighting the Arabic text. The Act came into force immediately upon publication.

name: PUNJAB HOLY QURAN (PRINTING AND RECORDING) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Holy Quran (Printing and Recording) (Amendment) Act, 2021

amends: The Punjab Holy Quran (Printing and Recording) Act, 2011
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for life or imprisonment extending to seven years but not less than three years, or fine of one hundred thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2011 Act to increase penalties for translating or interpreting the Holy Quran contrary to Muslim beliefs.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Holy Quran (Printing and Recording) Act, 2011 to strengthen provisions against the translation or interpretation of the Holy Quran contrary to Muslim beliefs. It substitutes Section 7 with stricter definitions of prohibited acts and increases penalties in Section 9, including a new provision for life imprisonment if done with unlawful intent. The Act also adds new sections regarding the cognizance and trial of offences under this legislation.

name: PUNJAB INFECTIOUS DISEASES (PREVENTION AND CONTROL) (AMENDMENT) ACT 2021

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Infectious Diseases (Prevention and Control) (Amendment) Act, 2021

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Infectious Diseases (Prevention and Control) Act, 2020 to facilitate its better implementation. It empowers the Secretary to frame temporary regulations via notification in the official Gazette to prevent outbreaks or spread of infectious diseases and to determine expense defrayal methods. Additionally, the Act repeals the Punjab Infectious Diseases (Prevention and Control) (Amendment) Ordinance, 2020.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government (Amendment) Act 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Local Government Act, 2019.

Specifically, it omits entries (k) and (v) in Part-I and entry (o) in Part-III of the Tenth Schedule. Additionally, the Act repeals the Punjab Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance 2020.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Public Representatives' Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021

The Punjab Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975

metadata.summary: This Act amends existing laws relating to the public representatives of the Province of Punjab. It updates salary figures and definitions in the Provincial Assembly Members Act, omits specific sections from three Special Assistants and Parliamentary Secretaries Ordinances, and grants lifetime perks to former Speakers. Additionally, it adds new security and staff provisions for former Chief Ministers in the Ministers Act.

name: PUNJAB TRANSPARENCY AND RIGHT TO INFORMATION (AMENDMENT) ACT 2021

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Transparency and Right to Information Act 2013 to modify provisions concerning the term of office for Commissioners and their powers during inquiries. It also updates requirements for the Commission to prepare annual reports by August 31st each year. The amendments were enacted by the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab on March 17, 2021.

name: PUNJAB CURRICULUM AND TEXTBOOK BOARD (AMENDMENT) ACT 2020

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Curriculum and Textbook Board (Amendment) Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Curriculum and Textbook Board Act 2015.
amends: The Punjab Curriculum and Textbook Board Act, 2015
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2015 Act to require prior approval from Muttahida Ulema Board for religious textbooks.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Curriculum and Textbook Board Act, 2015 to introduce new regulatory requirements for religious educational materials. It mandates that any textbook or curriculum related to Islam, including subjects like Islamiyat, History, Pakistan Studies, Urdu, and Literature, cannot be published without prior approval from the Muttahida Ulema Board Punjab. The Punjab Curriculum and Textbook Board is legally bound to obtain this specific approval before publishing such materials. The amendment came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government (Amendment) Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Local Government Act, 2019.
repeals: The Punjab Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 2020
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Local Government Act, 2019 by changing a time period and repeals an earlier Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Local Government Act, 2019 by substituting 'twenty one months' for 'one year' in section 3. It also repeals the Punjab Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 2020. The Act was passed by the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab and assented to by the Governor on July 1, 2020.

It applies to the Province of Punjab and was enacted by the Provincial Assembly. The Act also repeals the Punjab Village Panchayats and Neighbourhood Councils (Amendment) Ordinance, 2020.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Village Panchayats and Neighbourhood Councils Act, 2019 to update specific sections and schedules. It substitutes certain words and entries related to the number of permitted neighbourhoods in various metropolitan corporations like Lahore, Gujranwala, Rawalpindi, and Multan. The legislation also repeals the earlier Punjab Village Panchayats and Neighbourhood Councils (Amendment) Ordinance 2020.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Employees' Social Security (Amendment) Act, 2019

repeals: The Provincial Employees' Social Security (Amendment) Ordinance, 2019
metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Employees' Social Security Ordinance, 1965 to broaden the definition of an employee and repeals a previous amendment ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Employees' Social Security Ordinance, 1965 to broaden the legal definition of an employee within Punjab. Specifically, it substitutes a clause in section 2 to ensure that employees do not cease to be covered solely because their monthly wages exceed a government-determined threshold. The Act also repeals the Provincial Employees' Social Security (Amendment) Ordinance, 2019.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Public Representatives' Laws (Amendment) Act, 2019

It updates salary figures, allowances, and medical facilities for Members of the Assembly, Ministers, Speakers, and other officials. Additionally, it grants new privileges such as VIP lounge access and official/diplomatic passports, and provides lifetime security for former Chief Ministers who served a minimum term.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Regularization of Service (Amendment) Act, 2019

The amendment also updates eligibility criteria for appointment on a regular basis, including requirements regarding available vacancies, qualifications, performance, and opt-out options.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Zakat and Ushr (Amendment) Act, 2019
