metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Zakat and Ushr Act 2018 regarding committee composition, functions, and fund transfers.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Zakat and Ushr Act 2018 to update provisions related to District and Local Zakat and Ushr Committees. It modifies eligibility criteria for council members, expands the list of government secretaries involved in the Council, and adjusts the number of members in local committees. The legislation also clarifies fund transfer mechanisms and establishes procedures for appointing administrators when elections cannot be held or committees are not constituted.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Sound Systems (Regulation) (Amendment) Ordinance, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Sound Systems (Regulation) Act 2015.
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Sound Systems (Regulation) Act, 2015
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Sound Systems (Regulation) Act 2015 to allow up to four external sound systems.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Sound Systems (Regulation) Act 2015 to increase the permitted number of external sound systems from one to not more than four. It was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab under Article 128 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session and immediate action was deemed necessary. The amendment specifically substitutes the phrase 'one external sound system' with 'not more than four external sound systems' in section 4, subsection (2), clause (a) of the parent Act.

metadata.short_title: The Explosive Substances (Punjab Amendment) Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Explosive Substances Act, 1908.
metadata.one_line: Amends Section 7 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908 regarding consent to trial in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Explosive Substances Act, 1908 specifically for its application in the Province of the Punjab. It modifies Section 7 by substituting a full stop with a colon and adding a proviso concerning consent to proceed to trial. The amendment stipulates that consent is deemed given if the Provincial Government does not convey its decision within sixty days of receiving a report under section 173 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.

metadata.short_title: The Limitation (Punjab Amendment) Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Limitation Act, 1908
metadata.one_line: Amends the Limitation Act, 1908 to set a ninety-day limit for filing revision petitions under section 115 of the CPC.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Limitation Act, 1908 by inserting a new Article 162-A into its First Schedule. The amendment specifically addresses Part X of the schedule regarding revision petitions. It establishes a strict ninety-day limitation period for filing such petitions under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Sound Systems (Regulation) (Amendment) Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Sound Systems (Regulation) Act 2015.
repeals: The Punjab Sound Systems (Regulation) (Amendment) Ordinance, 2018
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Sound Systems (Regulation) Act 2015 to allow four external sound systems at places of worship.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Sound Systems (Regulation) Act 2015 to increase the permitted number of external sound systems at places of worship from one to four. The amendment specifically allows these systems for Azan, religious prayers, and announcements regarding lost or found items. It also repeals a previous Ordinance issued in 2018 on the same subject.

metadata.short_title: The Parks and Horticulture Authority (Amendment) Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Parks and Horticulture Authority Act 2012.
amends: The Parks and Horticulture Authority Act, 2012
repeals: The Parks and Horticulture Authority (Amendment) Ordinance, 2017
metadata.one_line: Amends the Parks and Horticulture Authority Act 2012 to update definitions, permissions for park usage, and leasing powers.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Parks and Horticulture Authority Act 2012 to align its provisions with current necessities. It expands the definition of 'person' to include bodies owned by federal or provincial governments. The Act also grants the Authority permission to lease public park areas for specific activities like food sales or plant provision, provided they do not harm the park's character. Additionally, it empowers the Authority to lease its sites or poles for outdoor advertisements under prescribed terms.

name: PUNJAB MAINTENANCE OF PUBLIC ORDER (AMENDMENT) ACT 2017

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Maintenance of Public Order (Amendment) Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960.
amends: The Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960
repeals: The Punjab Maintenance of Public Order (Amendment) Ordinance, 2017
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1960 Ordinance to replace District Coordination Officers with Deputy Commissioners.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960 to align it with the local government system under the Punjab Local Government Act 2013. It substitutes references to 'District Coordination Officer' with 'Deputy Commissioner' across multiple sections and clauses of the 1960 Ordinance. Additionally, it repeals the earlier Punjab Maintenance of Public Order (Amendment) Ordinance, 2017.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Ehtram-e-Ramazan (Amendment) Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Ehtram-e-Ramazan Ordinance, 1981.
metadata.parent_law: The Ehtram-e-Ramazan Ordinance, 1981
metadata.one_line: Amends the Ehtram-e-Ramazan Ordinance, 1981 to update provisions and rationalize rules for the Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Ehtram-e-Ramazan Ordinance, 1981 specifically for its application in the Province of the Punjab. The amendments update existing provisions to rationalize them and address ancillary matters. Key changes include substituting 'Pakistan' with 'the Punjab', increasing fines from five hundred rupees to five thousand or fifty thousand rupees depending on the section, expanding arrest powers for Magistrates and Assistant Commissioners, and replacing references to the Federal Government with the Provincial Government.

metadata.short_title: The Police Order (Amendment) Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Police Order, 2002
metadata.parent_law: The Police Order, 2002

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Police Order, 2002 specifically for its application to the Province of the Punjab. The amendment omits provisions relating to the appointment of the Provincial Police Officer from the National Public Safety Commission list. Additionally, the Act repeals the Police Order (Amendment) Ordinance, 2017.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Employees Efficiency, Discipline and Accountability (Amendment) Act, 2017

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Employees Efficiency, Discipline and Accountability Act, 2006 to specify time limits for punishments and grant appeal rights to former employees. It substitutes 'sixty days' for 'ninety days' in certain subsections regarding case decisions and allows the Cabinet Committee on Legislation to extend this period under specific circumstances. Additionally, it inserts text into section 4 to define punishment periods as specific durations considering government loss.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Parks and Horticulture Authority Act, 2012 to preserve trees on public land. It substitutes provisions regarding the requirement for written permission before cutting or removing trees from public land. The Act introduces specific penalties for contravening these new provisions, including imprisonment and fines.

It substitutes subsection (3) of section 7 in the parent Act to include provisions for such extensions. The legislation also validates actions taken by the Government between the repeal of a previous Ordinance and the commencement of this Act.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Maternity Benefits (Amendment) Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Maternity Benefits Ordinance, 1958.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Maternity Benefits Ordinance, 1958 to restrict employment of women during specific periods before and after delivery.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Maternity Benefits Ordinance, 1958 to strengthen protections for female employees. It substitutes Section 3 of the Ordinance to prohibit employers from engaging women in any work for six weeks following childbirth. Additionally, it restricts arduous work or long hours of standing for one month immediately preceding and succeeding the delivery period.

It inserts a new section making offences cognizable and non-bailable, allowing first-class Magistrates to conduct summary trials under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898. The Act also repeals the earlier Punjab Prohibition of Expressing Matters on Walls (Amendment) Ordinance, 2015.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Strategic Coordination Act 2014 to update the composition of the Provincial Security Council. It substitutes Section 3(1) of the parent Act to include specific government ministers, nominated assembly members, and police officials as council members. The amendment also specifies terms for nominated persons and designates the Director General as a member/secretary.

name: PUNJAB EMPLOYEES EFFICIENCY, DISCIPLINE AND ACCOUNTABILITY (AMENDMENT) ACT 2014

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Employees Efficiency, Discipline and Accountability Act, 2006 by substituting section 19. The amendment clarifies the procedure for employees (excluding those in specific categories) to prefer appeals to the Punjab Service Tribunal. It establishes time limits for filing appeals after a final order or if no final order is passed within sixty days.

metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Employees' Social Security Ordinance, 1965 to adjust benefits, definitions, and establish medical institutions in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Employees' Social Security Ordinance, 1965 to align wage limits with government determinations and restrict jurisdiction to the Province of Punjab. It modifies provisions regarding survivor's pensions, funeral grants, and contribution rates while establishing a framework for public-private partnerships in medical institutions. The Act also repeals the earlier Provincial Employees' Social Security (Amendment) Ordinance, 2013.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Animals Slaughter Control (Amendment) Act, 2013

amends: The Punjab Animals Slaughter Control Act, 1963
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Animals Slaughter Control Act, 1963 by redefining 'animal' to include specific halal domesticated species.
metadata.summary: This Act serves as an amendment to the Punjab Animals Slaughter Control Act, 1963. It specifically targets Section 2 of the parent Act to substitute the definition of 'animal'. The new definition includes bulls, bullocks, buffaloes, camels, cows, goats, ostriches, sheep, and any other halal animal of any age domesticated in captivity.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government (Amendment) Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act, further to amend the Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 2001.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 2001 to grant additional taxation powers and validate prior levies.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 2001 to provide the Government with additional power to prescribe taxes or fees not specifically listed in the Second Schedule. It authorizes the recovery of these new taxes by the Local Government through rules. Additionally, the Act validates any tax, cess, fee, rate, rent, toll, charge, or surcharge levied without proper procedure prior to its commencement, provided they were levied before the Punjab Local Government (Amendment) Act, 2010 came into force.

metadata.short_title: The Administrator General's (Amendment) Act, 2012

metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Administrator General's Act, 1913 to align its provisions with the current administrative structure of Punjab. It updates references from 'Province' to 'Punjab', adjusts asset value thresholds for granting certificates, and modernizes references to relevant companies legislation. The amendments streamline the appointment process and clarify the jurisdiction of the High Court regarding estate administration within the province.

The Act also repeals the earlier Bank of Punjab (Amendment) Ordinance, 2011.

metadata.short_title: The Official Trustees (Amendment) Act, 2012

metadata.summary: This Act serves to amend the Powers of Attorney Act, 1882. It substitutes a new subsection in section 1 of the said Act to extend its application to the whole of the Punjab. Additionally, it omits sections 4 and 5 from the original 1882 Act.

It updates references from the Basic Democracies Order, 1959 to the Electoral College Act, 1964 and adds goats to the list of animals covered. The text also inserts new clauses regarding the definition of 'area' and penalties for contraventions.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Police Act, 1861 specifically for its application to the Province of West Pakistan. It inserts a new section 34-B into the Police Act, 1861 regarding the summary disposal of certain offences. The amendment allows accused persons to appear by pleader or plead guilty via registered letter with a small fine, leading to conviction endorsement on their licence without further proceedings.

name: AGA KHAN PROPERTIES (SUCCESSION AND TRANSFER) ACT 2026

metadata.short_title: The Aga Khan Properties (Succession and Transfer) Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for automatic and undisputed succession and transfer of properties of Aga Khan to the successor of Aga Khan of the Shia Imami Ismaili Muslims in the Punjab.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from the 4th February 2025
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for automatic succession and transfer of Aga Khan properties in Punjab to his successor without legal formalities.
metadata.summary: The Act ensures the automatic and undisputed succession of properties held by the Aga Khan to his successor within the Province of Punjab. It eliminates the need for probate, succession certificates, or court orders for such transfers and exempts them from various taxes and fees. The legislation overrides conflicting laws and mandates that all relevant authorities update records to reflect the successor as the lawful owner immediately upon commencement.

metadata.short_title: The Akhtar Saeed University Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Akhtar Saeed University.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Akhtar Saeed University in the private sector in Lahore with powers to confer degrees and manage faculties.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Akhtar Saeed University as a body corporate in the private sector located in Lahore. It defines the university's structure, including the Board of Governors, Academic Council, and various committees for staff selection and budget planning. The university is empowered to establish faculties ranging from Medical & Dental Sciences to Artificial Intelligence, prescribe courses, hold examinations, and award degrees.

metadata.short_title: The Anti-Terrorism (Punjab Amendment) Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 to establish procedures for special security cases involving confidentiality and virtual trials.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 by inserting a new section regarding the trial and inquiry of special security cases. It empowers a designated authority to declare cases requiring extraordinary protection as special security cases. The amendment outlines strict confidentiality measures, including sealed records, anonymous identities for judicial personnel, and the use of virtual trials via video conferencing from prisons.

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Asset Management Authority of Punjab as a body corporate to effectively manage and utilize government assets. The Authority aims to attract local and foreign investments, undertake development projects, generate revenue, create jobs, and enhance provincial exports. It operates across the whole of Punjab with its headquarters in Lahore, functioning in collaboration with private investors and various government departments.

name: CENTRAL UNIVERSITY OF EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES ACT 2026

It defines the university's structure, including the Chancellor, Board, Vice Chancellor, and various committees for finance and selection. The legislation outlines the university's functions to provide education across multiple faculties such as Computer Science, Engineering, and Medicine, while also setting up mechanisms for staff appointment and financial management.

It grants licenses to persons for supplying energy in specified areas and establishes the role of Electric Inspectors appointed by the Provincial Government. The Act defines key terms such as 'consumer', 'licensee', and 'electric supply-line', outlines procedures for publishing notices and handling objections, and repeals the Indian Electricity Act, 1903.

metadata.short_title: The Hindu Gains of Learning Act, 1930
metadata.long_title: An Act to remove doubt as to the rights of a member of a Hindu undivided family in property acquired by him by means of his learning.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: This Act clarifies that property acquired through learning is the separate property of a Hindu family member.
metadata.summary: The Hindu Gains of Learning Act, 1930 removes doubt regarding the rights of members of a Hindu undivided family to property acquired through their own learning. It establishes that such gains are the exclusive and separate property of the acquirer, regardless of whether the learning was imparted by family members or aided by joint funds. The Act also clarifies that these rights apply even if the individual or family was supported by joint funds while acquiring the learning.

metadata.short_title: The Identification of Prisoners Act, 1920
metadata.long_title: An Act to authorise the taking of measurements and photographs of convicts and others.

metadata.summary: This Act authorizes the taking of measurements and photographs of convicted persons and those ordered to give security for good behavior. It also allows measurements to be taken from non-convicted persons arrested for serious offenses and empowers Magistrates to order such procedures during investigations. The Act defines key terms like 'measurements' and 'police officer', outlines the destruction of records upon acquittal, and grants the Provincial Government power to make rules.

metadata.short_title: The Motor Vehicles (Drivers) Ordinance, 1942

metadata.summary: The Motor Vehicles (Drivers) Ordinance, 1942 was promulgated by the Governor-General to address an emergency requiring the requisitioning of motor vehicle drivers. It establishes a register of persons capable of driving motor vehicles within the Province or area and empowers officers to require registered persons to present themselves for service. The document outlines penalties for non-compliance, including fines and imprisonment, and specifies that prosecutions require sanction from the Provincial Government unless the person is subject to military law.

It establishes specific definitions for terms like 'child marriage', 'guardian', and 'contracting party' to clarify legal responsibilities. The Act prescribes severe penalties for those who arrange, perform, or facilitate such marriages, including imprisonment and substantial fines. Additionally, it empowers courts to issue injunctions to prevent impending child marriages and repeals the Child Marriage Restraint Act of 1929 and a 2026 Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Consolidation of Holdings (Repeal) Act, 2026

metadata.summary: This Act repeals the Punjab Consolidation of Holdings Ordinance, 1960 to facilitate the implementation of land consolidation schemes. It mandates that confirmed schemes be implemented within 365 days by the Collector, while incomplete schemes with at least 70% completion are finished within 180 days. Schemes with less than 70% completion are de-notified and records transferred to the District Collector. The Board of Revenue is empowered to issue guidelines and establish digital systems for these purposes.

name: AQUACULTURE AUTHORITY OF THE PUNJAB ACT 2026

metadata.short_title: The Aquaculture Authority of the Punjab Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of Aquaculture Authority of the Punjab.

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Aquaculture Authority of the Punjab as a body corporate to develop the aquaculture sector and facilitate private stakeholders. It aims to regulate the industry, improve food security, create employment, and generate revenue within the province. The Authority is composed of various government secretaries, department heads, and members of the Provincial Assembly, with powers to frame rules and regulations for its operations.

name: CHENAB UNIVERSITY OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY, RAHIM YAR KHAN ACT 2026

metadata.short_title: The Chenab University of Science and Technology, Rahim Yar Khan Act, 2026

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Chenab University of Science and Technology, Rahim Yar Khan as a private sector university located in Rahim Yar Khan. The university is empowered to provide instruction across various faculties including Engineering, Sciences, Law, and Nursing, while also conducting research and awarding degrees. It defines the structure of the university, including the Patron (Governor), Board of Governors, Rector, and Academic Council, and outlines their respective functions regarding administration, finance, and academic affairs.

name: EVACUEE PROPERTY AND DISPLACED PERSONS LAWS (REPEAL) (AMENDMENT) ACT 2026

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Evacuee Property and Displaced Persons Laws (Repeal) Act, 1975 to incorporate new schemes for rural agricultural and urban property disposal. It expands the powers of officers and the Full Board, including civil court powers and protection from legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith. The amendment also introduces specific time limits for implementing final orders and addresses the abatement of pending proceedings under repealed acts.

metadata.short_title: The Forest (Amendment) Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Forest Act, 1927

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Forest Act, 1927 to introduce provisions regarding the management of reserved and protected forests. It empowers the Government to declare a reserved forest or any part thereof as no longer reserved, and similarly for protected forests, in cases involving projects of national importance by the Federal Government or the Provincial Government. These declarations can be made on such terms and conditions as the Government may prescribe.

It substitutes references to 'Chancellor' with 'Chairperson Board of Governors' in sections 4, 10, and 12. Additionally, it updates the list of faculties included in the university's schedule to include Sciences, Arts, Computer Sciences, Commerce, and Law.

metadata.short_title: COTHM Global Institute, Lahore Act 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the reconstitution of the COTHM Global Institute, Lahore.

metadata.summary: This Act provides for the reconstitution of the COTHM Global Institute, Lahore as a body corporate in the private sector. It establishes the Institute with its main campus in Lahore and defines its internal structure, including the Patron, Board, Academic Council, and various faculties. The Act outlines the functions of the Institute, such as providing education across multiple disciplines like Hospitality, AI, and Arts, while also setting up committees for finance planning and faculty selection.

metadata.short_title: The Police Order (Second Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Police Order, 2002.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Police Order, 2002 to introduce new definitions regarding Incident Commanders, riots, and unlawful assemblies. It establishes a Riot Management Unit under the supervision of an Additional Inspector General of Police to manage riots across the Province. The Act outlines procedures for declaring Riot Zones, coordinating between departments, using technology in coordination with the Punjab Safe City Authority, and prescribing strict trial timelines and property transfer restrictions for accused persons involved in such offences.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Employees' Social Security (Amendment) Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Provincial Employees' Social Security Ordinance, 1965.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Employees' Social Security Ordinance, 1965 to update specific clauses within that Ordinance. It increases a numerical limit from four to five in section 5 and modifies references to financial bodies. Additionally, it changes audit requirements for institutions to include the Auditor General of Pakistan alongside qualified chartered accountants. The Act also updates section 47-A to insert new wording regarding operational modes and adds conditions requiring healthcare institutions established under that section to meet relevant federal or provincial laws.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to allow 16-year-olds with permits to drive specific motorcycles.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to introduce provisions for juvenile driving. It allows persons aged sixteen or above to drive motorcycles up to 125 CC or equivalent electric motorcycles if they hold a juvenile driving permit issued by the licensing authority. Additionally, it omits specific words and subsections from section 89-B of the Ordinance regarding notified roads.

metadata.short_title: The Panjnad University Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Panjnad University.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Panjnad University in the private sector within Punjab with defined functions and committees.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Panjnad University as a body corporate in the private sector located in Lahore. It outlines the university's powers to provide instruction across various disciplines, establish departments, and conduct examinations. The Act also defines key bodies such as the Board of Governors, Academic Council, and Finance Committee, along with their respective functions and composition.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965.
metadata.parent_law: The Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965
metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to define end-of-life vehicles and establish a scrapping mechanism.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to introduce definitions for 'end-of-life vehicle' and 'scrapping of end-of-life vehicle'. It establishes a mechanism for the disposal and recycling of such vehicles through private facilities or those established by the Transport and Masstransit Department. The primary purpose is to strengthen air quality management, reduce vehicular emissions, and promote eco-friendly masstransit and electric vehicles.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles (Second Amendment) Act, 2026

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to modernize driving license procedures through electronic systems. It introduces new definitions for a Driving License Information Management System and an electronic ticketing system. The legislation also updates various sections regarding photographs, medical certificates, and penalties for offenses such as driving on the wrong side of the road or using tinted glasses.

metadata.short_title: The Public Sector Medical Universities (Amendment) Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the laws of the public sector medical universities.

The University of Child Health Sciences, Lahore Act, 2021 (XVIII of 2021)
metadata.one_line: Amends eligibility criteria for Vice Chancellors in Punjab's public sector medical universities.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the laws governing public sector medical universities in the Punjab to update eligibility requirements for the post of Vice Chancellor. The amendments primarily increase the minimum age from sixty-five to seventy years and specify detailed academic qualifications, including a requirement of at least ten years as a Professor and twenty publications in indexed journals. It applies to seven specific university acts and one ordinance, ensuring uniform standards across these institutions.

metadata.short_title: The Public Sector Universities (Amendment) Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the laws of certain public sector universities in the Punjab.
metadata.one_line: Amends specific university ordinances and acts in Punjab to update their names and titles.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the laws governing several public sector universities in the Punjab province. It specifically targets Ordinances from 2002 and Acts from 2013 related to various Government Colleges and Women's Universities across cities like Lahore, Faisalabad, Sialkot, and Bahawalpur. The primary mechanism involves substituting existing names with new titles that append 'as the University' or similar phrasing, while omitting the standalone word 'University' in specific sections.

name: PUNJAB AGRICULTURE, FOOD AND DRUG AUTHORITY (AMENDMENT) ACT 2025

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Agriculture, Food and Drug Authority (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Agriculture, Food and Drug Authority Act 2016.
amends: The Punjab Agriculture, Food and Drug Authority Act, 2016

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Agriculture, Food and Drug Authority Act 2016 by inserting new definitions into Section 2. It expands the scope of regulation to include alternative medicine, animal feed, biological medicines, biomedical devices, cosmetics, orthopaedic implants, raw materials, soil, and water contamination. The amendment also updates Section 3 regarding the Secretary to the Government, Home Department, and modifies Section 5 to include these new categories in forensic examination and testing duties.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Child Marriage Restraint Ordinance, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to restrain the solemnization of child marriages in Punjab and for the matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto.

metadata.one_line: This Ordinance restrains child marriages in Punjab, defines offences and penalties, and repeals the 1929 Act.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance aims to restrain the solemnization of child marriages in the Province of Punjab. It applies to all persons involved in arranging or performing such marriages, including guardians and registrars. The law establishes strict penalties for contracting child marriages, inducing abuse, trafficking children, and failing to prevent solemnization, while also providing powers for injunctions to stop impending marriages.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Act, 2026

metadata.one_line: An Act to levy, alter and rationalize taxes in Punjab while amending existing tax legislation.
metadata.summary: This Act levies, alters, and rationalizes certain taxes, fees, and duties within the Punjab. It comes into force on July 1, 2026, and amends several existing acts including those related to urban immovable property tax, motor vehicle taxation, sales tax on services, and motor vehicle transaction licenses. The legislation introduces new sections regarding input tax management through a risk-based evaluation system and adjusts penalty structures for various defaults.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Forensic Science Authority (Amendment) Act, 2026

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Forensic Science Authority Act 2025 by adding specific roles to Section 3. The amendments include the addition of a Director General for Agriculture, Food and Drug Authority, and a Chairman for the Punjab Information Technology Board as members. The Act was passed by the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab on April 22, 2026, and received assent on May 06, 2026.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Food Safety Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends several existing Acts in Punjab to align them with the newly established Food Safety and Consumer Protection Department. It updates departmental names, revises authority designations, and introduces a uniform appellate mechanism that guarantees hearing rights before adverse orders are passed. The amendments apply to laws covering sugar control, price regulation, consumer protection, food safety, agricultural marketing, and Halal development.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Higher Education Commission (Amendment) Act, 2026

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Higher Education Commission Act, 2014 by inserting a new subsection regarding eligibility for the Chairperson position. It stipulates that a person shall not be eligible for appointment as Chairperson if they are more than sixty-five years of age on the last date fixed for submission of applications. The amendment was passed by the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab and received assent from the Governor on February 04, 2026.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab High Security Zones (Establishment) Act, 2026

metadata.administering_body: Home Department of the Government of the Punjab

metadata.summary: The Punjab High Security Zones (Establishment) Act, 2026 provides a legal framework for declaring high security zones and designated areas within the province. It regulates public gatherings by requiring prior permission for events in designated areas while prohibiting them entirely in high security zones. The Act establishes Provincial and District Intelligence Committees to recommend zone declarations and manage applications, with penalties including imprisonment and fines for violations.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Judicial Academy Act, 2007 to shift the main campus to Kala Shah Kaku. It expands training functions to include officers of government departments, autonomous bodies, and private organizations. Additionally, it updates eligibility criteria for faculty members and the Director General position.

It updates the cess rate to 0.90% and introduces provisions for establishing pickets, check-posts, and monitoring stations to ensure proper collection. The legislation also grants officers enhanced powers to inspect goods, seek assistance from other agencies, and imposes penalties for obstruction or evasion.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Legal Aid (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Legal Aid Act 2018 to provide legal aid to indigent persons dispossessed of immovable property. It specifically extends coverage to those pursuing proceedings before Tribunals established under the Punjab Protection of Ownership of Immovable Property Act 2025. The amendment also updates definitions and procedures within the parent Act to include these new categories of cases and persons.

It introduces stricter penalties for illegal possession, clarifies key definitions regarding 'accused' and 'Judge', and establishes Scrutiny Committees in each district. The amendments also streamline judicial processes by omitting obsolete sections and providing indemnity to officials acting in good faith.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance aims to prevent the theft, unauthorized removal, and damage of public utilities infrastructure within the Punjab province. It establishes a specific enforcement authority and defines various terms related to infrastructure components and offenders like scrap dealers. The law prescribes severe criminal penalties, including imprisonment and substantial fines, for offenses such as theft, unauthorized possession, and willful damage.

name: PUNJAB REGULATION OF KITE FLYING ACT 2025

metadata.one_line: Regulates kite flying in Punjab to save lives and property by banning dangerous materials and mandating registration.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates kite flying in the Punjab to protect human life and public/private property. It prohibits the manufacture, sale, or use of kites with metallic wires or sharp materials like 'maanjha'. The law mandates registration for manufacturers and sellers, establishes penalties including imprisonment and fines for violations, and provides a framework for permissible kite flying under specific notifications.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Senior Citizens Welfare Act, 2026

It establishes the Punjab Senior Citizens Welfare Council and the Punjab Senior Citizens Welfare Fund to manage welfare services and grants. The Council is composed of government secretaries, assembly members, philanthropists, and other officials with powers to conduct research, formulate policies, and manage funds for indigent senior citizens.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Trusts Act, 2020 to designate the Director General Labour Welfare as the regulator for issuing No Objection Certificates in specific matters. It inserts provisions allowing the regulator to issue or cancel certificates with a right of appeal to the Secretary, Labour and Human Resource Department. Additionally, it establishes an appeal mechanism before the Senior Member, Board of Revenue, Punjab, for aggrieved trustees and substitutes 'Assistant Commissioner' for 'Assistant Director' in section 20.

It raises the age threshold from fourteen to sixteen years and designates the Director General, Social Welfare and Bait-ul-Maal, Punjab as the competent authority. The text also inserts new powers for a Controller to oversee anti-vagrancy operations and amend specific sections regarding penalties for employing children in alms solicitation.

metadata.short_title: The Registration (Amendment) Act, 2026

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Registration Act, 1908 to modernize land record management through electronic systems. It introduces definitions for biometric verification, electronic records, and electronic signatures, while establishing the role of the Punjab Land Records Authority. The legislation mandates the use of electronic record systems for documents registered after specific dates and imposes penalties for fraudulent misuse of these systems.

It inserts specific provisions into Section 27-A and Schedule-I of the parent Act to levy stamp duties on such assignments within or beyond twelve months. The legislation also substitutes certain figures in existing articles to adjust duty rates and repeals a previous Ordinance on the same subject.

metadata.short_title: The Stamp (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026

It reduces the duty on such deeds from 3% in rural areas to 1%, matching the existing urban rate, thereby eliminating discrimination between urban and rural transactions. The measures aim to simplify the law, reduce litigation costs, encourage formalization of property transfers, and enhance revenue stability for the Punjab government.

metadata.short_title: The Superior University, Lahore (Amendment) Act, 2026

The amendments also expand the Board's powers to manage various university facilities and units.

metadata.short_title: The Suthra Punjab Authority Act, 2026

It applies to the whole of Punjab and creates a body corporate with powers to acquire property and sue or be sued. The Authority consists of government officials, divisional commissioners, and technical experts nominated by the Chief Minister. The Act also defines key terms like 'waste' and 'waste management', sets up funds for operations, and prescribes penalties for offences such as burning waste or obstructing inspectors.

The legislation also introduces new definitions for terms like 'dangerous building' and 'heritage area', adjusts fines for offences, and adds specific penalties for sanitation violations within these zones.

It mandates that such inquiries be conducted by a joint team comprising a Superintendent of Police and other law enforcement agencies rather than solely by civil armed forces. The amended provisions regarding these specific sub-sections remain in force for a period of two years from 2025.

The legislation outlines functions such as instruction provision, research, and staff selection, while also setting up committees for finance and planning.

amends: The Defence Housing Authority Rawalpindi Act, 2013

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Defence Housing Authority Rawalpindi Act 2013 to align administrative terms with the new Division structure. It expands the definition of welfare activities to include serving and retired defence personnel and their families. metadata.short_title: The Drugs (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Drugs Act, 1976.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Drugs Act, 1976 to update Drug Court composition and appointment procedures.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Drugs Act, 1976 to revise the composition of Drug Courts. It specifies that the Chairperson must be a District and Sessions Judge appointed by the Provincial Government in consultation with the Chief Justice of the Lahore High Court. Additionally, it requires two members from the pharmaceutical or medical fields with fifteen years of experience. The amendment also clarifies the quorum requirements for Drug Courts.

metadata.short_title: The Drugs (Second Amendment) Act, 2025

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Drugs Act, 1976 to incorporate 'therapeutic goods' into its definitions and provisions. It specifically modifies Section 3 and Section 44 of the Drugs Act, 1976 to ensure therapeutic goods are treated alongside drugs regarding distribution and stock management. The legislation was passed by the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab and received assent on December 17, 2025.

metadata.short_title: The Forest (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Forest Act, 1927.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Forest Act, 1927 to update various definitions regarding flora, fauna, and departmental officers. It significantly increases penalties for offences committed in reserved forests, including higher imprisonment terms and fines. The legislation also introduces a new section to protect vulnerable native flora species and omits several older sections from the parent Act.

It creates a body corporate with perpetual succession, defining its structure including a Patron, Board, Rector, and various academic authorities. The University is empowered to offer instruction across multiple faculties, manage its own fund, and make rules and regulations for administration.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Labour Code, 2026

The Punjab Occupational Safety and Health Act 2019

metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and rationalizes laws concerning workers' rights, forced labor elimination, and working conditions in Punjab. It applies to all sectors within the province except civil servants, defense services, and police forces. The Code establishes mechanisms for dispute resolution, defines key terms like 'worker' and 'wage', and retains certain safety rules from repealed acts until new ones are made.

It empowers the Board of Governors to frame regulations, conduct examinations, award degrees, and manage finances through specific committees.

It confers upon the University the power to award degrees, diplomas, and certificates across various faculties including Fashion, Textile Design, Computing, and Applied Sciences. The Act defines the structure of the University, including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Board of Governors, and various committees responsible for finance, discipline, and academic functions.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Probation of Offenders Ordinance, 1960 to substitute 'the Punjab' for 'Pakistan' in its scope. It introduces a definition for 'community service' as unpaid work beneficial to the community. The Act mandates court considerations regarding offender capability and rehabilitation when ordering community service, placing probationers under the supervision of the Deputy Commissioner. Additionally, it extends the maximum duration of certain provisions from exceeding one year to less than ten years.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Employees' Social Security Ordinance, 1965 by inserting new provisions regarding financial benefits. It allows secured persons to receive financial benefits for purchasing essential commodities from notified outlets, subject to Government approval and fund availability. The amendment also modifies the long title and preamble of the parent Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Police Order (Amendment) Ordinance, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Police Order 2002.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Police Order, 2002 to address the need for an enhanced organizational response to combat serious and organized crimes. It establishes a new Crime Control Department headed by an Additional Inspector General of Police, comprising specialized units across districts and sub-divisions. The document outlines procedures for transferring investigations from District Police to this new department for specific heinous crimes listed in the Fourth Schedule, such as dacoity, robbery, kidnapping, and rape.

It empowers the Punjab Safe Cities Authority to record traffic violations and issue electronic violation tickets. The text establishes mechanisms for contesting charges, depositing fines electronically, and recovering outstanding amounts through vehicle impoundment and auction if fines remain unpaid.

The Act significantly increases penalties for offenses related to keeping, possessing, carrying, or displaying prohibited and non-prohibited bore weapons, as well as military stores.

It modifies provisions concerning officer appointments, eligibility criteria for private sector posts, and disciplinary matters within the Board. The Act also repeals a corresponding Ordinance passed earlier in 2025.

name: PUNJAB AUTISM SCHOOL AND RESOURCE CENTRE ACT 2025

It creates a body corporate known as the Centre, managed by a Board of Governors comprising government officials, experts, parents, and educationists. The Act defines key terms, outlines the constitution and functions of the Board, and empowers the Government to frame necessary rules and regulations.

It modifies provisions concerning the authority imposing fines for violations and redesignates District Judges as Consumer Courts under the Lahore High Court. The amendments also address the transfer of pending cases and employees from defunct consumer courts.

name: PUNJAB CENTER OF EXCELLENCE ON COUNTERING VIOLENT EXTREMISM ACT 2025

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Center of Excellence on Countering Violent Extremism to address challenges arising from terrorism and subversive activities. The Center is empowered to conduct research, develop strategies, create action plans, and provide technical support to government bodies. It also functions through a Board of Governors comprising key provincial officials to manage its affairs.

name: PUNJAB CONTROL OF NARCOTICS SUBSTANCES (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE 2025

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Control of Narcotics Substances Act, 2025 to ensure harmony with other laws like the CNSA 1997. It substitutes specific words in sections 38, 39, 40, 41, and 44 regarding bail conditions, court composition, and jurisdiction. The amendments aim to remove operational bottlenecks and clarify legal procedures for narcotics offences within Punjab.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Education Foundation (Amendment) Act, 2025

It specifically alters Section 5 of the parent Act by reducing a numerical requirement from three to two and adding conditions for Directors. The amendments mandate that three Directors must be members of the Provincial Assembly with at least one woman member, while requiring non-governmental Directors and academicians to possess demonstrable expertise.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Educational Institutions (Reconstitution) (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Educational Institutions (Reconstitution) Act 2021 to constitute certain educational institutions in Punjab.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Educational Institutions (Reconstitution) Act, 2021 to improve governance and management of educational institutions in Punjab. It aims to provide academic, financial, and administrative autonomy to enhance education quality. Specifically, it adds an entry for Chenab Colleges established under the Jhang Educational Trust to the Schedule of the amended Act.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Emergency Service (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Emergency Service Act 2006.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Emergency Service Act 2006 by substituting an expression in section 6.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Emergency Service Act 2006 to substitute specific words within section 6. It was passed by the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab on December 8, 2025, and received assent from the Governor on December 17, 2025. The amendment comes into force immediately upon publication in the Extraordinary Gazette.

name: PUNJAB ENERGY EFFICIENCY AND CONSERVATION AGENCY ACT 2025

Punjab Energy Efficiency and Conservation Agency Fund

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Energy Efficiency and Conservation Agency as a body corporate with perpetual succession. The Agency is designated under the National Energy Efficiency and Conservation Act, 2016, to implement its provisions and related matters. It includes powers to frame regulations, manage funds, prepare annual reports, and impose fines for contraventions.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Enforcement and Regulations (Amendment) Ordinance, 2025

It also modifies procedures for annual budget approval by the Authority and updates the process for issuing guidelines and codes of conduct. The document substitutes specific terms regarding authorized officers and budget submission within the parent Act.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Fertilizers Control Act, 2025

metadata.one_line: Regulates and controls the manufacture, supply, importation, distribution, and quality standards of fertilizers in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the regulation and control of fertilizers within the Province of Punjab. It covers the manufacture, supply, importation, distribution, dealership, quality standards, pricing, licensing, advertising, transportation, storage, sale, monitoring, and disposal of fertilizers. The Act ensures the availability of quality fertilizers for agricultural purposes and establishes various authorities including a Controller and Deputy Controller to enforce these regulations.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Finance Act, 1977.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Finance Act, 1977 by inserting new sub-sections into section 3. It mandates that drawing and disbursing officers or principal officers of local authorities must deduct tax from employee salaries and deposit it in the treasury. The Act also establishes liability for officers who fail to deduct or deposit the tax, allowing recovery orders by the Excise and Taxation Officer after providing an opportunity of being heard.

name: PUNJAB CONTROL OF NARCOTIC SUBSTANCES ACT 2025

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for control of narcotic substances, controlled substances and the production, processing, trafficking and transportation of such drugs and substances and the prevention of illicit narcotics related activities and for matters ancillary thereto and connected therewith.
repeals: Control of Narcotics Substance Act, 1997 (Act No. XXV of 1997)
metadata.one_line: An Act to control narcotic substances and prevent illicit narcotics-related activities in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the control of narcotic and controlled substances within the Province of Punjab. It covers the production, processing, trafficking, and transportation of these drugs while aiming to prevent illicit activities. The law defines key terms such as 'addict', 'assets', and 'cannabis' and establishes the Anti Narcotics Force (ANF) for enforcement purposes.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Financial Advisory Services Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Punjab Financial Advisory Services.
establishes: Board of the Punjab Financial Advisory Services
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Financial Advisory Services Authority to provide financial and management advisory services in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Financial Advisory Services, a body corporate with perpetual succession. The Authority is headed by a Board comprising government officials, assembly members, and private sector experts. It provides a wide range of services including financial planning, investment advisory, tax advice, and public financial management to various clients including administrative departments and private entities.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Act, 2025

amends: The Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act, 2012
metadata.max_penalty: one million rupees
metadata.one_line: Rationalizes sales tax on services in Punjab by amending the 2012 Act to declare specific services tax-free.
metadata.summary: This Act rationalizes the structure of sales tax on services within the Province of Punjab. It achieves this by amending the Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act, 2012 to insert new sections and substitute existing clauses regarding taxable and exempt services. The legislation specifically lists healthcare, education, public transport, and other government-provided services as tax-free under the First Schedule.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Forensic Science Authority Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Punjab Forensic Science Authority for forensic examination of documents, materials, equipment, impressions or other objects.

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Forensic Science Authority as a body corporate to conduct forensic examinations on various materials and objects. It defines key terms such as 'expert', 'forensic material', and the composition of the Authority, which includes members from various government departments and specialized experts. The Authority is empowered to provide scientific opinions to investigating agencies and other authorized bodies. Additionally, the Act provides for the absorption of existing forensic facilities and employees into the new Authority, repealing the previous Punjab Forensic Science Agency Act, 2007.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Infrastructure Development Cess (Amendment) Act, 2025

amends: The Punjab Infrastructure Development Cess Act, 2015

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Infrastructure Development Cess Act, 2015 by inserting a new section 5A regarding refunds. It empowers the Authority or its authorized officer to allow refunds of cess claimed to have been paid through inadvertence, error, or misconstruction. The amendment is subject to such conditions and restrictions as may be prescribed. The Act came into force immediately upon assent.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Judicial Academy (Amendment) Act, 2025

It expands the Board's powers to establish sub-campuses, formulate policies, and frame regulations for business conduct. The legislation also inserts provisions for constituting committees and making rules or regulations by the Government.

metadata.summary: This Act repeals the Punjab Khal Panchayat Act 2019 to facilitate the transfer of properties and personnel from the defunct Punjab Khal Panchayat Authority. It mandates the abolition of vacant positions, termination of specific contracts, and absorption of remaining employees into the Irrigation Department or the Surplus Pool of the General Administration Department. Additionally, it provides for the transfer of pension fund contributions to the Finance Department.

It inserts 'or a civil court' into Section 3, allowing civil courts to issue certificates following the Succession Act, 1925 procedure. Additionally, it omits Section 10 of the original 2021 Act.

It includes all housing schemes in rural areas approved under any law for the time being in force as rating areas. Additionally, it specifies that urban immovable property tax shall be levied, assessed, collected, and transferred to local governments under the Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958.

sub-section (2) of section 27 of the Punjab Development of Cities Act, 1976

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Horticulture Authority to develop and maintain public parks, green belts, and regulate outdoor advertisements like billboards and sky signs. It applies throughout the Punjab and comes into force immediately upon enactment. The Act also defines various terms related to land use and advertising structures while repealing specific sections of previous acts regarding horticulture authorities.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government Act, 2025

metadata.summary: The Punjab Local Government Act, 2025 is enacted to reconstitute and strengthen local governments as the third tier of government in Punjab. It aims to consolidate existing laws regarding the powers and functions of local governments to ensure meaningful devolution of political, administrative, and financial responsibility to elected representatives. The Act promotes good governance, effective service delivery, transparent decision-making, and institutionalized public participation at the local level.

name: PUNJAB PRIMARY AND SECONDARY HEALTHCARE SERVICES ACT 2025

metadata.one_line: Establishes a framework for primary and secondary healthcare services, facilities, and community health inspectors in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act provides the legal mechanism for delivering primary and secondary healthcare services across the province of Punjab. It establishes specific healthcare facilities including Maryam Nawaz Health Clinics and Hospitals, as well as Tehsil and District Headquarter Hospitals. The legislation outlines the roles of Community Health Inspectors, allows for outsourcing of service delivery through agreements, and mandates the digitization of public healthcare records.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Prohibition of Kite Flying Ordinance, 2001 to update definitions of 'child' and 'guardian'. It modifies penalty clauses for manufacturing or transporting kites, introduces specific fines for children under the Juvenile Justice System Act, 2018, and omits certain sections from the original Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Protected Areas (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Protected Areas Act 2020.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Protected Areas Act 2020 to include definitions for 'Board', 'ecotourism', and 'officer' referencing existing wildlife legislation. It inserts a new section on ecotourism principles, omits specific sections from the original act, and substitutes administrative references to the Director General, Wildlife and Parks. The amendments also increase imprisonment terms for certain defaults and adjust cognizance of offences.

metadata.summary: This Act creates an efficient and transparent administrative, legal, and fiscal framework to promote domestic and foreign investment in the mining and minerals sector within the Punjab. It establishes various committees and divisions, such as the Auction Committee and Exploration Promotion Division, to manage mineral titles through auctions and licensing processes. The legislation outlines obligations for title holders regarding financial deposits, environmental management plans, and local content requirements while repealing previous rules from 2002.

name: PUNJAB PROTECTION OF OWNERSHIP OF IMMOVABLE PROPERTY ACT 2025

metadata.long_title: An Act to protect lawful ownership of immovable property in the Punjab and to provide effective legal remedies against dispossession of a lawful owner from his immovable property and to provide a mechanism for expeditious resolution of disputes arising therefrom and for the matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto.

metadata.one_line: An Act to protect lawful ownership of immovable property in Punjab and provide mechanisms for expeditious dispute resolution.
metadata.summary: This Act protects lawful ownership of immovable property in the Punjab by providing effective legal remedies against dispossession. It establishes a Dispute Resolution Committee and a Tribunal to resolve disputes arising from illegal possession or other related matters. The Act defines key terms, creates offences for illegal possession with significant penalties, and empowers the Government to make rules and provide necessary premises for the Tribunal.

name: PUNJAB PROTECTION OF OWNERSHIP OF IMMOVABLE PROPERTY ORDINANCE 2025

metadata.one_line: This Ordinance protects lawful ownership of immovable property in Punjab by establishing a tribunal and committee to resolve disputes.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Protection of Ownership of Immovable Property Ordinance, 2025 was promulgated by the Governor of Punjab to protect lawful ownership against dispossession. It establishes a Dispute Resolution Committee and a Property Tribunal to provide expeditious resolution of disputes connected with immovable property. The Ordinance creates offences for illegal possession through fraud, force, or other means, punishable by imprisonment up to ten years, and overrides provisions of any other law.

name: PUNJAB PUBLIC AWARENESS AND DISSEMINATION OF INFORMATION ACT 2025

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Public Awareness and Dissemination of Information Act, 2025

metadata.summary: The Punjab Public Awareness and Dissemination of Information Act, 2025 establishes a legal framework for disseminating information about government projects, initiatives, programs, and policies. It applies to the Government of the Punjab and all public bodies within the province, requiring them to launch awareness campaigns through various media platforms. The Act defines key terms such as 'public body' and 'advertising agency', outlines parameters for campaigns including funding and timelines, and sets up a complaint redressal mechanism headed by the Director General.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the laws relating to public representatives of the Province of the Punjab. The amendments take effect immediately upon commencement of the related salary revision act.

It also repeals the Punjab Regularization of Service (Repeal) Ordinance 2025 that had previously been enacted. The Act includes a saving provision ensuring that actions taken under the repealed 2018 Act continue to have effect as if it had not been repealed.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance repeals the Punjab Regularization of Service Act 2018 to facilitate a shift from Basic Pay Scale to Lump Sum Pay Package. The primary objective is to reduce the financial burden on the Government exchequer regarding pensions and other liabilities. It was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab under Article 128 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session.

name: PUNJAB REGULATION OF KITE FLYING ORDINANCE 2025

metadata.one_line: Regulates kite flying in Punjab to save human life and property while allowing permissible activities under strict conditions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates kite flying in the Province of Punjab to protect human life, public and private property. It prohibits the use of metallic wires or threads coated with sharp materials but allows for 'permissible kite flying' under specific notifications issued by the Deputy Commissioner. The law establishes offences for unauthorized kite flying, manufacturing, or selling prohibited materials, prescribing severe penalties including imprisonment and fines. It also mandates registration for manufacturers and sellers of permissible materials and provides a regulatory framework for kite flying associations.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Road Safety Authority (Amendment) Act, 2025
