metadata.one_line: Amends the Lahore Arts Council Ordinance, 2002 by substituting 'Chief Minister' for 'Governor' in specific sections.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Lahore Arts Council Ordinance, 2002 to replace references to the Governor with the Chief Minister in sections 2, 8, and 13. It was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab under Article 128 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session. The previous amendment ordinance from 2002 is repealed by this document.

name: THE PUNJAB LOCAL GOVERNMENT (FIRST AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE 2003

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government (First Amendment) Ordinance, 2003
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 2001.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect from 31st December, 2002
metadata.parent_law: Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 2001
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 2001 by changing a specific date in section 24.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 2001 to alter a deadline mentioned in section 24. It was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab under Article 128 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session. The amendment substitutes the date '31st December, 2002' with '30th June, 2003' in a specific proviso.

name: THE INSTITUTE OF SOUTH ASIA LAHORE ORDINANCE 2003

metadata.short_title: The Institute of South Asia, Lahore, Ordinance, 2003
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the Institute of South Asia, Lahore and to provide for matters connected therewith or ancillary thereto
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Institute of South Asia, Lahore in Punjab for computer sciences and other branches of learning.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Institute of South Asia, Lahore as a corporate body with perpetual succession located in Lahore. It defines the functions of the Institute, including instruction in computer sciences, research, examinations, and degree conferral. The Board of Governors is vested with administration and management powers, while the Governor of the Punjab serves as the Patron.

metadata.short_title: The Bank of Punjab (Amendment) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Bank of Punjab Act, 1989 (XII of 1989).
metadata.commencement: at once, except section 3 which shall be deemed to have come into force with effect from 11 March 2000
metadata.parent_law: Bank of Punjab Act, 1989 (XII of 1989)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Bank of Punjab Act, 1989 regarding Board Chairman nomination and executive powers.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Bank of Punjab Act, 1989 to alter provisions concerning the Board of Directors. Specifically, it mandates that the Chairman be nominated by the Governor from amongst official Directors and restricts the Chairman's role to presiding over meetings without exercising executive authority. Additionally, it modifies tenure requirements for certain positions and removes the need for previous government approval in specific contexts.

metadata.short_title: The Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Cooperative Societies Act, 1925
metadata.parent_law: The Cooperative Societies Act, 1925
metadata.one_line: Amends the Cooperative Societies Act, 1925 by empowering the Registrar to amend society byelaws.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Cooperative Societies Act, 1925 to grant the Registrar powers to amend a society's byelaws if they are inconsistent with existing laws or in the interest of the society. It allows the Registrar to issue notices requiring amendments within sixty days and register them if the society fails to comply after being heard. Appeals against such orders lie to the Government within two months.

metadata.short_title: The Defamation Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make provisions in respect of defamation or matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
metadata.max_penalty: three months imprisonment and minimum Rs. 50,000 compensatory damages
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance defines defamation, sets out defences and remedies including apologies and damages.
metadata.summary: The Defamation Ordinance, 2002 provides legal provisions regarding defamation in written, oral, or visual forms. It distinguishes between slander and libel, outlines specific defences such as truth and public interest, and establishes procedures for filing actions including notice periods. The law prescribes remedies like apologies, damages with a minimum of Rs. 50,000, or imprisonment, while applying existing civil procedure codes.

name: DISPOSAL OF LAND BY DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITIES (REGULATION) (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE 2002

metadata.short_title: The Disposal of Land by Development Authorities (Regulation) (Amendment) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Disposal of Land by Development Authorities (Regulation) Act, 1998.

The text also modifies procedural aspects such as service of notices, time limits for decrees, and the transfer of cases between courts.

It grants the University powers to provide instruction, frame courses, hold examinations, and award degrees at various levels. The document defines key terms such as Academic Council, Syndicate, and affiliated colleges, while also setting up committees for affiliation and discipline.

The document outlines the university's powers to frame statutes, conduct examinations, award degrees, and affiliate other educational institutions while transferring all assets and employees from the former college to the new university.

It defines key terms such as 'infant', 'designated product', and 'health care facility' while establishing the National Infant Feeding Board. The law regulates the marketing and promotion of milk substitutes and feeding bottles, imposing penalties on manufacturers and distributors who contravene its provisions.

The Ordinance defines key terms such as 'horse-race' and 'race-course', outlines procedures for granting licenses, and prescribes penalties including fines up to five thousand rupees for holding unlicensed races or violating license conditions.

name: PUNJAB CONFERMENT OF PROPRIETARY RIGHTS ON NON-PROPRIETORS IN ABADI DEH ACT, 1995

It defines key terms such as 'abadi deh', 'non-proprietor', and administrative officers like the Collector and Commissioner. The Act establishes a mechanism for resolving disputes through the Collector and allows appeals to higher authorities within a 90-day limit. Finally, it repeals Ordinance XV of 1994 which had previously addressed similar issues.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Office of the Ombudsman in the Province of Punjab to protect people's rights and ensure adherence to the rule of law. It defines key terms such as 'maladministration' and 'Agency', outlines the appointment, tenure, and removal procedures for the Ombudsman, and grants powers to make rules. The Ordinance applies immediately upon promulgation and extends throughout the Province of Punjab.

It specifically modifies Section 30 (Section 3) of the parent Act to include this new power. The legislation also repeals the Punjab Health Foundation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1994.

metadata.summary: The Punjab Finance Act, 1995 was enacted to levy and enhance rates of certain taxes, duties, and fees within the province of Punjab. It amends the Stamp Act, 1899 by substituting specific fee amounts for various documents, including bonds, bills of exchange, and articles of association. Additionally, the Act establishes new tax rates for companies, factory owners, commercial establishments, importers/exporters, contractors, and professionals based on their capital or transaction values.

name: PUNJAB PROHIBITION OF EXPRESSING MATTERS ON WALLS ACT, 1995

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Prohibition of Expressing Matters on Walls Act, 1995
metadata.long_title: An Act to prohibit expression of matters on walls in the Punjab.

metadata.one_line: Prohibits affixing posters or writing on walls in Punjab and mandates removal of existing expressions.
metadata.summary: This Act prohibits the expression of matters on walls within the Province of Punjab to prevent public nuisance. It applies to anyone who affixes advertisements or writes on walls with the intention of attracting public attention, punishable by imprisonment up to six months or a fine of Rs.5,000. The Act allows exceptions for owners expressing particulars about themselves or their business and requires Local Councils to remove existing prohibited expressions within thirty days.

metadata.summary: This Act revises the salaries and other emoluments of holders of representative offices relating to the Punjab. It amends two existing Acts from 1974 and 1975 to update specific monetary figures, travel classes, and allowances for members and ministers. The Act also grants new entitlements such as first-class air travel abroad and a sumptuary allowance.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to further regulate local government in the Province of Punjab. It establishes District Assemblies comprising various council chairmen and government department heads to coordinate activities and settle disputes. The text also alters population thresholds for different types of councils and adds provisions regarding panchayats and liability for loss.

metadata.short_title: Civil Defence (Amendment) Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Civil Defence Act, 1952

metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Civil Defence Act, 1952 by substituting clause (1) of section 1A. It defines civil defence as measures affording defence against hostile attacks by foreign powers or depriving such attacks of their effect, whether taken before, during, or after the attack. The definition also includes remedial measures taken during calamities or disasters in peace time.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Agricultural Produce Markets (Amendment) Act, 1994

amends: The Punjab Agricultural Produce Markets Ordinance, 1978

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Agricultural Produce Markets Ordinance, 1978 to provide for the dissolution of Market Committees when general elections are announced. It mandates that upon such dissolution, all powers and functions of the committees cease, and their assets vest in the Government while liabilities are assumed by it. The Act also repeals the Punjab Agricultural Produce Markets (Amendment) Ordinance, 1994.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Bait-ul-Mal (Amendment) Act, 1994

metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Punjab Bait-ul-Mal Act, 1991 to establish a Bait-ul-Mal Council with specific powers and composition. It defines the roles of the Ameen and non-official members, setting terms of office and eligibility criteria for social workers and eminent individuals in education or health. The Act also amends provisions regarding District Bait-ul-Mal Committees and repeals a previous 1994 Amendment Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Compulsory Primary Education Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for compulsory primary education in the Province of the Punjab.
repeals: The Punjab Primary Education Ordinance, 1962 (XXIX of 1962)
metadata.max_penalty: fine up to five hundred rupees and imprisonment up to one month for parents; fine up to two hundred rupees and imprisonment up to one week for employers
metadata.one_line: This Act mandates compulsory primary education in Punjab and establishes authorities to enforce attendance.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Compulsory Primary Education Act, 1994 was enacted to provide for compulsory primary education within the Province of the Punjab. It defines key terms such as 'child', 'parent', and 'primary education school', and mandates that parents ensure their children attend a primary school until they complete the course, barring reasonable excuses like illness or lack of nearby schools. The Act empowers School Attendance Authorities to enforce compliance and imposes penalties on parents or employers who fail to ensure attendance without valid cause. It also repeals the earlier Punjab Primary Education Ordinance, 1962.

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the University of Arid Agriculture at Rawalpindi to bridge knowledge gaps between arid and irrigated areas. It creates a body corporate with perpetual succession, comprising a Chancellor, Pro-Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Syndicate, and Academic Council. The legislation outlines the university's powers to conduct research, award degrees, and manage property, while also repealing the previous 1994 Ordinance.

The legislation also introduces a new annual tax on video cassette traders categorized by business scale and specifies penalties for non-compliance.

The Act substitutes sections related to the Board's composition, meeting procedures, executive committee formation, and tenure of members. It also repeals a previous ordinance (IV of 1994) that had amended the 1970 Ordinance.

It inserts a proviso into Section 22 allowing an aggrieved person to make a complaint to the court of competent jurisdiction if the Collector or Cane Commissioner fails to decide on prosecution within sixty days. The Act came into force immediately upon its publication.

metadata.one_line: Amends the Weights and Measures (International System) Act, 1967 by defining weighing instruments.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Weights and Measures (International System) Act, 1967. It substitutes a new definition for 'weighing instrument' in section 2 of the parent Act. The amendment includes scales, beams, balances, spring balances, steelyards, electronic machines, and other weighing machines within this definition.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Family Courts (Amendment) Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the West Pakistan Family Courts Act, 1964
amends: The West Pakistan Family Courts Act, 1964
metadata.one_line: Amends the West Pakistan Family Courts Act, 1964 regarding court establishment and judge appointments.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the West Pakistan Family Courts Act, 1964 to facilitate the establishment of Family Courts in each district. It mandates the appointment of at least one woman Judge per district within six months and allows for flexible sitting arrangements across districts. The Act also updates qualifications for appointments and increases specific fee amounts mentioned in the original legislation.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Agricultural Income Tax Ordinance, 1993
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the imposition of a tax on agricultural income in the Punjab.
metadata.max_penalty: ten times the amount of tax avoided or recovered from a tenant
metadata.one_line: Imposes an annual tax on agricultural income from land in Punjab based on produce index units.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance imposes a tax on agricultural income accruing from land situated in the Punjab. It defines 'agricultural income' to include rent, revenue, and income from orchards or buildings connected to such land. The tax is assessed annually at rates specified in the Schedule based on produce index units, with specific provisions for orchards in Faisalabad and Toba Tek Singh districts. The Ordinance also establishes penalties for false statements regarding land holdings and prohibits landlords from recovering this tax from tenants.

metadata.short_title: Punjab Agricultural Produce Markets (Amendment) Ordinance, 1993
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Agricultural Produce Markets Ordinance, 1978
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1978 Ordinance to allow dissolution of Market Committees during election periods.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Agricultural Produce Markets Ordinance, 1978 to address political neutrality in market committees. It grants the Government power to dissolve Market Committees if a general election is announced and it is deemed necessary to prevent misuse of funds or influence for political purposes. Upon dissolution, members cease their roles, powers are transferred to appointed Administrators, and assets vest in the Government until new committees are constituted after the election.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Bait-ul-Mal (Amendment) Ordinance, 1993
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Bait-ul-Mal Act, 1991
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Bait-ul-Mal Act, 1991
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Bait-ul-Mal Act, 1991 to establish a Council and define its composition.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Bait-ul-Mal Act, 1991 to substitute Section 2 regarding the establishment of the Punjab Bait-ul-Mal Council. It defines the Council as a body corporate consisting of an Ameen and up to fourteen members, including non-official members who are social workers or experts. The Ordinance also adds provisions to Section 5 concerning the qualifications for members of District Bait-ul-Mal Committees.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Public Service Commission (Amendment) Ordinance, 1993
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Punjab Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1978
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1978
amends: The Punjab Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1978
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1978 regarding composition, tenure, and appointment procedures.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1978 to alter the composition and tenure of the Commission. It substitutes provisions regarding the number of members, their appointment by the Governor, and extends the term of office to seven years or until age sixty-three. The Ordinance also modifies section 4 regarding tenure and adds new clauses to section 7 concerning advisory roles for specific recruitment cases.

name: RULES OF PROCEDURE OF THE PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLY OF THE PUNJAB (AMENDMENT) 1993

The amendment was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab under Article 67 read with Article 127 of the Constitution on October 16, 1993.

metadata.short_title: The Antiquities (Amendment) Act, 1992

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Antiquities Act, 1975 to update terminology from 'Director' to 'Director-General'. It defines 'ancient' as existing for at least seventy-five years and vests ownership of all buried antiquities in the Federal Government. The Act also establishes an Advisory Committee comprising members from the Senate and National Assembly to determine cash rewards for handing over antiquities.

name: UNIVERSITY OF ENGINEERING AND TECHNOLOGY, TAXILA ACT, 1994

metadata.short_title: The University of Engineering and Technology, Taxila, Act, 1994

repeals: University of Engineering and Technology, Lahore Act, 1974
establishes: University of Engineering and Technology, Taxila

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the University of Engineering and Technology at Taxila with a main campus there and potential sub-campuses. It defines the university's corporate status, powers to confer degrees, and internal bodies including the Chancellor, Syndicate, and various committees. The Act also incorporates existing assets and personnel from the Lahore campus and provides for the amendment or repeal of its own statutes and regulations.

metadata.short_title: the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for abolition of bonded labour system
metadata.one_line: Abolishes the bonded labour system in Pakistan and extinguishes all bonded debts.
metadata.summary: This Act abolishes the bonded labour system throughout Pakistan to prevent economic and physical exploitation of the labour class. It declares all customs, contracts, and agreements related to bonded labour void and extinguishes any obligation to repay bonded debt or render bonded labour. The Act empowers Magistrates of the first class to try offences under it and ensures that no civil court can recover bonded debts after its commencement.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Act, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Act to continue and revise certain taxes and fees in the Punjab.
metadata.one_line: Continues and revises taxes and fees in Punjab, amending stamp, entertainment, and finance acts.
metadata.summary: This Act continues and revises certain taxes and fees applicable in the Province of Punjab. It amends the Stamp Act, 1899 regarding property transfer duties and the Punjab Entertainments Duty Act, 1958 concerning admission charges for various events. Additionally, it updates fee structures for driving licences and tests under the Punjab Finance Act, 1973.

metadata.short_title: The Protection of Economic Reforms Act, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for furtherance and protection of economic reforms
metadata.one_line: Provides legal protection for economic reforms, foreign currency freedom, and fiscal incentives across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act creates a liberal environment for savings and investments by providing legal protection to various economic reforms introduced since November 1970. It grants citizens the freedom to hold and transfer foreign currency without declaration or tax implications while ensuring banking secrecy. The legislation also protects fiscal incentives for investors, prevents compulsory acquisition of private enterprises, and ensures financial obligations remain in force.

metadata.short_title: The Bank of Punjab (Amendment) Act, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Bank of Punjab Act, 1989.
repeals: The Bank of Punjab (Amendment) Ordinance, 1992

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Bank of Punjab Act, 1989 to update figures related to ordinary shares and dividend percentages. It substitutes specific monetary values in Section 4 and changes a percentage figure in Section 7 of the parent Act. The legislation also repeals the earlier Bank of Punjab (Amendment) Ordinance, 1992.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Health Foundation Act, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Health Foundation.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
repeals: The Punjab Health Foundation Ordinance, 1992 (XXXV of 1992)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Health Foundation to promote and finance health sector development in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Health Foundation as a body corporate with perpetual succession to promote and finance the development of the health sector in the Province of Punjab. The Foundation is managed by a Board of Directors appointed by the Government, headed by a Managing Director who serves as the Chief Executive. Its functions include establishing health institutions, providing grants and loans to health facilities and doctors, and managing a dedicated Health Foundation Fund sourced from government grants, donations, and investments.

It defines specific categories of persons entitled to pre-emption rights, such as co-owners (Shafi Sharik) and those with special rights like irrigation or passage (Shafi Khalit). The Act outlines procedures for exercising these rights, priorities among multiple claimants, and provisions regarding the withdrawal of claims or revocation of sales.

It alters provisions concerning promotion, seniority calculation, and specific wording in sections 7, 8, 10, 11, 11-A, 16, and 21 of the parent Act. The Ordinance came into force immediately upon promulgation by the Governor of Punjab on July 22, 1984.

It also adds a proviso to Section 38 requiring an opportunity of being heard before taking action under that section. The Ordinance applies to the Province of Punjab and comes into force immediately upon promulgation by the Governor.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Educational and Training Institutions Ordinance, 1960. It specifically alters Section 4 to require that the Board consist of not less than nine members appointed by the Governor of the Punjab. The document was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab on July 31, 1984, and came into force immediately.

It specifically adds provisos to Section 16 regarding tax levies on such transactions and defines terms like 'banking company' and 'customer' in this context. The Ordinance also includes provisions for exemptions in cases of customer default and establishes a presumption regarding certificates issued by the banking company.

name: PUNJAB HOUSING FACILITIES FOR NON-PROPRIETIES IN RURAL AREAS (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1984

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Housing Facilities for Non-Proprietors in Rural Areas (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Housing Facilities for Non-Proprietors in Rural Areas Act, 1975 (V of 1975).

subjects: Punjab Housing Facilities for Non-Proprietors in Rural Areas Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1975 Act to require an opportunity of being heard in appeals under Section 7.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Housing Facilities for Non-Proprietors in Rural Areas Act, 1975. It adds a proviso to Section 7 requiring that no order in any appeal be passed without providing the affected person an opportunity of being heard. The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab on December 17, 1984, and came into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Preamble, Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 1979
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1979 Ordinance to empower urban local councils to inspect buildings and order demolition for violations.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 1979, specifically regarding building inspections. It empowers urban local councils to inspect any building constructed in violation of provisions or bye-laws. The text grants councils the authority to require alterations or order the demolition of non-compliant buildings, and allows for the imposition of fees on owners upon application.

name: PUNJAB MINERALS (CANCELLATION OF SAND LEASES IN RESTRICTED AREAS ORDINANCE, 1984

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Minerals (Cancellation of Sand Leases in Restricted Areas) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for cancellation of sand leases in certain areas of the Province of Punjab.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance empowers the Government of Punjab to cancel sand leases in restricted areas within the province.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the cancellation of sand leases in specific restricted areas of the Province of Punjab. It defines 'restricted areas' to include zones along the river Ravi, flood bunds, defence installations, and other public or historical works. The Government is authorized to cancel any such lease by notification without legal challenge.

name: PUNJAB MINISTERS (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1984

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Ministers Salaries (Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Ministers Salaries (Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975. It specifically targets Section 7 of the parent Act to correct a typographical error by substituting the word 'cars' for 'cars'. The amendment comes into force immediately upon promulgation by the Governor of the Punjab on October 24, 1984.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Youthful Offenders (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Youthful Offenders Ordinance, 1983.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Youthful Offenders Ordinance, 1983 to extend age limits and require a hearing before punishment.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Youthful Offenders Ordinance, 1983. It extends the upper age limit for youthful offenders from fifteen to sixteen years. Additionally, it requires that an opportunity of being heard be afforded before imposing certain punishments in the Punjab Seed Corporation Act, 1876. The Ordinance came into force immediately upon promulgation by the Governor of the Punjab.

name: PUNJAB PRIVATE EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS (PROMOTION AND REGULATION) ORDINANCE, 1984

metadata.one_line: This Ordinance promotes and regulates private educational institutions in Punjab through registration and rules.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the promotion and regulation of private educational institutions within the Province of Punjab. It defines key terms such as 'School', 'College', and 'Institution' and establishes a Registering Authority to oversee operations. The law mandates registration, outlines conditions for cancellation, sets penalties for unregistered operation, and empowers the Government to make necessary rules.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Reformatory Schools Act, 1897 to modify Section 17. Specifically, it replaces a comma after the word 'persons' with a full-stop and omits the phrase requiring at least two citizens of Pakistan. The amendment comes into force immediately upon promulgation by the Governor of Punjab on December 17, 1984.

metadata.short_title: The Stamp (Punjab Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to further amend the Stamp Act, 1899

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Stamp Act, 1899 applicable in the Province of the Punjab. It substitutes specific terms regarding debentures and adds a new definition for 'Participation Term Certificate'. Additionally, it modifies the exemption clause to cover certificates issued by companies or bodies corporate in terms of registered mortgage deeds.

metadata.short_title: University of Agriculture, Faisalabad (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend University of Agriculture Faisalabad Act, 1973.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the University of Agriculture Faisalabad Act, 1973. It was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab on September 20, 1984. The document comes into force at once and serves to update the existing university legislation.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the University of Engineering and Technology Act, 1974 by adding specific provisos to Sections 37 and 41. The amendments ensure that no order is passed under these sections without affording an opportunity of being heard to the affected institution or person. It was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab on December 17, 1984, in pursuance of the Provisional Constitution Order.

metadata.short_title: Zakat and Ushr (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Zakat and Ushr Ordinance, 1980

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Zakat and Ushr Ordinance, 1980 to prohibit the compulsory collection of Zakat on specific assets held in foreign currency. It modifies Section 3 and omits exclusions for foreign currency accounts from the First Schedule. The Ordinance was promulgated by the President under emergency powers due to immediate circumstances.

metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Bahauddin Zakariya University Act, 1975.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Bahauddin Zakariya University Act, 1975 to alter the territorial jurisdiction of the university. It substitutes references to 'Multan Division' with 'Multan and D.G. Khan Divisions and, till such time as may be notified by Government, the Okara district of Lahore Division'. The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab on June 25, 1983, and is deemed to have come into force from July 1, 1982.

name: COLONIZATION OF GOVERNMENT LANDS (PUNJAB) ACT (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1983

metadata.short_title: The Colonization of Government Lands (Punjab) Act (Amendment) Ordinance, 1983

metadata.max_penalty: five thousand rupees or with rigorous imprisonment not exceeding six months or with both
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1912 Colonization Act by increasing fees and penalties for unauthorized occupation of government land.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Colonization of Government Lands (Punjab) Act, 1912 to update financial penalties associated with land colonization. It substitutes a fee of one hundred rupees with five thousand rupees in section 24 and increases the penalty for offenses under section 33 to five thousand rupees or imprisonment up to six months. The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab on January 18, 1983, and came into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: The Constitution (Third Amendment) Order, 1983
metadata.long_title: An Order to amend Article 203F of the Constitution.
metadata.administering_body: Ministry of Law and Parliamentary Affairs
metadata.one_line: Amends Article 203F of the Constitution to extend appeal time limits.
metadata.summary: This Order amends Article 203F of the Constitution of Pakistan. It substitutes a colon with specific wording regarding appeals within six months of a decision. The amendment was promulgated by the President on July 28, 1983, in pursuance of the Proclamation of Martial Law.

name: PUNJAB (WILDLIFE PROTECTION, PRESERVATION, CONSERVATION AND MANAGEMENT) (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1983

metadata.short_title: The Punjab (Wildlife Protection, Preservation, Conservation and Management) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1983
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Punjab Wildlife (Protection, Preservation, Conservation and Management) Act, 1974.

amends: The Punjab Wildlife (Protection, Preservation, Conservation and Management) Act, 1974
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years or with fine ten thousand rupees or with both subject to minimum imprisonment for a period of two years and fine of five thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1974 Punjab Wildlife Act regarding board functions, hunting limits, and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Wildlife (Protection, Preservation, Conservation and Management) Act, 1974 to update provisions on the Board's advisory functions. It modifies restrictions on hunting occasions and significantly increases penalties for contraventions of specific sections. The changes include stricter minimum imprisonment terms and higher fines for offenses related to wildlife protection.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Court Fees (Abolition) Ordinance, 1983
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the abolition of court fee in respect of certain cases.
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on and from the first of August, 1978
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab, Law Department
metadata.one_line: Abolishes court fees for criminal cases and civil cases where relief does not exceed twenty-five thousand rupees.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance abolishes court fees for specific types of legal proceedings within the Punjab. It applies to all criminal cases and civil cases where the value of the relief claimed does not exceed twenty-five thousand rupees. The abolition covers all courts, including revenue courts, and is deemed effective from August 1, 1978.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Land Revenue (Amendment) Ordinance, 1983
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967.
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab, Law Department
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967 to increase revenue for owners exceeding specific land area limits.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967 to adjust land revenue calculations based on land ownership areas. It substitutes Section 56-A of the parent Act to specify increased revenue percentages for owners of irrigated or unirrigated land exceeding certain acreage thresholds. The provisions apply specifically to the Province of the Punjab and came into force immediately upon promulgation.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Land Utilization Authority (Amendment) Ordinance, 1983
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Land Utilization Authority Ordinance, 1981.
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Land Utilization Authority Ordinance, 1981
amends: The Punjab Land Utilization Authority Ordinance, 1981
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1981 Ordinance to add credit facilities for developing culturable waste land in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Land Utilization Authority Ordinance, 1981 to motivate land owners to develop their culturable waste land. It introduces provisions for granting credit facilities and loans specifically for improving such land, including irrigation works and flood protection. The text also details methods for recovering these loans from borrowers or sureties.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Small Industries Corporation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1983
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Punjab Small Industries Corporation Act, 1973.
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Small Industries Corporation Act, 1973
amends: The Punjab Small Industries Corporation Act, 1973
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Small Industries Corporation Act, 1973 to redefine 'Small handicraft Industry' regarding asset limits.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Small Industries Corporation Act, 1973 by substituting the definition of 'Small handicraft Industry' in Section 2. The amendment specifies that such an industry must be engaged in manufacturing producer or consumer goods where total assets (excluding land and buildings) do not exceed fifty lacs of rupees. It was promulgated by the Governor of Punjab on April 13, 1983, and came into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: The Universities Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1983
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the laws relating to certain Universities in the Punjab.
amends: The University of Agriculture Faisalabad Act, 1973
The University of Engineering and Technology Lahore Act, 1974
The Din Muhammad Zakariya Baha-ud-University Act, 1975
The Islamia University of Bahawalpur Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance amends four specific University Acts in Punjab to grant Chancellors revisional powers.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab on April 28, 1983, to amend laws relating to specific universities within the province. It inserts new sections into four existing Acts (University of Agriculture Faisalabad, University of Engineering and Technology Lahore, Din Muhammad Zakariya Baha-ud-University, and Islamia University of Bahawalpur). The amendments grant Chancellors revisional powers allowing them to call for and examine records of proceedings passed by any authority to ensure correctness, legality, or propriety. The Ordinance came into force immediately upon promulgation.

name: WEST PAKISTAN MUSLIM PERSONAL LAW (SHARIAT) ACT (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1983

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Act (Amendment Ordinance), 1983
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the West Pakistan Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Act, 1962.
amends: The West Pakistan Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Act, 1962
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab, Law Department
metadata.one_line: Amends the West Pakistan Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Act, 1962 regarding succession and agricultural land customs.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the West Pakistan Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Act, 1962 to address issues concerning succession and agricultural land. It inserts a new section 2-A that validates decrees based on custom or usage acquired prior to Act IX of 1948. The amendment ensures that such customs are not voided by the Muslim Personal Law if they were applicable before the Act came into force. It also provides for the abatement of pending suits related to these specific land transactions.

metadata.short_title: The Constitution (Amendment) Order, 1982
metadata.long_title: An Order to amend clause (1) of Article 181 of the Constitution by adding an explanation that a Judge of a High Court includes a person who has retired as a Judge of a High Court.
amends: The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan
key_definitions: Judge of a High Court (includes a person who has retired as a Judge of a High Court)
metadata.administering_body: Ministry of Law and Parliamentary Affairs
metadata.one_line: Amends the Constitution to include retired High Court judges within the definition of 'Judge of a High Court'.
metadata.summary: This Order amends clause (1) of Article 181 of the Constitution of Pakistan. It adds an explanation stating that the term 'Judge of a High Court' includes a person who has retired from that position. The amendment was promulgated by the President on February 28, 1982, and came into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: The Constitution (Fourth Amendment) Order, 1982
metadata.long_title: An order to amend Article 228 of the Constitution by substituting clause (4) regarding the appointment of the Chairman of the Islamic Council.
metadata.administering_body: Ministry of Law and Parliamentary Affairs
metadata.one_line: Amends the Constitution to require the President to appoint an Islamic Council member as Chairman.
metadata.summary: This Order amends Article 228 of the Constitution of Pakistan. It substitutes clause (4) to mandate that the President appoint one member of the Islamic Council as its Chairman. The Order was promulgated by the President on September 22, 1982, and came into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: The Constitution (Second Amendment) Order, 1982
metadata.long_title: An Order to amend Articles 203B, 203C, 203D, 203DD, 203F and to insert Article 203GG in the Constitution.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Constitution to define judicial terms and expand Supreme Court jurisdiction over Federal Shariat Court matters.
metadata.summary: This Order amends specific articles of the Constitution to redefine terms like 'Chief Justice' and 'Judge' within the context of the Federal Shariat Court. It grants the Supreme Court enhanced appellate jurisdiction over judgments involving death sentences or long imprisonment by the Federal Shariat Court. Additionally, it establishes that decisions of the Federal Shariat Court are binding on High Courts and subordinate courts.

metadata.short_title: The Constitution (Third Amendment) Order, 1982
metadata.long_title: An Order to amend Article 203F of the Constitution by constituting a Shariat Appellate Bench in the Supreme Court.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Constitution to establish a Shariat Appellate Bench in the Supreme Court consisting of Muslim Judges and Ulema.
metadata.summary: This Order amends Article 203F of the Constitution to constitute a Shariat Appellate Bench within the Supreme Court. The Bench is composed of three Muslim Judges and up to two Ulema appointed by the President as ad hoc members. It grants these Ulema the same powers, jurisdiction, and privileges as Supreme Court Judges while attending sittings.

metadata.short_title: The Land Reforms Regulation (Punjab Amendment) Ordinance, 1982
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to further amend the Land Reforms Regulation, 1972.
metadata.commencement: at once; sections 3, 4 and 5 deemed to have taken effect from 1978-03-15
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab, Law Department
metadata.one_line: Amends the Land Reforms Regulation, 1972 regarding tenancy, land alienation, and pre-emption rights in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Land Reforms Regulation, 1972 to address legal changes necessitated by the revocation of emergency provisions. It updates definitions of 'tenant' and modifies rules concerning the partition of jointly owned holdings and the alienation of land. The text also revises procedures for enforcing pre-emption rights and appeals before the Collector or Commissioner.

metadata.short_title: The Motion Pictures (Amendment) Ordinance, 1982
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Motion Pictures Ordinance, 1979
metadata.max_penalty: punishment provided in sub-section (2) of section 18 of the Motion Pictures Ordinance, 1979
metadata.one_line: Amends the Motion Pictures Ordinance, 1979 regarding admission charges and penalties for excess fees.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Motion Pictures Ordinance, 1979 to clarify provisions related to admission charges for film exhibitions. It adds specific wording to Section 13 regarding maximum charges and inserts a new subsection into Section 18. The amendment creates an offence for charging amounts in excess of fixed limits or selling tickets at higher costs, punishable under existing sections.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab to repeal the Punjab Administrative Vigilance Commission Ordinance, 1979. It applies to all posts within the Commission and its vigilance committees, terminating existing appointments and extinguishing associated rights and privileges. The document also empowers the Government to make necessary orders if difficulties arise in giving effect to the repeal.

metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Allama Iqbal Open University Act, 1974.

It restructures the Executive Council by adding new members and changing the number of specific representatives. The text also inserts provisions for transferring officers between government bodies and universities, and modifies statutes regarding faculty appointments.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the University of the Punjab Act, 1973 to update provisions on faculty attendance, Syndicate composition, and appointment procedures. It introduces new clauses regarding employee absence and modifies requirements for selecting Professors, Deans, and Department Chairs. Additionally, it facilitates transfers between government institutions and universities while ensuring consultation with relevant boards.

metadata.short_title: Arbitration (Amendment) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: AN ORDINANCE further to amend the Arbitration Act, 1940
metadata.parent_law: Arbitration Act, 1940
metadata.one_line: Amends the Arbitration Act, 1940 to require arbitrators to state reasons for awards in sufficient detail.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Arbitration Act, 1940 by inserting a new section 26A. The amendment mandates that arbitrators or umpires must state reasons for their awards in sufficient detail to enable courts to consider questions of law. If an award lacks sufficient reasons, the court may remit it to the arbitrator with a time limit to submit the corrected award; failure to comply renders the award void.

metadata.short_title: Banking Companies (Amendment) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962
metadata.parent_law: Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962
metadata.one_line: Amends the Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962 regarding loan amounts in section 22.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962 by adding specific text to the explanation of section 22. The amendment clarifies the inclusion of foreign currency loans obtained from the Federal Government or foreign agencies, as well as other rupee loans taken from the Federal Government. It was promulgated by the President on May 11, 1981, and came into force immediately.

name: CENSUS ORDINANCE, 1959 (APPLICATION TO TRIBAL AREAS) REGULATION, 1981

metadata.short_title: The Census Ordinance, 1959 (Application to Tribal Areas) Regulation, 1981

metadata.parent_law: Census Ordinance, 1959 (X of 1959)

metadata.summary: This Federal Regulation was made by the President in exercise of powers under the Proclamation of Martial Law Order No. I of 1977. It extends to the whole of the Tribal Areas and applies the provisions of the Census Ordinance, 1959 (X of 1959) to that region. The Regulation came into force immediately upon publication.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance validates certain orders passed by the Chairman or a Member of the Federal Land Commission prior to its commencement. It applies to orders made under specific regulations concerning the devolution and distribution of property in Dir, Swat, and Chitral. The validation is deemed to have always had effect, notwithstanding any contrary court order or decision.

metadata.short_title: The Qanun-e-Shahadat, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Order to revise, amend and consolidate the law of evidence as to bring it in conformity with injunctions of Islam as laid down in the Holy Quran and Sunnah.

metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends the law of evidence in Pakistan to align with Islamic injunctions.
metadata.summary: This Order consolidates and revises the law of evidence in Pakistan to bring it into conformity with the Holy Quran and Sunnah. It applies to all judicial proceedings, including those before arbitrators, throughout the whole of Pakistan. The text defines key terms such as 'fact', 'document', and 'evidence', establishes rules for witness competency, and outlines provisions regarding the relevancy of facts and presumptions.

Specifically, it substitutes clause (2) of Article 203C to limit the number of Muslim members appointed by the President and omits Article 203CC entirely. The Order was promulgated by the President on May 27, 1981, pursuant to the Laws (Continuance in Force) Order, 1977, and came into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: The Constitution (Second Amendment) Order, 1981
metadata.administering_body: Ministry of Law and Parliamentary Affairs

metadata.summary: This Order amends Article 203C of the Constitution to limit the number of Muslim members in the Supreme Court. It also omits Article 203CC from the Constitution. The Order was promulgated by the President on May 27, 1981, and came into force immediately.

metadata.administering_body: Ministry of Law and Parliamentary Affairs
metadata.one_line: Amends Article 259 of the Constitution regarding academic distinction in sports or nursing.
metadata.summary: This Order was made by the President under the Proclamation of 1977 (Continuance of Martial Law). It amends Article 259 of the Constitution to substitute specific words related to academic distinction. The amendment clarifies that such distinctions apply generally, in the field of sports, or in nursing.

metadata.short_title: The Ehteram-e-Ramazan Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for measures to observe the sanctity of the month of Ramazan
metadata.max_penalty: six months imprisonment or fine of one thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance prohibits eating, drinking, and smoking in public places during Ramazan fasting hours.
metadata.summary: The Ehteram-e-Ramazan Ordinance, 1981 was promulgated by the President to ensure the sanctity of the month of Ramazan. It prohibits persons obligated to fast from eating, drinking, or smoking in public places and restricts the serving of eatables in hotels and restaurants during fasting hours. The law also mandates the closure of cinema houses and theatres from sunset until three hours thereafter. Offences under this Ordinance are punishable by imprisonment up to six months for cinema violations or three months for eating violations, along with fines.

valid licence (subject to payment of security and fee)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Emigration Ordinance, 1979 by deeming certain 1922 licences valid under new rules.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Emigration Ordinance, 1979 to address licensing and fee requirements. It stipulates that a licence issued under the Emigration Act, 1922 is deemed issued under this Ordinance but is only valid if specific security and fees are paid. The law comes into force immediately and is deemed effective from March 23, 1979.

metadata.short_title: The Disabled Persons (Employment and Rehabilitation) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the employment, rehabilitation and welfare of disabled persons and for matters connected therewith.
metadata.commencement: on such day as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
establishes: National Council for Rehabilitation of Disabled Persons
Provincial Councils for Rehabilitation of Disabled Persons
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to one thousand rupees and, in the case of non-payment of fine, with an additional fine which may extend to ten rupees for every day during which the payment of fine is not made
metadata.administering_body: National Council (in consultation with the Federal Government)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance establishes councils and a fund to provide employment, rehabilitation, and welfare for disabled persons in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Disabled Persons (Employment and Rehabilitation) Ordinance, 1981 was promulgated by the President to facilitate the employment, rehabilitation, and welfare of disabled persons throughout Pakistan. It establishes a National Council at the federal level and Provincial Councils at the provincial level to formulate policy, coordinate execution, and oversee training and medical assistance. The Ordinance creates a Rehabilitation Fund to finance training centers, provide financial aid, disburse scholarships, and supply artificial limbs or surgical therapy. It also defines key terms such as 'disabled person' and 'establishment', and prescribes penalties for establishments failing to contribute to the Fund.

metadata.short_title: Employees' Cost of Living (Relief) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Employees' Cost of Living (Relief) Act, 1973
metadata.parent_law: Employees' Cost of Living (Relief) Act, 1973
metadata.one_line: Amends the Employees' Cost of Living (Relief) Act, 1973 to add a new sub-section regarding cost of living allowances.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Employees' Cost of Living (Relief) Act, 1973 by adding a new sub-section to Section 3. It mandates that employees whose wages exceed Rs. 100 per month must receive a cost of living allowance or equal piece-work allowance. The provision ensures relief against rises in the cost of living under existing agreements, settlements, or awards effective from July 1, 1981. It clarifies that such allowances are not deemed as increments for promotion purposes but specifically for relief due to price rises.

metadata.short_title: The Federal and Provincial Cabinets (Amendment) Order, 1981
metadata.parent_law: The Laws (Continuance in Force) Order, 1977
amends: The Federal and Provincial Cabinets Order, 1981
metadata.administering_body: Ministry of Law and Parliamentary Affairs
metadata.one_line: Amends the Federal and Provincial Cabinets Order, 1981 to protect service posts for appointed ministers.
metadata.summary: This Order amends the Federal and Provincial Cabinets Order, 1981 by inserting a new Article 10A. It ensures that persons in the service of Pakistan who are appointed as Federal or Provincial Ministers continue to hold their posts without disadvantageous changes to terms. Additionally, it allows the President or Governor to permit individuals holding other offices to continue holding them upon appointment as Ministers.

metadata.short_title: The Federal and Provincial Cabinets Order, 1981
amends: Federal Minister's Oath of Office Order, 1978 (P. O. No. 9 of 1978)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the structure and tenure for Federal and Provincial Cabinets and repeals a previous Oath Order.
metadata.summary: This Order establishes the composition of the Federal Cabinet and Provincial Cabinets, defining the roles of Federal Ministers, Ministers of State, and Provincial Ministers. It stipulates that these officials must be at least twenty-five years old and hold office during the pleasure of the President or Governor respectively. The document also prescribes the specific Oath of Office to be taken by these ministers and repeals the Federal Minister's Oath of Office Order, 1978.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Federal Employees Benevolent Fund and Group Insurance Act, 1969 to update the Second Schedule. metadata.short_title: Federal Public Service Commission (Amendment) Ordinance, 1981

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Federal Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1977. The amendments are deemed to have always been in force as of the date of the original Ordinance.

It also revises sections concerning imprisonment terms and substitutes lists of Frontier Corps units in the First Schedule. The Ordinance was promulgated by the President under Martial Law powers to take immediate action.

metadata.short_title: The High Court Judges (Travelling Allowance) (Amendment) Order, 1981

It substitutes specific kilogram values for maunds, kilometres for miles, and kilograms for pounds within the original text. Additionally, it updates currency rates from paisa per maund per mile to paisa per kilometre per kilogram.

name: HOLDERS OF REPRESENTATIVE OFFICES (PUNISHMENT FOR MISCONDUCT) (AMENDMENT) ORDER, 1981

metadata.summary: This Order amends the Holders of Representative Offices (Punishment for Misconduct) Order, 1977. It adds a clause stating that rules or orders made without the required sanction are deemed valid if issued by the competent authority. The amendment applies to the Federal Government and was promulgated under the powers of the President during the Martial Law era.

name: INDUSTRIAL DEVELOPMENT BANK OF PAKISTAN (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1981

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Industrial Development Bank of Pakistan Ordinance, 1961 to update definitions of credit facilities and shareholding structures. It modifies provisions related to board composition, security for loans, and limitation periods for legal actions. The changes also adjust references to other banking ordinances and clarify the roles of federal and provincial governments in bank operations.

It establishes a new hierarchy for gift-tax authorities under the Central Board of Revenue and updates jurisdictional powers. The document also introduces new sections regarding penalties for obstruction, adjustments of refunds against tax, and specific rates for taxable gifts.

It also increases the applicable interest rate on payments from six percent to twelve percent per annum. The changes were promulgated by the President under Martial Law powers and came into force immediately.

name: OFFICE OF THE CHIEF MARTIAL LAW ADMINISTRATOR, PAKISTAN MARTIAL LAW ORDER

The amendments introduce specific offences including cheating of trust, forgery, criminal misappropriation, and breach of honesty in respect of documents. These changes are made to the existing text of the prior order effective immediately.

metadata.summary: This Martial Law Order directs the Federal Government to assume control and management of several provincial electricity supply companies. The takeover aims to renovate old distribution systems, address voltage drops and frequent breakdowns, and expand power supply for better consumer service. It supersedes previous arrangements under the Economic Reforms Order of 1972.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Pakistan Penal Code by inserting three new sections: 402A, 402B, and 402C. Section 402A defines hijacking as unlawfully seizing or exercising control over an aircraft by threats, force, or show of force. Sections 402B and 402C prescribe punishments for committing hijacking, conspiring to commit it, and harbouring hijackers respectively. The penalties include death, imprisonment for life, and fines.

It also modifies fee structures for services provided by the Registrar of Firms and adds provisions requiring firms with undesirable name components to alter their names within one month.

The document also provides for the dissolution of the existing research committee, transferring its assets, staff, and liabilities to the new Commission.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sales Tax Act, 1951 to modify section 3. It adds a proviso concerning the payment of tax on specified goods where the Board does not direct otherwise. The new provision ensures that such tax is payable in the same manner as excise duty would have been had rules been made under the said clause.

metadata.short_title: The State Bank of Pakistan (Amendment) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the State Bank of Pakistan Act, 1956

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the State Bank of Pakistan Act, 1956 to restrict court access to unpublished bank records. It substitutes specific time limits in sections 17 and 18 and adds a new section protecting banking reports from being treated as published evidence without Governor permission.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Land Utilization Authority Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of a Land Utilization Authority in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Punjab
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Land Utilization Authority to manage culturable waste land in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Punjab Land Utilization Authority within the Province of Punjab. The Authority is empowered to take control, survey, and prepare schemes for culturable temporarily waste land. It also sets up a Board comprising various government secretaries and officials to administer the Authority's functions.

metadata.short_title: The Baha-ud-Din Zakariya University (Amendment) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Baha-ud-Din Zakariya University Act, 1975.
metadata.parent_law: The Baha-ud-Din Zakariya University Act, 1975
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab, Education Department
metadata.one_line: Amends the Baha-ud-Din Zakariya University Act, 1975 regarding curriculum, governance, and staff appointments.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Baha-ud-Din Zakariya University Act, 1975 to introduce compulsory 'Islamic and Pakistan Studies' for Bachelor's degrees. It modifies the composition of the Syndicate by adding new members and appointing a Pro-Vice-Chancellor. The text also updates provisions regarding financial auditing, staff transfers to government posts, and the structure of teaching departments.

name: COMPANIES (MANAGING AGENCY AND ELECTION OF DIRECTORS) (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1980

metadata.short_title: Companies (Managing Agency and Election of Directors) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1980

amends: Companies (Managing Agency and Election of Directors) Order, 1972
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1972 Order regarding managing agencies and director elections to include federal undertakings.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Companies (Managing Agency and Election of Directors) Order, 1972. It modifies specific clauses within that Order and adds a new paragraph concerning agreements or contracts formed with Federal Government undertakings. The amendment aims to allow these entities to contribute to the economic development of Pakistan in collaboration with financial institutions.

metadata.short_title: The Constitution (Amendment) Order, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Order to amend Article 199 of the Constitution and to substitute Chapter 3A in Part VII of the Constitution relating to the Federal Shariat Court.
amends: The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Federal Shariat Court and amends the Constitution to grant it powers over laws repugnant to Islam.
metadata.summary: This Order establishes the Federal Shariat Court consisting of five members appointed by the President. It amends Article 199 of the Constitution to restrict judicial review regarding Martial Law orders and sentences passed by Military Courts. The Order also substitutes a new Chapter in Part VII of the Constitution defining the Court's jurisdiction, powers, and administrative arrangements.

metadata.short_title: The Constitution (Fourth Amendment) Order, 1980
metadata.parent_law: The Laws (Continuance in Force) Order, 1977
metadata.administering_body: Ministry of Law and Parliamentary Affairs
metadata.one_line: An Order amending Article 228 of the Constitution made by the President on November 30, 1980.
metadata.summary: This Order was made by the President in pursuance of a Proclamation dated July 5, 1977. It exercises powers enabling the President to amend the Constitution specifically regarding Article 228. The Order substitutes specific words within clause (2) of Article 228 of the Constitution. It came into force immediately upon publication.

name: PUNJAB CODE VOLUME-I PART-III OF IV

repeals: The Excise (Spirits) Act, 1863

The Excise Act, 1896
The Excise (Amendment) Act, 1906
key_definitions: situate within or adjacent to Siwalik mountain range
bona fide domestic or agricultural purposes
metadata.one_line: An Act to preserve land in the Punjab, regulate permits for grazing and cultivation, and repeal earlier excise acts.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the preservation of land within or adjacent to the Siwalik mountain range in the Province of the Punjab. It regulates the issuance of permits for grazing livestock, cultivating land, or erecting buildings on reserved areas. The Act also contains provisions regarding the collection of stamp duties and repeals several earlier Excise Acts.

metadata.short_title: The Constitution (Third Amendment) Order, 1980
metadata.parent_law: The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973 (via Proclamation of 1977)
amends: The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
metadata.administering_body: Ministry of Law and Parliamentary Affairs
metadata.one_line: Amends the Constitution to add an explanation regarding Muslim Sunnah sects in Article 227.
metadata.summary: This Order amends the Constitution by adding an explanation to Article 227 concerning the application of personal law. The amendment clarifies that 'Muslim Sunnah sect' means any sect as interpreted by the Quran and Sunnah. It was promulgated by the President on September 17, 1980, and came into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: The Constitution (Second Amendment) Order, 1980
metadata.administering_body: Ministry of Law and Parliamentary Affairs
metadata.one_line: Amends the Constitution regarding Supreme Court jurisdiction, judge resignation, and decision-making procedures.
metadata.summary: This Order amends Article 203C to insert a requirement that a member be a Muslim and adds a new clause allowing non-Supreme Court judges to resign by writing to the President. It omits Article 203D(4), inserts a new Article 203DD regarding court jurisdiction, and amends Articles 203E and 203J concerning court composition and decision-making processes.

metadata.short_title: The Election Commission (Reconstitution) Order, 1980
metadata.parent_law: The Proclamation of the 1977 fifth (CMLA day of Order July, No. 1977) with the Laws exercise (Continuance of all in powers Force) enabling Order
metadata.one_line: Reconstitutes the Election Commission by ceasing the incumbent and appointing a Supreme Court Judge as Acting Chief.
metadata.summary: This Order reconstitutes the Election Commission immediately upon its commencement. It mandates that any Chief Election Commissioner holding office at the time of this Order must cease to hold office. The President is authorized to appoint a Judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court to act as the Chief Election Commissioner once the office becomes vacant.

name: HIGH COURT JUDGES (OATH OF OFFICE) (AMENDMENT) ORDER, 1980

metadata.summary: This Order amends the High Court Judges (Oath of Office) Order, 1977. It directs that specific words be added to the Schedule of the 1977 Order after the phrase 'Allah Almighty'. The amendment is made in pursuance of the Proclamation of July 5, 1977 and under the powers of the Laws (Continuance in Force) Order, 1977. It comes into force immediately upon publication.

metadata.short_title: The Laws (Continuance in Force) (Eleventh Amendment) Order, 1980

metadata.summary: This Order was promulgated by the Chief Martial Law Administrator on August 11, 1980, under powers granted by a Proclamation of Martial Law. It amends the Laws (Continuance in Force) Order, 1977 by substituting the word 'seven' with 'eight' in Article 2, clause (I). The document serves to maintain legal continuity during martial law by updating specific terminology within existing orders.

metadata.short_title: Distribution of Property (Chitral) Order, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Order to provide for the distribution of properties in the former State of Chitral.
metadata.commencement: at once and shall be deemed to have taken effect on the fifteenth day of March, 1978

key_definitions: Provincial Government (Government of the North-West Frontier Province)
metadata.one_line: This Order distributes properties in former Chitral between State and private ownership, establishing review mechanisms and penalties for obstruction.
metadata.summary: This Order provides for the distribution of properties in the former State of Chitral. It determines which properties belong to the State and which are private property of the ex-Mehtar. The Order establishes procedures for reviewing decisions made by the Federal or Provincial Government, including time limits for applications and powers of appellate courts. It also defines offences related to obstructing orders and specifies that no court shall question actions taken under this Order.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Agricultural Produce Markets (Amendment) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Punjab Agricultural Produce Markets Ordinance, 1978

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Agricultural Produce Markets Ordinance, 1978 to update classifications for livestock and references to local government bodies. It specifically deletes certain livestock categories from a list and adds 'zila council' terminology where applicable. The changes apply to the whole of the Province of Punjab and come into force immediately upon promulgation by the Governor.

name: MONOPOLIES AND RESTRICTIVE TRADE PRACTICES (CONTROL AND PREVENTION) (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1980

metadata.short_title: Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices (Control and Prevention) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1980

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices (Control and Prevention) Ordinance, 1970. It modifies sections related to the Authority's functions, stock orders, and definitions of restrictive trade practices. The text updates specific clauses regarding percentages, undertakings, and provincial references within the existing ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to streamline, and enhance the rates of certain taxes and duties in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance streamlines and enhances tax rates on electricity, vehicles, and other duties in Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1980 was promulgated to streamline and enhance the rates of certain taxes and duties within the Province of the Punjab. It substitutes specific entries in existing finance acts and ordinances regarding schedules for motor vehicle registration fees, electricity duties, and other levies. The document also outlines procedures for assessment and collection, bars civil suits against assessments made under it, and grants power to the Government to make rules for its implementation.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Industrial Development Board (Amendment) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Industrial Development Board Act, 1973.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Industrial Development Board Act, 1973 to update terminology within specific sections. It substitutes the word 'Board' for 'industries' in section 2, clause (h). Additionally, it replaces clauses in section 5 regarding the Managing Director and updates section 6 concerning industries under control. The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab on February 23, 1980.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Economic Research Institute Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Economic Research Institute as a statutory body.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Economic Research Institute as a statutory body to conduct economic and socio-economic research.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Punjab Economic Research Institute as a statutory body with perpetual succession. The Institute is tasked with conducting research in economics, demography, and socio-economic problems, providing information on modern techniques, and publishing results. It advises the Government on economic policies and provides training facilities. The administration and management of the Institute vest in a Board consisting of government officials and non-official members.

name: PUNJAB REAL ESTATE AGENTS AND MOTOR VEHICLES DEALERS (REGULATION OF BUSINESS) ORDINANCE, 1980

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Real Estate Agents and Motor Vehicles Dealers (Regulation of Business) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate the business of real estate agents and motor vehicles dealers in the Province of Punjab.
metadata.max_penalty: six months imprisonment or fine of Rs. 5,000 or both
metadata.one_line: Regulates business, registration, and penalties for real estate agents and motor vehicle dealers in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the business of real estate agents and motor vehicles dealers within the Province of Punjab. It establishes requirements for registration with a designated authority, including fees, security, and specific disqualifications such as being a minor or having a criminal record. The document outlines procedures for obtaining and renewing certificates, maintaining accounts, and provides penalties for non-compliance or malpractice.

metadata.short_title: Securities and Exchange (Amendment) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Capital Issues (Continuance of Control) Act, 1947.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Capital Issues (Continuance of Control) Act, 1947 to update the list of recognized investment instruments. It specifically adds 'Modaraba Certificates' and 'Mutual Fund Units' to the definition of securities while removing references to 'Participation Term Bonds'. The amendment also updates punctuation and terminology in various sections regarding pledging and hypothecation.

metadata.short_title: The University of the Punjab (Amendment) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the University of the Punjab Act, 1973.
amends: The University of the Punjab Act, 1973
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab, Law Department

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the University of the Punjab Act, 1973 to introduce 'Islamic and Pakistan Studies' as a compulsory subject at the Bachelor's Degree level. It establishes the office of Pro-Vice-Chancellor, modifies the composition of the Syndicate to include specific representatives, and updates provisions regarding staff appointments and expenditure rules.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Excise Duty on Minerals (Labour Welfare) Act, 1967. It substitutes the words 'one rupee' with 'fifty five paisa' in Section 3 of the parent Act. The amendment was promulgated by the President under emergency powers to take immediate action.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Education Foundation Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the Punjab Education Foundation.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Education Foundation to promote and finance educational activities in the province.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Punjab Education Foundation as a body corporate with perpetual succession. The Foundation is tasked with promoting and financing surveys, studies, and projects related to universal literacy, employment-oriented skills, and educational research. Its Board of Trustees includes representatives from various government departments, universities, and eminent scholars to guide its policy and administration.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Industrial Development Board (Amendment) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Industrial Development Board Act, 1973.
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Industrial Development Board Act, 1973
amends: The Punjab Industrial Development Board Act, 1973
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab, Law Department
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1973 Act to allow the Board to sell shares or transfer assets with Government approval.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Industrial Development Board Act, 1973 to enable the Board to sell its shares or transfer assets of completed projects. The amendment requires Government approval for such transactions. It was promulgated by the Governor of Punjab on April 12, 1979, and came into force immediately.

name: PUNJAB LIVESTOCK ASSOCIATIONS AND LIVESTOCK ASSOCIATIONS UNION (REGISTRATION AND CONTROL) ORDINANCE, 1979

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Livestock Associations and Livestock Associations Unions (Registration and Control) Ordinance, 1979
