metadata.one_line: This Ordinance provides for the registration, control, and bye-laws of livestock associations and unions in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes a legal framework for the registration and control of village livestock associations and their unions in the Province of Punjab. It defines the qualifications for forming an association, the process for registering bye-laws, and limits member liability to their shareholding. The Ordinance also outlines rules regarding member disqualifications, dispute resolution mechanisms involving the Board, and the power of the Government to make further rules.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 1979
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 1979 pursuant to a proclamation order.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 1979. It was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab on August 21, 1979. The amendment is made in pursuance of Proclamation Order No. 1 of 1977 regarding laws continuation during emergency.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government (Fourth Amendment) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 1979
key_definitions: misconduct (includes diversion of funds, bribery, corruption)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 1979 regarding election disputes, asset declarations, and removal from office.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to address election disputes, asset declarations, and grounds for removal of council members. It introduces provisions allowing aggrieved persons to apply to Election Authorities within seven days of result declaration regarding contraventions of provisions. The text also mandates asset declarations by every member within thirty days of the first meeting and outlines specific disqualifications and procedures for removing chairmen, vice-chairmen, or members from office due to misconduct or absence.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 1979 (Second Amendment)
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 1979
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 1979

metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to prohibit candidates from associating with political parties during elections.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to prevent candidates from contesting elections on a party basis. It prohibits candidates from giving themselves out as nominees of political parties, receiving financial assistance from them, or displaying affiliation to any party. Contravention leads to disqualification by the Election Authority for up to four years.

metadata.short_title: Zakat and Ushr Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make provisions relating to the assessment, collection and disbursement of Zakat and Ushr
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: Zakat and Ushr (Organisation) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance establishes the framework for assessing, collecting, and disbursing Zakat and Ushr across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Zakat and Ushr Ordinance, 1980 provides legal provisions for the assessment, collection, and disbursement of Zakat and Ushr in Pakistan. It applies to Muslim citizens and companies where the majority ownership is held by such citizens. The Ordinance establishes various administrative bodies including a Central Council, Provincial Councils, and local committees at the district, tehsil, and village levels to manage these funds. It repeals the previous Zakat and Ushr (Organisation) Ordinance, 1979.

name: PUNJAB PREVENTION OF GAMBLING AMENDMENT ORDINANCE, 1979

metadata.one_line: Amends the 1978 Gambling Ordinance to grant police officers powers to arrest and seize gaming instruments.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Prevention of Gambling Ordinance, 1978 by inserting a new section. The amendment grants police officers of the rank of Sub-Inspector or higher specific powers regarding gambling offences. These powers include arresting persons without a warrant for committing offences under Section 5, searching persons to seize gaming instruments, and seizing gaming moneys or articles suspected of being used for such offences.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Urban Rent Restriction (Amendment) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to further amend the Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Ordinance, 1959.
amends: The Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Ordinance, 1959
repeals: The Punjab Urban Rent Restriction (Amendment) Ordinance, 1978 (I of 1978)
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1959 Rent Restriction Ordinance regarding fair rent calculation and eviction rights for salaried landlords.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Ordinance, 1959 to update procedures for fixing fair rent and introducing new provisions for tenant eviction. It specifically grants eviction rights to landlords who are salaried employees, widows, or minor orphans under certain conditions. The document also inserts a new section regarding appeals against Controller orders to the District Judge.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Waqf Properties Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the proper management and administration of Waqf Properties in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.commencement: from the date of publication in the official Gazette

metadata.summary: The Punjab Waqf Properties Ordinance, 1979 was promulgated by the Governor to regulate the management of Waqf properties within the Province of Punjab. It creates a Chief Administrator of Auqaf and Deputy Administrators to oversee these properties, which include mosques, shrines, and other pious endowments. The Ordinance also provides for the registration of such properties, the employment of public servants, and the regulation of Islamic religious education institutions.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance (Amendment) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1978.

Specifically, it substitutes references to fixed percentages with actual occupied units in certain clauses and deletes a proviso in clause (e). The Ordinance comes into force immediately upon promulgation by the Governor of the Punjab.

name: WEST PAKISTAN WATER AND POWER DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1979

metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to further amend the West Pakistan Water and Power Development Authority Act, 1958

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the West Pakistan Water and Power Development Authority Act, 1958 to update names from 'West Pakistan' to 'Pakistan'. It adds provisions protecting employees removed or retired under specific orders from legal challenges regarding their termination of service. The changes apply to proceedings before courts or tribunals prior to September 30, 1975, and the coming into force of this Ordinance.

name: COLONIZATION OF GOVERNMENT LANDS (PUNJAB AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1978

metadata.short_title: The Colonization of Government Lands (Punjab) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1978

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Colonization of Government Lands (Punjab), Act, 1912, to address issues regarding fraudulent acquisition of tenancy rights. It empowers the Board of Revenue to resume land or reduce its area if a person acquired tenancy rights through fraud, misrepresentation, or was ineligible for such rights. name: FOODSTUFFS AND FERTILIZERS (CANCELLATION OF AUTHORIZATIONS AND DEALERSHIPS) ORDINANCE, 1978

metadata.one_line: Provides for the cancellation of authorizations and dealerships for foodstuffs and fertilizers in Punjab without compensation.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance empowers the Government of the Punjab to cancel authorizations under the West Pakistan Foodstuffs Distribution Order, 1967, and dealerships under the Punjab Fertilizers (Control) Order, 1973. It allows for such cancellations without paying any compensation to the affected parties. The Ordinance also delegates powers to officers to exercise these functions and provides legal protection against suits or injunctions regarding actions taken in good faith.

name: MURREE KAHUTA HILLY AREAS DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (REPEAL) ORDINANCE, 1978

metadata.summary: This Ordinance repeals the Murree Kahuta Hilly Areas Development Authority Act, 1975. It clarifies definitions regarding immovable property and unauthorised occupants within autonomous bodies. The amendment empowers autonomous bodies to evict such occupants using necessary force without compensation for crops or structures left after a notice period. Additionally, it bars civil courts from granting injunctions against such evictions and allows requisitioning police assistance.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Civil Courts (Amendment) Ordinance, 1978

It substitutes the word 'fifty' for 'twenty five' in Sub-section (1) of Section 18, clause (a). The amendment was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab on September 20, 1978, and came into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Corporation Employees (Special Powers) Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to invest the Governor with certain powers in respect of persons in Corporation Service.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance empowers the Governor of the Punjab to exercise special authority over persons in Corporation Service. It allows for the removal or reversion of specific employees appointed between January 1, 1972 and July 5, 1977 without prior notice. Affected individuals have the right to submit a representation or petition for review within fifteen days. The Ordinance also deems removed persons as civil servants for the purposes of the Punjab Service Tribunals Act, 1974.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance (Amendment) Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Finance Act, 1964.
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Finance Act, 1964

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Finance Act, 1964 to update a specific monetary value in Section 12. It substitutes the phrase 'twenty two maund' with 'fifty six hundred paisa' within the relevant subsection. The legislation was promulgated by the Governor of Punjab on May 27, 1978, and came into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance (Amendment) Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1978.
repeals: Section 5 of the Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1978
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab, Law Department

metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab to amend the Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1978. It extends to the entire Province of the Punjab and came into force immediately upon publication. The document specifically repeals Section 5 of the original ordinance with effect from July 1, 1978.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to levy and enhance the rates of certain taxes and duties in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance amends various tax acts in Punjab to levy and enhance rates on electricity, hotels, and vehicles.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Finance Ordinance, 1978 was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab to amend existing tax laws. It enhances tax rates on electricity consumption, introduces a new duty on hotel stays based on room charges, and adjusts vehicle taxation schedules. The document also provides for rebates if taxes are paid in lump sums and specifies different rates for hill stations.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Land Revenue (Amendment) Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to further amend the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967.
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967
repeals: The Punjab Land Revenue (Abolition) Act, 1977
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab, Law Department
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967 regarding tax exemptions and enhanced rates for specific land owners.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967 to restore certain provisions repealed by the Punjab Land Revenue (Abolition) Act, 1977. It establishes new categories of land ownership that qualify for revenue exemptions and defines enhanced tax rates for owners exceeding specific acreage limits for irrigated and unirrigated land starting from Rabi 1976-77. The law applies to the entire Province of Punjab and comes into force immediately upon promulgation by the Governor.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Local Government Act, 1975
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Local Government Act, 1975

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Local Government Act, 1975 by adding a new sub-section to Section 43. The amendment declares that persons in the Local Council Service are deemed to be local servants for the purposes of the Punjab Service Tribunals Act, 1974. It applies to the Province of Punjab and comes into force immediately upon promulgation.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Prevention of Gambling Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the prevention of gambling.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Punjab
repeals: The Punjab Prevention of Gambling Ordinance, 1961
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance prevents gambling in Punjab by defining offenses and penalties for running common gaming houses.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Prevention of Gambling Ordinance, 1978 was promulgated to provide for the prevention of gambling within the Province of Punjab. It defines key terms such as 'common gaming house' and 'gaming', which includes wagering or betting on figures, numbers, dates, or natural events. The document establishes penalties for owners, occupiers, and individuals found playing in common gaming houses or public places, ranging from fines to imprisonment up to three years for repeat offenders.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Prohibition Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to prohibit the manufacture, sale and consumption of intoxicating liquors in the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six years or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: Prohibits manufacture, sale and consumption of intoxicating liquors in Punjab with penalties and licensing powers.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance prohibits the manufacture, sale, and consumption of intoxicating liquors within the Province of Punjab. It defines key terms such as 'intoxicating liquor' and 'manufacture', and establishes offences for importing, exporting, transporting, or selling these substances. The law empowers Prohibition Officers (often Collectors) to enforce regulations, issue licences, and confiscate illicit goods, while providing specific exemptions for diplomatic agents.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Public Service Commission (Amendment) Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1978

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1978 to clarify the eligibility for chairmanship and the commencement of office. It substitutes Section 6 to allow members other than the Chairman to be appointed as Chairmen under specific conditions. Additionally, it redefines the functions of the Commission to include conducting tests for recruitment, advising on provincial service terms, and performing other prescribed duties.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal and, with certain modifications, re-enact the Punjab Public Service Commission Act, 1974.
repeals: The Punjab Public Service Commission Act, 1974
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance repeals and re-enacts the Punjab Public Service Commission Act, 1974 with modifications.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab to repeal and modify the Punjab Public Service Commission Act, 1974. It establishes the composition, appointment, terms, and removal procedures for members of the Punjab Public Service Commission. The document outlines the Commission's functions regarding civil service selection and advises the Governor on qualifications. It also mandates the preparation of an annual report and grants power to make rules.

name: PUNJAB REQUISITIONING OF STAGE CARRIAGES (TEMPORARY POWERS) (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1978

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Requisitioning of Stage Carriages (Temporary Powers) Ordinance, 1970. It substitutes references to 'Motor Vehicles' with 'Stage Carriages' and deletes specific exclusions regarding tribal areas. The amendment also modifies procedures for requisitioning vehicles, requiring District Magistrates to provide opportunities for owners to show cause before action is taken. Additionally, it establishes a compensation mechanism for vehicle owners based on depreciation and a profit margin when their vehicles are kept in possession by the District Magistrate.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Thal (Increase in Value) Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the levy of a tax on lands from which irrigation facilities have been extended or are likely to be extended due to the introduction of irrigation in the Thal areas.

metadata.one_line: This Ordinance levies a tax on lands in the Thal area receiving irrigation and repeals the 1940 Act.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the immediate levy of a tax on lands in the Thal areas where irrigation facilities have been or are likely to be extended. The tax is imposed on land owners, mortgagees, or tenants depending on possession rights, with rates specified by the Board of Revenue. It repeals the Punjab (Thal Increase in Value) Act, 1940, and validates all actions taken under the repealed Act as if done under this new Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 1979

metadata.summary: The Punjab Local Government Ordinance, 1979 was promulgated to consolidate and amend existing laws relating to local government in the Province of Punjab. It provides for the constitution and continuance of local government institutions, including local councils, municipal committees, and municipal corporations. The Ordinance applies to the whole of the Province except cantonment areas and comes into force immediately upon publication.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Urban Rent Restriction (Amendment) Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Ordinance, 1959

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Ordinance, 1959 to further regulate urban rent restrictions. It introduces new provisions for appointing additional Rent Controllers, defines methods for fixing fair rent based on local circumstances, and establishes procedures for handling disputes between landlords and tenants. The document also updates sections regarding appellate authorities, appeal timelines, and powers to award compensation for frivolous applications.

metadata.short_title: The Constitution (Sixth Amendment) Act, 1976

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Constitution of Pakistan to extend the tenure of the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court until completion of a five-year term. It also allows a Chief Justice of a High Court to continue in office until completing a term after attaining the age of sixty-two. The Act includes Kohistan district and Mansehra in the definition of Tribal Areas and updates definitions related to parliamentary officers.

It omits certain words from clauses and headings while adding a colon after a proviso. The amendment clarifies that cost of living allowance shall not form part of the wages of a worker under specified acts.

The amendment substitutes the word 'fifty-eighth' with 'sixtieth' in Section 12, clause (1) of the 1974 Act. The Act comes into force immediately but is deemed effective from November 22, 1976.

It explicitly repeals the Punjab Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1961, and the Bahawalpur State Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1949. The legislation includes saving clauses ensuring that land revenue or taxes becoming due before Rabi 1976-77 remain payable under existing laws.

The Managing Director is appointed by the Government and serves as ex-officio Secretary of the Board. The Act also grants the Government power to alter membership or change the number of Directors via notification.

It specifically increases taxes on motor vehicles based on weight and capacity, raises entertainment duties on admissions, and adjusts stamp duties on conveyances and agricultural land. The legislation also repeals specific sections of previous acts and substitutes schedules related to vehicle taxation and stamp duties.

It applies to all existing leases granted by officers or authorities other than the Deputy Commissioner through open auction, excluding those held by government departments or bodies established under law. The Act mandates immediate termination of these leases while providing a mechanism for the Government to pay compensation to lessees for roads and buildings constructed for mining operations. Decisions regarding compensation are final and conclusive, preventing legal challenges in any court.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Canal and Drainage Act, 1873 to further regulate canal and drainage works within the Province of Punjab. It introduces new definitions for water courses, establishes irrigation committees comprising cultivators and canal officers, and outlines procedures for changing water sources or constructing link water-courses. The legislation also defines offences related to damaging canal works and sets fines as compensation for injured persons.

The amendment specifies that in performing his functions, the Chancellor must act and be bound in the same manner as the Governor of the Province under Article 105 of the Constitution. The Act was passed by the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab and assented to by the Governor on March 12, 1975.

metadata.summary: The Federal Adaptation of Laws Order, 1975 is a Presidential Order made under Article 268 of the Constitution to adapt existing laws immediately before its commencement. It directs the substitution of expressions like 'Central Government' with 'Federal Government', 'Centre' with 'Federation', and adjusts references to specific provinces or tribal areas to reflect the constitutional structure. The Order applies to a wide range of statutes listed in the Schedule, ensuring they remain consistent with the Constitution while retaining their material effect until repealed or amended.

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Islamia University of Bahawalpur as a body corporate with an autonomous status. It provides for the university's constitution, including the Chancellor, Senate, Syndicate, and Academic Council. The university is empowered to provide instruction in Islamic learning, allied disciplines, and sciences, conduct examinations, and award degrees. The Act also repeals the West Pakistan Jamia Islamia (Bahawalpur) Ordinance, 1964, transferring its assets and liabilities to the new university.

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Lahore Water and Sewerage Authority as a body corporate to facilitate the execution of the Lahore Water Supply, Sewerage and Drainage Scheme. The Authority consists of members including representatives from local government committees, the Provincial Assembly, and various departmental secretaries, along with a Managing Director appointed by the Government. It defines key terms such as 'Authority', 'Corporation', and 'Scheme', outlines the composition and powers of the Authority, and prescribes penalties for offenses like obstructing duties or damaging water infrastructure.

metadata.short_title: The Lahore Development Authority Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the Constitution of the Lahore Development Authority.

The Town Improvement Act, 1922
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the Lahore Development Authority to improve metropolitan development in Lahore.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the constitution of the Lahore Development Authority (LDA) as a body corporate. The LDA is tasked with improving the quality of life in the Lahore metropolitan area through integrated planning and optimum utilization of resources. Its functions cover housing, industrial development, traffic, transportation, health, education, water supply, sewerage, drainage, and solid waste disposal. The Act also repeals the Lahore Water and Sewerage Authority Act, 1975, and the Town Improvement Act, 1922, transferring their functions and assets to the new Authority.

metadata.short_title: The Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1975

The amendment is enacted under the Proclamation of Emergency referred to in Article 280 of the Constitution. It comes into force immediately upon publication.

It substitutes specific clauses in Section 3 to define periods when exemptions do not apply, specifically during session breaks or for reasons of state security. The amendment was deemed effective on February 8, 1975.

It modifies provisions concerning the Syndicate's ability to propose statutes affecting university authority and restricts their disciplinary power over officers and teachers. Additionally, it revises retirement conditions for university employees, allowing early retirement after twenty-five years of service or at age fifty-eight upon direction.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Murree-Kahuta Hilly Areas Development Authority to oversee development projects in specific hilly regions of Rawalpindi District. The Authority is empowered to implement schemes for agriculture, industry, tourism, housing, and environmental conservation while acquiring and managing property. Its composition includes the Chief Minister, Provincial Assembly members from relevant constituencies, and local council representatives, with powers delegated to a Director-General.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Political Parties Act, 1962 to ensure its provisions accord with the Constitution of Pakistan. It defines the Constitution as that of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan and prohibits political parties formed to propagate opinions prejudicial to national sovereignty or integrity. The Act empowers the Federal Government to dissolve such parties and refers dissolution matters to the Supreme Court for a final decision within fifteen days.

It clarifies the exclusive jurisdiction over civil servants' terms and conditions, including disciplinary matters, and sets specific rules for appeals against departmental orders. The Act also repeals the earlier Punjab Ordinance No. IX of 1975.

It substitutes new sections defining the composition of Tribunals, their jurisdiction over civil servants' terms and conditions, and procedures for filing appeals against departmental orders. Additionally, it deletes existing sections 6 and 7 of the principal Act.

It empowers the Managing Director to issue notices for payment and declare persons who fail to pay as defaulters. Such declarations allow the Corporation to recover amounts as arrears of land revenue from the defaulter or their surety under the Revenue Recovery Act, 1890. The Act also repeals a conflicting Ordinance passed in the same year.

It creates a corporate body consisting of a Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Senate, Syndicate, and Academic Council. The University is empowered to prescribe courses, hold examinations, award degrees, affiliate institutions, and maintain discipline among students.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Civil Servants Act, 1974 to update provisions on civil servant retirement. It establishes specific dates for retirement based on post equivalence, years of service, or age, allowing for directions in the public interest. The text also defines 'competent authority' as the appointing authority or a duly authorized person not lower in rank than the civil servant concerned.

name: PUNJAB COUNCIL OF THE ARTS ACT, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Council of the Arts Act, 1975

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Council of the Arts to provide patronage for the development of arts and culture. The Council is headed by a Board of Governors and managed by an Executive Committee and an Executive Director. Its functions include advising the government on policy, coordinating with other cultural organizations, managing institutions like museums and galleries, and organizing festivals. The Council's funds are derived from federal and provincial grants, donations, and income from its activities.

name: PUNJAB COUNCIL OF THE ARTS ORDINANCE, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Council of the Arts Ordinance, 1975

metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Punjab Council of the Arts to patronize, promote, and develop arts and culture within the Province of Punjab. The Council is constituted as a body corporate with perpetual succession, managed by a Board of Governors including the Chief Minister and various officials, and overseen by an Executive Committee. Its functions include organizing cultural events, managing art institutions, assisting cultural organizations, and regulating their activities, funded through government grants and donations.

It grants the Government power to modify the Schedule, make rules for implementation, and recover arrears as if they were land revenue.

metadata.summary: This Act provides for housing facilities for non-proprietors, defined as persons who do not own agricultural land or immovable property anywhere in the country. It applies to all rural areas in the Province of Punjab, excluding urban areas as defined by local government laws. The Act empowers Collectors to prepare housing schemes and acquire land for residential sites, offering compensation up to Rupees five thousand per acre. The Corporation is managed by a Board consisting of government nominees and operates under the general direction of the Government of the Punjab. It applies to all minerals except those necessary for national security or nuclear energy generation.

metadata.one_line: Removes legal difficulties regarding the rights of refugee females over limited estates and repeals a previous ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act addresses issues concerning refugee females who were erroneously treated as full owners of property instead of limited owners under custom. It restores their status as limited owners and allows affected persons to challenge decrees treating them as full owners within one year of the Act's commencement. The legislation also bars anyone claiming adverse possession in such properties from pleading against lawful heirs of the last male holder. Finally, it repeals the Punjab Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Ordinance, 1975.

It inserts specific wording into Article 106 regarding the Quadiani and Lahori groups who identify as Ahmadis. Additionally, it adds a new clause to Article 260 defining a person who does not believe in the finality of Prophethood or claims prophethood after Muhammad as not being a Muslim for constitutional purposes.

metadata.short_title: The Employees' Cost of Living (Relief) Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for payment of a cost of living allowance to employees and for matters ancillary thereto
repeals: The Employees' Cost of Living (Relief) Ordinance, 1973 (XXII of 1973)
metadata.max_penalty: simple imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: Provides for payment of a cost of living allowance to employees and repeals the corresponding 1973 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act mandates that every employee employed on or after August 1, 1973, must receive a cost of living allowance from their employer. The allowance is set at thirty-five rupees per month for those earning up to seven hundred rupees, or adjusted so total wages reach seven hundred and thirty-five rupees for higher earners. It defines key terms like 'employee', 'employer', and 'undertaking' broadly to include various industries and establishments. Employers failing to pay face penalties including imprisonment or fines, and aggrieved employees can seek recovery through authorized authorities.

metadata.short_title: The Municipal Administration (Punjab Amendment) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Municipal Administration Ordinance, 1960, in its application to the Province of the Punjab.
repeals: The Municipal Administration Ordinance No. IV of 1974
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or fine of five thousand rupees, or both; continuing offence punishable with further fine up to one hundred rupees per day
metadata.one_line: Amends the Municipal Administration Ordinance, 1960 regarding encroachments and trespass in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Municipal Administration Ordinance, 1960 to address encroachments on municipal property such as open spaces, streets, roads, drains, and graveyards. It empowers Municipal Committees to remove unauthorized encroachments and imposes penalties for trespassing into buildings vested in a Committee. The Act also substitutes sections regarding punishments for contraventions and repeals the Municipal Administration Ordinance No. IV of 1974.

metadata.short_title: West Pakistan Rangers (Amendment) Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the West Pakistan Ordinance, 1959
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan (implied by Parliament enactment and general publication)
metadata.one_line: Amends the West Pakistan Rangers Ordinance, 1959 by substituting 'Pakistan Rangers' and changing 'Central' to 'Federal'.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the West Pakistan Rangers Ordinance, 1959 to update terminology reflecting the transition from Central to Federal governance. It substitutes 'Pakistan Rangers' for 'West Pakistan Rangers' throughout the Ordinance. Additionally, it changes references from 'Central Government' to 'Federal Government' in specific sections regarding powers and duties.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Administrative Tribunals Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Administrative Tribunals to exercise jurisdiction regarding matters relating to the terms and conditions of service in respect of services of the Province of the Punjab.
repeals: The Punjab Civil Services (Appellate Tribunals) Ordinance, 1970
metadata.one_line: Establishes Administrative Tribunals in Punjab to adjudicate disputes regarding civil servants' terms and conditions of service.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes Administrative Tribunals in the Province of Punjab with exclusive jurisdiction over matters relating to the terms and conditions of service for provincial civil servants. It outlines the qualifications, tenure, and appointment procedures for Tribunal Chairmen and Members, while also incorporating High Court rules regarding evidence and records. The Act repeals the earlier Punjab Civil Services (Appellate Tribunals) Ordinance, 1970, and provides mechanisms for appeals, including time limits and provisions for defaulting parties.

name: PUNJAB ANIMALS COMPOUND FEEDING STUFF ACT, 1974

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Animals Compound Feeding Stuff Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the manufacture and marketing of animals compound feeding stuff in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may appoint
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years or with fine or with both
metadata.one_line: Regulates the manufacture and marketing of animal compound feeding stuff in Punjab through licensing and labelling rules.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the manufacture and marketing of compound feeding stuff for animals within the Province of the Punjab. It establishes a licensing system managed by an Inspection Officer, requiring licenses for manufacturing and prohibiting the sale of unlicensed or adulterated products. The legislation defines key terms such as 'adulterated' and 'misbranded' feeding stuff, mandates proper packing and labelling, and grants inspectors powers to seize samples and prosecute offenders who contravene its provisions.

name: PUNJAB COTTON CONTROL (VALIDATION OF TRANSPORTATION FEE) ACT, 1974

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Cotton Control (Validation of Transportation Fee) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to validate the levy, charging, collection and realisation of transportation fee under the West Punjab Cotton (Control) Act, 1949, and the Bahawalpur Cotton (Control) Act, 1949.
metadata.one_line: Validates the levy and collection of transportation fees under specific 1949 cotton control acts in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act validates the levy, charging, collection, and realisation of transportation fees imposed under the West Punjab Cotton (Control) Act, 1949, and the Bahawalpur Cotton (Control) Act, 1949. It applies to the whole of the Punjab and deems any such fees levied before this Act came into force as validly collected. The Act ensures that fees not refunded or adjusted against other Pakistan fees payable under the West Pakistan Cotton (Control) Ordinance, 1966, shall not be recovered.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to continue and levy certain taxes and fees in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
metadata.commencement: on and from the first day of July, 1974
amends: The Punjab Finance Act, 1973 (Punjab Act No. XIV of 1973)
West Pakistan Urban Property Tax Ordinance, 1958
repeals: section 8 of West Pakistan Finance Ordinance, 1969
metadata.one_line: Continues and levies specific taxes and fees in Punjab while amending existing revenue laws.
metadata.summary: This Act continues and levies certain taxes and fees within the Province of the Punjab. It amends the Punjab Finance Act, 1973 to update licence fees for cotton ginning factories and balajng presses. Additionally, it modifies rates and wording in the Urban Property Tax Ordinance, 1958, the Entertainment Duty Act, 1956, and repeals a specific section of the West Pakistan Finance Ordinance, 1969.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Civil Servants Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the appointment to, and the terms and conditions of service in respect of the services of the Province of the Punjab.
repeals: The Punjab Civil Servants Ordinance, 1974
key_definitions: permanent without limit post of time
metadata.one_line: Regulates appointment, terms, and conditions for civil servants in the Province of Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the appointment to, and the terms and conditions of service for civil servants in the Province of Punjab. It defines key terms such as 'civil servant', 'ad hoc appointment', and 'pay', and establishes procedures for initial recruitment, probation, confirmation, and seniority. The Act also provides for appeals regarding orders relating to terms of service and repeals the previous Punjab Civil Servants Ordinance, 1974.

name: PUNJAB LIVESTOCK, DAIRY AND POULTRY DEVELOPMENT BOARD ACT, 1974

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Livestock, Dairy and Poultry Development Board Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Livestock, Dairy and Poultry Development Board in the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
repeals: The Punjab Livestock Dairy and Poultry Development Board Ordinance, 1973 (Punjab Ordinance No. XXI of 1973)
establishes: Punjab Livestock, Dairy and Poultry Development Board
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Livestock, Dairy and Poultry Development Board to manage public sector projects in the province.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Livestock, Dairy and Poultry Development Board as a body corporate within the Province of Punjab. The Board is empowered to acquire, hold property, and manage livestock, dairy, poultry, and allied projects in the public sector. It consists of a Chairman, various government secretaries, non-official members, and a Managing Director, operating under the directions of the Government of the Punjab.

name: PUNJAB PLANTATION AND MAINTENANCE OF TREES ACT, 1974

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Plantation and Maintenance of Trees Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for plantation and maintenance of trees in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Punjab
metadata.max_penalty: fine not exceeding one rupee per tree
metadata.administering_body: Forestry Department, Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the plantation and maintenance of trees in Punjab, defining terms and imposing penalties for non-compliance.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Plantation and Maintenance of Trees Act, 1974 was enacted to promote tree planting and care within the Province of Punjab. It defines key terms such as 'Department', 'Government', 'land', and 'occupier' to clarify responsibilities. The Act mandates that occupiers must plant a prescribed number of trees on their land and maintain them, with penalties including fines for failure to comply.

name: PUNJAB PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLY SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES OF MEMBERS ACT, 1974

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Provincial Assembly Salaries, Allowances and Privileges of Members Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the salaries, allowances and privileges of the Members of the Provincial Assembly of the Province of Punjab.
metadata.commencement: at once, but deemed to have taken effect on and from the 1st day of October, 1974
repeals: Punjab Provincial Assembly (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges of Members) Order, 1972
Punjab Ordinance No. XII of 1974
metadata.one_line: This Act provides salaries, allowances, and privileges for members of the Punjab Provincial Assembly.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the framework for paying salaries, daily allowances, and travel expenses to members of the Punjab Provincial Assembly. It defines specific terms such as 'Member' and 'session', sets rates for various modes of transport, and provides facilities like telephone connections and office accommodation. The Act also grants tax exemptions and special allowances to the Leader of the Opposition.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Public Service Commission Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for a Public Service Commission for the Province of the Punjab.
repeals: The Punjab Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1973 (Punjab Ordinance No. XVIII of 1973)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Public Service Commission to conduct recruitment tests and advise on provincial service terms.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the establishment of a Public Service Commission for the Province of the Punjab. The Commission consists of five members appointed by the Governor, with one nominated as Chairman. Its functions include conducting examinations for recruitment to provincial services and advising the Government on terms and conditions of service. The Act also empowers the Governor to make rules for carrying out its purposes and repeals the earlier 1973 Ordinance.

name: PUNJAB TENDOO LEAVES (PROHIBITION ON POSSESSION AND USE IN THE BORDER BELT) ACT, 1974

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Tendoo Leaves (Prohibition on Possession and Use in the Border-Belt) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for prohibition in the border-belt of the Province of the Punjab, including the manufacture of bidi and matters incidental and supplemental thereto.
metadata.territorial_extent: the Province of the Punjab, including the border-belt (area extending upto ten miles inside the Province of the Punjab from the International boundary line of Pakistan)
repeals: Punjab Ordinance No. XXII of 1973
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: Prohibits possession and use of tendoo leaves and manufacture of bidi in the Punjab border-belt.
metadata.summary: This Act prohibits the possession and use of tendoo leaves and the manufacture of bidi within the border-belt of the Province of the Punjab. It defines key terms such as 'border-belt' and 'tendoo leaf', establishes penalties including imprisonment and fines for contraventions, and grants police powers to seize items and search premises related to offences under the Act. The Act also repeals a previous Ordinance from 1973.

name: PUNJAB WILDLIFE (PROTECTION, PRESERVATION, CONSERATION AND MANAGEMENT) ACT, 1974

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Wildlife (Protection, Preservation, Conservation and Management) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the protection, preservation, conservation and management of wildlife in the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
repeals: The Punjab Wildlife (Protection, Preservation, Conservation and Management) Ordinance, 1972
The Elephant Preservation Act, 1879
The Wild Bird and Animal Protection Act, 1912
The West Pakistan Wildlife Protection Ordinance, 1959
metadata.one_line: This Act protects and manages wildlife in Punjab by establishing a Board, defining offences, and repealing older laws.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Wildlife (Protection, Preservation, Conservation and Management) Act, 1974 was enacted to regulate the protection and management of wildlife within the Province of the Punjab. It establishes the Punjab Wildlife Management Board as a corporate body responsible for policy decisions regarding conservation and game management. The Act defines various terms such as 'game animal', 'hunt', and 'officer', and creates offences related to hunting in reserved areas or without proper licenses. Furthermore, it repeals several previous enactments including the 1972 Ordinance and older acts from 1879 and 1912 that applied to the province.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Laws (Adaptation) Order, 1974
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on the 14th day of August, 1973
amends: The West Punjab Alienation of Land Act (XII of 1900)
The Hindu Gains Learning Act (XXX of 1930)
The Multi-Unit Co-operative Societies Act (VI of 1942)

The Colonization of Government Lands (Punjab) Act (V of 1912)
The West Pakistan Private Colleges Management and Control Ordinance (XX of 1970)
The West Pakistan Finance (Punjab) Ordinance (XXI of 1970)
The West Pakistan Private Colleges Management and Control (Punjab Amendment) Ordinance (X of 1970)
metadata.one_line: An Order adapting various laws to replace 'Central' with 'Federal' and 'West Pakistan' with 'Punjab'.
metadata.summary: This Order is made by the Governor of the Punjab under Article 268 of the Constitution to adapt existing laws for the province. It substitutes terms like 'Central' with 'Federal', 'West Pakistan' with 'Punjab', and 'North Western Frontier' with 'the Province'. The Order applies to a long list of Acts and Ordinances, bringing them into accord with provincial jurisdiction immediately upon promulgation.

metadata.short_title: The University of the Punjab (Amendment) Ordinance, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the University of the Punjab Act, 1973.
metadata.parent_law: The University of the Punjab Act, 1973
amends: The University of the Punjab Act, 1973
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab Law Department
metadata.one_line: Amends the University of the Punjab Act, 1973 to allow relaxation of appointment qualifications based on scholarship.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the University of the Punjab Act, 1973 to facilitate the appointment of officers despite existing statutory restrictions. It empowers the Chancellor to relax qualification requirements for specific posts if there is outstanding scholarship or contribution to learning. The power is exercised individually in cases recommended by the concerned appointing authority. The Ordinance was promulgated because the Provincial Assembly was not in session.

metadata.short_title: The Weights and Measures (Metric System) (Amendment) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Weights and Measures (Metric System) Act, 1967
amends: The Weights and Measures (Metric System) Act, 1967
metadata.one_line: Amends the Weights and Measures (Metric System) Act, 1967 to align with international standards.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Weights and Measures (Metric System) Act, 1967 to update terminology from 'metric' to 'International' and 'Federal Government' to 'Central Government'. It inserts new definitions for 'mole' and 'second' based on atomic and cesium standards, and redefines 'kelvin' using thermodynamic temperature fractions. The amendments come into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: West Pakistan Arms (Amendment) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the West Pakistan Arms Ordinance, 1965
metadata.one_line: Amends the West Pakistan Arms Ordinance, 1965 to replace 'West Pakistan' with 'Pakistan' and clarify licensing powers.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the West Pakistan Arms Ordinance, 1965 to update terminology from 'West Pakistan' to 'Pakistan' and 'Central Government' to 'Federal Government'. It clarifies that the Federal Government holds exclusive power to issue licenses for prohibited arms and ammunition via notification, while Provincial Governments retain licensing powers only for non-prohibited weapons. The Act also amends specific sections of the parent Ordinance regarding definitions and omitted clauses.

name: UNIVERSITY OF ENGINEERING AND TECHNOLOGY, LAHORE ACT, 1974

metadata.short_title: The University of Engineering and Technology, Lahore, Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to re-constitute and reorganize the University of Engineering and Technology, Lahore.
repeals: The West Pakistan University of Engineering and Technology Ordinance, 1961
The Punjab University of Engineering and Technology Ordinance, 1974
establishes: University of Engineering and Technology, Lahore
metadata.one_line: This Act reconstitutes and reorganizes the University of Engineering and Technology, Lahore, repealing previous ordinances.
metadata.summary: The University of Engineering and Technology, Lahore, Act, 1974 was enacted to reconstitute and reorganize the university for improved teaching, research, and administration. It establishes a corporate body with perpetual succession, defining its powers to award degrees, prescribe courses, and manage property. The Act creates various governing bodies including the Senate, Syndicate, and Academic Council, while repealing the West Pakistan University of Engineering and Technology Ordinance, 1961 and the Punjab University of Engineering and Technology Ordinance, 1974.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Finance (Punjab Amendment) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the West Pakistan Finance Act, 1964, in its application to the Province of the Punjab.
repeals: The West Pakistan Finance (Punjab Amendment) Ordinance, 1974
metadata.one_line: Amends the West Pakistan Finance Act, 1964 regarding fees in Punjab and repeals a related Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the West Pakistan Finance Act, 1964 as it applies to the Province of the Punjab. Specifically, it substitutes the fee amount from twelve paisa to twenty paisa in certain sections. The Act also repeals the earlier West Pakistan Finance (Punjab Amendment) Ordinance, 1974.

metadata.short_title: Workers' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Workers' Welfare Fund Ordinance, 1971
metadata.one_line: Amends the Workers' Welfare Fund Ordinance, 1971 to establish Provincial Workers' Welfare Boards and substitute 'Federal Government' for 'Central Government'.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Workers' Welfare Fund Ordinance, 1971 to replace references to the Central Government with the Federal Government. It establishes new Workers' Welfare Boards in each province to manage allocated funds and projects. The Act also modifies the composition of the Governing Body and inserts provisions for the constitution, powers, and property holding of these new boards.

metadata.short_title: West Pakistan Arms (Amendment) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the West Pakistan Arms Ordinance, 1965
metadata.one_line: Amends the West Pakistan Arms Ordinance, 1965 to replace 'West Pakistan' with 'Pakistan' and centralize licensing powers.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the West Pakistan Arms Ordinance, 1965 by substituting references to 'West Pakistan' with 'Pakistan' and 'Central Government' with 'Federal Government'. It grants the Federal Government exclusive power to issue licenses for prohibited bore weapons while allowing Provincial Governments to license non-prohibited weapons. The Act also amends specific sections regarding definitions of government authority and omits certain clauses from the original Ordinance.

name: ASSISTANT SETTLEMENT COMMISSIONERS VALIDATION OF ORDERS ACT, 1973

metadata.short_title: The Assistant Settlement Commissioners (Validation of Orders) Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to validate certain orders passed by the Assistant Settlement Commissioners or rendered invalid
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on the twenty-sixth day of March, 1958
amends: The Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1958
metadata.one_line: Validates orders made by Assistant Settlement Commissioners under the Displaced Persons Act, 1958, despite lack of delegated powers.
metadata.summary: This Act validates certain orders passed by Assistant Settlement Commissioners exercising powers under the Chief Settlement Commissioner. It declares these orders validly made and effective as if the powers had been properly delegated to them. The validation applies notwithstanding any conflicting court decrees or provisions in the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1958.

metadata.short_title: The Co-operative Societies (Reforms) Order (Punjab Amendment) Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Co-operative Societies (Reforms) Order, 1972 (P. O. No. 9 of 1972), in its application to the Province of the Punjab.

amends: The Co-operative Societies (Reforms) Order, 1972 (P. O. No. 9 of 1972)

The Co operative Societies (Reforms) Order (Punjab Amendment) Ordinance, 1973 (Panjab Ordinance No. III of 1973)

metadata.summary: This Act amends the application of the Co-operative Societies (Reforms) Order, 1972 to the Province of Punjab. It substitutes specific figures in Article 5 regarding committee member limits and introduces new clauses for managing societies when committees are superseded by an administrator appointed by the Registrar. The Act also repeals two previous ordinances concerning the same subject matter.

metadata.short_title: The Co-operative Societies (Reforms) Order (Punjab Amendment) Ordinance, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Co-operative Societies (Reforms) Order, 1972, in its application to the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from the 21st day of April, 1972
metadata.parent_law: Co-operative Societies (Reforms) Order, 1972
metadata.one_line: Amends the Co-operative Societies (Reforms) Order, 1972 regarding committee supersession and elections in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Co-operative Societies (Reforms) Order, 1972 specifically for its application to the Province of the Punjab. It substitutes clauses concerning the management of societies when a committee is superseded due to member vacancies exceeding one-third. The amendment mandates that an administrator appointed by the Registrar shall manage affairs until new members are elected between December 1, 1972, and February 28, 1973.

name: CO-OPERATIVE SOCIETIES (REFORMS) ORDER (PUNJAB SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1973

metadata.short_title: The Co-operative Societies (Reforms) Order (Punjab Second Amendment) Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Co-operative Societies (Reforms) Order, 1972 in its application to the Province of the Punjab.
metadata.parent_law: The Co-operative Societies (Reforms) Order, 1972
metadata.one_line: Amends the Co-operative Societies (Reforms) Order, 1972 regarding election dates and rights in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Co-operative Societies (Reforms) Order, 1972 specifically for its application to the Province of the Punjab. It substitutes specific date ranges related to elections within the Order and clarifies that no rights accrued from previous election proceedings are deemed ineffective upon this Act's commencement. The legislation was passed by the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab and received assent on March 24, 1973.

metadata.administering_body: Ministry of Law and Parliamentary Affairs

metadata.summary: This Order was made by the President on May 17, 1973, pursuant to Article 279 of the Interim Constitution. It amends Article 246 by omitting paragraph (a) of clause (1) and clauses (4) and (5). The Order came into force immediately upon publication.

metadata.summary: This Order amends Article 201 of the Interim Constitution of Pakistan to clarify the qualifications for Supreme Court judges. Specifically, it substitutes text in clause (3)(a) to include members of the Defence Services and persons subject to laws relating to those services. The amendment was made by the President on July 2, 1973, and came into force immediately.

metadata.summary: This Order amends Article 56 of the Interim Constitution of Pakistan. It substitutes the titles 'Chief of Staff of the Pakistan Army', 'Navy', and 'Air Force' with 'Chief of the Army Staff', 'Naval Staff', and 'Air Staff' respectively. The amendment is deemed to have taken effect from April 21, 1972, though promulgated in June 1973.

name: CONSTITUTION OF THE ISLAMIC REPLIC OF PAKISTAN PART-I

metadata.short_title: The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan and to define its fundamental rights, principles of policy, structure of government, and legislative lists.
repeals: The Constitution of Pakistan, 1956
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Islamic Republic of Pakistan and defines its fundamental rights, government structure, and legislative powers.
metadata.summary: This document establishes the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, enacted by the National Assembly on April 10, 1973, and authenticated by the President on April 12, 1973. It outlines the fundamental rights of citizens, principles of policy, structure of the federation including the President, Parliament, and Federal Government, as well as provincial assemblies and governments. The Constitution defines legislative lists for the Federation and Concurrent List, financial procedures, and transitional provisions to adapt existing laws.

name: CONSTITUTION OF THE ISLAMIC REPLIC OF PAKISTAN PART-III

metadata.short_title: The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan and to define its fundamental rights, structure, and functions.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the framework for the Islamic Republic of Pakistan including its courts, assemblies, and fundamental rights.
metadata.summary: This document establishes the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, defining the structure of the Supreme Court and High Courts. It outlines procedures for elections to the National Assembly and Senate, including timelines for filling vacancies. The text also validates actions taken during Martial Law between 1969 and 1971 and sets conditions for emergency proclamations.

name: CONSTITUTION OF THE ISLAMIC REPLIC OF PAKISTAN PART-IV

metadata.short_title: The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan and to define its structure, powers, and functions.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the structure of the first National Assembly, Senate, and Provincial Assemblies under the 1973 Constitution.
metadata.summary: This document outlines the composition, term of office, and qualifications for members of the first National Assembly, Senate, and Provincial Assemblies under the new Constitution. It details procedures for filling casual vacancies, taking oaths of office, and the vesting of property between the Federal Government and Provincial Governments. Additionally, it lists regulations that cannot be altered without the President's sanction.

metadata.short_title: The Constitution Seventh Amendment Order, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Order to amend the Constitution of Pakistan by substituting a proviso in Article 9 regarding preventive detention.
amends: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan
key_definitions: Constitution (Interim Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan)
metadata.one_line: Amends Article 9 of the Interim Constitution to exclude persons detained under preventive detention laws from its application.
metadata.summary: This Order amends Article 9 of the Interim Constitution of Pakistan by adding a proviso. The amendment ensures that the clause regarding equality before the law does not apply to persons arrested or detained under any law providing for preventive detention prior to the commencement of this Order. It was promulgated by the President on April 12, 1973, and came into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: The Constitution Tenth Amendment Order, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Order to amend Article 109 of the Constitution and insert a new Article 131A regarding budgetary provisions.
key_definitions: Constitution (Interim Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan)
metadata.administering_body: Ministry of Law and Parliamentary Affairs
metadata.one_line: Amends the Constitution to insert Article 131A on budgetary provisions when Provincial Assemblies are not in session.
metadata.summary: This Order amends the Constitution by omitting clause (1) of Article 109 and inserting a new Article 131A. The new article empowers the Governor to prepare an Annual Budget Statement and schedule of authorised expenditure for the financial year ending June 30, 1974, when the Provincial Assembly is not in session. It also authorizes the withdrawal of moneys from the Provincial Consolidated Fund for necessary expenditures over and above the authorized limit.

metadata.short_title: The Constitution Thirteenth Amendment Order, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Order to amend the Fourth Schedule to the Constitution of Pakistan by substituting entries in the Provincial and Concurrent Legislative Lists.
metadata.parent_law: Constitution
metadata.administering_body: Ministry of Law and Parliamentary Affairs
metadata.one_line: Amends the Constitution's Fourth Schedule to update legislative lists regarding land reforms.
metadata.summary: This Order amends the Fourth Schedule to the Constitution of Pakistan by substituting specific entries in the Provincial and Concurrent Legislative Lists. It updates references to various Land Reforms Regulations, including those for Baluchistan, Dir, and Swat. The Order comes into force immediately and is deemed to have taken effect from April 21, 1972.

metadata.short_title: The Constitution Twelfth Amendment Order, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Order to amend the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan by inserting a proviso in Article 61 and amending the Fourth Schedule.
amends: The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan
metadata.administering_body: Ministry of Law and Parliamentary Affairs
metadata.one_line: Amends the Constitution to include Land Reforms Regulation, 1972 in legislative lists.
metadata.summary: This Order amends the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan by inserting a proviso into Article 61. It substitutes specific wording in entry 20 of the Provincial Legislative List within the Fourth Schedule regarding land reforms. Additionally, it adds a new entry to part II of the Concurrent Legislative List concerning the Land Reforms Regulation, 1972.

metadata.short_title: Federal Security Force Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the constitution and regulation of the Federal Security Force
repeals: Federal Security Force Ordinance, 1973 (X of 1973)
metadata.one_line: This Act constitutes and regulates the Federal Security Force to assist civil administration in maintaining law and order.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the constitution, regulation, and maintenance of the Federal Security Force. It applies to all members and officers wherever they serve and comes into force immediately. The Force assists the civil administration in maintaining law and order during large-scale unlawful demonstrations or serious breaches of law and order, as well as assisting the Police in dealing with dangerous criminals, carrying out road patrols, traffic checks, and checking illicit traffic. The Act defines various terms related to the Force, outlines the appointment of officers from the Armed Forces, Civil Armed Forces, or Police Service, and details the recruitment process involving a recruiting roll and affirmation of allegiance.

name: GREATER LAHORE WATER SUPPLY, SEWERAGE AND DRAINAGE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1973

metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Greater Lahore Water Supply, Sewerage and Drainage Ordinance, 1967. It adds a new paragraph defining 'Regulations' and introduces Section 9-A to empower the Trust to make regulations regarding material, accounts, and procedures. The Act also repeals the Greater Lahore Water Supply, Sewerage and Drainage (Amendment) Ordinance, 1973.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Land Reforms Regulation, 1972 to regulate land transfers by gift, particularly concerning heirs and widowed sisters. It grants additional land possession rights to owners of agricultural tractors or tubewells installed before specific dates. The Act also modifies provisions regarding the partition of joint holdings and defines terms like 'civil service' and 'grantee of land'. Finally, it repeals the Land Reforms (Punjab Amendment) Ordinance, 1972.

metadata.short_title: The Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1973

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Land Reforms Regulation, 1972 to further regulate land reforms in Pakistan. It establishes the Federal Land Commission with specific powers to assist the Federal Government and coordinate work across provinces. The Act also substitutes text regarding revisional powers of the Federal Government and defines family members for legal purposes.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the application of Martial Law Regulation No. 118 specifically to the Province of the Punjab. It deletes specific paragraphs from the original regulation and substitutes new text concerning the rights and assets of privately managed colleges or schools vested in the Provincial Government. The Act also repeals the Punjab Ordinances Temporary Enactment Act, 1973, to the extent that it enacted provisions of the related Ordinance.

metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Mines Act, 1923 to improve conditions for mine workers. It introduces provisions for canteens, shelters, and first-aid rooms in mines employing over one hundred persons. The Act also strengthens secrecy regarding complaint sources and extends the powers of Magistrates to impose higher fines. Additionally, it repeals the earlier Mines (Amendment) Ordinance, 1973.

It grants the Administrator powers to dispose of rights, liabilities, properties, and assets of the Authority and discharge them as directed by the Government. Additionally, it allows the Administrator to write off losses with administrative powers similar to those given to the Government for larger losses.

metadata.short_title: Pakistan Citizenship (Second Amendment) Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Pakistan Citizenship Act, 1951
metadata.one_line: Amends the Pakistan Citizenship Act, 1951 to grant citizenship to persons migrated from Jammu and Kashmir.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Pakistan Citizenship Act, 1951 by inserting a new section 14B. The amendment grants citizenship status to persons who migrated from the State of Jammu and Kashmir with the intention of residing there, pending a final determination of the relationship between Pakistan and that State. It applies to the whole of Pakistan and came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab Privileges Act, 1972. The Multan Improvement Trust is empowered to allot sites, determine prices, and enforce construction rules, with penalties for contravention.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Acquisition of Land (Housing) Act, 1973 to redefine 'Housing Scheme' and introduce new provisions for land acquisition in kachi abadi areas. It limits land owners in such areas to one developed site in lieu of compensation, with the balance payable via cash, bonds, or annuities over twenty years. The Act also repeals Punjab Ordinance No. VI of 1973 and comes into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Acquisition of Land (Housing) (Amendment) Act, 1973

It allows compensation to be paid partly via developed sites or cash bonds over twenty years, with specific exceptions for health and education facilities. The Act also repeals Punjab Ordinance No. VI of 1973.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Acquisition of Land (Housing) Act, 1973 to redefine 'Housing Scheme' to include specific residential facilities and utility services. It also introduces a restriction in Section 11 limiting land owners to one developed site for katchi abadi improvement projects, with remaining compensation payable via cash or bonds over twenty years. The legislation was promulgated by the Governor of Punjab under emergency powers because the Provincial Assembly was not in session.

It includes autonomous bodies, Peoples Local Councils, and Town Improvement Trusts within this definition for undertaking housing schemes. The Act stipulates that these organizations must comply with government directions regarding housing implementation or face takeover of their schemes by the Government.

The amendment changes punctuation and adds a provision allowing the Government to declare any other organization as an 'Official Development Organization' through a notification in the official Gazette. metadata.short_title: The Punjab Acquisition of Land (Housing) Act, 1973

metadata.one_line: Provides for the acquisition of land in Punjab for housing schemes and related matters.
metadata.summary: This Act facilitates the acquisition of land within the Province of Punjab specifically for housing schemes in both urban and rural areas. It outlines the powers of the Deputy Commissioner to survey land, determine compensation through agreement or Collector's award, and manage public notices. The legislation also defines key terms such as 'housing scheme' and 'Official Development Agency', repeals the corresponding 1973 Ordinance, and validates actions taken under that ordinance prior to this Act's commencement.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Acquisition of Land (Housing) Ordinance, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for acquisition of land for housing schemes in the Province and for matters incidental thereto.
metadata.one_line: Provides for acquisition of land in Punjab for housing schemes and related matters.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance empowers the Government of the Punjab to acquire land within the province for approved housing schemes in both urban and rural areas. It defines key terms such as 'housing scheme' and 'Official Development Agency', outlines procedures for public notice and survey, and establishes the powers of the Collector and Deputy Commissioner regarding compensation and inquiries. The Ordinance applies immediately upon promulgation and exempts awards made under it from stamp duty.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Administrative Tribunals Ordinance, 1973

metadata.one_line: Establishes Administrative Tribunals in Punjab to handle civil servants' service matters and appeals.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes Administrative Tribunals within the Province of Punjab to exercise exclusive jurisdiction over terms, conditions, and disciplinary matters regarding civil servants. It defines the composition of these tribunals, including a Chairman and two members with specific experience requirements. The document outlines the process for filing appeals against departmental orders, specifying time limits and exceptions for certain types of decisions like promotions or penalties other than dismissal. Additionally, it repeals the previous Punjab Civil Services (Appellate Tribunals) Ordinance, 1970, transferring pending cases to the new tribunals.

name: PUNJAB AGRICULTURAL DEVELOPMENT AND SUPPLIES CORPORATION ACT, 1973

subjects: West Pakistan Agricultural Development Corporation dissolution
establishes: Punjab Agricultural Development and Supplies Corporation
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Agricultural Development and Supplies Corporation to increase agricultural production in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Agricultural Development and Supplies Corporation within the Province of the Punjab. Its primary purpose is to increase agricultural production by succeeding to the business, projects, undertakings, and properties of the Supply Wing of the defunct West Pakistan Agricultural Development Corporation following its dissolution. The Act defines the Corporation as a body corporate with perpetual succession, outlines the composition of its Board including government officials and non-official members, and provides for the transfer of employees and liabilities from the former corporation to the new entity.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Essential Articles (Control) Act, 1973

metadata.summary: This Act regulates the production, acquisition, distribution, prices, storage, and movement of essential articles in the Province of the Punjab. It empowers the Government to issue notified orders to control supply, fix prices, require licenses, and collect information for public interest. The Act applies to a wide range of goods including food items, construction materials, vehicles, and medicines, remaining in force for ten years.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Essential Articles (Control) Ordinance, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for and regulate production, acquisition, supply, prices, distribution, keeping, disposal, storage, movement, transportation of, and trade and commerce in certain essential articles in the Province of the Punjab.

metadata.summary: The Punjab Essential Articles (Control) Ordinance, 1973 was promulgated by the Governor to control the production, supply, and distribution of essential articles in the Province of Punjab. It empowers the Government to issue orders regulating prices, licensing, stock holding, and prohibiting detrimental transactions for a period of three years. The Ordinance applies to the whole of Punjab and includes a schedule listing specific essential articles such as iron, steel, cement, vehicles, drugs, and food items.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Fertilizers (Control) Order, 1973
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab

metadata.summary: The Punjab Fertilizers (Control) Order, 1973 regulates the business of selling, importing, and producing fertilizers within the Province of Punjab. It empowers a Controller to specify dealers, fix maximum prices, limit stock quantities, and require detailed information on imports and production costs. The Order also grants powers for inspection, seizure of contraband, and exemptions for government purchases.

It sets specific tax amounts per ticket for cinema houses and race courses based on ticket value. The Act also repeals the previous Punjab Flood Relief Cess Ordinance, 1973.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Finance (Amendment) Ordinance, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Finance Act, 1973.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Finance Act, 1973 to adjust fee structures and conditions for payment. It applies to the whole of the Punjab and comes into force immediately upon promulgation by the Governor. The amendment specifies new amounts for fees paid within prescribed periods and introduces provisions regarding sufficient cause for failure to pay.

metadata.summary: This document establishes the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, enacted by the National Assembly on April 10, 1973. It outlines the fundamental rights of citizens, the structure of federal and provincial governments, and the distribution of legislative powers between them. The Constitution also provides for the establishment of various institutions, including the Supreme Court, High Courts, and the Council of Common Interests.

The legislation also explicitly repeals the Punjab Finance (Amendment) Ordinance, 1973.

It amends several existing statutes including those related to agricultural income tax, motor vehicles, urban property tax, court fees, and family courts. The legislation establishes new rates for cinema taxes, modifies vehicle taxation schedules, adjusts property tax exemptions, and sets specific fees for cotton factory licences and operations.

The Board consists of a Chairman, Directors nominated by the Government, and a Managing Director appointed to serve as the chief executive officer. It applies to industries listed in the Schedule, including cotton textiles, sugar, rice milling, flour milling, and vegetable oil production.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Industrial Development Board Ordinance, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of an Industrial Development Board in Punjab.
