It applies to the provinces of Punjab, Sind, and North-West Frontier (formerly NWFP). The funds are appropriated for various services including irrigation, administration, justice, health, and debt services as detailed in the Schedule.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Finance Ordinance, 1960

metadata.summary: The West Pakistan Finance Ordinance, 1960 was promulgated to continue and enhance specific taxes within the Province of West Pakistan. It imposes surcharges on land revenue and agricultural income-tax in designated districts, increases stamp duties, levies taxes on cinemas and professionals, and introduces tolls on freight transported by road. Additionally, it establishes a development cess on lands in the province and grants powers to amend related Acts or make rules for tax collection.

name: WEST PAKISTAN GOVERNMENT EDUCATIONAL AND TRAINING INSTITUTION ORDINANCE, 1960

metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes Boards of Governors to manage and control Government Educational and Training Institutions in West Pakistan. The Board is a body corporate with powers to hold property, enter contracts, and employ staff. It consists of up to nine members appointed by the Governor, including an official Chairman. The Ordinance outlines the composition of the Board, its financial management through a 'Board Fund', accounting requirements, and the power to make regulations for its functioning.

name: WEST PAKISTAN HORSE-RACE BETTING TAX (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1960

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the West Pakistan Horse-race Betting Tax Act, 1958 to adjust tax levies on backers and introduce new operational rules for book-makers. It empowers the Government to set specific times and places for betting, mandate cheque payments for winnings, and require lists of credit bets to be supplied to a prescribed authority. The changes are implemented through notifications in the Official Gazette.

name: WEST PAKISTAN HISTORICAL MOSQUES FUND CESS ORDINANCE, 1960

metadata.one_line: This Ordinance imposes a cess on land revenue and urban property tax to fund the repair and maintenance of historical mosques in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The West Pakistan Historical Mosques Fund Cess Ordinance, 1960 establishes a mechanism to raise funds for the repair, maintenance, and endowment of historically significant mosques. It imposes a specific cess on land revenue and urban immovable property tax payable by Muslims within the province. The collected funds are placed in a dedicated fund under government control, which can also receive grants and donations. These resources are utilized for paying salaries to officers employed under the Ordinance and covering the costs of repairing and maintaining historical mosques.

It empowers the Government to arrest and detain individuals suspected of acting prejudicially to public safety, including those involved in black-marketing or smuggling. The document also grants authorities power to prohibit specific publications and repeals several earlier Public Safety Acts from various provinces.

The document defines key terms such as 'loan', 'interest', and 'money-lender' while excluding certain transactions like bank deposits or loans between traders in the regular course of business. It also repeals several earlier enactments related to money-lenders and debt relief across different provinces.

metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the development of Kalri Lake area in Thatta District of West Pakistan.

metadata.max_penalty: fine not exceeding five hundred rupees for every failure, and a further fine extending to fifty rupees per day for continuing breach
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance establishes a Board to develop the Kalri Lake area in Thatta District, West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the speedy and coordinated development of the Kalri Lake area in Thatta District of West Pakistan. It constitutes a Board called 'The Kalri Lake Development Board' with five members, including government officials and a non-official member, to manage the lake's improvement and expansion. The Board is empowered to frame schemes, control land usage, recover dues as land revenue arrears, and impose fines for non-compliance with its requisitions.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab University (West Pakistan Amendment) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab University Act of 1954.
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab University Act, 1954
key_definitions: principal Act (The Punjab University Act of 1954)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab University Act, 1954 by substituting 'West Pakistan' for 'Punjab' in specific sections.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab University Act of 1954 to reflect the administrative changes following the Presidential Proclamation of October 7, 1958. It substitutes the word 'Punjab' with 'West Pakistan' in Section 16 regarding A-Ea-officio Fellows and Section 21 concerning the Board of Secondary Education. Additionally, it adds a new clause to Section 21 to include the Chairman of the Board of Secondary Education, Lahore.

name: SIND EXCISE LAWS (WEST PAKISTAN AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The Sind Excise Laws (West Pakistan Amendment) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Abkari Act, 1878, and the Sind Consumption of Intoxicants Restriction Act, 1940, for the purpose of including the District of Khairpur within their scope.
metadata.territorial_extent: the Districts of Dadu, Hyderabad, Tharparkar, Upper Sind Frontier, Larkana, Nawabshah, Sanghar, Sukkur, Thatta and Khairpur
amends: The Sind Consumption of Intoxicants Restriction Act, 1940
repeals: The Khairpur Abkari Act No. I of 1895
key_definitions: Districts of Dadu, Hyderabad, Tharparkar, Upper Sind Frontier, Larkana, Nawabshah, Sanghar, Sukkur, Thatta and Khairpur
metadata.one_line: Amends Sind Abkari and Intoxicants Restriction Acts to include Khairpur district.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Abkari Act, 1878, and the Sind Consumption of Intoxicants Restriction Act, 1940. Its purpose is to extend the scope of these laws to include the District of Khairpur. It substitutes specific clauses in the amended Acts to list Khairpur alongside other districts within the Province of Sind. Additionally, it repeals the Khairpur Abkari Act No. I of 1895 while preserving all actions and proceedings taken under that repealed Act.

name: SIND ACTS (EXTENSION TO KHAIRPUR DISTRICT) ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The Sind Acts (Extension to Khairpur District) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to extend certain Sind Acts to Khairpur District and to repeal the corresponding and certain other Khairpur Acts.
repeals: Notice to Police of Suspicious Characters Act, 1898
The Khairpur Tonga Act, 1905
The Khairpur Bullock Cart Act, 1929
The Khairpur State Irrigation Act, 1929
The Khairpur State Courts Act, 1941
The Khairpur State Primary Education Act, 1945
The Khairpur State Municipal Act, 1947
The Khairpur State Small Towns Act, 1947
The Hurs Control Act, 1947
The Khairpur Control of Disorderly Persons Act, 1953
The Khairpur Essential Articles (Control of Price, Movement and Anti-hoarding) Act, 1954
metadata.one_line: Extends specific Sind Acts to Khairpur District and repeals corresponding local Khairpur legislation.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance extends various existing Sind Acts to the Khairpur District. It simultaneously repeals a list of corresponding local acts previously in force in Khairpur. The extension covers areas such as irrigation, municipal administration, courts, education, and public conveyances.

name: SIND LAND REVENUE CODE (WEST PAKISTAN AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The Sind Land Revenue Code (West Pakistan Amendment) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Land Revenue Code, 1879.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Land Revenue Code, 1879 by inserting a new section regarding the appointment of an Additional Commissioner in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Land Revenue Code, 1879 to address administrative needs within West Pakistan. It inserts a new section (5-A) that empowers the Provincial Government to appoint an Additional Commissioner. This official is authorized to discharge all or any of the functions of the Commissioner under the Act.

metadata.short_title: The Sind University (West Pakistan Amendment) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind University Act, 1947.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind University Act, 1947 regarding Vice-Chancellor appointment and tenure in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind University Act, 1947 to modify provisions concerning the Vice-Chancellor. It stipulates that the Vice-Chancellor is appointed by the Chancellor on terms determined by the Chancellor. The amendment also sets a three-year term of office for the Vice-Chancellor and outlines arrangements for temporary vacancies due to leave or illness.

metadata.short_title: The Thal Development (West Pakistan Amendment) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Thal Development Act, 1949.
metadata.parent_law: The Thal Development Act, 1949
metadata.one_line: Amends the Thal Development Act, 1949 by deleting Section 7 and modifying Section 9 regarding member removal.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Thal Development Act, 1949 to facilitate changes in its provisions. It deletes Section 7 of the principal Act and modifies Section 9 to allow the Provincial Government to remove any member at any time without assigning a reason. The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of West Pakistan on April 6, 1959.

metadata.short_title: The Stamp (West Pakistan Amendment) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Stamp Act, 1899, in its application to the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan, except the Federal Capital and the Special Areas
repeals: The Sind Finance Act, 1932 (Chapters IV and V)
The Indian Stamp (N.-V.F.P.) (Amendment) Act, 1948
The Stamp (Punjab Amendment) Act, 1954
metadata.one_line: Amends the Stamp Act, 1899 for West Pakistan by replacing Crown references with Government and repealing specific enactments.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the application of the Stamp Act, 1899 to the Province of West Pakistan. It substitutes references to 'Crown' or 'His Majesty' with 'Government' or 'Pakistan' throughout the principal Act and its schedules. Additionally, it repeals specific chapters of the Sind Finance Act, 1932, the Indian Stamp (N.-V.F.P.) (Amendment) Act, 1948, and the Stamp (Punjab Amendment) Act, 1954 to the extent specified.

name: THAL DEVELOPMENT (WEST PAKISTAN SECOND AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The Thal Development (West Pakistan Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Thal Development Act, 1949.
metadata.parent_law: The Thal Development Act, 1949
metadata.one_line: Amends the Thal Development Act, 1949 by allowing the Provincial Government to delegate powers to subordinate authorities.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Thal Development Act, 1949 to facilitate the delegation of powers, duties, and functions. It empowers the Provincial Government of West Pakistan to delegate any of its functions under the Act to any authority subordinate to it via notification. The amendment is inserted into Chapter X of the Act after section 82 as a new section 83.

name: WEST PAKISTAN (ADAPTATION AND REPEAL OF LAWS) (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan (Adaptation and Repeal of Laws) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the West Pakistan (Adaptation and Repeal of Laws) Act, 1957.
metadata.parent_law: The West Pakistan (Adaptation and Repeal of Laws) Act, 1957
amends: The West Pakistan (Adaptation and Repeal of Laws) Act, 1957
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1957 Adaptation Act regarding Baluchistan States Union functions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the West Pakistan (Adaptation and Repeal of Laws) Act, 1957. It specifically substitutes an entry in Schedule II relating to the Baluchistan States Union. The substitution defines the relevant authority as the Provincial Government or any officer empowered by the Governor to perform Wazir-i-Azam functions, excluding judicial court matters.

name: WEST PAKISTAN (GWADUR) EXTENSION OF LAWS ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan (Gwadur) Extension of Laws Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to extend certain laws to Gwadur
metadata.territorial_extent: Gwadur (those territories which were included in Pakistan on the 8th day of September, 1958)
key_definitions: Gwadur (those territories which were included in Pakistan on the 8th day of September, 1958)
metadata.one_line: Extends specific maritime and land revenue laws to the territory of Gwadur.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance extends the provisions of various existing enactments to the territory of Gwadur, which was included in Pakistan on September 8, 1958. It applies laws related to ship registration, ports, inland vessels, merchant shipping, coasting vessels, and land revenue. Specific modifications are made to the Coasting Vessels Act, 1938, to include Gwadur within its territorial scope.

name: WEST PAKISTAN AGRICULTURAL BANK (RECOVERY OF DUES) ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Agricultural Bank (Recovery of Dues) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide facilities to the Agricultural Bank for recovering its dues.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan, except the Federal Capital and the Special Areas
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance empowers the Agricultural Bank to recover dues by pledging, mortgaging, hypothecating, or assigning property.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides facilities for the West Pakistan Agricultural Bank to recover its dues. It authorizes agriculturists and co-operative societies to pledge, mortgage, hypothecate, or assign movable or immovable property to secure loans advanced under the Agricultural Bank Act, 1957. The Bank is empowered to dispose of such pledged property to recover dues, overriding any conflicting laws.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Agricultural Pests Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to the eradication of agricultural pests in the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan, except the Federal Capital and the Special Areas
metadata.commencement: on such date or dates as Government may, by notification, specify
repeals: The North-West Frontier Province Sugarcane Savings Act, 1950
The Sind Boll Worm Act, 1947
The North-West Frontier Province Fruit-Fly (Preventive Measures) Act, 1950
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates laws on eradicating agricultural pests in West Pakistan, defining powers for inspectors and occupiers.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends and consolidates the law regarding the eradication of agricultural pests in the Province of West Pakistan. It defines key terms such as 'agricultural pest' and 'occupier', and grants the Government power to prescribe preventive measures and prohibit certain cultivation methods or crop sales. Inspectors are empowered to enter land, seize infested crops, and enforce compliance, with costs recoverable as arrears of land revenue if not paid by the occupier.

name: WEST PAKISTAN APPROPRIATION (AMENDMENT AND EXTENSION) ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Appropriation (Amendment and Extension) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the West Pakistan Appropriation Act, 1958
metadata.parent_law: The West Pakistan Appropriation Act, 1958
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1958 Appropriation Act to extend funds for April-June 1959 in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the West Pakistan Appropriation Act, 1958 to prevent the lapse of unappropriated sums as of March 31, 1959. It allows these funds to be used for services listed in the Schedule during a transitional period from April 1, 1959, to June 30, 1959. The measure bridges the gap between the old financial year ending March 31, 1959, and the new financial year beginning July 1, 1959.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Appropriation (Second) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to authorise payment and appropriation of certain sums out of the Provincial Consolidated Fund for the service of the financial year 1959-60.
metadata.one_line: Authorizes payment and appropriation of sums from the Provincial Consolidated Fund for West Pakistan's financial year 1959-60.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance authorizes the payment and appropriation of specific sums from the Provincial Consolidated Fund of West Pakistan. It covers various services and purposes including administration, justice, police, education, health, agriculture, and capital works for the financial year 1959-60. The total amount authorized amounts to approximately two hundred and forty-four crores rupees, detailed in the attached Schedule.

name: WEST PAKISTAN CONTEMPT OF COURTS (REPEAL) ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Contempt of Courts (Repeal) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal the North-West Frontier Province Contempt of Courts Act, 1938, the Khairpur State Contempt of Courts Act, 1950 and the Contempt of Courts (Sind Amendment) Act, 1951.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government of West Pakistan may by notification appoint
repeals: North-West Frontier Province Contempt of Courts Act, 1938
Khairpur State Contempt of Courts Act, 1950
Contempt of Courts (Sind Amendment) Act, 1951
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance repeals three specific Contempt of Courts Acts applicable in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of West Pakistan to repeal existing contempt of courts legislation. It specifically targets the North-West Frontier Province Contempt of Courts Act, 1938, the Khairpur State Contempt of Courts Act, 1950, and the Contempt of Courts (Sind Amendment) Act, 1951. The Ordinance came into force on a date to be appointed by the Government of West Pakistan via notification.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Appropriation Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to authorise payment and appropriation of certain sums out of the Provincial Consolidated Fund for the service of the period of three months ending on the 30th June, 1959.
metadata.one_line: Authorizes payment and appropriation of sums from the Provincial Consolidated Fund for services in West Pakistan until June 30, 1959.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance authorizes the Governor of West Pakistan to pay and appropriate specific sums from the Provincial Consolidated Fund. The funds cover various charges including capital outlay, working expenses, public debt reduction, and administrative services for a three-month period ending on June 30, 1959. Detailed schedules list authorized amounts for sectors such as agriculture, education, health, police, and civil works.

name: WEST PAKISTAN DETERMINATION OF LAND REVENUE AND WATER RATE ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Determination of Land Revenue and Water Rate Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the separation of land revenue from water rate and re-assessment of land revenue and water rate.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of West Pakistan, except the Federal Capital and the Special Areas
metadata.commencement: from such date or such season... as may be specified in notification
metadata.one_line: Separates land revenue from water rate and provides for their re-assessment in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated to separate the composite charge of land revenue and water rate levied in certain areas of West Pakistan. It empowers the Government to issue notifications allowing authorities to separate these charges and reassess them as deemed convenient. The provisions apply to the whole of West Pakistan, excluding the Federal Capital and Special Areas, with specific rules becoming payable from dates specified in official notifications.

name: WEST PAKISTAN DISCONTINUANCE OF SIND MOSQUE AND HOSTELS FUND ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Discontinuance of Sind Mosque and Hostels Fund Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the discontinuance of the Sind Mosque and Hostels Fund established under the Sind Mosque and Hostels Fund Cess Act, 1951.
repeals: The Sind Mosque and Hostels Fund Cess Act, 1951
metadata.one_line: Discontinues the Sind Mosque and Hostels Fund established under the 1951 Act and utilizes its balance for maintaining historical mosques in former Sind.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the discontinuance of the Sind Mosque and Hostels Fund, which was previously established under the Sind Mosque and Hostels Fund Cess Act, 1951. It repeals the 1951 Act and directs that the remaining balance of the fund be utilized for the repair and maintenance of historically significant mosques in the former Province of Sind as specified by the Provincial Government. The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor-General on July 22, 1959, following a Presidential Proclamation from October 7, 1958.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Finance Act (Amendment) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the West Pakistan Finance Act, 1958.
metadata.parent_law: The West Pakistan Finance Act, 1958
metadata.one_line: Amends the West Pakistan Finance Act, 1958 by omitting section 6.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the West Pakistan Finance Act, 1958. It omits section 6 of that Act. The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of West Pakistan on February 12, 1959, pursuant to the Presidential Proclamation of October 7, 1958.

name: WEST PAKISTAN FINANCE ACT (SECOND AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Finance Act (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the West Pakistan Finance Act, 1958.
metadata.parent_law: The West Pakistan Finance Act, 1958
metadata.one_line: Amends the West Pakistan Finance Act, 1958 to adjust tax dates and introduce new levies on cinemas and professionals.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the West Pakistan Finance Act, 1958 by changing specific dates in sections 5, 8, 11, and 15. It introduces a new section 17-A imposing taxes on cinema owners and various professional classes including legal practitioners and clearing agents. Additionally, it establishes surcharges on motor vehicles used for goods transport, passenger hire, or private use within West Pakistan.

name: WEST PAKISTAN CONTROL OF GOONDAS ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Control of Goondas Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to consolidate and amend the law relating to the control of disorderly in the persons commonly known as goondas in the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan except the Federal Capital and the Special Districts
repeals: The Punjab Control of Goondas Act, 1951
The Sind Control of Goondas Act, 1952
The Sind Acts (Extension to Khairpur District) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates and amends laws regarding goondas in West Pakistan by establishing tribunals under District Magistrates.
metadata.summary: The West Pakistan Control of Goondas Ordinance, 1959 was promulgated to consolidate and amend the law concerning disorderly persons known as goondas. It establishes Tribunals consisting of District Magistrates or empowered Magistrates to conduct inquiries. The Ordinance grants these Tribunals powers similar to a District Magistrate under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, for issuing summonses, warrants, and compelling witness attendance. It also outlines procedures for arresting goondas, taking bonds with sureties, transferring cases between tribunals, and removing names from the goonda list upon proof of good behavior.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan General Clauses (Amendment) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to further amend the West Pakistan General Clauses Act, 1956.
metadata.parent_law: The West Pakistan General Clauses Act, 1956
amends: The West Pakistan General Clauses Act, 1956
metadata.one_line: Amends the definition of 'financial year' in the West Pakistan General Clauses Act, 1956.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the West Pakistan General Clauses Act, 1956 by substituting clause (25) of section 2. It redefines the term 'financial year' to cover different periods before and after April 1, 1959. The amendment was promulgated by the Governor of West Pakistan on November 3, 1959.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Finance Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for continuance and enhancement of certain taxes in West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the Province of West Pakistan, except the Federal Capital and the Special Areas
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance continues and enhances various taxes including land revenue, agricultural income-tax, stamp duty, cinema tax, and betting tax in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The West Pakistan Finance Ordinance, 1959 was promulgated to continue certain existing taxes and enhance others within the Province of West Pakistan. It imposes surcharges on land revenue and agricultural income-tax in specific districts, amends stamp duty rates for acknowledgements and receipts, and levies new taxes on cinemas, betting, legal practitioners, and motor vehicles. The Ordinance applies to the whole of West Pakistan except the Federal Capital and Special Areas, with specific sections extending only to designated districts.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Goats (Restriction) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to restrict the number of goats in West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan, except the Federal Capital and the Special Areas
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to six months or fine up to five hundred rupees or both, plus forfeiture of the goat
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance restricts grazing and keeping of goats in West Pakistan and regulates their movement and slaughter.
metadata.summary: The West Pakistan Goats (Restriction) Ordinance, 1959 was promulgated to restrict the number of goats in the Province of West Pakistan. It grants the Government power to declare areas where grazing or keeping goats becomes unlawful after specified periods following notification. The Ordinance also regulates the movement and slaughter of goats, including setting limits on the proportion of goats to sheep that may be slaughtered. Contravention of its provisions attracts imprisonment up to six months, a fine up to five hundred rupees, or both, along with forfeiture of the goat.

name: WEST PAKISTAN HINDU WOMEN'S RIGHTS TO AGRICULTURAL LAND ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Hindu Women's Rights to Agricultural Land Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to consolidate rights to agricultural land in the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan except the Federal Capital
repeals: Women's Rights to Property Act, 1942 (N.W.F.P.)
Women's Rights to Property Act, 1943 (Sind)
metadata.one_line: Consolidates rights to agricultural land for Hindu women in West Pakistan and repeals earlier provincial acts.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance consolidates the rights of Hindu women to agricultural land in the Province of West Pakistan. It applies where a Hindu dies intestate regarding agricultural land, ensuring widows receive shares equivalent to sons under specific schools of Hindu law. The document repeals conflicting enactments from North-West Frontier Province and Sindh while preserving existing tenancy rights.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Juvenile Smoking Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to prevention of smoking of tobacco by juveniles in the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan, except the Federal Capital and the Special Areas
repeals: The Punjab Juvenile Smoking Act, 1918
The Punjab Juvenile Smoking Act, 1918 as applicable to the former State of Bahawalpur
The North-West Frontier Province Juvenile Smoking Act, 1933
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to one hundred rupees
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance prevents juveniles from smoking tobacco in West Pakistan and repeals earlier provincial acts.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends and consolidates laws regarding the prevention of juvenile smoking in West Pakistan. It defines key terms such as 'juvenile' (under sixteen years) and 'public place', and prescribes fines for selling or giving tobacco to juveniles. The document also authorizes the seizure and destruction of tobacco found in the hands of a smoking juvenile and repeals three earlier acts from Punjab, Bahawalpur, and NWFP.

name: WEST PAKISTAN LAND DISPOSITIONS (SAVING OF SHAMILAT) ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Land Dispositions (Saving of Shamilat) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for a uniform interpretation of general expressions with regard to disposition of 'Shamilat' lands in the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan except the Federal Capital and the Special Areas
repeals: The Punjab Land Dispositions (Saving of Shamilat) Act, 1951
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance provides uniform interpretation for 'Shamilat' lands in West Pakistan and repeals the 1951 Punjab Act.
metadata.summary: The West Pakistan Land Dispositions (Saving of Shamilat) Ordinance, 1959 was promulgated to provide a uniform interpretation of general expressions regarding the disposition of 'Shamilat' lands in the Province of West Pakistan. It defines 'Shamilat' as land described as such in the Record of Rights and stipulates that such lands are not included in dispositions unless specifically mentioned. The Ordinance applies to the whole of West Pakistan, excluding the Federal Capital and Special Areas, and repeals the Punjab Land Dispositions (Saving of Shamilat) Act, 1951.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Land Utilization Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the utilization of proprietary waste and arable lands for growing food and other crops.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan, except the Federal Capital and the Special Areas
repeals: The Punjab Land Utilization Act, 1954
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance provides for utilizing waste and arable lands in West Pakistan for growing food crops.
metadata.summary: The West Pakistan Land Utilization Ordinance, 1959 was promulgated to utilize proprietary waste and arable lands for growing food and other crops. It empowers the Collector to direct that uncultivated land be brought under cultivation within two years if it has not been cultivated for two consecutive years. The Ordinance outlines procedures for serving orders on interested parties, hearing objections, declaring land for lease, and taking possession of such land.

name: WEST PAKISTAN MOTOR VEHICLES TAXATION (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the West Pakistan Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958.
metadata.parent_law: The West Pakistan Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958
amends: The West Pakistan Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1958 Motor Vehicles Taxation Act to exempt tractors and remove private carriers from the schedule.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the West Pakistan Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958 to adjust tax rates and exemptions. It substitutes provisions in Section 3 regarding lower tax rates for specific vehicle classes and areas. Additionally, it exempts tractors and trailers used for agriculture from the Act's application and omits references to private carriers and Article 4 from the Schedule.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Highways Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to consolidate and amend the law relating to highways in the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan except the Federal Capital
repeals: The West Punjab Highways Act, 1948
The North-West Frontier Province Road Development Prevention Act, 1946
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to fifty rupees
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends the law relating to highways, authorities, and traffic regulation in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance consolidates and amends the laws regarding highways in the Province of West Pakistan. It establishes Highway Authorities responsible for laying out, maintaining, and regulating highways, including provisions for encroachments and vehicle standards. The document also repeals previous enactments related to highways in West Punjab and the North-West Frontier Province.

name: WEST PAKISTAN NATIONAL CALAMITIES (PREVENTION AND RELIEF) (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan National Calamities (Prevention and Relief) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the West Pakistan National Calamities (Prevention and Relief) Act, 1958.
metadata.parent_law: The West Pakistan National Calamities (Prevention and Relief) Act, 1958
amends: The West Pakistan National Calamities (Prevention and Relief) Act, 1958
metadata.one_line: Amends the West Pakistan National Calamities (Prevention and Relief) Act, 1958 by adding a reference to the Khairpur National Calamities Act.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the West Pakistan National Calamities (Prevention and Relief) Act, 1958. It specifically adds a reference to the Khairpur National Calamities (Prevention and Relief) Act, 1954 within Section 12 of the parent Act. The amendment ensures that the Khairpur Act is deemed to have always been part of the referenced list in the 1958 legislation.

metadata.short_title: WEST PAKISTAN RANGERS (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1969
metadata.parent_law: WEST PAKISTAN RANGERS (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1959
metadata.one_line: Amends the West Pakistan Rangers (Amendment) Ordinance, 1959 regarding smuggling prevention and clause structure.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the West Pakistan Rangers (Amendment) Ordinance, 1959. It modifies specific clauses in Section 6 to include co-ordination of Police and civil agencies for preventing smuggling. Additionally, it alters Section 7 by adding words, deleting a clause, and renumbering another, and changes a number in Section 20 from three to six.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Rangers Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to constitute a force called the West Pakistan Rangers for the protection of and maintenance of order in the border areas in the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan except the Federal Capital and the Special Areas
repeals: The West Pakistan Border Police Act, 1958
metadata.one_line: Constitutes the West Pakistan Rangers force for border protection and order maintenance in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the West Pakistan Rangers, a force under the operational control of the Army, to protect borders and maintain order. It defines the roles of the Director-General and Deputy Director-General, outlines recruitment from existing police forces, and grants powers to assist civil police in crime prevention and smuggling detection. The Ordinance also provides for rules regarding pay, conditions of service, and departmental punishments.

metadata.short_title: West Pakistan Nursing Services Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the constitution and functions of a Nursing Services Council for West Pakistan.
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to three hundred rupees
metadata.one_line: Establishes the West Pakistan Nursing Services Council and regulates the registration of nurses, midwives, and health visitors.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the West Pakistan Nursing Services Council to regulate nursing services in West Pakistan. It defines key terms such as 'nurse', 'midwife', and 'dai' based on recognized diplomas or certificates from institutions approved by the Pakistan Nursing Council Act, 1952. The Council is a body corporate with powers to sue, contract, and maintain registers of practitioners. It also outlines the composition of the Council, election procedures, and penalties for false representation regarding registration status.

name: WEST PAKISTAN REQUISITIONING OF IMMOVABLE PROPERTY (TEMPORARY POWERS) (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Requisitioning of Immovable Property (Temporary Powers) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the West Pakistan Requisitioning of Immovable Property (Temporary Powers) Act, 1956.
metadata.parent_law: The West Pakistan Requisitioning of Immovable Property (Temporary Powers) Act, 1956
amends: The West Pakistan Requisitioning of Immovable Property (Temporary Powers) Act, 1956
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1956 Requisitioning Act by substituting references to government officers and offices.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the West Pakistan Requisitioning of Immovable Property (Temporary Powers) Act, 1956. It specifically substitutes the words 'the officers or offices of the Central Government, the Provincial Government or any corporate body established by or under the authority of the Central Government or the Provincial Government' in section 3 of the parent Act. The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of West Pakistan on January 31, 1959.

name: WEST PAKISTAN RICE (RESTRICTIONS ON CULTIVATION) ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Rice (Restrictions on Cultivation) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate the cultivation of rice in the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan except the Federal Capital and the Special Areas
metadata.max_penalty: fine extending to ten times the land revenue assessment chargeable for the crop or simple imprisonment not exceeding six months or both
metadata.one_line: Regulates rice cultivation in West Pakistan to prevent water-logging and salinity damage.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the cultivation of rice in the Province of West Pakistan to check the increase of water-logging and resultant land damage. It empowers the Board of Revenue to impose restrictions on rice cultivation in specified areas, provided cultivators can gather their standing crop before such restrictions take effect. The Ordinance prescribes penalties for contravention, including fines up to ten times the land revenue assessment or imprisonment not exceeding six months, and bars civil courts from entertaining claims regarding actions taken under it in good faith.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Supplementary Appropriation Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to authorise out of the Provincial Consolidated Fund for certain service of the period of fifteen months ending on the 30th day of June, 1959.
metadata.one_line: Authorizes expenditure from the Provincial Consolidated Fund for fifteen months ending June 30, 1959.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance authorizes the payment and appropriation of sums from the Provincial Consolidated Fund for services during a fifteen-month period ending on June 30, 1959. It covers various expenditures including land revenue, provincial excise, police, agriculture, education, health, and public debt charges. The total authorized amount does not exceed Rs. 73,49,27,920, with specific sums allocated to different departments and purposes as detailed in the Schedule.

name: WEST PAKISTAN SURVEY AND RECTANGULATION OF LANDS ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Survey and Rectangulation of Lands Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the survey and rectangulation of lands in the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of West Pakistan except the Federal Capital and Special Areas
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Board of Revenue may direct
establishes: Board of Revenue (implied authority to make rules)
metadata.max_penalty: six months imprisonment or fine up to one thousand rupees or both
key_definitions: West Pakistan Survey and Rectangulation of Lands Ordinance
metadata.one_line: Provides for the survey and rectangulation of lands in West Pakistan with provisions on costs, penalties, and rules.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the survey and rectangulation of lands throughout West Pakistan, excluding the Federal Capital and Special Areas. It empowers the Board of Revenue to direct operations and frame necessary rules while allowing the Provincial Government to remit costs in whole or part. The document establishes penalties for obstructing operations and grants indemnity to public servants acting in good faith, while excluding civil courts from jurisdiction over acts done under it.

name: WEST PAKISTAN TOBACCO VEND ACT (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Tobacco Vend Act (Amendment) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the West Pakistan Tobacco Vend Act, 1958.
metadata.parent_law: The West Pakistan Tobacco Vend Act, 1958
amends: The West Pakistan Tobacco Vend Act, 1958
metadata.one_line: Amends the West Pakistan Tobacco Vend Act, 1958 by inserting powers for authorized persons.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the West Pakistan Tobacco Vend Act, 1958 to expand enforcement capabilities. It inserts a provision allowing any person authorized by the Collector to exercise powers previously restricted to the Collector alone. The amendment applies to the whole of West Pakistan and was promulgated on March 25, 1959.

name: WEST PAKISTAN URBAN IMMOVABLE PROPERTY TAX ACT (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Urban Immovable Property Tax Act (Amendment) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the West Pakistan Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958.
metadata.parent_law: The West Pakistan Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958
amends: The West Pakistan Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958
key_definitions: owner (includes a mortgagee with possession, a lessee in perpetuity and a trustee having possession of a trust property)
buildings and lands (other than those leased in perpetuity, vesting in the Federal Government)
metadata.one_line: Amends the West Pakistan Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958 to expand the definition of owner and tax applicability.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the West Pakistan Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958 to clarify who is considered an 'owner' for tax purposes. It includes mortgagees with possession, lessees in perpetuity, and trustees having possession of trust property within the definition of owner. Additionally, it specifies that tax is due from owners of buildings and lands, excluding those leased in perpetuity to the Federal Government.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Undesirable Companies Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to prohibit the registration of companies for carrying on business for certain undesirable purposes and to provide for the winding up and dissolution of such companies.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan, except the Federal Capital and the Special Areas
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine or with both
metadata.administering_body: Registrar (appointed under section 248 of the Companies Act, 1913)
metadata.one_line: Prohibits registration and operation of companies conducting business for specified undesirable purposes in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance prohibits the registration of companies operating within West Pakistan for specific undesirable purposes, such as schemes involving payments determined by chance or lottery. It mandates the immediate winding up and dissolution of existing undesirable companies upon commencement. The law empowers the registrar to inspect documents, seize assets, and take over management of non-compliant companies, while prescribing criminal penalties including imprisonment and fines for violations.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Usurious Loans Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to consolidate the law relating to usurious loans in the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan except the Federal Capital and the Special Areas
repeals: The Usurious Loans Act, 1918
The Indebtedness Relief of Usurious Loans Act, 1934
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws on usurious loans in West Pakistan and empowers courts to relieve debtors of excessive interest.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance consolidates the law relating to usurious loans in the Province of West Pakistan. It defines key terms such as 'interest' and 'loan' and grants courts powers to reopen transactions, take accounts between parties, and relieve debtors from liability for excessive interest. The Ordinance sets specific thresholds for what constitutes excessive interest based on whether a loan is secured or unsecured and applies to suits instituted after its commencement regarding loans made since 1918.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Vaccination (Amendment) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the West Pakistan Vaccination Ordinance, 1958.
metadata.parent_law: The West Pakistan Vaccination Ordinance, 1958
metadata.one_line: Amends the West Pakistan Vaccination Ordinance, 1958 by adding definitions and modifying sections.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the West Pakistan Vaccination Ordinance, 1958 to update specific definitions and procedural clauses. It adds new definitions for 'prescribed', 'Superintendent of Vaccination', and 'vaccinator' while modifying references to vaccination seasons and appointment authorities. The changes aim to clarify operational terms and administrative procedures within the existing vaccination framework.

name: WEST PAKISTAN URBAN RENT RESTRICTION ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Urban Rent Restriction Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to restrict the limits of increase of urban rent of certain premises within the Province and the eviction of tenants therefrom in the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: all the urban areas in West Pakistan
metadata.commencement: at once for sections 1(4), 1(5) and 19; remaining provisions deemed to have taken effect on the date of expiry of the West Pakistan Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1957
repeals: the Baluchistan Rent Control Regulation, 1945
the North-West Frontier Province House Control Act, 1946
the Bahawalpur State Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1947
the Sind Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1952
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance restricts rent increases and evictions in urban areas of West Pakistan by establishing fair rent controls.
metadata.summary: The West Pakistan Urban Rent Restriction Ordinance, 1959 was promulgated to limit rent increases and prevent the eviction of tenants in urban areas of West Pakistan. It applies to all urban areas within the province except the Capital and Special Areas. The Ordinance establishes a 'Controller', a judicial officer appointed by the Provincial Government, who is responsible for fixing fair rents based on specific factors such as previous rents, construction costs, and rental values. It repeals several earlier rent control laws from Baluchistan, N.W.F.P., Bahawalpur, and Sindh, and deems its provisions to have taken effect upon the expiry of the West Pakistan Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1957.

name: WEST PAKISTAN WATER AND POWER DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the West Pakistan Water and Power Development Authority Act, 1958 to facilitate the transfer of assets and liabilities from the Electricity Department to the Authority. It grants the Authority powers to undertake schemes sponsored by the Central Government or other agencies under specific terms. Additionally, it modifies service conditions for personnel in the Electricity and Irrigation Departments, allowing them to serve under the Authority if required by the Government.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Waqf Properties Ordinance, 1959

metadata.summary: This Ordinance consolidates and amends the law relating to the management of Waqf properties in the Province of West Pakistan. It establishes an Administrator for Waqfs, defines key terms such as 'Waqf property' and 'charitable purposes', and outlines the powers of the Government and Administrator. The document also provides for the framing of rules, the appointment of officers, and the procedure for challenging notifications regarding waqf properties in District Courts.

metadata.short_title: The Boilers (West Pakistan Amendment) Ordinance, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Boilers Act, 1923, in its application to the Province of West Pakistan.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Boilers Act, 1923 specifically for its application to the Province of West Pakistan. It substitutes new definitions for various inspector ranks and updates sections regarding appointments and powers within the provincial government. The amendments clarify the roles of Additional Chief Inspectors and Deputy Chief Inspectors, granting them specific powers directed by the Provincial Government.

metadata.short_title: The Cinematograph (West Pakistan Amendment) Act, 1958

repeals: The Cinematograph (West Pakistan) Ordinance, 1957

metadata.summary: This Act amends and extends the Cinematograph Act, 1918 to apply specifically to the Province of West Pakistan. It substitutes provisions regarding the territorial extent of the Act and adds new sections concerning safety precautions, certificate validity, appeals to the Provincial Government, and suspension of certificates by District Magistrates or the Provincial Government on grounds of law and order. The Act also repeals the Cinematograph (West Pakistan) Ordinance, 1957.

metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Cinematograph Act, 1918, in its application to the Province of West Pakistan.

It substitutes the word 'one-half' with the word 'cone-' in section 7, subsection (1) of the said Act as inserted by the Cinematograph (West Pakistan Amendment) Act, 1958. The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of West Pakistan on December 31, 1958, pursuant to a Proclamation.

name: CITY OF LAHORE CORPORATION (WEST PAKISTAN AMENDMENT) ACT, 1958

metadata.short_title: The City of Lahore Corporation (West Pakistan Amendment) Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the City of Lahore Corporation Act, 1941.

repeals: The City of Lahore Corporation (West Pakistan Amendment) Ordinance, 1958
metadata.one_line: Amends the City of Lahore Corporation Act, 1941 by substituting an Administrative Committee for the Administrator and repealing a related Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the City of Lahore Corporation Act, 1941 to replace the 'Administrator' with an 'Administrative Committee' appointed by the Provincial Government. It details the consequences of supersession, including the vacation of seats, vesting of property in the committee, and the election of a Chairman and Vice-Chairman. The Act also grants the Provincial Government powers to remove members, vary the number of members, or replace the committee entirely.

name: WEST PAKISTAN WILD LIFE PROTECTION ORDINANCE, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Wild Life Protection Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to protection of wild life in the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: West Pakistan, except the Federal Capital and the Special Areas
repeals: the Punjab Wild Birds and Wild Animals Protection Act, 1954
the North-West Frontier Province Wild Birds and Wild Animals Protection Act, 1950
the Sind Wild Birds and Wild Animals Protection Act, 1940
the Bahawalpur State Wild Birds and Wild Animals Protection and Shikar Act, 1945
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates and amends laws protecting wildlife in West Pakistan, establishing licensing and sanctuary systems.
metadata.summary: The West Pakistan Wild Life Protection Ordinance, 1959 was promulgated to amend and consolidate existing laws regarding the protection of wild life in the Province. It establishes a regulatory framework involving Game Wardens and Inspectors who oversee the issuance of licences, permits, and special permits required for possessing, using, or killing specific wild birds and animals. The Ordinance empowers the Government to declare sanctuaries and reserves where killing is prohibited, restricts the import and export of wildlife, and outlines various offences with corresponding penalties. It also repeals several previous provincial acts related to wild bird and animal protection across Punjab, NWFP, Sindh, and Bahawalpur.

name: CITY OF LAHORE CORPORATION (WEST PAKISTAN AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1958

metadata.short_title: The City of Lahore Corporation (West Pakistan Amendment) Ordinance, 1958
metadata.long_title: AN ORDINANCE to amend the City of Lahore Corporation Act, 1941
amends: The City of Lahore Corporation Act, 1941
metadata.one_line: Amends the City of Lahore Corporation Act, 1941 to replace the Corporation with an Administrative Committee under Provincial Government control.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the City of Lahore Corporation Act, 1941 to facilitate immediate action when the Provincial Assembly is not in session. It substitutes the term 'Administrator' with 'Administrative Committee' and outlines the consequences of superseding the Corporation, including the vacation of seats and the vesting of property in the new committee. The Administrative Committee is established as a corporate body subject to the control of the Provincial Government, which holds powers to appoint members, vary their number, or replace the committee entirely.

metadata.short_title: The Industrial Statistics (West Pakistan Amendment) Ordinance, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Industrial Statistics Act, 1942.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Industrial Statistics Act, 1942 to facilitate its application within the Province of West Pakistan. It empowers the Provincial Government to delegate the powers and functions of the statistics authority to any other officer or subordinate authority. Such delegation is subject to conditions specified in directions issued by the Provincial Government.

metadata.short_title: The Land Acquisition (West Pakistan Amendment) Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, in its application to certain districts of the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the districts of Lahore, Lyallpur, Khanewal, Gujranwala, Mianwali, Gujrat, Jhelum, Campbellpur, Dera Ghazi Khan, Multan, Rawalpindi, Shahpur, Montgomery, Multan, Jhang, Sheikhupura and Sialkot
metadata.one_line: Amends the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 for specific districts in West Pakistan by substituting sections and omitting words.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 to apply its provisions to certain districts of West Pakistan. It substitutes references to 'section 5-A' with 'sections 5 and 5-A' and omits specific words regarding local authorities in section 18. The amendments also update references in section 23 from 'section (1)' to 'sub-section (1) of section 4'. The Act came into force immediately upon publication.

metadata.short_title: The Motor Vehicles (West Pakistan Amendment) Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, in its application to the Province of West Pakistan.

The North-West Frontier Province Road Transport (Nationalisation) Act, 1951

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 specifically for its application to the Province of West Pakistan. It establishes the West Pakistan Road Transport Board as a body corporate with perpetual succession to operate road transport services. The legislation validates past actions taken under previous rules and repeals three specific enactments related to transport boards in Punjab and NWFP.

metadata.short_title: The Motor Vehicles (West Pakistan Amendment) Ordinance, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, in its application to the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of West Pakistan except the Federal Capital and the Special Areas
metadata.commencement: immediately on the expiry of the Motor Vehicles (West Pakistan Amendment) Act, 1957
repeals: Punjab Transport Board Act, 1948
North-West Frontier Province Road Transport (Nationalisation) Act, 1951
metadata.one_line: Amends the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 to establish a unified Road Transport Board for West Pakistan and repeals earlier provincial transport acts.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 to apply it to West Pakistan by establishing the West Pakistan Road Transport Board. It consolidates the undertakings of existing road transport boards into this new entity, transferring all assets, liabilities, and contracts. The Ordinance also validates previous rules made under the Punjab Road Transport Board Rules, 1952, and repeals conflicting provincial legislation.

name: NORTH-WEST FRONTIER PROVINCE TOWN IMPROVEMENT (WEST PAKISTAN AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1958

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the North-West Frontier Province Town Improvement Act, 1954 to address circumstances arising after the dissolution of the Provincial Assembly and abrogation of the Constitution. It mandates that three seats on a Municipal Committee Trust be filled by the Provincial Government during the period of supersession under the NWFP Municipal Act, 1950. The Ordinance specifies that appointed Trustees serve for three years or until the Trust is dissolved, whichever is less, and outlines conditions for their cessation upon the reconstitution of the Municipal Committee.

metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Pakistan Red Cross Society Act, 1920 to update specific sections. It expands the definition of 'aircraft' to include various flying machines and related components. Additionally, it modifies provisions concerning officer pay, allowances, ranks, and powers to convene district courts martial.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance extends the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 to the entire Province of West Pakistan. It inserts new sections defining military custody, military rewards, and aircraft components, while also modifying provisions regarding officer ranks and pay allowances. Additionally, the Act repeals the Undesirable Companies Ordinance, 1957, and deems actions under that Ordinance to be valid under this Act.

metadata.short_title: The Prisons (West Pakistan Amendment) Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Prisons Act, 1894, in its application to the Province of West Pakistan.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Prisons Act, 1894 specifically for its application to the Province of West Pakistan. The amendments also modify sections 5 and 11 of the principal Act to reference the Deputy Inspector-General in reporting and sending processes.

The Act also repeals the Sind District Municipal (West Pakistan Amendment) Ordinance, 1957.

It applies to various types of municipal committees and municipalities constituted under specific acts of Punjab, Sind, N.W.F.P., and Quetta. Upon supersession, all powers and duties of the municipal authority are exercised by the Commissioner appointed by the Division concerned. The Ordinance also bars any legal proceedings or suits against the Government or any person for damages caused by such supersession.

It also repeals previous betting tax acts from Sindh and Punjab, ensuring a unified legal basis for horse-race betting taxation across West Pakistan.

metadata.summary: This Act constitutes the West Pakistan Local Authorities Election Commission to study and report on various aspects of local authority elections. The Commission is tasked with investigating matters such as constituency delimitation, representation of women and special interests, election procedures, and defining corrupt practices. Upon receiving the Commission's report, the Government must pass orders to reform the election system, which will effectively cancel pending election proceedings until the new system is implemented.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the West Pakistan Local Authorities Election Commission to make recommendations on local authority elections. The Commission is tasked with investigating matters such as constituency delimitation, voter registration, polling procedures, and defining corrupt practices. Upon receiving the Commission's report, the Government must pass orders within three months. Until these reforms are implemented, no new elections can be held for a period not exceeding six months, and all existing election proceedings are deemed cancelled.

The Act also outlines the effects of repeal, ensuring that rights acquired or penalties incurred prior to repeal remain unaffected, and establishes rules for citing enactments and serving documents.

metadata.one_line: This Ordinance restricts rent increases and eviction in specific urban areas of West Pakistan, establishing a Controller to fix fair rents.
metadata.summary: The West Pakistan Urban Rent Restriction Ordinance, 1956 was promulgated by the Governor under Article 102 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session. It applies to urban areas in ten specific districts of West Pakistan and aims to restrict rent increases and tenant evictions. The Ordinance empowers a Controller appointed by the Provincial Government to determine fair rents based on historical data, construction costs, and property tax assessments. It explicitly excludes evacuee properties defined under the Administration of Evacuee Property Ordinance, 1949, and provides transitional provisions regarding appeals filed under the Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1952.

It empowers the Government to appoint Committees with corporate status to investigate encroachments, determine compensation, and manage graveyard areas. The Ordinance also establishes Tribunals to adjudicate applications regarding land exclusion from graveyard limits and authorizes the Government to make rules for its implementation.

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Province of West Pakistan by integrating the territories of Punjab, NWFP, Sind, Baluchistan, and various princely states. It provides for the creation of a High Court to replace existing courts in Lahore and Baluchistan. The Act also details financial provisions for the new province, special administrative rules for tribal areas, and comprehensive procedures for holding general elections within the newly formed entity.

name: PUNJAB CONSERVATION OF CATTLE (MEATLESS DAYS) ACT, 1954

metadata.summary: The Punjab Conservation of Cattle (Meatless Days) Act, 1954 was enacted to provide for the conservation of cattle in the Province of Punjab. It prohibits the slaughter or sale of meat on all Tuesdays and Wednesdays throughout the year, with specific exemptions for calves under three years old in certain urban areas. The Act empowers designated officers to enter premises, seize carcasses, and dispose of them if they are liable to decay. It also outlines penalties for contravention, including imprisonment or fines, and grants the Government power to frame rules and grant exemptions.

The amendment also involves minor punctuation changes and omits a comma after the word 'occupancy'. The Act comes into force immediately upon the expiry of the previous 1954 Amendment Act.

metadata.summary: The Punjab Land Utilization Act, 1954 aims to utilize proprietary waste and arable lands to promote food crop growth. It empowers the Collector to order the reclamation of uncultivated land within two years and allows the Government to take such land on lease if objections are not resolved. The Act outlines procedures for serving notices, hearing objections, measuring land, and granting leases, while also defining key terms like 'land' and 'tenant'.

It adds a requirement for written appeals for subscriptions to include a true copy of the licence granted by the District Magistrate. Additionally, it substitutes Section 8 to grant inspection powers to District Magistrates, gazetted officers, and other authorized persons over these institutions, subject to a fifteen-minute notice.

It substitutes sections regarding the dismissal of suits against unregistered money lenders and inserts new sections creating offences for carrying on business without registration or holding a licence, and for charging interest rates higher than those described under the Punjab Relief of Indebtedness Act, 1934. The amendments apply to the whole of Punjab and come into force immediately, with specific transitional provisions for existing money lenders.

The amendment adds a new section prohibiting courts or authorities from granting injunctions, ejectment orders, or appointing receivers for requisitioned buildings. It also establishes a presumption that orders signed by authorized authorities were made under the Ordinance's powers.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance empowers the Provincial Government of Punjab to temporarily requisition any building if deemed necessary or expedient. It defines key terms such as 'building', 'owner', and types of repairs, outlining procedures for notice periods, possession delivery, and cost allocation for repairs. The document also grants powers to obtain information, use force for compliance, and issue injunctions against ejectment orders while establishing penalties for providing false information.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Secondary Education Act, 1954

The Act defines key terms such as 'College', 'University', and 'Government' and outlines the composition, powers, and duties of the Board, its Chairman, Secretary, and various committees including the Finance Committee.

It repeals the earlier 1933 Act and establishes a system where different schedules dictate whether animals can be killed year-round, require special permits, or cannot be possessed as pets. The Act grants the Government powers to declare sanctuaries and reserves, regulate import/export, and issue special licences for scientific research or public purposes.

metadata.summary: The Punjab Development Fund Cess Act, 1954 was enacted to raise funds for the development of the Province of Punjab. It imposes a cess on all lands based on land revenue or occupier's rate payable by the person liable for payment. The cess is assessed and collected in the same manner as land revenue or occupier's rates under existing statutes, with provisions for exemptions by the Provincial Government.

name: PUNJAB EDUCATION (CONTROL OF UN-RECOGNIZED PRIVATE INSTITUTIONS) ACT, 1953

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Education (Control of Unrecognized Private Institutions) Act, 1953
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for Government control over unrecognized private educational institutions in the Punjab.

metadata.one_line: This Act regulates and registers unrecognized private educational institutions in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for government control over unrecognized private educational institutions in the Province of Punjab. It mandates registration for existing institutions within three months of commencement and prohibits new unregistered institutions from functioning. The Provincial Government can inspect schools, exempt specific provisions, and frame rules to implement the Act.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Electricity Duty (Repeal) Ordinance, 1954
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal the Punjab Electricity Duty Act, 1948

metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab under section 88 of the Government of India Act, 1935. It was issued because the Legislature of the Punjab was not in session and immediate action was required to repeal existing legislation. The document repeals the Punjab Electricity Duty Act, 1948, with effect from April 1, 1954.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Disturbances (Public Inquiry) Act, 1953
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the constitution of a Court of Inquiry for holding a public inquiry into the circumstances connected with the responsibility for the recent Punjab disturbances.
repeals: Punjab Disturbances (Public Inquiry) Ordinance
metadata.max_penalty: three years imprisonment or fine or both
metadata.one_line: Constitutes a Court of Inquiry to investigate the circumstances and responsibility for the recent Punjab disturbances.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a Court of Inquiry composed of two High Court Judges to investigate the Punjab disturbances that led to Martial Law in March 1953. The Court has powers similar to a High Court under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, including enforcing attendance, compelling document production, and examining witnesses. It may sit in Lahore or other places deemed expedient and must submit its report to the Provincial Government for publication.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Entertainments Duty (Amendment) Act, 1953
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Entertainments Duty Act, 1936.

key_definitions: different classes in a place which is a place of entertainment
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Entertainments Duty Act, 1936 regarding admission fees and duty exemptions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Entertainments Duty Act, 1936 to clarify provisions on admission fees and duty levies. It introduces new sections regarding security for duty payment when exemptions are granted and defines conditions for philanthropic or educational purposes. The Act also establishes procedures for reviewing orders by the Excise Commissioner and sets penalties for contraventions.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Land Revenue (Amendment) Ordinance, 1954
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1887.
metadata.parent_law: Government of India Act, 1935
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1887 regarding evacuee property and allottees.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1887 to address specific provisions concerning land revenue. It was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab under section 88 of the Government of India Act, 1935, because the Legislature was not in session. The text details textual changes to subsection (1) of section 34 regarding evacuees and allottees.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1954
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1924
amends: The Punjab Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1924

Vehicles plying for hire and ordinarily used for the transport of passengers not exclusively within the limits of Corporation, Municipal and Cantonment areas
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1924 Act to adjust vehicle taxation based on seating capacity and usage area.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1924 to introduce new tax categories for vehicles used for passenger transport. It distinguishes between vehicles operating exclusively within municipal or cantonment limits and those operating outside these areas. The text establishes specific tax rates based on seating capacity for non-exclusive area vehicles and provides a 10 percent tax deduction for certain entitled persons.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Public Safety (Amendment) Act, 1954
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the West Punjab Public Safety Act, 1949.
metadata.one_line: Amends the West Punjab Public Safety Act, 1949 regarding detention procedures and access to records.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the West Punjab Public Safety Act, 1949 to regulate the rights of detained persons. It mandates that a detained individual may represent themselves through any person, not just a legal practitioner, when appearing before the High Court at Lahore. The Chief Justice must make relevant material available to the detainee after examining them and making necessary inquiries. Additionally, the Act stipulates that findings and records regarding detention proceedings are confidential and governed by the Official Documents Secrets Act, 1923.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Essential Articles Act, 1953
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the prices, possession and control of consumption of essential articles within the Province of the Punjab.
repeals: Punjab Essential Articles Ordinance, 1953
metadata.one_line: Regulates prices and control of essential articles in Punjab through government notifications.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the prices, possession, and control of essential articles within the Province of Punjab. It empowers the Government to fix maximum prices for retailers, wholesalers, and importers by notification. The Act defines key terms such as 'essential articles', 'retailer', and 'wholesaler' and prohibits selling above fixed maximum prices or without required markings.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Trade Employees (Amendment) Act, 1953
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Trade Employees Act, 1940
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1940 Act to regulate shop opening and closing hours in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Trade Employees Act, 1940 to specify new operating hours for shops and commercial establishments. It mandates that such places must open no earlier than half-past eight in the morning or half-past nine in winter, and close no later than half-past six in the evening or half-past nine in summer. The legislation includes a proviso allowing customers who were present within fifteen minutes of closing time to be served during that period.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab University Act (Amendment) Ordinance, 1954
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab University Act, 1882, and the Universities Act, 1904.
metadata.one_line: Amends university acts to grant inspection powers to the Chancellor and transfer exam functions to the Board.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab University Act, 1882, and the Universities Act, 1904 to empower the Chancellor to conduct inspections and inquiries into university buildings and activities. It also mandates that from 1955, the University of the Punjab will cease conducting Matri-culation and Classical Intermediate examinations, transferring these functions to the Board of Secondary Education pending its full establishment.

name: PUNJAB WILD BIRDS AND WILD ANIMALS PROTECTION ORDINANCE, 1954

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Wild Birds and Wild Animals Protection Ordinance, 1954
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make better provision for the protection and preservation of certain wild birds and wild animals in the Punjab.

metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment of six months or fine extending to Rs. 500, or both; for specific acts, fine extending to Rs. 100
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates the killing, capturing, possession, and sale of wild birds and animals in the Punjab through schedules and permits.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Wild Birds and Wild Animals Protection Ordinance, 1954 was promulgated to improve provisions for protecting and preserving specific wild birds and animals in the Punjab. It categorizes these species into three schedules, dictating whether they can be killed, captured, or possessed without restriction, with a license, or under special permits. The Ordinance also empowers the Government to declare sanctuaries and reserves, restricts the use of traps and nets, and establishes penalties for breaches of its provisions.

metadata.short_title: The Charitable Funds (Regulation of Collections) Act, 1953

metadata.summary: This Act provides for the regulation, administration, and accounting of collections of charitable donations while aiming to prevent fraud. It defines specific terms such as 'private fund' and 'charitable fund' based on the value of donations collected. The Act mandates that no collection can be made without a declaration delivered to a sanctioning authority and imposes conditions regarding the custody and administration of funds.

name: CITY OF LAHORE CORPORATION (EXTENSION OF TERM OF COUNCILLORS) ORDINANCE, 1953

metadata.short_title: The City of Lahore Corporation (Extension of Term of Councillors) Ordinance, 1953

metadata.one_line: Extends the term of office for Councillors of the City of Lahore Corporation and amends related election provisions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance extends the term of office for the existing Councillors of the City of Lahore Corporation beyond their scheduled expiration date. It also provides for the election of new Councillors to fill vacancies arising from the extended term. The document amends the City of Lahore Corporation Act, 1941, to adjust procedures for electing the Mayor, Deputy Mayor, and Standing Committee members to align with the extended timeline.

name: Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act (Amendment) Ordinance, 1953

metadata.short_title: Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act (Amendment) Ordinance, 1953

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1948 by inserting new subsections and adding a new section at the end. It introduces specific offences related to public servants under the Prevention of Corruption Act and expands the Second Schedule to include various sections of the Pakistan Penal Code concerning attempts, abetments, and conspiracies. The amendments are deemed to have taken effect from November 17, 1953.

name: PUNJAB ARTICLES OF DAILY USE ORDINANCE, 1953
