metadata.short_title: The West Punjab District Boards (Appointment of Members) Act, 1949
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the appointment of refugee members to fill seats vacated by migrated Hindu or Sikh members of District Boards in West Punjab.
metadata.one_line: This Act allows the West Punjab Provincial Government to appoint refugee members to fill seats vacated by migrated Hindus or Sikhs in District Boards.
metadata.summary: The West Punjab District Boards (Appointment of Members) Act, 1949 empowers the Provincial Government of West Punjab to appoint refugees as members to District Boards. This provision applies specifically when a seat held by an elected Hindu or Sikh member has been vacated due to migration from West Punjab under section 14-A of the Punjab District Boards Act, 1883. The appointed refugee serves for the unexpired portion of the original member's term of office. The term 'refugee' is defined by reference to Pakistan Ordinance No. XVIII of 1948.

name: WEST PUNJAB ELECTRICITY (EMERGENCY POWERS) (CONTROL OF SUPPLY) ACT, 1949

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Electricity (Emergency Powers) (Control of Supply) Act, 1949
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the continuance and use of, and control the supply of electrical consumption, distribution and use of, and rates for the supply of energy in the Province of West Punjab
metadata.commencement: immediately on the expiry of the Punjab Electricity (Emergency Powers) Act, 1947
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to six months or fine or both
metadata.one_line: An Act empowering the Provincial Government to control and restrict electricity supply in West Punjab during emergencies.
metadata.summary: This Act provides emergency powers to the Governor-General and the Provincial Government of West Punjab to control the supply, consumption, distribution, and use of electrical energy. It allows the government to issue orders restricting or discontinuing supply to consumers who violate directions, exceed maximum demand, or connect loads beyond notified limits. The Act also empowers the government to refuse supply, restrict reconnection after discontinuance, increase rates, and impose penalties for contravention of its provisions.

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Excise (Amendment) Act, 1949
metadata.long_title: An act to amend the Punjab Excise Act, 1914.
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Excise Act, 1914
key_definitions: said Act (referring to the Punjab Excise Act, 1914)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Excise Act, 1914 regarding prohibition and possession of intoxicants in West Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Excise Act, 1914 to update references to the Financial Commissioner and Excise Commissioner. It substitutes specific subsections related to prohibiting or restricting the possession and consumption of intoxicants by the Provincial Government. The amendments also adjust punctuation and add words regarding rules made under the said Act.

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab General Clauses (Amendment) Act, 1949
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab General Clauses Act, 1898.
metadata.commencement: immediately after the expiry of the clause
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab General Clauses Act, 1898 to update definitions and terms for the Federation of Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab General Clauses Act, 1898 to align its terminology with the establishment of the Dominion of India and the Federation of Pakistan. It substitutes and adds new clauses defining terms such as 'Colony', 'India', 'Pakistan', and 'Provincial Government' to reflect the post-1947 political landscape. The legislation ensures that references to colonial authorities are updated to correspond with the Governor-General, Provincial Governments, or Chief Commissioners acting within their respective scopes of authority.

name: WEST PUNJAB MUHAJIR FUND CESS ACT, 1949

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Muhajir Fund Cess Act, 1949
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the raising of funds for relief of refugees in West Punjab
metadata.status_evidence: It shall remain in force for one year.
metadata.one_line: Imposes a cess on land revenue in West Punjab to fund refugee relief for one year.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the imposition of a cess on land revenue in West Punjab to raise funds for the relief of refugees. The cess is levied at a rate of two annas per rupee of land revenue assessed. It applies to the whole of West Punjab and was deemed to come into force with effect from the Rabi harvest of 1948-49. The Act remains in force for one year only.

name: WEST PUNJAB MUNICIPAL FIRE BRIGADE ACT, 1949

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Municipal Fire Brigade Act, 1949
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the organisation of fire-brigades in municipal towns in West Punjab
repeals: Sections 319, 320 and subsection (1) of section 240 of the City of Lahore Corporation Act, 1941
Sections 93, 94, 95 and clause (m) of section 240 of the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911
metadata.one_line: This Act organizes fire-brigades in municipal towns in West Punjab and grants powers for fire-fighting and emergency control.
metadata.summary: The West Punjab Municipal Fire Brigade Act, 1949 provides for the organization of fire-brigades in municipal towns within West Punjab. It defines key terms such as 'fire-fighting service' and 'municipal authority', empowering municipal authorities to establish and maintain fire-fighting services under standing orders from the Provincial Government. The Act grants emergency powers to magistrates, police officers, and fire-brigade members during fires, including breaking into premises and shutting off water mains. It also allows the Provincial Government to take direct control of inadequate fire services or appoint persons to manage them at municipal expense.

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Public Safety Act, 1949
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for special measures to ensure public safety and maintenance of public order
repeals: Punjab Public Safety Ordinance, 1940
Punjab Public Safety Act, 1947
metadata.max_penalty: three years imprisonment or fine or both
metadata.one_line: Provides special measures for public safety and order in West Punjab including arrest and detention powers.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Government, District Magistrate, and authorized servants to arrest persons without a warrant if necessary for public safety. It allows detention for up to one month initially, renewable for six-month periods, with specific procedures for reporting arrests and handling absconders. The Act applies to the whole of West Punjab and deems itself in force from August 15, 1949, superseding previous emergency laws.

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Qaumi Razakars Act, 1949
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the constitution of the Qaumi Razakars
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for one month or fine of Rs. 50 or both; imprisonment up to six months and fine up to one hundred rupees for unauthorized wearing of uniform
metadata.one_line: This Act constitutes the Qaumi Razakars in West Punjab for internal defence and law maintenance.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the constitution of the Qaumi Razakars in West Punjab to assist in maintaining law and order, national reconstruction, and internal defence. The District Magistrate is empowered to constitute these bodies, appoint members, call them out for training or service, and regulate their organization and discipline through rules. Members are granted powers similar to police forces when acting in aid of such services, while specific provisions outline penalties for neglecting duties or unauthorized wearing of uniforms.

name: ADAPTATION OF CENTRAL ACTS AND ORDINANCE ORDER, 1949

metadata.short_title: The Adaptation of Central Acts and Ordinances Order, 1949
metadata.one_line: An Order adapting Central Acts and Ordinances from British India to apply in Pakistan with necessary modifications.
metadata.summary: This Order provides for the adaptation of laws existing immediately before Independence Day to continue as law in Pakistan. It directs the substitution of references to 'British India' with 'Pakistan' or specific provinces, and modifies titles and expressions in various Central Acts and Ordinances listed in the Schedule. The Order ensures that provisions regarding Secretaries to Government are adapted for Provincial Governments in Pakistan.

name: WEST PUNJAB REFUGEES (REGISTRATION OF LAND CLAIMS) ACT, 1949

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Refugees (Registration of Land Claims) Act, 1949
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the registration of claims in respect of lands abandoned by refugees.
repeals: The West Punjab Refugees (Registration of Land Claims) Ordinance, 1948
metadata.max_penalty: five years rigorous imprisonment or fine up to five thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Provides for the registration of land claims abandoned by refugees in West Punjab following partition.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a mechanism for registering claims regarding land abandoned by refugees due to civil disturbances or the partition of India. It defines specific terms such as 'claim', 'land', and 'refugee' within the context of territories now in East Punjab, Delhi, and certain states. The Act empowers Settlement Officers and Assistant Settlement Officers to register these claims based on affidavits submitted by refugees. It also outlines penalties for submitting false information or making multiple claims regarding the same land.

name: WEST PUNJAB SMALL TOWNS (APPOINTMENT OF MEMBERS) ACT, 1949

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Small Towns (Appointment of Members) Act, 1949
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the appointment of members in small towns of West Punjab.
amends: The Punjab Hindu Small Towns (Appointment of Members) Act, 1922
metadata.one_line: This Act allows the West Punjab Provincial Government to appoint refugee members to town committees in small towns.
metadata.summary: The West Punjab Small Towns (Appointment of Members) Act, 1949 empowers the Provincial Government of West Punjab to appoint refugees as members of town committees. This provision applies specifically to cases where a member has migrated from West Punjab and was removed from their position under the Punjab Hindu Small Towns (Appointment of Members) Act, 1922. The term 'refugee' is defined by reference to Pakistan Ordinance No. XVIII of 1948. The Act ensures that the unexpired term of the office held by the displaced member is preserved for the newly appointed refugee.

name: WEST PUNJAB THAL (INCREASE IN VALUE) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1949

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Thal (Increase in Value) (Amendment) Act, 1949
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Thal (Increase in Value) Act, 1940.
amends: The Punjab Thal (Increase in Value) Act, 1940
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Thal (Increase in Value) Act, 1940 by changing tax thresholds and deleting specific subsections.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Thal (Increase in Value) Act, 1940 to adjust tax provisions regarding property transfers. It substitutes the word 'thirty' with 'sixty' in section 3(2), deletes section 4(4) and a proviso in section 7, and adds a new proviso requiring tax payment before non-inheritance transfers take effect. The Act received assent on June 2, 1949, and came into force immediately.

name: WEST PUNJAB REQUISITIONING OF IMMOVABLE PROPERTY (TEMPORARY POWERS) ACT, 1949

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Requisitioning of Immovable Property (Temporary Powers) Act, 1949
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide temporarily for the requisitioning and acquisition of immovable property
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Punjab
metadata.commencement: immediately after the expiry of the Punjab Requisitioning of Immovable Property (Temporary Powers) Act, 1947
amends: The Punjab Requisitioning of Immovable Property (Temporary Powers) Act, 1947
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to one year or fine or both
metadata.one_line: Provides temporary powers for requisitioning and acquiring immovable property in West Punjab with compensation mechanisms.
metadata.summary: This Act provides temporary powers for the Provincial Government to requisition and acquire immovable property deemed necessary or expedient. It outlines procedures for releasing property, determining fair compensation through agreement or arbitration, and appointing arbitrators and assessors. The Act also grants immunity to officials acting in good faith and ensures continuity of rights under previous legislation.

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Town Improvement (Amendment) Act, 1949
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Town Improvement Act, 1922 (Punjab Act IV of 1922)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Town Improvement Act, 1922 by replacing the word 'six' with 'four' in section 12.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Town Improvement Act, 1922. It was enacted by the Governor of West Punjab on October 28, 1949, and came into force immediately. The amendment specifically substitutes the word 'six' with the word 'four' in section 12(1)(b) of the 1922 Act.

name: WEST PUNJAB URBAN RENT RESTRICTION ACT, 1949

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949
metadata.long_title: An Act to restrict the increase of rent of certain premises situated within the limits of urban areas, and the eviction of tenants therefrom
metadata.territorial_extent: all urban areas in West Punjab
metadata.commencement: immediately after the expiry of Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1947
repeals: Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1947
metadata.max_penalty: one thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act restricts rent increases and eviction in urban areas of West Punjab for a three-year period.
metadata.summary: The West Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949 was enacted to limit rent hikes and prevent tenant evictions within urban areas of West Punjab. It applies to all urban areas except Cantonment zones and remains in force for three years following the expiry of the previous 1947 Act. The Act establishes a Controller appointed by the Provincial Government to determine fair rents based on local rates, improvements, and property tax assessments. It defines key terms such as landlord, tenant, and residential buildings, while outlining penalties for contravention and procedures for rule-making.

metadata.short_title: The Arbitral Tribunal (Dissolution) Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act to dissolve the Arbitral Tribunal Order, 1947 and repeal the Arbitral Tribunal Ordinance, 1947
repeals: The Arbitral Tribunal Ordinance, 1947
metadata.one_line: Dissolves the Arbitral Tribunal Order of 1947 and transfers pending cases to District Magistrates.
metadata.summary: This Act dissolves the Arbitral Tribunal established under the Arbitral Tribunal Order, 1947. It ensures that awards made by the dissolved tribunal remain binding on all parties. Pending cases are transferred to the District Magistrate of Lahore for further proceedings.

metadata.short_title: The Code of Civil Procedure (Amendment) Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
repeals: The Arbitral Tribunal Order, 1947
The West Punjab Special Tribunal (Abolition) Act, 1948
metadata.max_penalty: two years rigorous imprisonment or fine or both
metadata.one_line: Amends the Code of Civil Procedure to regulate public subscriptions and abolishes special arbitral tribunals.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 to prevent abuses in the collection of public subscriptions for political purposes. It also dissolves the Arbitral Tribunal Order of 1947 and abolishes the West Punjab Special Tribunal constituted under the Independence (Special Tribunals) Order, 1947. The Act empowers District Magistrates to hear cases transferred from these abolished tribunals and defines offenses related to embezzlement of public funds.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Forest (West Punjab Amendment) Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Indian Forest Act, 1927, in its application to West Punjab
metadata.parent_law: The Indian Forest Act, 1927
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Forest Act, 1927 to apply its provisions to West Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Indian Forest Act, 1927 specifically regarding its application to West Punjab. It was enacted by the Provincial Legislature and received assent from the Governor on February 18, 1948. The legislation extends the scope of the 1927 Act to cover the whole of West Punjab, replacing previous limitations or omissions in that region.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Stamp (West Punjab Amendment) Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, in certain respects in its application to West Punjab
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Provincial Government may by notification appoint in this behalf
key_definitions: said Act (referring to the Indian Stamp Act, 1899)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 regarding stamp duties on various instruments in West Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 specifically for its application to West Punjab. It revises the existing scale of stamp duties by substituting Schedules I and I-A with new schedules appended to this Act. The legislation covers a wide range of instruments including debt acknowledgments, administration bonds, adoption deeds, wills, trust declarations, and warrants for goods, specifying proper stamp duties for each.

name: WEST PUNJAB AGRICULTURAL INCOME TAX ACT, 1948

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the levy of a tax on agricultural income accruing from lands situate in West Punjab
metadata.max_penalty: assessment of tax without statement to the best of his knowledge upon failure to comply with notice
metadata.one_line: This Act levies agricultural income tax on lands in West Punjab based on land revenue slabs.
metadata.summary: The West Punjab Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1948 imposes a tax on agricultural income from lands situated in West Punjab. The tax is assessed by the Collector of the district where the land is situated and is payable in instalments fixed by the Financial Commissioner. It defines specific terms related to land ownership, assessment circles, and government authority, while establishing tax rates based on land revenue slabs and providing for exemptions via notification.

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Border Police Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the constitution of a Border Police
repeals: The Home Guards Ordinance, 1947
metadata.one_line: Constitutes a Border Police in West Punjab with powers equivalent to regular police officers.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Border Police in West Punjab to protect persons, property, and public safety. Members are appointed by the Inspector-General of Police and possess the same powers, privileges, and protections as regular police officers. The Act also repeals the Home Guards Ordinance, 1947, deeming actions under that ordinance to be valid under this new legislation.

name: WEST PUNJAB CODE OF CRIMINAL PROCEDURE AND POLICE ACT (AMENDING) ORDINANCE, 1948

metadata.short_title: West Punjab Code of Criminal Procedure and Police Act (Amending) Ordinance, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide a shorter period for the disposal of unclaimed property or property in respect of which an offence is alleged or suspected to have been committed.
metadata.parent_law: Government of India Act, 1935
metadata.one_line: Amends the Code of Criminal Procedure and Police Act to shorten disposal periods for unclaimed or looted property in West Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends provisions regarding the disposal of unclaimed or looted property under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, and the Police Act, 1861. It reduces the time limit for such disposal from six months to one month. The Ordinance applies to the whole of West Punjab and validates actions taken by rehabilitation authorities as if they complied with the amended provisions.

name: WEST PUNJAB CONTROL OF REFUGEES ORDINANCE, 1948

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Control of Refugees Ordinance, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the control of refugees in West Punjab.
metadata.parent_law: Government of India Act, 1935
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment not exceeding three years or fine not exceeding five hundred rupees or both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance empowers magistrates and police to direct refugees in camps and prescribes penalties for disobedience.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of West Punjab under the Government of India Act, 1935, because the Legislature was not in session. It defines 'Refugee' as a person formerly domiciled in India who came to Pakistan due to civil disturbances and establishes the post of Refugee Commissioner. The law empowers magistrates and police officers to direct refugees in camps to move or refrain from action as specified, with penalties for disobedience.

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Thal Development Act, 1949
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the speedy development of the area brought under irrigation in execution of the Thul Project, and for the re-settlement thereof of refugees and others and for the levy of Development Fee.
metadata.territorial_extent: the districts of Mianwali, Muzaffargarh and Shahpur District; may be extended to any other part of the Province of West Punjab by notification
amends: The West Punjab Thal Development Act, 1949
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Thal Development Authority to manage irrigation projects, refugee resettlement, and levy development fees in West Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the speedy development of areas brought under irrigation via the Thul Project in West Punjab. It establishes the Thal Development Authority as a corporate body to carry out these provisions and handle the re-settlement of refugees. The Act defines key terms related to land, tenancy, and local authorities, and outlines the constitution, term of office, and removal procedures for the Authority's members.

name: West Punjab Development of Damaged Areas Ordinance, 1948

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Damaged Areas (Development) Ordinance, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the development of damaged areas in West Punjab.
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment which may extend to two years or with fine which may extend to Rs. 1,000 or with both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance empowers the Provincial Government to declare damaged areas and frame schemes for their development, acquisition, and improvement.
metadata.summary: The West Punjab Damaged Areas (Development) Ordinance, 1948 was promulgated by the Governor of West Punjab under section 88 of the Government of India Act, 1935. It applies to the whole of West Punjab and comes into force immediately. The Ordinance allows the Provincial Government to declare areas as damaged and frame schemes for their development, which may include land acquisition, demolition of unfit buildings, laying out streets, and providing public amenities like water supply and drainage.

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Electricity Duty Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act to levy a duty on electrical energy consumed for lights, fans and certain other appliances in West Punjab
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to two hundred rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act levies a duty on electrical energy consumed for lights, fans and appliances in West Punjab.
metadata.summary: The West Punjab Electricity Duty Act, 1948 imposes a duty on the consumption of electrical energy for specific purposes like lighting and fans within West Punjab. It defines various categories of consumers and licensees, including bulk supply recipients and industrial undertakings. The Act outlines the rates for duty based on metered or unmetered connections and provides mechanisms for collecting dues, recovering arrears as land revenue, and appointing inspecting officers.

name: West Punjab Legislative Assembly Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's Salaries (Amendment) Act, 1948

metadata.short_title: West Punjab Legislative Assembly Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's Salaries (Amendment) Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the West Punjab Legislative Assembly Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's Salaries Act, 1937
amends: West Punjab Legislative Assembly Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's Salaries Act, 1937
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1937 Salaries Act to provide a free house or increased allowance for the Speaker and Deputy Speaker.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the West Punjab Legislative Assembly Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's Salaries Act, 1937. It was enacted to make provision for a residential house for the Speaker of the West Punjab Legislative Assembly. The amendment replaces the full stop at the end of section 2 of the 1937 Act with a semi-colon and adds provisions for a free furnished house or an allowance of Rs. 1,600 per year.

name: West Punjab Motor Spirit (Taxation of Sales) (Amendment) Act, 1948

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Motor Spirit (Taxation of Sales) (Amendment) Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Motor Spirit (Taxation of Sales) Act, 1939
amends: The Punjab Motor Spirit (Taxation of Sales) Act, 1939
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1939 Motor Spirit Taxation Act by substituting tax rates in Section 3.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Motor Spirit (Taxation of Sales) Act, 1939. It specifically targets Section 3 of the 1939 Act to change the tax wording from 'three pies' and 'six pies' to 'annas'. The legislation was promulgated by the Governor on February 18, 1948, and came into force immediately.

name: West Punjab Muhajir Fund Cess (Amendment) Act, 1948

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Muhajar Fund Cess (Amendment) Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the West Punjab Muhajar Fund Cess Act, 1948
amends: The West Punjab Muhajar Fund Cess Act, 1948
metadata.one_line: Amends the West Punjab Muhajar Fund Cess Act, 1948 to correct a typographical error in section 13.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the West Punjab Muhajar Fund Cess Act, 1948 by correcting a mistake in its draft. Specifically, it substitutes the figure '1947' for '1948' in subsection (3) of section 13 of the original Act. The amendment is effective immediately upon passing.

name: West Punjab Muhajir Fund Cess Act, 1948

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Muhajir Fund Cess Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the raising of funds for relief of refugees in West Punjab
metadata.one_line: An Act to raise funds via a cess for the relief of refugees in West Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the imposition of a cess to raise funds specifically for the relief of refugees in West Punjab. The funds are intended to support the Kharif harvest season of 1948 and subsequent periods. The legislation applies to the entire territory of West Punjab and remains in force for one year from its commencement date.

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Highways Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the construction and development of highways in West Punjab
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Provincial Government may, by notification in the official gazette, appoint
metadata.max_penalty: fine of one thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: An Act to provide for the construction, development, and regulation of highways in West Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a Highway Authority to oversee the construction and maintenance of highways in West Punjab. It grants powers to the authority to regulate traffic, prevent encroachments, remove obstacles, and impose fines for violations. The Act also provides mechanisms for determining compensation when actions by the Highway Authority cause loss or damage.

name: West Punjab Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Applications Act, 1948

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the application of the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) to Muslims in West Punjab at the time of the death of any owner had the full property devolved on her if she would have inherited been applicable had the termination of the limited interest of the female heir occurred.
metadata.one_line: Applies Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) to inheritance cases involving female heirs in West Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act applies the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) to Muslims in West Punjab regarding property succession at the time of an owner's death. It specifically addresses situations where a female heir holds a limited interest that terminates upon marriage, ensuring her successors inherit as if she had inherited full property rights. The legislation extends to the entire territory of West Punjab and comes into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The West Panjab Municipal (Amendment) Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911 regarding building committee sanctions and procedural timelines.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911 to insert a new subsection into section 193. It establishes procedures for municipal committees when evaluating proposed building schemes that might interfere with existing structures. The amendment mandates written communication of refusal grounds within six days and deems applications sanctioned if no refusal is issued within the specified time or if provincial government sanction is not received within twelve months.

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Public Safety (Amendment) Ordinance, 1948
metadata.parent_law: Government of India Act, 1935
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Public Safety Act, 1947 by limiting the duration of provincial government orders to six months.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of West Punjab under section 88 of the Government of India Act, 1935, because the Legislature was not in session. It amends section 5 of the Punjab Public Safety Act, 1947 to restrict provincial government orders made under subsection (3) to a maximum period of six months. The Ordinance allows for the renewal of such orders before their expiry but mandates that they cannot remain in force beyond six months unless renewed or cancelled.

name: WEST PUNJAB REFUGEES (REGISTRATION OF LAND CLAIMS) ORDINANCE, 1948

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Refugees (Registration of Land Claims) Ordinance, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the registration of claims by refugees in respect of land abandoned since March 1, 1947.
metadata.parent_law: Government of India Act, 1935
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment which may extend to five years or with fine up to rupees five thousand or with both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance establishes a process for refugees in West Punjab to register claims regarding land abandoned since March 1947.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of West Punjab to enable immediate action regarding refugee land claims while the Legislature was not in session. It defines specific terms such as 'refugee', 'land', and 'claim' relating to properties abandoned since March 1, 1947, due to civil disturbances or partition. The document empowers Settlement Officers to register these claims based on affidavits submitted by refugees and grants them the powers of a Civil Court for attesting such documents. It also outlines offences related to submitting false claims or duplicative submissions, punishable by imprisonment up to five years or fines.

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Special Tribunal (Abolition) Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act to abolish the West Punjab Special Tribunal as constituted under the Indian Independence (Special Tribunals) Order, 1947
amends: The West Punjab Special Tribunal (Abolition) Act, 1948
repeals: The Indian Independence (Special Tribunals) Order, 1947
metadata.one_line: Abolishes the West Punjab Special Tribunal and transfers its pending cases to the District Magistrate of Lahore.
metadata.summary: This Act abolishes the West Punjab Special Tribunal established under the Indian Independence (Special Tribunals) Order, 1947. It declares that the tribunal shall stand abolished immediately and that any pending cases before it are to be transferred to the District Magistrate of Lahore. The District Magistrate is vested with all powers previously held by the Special Tribunal, including the authority to try offences mentioned in the schedule appended to the Act.

name: West Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax (Fourth Amendment) Act, 1948

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax (Fourth Amendment) Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1948
amends: The Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1948
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1948 regarding annual value limits in rating areas.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1948. It specifically substitutes a clause concerning buildings and lands with an annual value not exceeding one hundred and eighty rupees in a rating area. The amendment was enacted by the Provincial Legislature of West Punjab and received assent on April 7, 1948.

name: West Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax (Third Amendment) Act, 1948

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax (Third Amendment) Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1940
amends: The Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1940
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1940 regarding valuation lists and tax recovery procedures.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1940. It was promulgated by the Governor of West Punjab on February 16, 1948, but is deemed to have taken effect from January 13, 1941. The legislation specifically addresses amendments related to valuation lists, including provisions for cases where a list has been lost or destroyed due to circumstances beyond control. It extends to the whole of West Punjab.

name: West Punjab Protection of Evacuee Property Act, 1948

metadata.short_title: The West Punjab Protection of Evacuee Property Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the protection and care of the property of evacuees from West Punjab
repeals: West Punjab Protection of Evacuee Property Ordinance, 1947
metadata.one_line: This Act protects evacuee property in West Punjab by appointing custodians and regulating its vesting and transfer.
metadata.summary: The West Punjab Protection of Evacuee Property Act, 1948 was enacted to protect the property of evacuees from West Punjab. It empowers the Provincial Government to appoint Custodians, Additional Custodians, Deputy Custodians, and Assistant Custodians for managing such property. The Act provides for the vesting, pooling, and transfer of evacuee property to rehabilitation authorities or other prescribed persons, while also defining key terms like 'Evacuee', 'Property', and 'Rehabilitation Authority'. It repeals the earlier West Punjab Protection of Evacuee Property Ordinance, 1947, and comes into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Police (Punjab Amendment) Act, 1947
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Police Act, 1861
metadata.commencement: on the commencement of the Police Act, 1861
metadata.one_line: Amends the Police Act, 1861 regarding dismissal, suspension, rank reduction, and increment stoppage.
metadata.summary: This Act amends section 7 of the Police Act, 1861 to insert specific phrases regarding dismissal, suspension, or reduction in rank within a time-scale. It also adds a new clause concerning the stoppage of increments. The Act was enacted by the Governor of Punjab on September 26, 1947, and came into force simultaneously with the commencement of the Police Act, 1861.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Cotton (Control) Act, 1947
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the control and regulation of the production, movement, supply and distribution of cotton and trade and commerce in cotton.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
repeals: Punjab Foreign Cotton Control Ordinance, 1946
Punjab Cotton Control Ordinance, 1946
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act empowers the Provincial Government to control cotton production, supply, distribution, and trade via orders.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Cotton (Control) Act, 1947 was enacted by the Governor of West Punjab to regulate the production, movement, supply, and distribution of cotton. It grants the Provincial Government broad powers to issue orders regarding licensing, price control, storage, transport, and information collection related to cotton trade. The Act also establishes penalties for contravention of these orders, including imprisonment up to three years or fines, and deems certain pre-existing Defence of India Rules orders as valid under this new legislation.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Disturbed Areas (Amendment) Act, 1947
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Disturbed Areas Act, 1947
metadata.max_penalty: death
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Disturbed Areas Act, 1947 by adding offences related to explosions and possession of explosives punishable by death.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Disturbed Areas Act, 1947 to introduce new sections regarding causing explosions and possessing explosives in disturbed areas. It establishes that causing an explosion likely to endanger life or damage property can be punished with death instead of other punishments. Additionally, it makes possession of explosive substances punishable by death if there is a reasonable suspicion they are not for a lawful object.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Disturbed Areas Act, 1947
metadata.long_title: An Act to make better provision for the suppression and maintenance of public order in the restoration and disturbed areas of the Punjab.
metadata.max_penalty: death
metadata.one_line: An Act empowering the Provincial Government to declare disturbed areas and impose death penalties for specific offences.
metadata.summary: This Act provides powers to the Provincial Government to declare areas in Punjab as 'disturbed areas' via notification. It allows for the imposition of the death penalty for certain offences committed within these areas, even if they are punishable under the Indian Penal Code. The Act also grants police and magistrates the power to fire upon persons violating orders in disturbed areas, subject to prior sanction for prosecution.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Damaged Areas Act, 1947
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for salvage and disposal of property and clearance of debris in areas struck by riots
metadata.territorial_extent: all urban areas in the Punjab
metadata.commencement: at once for sections 1, 2, and 3; other provisions on such date as notified by the Provincial Government
metadata.one_line: Provides for salvage, disposal of property and debris clearance in riot-stricken urban areas of Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Provincial Government to declare urban areas as damaged areas following riots. It establishes mechanisms for salvaging and disposing of debris and property, appointing Claims Commissioners to handle claims, and amending existing municipal laws for application to these specific areas. The Act also provides general indemnity to government officers acting under its provisions.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab General Clauses (Amendment) Act, 1947
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab General Clauses Act, 1898
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab General Clauses Act, 1898 to preserve amendments upon repeal and update terminology.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab General Clauses Act, 1898 by inserting a new section regarding the effect of repeals on existing amendments. It also updates specific sections within the parent Act to change terms like 'notification' to 'order' or 'issue', and adds provisions concerning the expiry of Ordinances.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Land Revenue (Matured Area) Act, 1947
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for empowering the Provincial Government to prescribe the mode of determining the matured area during rabi 1946-47, in respect of certain lands, for purposes of assessment of land revenue.
metadata.one_line: Empowers the Provincial Government to prescribe how matured area is determined for land revenue assessment during rabi 1946-47.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Provincial Government of Punjab to prescribe the method for determining the matured area during the rabi harvest of 1946-47. The determination applies specifically to certain lands for the purpose of assessing land revenue. Orders made under this section cannot be questioned in any court, and no legal proceedings can be taken against the Crown or its officers for actions taken in pursuance of the Act.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Land Trespass (Emergency Provisions) Act, 1947
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for punishment of unlawful cultivation of land and ejectment of trespassers therefrom
metadata.territorial_extent: the District of Gurgaon (extendable to any other district of the Punjab Province)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years or with fine or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act punishes unlawful cultivation in Punjab and allows ejectment of trespassers with compensation.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Land Trespass (Emergency Provisions) Act, 1947 was enacted by the Governor of the Punjab to address unlawful cultivation of land. It applies initially to the District of Gurgaon but can be extended to other districts via notification. The Act defines 'land' and 'cultivation', punishes unlawful cultivation with imprisonment up to two years or a fine, and empowers courts to order ejectment of trespassers upon payment of compensation.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Municipal (Amendment) Act, 1947
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911
key_definitions: said Act (referring to the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911 to empower committees to establish fire brigades.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911 to allow municipal committees to establish and maintain fire brigades. It grants these committees the power to provide necessary implements, machinery, and communication means for efficient duty discharge. The amendments are made under powers assumed by the Governor of the Punjab pursuant to section 93 of the Government of India Act, 1935.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Electricity (Emergency Powers) Act, 1947
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the continuance of powers to control the supply, consumption, distribution and use of and the rates for the supply of electrical energy.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
metadata.commencement: immediately on the expiry of the Emergency Ordinance, 1946
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act empowers the Provincial Government to control electricity supply, consumption, and rates during emergencies.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Electricity (Emergency Powers) Act, 1947 provides powers to control the supply, consumption, distribution, and use of electrical energy in the Province of the Punjab. It allows the Provincial Government to prohibit or restrict supply, discontinue supply under certain circumstances, fix rates, and manage requisitions during emergencies. The Act also outlines penalties for contraventions and protects actions taken under its provisions.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Public Safety (Amendment) Act, 1947
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Public Safety Act, 1947.
key_definitions: said Act (referring to the Punjab Public Safety Act, 1947 as amended)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Public Safety Act, 1947 by re-numbering sections and substituting words in section 37.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Public Safety Act, 1947 to address procedural aspects of trial for specific offences. It re-numbers existing section 35 as subsection (1) and adds a new subsection clarifying that provisions apply to offences committed before the Act's commencement in dangerously disturbed areas. Additionally, it substitutes words in section 37 regarding police reports and the jurisdiction of Courts of Session versus Magistrates.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Public Safety (Second Amendment) Act, 1947
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Panjab Public Safety Act, 1947
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Public Safety Act, 1947 to empower District Magistrates to remove obstructions impeding police or fire brigades.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Public Safety Act, 1947 by inserting a new section (13-A). It empowers the District Magistrate or authorized first-class Magistrates in Lahore and notified areas to order the removal of obstructions that impede police or fire brigade operations. If the ordered person fails to comply, authorities may take necessary steps to remove the obstruction immediately. The Provincial Government retains the power to cancel or vary such orders.

name: PUNJAB REQUISITIONING OF IMMOVABLE PROPERTY (TEMPORARY POWERS) ACT, 1947

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Requisitioning of Immovable Property (Temporary Powers) Act, 1947
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide temporarily for the requisitioning and acquisition of immovable property
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the Punjab
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to one year or fine or both
metadata.one_line: Provides temporary powers for the Provincial Government to requisition and acquire immovable property in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Provincial Government to temporarily requisition and acquire immovable property within the Province of Punjab when deemed necessary or expedient. It outlines procedures for acquiring such property, including exemptions for religious worship sites and Cantonment areas, and establishes a framework for determining compensation through arbitration if no agreement is reached. The Act also grants powers to require information, use force for compliance, and provides legal immunity for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Special Tribunals Act, 1947
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the setting up of Special Tribunals for the trial of criminal offences
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Punjab
metadata.one_line: Establishes Special Tribunals in Punjab to try criminal offences with specific procedures and powers.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the constitution of Special Tribunals by the Provincial Government to try criminal offences throughout the Province of Punjab. The tribunals consist of three members qualified as High Court judges, with one appointed as President. They follow a simplified procedure under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, allowing for restricted public access and limited bail conditions. The Act grants these tribunals exclusive jurisdiction over tried cases, preventing interference from other courts or appeals.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Special Tribunals (Continuance) Act, 1947
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the continuance of Special Tribunals at Lahore constituted under the Criminal Law Amendment Ordinance, 1943.
metadata.commencement: immediately on the expiry of a period of six weeks from the 3rd March, 1947
repeals: The Punjab Special Tribunals (Continuance) Ordinance, 1946
metadata.one_line: Continues the jurisdiction and function of Special Tribunals at Lahore for cases not disposed of before March 1947.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the continuance of three Special Tribunals located in Lahore that were constituted under the Criminal Law Amendment Ordinance, 1943. It ensures these tribunals can continue to dispose of cases allotted to them before the expiration of a six-week period following March 3, 1947. The Act validates proceedings held prior to its commencement and declares that no new proceedings need to be recommenced for orders issued by the tribunals.

name: ANDAMAN AND NICOBAR ISLANDS POLICE FORCE (TEMPORARY PROVISIONS) ORDINANCE, 1945

metadata.short_title: Andaman and Nicobar Islands Police Force (Temporary Provisions) Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance temporarily to regulate the Andaman and Nicobar Islands police force
key_definitions: Andaman and Nicobar Islands Police Force
metadata.one_line: Temporarily regulates the Andaman and Nicobar Islands Police Force during an emergency in British India.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides temporary provisions to regulate the Andaman and Nicobar Islands Police Force while it is elsewhere in British India. It specifically aims to ensure discipline among members of the force. The Ordinance extends to the whole of British India and comes into force immediately upon promulgation.

metadata.short_title: The Armed Forces (Special Powers) Amendment Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Ordinance, 1942
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of India (as per Gazette of India Extraordinary header)
key_definitions: officer in charge of the nearest police station
metadata.one_line: Amends the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Ordinance, 1942 regarding arrest reporting procedures.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Ordinance, 1942 to improve arrest reporting protocols. It mandates that persons arrested under this Ordinance must be reported immediately to the officer in charge of the nearest police station or the appropriate military officer if the person is subject to military law. The amendment also requires a report detailing the circumstances occasioning the arrest to accompany the notification.

metadata.short_title: The Badshahi Mosque Fund Cess Act, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the raising of a cess on land owned by Muslims or Muslim institutions in Punjab for the repair, maintenance and endowment of the Badshahi Mosque.
metadata.one_line: Imposes a land cess in Punjab to fund the repair and maintenance of the Badshahi Mosque.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a special cess on land owned by Muslims or Muslim institutions within the Province of Punjab. The revenue collected is specifically designated for the repair, maintenance, and endowment of the Badshahi Mosque. The cess applies to land with an annual value exceeding one rupee and eight annas, levied at a rate of three pies per rupee of annual value.

metadata.short_title: Bills of Exchange Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make emergency provision in connection with bills of exchange payable outside British India.
metadata.one_line: An emergency ordinance regarding bills of exchange payable outside British India during war conditions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides emergency provisions concerning bills of exchange that are payable outside British India. It was promulgated by the Governor-General on November 2, 1945, to address issues arising from war conditions. The text outlines procedures for evidence in court and indemnity for claims against persons affected by such conditions.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Public Safety Act, 1947
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for special measures to ensure public safety and maintenance of public order
repeals: Punjab Public Safety Ordinance, 1946
metadata.one_line: Provides special measures for public safety and order in Punjab, including arrest powers and collective fines.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Provincial Government to take special measures to ensure public safety and maintain public order. It grants authorities the power to arrest suspected persons without a warrant, control publications, prohibit meetings, and impose collective fines on inhabitants of dangerously disturbed areas. The Act also provides for the continuation of orders made under the repealed Punjab Public Safety Ordinance, 1946.

metadata.short_title: The Criminal Law (1943 Amendment) Second Amending Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Criminal Law Amendment Ordinance, 1943
metadata.one_line: Amends the Criminal Law Amendment Ordinance, 1943 regarding Special Tribunals and court jurisdiction.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor-General to further amend the Criminal Law Amendment Ordinance, 1943. It modifies the long title and preamble of the parent Ordinance by removing specific references to punishments under the Indian Penal Code. The text establishes the composition of Special Tribunals, requiring members to be qualified High Court judges or experienced judicial officers/professionals. Additionally, it amends the Schedule to specify offences related to hoarding, profiteering, and defence of India that fall under the jurisdiction of these tribunals.

metadata.short_title: Defence of India (Amendment) Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Defence of India Act, 1939.
metadata.parent_law: Defence of India Act, 1939
metadata.one_line: Amends the Defence of India Act, 1939 by adding specific words to sections 2 and 17.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor-General on August 3, 1945, to amend the Defence of India Act, 1939. It inserts specific phrases into subsection (3) of section 2 and adds words to subsections (1) and (2) of section 17 of the 1939 Act. The amendments are deemed to have always been in force. The Ordinance comes into force immediately upon promulgation.

metadata.short_title: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Criminal Law (Amendment) Ordinance, 1943
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of India (as per Gazette header 'GAZETTE OF INDIA')
metadata.parent_law: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Ordinance, 1943
metadata.one_line: Amends the Criminal Law (Amendment) Ordinance, 1943 regarding Special Tribunals and case allocation.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Criminal Law (Amendment) Ordinance, 1943 to modify provisions related to Special Tribunals. It substitutes specific words in sections and schedules, omits certain subsections, and renumbers sections to adjust tribunal jurisdiction and case allocation procedures. The changes are made under emergency powers exercised by the Governor-General of India.

metadata.short_title: The Defence of India (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Defence of India Act, 1939
metadata.parent_law: The Defence of India Act, 1939
metadata.one_line: Amends the Defence of India Act, 1939 to add provisions regarding forfeiture adjudication.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor-General to further amend the Defence of India Act, 1939. It addresses an emergency situation requiring additional amendments to the existing Act. Specifically, it adds a clause to subsection (3) of section 2 of the Defence of India Act, 1939 concerning the adjudication of forfeiture by a Court or other authority.

metadata.short_title: The Defence of India (Fourth Amendment) Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Defence of India Act, 1939.
metadata.parent_law: The Defence of India Act, 1939
metadata.one_line: Amends the Defence of India Act, 1939 regarding requisitioned property compensation and arbitration.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Defence of India Act, 1939 to address issues related to the requisition of property during an emergency. It inserts new sections (19A and 19B) concerning the determination of market value for requisitioned property, the finality of government decisions on compensation, and procedures for restoring property after the emergency ends. The Ordinance applies to the whole of India under the Governor-General's authority.

metadata.short_title: The Excess Profits Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Excess Profits Tax Ordinance, 1943
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of India (as per Gazette header 'GOVERNMENT OF INDIA')
metadata.parent_law: Excess Profits Tax Ordinance, 1943
metadata.one_line: Amends the Excess Profits Tax Ordinance, 1943 regarding accounting periods ending after December 31, 1944.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor-General under emergency powers to amend the Excess Profits Tax Ordinance, 1943. It specifically alters provisions related to chargeable periods ending after December 31, 1944, substituting specific figures and adding new subsections. The amendment applies immediately upon promulgation.

metadata.short_title: The Factories (Amendment) Act, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Factories Act, 1934
metadata.parent_law: The Factories Act, 1934
metadata.one_line: Amends the Factories Act, 1934 regarding worker holidays, wages, and inspector powers.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Factories Act, 1934 to provide specific provisions for annual holidays and compensatory leave for workers. It grants inspectors the power to make rules and exempts factories that offer substantially similar benefits. The amendments also update sections regarding contraventions of holiday and wage rules.

metadata.short_title: The Explosives (Amendment) Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to further amend the Indian Explosives Act, 1884
metadata.parent_law: Indian Explosives Act, 1884
metadata.max_penalty: fine of five hundred rupees or imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with both
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Explosives Act, 1884 regarding accident notices and inquiry procedures.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Indian Explosives Act, 1884 to require notice of accidents attended by loss of human life or serious injury. It establishes new sections for conducting inquiries into such accidents, granting powers to appoint assessors and regulate inquiry proceedings. The Central Government is empowered to make rules regulating these inquiries and exempt certain explosives from specific provisions.

metadata.short_title: Indian Army (Amendment) Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Indian Army Act, 1911 and the National Service (European British Subjects) Act, 1940.
key_definitions: person referred to in any section
inquiry into conduct of prisoner of war
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Army Act and National Service Act regarding POW conduct inquiries and pay withholding.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Indian Army Act, 1911 and the National Service (European British Subjects) Act, 1940 to address emergency powers. It inserts new sections concerning inquiries into the conduct of prisoners of war and the power to withhold pay and allowances. The legislation applies to European British subjects serving in the army and was promulgated by the Governor-General under emergency provisions.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Companies (Amendment) Act, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Indian Companies Act, 1913
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Companies Act, 1913 regarding employee rights in recognized provident funds.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Indian Companies Act, 1913 by adding a subsection to section 282B. The amendment clarifies that the provisions of the 1913 Act do not affect an employee's rights under recognized provident fund rules to obtain advances or withdraw money standing to their credit. It specifically references funds recognized under clause (a) of section 58A of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922.

name: INDIAN ARMY AND INDIAN AIR FORCE (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1945

metadata.short_title: The Indian Army and Indian Air Force (Amendment) Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Indian Army Act, 1911, and the Indian Air Force Act, 1932
metadata.parent_law: Government of India Act, 1935
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Army Act 1911 and Indian Air Force Act 1932 regarding POWs and enemy territory definitions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Indian Army Act of 1911 and the Indian Air Force Act of 1932 to address issues related to prisoners of war and enemy territory. It inserts new clauses defining 'enemy territory' and adjusts time computation periods for offences committed after December 7, 1941. The amendments are deemed to have always been in effect from that date.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922
metadata.parent_law: Indian Income-tax Act, 1922
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922 regarding earned income and firm registration.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922 to address issues arising from an emergency. It defines earned income and clarifies the treatment of unregistered Hindu undivided families and firms for tax purposes. The amendments include changes to sections regarding business profits, personal services, and the calculation of total income.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Merchandise Marks (Amendment) Supplementary Act, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Indian Merchandise Marks Act, 1941
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Merchandise Marks Act, 1941 regarding cotton thread specifications and factory rules.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Indian Merchandise Marks Act, 1941 to update definitions related to cotton thread, sewing, darning, and crochet. It substitutes specific words in sections concerning factory premises and workers' benefits under the Factories Act, 1934. The legislation also adds provisions regarding income-tax exemptions for provident funds where work is done by members of a family or cooperative society.

name: MILITARY OPERATIONAL AREA (SPECIAL POWERS) AMENDMENT ORDINANCE, 1945

metadata.short_title: The Military Operational Area (Special Powers) Amendment Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Military Operational Area (Special Powers) Ordinance, 1943
metadata.parent_law: The Military Operational Area (Special Powers) Ordinance, 1943
amends: The Military Operational Area (Special Powers) Ordinance, 1943
key_definitions: said Ordinance (refers to the Military Operational Area (Special Powers) Ordinance, 1943)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Military Operational Area (Special Powers) Ordinance, 1943 by substituting specific terms regarding military command.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Military Operational Area (Special Powers) Ordinance, 1943. It substitutes the term 'General Officer Commanding' for 'the General Officer Commanding military forces' in section 3 and makes similar changes to other sections. The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor-General on August 23, 1945, but is deemed to have come into force on June 1, 1945.

metadata.short_title: The Patents and Designs Act (Amendment) Act, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Indian Patents and Designs Act, 1911.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of India (implied by 'Indian Patents and Designs Act')
amends: The Indian Patents and Designs Act, 1911
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Patents and Designs Act, 1911 regarding specifications, applications, and examination procedures.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Indian Patents and Designs Act of 1911 to clarify definitions and procedures related to patent applications. It introduces specific requirements for provisional and complete specifications, including descriptions of inventions and statements as to whether they are performed in India. The legislation also addresses the submission of models or samples, time limits for sealing applications, and fees payable to the Controller.

metadata.short_title: The Mines (Amendment) Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Indian Mines Act, 1923
metadata.parent_law: Indian Mines Act, 1923
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Mines Act, 1923 regarding supervision of rooms reserved for women workers in mines.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Indian Mines Act, 1923 to address emergency conditions affecting mine safety and worker welfare. It specifically inserts provisions concerning the maintenance of rooms ordinarily reserved for women employed in mines. The amendment also adds rules regarding the number and extent of supervision required for such reserved rooms.

metadata.short_title: The Mines Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Mines Maternity Benefit Act, 1941.
key_definitions: owner or manager of a mine
metadata.one_line: Amends the Mines Maternity Benefit Act, 1941 regarding maternity benefits for women in mines.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Mines Maternity Benefit Act, 1941 to regulate maternity benefits for women employed below ground in mines. It introduces requirements for informing mine owners about pregnancy, provisions for creche facilities, and rules regarding medical examinations and leave entitlements. The amendments also update references to Central Government officers and inspection procedures.

name: NATIONAL SERVICE, (EOURPEAN BRITISH SUBJECTS) AMENDMENT ORDINANCE, 1945

metadata.short_title: The National Service (European British Subjects) Amendment Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the National Service Act, 1940 (European British Subjects) Act, 1940.
metadata.parent_law: The National Service Act, 1940 (European British Subjects) Act, 1940
amends: The National Service Act, 1940 (European British Subjects) Act, 1940
metadata.one_line: Amends the National Service Act of 1940 regarding leave and appointments for European British subjects.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the National Service Act, 1940 (European British Subjects) to address issues arising from an emergency. It modifies provisions related to leave of absence, appointments to act in place of officers, and military custody arrangements. The amendments apply to European British subjects serving under the Crown.

metadata.short_title: The Present War (Definition) Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to define the meaning of 'war' and like expressions occurring in any enactment or other instrument.
metadata.one_line: Defines the meaning of 'war' and related expressions in enactments or instruments during the period from September 1939 to August 1941.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance clarifies the legal definition of 'war' and similar terms used in any enactment, rule, contract, deed, or other instrument. It applies to the period starting from September 1939 and ending on the third day of August 1941. The legislation ensures that references to war include the present hostilities unless the context indicates otherwise. It extends to the whole of British India and comes into force immediately upon promulgation.

name: NATIONAL SERVICE, (EOURPEAN BRITISH SUBJECTS) AMENDMENT ORDINANCE, 1945

metadata.short_title: The National Service (European British Subjects) Amendment Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the National Service (European British Subjects) Act, 1940.
metadata.parent_law: The National Service (European British Subjects) Act, 1940
amends: The National Service (European British Subjects) Act, 1940
metadata.one_line: Amends the National Service Act, 1940 regarding definitions and notice procedures for European British subjects.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the National Service (European British Subjects) Act, 1940 in response to an emergency. It substitutes specific clauses defining 'competent authority' and 'Officer Commanding' within the context of national service areas. The text also modifies provisions regarding the service of notices under the Act.

metadata.short_title: Provincial Debt Laws (Temporary Validation) Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to temporarily validate Provincial debt laws in certain respects while an emergency has arisen.
metadata.one_line: Temporarily validates provincial debt laws relating to promissory notes and money-lenders during an emergency.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance temporarily validates certain Provincial debt enactments enacted before December 12, 1944. It applies specifically to matters relating to promissory notes, transactions based on them, court declarations, orders, decrees, or arbitral awards arising from such transactions. The validation ensures these laws are deemed valid and effectual as if enacted by the Central Legislature for all relevant purposes.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Agricultural Produce Markets (Amendment) Act, 1944
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939.
amends: The Punjab Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939
key_definitions: Punjab Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939 (referred to as 'the said Act')
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939 regarding market committees and employee funds.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939 to add provisions concerning market committees for the benefit of employees. It includes specific amendments to sections 4, 27, and 28 of the said Act, addressing matters related to provident funds and market area definitions. The Act came into force immediately upon promulgation by the Governor on January 8, 1945.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Criminal Law (Amendment) Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to extend the validity of the Punjab Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1935.
metadata.one_line: Extends the validity of the Punjab Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1935 until April 30, 1946.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of the Punjab to extend the validity period of the Punjab Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1935. It substitutes a specific subsection within the original Act to ensure it remains in force until April 30, 1946. The Ordinance came into force immediately upon promulgation on November 30, 1945.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Consolidation of Holdings (Amendment) Act, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Consolidation of Holdings Act, 1919.
amends: The Punjab Consolidation of Holdings Act, 1919

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Consolidation of Holdings Act, 1919 to update provisions related to co-operative societies. It modifies sections concerning the Registrar's role as arbitrator in disputes over holding re-arrangements and alters decision-making thresholds within societies. The Act also omits specific clauses and substitutes new text regarding procedural rules for society members.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab District Boards (Amendment) Act, 1944
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab District Boards Act, 1883
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab District Boards Act, 1883 regarding local rates and exemptions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab District Boards Act, 1883 to establish a local rate of one anna per rupee on land. It grants the Provincial Government power to exempt specific lands or areas from this rate via notification. Additionally, it allows for the abolition or omission of the local rate upon the recommendation of a district board.

name: RESERVE BANK OF INDIA (TEMPORARY AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1945

metadata.short_title: The Reserve Bank of India (Temporary Amendment) Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to temporarily amend the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934

amends: The Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
metadata.one_line: Temporarily amends the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 during an emergency involving British Military Administration in Burma.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance temporarily amends the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 to address an emergency situation. It grants powers to the Central Government and the Reserve Bank of India regarding banking operations, currency functions, and remittances in relation to the British Military Administration in Burma. The amendment includes provisions for inquiries, reporting, and specific banking facilities exempt from certain rules during the temporary period.

metadata.short_title: The Sikh Gurdwaras (Amendment) Act, 1944
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925 regarding board elections, member qualifications, and land revenue definitions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925 to update provisions concerning the election of Board members and their qualifications. It introduces specific categories for Sikh sub-sects such as Mazhabi, Ramdaria, Amritdhari, and Kabirpanthis, while also defining terms like 'Patit pyaras' and restricting certain practices for voters. The legislation further modifies sections related to land revenue, local committee management, and the powers of the Board regarding gurdwara funds and contributions.

metadata.short_title: War Injuries (Compensation Insurance) Amendment Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the War Injuries (Compensation Insurance) Act, 1943.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the War Injuries (Compensation Insurance) Act, 1943 to address specific cases involving military personnel. It clarifies provisions related to officers who have deserted to the enemy, allowed themselves to be taken prisoner, or committed acts of disobedience and neglect of duty. The text also includes amendments to sections regarding the computation of time spent by a person in question as a prisoner of war or in enemy territory.

metadata.short_title: The War Risks (Factories) Insurance (Amendment) Ordinance, 1945
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the War Risks (Factories) Insurance Ordinance, 1942

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the War Risks (Factories) Insurance Ordinance, 1942 to clarify definitions related to explosives and munitions. It specifically addresses risks arising from explosions or fire in connection with the storage or transportation of such items. The amendment was promulgated by the Governor-General on June 1, 1945, and came into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: War Risks (Goods) Insurance (Termination) Ordinance, 1945

metadata.short_title: The Epidemic Diseases (Punjab Amendment) Act, 1944

It subjects the exercise of delegated powers by the Provincial Government to restrictions, limitations, and conditions specified by general or special orders. Additionally, it empowers a Deputy Commissioner to exercise these powers under the control and revision of the Provincial Government.

metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Women's Auxiliary Corps Ordinance, 1942

It also inserts new wording regarding His Majesty's Government in connection with the Armed Forces of the Crown. The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor-General on January 5, 1945, and came into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Aircraft (Amendment) Act, 1944
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Indian Aircraft Act, 1934.

It inserts specific clauses related to the authority for establishing air transport services and information requirements for applicants or holders of licenses. Additionally, it adds provisions requiring rules made under the Act to be laid before both Chambers of the Central Legislature within a specified period.

metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Pre-emption Act, 1913

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Pre-emption Act, 1913 by adding a new section designated as 21-A. The amendment applies to all suits instituted after the commencement of this Act concerning pre-emption rights. It specifically addresses situations where a suit is filed by a vendee-defendant following an improvement, inheritance, or cession made in their status.

metadata.commencement: on or after the commencement of this Act

The amendment applies to all suits or appeals instituted after the commencement of this Act involving improvement or inheritance. It clarifies that pre-emption rights shall not be affected when the defendant is in the status of a vendee-defendant in such suits.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Land Preservation (Chos) (Amendment) Act, 1944
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Land Preservation (Chos) Act, 1900.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Land Preservation (Chos) Act, 1900 to update provisions on erosion control measures. It expands the definition of 'rightholder' to include persons with rights to land, forest produce, or pasture who are not tenants or mortgagees. The legislation also modifies sections regarding earthworks, drainage, and the powers of the Deputy Commissioner in executing these measures within the Punjab.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937. It specifically addresses provisions related to grade designations and measures marks for quality control. The text indicates amendments to clauses concerning inspection and promotion of such articles.

name: CODE OF CRIMINAL PROCEDURE AMENDMENT ACT, 1943
