metadata.summary: This Act amends the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 to address procedures involving witnesses residing in Tribal Areas or Indian Political States. It allows commissioners exercising Magistrate powers to delegate duties and forward commissions to State Courts via official gazette or notification. Specific textual amendments are made to sections 503 and 307 of the Code to clarify officer roles and execution conditions.

name: CODE OF CRIMINAL PROCEDURE SECOND AMENDMENT ACT, 1943

metadata.short_title: The Code of Criminal Procedure (Second Amendment) Act, 1943
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 to allow husbands in armed forces to authorize others to make complaints on their behalf.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 to address situations where a husband serving in His Majesty's Armed Forces is unable to obtain leave of absence. It allows an authorized person to make a complaint on his behalf if he is precluded from doing so due to service conditions. The Act inserts a new section 199B detailing the form and requirements for such authorisation documents, including statements of allegations and certificates signed by the commanding officer.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Trade Employees (Amendment) Act, 1943
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Trade Employees Act, 1940
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Trade Employees Act, 1940 regarding working hours, definitions, and exemptions for specific establishments.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Trade Employees Act, 1940 to update definitions of employees and employers, adjust working hours, and redefine commercial establishments. It introduces exemptions for government offices, railways, hospitals, and specific retail sectors like funeral shops or cinemas. The legislation also clarifies liability rules for agents and servants acting without knowledge and omits certain previous sections.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Companies (Amendment) Act, 1943
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the said Indian Companies Act, 1913
key_definitions: provisions for bad and doubtful debts

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Indian Companies Act, 1913 to alter provisions concerning bad and doubtful debts. It specifically addresses Table A in the First Schedule and the Third Schedule of the said Act. The amendments include substitutions for sub-heads related to banking companies and provisions for bad and doubtful debts.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Tea Control (Second Amendment) Act, 1943
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Indian Tea Control Act, 1938.
metadata.parent_law: Indian Tea Control Act, 1938
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Tea Control Act, 1938 regarding export licenses, land planting dates, and troop amenities.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Indian Tea Control Act, 1938 to update provisions related to tea exports and land usage. It substitutes clauses in section 11 regarding Red Cross Society involvement and troop amenities, modifies section 17 concerning special license refusal powers, and adjusts definitions of land planted with tea in section 29. Additionally, it inserts new sub-sections into section 33 of the parent Act.

metadata.short_title: The Victoria Memorial (Amendment) Act, 1943
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Victoria Memorial Act, 1903
key_definitions: majority of those present and voting
acts done in pursuance of majority decision
metadata.one_line: Amends the Victoria Memorial Act, 1903 regarding trustee decisions and powers.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Victoria Memorial Act, 1903 to clarify the powers of Trustees. It specifies that acts done by a majority of present and voting Trustees are deemed to be acts of the Trustees themselves. The amendment also addresses procedures for impairing the Trustee's Authority.

metadata.short_title: The Motor Vehicles (Drivers) Amendment Act, 1943
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1942
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to one thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Amends the Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1942 regarding employer duties to reinstate drivers and compensation for failure.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1942 to impose specific duties on employers regarding the reinstatement of drivers whose employment was terminated. It establishes a mechanism where an employer must reinstate a driver or pay compensation equal to six months' remuneration if reinstatement is impracticable. The Act also prescribes penalties for employers who fail to obey orders passed under these provisions, including fines and mandatory re-employment.

name: Code of Civil Procedure (Second Amendment) Act, 1942

metadata.short_title: The Code of Civil Procedure (Second Amendment) Act, 1942
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of India (as per Gazette of India promulgation)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 regarding court-fee recovery after a suit abates due to plaintiff's death.
metadata.summary: This Act amends Order XXXIII of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 to address court-fee recovery when a suit abates due to the death of a plaintiff. It inserts a new rule (11A) allowing the Provincial Government to recover unpaid court-fees from the deceased plaintiff's estate. Additionally, it modifies existing rules to include the new provision and authorizes the Collector to recover these fees as if they were land revenue arrears.

name: CODE OF CIVIL PROCEDURE (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1942

metadata.short_title: The Code of Civil Procedure (Second Amendment) Act, 1942

metadata.one_line: Amends the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 regarding court fee recovery after a pauper plaintiff's death.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 to address the abatement of suits due to the death of a pauper plaintiff. It inserts a new rule (11A) allowing the Provincial Government to recover court fees from the deceased plaintiff's estate. Additionally, it modifies rules regarding the forwarding of decrees and the recovery of court fees as if they were land revenue arrears.

name: Cotton Ginning and Pressing Factories (Amendment) Act 1942

metadata.short_title: The Cotton Ginning and Pressing Factories (Amendment) Act, 1942
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Cotton Ginning and Pressing Factories Act, 1925.

amends: The Cotton Ginning and Pressing Factories Act, 1925

metadata.one_line: Amends the 1925 Act to require weekly cotton ginning returns in Chief Commissioners' Provinces.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Cotton Ginning and Pressing Factories Act, 1925 by inserting a new section requiring weekly returns on cotton ginned quantities. It applies initially to Chief Commissioners' Provinces but allows other provinces to adopt it via notification. The Act mandates that factory owners submit these returns to the relevant authority and prohibits publishing individual factory data while compiling provincial totals.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Boilers (Amendment) Act, 1942

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Indian Boilers Act, 1923 by adding a new clause to Section 3. The amendment specifically includes boilers appertaining to sterilizers or disinfectors commonly used in hospitals if they do not exceed twenty gallons in capacity. It was received assent from the Governor-General on March 2, 1942, and promulgated for general information.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Companies (Second Amendment) Act, 1942
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Indian Companies Act, 1913.

metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Companies Act, 1913 to define companies using 'bank' in their name as banking companies.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Indian Companies Act, 1913 by adding a proviso to section 277F. It stipulates that any company using the word 'bank' in its name while carrying on banking business shall be deemed a banking company. This applies even if accepting deposits is not the principal business of the company. The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification, provided it is not earlier than one year after publication.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Limitation (Amendment) Act, 1942
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Indian Limitation Act, 1908.

metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Limitation Act, 1908 regarding payment of debts and legacies.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Indian Limitation Act, 1908 to adjust limitation periods when payments are made on account of a debt or interest before expiration. It specifically addresses scenarios involving legacy payments and authorizes agents to make such payments. The amendment ensures that a fresh period of limitation is computed from the date of payment.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Limitation (Amendment) Act, 1942
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Indian Limitation Act, 1908.
metadata.parent_law: Indian Limitation Act, 1908
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Limitation Act, 1908 regarding limitation periods for interest on legacies.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Indian Limitation Act, 1908 to address the computation of limitation periods. Specifically, it substitutes a provision concerning interest on a legacy paid before the expiration of the prescribed period. When such payment is made by the person entitled or their authorized agent, a fresh period of limitation shall be computed from the date of payment.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Limitation (Amendment) Act, 1942
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Indian Limitation Act, 1908.
metadata.parent_law: Indian Limitation Act, 1870 (IX of 1908)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Limitation Act, 1908 regarding payment on account of debt or legacy before limitation expires.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Indian Limitation Act, 1908 to address specific scenarios involving debt and legacy payments. It substitutes subsection (1) of section 20 to clarify how the substantive period is computed when payment is made on account of a debt or legacy before the limitation period expires. The amendment stipulates that if such payment is duly authorized by an agent, the liable party shall be deemed to have paid from the fresh time when the payment was made.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Limitation (Amendment) Act, 1942
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Indian Limitation Act, 1908.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Limitation Act, 1908 regarding legacy payments and limitation periods.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Indian Limitation Act, 1908 to address issues concerning legacy payments. It substitutes specific text in Section 20 regarding the computation of limitation periods when a legacy payment is made before the account of a debt or interest is closed. The amendment clarifies that a fresh period of limitation shall be computed from the time when the legacy payment was made.

metadata.short_title: The Industrial Statistics Act, 1942

metadata.one_line: This Act facilitates the collection of industrial statistics by empowering provincial governments to appoint authorities and set rules.
metadata.summary: The Industrial Statistics Act, 1942 was enacted to facilitate the collection of specific statistics relating to industries across British India. It empowers Provincial Governments to direct the collection of data on factories, labour welfare, wages, housing, and industrial disputes through appointed statistics authorities. The Act grants these authorities access to records and premises while ensuring confidentiality for individual returns unless consent is given or prosecution is involved. Non-compliance with information requirements or disclosure of confidential data attracts specific penalties under the Act.

metadata.short_title: The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 1942

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Electricity (Emergency Powers) Act, 1941

The Act outlines procedures for transferring property, making rules, awarding compensation, and imposing penalties for disobedience.

metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Punjab
metadata.commencement: general information (no specific commencement date stated)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Land Preservation (Chos) Act, 1900 regarding erosion and sub-soil conservation.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Land Preservation (Chos) Act, 1900 to include provisions for sub-soil conservation and erosion prevention. It authorizes the Provincial Government to issue notifications directing measures in areas liable to erosion, particularly within the Siwalik mountain range or adjacent districts. The amendment also modifies specific sections of the original 1900 Act by omitting certain words and substituting new text related to government directions.

name: PUNJAB LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY (ALLOWANCES OF MEMBERS) ACT, 1942

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Legislative Assembly (Allowances of Members) Act, 1942
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for allowances of the Speaker and certain members of the Panjab Legislative Assembly.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Provincial Government may notify by notification
repeals: The Punjab Legislative Assembly (Allowances of Members) Act, 1937
metadata.one_line: Provides allowances for the Speaker and members of the Punjab Legislative Assembly, repealing the 1937 Act.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a framework for paying compensatory, travelling, and halting allowances to the Speaker and members of the Punjab Legislative Assembly. It defines terms such as 'Assembly', 'Committee', and 'Member' and sets conditions under which allowances may be withheld if attendance requirements are not met. The Act empowers the Provincial Government to make rules regarding the payment of these allowances and their interpretation, repealing the previous 1937 legislation.

name: PUNJAB LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY (WAR SERVICE) AMENDMENT) ACT, 1942

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Legislative Assembly (War Service) Amendment Act, 1942
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab Legislative Assembly (War Service) Act, 1940
amends: The Punjab Legislative Assembly (War Service) Act, 1940
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1940 War Service Act regarding compensatory allowances for assembly members.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Legislative Assembly (War Service) Act, 1940 to clarify provisions concerning compensatory allowances. It specifically addresses the calculation of allowances when a member attends fewer than ninety percent of meetings in a month or is under detention. The amendment substitutes specific words in Section 2 of the parent Act to align references with the Central Defence Department Government.

name: PUNJAB LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY (WAR SERVICE, AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1942

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Legislative Assembly (War Service, Amendment) Ordinance, 1942
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Punjab Legislative Assembly (War Service) Act, 1940.
metadata.parent_law: Government of India Act, 1935
amends: The Punjab Legislative Assembly (War Service) Act, 1940
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Legislative Assembly (War Service) Act, 1940 regarding Defence Department employment during war.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Legislative Assembly (War Service) Act, 1940 to address circumstances necessitating changes. It substitutes specific words in the long title and section 2 of the parent Act concerning the Defence Department. The amendment clarifies that the holder of an office shall be engaged in employment directly certified by the Governor as being concerned with the prosecution of the war.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Relief of Indebtedness (Amendment) Act, 1942
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Punjab Relief of Indebtedness Act, 1934.
amends: The Punjab Relief of Indebtedness Act, 1934
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Relief of Indebtedness Act, 1934 to clarify board proceedings and debt liability.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Relief of Indebtedness Act, 1934 to further regulate relief measures for indebted persons in Punjab. It adds provisions regarding the questioning of board proceedings and clarifies the finality of decisions made by Conciliation Boards on loan or debt liability. The legislation also inserts new sections to handle questions arising under the Act concerning whether a person is a debtor or if a loan exists.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Relief (Amendment) of Indebtedness Act, 1942
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Punjab Relief of Indebtednes Act, 1934.
amends: The Punjab Relief of Indebtedness Act, 1934
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Relief of Indebtedness Act, 1934 regarding debt proceedings and board decisions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Relief of Indebtedness Act, 1934 to modify provisions concerning debt boards and applications. It clarifies that decisions by the Debt Conciliation Board on whether a loan or liability constitutes a debt are final and cannot be questioned in court. Additionally, it inserts new clauses regarding statements filed for debts and extends protection against recovery of property specifically charged with the debt.

metadata.short_title: Workmen's Compensation (Amendment) Act, 1942
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923.
metadata.territorial_extent: general information (implied whole of India/Pakistan context based on Gazette)
repeals: Workmen's Compensation (Second Amendment) Act, 1939
key_definitions: War Allowances War (Mercantile Pensions Marine, etc.) Scheme, 1939
Navy, Marine, Army, Air Force or War Pensions Act, 1939
metadata.one_line: Amends the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 regarding war allowances and repeals the 1939 Amendment Act.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 to address provisions related to war allowances and pensions. It substitutes specific clauses in Section 15 regarding schemes for War Allowances and Detention Allowances made under various acts from 1939 and 1941. The Act clarifies that failure to give notice or make a claim is not a bar to proceedings if an application was made under the relevant war schemes and a Provincial Government certificate confirms the injury nature, provided proceedings are commenced within one month of receiving the certificate. Finally, it repeals the Workmen's Compensation (Second Amendment) Act, 1939.

It amends certain existing Acts to apply them correctly to Berar subjects and references the Nizam of Hyderabad. Additionally, it repeals a list of older Acts that previously applied to Berar under different orders.

metadata.short_title: The Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Act, 1941
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 regarding service and execution of summonses and warrants outside British India.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 to facilitate the sending and execution of legal processes outside British India. It establishes procedures for serving summonses and executing arrest warrants issued in British India at locations under the jurisdiction of Central Government or Crown Representative Courts. Additionally, it outlines how such foreign courts should handle received processes as if they were local, ensuring proper procedure for arrested persons.

name: Code of Criminal Procedure (Second Amendment) Act, 1941

metadata.short_title: The Code of Criminal Procedure (Second Amendment) Act, 1941
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 regarding service and execution of processes outside British India.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 to facilitate the service of summons and execution of warrants issued by courts in British India at places outside its local jurisdiction. It establishes procedures for sending such documents to presiding officers of courts established by the Central Government or Crown Representative in other parts of India. The Act ensures that processes received from outside British India are treated as if they originated within the local limits of the receiving court's jurisdiction.

metadata.short_title: Essential Services (Maintenance) Ordinance, 1941
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make provision for the maintenance of certain essential services.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year and fine
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance provides for the maintenance of essential services during emergencies in British India.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated to make emergency provision for the maintenance of certain essential services. It applies to all employment under the Crown or a Provincial Government deemed essential for securing public order, defence, war, safety, prosecution, maintaining the community, supplies, or services necessary in an official Gazette notification. The Ordinance empowers the Central or Provincial Government to declare specific employments or classes of employment as essential and to make rules regulating conditions of service.

metadata.short_title: The Factories (Amendment) Act, 1941
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Factories Act, 1934.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Factories Act, 1934 to allow provincial governments to declare provisions applicable to places with ten or more workers.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Factories Act, 1934 by empowering Provincial Governments to declare specific provisions applicable to certain places. It allows for notifications in the official Gazette to apply factory regulations to any place where a manufacturing process is carried on with ten or more workers. The Act defines such places as deemed factories to the extent that the declared provisions are made applicable.

metadata.short_title: The Federal Court Act, 1941
metadata.long_title: An Act to empower the Federal Court to make rules for regulating the presentation of appeals lying to that Court.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: Section IIIA of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
rule 17 of Order XLV of the First Schedule to the said Code
metadata.one_line: Empowers the Federal Court to make rules for regulating appeals and repeals specific sections of the Code of Civil Procedure.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Federal Court to create rules governing the presentation and prosecution of appeals before it. It specifically authorizes the court to make provisions regarding security for costs, proceedings in High Courts connected with such appeals, and the transmission of records. The legislation repeals Section IIIA of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and Rule 17 of Order XLV of its First Schedule which previously regulated these matters.

metadata.short_title: The Insurance (Amendment) Act, 1941
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Insurance Act, 1938.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Insurance Act, 1938 regarding insurer registration, policy lapses, and account keeping.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Insurance Act, 1938 to update definitions of insurers and provident societies. It introduces annual renewal requirements for insurer registrations with associated fees and penalties for non-compliance. The legislation also modifies provisions regarding policy lapses due to non-payment of premiums and adjusts clauses related to commission charges and investment activities.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1941
metadata.long_title: An Act to restrict the increase of rents on certain premises situated within the limits of urban areas in the Punjab.
metadata.territorial_extent: all urban areas in the Punjab
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may appoint by notification in the Official Gazette
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for one year and fine of five thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act restricts rent increases on premises in urban areas of Punjab and defines key terms like landlord and tenant.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1941 was enacted to limit the increase of rents on specific premises located within urban areas in the Punjab province. It applies to all urban areas in the region and defines critical terms such as 'landlord', 'tenant', 'premises', and 'standard rent' for regulatory purposes. The legislation grants police officers powers to arrest individuals committing offenses under the Act and authorizes entry into places with proper sanction, while excluding certain premises like cantonments or those used for business from its scope.

metadata.short_title: The Agricultural Produce Cess Act, 1940
metadata.long_title: An Act to make better financial provision for the Imperial Council of Agricultural Research.
metadata.one_line: Imposes a cess on certain agricultural produce exported from British India to fund the Imperial Council of Agricultural Research.
metadata.summary: This Act imposes a cess on specific articles of agricultural produce exported from British India. The proceeds are paid to the Imperial Council of Agricultural Research for its better financial provision. The Central Government is empowered to make rules regarding refunds, reserve funds, and tariff values in consultation with the Council.

metadata.short_title: The Arbitration Act, 1940
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate Arbitration and amend the law relating to arbitration in British India
repeals: Act IX of 1899 (The Indian Arbitration Act, 1899)
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends the law relating to arbitration in British India.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the law relating to arbitration in British India and amends previous legislation. It defines key terms such as arbitration agreements, awards, and courts involved in arbitration proceedings. The Act outlines procedures for appointing arbitrators and umpires, handling vacancies, conducting proceedings, and setting aside awards on specific grounds. It also addresses the impact of insolvency on arbitration agreements and provides powers to courts regarding interim awards and superseding references.

metadata.short_title: The Factories (Punjab Amendment) Act, 1940
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Factories Act, 1934, in its application to the Punjab.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Provincial Government may notify
metadata.max_penalty: 100 rupees for each day of contravention; fine up to 5,000 rupees; or imprisonment up to two years
metadata.one_line: Amends the Factories Act, 1934 to regulate factory establishment and registration in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Factories Act, 1934 specifically for its application to the Punjab province. It introduces restrictions on establishing or extending factories without permission from the Provincial Government and mandates a registration system for factories carrying out specific manufacturing processes. The Act also outlines penalties for contravention of new provisions regarding factory establishment, registration certificates, and fees.

metadata.short_title: The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 1940
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 regarding limits on stage carriage permits and route specifications.
metadata.summary: This Act serves to amend the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939. It specifically modifies Section 48 to limit the number of stage carriages or permits granted for any specified type within a region or route. The text also re-letters existing clauses and inserts new sub-clauses regarding restrictions on stage carriages operating only on specified routes or in specified areas.

metadata.short_title: Payment of Wages (Amendment) Ordinance, 1940
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Payment of Wages Act, 1936.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of India (as per Gazette header 'GOVERNMENT OF INDIA' and 'Acts of the Indian Legislature')
key_definitions: securities of the Government of India
securities of the Government of the United Kingdom
metadata.one_line: Amends the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 to allow deductions for approved War Savings schemes.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 to enable employers to make deductions from wages for investment in approved War Savings schemes. It specifically allows deductions for the purchase of securities issued by the Government of India or the Government of the United Kingdom with written authorization from an approved person. The amendment modifies Section 7 and Section 13 of the said Act to incorporate these new provisions regarding war savings investments.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Alienation of Land (Amendment) Act, 1940
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Panjab Alienation of Land Act, 1900.
amends: The Panjab Alienation of Land Act, 1900
metadata.one_line: Amends the Panjab Alienation of Land Act, 1900 regarding civil court jurisdiction and Deputy Commissioner powers.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Panjab Alienation of Land Act, 1900 to restrict civil court jurisdiction in matters concerning Deputy Commissioners. It inserts a new section defining the Deputy Commissioner's exclusive power to dispose of cognizance in specific cases. Additionally, it amends sections 8-B and 8-C by substituting references from 'Collector' to 'Deputy Commissioner'.

metadata.short_title: The Badshahi Mosque Fund Cess Act, 1939
metadata.long_title: An Act for the repair, provide maintenance for the creation and endowment of a fund for the Badshahi Mosque, Lahore.
metadata.one_line: Imposes a cess on land revenue to fund repairs and maintenance for the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore.
metadata.summary: This Act imposes a cess on the annual value of land owned by the Crown, Muslim institutions, or occupied by Muslims to create a fund for the Badshahi Mosque. The cess is levied at specific rates based on the annual value of the land and collected alongside land revenue. Proceeds are applied to the repair and endowment of the mosque after deducting collection expenses.

metadata.short_title: The Code of Civil Procedure (Amendment) Act, 1939
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for a certain purpose.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 regarding salary disbursement and officer appointments.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 to update provisions related to the Northern India Salt Department. It substitutes specific sections concerning the appointment of officers to control administration and modifies rules regarding the disbursement of salaries and allowances by courts. The amendments clarify instructions for disbursing authorities when salary limits are exceeded.

name: COTTON GINNING AND PRESSING FACTORIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1939

metadata.short_title: The Cotton Ginning and Pressing Factories (Amendment) Act, 1939
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Cotton Ginning and Pressing Factories Act, 1925, for certain purposes.
amends: Cotton Ginning and Pressing Factories Act, 1925
metadata.one_line: Amends the Cotton Ginning and Pressing Factories Act, 1925 regarding structural changes, gins usage, and bale marking.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Cotton Ginning and Pressing Factories Act, 1925 to regulate structural alterations in cotton ginning factories. It mandates that new constructions must minimize compliance issues with specific clauses and requires existing structures built after a certain date to follow approved plans. The Act also updates provisions regarding the use of roller gins and establishes presumptions about bale marking under the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.

metadata.short_title: The Employment of Children (Amendment) Act, 1939
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Employment of Children Act, 1938.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of India (as per 'Acts of the Indian Legislature')
metadata.one_line: Amends the Employment of Children Act, 1938 to restrict child employment in specific workshops and processes.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Employment of Children Act, 1938 to regulate child labor in workshops. It defines specific premises as workshops, prohibits employing children under twelve years old in certain processes, and introduces requirements for medical certificates regarding a child's age. The Act also empowers the Provincial Government to amend schedules of prohibited processes and outlines procedures for disputes over a child's age.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Oaths (Amendment) Act, 1939
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Indian Oaths Act, 1873, for a certain purpose.
metadata.parent_law: Indian Oaths Act, 1873
key_definitions: child under twelve years of age
witness who does not understand the nature of an oath or affirmation
Court or person having authority to examine such witness
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Oaths Act, 1873 regarding oaths for child witnesses under twelve.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Indian Oaths Act, 1873 to address situations involving child witnesses under twelve years of age. It stipulates that if a court or authorized person believes a child witness does not understand the nature of an oath or affirmation, the standard provisions regarding oaths shall not apply. Consequently, the absence of an oath does not render evidence inadmissible nor does it affect the witness's obligation to state the truth.

metadata.short_title: The Panth Piploda Courts (Amendment) Act, 1939
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Panth Piploda Courts Regulation, 1931, for a certain purpose.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Panth Piploda Courts Regulation, 1931 to allow appointment of further Additional Judges by the Central Government.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Panth Piploda Courts Regulation, 1931, specifically adding a sub-section to section 8. It empowers the Central Government to appoint a person as a further Additional Judge when the Court requires aid for disposing of pending business according to law.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Debtors' Protection (Amendment) Act, 1939
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Debtors' Protection Act, 1936.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Debtors' Protection Act, 1936 by adding definitions and sections regarding Commissioners.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Debtors' Protection Act, 1936 to provide further protection for debtors. It inserts a new section 6-A defining the Financial Commissioner and adds a definition for 'Commissioner' in section 8(3). The Act was enacted by the Provincial Assembly of Punjab on November 20, 1939.

metadata.one_line: Amends various Indian statutes and repeals obsolete or unnecessary enactments.
metadata.summary: This Act amends a wide range of existing Indian legislation to update terminology, references, and provisions. It also expressly repeals several older acts that are considered spent, unnecessary, or no longer in force. The Act includes savings clauses to protect existing rights, liabilities, and legal procedures unaffected by the amendments or repeals.

metadata.short_title: The Workmen's Compensation (Amendment) Act, 1939
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923, for a certain purpose.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 regarding wage calculations and court proceedings for non-monthly workers.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 to clarify the definition of 'monthly wages' and remove doubts about eligibility for workers paid on a non-monthly basis. It restores court proceedings if a worker was incorrectly denied status due to their wage structure. The amendments apply to proceedings concluded after July 1, 1934.

metadata.short_title: The Child Marriage Restraint (Second Amendment) Act, 1938
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of India (as per Gazette of India promulgation)
metadata.max_penalty: fine up to one thousand rupees or imprisonment (but no woman shall be punishable with imprisonment)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929 by inserting new sections regarding court injunctions and complaint procedures.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929 to strengthen provisions against child marriages. It introduces powers for courts to issue injunctions against arranged marriages in contravention of the Act and allows for the dismissal of complaints if security is not furnished. The Act also adds a new section creating an offence for disobeying court injunctions, with specific protection ensuring no woman is punishable by imprisonment.

metadata.short_title: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1938
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the criminal law.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Provincial Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment or fine for a term which may extend to one year
metadata.one_line: Amends criminal law regarding dissuasion from joining military forces and related offenses.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the criminal law to provide punishment for acts intended to adversely affect the recruitment of persons to serve in His Majesty's Forces. It specifically addresses dissuading or attempting to dissuade the public from entering Military, Naval, or Air Forces. The Act also covers offenses related to mutiny or insubordination under existing army, navy, and air force discipline acts. Punishment for these offenses may extend to one year imprisonment or a fine, subject to previous sanction of the Provincial Government.

metadata.short_title: The Cutchi Memons Act, 1938
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide that all Cutchi Memons shall be governed in matters of succession and inheritance by the Muhammadan Law.

repeals: The Cutchi Memons Act, 1920
metadata.one_line: Provides that all Cutchi Memons are governed by Muhammadan Law in matters of succession and inheritance.
metadata.summary: This Act stipulates that all Cutchi Memons shall be governed by the Muhammadan Law regarding succession and inheritance. It ensures that rights or liabilities acquired before its commencement remain unaffected. The Act also repeals the earlier Cutchi Memons Act, 1920.

metadata.short_title: The Dangerous Drugs (Amendment) Act, 1938
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Dangerous Drugs Act, 1930.
metadata.parent_law: The Dangerous Drugs Act, 1930
key_definitions: without being removed from being carried on a ship or conveyance
metadata.one_line: Amends the Dangerous Drugs Act, 1930 by adding a definition regarding bringing drugs into ports.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Dangerous Drugs Act, 1930 to include a specific definition related to drug trafficking. It clarifies the act of bringing dangerous drugs into any port intended for British India without removal from a ship or conveyance. The amendment was received by the Governor-General on February 26, 1938, and promulgated for general information.

metadata.short_title: The Employment of Children Act, 1938
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the admission of children to certain industrial employments.
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to five hundred rupees
metadata.one_line: Regulates admission of children to industrial employments in railways and ports across British India.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the admission of children to specific industrial employments within British India. It prohibits the employment of children under fifteen years of age in railway transport occupations and industries covered by the Indian Ports Act, 1908. The legislation establishes penalties for contravention, limits prosecution procedures, and provides for the issuance of certificates confirming a child has completed their fifteenth year.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Aircraft (Amendment) Act, 1938
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Indian Aircraft Act, 1934.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Aircraft Act, 1934 to empower the Central Government to make temporary rules regarding aircraft during epidemic outbreaks.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Indian Aircraft Act, 1934 to provide additional powers to the Central Government. It allows the government to take necessary measures and make temporary rules concerning aircraft, travelers, and aerodromes if an outbreak or threat of a dangerous epidemic disease occurs in India. These emergency rules can remain in force for up to three months unless extended by special order.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Coffee Cess (Amendment) Act, 1938
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Indian Coffee Cess Act, 1935, for a certain purpose.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Central Government by notification in the official Gazette may appoint
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Coffee Cess Act, 1935 regarding planters' association nominations.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Indian Coffee Cess Act, 1935 to update provisions related to planters' associations. It substitutes specific sub-clauses concerning nominations by the Coorg, Mysore, and Indian Planters' Associations. The Act received assent on April 8, 1938, and comes into force upon a future date appointed by the Central Government via official Gazette notification.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Companies (Amendment) Act, 1938
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Indian Companies Act, 1913, for certain purposes.
metadata.commencement: on the commencement of the Indian Companies (Amendment) Act, 1938
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Companies Act, 1913 regarding branch offices, banking limits, and winding up procedures.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Indian Companies Act, 1913 to update provisions related to branch office reporting, balance sheet copies, and director duties. It introduces restrictions on banking companies forming subsidiaries or holding shares in other companies. The Act also clarifies the role of liquidators in legal proceedings and adjusts winding up rules for specific historical contexts.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Finance Act, 1938

metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of British India, including British Baluchistan and the Sonthal Parganas
amends: Indian Post Office Act, VI of 1898

The Act ensures that no suit instituted within two years of its commencement shall be barred by limitation if it would not have been barred had the 1904 Act remained in force.

It defines key terms such as 'workman', 'employer', and various types of disablement, including partial and total. The Act applies to the whole of British India and sets out provisions for calculating wages and determining liability for injuries sustained during employment.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Penal Code (Amendment) Act, 1921
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Indian Penal Code.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Penal Code by adding section 121A and repealing sections 61 and 62.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Indian Penal Code by inserting a new section 121A regarding forfeiture of property and liability to fine. It also repeals sections 61 and 62 of the said Code. The Act was promulgated on September 29, 1921.

It also provides for the omission of a specific proviso in section 67 of the said Act.

metadata.one_line: An Act determining the salary of the Deputy-President of the Legislative Assembly at one rupee per month.
metadata.summary: This Act determines the salary for the Deputy-President of the Legislative Assembly. The salary is fixed at a rate of one rupee per mensem. Any doubts regarding whether a person was engaged in official work connected with the Assembly shall be referred to the President of the said Assembly for a final decision.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Lac Cess Act, 1921
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the levy and payment of a cess on lac exported from British India.
metadata.one_line: This Act levies a cess on exported lac and establishes the Lac Association to manage proceeds.
metadata.summary: The Indian Lac Cess Act, 1921 provides for the levy of a customs duty known as 'lac cess' on all lac exported from British India. The Act establishes the Lac Association to keep accounts of monies received and expended, subject to audit by the Governor-General in Council. It grants the Governor-General power to make rules regarding the association's operations, publication of reports, and the disposal of proceeds, which may be invested or used for promoting lac cultivation and scientific research.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 to address issues related to the service of summons on defendants. It provides mechanisms for dismissing suits if a defendant fails to appear after multiple summonses and avoids service of process. The Act also allows courts to extend time periods in specific cases where there is a sufficient cause.

The Act also updates definitions for original tenants and lineal descendants, including adopted sons with registered deeds.

It stipulates that after one year has elapsed from the date of such a report, no action shall be taken in the case of a sub-section so reported. The Act also covers regulations for burial grounds, control of dogs, suppression of nuisances, and procedures for arbitration and appeals.

metadata.summary: This Act provides for the appointment of census officers and their duties in connection with the taking of the census. It defines who must assist in the enumeration, including householders and village authorities, and outlines the obligation to answer questions truthfully. The Act also grants powers to local governments to enforce access for census purposes and prescribes penalties for refusal or false returns.

It substitutes specific time periods for serving notices and adds provisions allowing courts to order alternative security in cases involving deceased respondents who did not appear. The amendments ensure that proceedings can continue effectively even when a party has died, provided appropriate notice is given within specified limits.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Indian Extradition Act, 1903 to facilitate extradition proceedings. It inserts provisions allowing a District Magistrate or Chief Presidency Magistrate to record statements of accused persons arrested in accordance with local government orders. The amendment specifically addresses the procedure for recording statements before proceeding further in extradition cases.

metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regarding the office, powers, and duties of Official Trustees in British India.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law relating to the office of Official Trustee across British India and Native States. It defines the appointment, corporate status, and powers of the Official Trustee and Deputy Official Trustee, including their audit responsibilities and liabilities. The Act also repeals earlier legislation concerning official trustees and administrators of estates.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 by substituting specific figures in Schedule I related to stamp duties on bills or notes. It adjusts the payable amounts based on the value of the instrument, distinguishing between cases where more is payable than one rupee versus other thresholds. The Act also substitutes 'Article No. 5(e)' with 'Article No. 5(6)' in Section 23A of the parent Act.

metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887 regarding civil court jurisdiction and procedure for tenancy suits.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887 by adding a proviso to section 18. It addresses procedural matters in civil courts concerning tenancy suits. Specifically, it outlines conditions where a matter must be decided by a Civil Court and details procedures for returning plaints to the Collector when the suit value exceeds Rs. 1,000 or involves specific groups of cases.

metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regarding the office and duties of the Administrator General in India.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends previous legislation concerning the Administrator General's office and duties across British India. It outlines powers related to granting probate and letters of administration, managing estates of deceased persons, and handling unclaimed assets. The Act also establishes procedures for revocation of grants, auditing accounts, and defining the liability of the Government in suits against the Administrator General.

metadata.short_title: The Prisons (Amendment) Act, 1910
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Prisons Act, 1894.

metadata.summary: This Act amends section 52 of the Prisons Act, 1894. It inserts specific wording after 'Magistrate' and substitutes a proviso regarding the transfer of cases for trial by a District Magistrate first class or other designated magistrates. The amendments relate to the roles of Presidency Magistrates, Chief Magistrates, and First Class Magistrates.

metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 to adjust stamp duties on various financial instruments. It specifically revises rates for bills of exchange, loan agreements, and debentures, distinguishing between transferable and non-transferable securities. The legislation also clarifies exemptions and duties applicable to stock exchange transactions and brokerage notes.

metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to insolvency in towns having for their seat or within their limits a High Court or a Civil Court exercising ordinary original civil jurisdiction throughout an area not less than that of a District.

metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regarding insolvency proceedings in Presidency towns with High Courts.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law relating to insolvency in towns having a High Court or equivalent civil jurisdiction. It establishes the constitution and powers of courts handling insolvency, defines the role of the official assignee, and outlines procedures for proving debts, distributing property, and discharging insolvents. The Act also details appeals, penalties for fraudulent conduct, and provisions for small insolvencies.

metadata.short_title: Explosive Substances Act, 1908
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the law relating to explosive substances.
metadata.max_penalty: transportation for life or any shorter term, to which fine may be added, or with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, to which fine may be added
metadata.one_line: Amends laws regarding explosive substances by increasing penalties and criminalizing possession with unlawful intent.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the law relating to explosive substances to address inadequacies in existing legislation. It expands the scope of offenses to include attempts to cause explosions and making or possessing explosives with intent to endanger life or property. The Act shifts the burden of proof regarding lawful possession to the individual and provides severe penalties, including transportation and imprisonment, for violations.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1908
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the more speedy trial of certain offences and for the prohibition of associations dangerous to the public peace.
metadata.territorial_extent: The Provinces of Bengal and Eastern Bengal and Assam (extendable to other Provinces)
establishes: Special Bench of the High Court
metadata.max_penalty: three years imprisonment or fine or both
metadata.one_line: Provides for speedy trial of certain offences and suppression of dangerous associations via Special Benches.
metadata.summary: This Act facilitates the speedy trial of specific offences by establishing a Special Bench of three Judges in the High Court to conduct trials without a jury. It introduces an ex-parte inquiry process where the accused is not present during initial evidence collection, allowing for bail refusal if further inquiry into guilt is warranted. Additionally, the Act empowers authorities to declare associations dangerous to public peace as unlawful and imposes severe penalties on members or promoters of such groups.

It defines key terms such as applicant, defendant, and suit, and establishes specific time limits within which legal actions must be instituted. The Act also provides for the acquisition of ownership by possession and includes provisions for savings and repeals of previous enactments.

It establishes the roles of Registrars and Sub-Registrars, outlines procedures for presenting documents, and sets rules for fees and penalties. The Act applies across British India and includes specific provisions for Sindh and military cantonments.

The amendment clarifies that securities for money include debentures issued by municipal bodies or trustees of port presidency-towns like Rangoon Town or the port of Karachi.

It adds provisions regarding notifications issued by the Local Government and substitutes specific clauses in section 18 of the said Act. The Act also repeals certain sections of the United Provinces Excise Law Amendment Act, 1904.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Coinage Act, 1906

metadata.summary: This Act consolidates previous legislation regarding the coinage of India. It defines various types of coins as legal tender, including gold, silver, nickel-silver, and bronze. The Act establishes procedures for cutting diminished or defaced coins and provides powers to make rules regarding mint operations and coin dimensions.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Merchant Shipping (Amendment) Act, 1906
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the law relating to merchant seamen.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Merchant Shipping Act, 1859 regarding seamen's agreements and discharge.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the law relating to merchant seamen by adding specific provisions to Section 23 of the Indian Merchant Shipping Act, 1859. It addresses the termination of agreements for foreign-going ships registered in British India or trading with the United Kingdom. The amendment ensures that such agreements do not extend over two voyages and must terminate within six months from execution or arrival at a port.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Stamp (Amendment) Act, 1906
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Indian Stamp Act, 1899.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 regarding stamp duties on fire insurance policies and receipts.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 to adjust stamp duty rates for fire insurance policies and receipts. It specifies new duties based on the sum insured and whether a policy is original or duplicate. The amendments also add provisions regarding receipts given for premiums or consideration within one month.

metadata.short_title: Indian Tariff (Amendment) Act, 1906
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Indian Tariff Act, 1894
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Tariff Act, 1894 by increasing duties on spirits and liqueurs effective February 26, 1906.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Indian Tariff Act, 1894 to increase duties on specific types of spirits and liqueurs. It substitutes new duty rates for spirits measured in Imperial Gallons or six-quart bottles, raising the rate from Rs. 6 to Rs. 10 per gallon. The amendments apply to spirits with a strength less than London proof and come into force on February 26, 1906.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Presidency Small Cause Courts Act, 1882 to address issues related to costs in suits and procedural requirements. It introduces provisions for drawing up statements of facts when doubts arise about a decree's effect on merits. The Act also modifies sections regarding references to the High Court and applications under the Civil Procedure Code.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Incumbered Estates Act, 1896 to provide better protection to debtors and their sureties. It substitutes specific words in sections 2 and 5 of the parent Act and repeals sections 22(1) and 22(r). The legislation also repeals two earlier Acts from 1881 and 1884 related to incumbered estates.

metadata.short_title: The Court-fees (Amendment) Act, 1905
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Court-fees Act, 1870.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Court-fees Act, 1870 by substituting 'immoveable property' with 'immovable property'.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Court-fees Act, 1870 to correct terminology regarding property types. Specifically, it substitutes the word 'immoveable' with 'immovable' in section 2, sub-section (i) of the 1870 Act. The amendment applies to references concerning tenancy and immovable property found within the original statute.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Minor Canals Act, 1905
metadata.long_title: An Act to make better provision for the construction of minor canals and water-courses in the Punjab and its dependencies.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Punjab and its dependencies
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the construction, maintenance, and water distribution of minor canals in the Punjab.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Minor Canals Act, 1905 provides legal provisions for the construction and management of minor canals and water-courses within the Punjab. It grants powers to the Collector and Local Government regarding land acquisition, water regulation, and the imposition of water dues. The Act also outlines procedures for resolving disputes, compensating affected parties, and removing obstructions to ensure proper water flow.

name: AN ACT TO REVIVE AND CONTINUE SECTION 8B OF THE INDIAN TARIFF ACT, 1894

metadata.summary: This Act was enacted by the Governor-General in Council to revive and continue Section 8B of the Indian Tariff Act, 1894. It came into force on the first day of April 1904. The Act also repeals Sub-section (2) of section 1 of the Tariff (Amendment) Act, 1902.

metadata.short_title: The Co-operative Credit Societies Act, 1904
metadata.long_title: An Act to encourage thrift and help among agriculturists and for providing credit to co-operative societies
metadata.one_line: An Act to encourage thrift and provide credit to co-operative societies registered under this Act.
metadata.summary: This Act encourages thrift and provides credit facilities among agriculturists through the formation of co-operative societies. It establishes the Registrar as the authority for registration and management oversight of these societies. The legislation defines membership criteria, limits on capital held by members, and outlines procedures for audit, inspection, and dispute resolution via arbitration.

metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of British India, the Santhal Parganas and the Pargana of Spiti

metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 regarding duties on instruments involving marketable securities and specific agreements.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 to clarify stamp duty charges on instruments related to marketable securities. It adds definitions for 'security of a marketable stock or mine' and modifies sections concerning leases, mortgages, pawn agreements, and pledges. The amendments specify how duties are calculated for deposits made as security and adjust entries in the Act's schedule regarding exempted instruments.

metadata.short_title: The Local Authorities Loan Act, 1904
metadata.long_title: An Act to make further provision regarding the borrowing of money by certain local authorities.
metadata.one_line: This Act empowers certain local authorities to borrow money and sets conditions for repayment.
metadata.summary: The Local Authorities Loan Act, 1904 provides further powers for specific local authorities to borrow money. It regulates the conditions under which such borrowing can occur and establishes limits on the total amount borrowed relative to previous loans. The Act applies only to local authorities specified in the Schedule attached to the legislation.

metadata.summary: This Act regulates the Border Military Police Force in the North-West Frontier Province. It defines the force's constitution, appointment of officers and men, superintendence, and conditions of service. The legislation also outlines various offences committed by members of the force and prescribes punishments ranging from fines to transportation for life.

The legislation also provides mechanisms for compensation for damage, penalties for non-compliance, and provisions for the revocation of licenses.

metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for imposing restrictions on the use and enjoyment of land in the vicinity of defence works and other obstructions, and for determining the amount of compensation to be made on account of such imposition.

metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Local Government to impose restrictions on the use of land near defence works to keep them free from obstructions. It establishes a legal framework for determining compensation payable to persons affected by these restrictions. The Act defines key terms such as 'land', 'person interested', and 'Collector', and outlines the procedures for inquiries, awards, and appeals.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provident Funds Act of 1897 to provide further protection for subscribers and depositors. It ensures that sums in a Provident Fund are not liable to attachment under any court decree or order. The legislation also clarifies the distribution of funds upon the death of a subscriber or depositor, prioritizing payments to widows and children.

The Act outlines procedures for appointing guardians, managing properties, and handling unclaimed assets upon death.

repeals: XIV The Code of Civil Procedure, 1882
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws relating to civil procedure in British India.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the laws relating to civil procedure in British India. It defines the jurisdiction of courts, procedures for instituting suits, execution of decrees, appeals, and arbitration. The Act also repeals earlier enactments and provides for the amendment of other related statutes.

name: AN ACT TO AMEND AND PROVIDE FOR THE FURTHER CONTINUANCE OF THE CURRENCY CONVERSION (ARMY ANNUAL) ACT, 1899

metadata.short_title: The Currency Conversion (Army Annual) Amendment Act, 1900
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend and provide for the further continuance of the Currency Conversion (Army Annual) Act, 1899
repeals: section 2 of the Currency Conversion (Army Annual) Act, 1899
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1899 Currency Conversion Act regarding army annual payments and repeals its section 2.
metadata.summary: This Act amends and provides for the further continuance of the Currency Conversion (Army Annual) Act, 1899. It substitutes provisions related to the calculation of sums in British currency equivalent to Indian rupees. The Act repeals section 2 of the original 1899 legislation.

name: AN ACT TO PROVIDE FOR THE COURT-FEE PAYABLE ON CERTAIN APPLICATIONS TO THE COURT OF THE FINANCIAL COMMISSIONER OF THE PUNJAB

metadata.short_title: The Court-Fee Act, 1900
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the Court-fee payable on certain applications to the Court of the Financial Commissioner of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: Amends previous Acts to specify court fees for applications to the Financial Commissioner of the Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act amends several earlier statutes regarding court fees payable on specific applications. It applies to the Court of the Financial Commissioner of the Punjab within its revisional jurisdiction. The legislation was enacted by the Governor-General of India and received assent on June 30, 1900.

metadata.short_title: The Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1900
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Law of Evidence with respect to Bankers' Books, Letters Patent; and for other purposes.
key_definitions: Act of the Governor General of India in Council
metadata.one_line: Amends the Law of Evidence regarding the admissibility of bankers' books and letters patent.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 to specifically address evidence related to bankers' books. It defines terms such as 'company' in the context of registered companies under any Parliament or the Governor-General. The legislation was promulgated by the Government of India and came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Prisoners Act, 1900
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to prisoners in British India.
metadata.commencement: on the date of publication in the Gazette
repeals: Act III of 1866
Act VIII of 1897
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws relating to prisoners, warrants, licences, and prison administration in British India.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the law regarding prisoners in British India, covering their custody, transfer, removal, and execution of sentences. It defines the powers of officers in charge of prisons, procedures for delivering persons under warrant, and regulations concerning licences and reformatory schools. The Act also addresses the transfer of actionable claims and debts, including warranties of solvency, and repeals earlier inconsistent enactments.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Land Preservation (Chos) Act, 1900
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the better preservation and protection of certain portions of the mountain or forests within the Punjab; and to regulate, restrict or prohibit the action of chos, forests flowing through such mountain range or affected or liable to be within that range, by deforestation or by the action of streams.
metadata.one_line: Regulates preservation of forests and chos streams in Punjab, restricting deforestation and resource extraction.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the better preservation and protection of mountain ranges, forests, and chos (streams) within the Punjab. It empowers the Local Government to regulate, restrict, or prohibit activities such as deforestation, timber cutting, cattle grazing, stone quarrying, and burning within notified areas. The legislation applies to the whole of Pakistan and comes into force immediately upon publication.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Limitation (Ancestral Land Alienation) Act, 1900
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the period of limitation of suits arising out of ancestral land alienation in the Punjab.
metadata.one_line: Regulates limitation periods for suits regarding ancestral land alienation in Punjab under customary law.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the period of limitation for suits arising from the alienation of ancestral land in the Punjab. It applies to cases governed by Customary Law and clarifies definitions such as 'instituted' and 'land' in relation to the Indian Limitation Act, 1877. The Act specifies time limits for various types of suits, including those involving heirs, declaratory decrees, and mortgages, ensuring that claims are brought within prescribed periods.

metadata.short_title: The Repealing and Amending Act, 1903
metadata.long_title: An Act to facilitate the citation of certain enactments, to amend certain enactments and to repeal certain other enactments.

metadata.one_line: An Act to facilitate citation, amend specific enactments, and repeal obsolete laws across British India.
metadata.summary: This Act was enacted by the Governor-General's Council to streamline legal citations and remove obsolete legislation. It amends various regulations concerning land revenue, municipal acts, and civil courts while repealing specific outdated sections and entire acts deemed unnecessary. The provisions apply generally to the territories under the Government of India at the time, including Punjab.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Arbitration Act, 1899
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law relating to arbitration and award
metadata.one_line: Amends the law relating to arbitration and award in India.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the existing laws regarding arbitration and awards in India. It provides for the appointment of arbitrators and umpires, the powers of courts in relation to arbitration proceedings, and the enforcement of awards. The Act also covers matters such as costs, delays in making awards, and the conduct of arbitration proceedings.

metadata.short_title: The Reformatory Schools Act, 1897
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Reformatory Schools for youthful offenders.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of British India (except territories administered by the Lieutenant-Governor of the Punjab)
repeals: Act V of 1870
metadata.max_penalty: transportation or imprisonment for fifteen years
metadata.one_line: Establishes reformatory schools for youthful offenders and defines their management and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the establishment and management of Reformatory Schools for youthful offenders convicted of offences punishable by transportation or imprisonment. It creates a Board of Management and an Inspector-General to oversee these institutions, which are intended to be inspected at least once every three years. The Act outlines procedures for sending offenders to these schools instead of regular jails, issues licenses for their employment, and defines the powers of District Magistrates and Courts in relation to youthful offenders.

metadata.short_title: The Land Acquisition Act, 1894
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law for the acquisition of land for public purposes and for compensation and to provide for the determination of such compensation
repeals: The Land Acquisition Act, 1870
metadata.one_line: Amends the law for acquiring land for public purposes and determining compensation in British India.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the existing laws regarding the acquisition of land for public purposes within British India. It defines key terms such as 'land', 'person claiming to be interested', and 'Collector' to facilitate the process. The Act provides mechanisms for determining compensation, entering land for surveys, and making rules for enforcement by the Local Government.

metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Guardian and Ward.

metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regarding guardianship of minors in British India.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law relating to guardians and wards. It applies to the whole of British India and establishes procedures for appointing guardians for minors. The Act defines key terms such as 'guardian', 'ward', and 'minor', and outlines the powers and duties of guardians regarding the person and property of wards. It also repeals numerous previous enactments related to minors and courts across different provinces.

name: AN ACT TO AMEND THE INDIAN COMPANIES ACT, 1882

metadata.short_title: Act VI of 1887
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Indian Companies Act, 1882.
metadata.parent_law: Indian Companies Act, 1882
metadata.one_line: Amends the Indian Companies Act, 1882 regarding debt priority and liquidator duties during winding-up.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Indian Companies Act, 1882 to establish specific priorities for debts payable during a company's winding-up. It grants priority to revenue, taxes, cesses, rates, and salaries of clerks or servants not exceeding one thousand rupees, as well as wages of labourers or workmen not exceeding five hundred rupees. These claims rank equally among themselves and must be paid before other debts if the assets are insufficient.

metadata.short_title: The General Clauses Act, 1887
metadata.long_title: An Act to define certain terms used in Acts and to make provisions as to the construction of such Acts
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of India (as per Gazette of India publication)
metadata.one_line: Defines terms used in Acts and provides rules for construction of legislation.
metadata.summary: This Act defines specific terms commonly used in Indian legislation and establishes rules for interpreting statutes. It applies to all Acts made by the Governor-General's Council and addresses issues related to local authorities, publication of rules, and the construction of provisions regarding offences and penalties. The Act came into force immediately upon promulgation.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Small Cause Courts Act, 1887
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the established law relating to the Courts of Small Causes.
repeals: Act XI of 1865
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends law relating to Courts of Small Causes in British India.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the established law regarding Courts of Small Causes across British India. It establishes these courts, defines their jurisdiction over civil suits involving money or debts, and outlines procedures for trials, decrees, and executions. The Act also details the appointment of judges, appeals, and specific types of suits cognizable by these courts.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Ports Act, 1889
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the laws relating to Ports and port-charges.
