Act III of 1872 (Calcutta Port Commissioners)
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws relating to ports, port-charges, vessel safety, and pilotage in India.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends existing laws regarding ports and port charges in India. It defines the powers of local governments, harbour masters, and conservators of ports. The legislation establishes rules for vessel safety, pilotage requirements, and the levying of port dues. It also repeals several earlier acts related to ports and shipping.

name: AN ACT TO AMEND ACT XXII OF 1881

metadata.short_title: Act VI of 1885
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend Act XXII of 1881
metadata.one_line: Amends Act XXII of 1881 regarding Excise officers' powers and court cognizance of offences.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Local Government Act XXII of 1881 to clarify the powers conferred on Excise-officers. It substitutes specific salary words in section 47 and modifies section 20 regarding complaints by Collectors or Excise-officers. The Act also repeals certain words in section 20 concerning the time limits for instituting prosecutions after the expiry of a specified period.

metadata.short_title: The Suits Valuation Act, 1887
metadata.long_title: An Act to prescribe the mode of determining the jurisdiction of Courts in certain suits relating to land.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Governor General in Council, by notification in the Gazette of India, directs
repeals: Act VII of 1884
metadata.one_line: Prescribes the mode of determining court jurisdiction for suits relating to land in British India.
metadata.summary: This Act prescribes the method for determining the jurisdictional value of suits relating to land. It empowers the Local Government to make rules for valuing land and interests in land within specific areas. The Act also addresses issues regarding over-valuation and objections raised before appellate courts, ensuring that procedural defects do not affect the merits of a suit.

metadata.short_title: The Land Acquisition (Mines) Act, 1885
metadata.long_title: An Act to enable the Local Government to acquire land for mines and to provide for compensation and other matters connected therewith.
metadata.territorial_extent: the territories under the administration of the Lieutenant-Governor of Punjab and its dependencies
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to two hundred rupees
metadata.one_line: Enables the Local Government to acquire land for mines and provides compensation mechanisms.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Local Government in Punjab to declare that land is needed for mine purposes and to acquire it accordingly. It outlines procedures for giving notice, determining compensation, and preventing or restricting the working of mines if necessary. The Act also defines key terms such as 'Local authority' and 'Company', and establishes penalties for refusing inspection or failing to repair damage caused by mining operations.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Explosives Act, 1884
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the manufacture, transportation, importation and possession of explosives.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Governor General in Council, by notification in the Gazette of India, appoints
repeals: Act XII of 1876
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to three thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Regulates the manufacture, importation, transportation and possession of explosives in India.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the manufacture, transportation, importation, and possession of explosives to ensure public safety. It grants powers to make rules regarding licensing, fees, and inspection procedures for explosives. The Act defines various terms related to explosives and establishes penalties for offences committed under it.

metadata.short_title: The Powers of Attorney Act, 1882
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law relating to powers of attorney and instruments creating them
key_definitions: instrument creating a power of attorney
metadata.one_line: Amends the law relating to powers of attorney and instruments creating them in India.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the legal framework governing powers of attorney and the instruments that create them. It establishes rules regarding certified copies of deposited instruments and their evidentiary value in High Courts. The legislation includes specific provisions protecting married women and minors from unauthorized powers of attorney.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Trusts Act, 1882
metadata.long_title: An Act to define and amend the law relating to private trusts and trustees
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of India (excluding the territories administered by the Lieutenant-Governors of the North-West Provinces and Oudh, the Central Provinces, Assam, and the Chief Commissioner's Province)
repeals: Act XXV of 1866
The Statute of Frauds (29 Car. II)
The Specific Relief Act, 1877
metadata.one_line: Defines and amends the law relating to private trusts, trustees, beneficiaries, and related obligations in India.
metadata.summary: This Act defines and amends the law relating to private trusts and trustees within British India. It outlines the creation of trusts, duties and liabilities of trustees, rights of beneficiaries, and powers regarding trust property management. The Act also includes provisions for the extinction of trusts and repeals earlier enactments such as the Statute of Frauds and parts of the Specific Relief Act.

name: AN ACT TO AMEND THE LAND IMPROVEMENT ACT, 1871

metadata.short_title: Act XXI of 1876
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Land Improvement Act, 1871.
metadata.commencement: on the twenty-eighth day of December 1876
metadata.one_line: Amends the Land Improvement Act, 1871 regarding recovery of advances and definitions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Land Improvement Act, 1871 to remove doubts about its provisions. It clarifies how arrears from borrowers or sureties are treated as land revenue debts and defines 'improvement' to include suitable buildings for museums in Calcutta. The Act extends to the whole of British India and came into force on December 28, 1876.

name: AN ACT TO EXTEND THE CRIMINAL TRIBES ACT, 1871 (ACT VII OF 1876)

metadata.short_title: The Native Passenger Ships Act, 1876
metadata.long_title: An Act to extend the Criminal Tribes Act, 1871 (Act VII of 1876)
metadata.one_line: Extends the Criminal Tribes Act, 1871 to include regulations for native passenger ships in the Lower Provinces.
metadata.summary: This Act extends the provisions of the Criminal Tribes Act, 1871 to cover native passenger ships. It amends specific sections of the earlier Act by inserting new clauses regarding landowners, occupiers, and agents. The legislation applies to the Lower Provinces and involves the Lieutenant-Governors of Bengal.

name: AN ACT TO PROVIDE FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF THE PUBLIC MUSEUM OF CALCUTTA

metadata.short_title: Act XXII of 1876
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the management of the Public Museum of Calcutta
metadata.commencement: on the twenty-eighth day of December 1876
repeals: Act XVII of 1866
Act XXVI of 1871
metadata.one_line: An Act to provide for the management of the Public Museum of Calcutta and amend previous Acts.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the management of the Public Museum of Calcutta by establishing a body of Trustees. It amends previous legislation regarding land improvement and museum collections, defining terms such as 'improvement' and outlining the powers of the Collector and Trustees. The Act covers the preservation of collections, management of library and museum buildings, and the administration of trust property.

metadata.short_title: The Bhaunagar Act, 1876
metadata.long_title: An Act to validate certain acts of executive authority done in the Scheduled villages of Bhaunagar and to provide for their cession to Her Majesty's dominions.
metadata.territorial_extent: British India (specifically the Scheduled villages of Bhaunagar)
metadata.one_line: Validates executive acts in Bhaunagar villages and cedes them to British India.
metadata.summary: This Act validates all acts, proceedings, and sentences done by the Political Agent in the Scheduled villages of Bhaunagar prior to February 1st, 1866. It formally cedes these villages from the Thakur's possession to Her Majesty's dominions following a notification dated December 5th, 1876. The legislation also provides indemnity to the Thakur and his successors against any liability arising from future proceedings regarding these lands.

metadata.short_title: The Bombay Municipal Debentures Act, 1876
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law relating to the transfer of mortgages of rates and taxes levied by the Bombay Municipal Corporation for the purposes of that Act, and to provide for their consolidation.
metadata.one_line: Amends laws regarding transfer and consolidation of Bombay Municipal Corporation mortgages.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the legal framework governing the transfer of mortgages related to rates and taxes levied by the Bombay Municipal Corporation under the 1865 Act. It provides mechanisms for consolidating these mortgages into a single debenture held by the Corporation, thereby simplifying management and reducing stamp duty liabilities. The legislation also defines the powers of appointed Managers and clarifies that they are deemed public servants within the meaning of the Indian Penal Code.

metadata.short_title: The Transfer of Property Act, 1882
metadata.long_title: An Act to define and amend the law relating to transfer of property by sale, mortgage, lease, gift, exchange, and other modes of alienation.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of India (excluding Jammu and Kashmir)
repeals: Act IV of 1872
metadata.one_line: Defines and amends the law relating to transfer of property by sale, mortgage, lease, gift, exchange, and other modes.
metadata.summary: This Act defines and amends the law regarding the transfer of property in India. It covers various methods of alienation including sale, mortgage, lease, gift, and exchange. The legislation also addresses foreclosure, redemption, actionable claims, and the rights and liabilities of parties involved in these transactions.

metadata.short_title: The Dramatic Performances Act, 1876
metadata.long_title: An Act for the better control of public dramatic performances.
metadata.max_penalty: three months imprisonment or fine
metadata.one_line: Controls public dramatic performances to prevent obscenity, defamation, and sedition.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Local Government to prohibit public dramatic performances that are obscene, defamatory, or seditious. It grants Magistrates the authority to issue orders prohibiting such performances and to seize houses or rooms used for them. The Act applies throughout British India and comes into force immediately upon promulgation.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Merchant Seamen's Act, 1876
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law relating to Merchant Seamen in India.
metadata.territorial_extent: India; to the whole of India
metadata.max_penalty: one thousand rupees or imprisonment for three months or both
metadata.one_line: Amends laws regarding merchant seamen in India concerning discharge, distress, desertion, and imprisonment.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the law relating to merchant seamen in India. It addresses issues such as the discharge of distressed seamen, the prohibition of engaging native seamen without leave, and penalties for desertion or absence. The Act also establishes rules for dealing with imprisoned seamen and apprentices, and clarifies definitions regarding wages and value.

metadata.short_title: The Native Coinage Act, 1876
metadata.long_title: An Act to enable the Governor-General in Council to declare such coins made in any Native State of India as legal tender in British India.
metadata.one_line: This Act allows the Governor-General to declare coins from Native States as legal tender in British India.
metadata.summary: The Native Coinage Act, 1876 empowers the Governor-General in Council to declare coins minted in Native States of India as legal tender within British India. It applies to gold, silver, and copper coins and ensures they meet specific standards regarding fineness, weight, and design devices. The Act also grants the authority to impose charges for coinage and refining, while prohibiting the importation of foreign coins without permission.

metadata.short_title: The Opium Act, 1876
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law relating to opium.
repeals: Act No. VII of 1836
Act No. XI of 1840
Act No. XXI of 1856
Act No. X of 1871
metadata.one_line: Amends laws relating to opium cultivation, manufacture, import, export, and sale in British India.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the existing laws relating to opium in British India. It covers the cultivation of poppy, manufacture, possession, transport, importation, exportation, and sale of opium. The Act grants powers to the Governor-General in Council to make rules regarding these subjects and repeals several earlier enactments.

metadata.short_title: The Native Passenger Ships Act, 1876
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Native Passenger Ships.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Governor General in Council directs by a notification in the Gazette of India
repeals: Act XXV of 1859
Act XII of 1870
Act XII of 1872
Madras Act II of 1862
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regarding native passenger ships, certificates, overcrowding, and penalties in British India.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law relating to native passenger ships operating within British India. It establishes requirements for certificates, limits on passenger numbers, health standards, and provisions for intermediate voyages. The Act empowers officers to inspect ships and imposes penalties for non-compliance with regulations regarding safety, overcrowding, and passenger welfare.

metadata.short_title: The Repealing Act, 1876
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal certain enactments and to amend others.
metadata.one_line: An Act repealing numerous Acts of the Governor-General and Governors passed between 1835 and 1874.
metadata.summary: This Act serves to repeal specific sections or entire enactments of various laws passed by the Governor-General in Council and Governors of Bombay, Bengal, and Madras. It addresses obsolete provisions related to courts, taxes, public servants, and local administration across British India. The repeals are detailed in a comprehensive schedule listing the original Act numbers, subjects, and the specific extent of the repeal.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Incumbered Estates Act, 1876
metadata.long_title: An Act to relieve from Incumbrances the estates of debtor's debts and property, liabilities whether moveable or immoveable, of Jagirdars and Zamindars in Sindh.
metadata.max_penalty: punishment for false averments in the statement submitted to the Commissioner
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the relief of indebted Jagirdars and Zamindars in Sindh by managing their estates to discharge debts.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Incumbered Estates Act, 1876 was enacted to relieve Jagirdars and Zamindars in Sindh from heavy debts and liabilities on their estates. It establishes a Commissioner to inquire into the debtor's situation and a Manager to take control of the property for management and liquidation purposes. The Act outlines the powers of the Manager to recover rents, pay debts, and dispose of property, as well as provisions for appeals and the restoration of ownership once debts are discharged.

metadata.short_title: The Stage Carriages (Amendment) Act, 1876
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Stage Carriages Act, 1861.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Stage Carriages Act, 1861 to extend provisions regarding horse-drawn carriages and passengers for hire.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Stage Carriages Act, 1861 by substituting specific expressions and provisions. It extends the application of the Act to include all horse-drawn carriages used for conveying passengers for hire to or from any place in India. The legislation ensures that existing licensing and regulatory provisions apply equally to these vehicles.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Oaths Act, 1873
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to oaths, affirmations and solemnities, and to repeal certain enactments relating thereto
metadata.commencement: on the first day of May 1873
repeals: Act X of 1878
metadata.max_penalty: punishment for perjury under the Penal Code
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regarding oaths, affirmations, and solemnities used in courts across British India.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the law relating to oaths, affirmations, and solemnities administered in courts. It applies to witnesses, jurors, interpreters, and native priests within British India. The Act provides procedures for administering oaths or affirmations, including specific forms for different religious groups, and outlines penalties for refusing to take an oath or giving false evidence.

metadata.summary: This Act regulates irrigation, navigation, and drainage across the territories of the North-Western Provinces, Punjab, Oudh, and Central Provinces. It establishes powers for canal officers to levy dues, stop water supply, and recover damages caused by obstructions or accidents. The legislation also defines offences related to canals and drainage works, prescribing penalties including fines and imprisonment, while repealing several earlier acts concerning water rents and navigation.

metadata.one_line: This Act repeals numerous obsolete statutes and regulations applicable to British India.
metadata.summary: The Repealing Act, 1873 was enacted by the Governor-General's Council to repeal a long list of obsolete enactments. It covers various subjects including civil procedure, revenue laws, customs duties, and judicial appointments across British India. The Act specifies that repeals do not affect remedies or rights acquired under the repealed laws before their repeal.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Christian Marriage Act, 1872
metadata.long_title: An Act to remove Doubts as to the Validity of certain Marriages had and solemnized within the British Territories in India; and for other purposes.

metadata.one_line: Regulates solemnization and registration of marriages among Christians in British India.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the solemnization and registration of marriages among Christians within the British Territories in India. It establishes procedures for giving notice, obtaining certificates from Marriage Registrars, and securing consent from guardians where necessary. The Act also outlines penalties for false certificates or solemnizing marriages without due authority and repeals several earlier enactments regarding marriage validity.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Laws Act, 1872
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the laws relating to civil and criminal judicature, pre-emption, land revenue, insolvency, police officers, armed men, foreign vagrants, and miscellaneous matters in the Punjab.
repeals: Enactments specified in the second schedule
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment and fine
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regarding civil/criminal courts, pre-emption, land revenue, and police in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends various laws applicable to the Province of the Punjab as of March 28, 1872. It covers a wide range of subjects including civil and criminal judicature, pre-emption rights on immovable property, land revenue regulations, insolvency proceedings, and police powers. The Act also addresses specific issues such as the slaughter of kine, control over armed men, foreign vagrants, and the jurisdiction of Courts of Wards. It repeals earlier enactments listed in its schedules to unify the legal framework.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Limitation Act, 1871
metadata.long_title: An Act for the limitation of suits and for other purposes

Act XI of 1855
Act XXV of 1857
metadata.one_line: This Act limits the time within which suits and applications can be instituted in British India.
metadata.summary: The Indian Limitation Act, 1871 consolidates laws relating to the limitation of suits and applications. It prescribes specific time periods for instituting various types of legal actions, including those involving disability, fraud, or mistake. The Act also details how these periods are computed and lists numerous repealed enactments that previously governed similar matters.

metadata.short_title: The Indian Contract Act, 1872
metadata.long_title: An Act to define the when, how and to what extent contracts may be formed, the when they become enforceable by law, the rescission of such contracts, the performance thereof, the discharge of parties thereto, and the remedies for breach of contract.
metadata.commencement: on the first day of September, 1872
repeals: Act VI of 1872
metadata.one_line: Defines the formation, enforceability, performance, and remedies for breach of contracts in British India.
metadata.summary: This Act defines when contracts are formed and how they become legally enforceable. It outlines the conditions under which agreements are valid, void, or voidable, including requirements for free consent and capacity. The legislation also covers the performance of contracts, discharge of parties, and remedies available in case of breach, such as damages and specific performance.

name: AN ACT FOR THE SUPPRESSION OF MURDEROUS OUTRAGES IN CERTAIN DISTRICTS OF THE PUNJAB

metadata.short_title: An Act for the Suppression of Murderous Outrages in Certain Districts of the Punjab
metadata.long_title: An Act for the Suppression of Murderous Outrages in Certain Districts of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: This Act provides special procedures and penalties for suppressing murderous outrages committed by fanatics in certain districts of Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act was enacted to address frequent murders and vexatious practices by fanatics in specific districts of the Punjab. It establishes a special trial procedure before the Commissioner of the Division, allowing for trials with the aid of Assessors appointed by the Commissioner. The Act mandates that upon conviction, the offender's property is forfeited to the Government and their body disposed of as the Commissioner thinks fit. It also provides for inquests into deaths resulting from wounds received during these offences and allows for the detention of suspected persons pending orders from the Lieutenant Governor.

name: AN ACT RELATING TO MESNE PROFITS AND TO IMPROVEMENTS MADE BY HOLDERS UNDER DEFECTIVE TITLES IN CASES

metadata.short_title: The Mesne Profits Act, 1855
metadata.long_title: An Act relating to holders under defective titles in cases to which the English Law is applicable.
metadata.one_line: Provides compensation to bond fide holders under defective titles for improvements or mesne profits when evicted.
metadata.summary: This Act secures the value of improvements made by bond fide holders under defective titles in cases where English law applies. It ensures that such holders are not charged with rent or profits if they were unaware of a defect in their title at the time of payment. If a holder erects a building or makes an improvement believing they hold a fee simple estate, they are entitled to compensation for the value of those improvements or the option to purchase the land interest upon eviction by someone with a better title.

name: AN ACT TO ENABLE EXECUTORS, ADMINISTRATORS OR REPRESENTATIVES TO SUE AND BE SUED FOR CERTAIN WRONGS

metadata.short_title: Act XII of 1855
metadata.long_title: An Act to enable Executors, Administrators or Representatives to sue and be sued for certain wrongs.
metadata.one_line: Enables executors and administrators to sue/be sued for wrongs committed by a deceased person within one year of death.
metadata.summary: This Act allows actions to be maintained against or by the executors, administrators, or representatives of a deceased person for wrongs committed during their lifetime. It applies specifically to cases where pecuniary loss has occurred to the estate due to such wrongs. The action must be commenced within one year after the death of the person who committed the wrong. Furthermore, if damages are recoverable under English law, they shall be paid in like order of administration as simple contract debts.

name: AN ACT TO PROVIDE COMPENSATION TO FAMILIES FOR LOSS OCCASIONED BY THE DEATH OF A PERSON CASUED BY ACTIONABLE WRONG

metadata.short_title: The Fatal Accidents Act, 1855
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide compensation to families for loss occasioned by the death of a person caused by actionable wrong
metadata.territorial_extent: India (as per text 'promulgated for general information' under Governor-General)
metadata.one_line: Provides compensation to families for loss caused by death resulting from actionable wrongs.
metadata.summary: This Act allows families to claim damages for the death of a person caused by an actionable wrong, even if the death occurred during a crime. The action is brought in the name of the executor or administrator of the deceased estate. Claims must be filed within twelve months of the death, and recovered amounts become part of the deceased's assets.

name: PUNJAB UNIVERSITY OF TECHNOLOGY RASUL (AMENDMENT) ACT 2025

metadata.short_title: The Punjab University of Technology Rasul (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Punjab University of Technology Rasul Act 2018

metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab University of Technology Rasul Act 2018 to update its name and add employee repatriation options.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab University of Technology Rasul Act 2018 to substitute 'Rasul, Mandi Baha Uddin' for 'Technology Rasul' in the long title. It also updates references to the institution's name throughout the Act and adds a provision allowing employees transferred under specific subsections to exercise a one-time option for repatriation to their original service. Additionally, it expands the scope of study fields in section 4 to include engineering, sciences, management, and related fields.

name: PUNJAB URBAN IMMOVABLE PROPERTY TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT 2025

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958.
amends: The Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958
subjects: Excise, Taxation and Narcotics Control Department

metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958 to add whistleblower definitions and reward mechanisms.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958 to introduce provisions for rewarding whistleblowers who report tax evasion, fraud, or corruption. It defines a 'whistleblower' as a person reporting concealment or evasion leading to tax collection and establishes a reward system sanctioned by the Commissioner out of imposed penalties. Additionally, it creates a separate provision for rewarding officers and officials of the Excise, Taxation and Narcotics Control Department for meritorious conduct in detecting such cases.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Vagrancy (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Punjab Vagrancy Ordinance, 1958.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Vagrancy Ordinance, 1958 to expand definitions of 'person' to include transgender individuals and introduce a new definition for 'organizer'. It substitutes sections on punishment, cognizance, and jurisdiction to impose stricter penalties for organizing or employing persons and children for vagrancy. The amendments also clarify that offences under the Ordinance are cognizable and non-bailable, except those under section 9.

metadata.short_title: The Court Fees Act, 1870
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the enactments relating to court-fees in British India.

Act No. XXXII of 1865
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws regarding court fees and stamp duties for various courts in British India.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates previous enactments relating to the levy and collection of court fees in British India. It applies to High Courts, District Courts, Small Cause Courts, and other subordinate courts within the Presidency towns. The legislation outlines procedures for determining fees based on market value or fixed amounts, rules for stamping documents, exemptions for specific types of cases, and mechanisms for refunds or objections. It also repeals earlier acts concerning court fees in certain regions.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Punjab Wildlife (Protection, Preservation, Conservation and Management) Act, 1974 to update definitions regarding protected areas and captive animals. It introduces new provisions against cruelty to animals, regulates the use of hawks, falcons, and dogs for hunting without a special license, and establishes specific procedures for investigation and trial of offences by Special Courts. The legislation also omits certain sections from the original 1974 Act and sets compensation limits for repeat offenders.

The legislation also provides for the creation of governing bodies like the Academic Council and Selection Board, along with financial committees to manage the university's operations.

metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the South Hill University.

It empowers the university to offer instruction across diverse faculties including Engineering, Law, Medicine, and AI, while establishing mechanisms for finance, planning, and faculty selection.

metadata.summary: The Act provides for the reconstitution of the Sugarcane Research and Development Board with its headquarters at Lahore. It defines the composition of the Board, including members from various government departments, universities, and the Pakistan Sugar Mills Association. The Board is empowered to conduct research on sugarcane varieties, promote best farm management practices, and perform environmental impact studies under the supervision of the Government.

It creates District Bait-ul-Mal Committees to ensure equitable distribution of funds to the deserving and needy, including the elderly, disabled, students, and poor families. The Act outlines procedures for financial assistance, audit requirements, and the power of the Council to make rules.

name: PUNJAB INFORMATION OF TEMPORARY RESIDENTS ORDINANCE 2015 [URDU VERSION]

metadata.short_title: Ordinance for Information of Temporary Residents Punjab 2015
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance for the purpose that all relevant information regarding migrants and other temporary residents be collected.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for up to six months and a fine ranging from ten thousand rupees to one lakh rupees
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab, Department of Law and Parliamentary Affairs
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance mandates information collection on temporary residents in Punjab to curb terrorism and crime.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes a legal framework for collecting information regarding migrants and temporary residents within the province of Punjab. It requires owners, landlords, hoteliers, and tenants to provide specific details about guests and occupants to the police within strict timeframes, such as three hours or forty-eight hours depending on the situation. The collected data is intended to be used by the police for community policing, intelligence gathering, and investigating terrorist crimes and other offenses under the Pakistan Penal Code. The document also outlines penalties for non-compliance, including imprisonment and fines, while defining key terms like 'Hotel', 'Hostel', and 'Tenant'.

The law also mandates the forfeiture of seized property upon conviction and authorizes the Government to classify weapons via notifications.

The law applies to the entire Province of Punjab and comes into force immediately upon publication.

It prohibits unnecessary noise, restricts usage near places of worship during prayer times, and bans sectarian broadcasts. The Government determines specific limits via notification, while police officers conduct inspections and seize offending equipment. Violations attract imprisonment up to six months and fines between 25,000 and 100,000 rupees.

name: ASSET MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY OF PUNJAB ORDINANCE 2026

metadata.short_title: The Asset Management Authority of Punjab Ordinance, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish the Asset Management Authority of Punjab.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Asset Management Authority of Punjab to manage and monetize government assets in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Asset Management Authority of Punjab as an autonomous statutory body to effectively manage and utilize government assets. The Authority is empowered to attract investment, undertake development projects, and generate revenue through transparent, market-driven mechanisms such as auctions, leases, and public-private partnerships. It aims to address under-utilized provincial assets, enhance fiscal requirements, and improve service delivery by creating a centralized digital inventory and utilizing best-practice governance models.

name: PUNJAB WATER AND SANITATION AUTHORITY ACT 2025

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Water and Sanitation Authority Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of the Punjab Water and Sanitation Authority
repeals: Lahore Development Authority Act, 1975 (XXX of 1975)
Punjab Development of Cities Act, 1976 (XIX of 1976)
Punjab Water Act, 2019 (XXI of 2019)
establishes: Punjab Water and Sanitation Authority Fund
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Punjab Water and Sanitation Authority to oversee water supply and sanitation systems in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Water and Sanitation Authority to develop, operate, and maintain water supply and sanitation systems while conserving groundwater. The Authority is a body corporate with powers to acquire property and enforce policies across specified districts in Punjab. It supersedes previous regulations under the Lahore Development Authority Act, 1975 and the Punjab Development of Cities Act, 1976, ensuring continuity for ongoing projects and employees.

name: ALI BIN USMAN INSTITUTE, MULTAN ACT 2025

metadata.short_title: Ali Bin Usman Institute, Multan Act 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Ali Bin Usman Institute, Multan.
metadata.one_line: Establishes Ali Bin Usman Institute, Multan as a private sector body corporate with perpetual succession.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Ali Bin Usman Institute, Multan in the private sector with its main campus located at Multan. The Institute is constituted as a body corporate having perpetual succession and a common seal, empowered to acquire, hold, and dispose of property. It functions through various bodies including an Academic Council, Board of Governors, and committees for finance and planning, offering degrees across multiple faculties such as Management Sciences, Law, Medicine, and Engineering.

name: PUNJAB EDUCATION, CURRICULUM, TRAINING AND ASSESSMENT AUTHORITY ACT 2025

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Education, Curriculum, Training and Assessment Authority Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to transform, innovate and raise educational standards to achieve excellence by cohesively coordinating curriculum and textbook development, student assessments and examinations, teacher training and robust monitoring and evaluation regime in the Punjab
repeals: The Punjab Curriculum and Textbook Board Act, 2015 (Act VI of 2015)
The Punjab Examination Commission Act, 2010 (Act XI of 2010)
establishes: Punjab Education, Curriculum, Training and Assessment Authority
metadata.one_line: Establishes a new Authority to coordinate curriculum, assessments, and teacher training in Punjab while repealing previous boards.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Punjab Education, Curriculum, Training and Assessment Authority to transform and raise educational standards in the province. It coordinates curriculum development, textbook production, student assessments, examinations, and teacher training under a robust monitoring regime. The Authority is established as a body corporate with headquarters in Lahore, comprising members from various government departments, academia, and civil society. Upon its commencement, this Act repeals the Punjab Curriculum and Textbook Board Act 2015 and the Punjab Examination Commission Act 2010, transferring their functions, employees, and posts to the new Authority.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Land Revenue (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967.
metadata.parent_law: The Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Punjab, Law and Parliamentary Affairs Department
metadata.one_line: Amends the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967 to integrate digital systems, update definitions, and streamline revenue administration in Punjab.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967 to align land revenue administration with modern technology and advancements in electronic processes. It updates definitions for terms like 'Digital Cadaster' and 'Patwar', omits references to Tribal Areas which do not exist in Punjab, and facilitates digital service of notices and summons. The document also harmonizes the Act with the Punjab Land Records Authority Act, 2017, and introduces timelines for mutations and partitions to reduce litigation.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Locum Hiring Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for quality healthcare services by making availability of specialized human resource on locum basis.
metadata.administering_body: Specialized Healthcare and Medical Education Department of the Government of the Punjab
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the hiring of locum medical staff in Punjab to ensure quality healthcare services.
metadata.summary: The Punjab Locum Hiring Act, 2025 establishes a framework for hiring specialized human resources on a temporary or contract basis to improve healthcare service availability. It creates a Locum Policy Committee to identify resource deficiencies and approve hiring terms, while also forming Department Selection Committees to manage the recruitment process transparently. The Act defines key terms such as 'locum', 'clinical staff', and 'Institution', and outlines duties for hired staff including adherence to safety guidelines and protocols.
